<P>The eighth season of <I><A href="/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_(TV_series)" title="The Walking Dead (TV series)">The Walking Dead</A></I>, an American <A href="/wiki/Apocalyptic_and_post-apocalyptic_fiction" title="Apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction">post-apocalyptic</A> <A href="/wiki/Horror_fiction" title="Horror fiction">horror</A> <A href="/wiki/Television_series" class="mw-redirect" title="Television series">television series</A> on <A href="/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel)" title="AMC (TV channel)">AMC</A>, premiered on October 22, 2017,<SUP id="cite_ref-S8premiere_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-S8premiere-1">[1]</A></SUP> and will consist of 16 episodes<SUP id="cite_ref-ew_s8_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ew_s8-2">[2]</A></SUP> split into two eight-episode parts, with the second part debuting on February 25, 2018.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Developed for television by <A href="/wiki/Frank_Darabont" title="Frank Darabont">Frank Darabont</A>, the series is based on the <A href="/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_(comic_book)" title="The Walking Dead (comic book)">eponymous series of comic books</A> by <A href="/wiki/Robert_Kirkman" title="Robert Kirkman">Robert Kirkman</A>, <A href="/wiki/Tony_Moore_(artist)" title="Tony Moore (artist)">Tony Moore</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Charlie_Adlard" title="Charlie Adlard">Charlie Adlard</A>. The executive producers are Kirkman, David Alpert, <A href="/wiki/Scott_M._Gimple" title="Scott M. Gimple">Scott M. Gimple</A>, <A href="/wiki/Greg_Nicotero" title="Greg Nicotero">Greg Nicotero</A>, <A href="/wiki/Tom_Luse" title="Tom Luse">Tom Luse</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Gale_Anne_Hurd" title="Gale Anne Hurd">Gale Anne Hurd</A>, with Gimple as <A href="/wiki/Showrunner" title="Showrunner">showrunner</A> for the fifth consecutive season. The eighth season has received mostly positive reviews.</P>
<P>This season adapts the "All Out War" story arc from the comics, with the survivors of the Alexandria Safe-Zone, the Hilltop, the Kingdom, and later the Scavengers taking on <A href="/wiki/Negan" title="Negan">Negan</A> (<A href="/wiki/Jeffrey_Dean_Morgan" title="Jeffrey Dean Morgan">Jeffrey Dean Morgan</A>) and the Saviors.<SUP id="cite_ref-s8regulars_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-s8regulars-4">[4]</A></SUP></P>

<P>The eighth season features twenty series regulars overall. For this season, <A href="/wiki/Katelyn_Nacon" title="Katelyn Nacon">Katelyn Nacon</A>, <A href="/wiki/Khary_Payton" title="Khary Payton">Khary Payton</A>, <A href="/wiki/Steven_Ogg" title="Steven Ogg">Steven Ogg</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Pollyanna_McIntosh" title="Pollyanna McIntosh">Pollyanna McIntosh</A> were promoted to series regular status, after previously having recurring roles, while <A href="/wiki/Seth_Gilliam" title="Seth Gilliam">Seth Gilliam</A> and <A href="/wiki/Ross_Marquand" title="Ross Marquand">Ross Marquand</A> were added to the opening credits.</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Starring">Starring</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Walking_Dead_(season_8)&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Starring">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<UL>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Andrew_Lincoln" title="Andrew Lincoln">Andrew Lincoln</A> as <A href="/wiki/Rick_Grimes" title="Rick Grimes">Rick Grimes</A>, the series' <A href="/wiki/Protagonist" title="Protagonist">protagonist</A>, a former sheriff and the leader of Alexandria, who is leading a new alliance to fight Negan and the Saviors.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Norman_Reedus" title="Norman Reedus">Norman Reedus</A> as <A href="/wiki/Daryl_Dixon" title="Daryl Dixon">Daryl Dixon</A>, Rick's right-hand man, the group's primary hunter and a recruiter for Alexandria.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Lauren_Cohan" title="Lauren Cohan">Lauren Cohan</A> as <A href="/wiki/Maggie_Greene" title="Maggie Greene">Maggie Rhee</A>, the pregnant widow of <A href="/wiki/Glenn_Rhee" title="Glenn Rhee">Glenn</A> and a leading figure of the Hilltop.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Chandler_Riggs" title="Chandler Riggs">Chandler Riggs</A> as <A href="/wiki/Carl_Grimes" title="Carl Grimes">Carl Grimes</A>, Rick's bold and courageous teenage son.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Danai_Gurira" title="Danai Gurira">Danai Gurira</A> as <A href="/wiki/Michonne" title="Michonne">Michonne</A>, Rick's katana-wielding girlfriend, who acts as a mother figure to Carl and Judith.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Melissa_McBride" title="Melissa McBride">Melissa McBride</A> as <A href="/wiki/Carol_Peletier" title="Carol Peletier">Carol Peletier</A>, a fierce survivor who is spurred into fighting the Saviors as revenge for the deaths of her friends.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Lennie_James" title="Lennie James">Lennie James</A> as <A href="/wiki/Morgan_Jones_(The_Walking_Dead)" title="Morgan Jones (The Walking Dead)">Morgan Jones</A>, the first survivor Rick had ever encountered, who now resides in the Kingdom and fights for his sanity.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Alanna_Masterson" title="Alanna Masterson">Alanna Masterson</A> as <A href="/wiki/Tara_Chambler" title="Tara Chambler">Tara Chambler</A>, a caring, witty member of the group and supply runner for Alexandria who serves as a liaison with Oceanside.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Josh_McDermitt" title="Josh McDermitt">Josh McDermitt</A> as <A href="/wiki/Eugene_Porter" title="Eugene Porter">Eugene Porter</A>, a timorous former member of the group whose resourcefulness leads Negan to take him under his wing.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Christian_Serratos" title="Christian Serratos">Christian Serratos</A> as <A href="/wiki/Rosita_Espinosa" title="Rosita Espinosa">Rosita Espinosa</A>, an impulsive member of the group, who is motivated to avenge her ex-boyfriend Spencer and Abraham's death.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Seth_Gilliam" title="Seth Gilliam">Seth Gilliam</A> as <A href="/wiki/Gabriel_Stokes_(The_Walking_Dead)" title="Gabriel Stokes (The Walking Dead)">Gabriel Stokes</A>, a priest who has become hardened from his experiences with Rick's group.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Ross_Marquand" title="Ross Marquand">Ross Marquand</A> as <A href="/wiki/Aaron_(The_Walking_Dead)" title="Aaron (The Walking Dead)">Aaron</A>, an Alexandrian recruiter who brought Rick's group to Alexandria and is currently in the fight against the Saviors.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Jeffrey_Dean_Morgan" title="Jeffrey Dean Morgan">Jeffrey Dean Morgan</A> as <A href="/wiki/Negan" title="Negan">Negan</A>, the sociopathic and charismatic leader of the Saviors who serves as the season's primary antagonist.</LI>
</UL>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Also_starring">Also starring</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Walking_Dead_(season_8)&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Also starring">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<UL>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Austin_Amelio" title="Austin Amelio">Austin Amelio</A> as <A href="/wiki/Dwight_(The_Walking_Dead)" title="Dwight (The Walking Dead)">Dwight</A>, a former subordinate of Negan who now works for Rick as a double agent against the Saviors.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Tom_Payne_(actor)" title="Tom Payne (actor)">Tom Payne</A> as <A href="/wiki/Paul_%22Jesus%22_Monroe" title="Paul "Jesus" Monroe">Paul "Jesus" Rovia</A>, a scout for the Hilltop.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Xander_Berkeley" title="Xander Berkeley">Xander Berkeley</A> as <A href="/wiki/Gregory_(The_Walking_Dead)" title="Gregory (The Walking Dead)">Gregory</A>, the selfish and hypocritical leader of the Hilltop whose influence diminished with Maggie's prominence.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Khary_Payton" title="Khary Payton">Khary Payton</A> as <A href="/wiki/King_Ezekiel" title="King Ezekiel">King Ezekiel</A>, the charismatic leader of the Kingdom who allies with Rick against the Saviors.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Steven_Ogg" title="Steven Ogg">Steven Ogg</A> as Simon, a former mortgage broker and Negan's ruthless second-in-command.<SUP id="cite_ref-New_Regulars_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-New_Regulars-5">[5]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Katelyn_Nacon" title="Katelyn Nacon">Katelyn Nacon</A> as Enid, a former member of Alexandria who moved to Hilltop to be with Maggie, and has formed a relationship with Carl.<SUP id="cite_ref-New_Regulars_5-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-New_Regulars-5">[5]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Pollyanna_McIntosh" title="Pollyanna McIntosh">Pollyanna McIntosh</A> as Jadis, the deceptive leader of the Scavengers who betrayed Rick's group, and maintains a neutral stance in the war.<SUP id="cite_ref-New_Regulars_5-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-New_Regulars-5">[5]</A></SUP></LI>
</UL>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Production">Production</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Walking_Dead_(season_8)&action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section: Production">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P><I>The Walking Dead</I> was renewed by AMC for a 16-episode eighth season on October 16, 2016,<SUP id="cite_ref-ew_s8_2-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ew_s8-2">[2]</A></SUP> and that same month it was reported that <A href="/wiki/Maria_Bello" title="Maria Bello">Maria Bello</A> would have a role on the show.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> Production began on April 25, 2017, in <A href="/wiki/Atlanta,_Georgia" class="mw-redirect" title="Atlanta, Georgia">Atlanta, Georgia</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> On July 12, 2017, production was shut down after stuntman <A href="/wiki/John_Bernecker" title="John Bernecker">John Bernecker</A> was killed, after falling more than 20 feet onto a concrete floor.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> Production resumed on July 17.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The season premiere, which also serves as the series' milestone <A href="/wiki/100_episodes" title="100 episodes">100th episode</A>, was directed by executive producer <A href="/wiki/Greg_Nicotero" title="Greg Nicotero">Greg Nicotero</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Director801_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Director801-10">[10]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In November 2017, it was announced that <A href="/wiki/Lennie_James" title="Lennie James">Lennie James</A> who portrays <A href="/wiki/Morgan_Jones_(The_Walking_Dead)" title="Morgan Jones (The Walking Dead)">Morgan Jones</A>, would be leaving <I>The Walking Dead</I> after the conclusion of this season, and he will join the cast of the spin-off series <I><A href="/wiki/Fear_the_Walking_Dead" title="Fear the Walking Dead">Fear the Walking Dead</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP></P>

</TR>

<TH scope="row" id="ep103" style="text-align:center">103</TH>
<TD>4</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"<A href="/wiki/Some_Guy_(The_Walking_Dead)" title="Some Guy (The Walking Dead)">Some Guy</A>"</TD>
<TD>Dan Liu</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/David_Leslie_Johnson" title="David Leslie Johnson">David Leslie Johnson</A></TD>
<TD>November 12, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-11-12</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.69<SUP id="cite_ref-8.04_15-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8.04-15">[15]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #555752">Ezekiel's group is overwhelmed by the Saviors, who kill all of them except for Ezekiel himself and Jerry. Carol clears the inside of the compound, killing all but two Saviors, who almost escape but are eventually caught by Rick and Daryl. En route to the Kingdom, Ezekiel, Jerry, and Carol are surrounded by walkers, but Shiva sacrifices herself to save them. The trio returns to the Kingdom, where Ezekiel's confidence in himself as a leader has diminished.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep104" style="text-align:center">104</TH>
<TD>5</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"<A href="/wiki/The_Big_Scary_U" title="The Big Scary U">The Big Scary U</A>"</TD>
<TD>Michael E. Satrazemis</TD>
<TD><I>Story by</I> : Scott M. Gimple & David Leslie Johnson & <A href="/wiki/Angela_Kang" title="Angela Kang">Angela Kang</A><BR />
<I>Teleplay by</I> : David Leslie Johnson & Angela Kang</TD>
<TD>November 19, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-11-19</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>7.85<SUP id="cite_ref-8.05_16-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8.05-16">[16]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #555752">After confessing their sins to each other, Gabriel and Negan manage to escape from the trailer. Simon and the other lieutenants grow suspicious of each other, knowing that Rick’s forces must have inside information. The workers in the Sanctuary become increasingly frustrated with their living conditions, and a riot nearly ensues, until Negan returns and restores order. Gabriel is locked in a cell, where Eugene discovers him sick and suffering. Meanwhile, Rick and Daryl argue over how to take out the Saviors, leading Daryl to abandon Rick.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep105" style="text-align:center">105</TH>
<TD>6</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"<A href="/wiki/The_King,_the_Widow,_and_Rick" title="The King, the Widow, and Rick">The King, the Widow, and Rick</A>"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/John_Polson" title="John Polson">John Polson</A></TD>
<TD>Angela Kang & Corey Reed</TD>
<TD>November 26, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-11-26</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.28<SUP id="cite_ref-8.06_17-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8.06-17">[17]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #555752">Rick visits Jadis in hopes of convincing her to turn against Negan; Jadis refuses, and locks Rick in a shipping container. Carl encounters Siddiq in the woods and recruits him to Alexandria. Daryl and Tara plot to deviate from Rick’s plans by destroying the Sanctuary. Ezekiel isolates himself at the Kingdom, where Carol tries to encourage him to be the leader his people need. Maggie has the group of captured Saviors placed in a holding area and forces Gregory to join them as punishment for betraying Hilltop.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep106" style="text-align:center">106</TH>
<TD>7</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"<A href="/wiki/Time_for_After" title="Time for After">Time for After</A>"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Larry_Teng" title="Larry Teng">Larry Teng</A></TD>
<TD>Matthew Negrete & Corey Reed</TD>
<TD>December 3, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-12-03</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>7.47<SUP id="cite_ref-8.07_18-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8.07-18">[18]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #555752">After learning of Dwight's association with Rick's group, Eugene affirms his loyalty to Negan and outlines a plan to get rid of the walkers surrounding the Sanctuary. With help from Morgan and Tara, Daryl drives a truck through the Sanctuary’s walls, flooding its interior with walkers, killing many Saviors. Rick finally convinces Jadis and the Scavengers to align with him, and they plan to force the Saviors to surrender. However, when they arrive at the Sanctuary, Rick is horrified to see the breached walls and no sign of the walker herd.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep107" style="text-align:center">107</TH>
<TD>8</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"<A href="/wiki/How_It%27s_Gotta_Be" title="How It's Gotta Be">How It's Gotta Be</A>"</TD>
<TD>Michael E. Satrazemis</TD>
<TD>David Leslie Johnson & Angela Kang</TD>
<TD>December 10, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-12-10</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>7.89<SUP id="cite_ref-8.08_19-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8.08-19">[19]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #555752">Eugene's plan allows the Saviors to escape, and separately, the Saviors waylay the Alexandria, Hilltop, and Kingdom forces. The Scavengers abandon Rick, after which he returns to Alexandria. Ezekiel ensures that the Kingdom residents are able to escape before locking himself in the community with the Saviors. Eugene aids Gabriel and Doctor Carson in escaping the Sanctuary in order to ease his conscience. Negan attacks Alexandria, but Carl devises a plan to allow the Alexandria residents to escape into the sewers. Carl reveals he was bitten by a walker while escorting Siddiq to Alexandria.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep108" style="text-align:center">108</TH>
<TD>9</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"<A href="/wiki/Honor_(The_Walking_Dead)" title="Honor (The Walking Dead)">Honor</A>"</TD>
<TD>Greg Nicotero</TD>
<TD>Matthew Negrete & Channing Powell</TD>
<TD>February 25, 2018<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2018-02-25</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.28<SUP id="cite_ref-8.09_20-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8.09-20">[20]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #555752">After the Saviors leave Alexandria, the survivors make for the Hilltop while Rick and Michonne stay behind to say their final goodbyes to a dying Carl, who pleads with Rick to build a better future alongside the Saviors before killing himself. In the Kingdom, Morgan and Carol launch a rescue mission for Ezekiel. Although they are successful and retake the Kingdom, the Saviors' lieutenant Gavin is killed by Benjamin's vengeful brother Henry.</TD>
</TR>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Release">Release</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Walking_Dead_(season_8)&action=edit&section=15" title="Edit section: Release">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The first trailer for the season was released on July 21, 2017, at <A href="/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con" title="San Diego Comic-Con">San Diego Comic-Con</A>. The second trailer was released on February 1, 2018, for the second part of the season.<SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Reception">Reception</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Walking_Dead_(season_8)&action=edit&section=16" title="Edit section: Reception">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Critical_response">Critical response</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Walking_Dead_(season_8)&action=edit&section=17" title="Edit section: Critical response">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The eighth season of <I>The Walking Dead</I> has received mostly positive reviews from critics. On <A href="/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes" title="Rotten Tomatoes">Rotten Tomatoes</A>, the season holds a score of 73% with an <A href="/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean" title="Weighted arithmetic mean">average rating</A> of 6.9 out of 10, based on 13 reviews, and an average episode score of 69%. The site's critical consensus reads: "<I>The Walking Dead</I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</SPAN>s eighth season energizes its characters with some much-needed angst and action, though it's still occasionally choppy and lacking forward-moving plot progression."<SUP id="cite_ref-RT_S8_23-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-RT_S8-23">[23]</A></SUP></P>

<A href="/wiki/File:Laurel_wreath_fa13.gif" class="image"><IMG alt="Laurel wreath fa13.gif" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Laurel_wreath_fa13.gif/16px-Laurel_wreath_fa13.gif" width="16" height="14" class="noviewer" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Laurel_wreath_fa13.gif/24px-Laurel_wreath_fa13.gif 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Laurel_wreath_fa13.gif/32px-Laurel_wreath_fa13.gif 2x" data-file-width="74" data-file-height="65" /></A> <A href="/wiki/Portal:Hellenismos" title="Portal:Hellenismos">Hellenismos portal</A></TD></TR><TR><TD style="text-align:right;font-size:115%;padding-top: 0.6em;"><DIV class="plainlinks hlist navbar mini"><UL><LI class="nv-view"><A href="/wiki/Template:Ancient_Greek_religion" title="Template:Ancient Greek religion"><ABBR title="View this template">v</ABBR></A></LI><LI class="nv-talk"><A href="/wiki/Template_talk:Ancient_Greek_religion" title="Template talk:Ancient Greek religion"><ABBR title="Discuss this template">t</ABBR></A></LI><LI class="nv-edit"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:Ancient_Greek_religion&action=edit"><ABBR title="Edit this template">e</ABBR></A></LI></UL></DIV></TD></TR></TBODY></TABLE>
<P>In <A href="/wiki/Greek_mythology" title="Greek mythology">Greek mythology</A>, <B>Persephone</B> (<SPAN class="nowrap"><SPAN class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt"><A href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<SPAN style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><SPAN title="'p' in 'pie'">p</SPAN><SPAN title="/ər/: 'er' in 'letter'">ər</SPAN><SPAN title="/ˈ/: primary stress follows">ˈ</SPAN><SPAN title="'s' in 'sigh'">s</SPAN><SPAN title="/ɛ/: 'e' in 'dress'">ɛ</SPAN><SPAN title="'f' in 'find'">f</SPAN><SPAN title="/ə/: 'a' in 'about'">ə</SPAN><SPAN title="'n' in 'nigh'">n</SPAN><SPAN title="/i/: 'y' in 'happy'">i</SPAN></SPAN>/</A></SPAN></SPAN>; <A href="/wiki/Greek_language" title="Greek language">Greek</A>: <SPAN lang="el">Περσεφόνη</SPAN>), also called <B>Kore</B> (<SPAN class="nowrap"><SPAN class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt"><A href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<SPAN style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><SPAN title="/ˈ/: primary stress follows">ˈ</SPAN><SPAN title="'k' in 'kind'">k</SPAN><SPAN title="/ɔːr/: 'ar' in 'war'">ɔːr</SPAN><SPAN title="/iː/: 'ee' in 'fleece'">iː</SPAN></SPAN>/</A></SPAN></SPAN>; "the maiden"), is the daughter of <A href="/wiki/Zeus" title="Zeus">Zeus</A> and <A href="/wiki/Demeter" title="Demeter">Demeter</A> and is the queen of the <A href="/wiki/Greek_underworld" title="Greek underworld">underworld</A>. <A href="/wiki/Homer" title="Homer">Homer</A> describes her as the formidable, venerable majestic princess of the underworld, who carries into effect the curses of men upon the souls of the dead. Persephone was married to <A href="/wiki/Hades" title="Hades">Hades</A>, the god of the underworld.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson462_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson462-1">[1]</A></SUP> The myth of her abduction represents her function as the <A href="/wiki/Personification" class="mw-redirect" title="Personification">personification</A> of <A href="/wiki/Vegetation" title="Vegetation">vegetation</A>, which shoots forth in <A href="/wiki/Spring_(season)" title="Spring (season)">spring</A> and withdraws into the earth after harvest; hence, she is also associated with spring as well as the fertility of vegetation. Similar myths appear in the <A href="/wiki/Orient" title="Orient">Orient</A>, in the cults of male gods like <A href="/wiki/Attis" title="Attis">Attis</A>, <A href="/wiki/Adonis" title="Adonis">Adonis</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Osiris" title="Osiris">Osiris</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> and in <A href="/wiki/Minoan_civilization" title="Minoan civilization">Minoan</A> <A href="/wiki/Crete" title="Crete">Crete</A>.
</P><P>Persephone as a <A href="/wiki/Vegetation_deity" title="Vegetation deity">vegetation goddess</A> and her mother Demeter were the central figures of the <A href="/wiki/Eleusinian_mysteries" class="mw-redirect" title="Eleusinian mysteries">Eleusinian mysteries</A>, which promised the initiated a more enjoyable prospect after death. In some versions, Persephone is the mother of <A href="/wiki/Zeus" title="Zeus">Zeus</A>'s sons <A href="/wiki/Dionysus" title="Dionysus">Dionysus</A>, <A href="/wiki/Iacchus" title="Iacchus">Iacchus</A>, or <A href="/wiki/Zagreus" title="Zagreus">Zagreus</A>. The origins of her cult are uncertain, but it was based on very old agrarian cults of agricultural communities.
</P><P>Persephone was commonly worshipped along with Demeter and with the same mysteries. To her alone were dedicated the mysteries celebrated at Athens in the month of <A href="/wiki/Anthesterion" class="mw-redirect" title="Anthesterion">Anthesterion</A>. In <A href="/wiki/Art_in_ancient_Greece" class="mw-redirect" title="Art in ancient Greece">Classical Greek art</A>, Persephone is invariably portrayed robed, often carrying a <A href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/sheaf" class="extiw" title="wikt:sheaf">sheaf</A> of grain. She may appear as a mystical divinity with a sceptre and a little box, but she was mostly represented in the process of being carried off by <A href="/wiki/Hades_(mythology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Hades (mythology)">Hades</A>.
</P><P>In <A href="/wiki/Roman_mythology" title="Roman mythology">Roman mythology</A>, she is called <A href="/wiki/Proserpina" title="Proserpina">Proserpina</A>, and her mother, <A href="/wiki/Ceres_(Roman_mythology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ceres (Roman mythology)">Ceres</A> and her father <A href="/wiki/Jupiter(Mythology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Jupiter(Mythology)">Jupiter</A>.
</P>
