<UL><LI><UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Piraeus" title="Piraeus">Piraeus</A>: The <I>Skirophoria</I>, a festival related to the <A href="/wiki/Thesmophoria" title="Thesmophoria">Thesmophoria</A>.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Megara" title="Megara">Megara</A>: Cult of Demeter <I>thesmophoros</I> and Kore. The city was named after its <I>megara</I> .<SUP id="cite_ref-93" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-93">[88]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Aegina" title="Aegina">Aegina</A>: Cult of Demeter <I>thesmophoros</I> and Kore.</LI>
<LI><A href="/w/index.php?title=Phlya&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Phlya (page does not exist)">Phlya</A>, near Koropi, in the <A href="/wiki/Mystery_religions" class="mw-redirect" title="Mystery religions">mysteries</A> of Phlya: These have very old roots and were probably originally dedicated to Demeter <A href="/wiki/Pandora" title="Pandora">Anesidora</A>, Kore, and <A href="/wiki/Zeus" title="Zeus">Zeus</A> Ktesios, who was the god of the underground stored grain. Pausanias mentions a temple of Demeter-Anesidora, Kore <A href="/wiki/Greek_primordial_deities" title="Greek primordial deities">Protogone</A>, and Zeus Ktesios. The surname Protogonos, indicates a later <A href="/wiki/Orphic" class="mw-redirect" title="Orphic">Orphic</A> influence. It seems that the mysteries were related to the mysteries of <A href="/wiki/Andania" title="Andania">Andania</A> in <A href="/wiki/Messene" title="Messene">Messene</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson668_94-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson668-94">[89]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><B>Boeotia</B>:
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Ancient_Thebes_(Boeotia)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ancient Thebes (Boeotia)">Thebes</A>, which Zeus is said to have given to her as an acknowledgement for a favour she had bestowed upon him.<SUP id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-95">[90]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Pausanias_(geographer)" title="Pausanias (geographer)">Pausanias</A> records a grove of <A href="/wiki/Cabeiri" title="Cabeiri">Cabeirian</A> Demeter and the Maid, three miles outside the gates of Thebes, where a ritual was performed, so-called on the grounds that Demeter gave it to the <A href="/wiki/Cabeiri" title="Cabeiri">Cabeiri</A>, who established it at Thebes. The Thebans told Pausanias that some inhabitants of <A href="/wiki/Naupactus" class="mw-redirect" title="Naupactus">Naupactus</A> had performed the same rituals there, and had met with divine vengeance.<SUP id="cite_ref-96" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-96">[91]</A></SUP> The Cabeirian mysteries were introduced from <A href="/wiki/Asia_Minor" class="mw-redirect" title="Asia Minor">Asia Minor</A> at the end of the archaic period. Nothing is known of the older cult, and it seems that the Cabeiri were originally wine-<A href="/wiki/Daemon_(mythology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Daemon (mythology)">daemons</A>. Inscriptions from the temple in Thebes mention the old one as Cabir, and the new one as son (pais), who are different.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson668_94-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson668-94">[89]</A></SUP> According to Pausanias, Pelarge, the daughter of Potnieus, was connected with the cult of Demeter in the Cabeirian (<A href="/wiki/Potnia" title="Potnia">potniai</A>).<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson151_88-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson151-88">[83]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI>A feast in Boeotia, in the month <I>Demetrios</I> (<A href="/wiki/Attic_calendar" title="Attic calendar">Pyanepsion</A>), probably similar with the <A href="/wiki/Thesmophoria" title="Thesmophoria">Thesmophoria</A>.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Ancient_Thebes_(Boeotia)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ancient Thebes (Boeotia)">Thebes</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore in a feast named <A href="/wiki/Thesmophoria" title="Thesmophoria">Thesmophoria</A> but probably different. It was celebrated in the summer month <I>Bukatios</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Diodor_97-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Diodor-97">[92]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><B>Peloponnese</B> (except Arcadia)<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP>
<UL><LI><B>Hermione</B>: An old cult of Demeter <A href="/wiki/Chthonic" title="Chthonic">Chthonia</A>, Kore, and <I>Klymenos</I> (<A href="/wiki/Hades" title="Hades">Hades</A>). Cows were pushed into the temple, and then they were killed by four women. It is possible that Hermione was a mythical name, the place of the souls.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Asine" title="Asine">Asine</A>: Cult of Demeter <A href="/wiki/Chthonic" title="Chthonic">Chthonia</A>. The cult seems to be related to the original cult of Demeter in Hermione.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Lakonia" class="mw-redirect" title="Lakonia">Lakonia</A>: Temple of Demeter <I>Eleusinia</I> near <A href="/wiki/Taygetos" class="mw-redirect" title="Taygetos">Taygetos</A>. The feast was named <I>Eleuhinia</I>, and the name was given before the relation of Demeter with the cult of <A href="/wiki/Eleusis" title="Eleusis">Eleusis</A>.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Lakonia" class="mw-redirect" title="Lakonia">Lakonia</A> at Aigila: Dedicated to Demeter. Men were excluded.</LI>
<LI>near <A href="/wiki/Sparta" title="Sparta">Sparta</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore, the Demeters (Δαμάτερες, "Damaters"). According to Hesychius, the feast lasted three days (Thesmophoria).</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Corinth" title="Corinth">Corinth</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Pluton.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Triphylia" title="Triphylia">Triphylia</A> in <A href="/wiki/Elis" title="Elis">Elis</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Hades.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Pellene" title="Pellene">Pellene</A>: Dedicated to the <I>Mysian</I> Demeter. Men were excluded. The next day, men and women became naked.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Andania" title="Andania">Andania</A> in <A href="/wiki/Messenia" title="Messenia">Messenia</A> (near the borders of Arcadia): Cult of the Great goddesses, Demeter and <I>Hagne</I>. Hagne, a goddess of the spring, was the original deity before Demeter. The temple was built near a spring.</LI></UL></LI>
<LI><B>Arcadia</B><SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson478_26-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson478-26">[23]</A></SUP>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Pheneos" class="mw-redirect" title="Pheneos">Pheneos</A> : Mysteries of Demeter <I>Thesmia</I> and Demeter <I>Eleusinia</I>. The Eleusinian cult was introduced later. The priest took the <I>holy book</I> from a natural cleft. He used the mask of Demeter <I>Kidaria</I>, and he hit his stick on the earth, in a kind of agrarian magic. An Arcadian dance was named kidaris.</LI>
<LI><B>Pallantion</B> near <A href="/wiki/Tripoli,_Greece" title="Tripoli, Greece">Tripoli</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Karyai_(ancient_city)" class="mw-redirect" title="Karyai (ancient city)">Karyai</A>: Cult of Kore and Pluton.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Tegea" title="Tegea">Tegea</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore, the <I>Karpophoroi</I>, "Fruit givers".</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Megalopolis,_Greece" title="Megalopolis, Greece">Megalopolis</A>: Cult of the Great goddesses, Demeter and <I>Kore Sotira</I>, "the savior".</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Mantineia" title="Mantineia">Mantineia</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore in the fest <I>Koragia</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-98" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-98">[93]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Trapezus,_Arcadia" title="Trapezus, Arcadia">Trapezus</A>: Mysteries of the Great goddesses, Demeter and Kore. The temple was built near a spring, and a fire was burning out of the earth.</LI>
<LI>near <A href="/wiki/Thelpusa" title="Thelpusa">Thelpusa</A> in Onkeion: Temple of Demeter Erinys (vengeful) and Demeter Lusia (bathing). In the myth Demeter was united with <A href="/wiki/Poseidon" title="Poseidon">Poseidon Hippios</A> (horse) and bore the horse <A href="/wiki/Arion_(mythology)" title="Arion (mythology)">Arion</A> and the unnamed. The name <A href="/wiki/Despoina" title="Despoina">Despoina</A> was given in West Arcadia.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Phigalia" title="Phigalia">Phigalia</A>: Cult of the mare-headed Demeter (black), and <A href="/wiki/Despoina" title="Despoina">Despoina</A>. Demeter was depicted in her archaic form, a Medusa type with a horse's head with snaky hair, holding a dove and a dolphin.<SUP id="cite_ref-99" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-99">[94]</A></SUP> The temple was built near a spring.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Lycosura" title="Lycosura">Lycosura</A>,<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Despoina" title="Despoina">Despoina</A></DIV> Cult of Demeter and <A href="/wiki/Despoina" title="Despoina">Despoina</A>. In the portico of the temple of Despoina there was a tablet with the inscriptions of the mysteries. In front of the temple there was an altar to Demeter and another to Despoine, after which was one of the Great Mother. By the sides stood <A href="/wiki/Artemis" title="Artemis">Artemis</A> and <A href="/wiki/Anytos" title="Anytos">Anytos</A>, the Titan who brought up Despoine. Besides the temple, there was also a hall where the Arcadians celebrated the mysteries<SUP id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-100">[95]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-101">[96]</A></SUP> A fire was always burning in front of the temple of <A href="/wiki/Pan_(mythology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Pan (mythology)">Pan</A> (the goat-god), the god of the wild, shepherds and flocks. In a relief appear dancing animal-headed women (or with animal-masks) in a procession. Near the temple have been found terracotta figures with human bodies, and heads of animals.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson478_26-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson478-26">[23]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><B>Islands</B>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Paros" title="Paros">Paros</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Zeus-Eubuleus.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Amorgos" title="Amorgos">Amorgos</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Zeus-Eubuleus.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Delos" title="Delos">Delos</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Zeus-Eubuleus. Probably a different feast with the name <A href="/wiki/Thesmophoria" title="Thesmophoria">Thesmophoria</A>, celebrated in a summer month (the same month in Thebes). Two big loaves of bread were oferred to the two goddesses. Another feast was named <I>Megalartia</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Diodor_97-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Diodor-97">[92]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Mykonos" title="Mykonos">Mykonos</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and <A href="/wiki/Zeus" title="Zeus">Zeus</A>-Buleus.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Crete" title="Crete">Crete</A> : Cult of Demeter and Kore, in the month Thesmophorios.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Rhodes" title="Rhodes">Rhodes</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore, in the month Thesmophorios. The two goddesses are the Damaters in an inscription from <A href="/wiki/Lindos" title="Lindos">Lindos</A></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Asia_Minor" class="mw-redirect" title="Asia Minor">Asia Minor</A>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Knidos" title="Knidos">Knidos</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Pluton.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP> Agrarian magic similar to the one used in <A href="/wiki/Thesmophoria" title="Thesmophoria">Thesmophoria</A> and in the cult of the <A href="/wiki/Potnia" title="Potnia">potniai</A> (<A href="/wiki/Cabeiri" title="Cabeiri">Cabeirian</A>).<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Ephesos" class="mw-redirect" title="Ephesos">Ephesos</A> : Cult of Demeter and Kore, celebrated at night-time.<SUP id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-102">[97]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Priene" title="Priene">Priene</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore, similar to the Thesmophoria.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Sicily" title="Sicily">Sicily</A></LI></UL>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Head_of_Persephone._Earthenware._From_Sicily,_Centuripae,_c._420_BCE._The_Burrell_Collection,_Glasgow,_UK.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/Head_of_Persephone._Earthenware._From_Sicily%2C_Centuripae%2C_c._420_BCE._The_Burrell_Collection%2C_Glasgow%2C_UK.jpg/220px-Head_of_Persephone._Earthenware._From_Sicily%2C_Centuripae%2C_c._420_BCE._The_Burrell_Collection%2C_Glasgow%2C_UK.jpg" width="220" height="331" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/Head_of_Persephone._Earthenware._From_Sicily%2C_Centuripae%2C_c._420_BCE._The_Burrell_Collection%2C_Glasgow%2C_UK.jpg/330px-Head_of_Persephone._Earthenware._From_Sicily%2C_Centuripae%2C_c._420_BCE._The_Burrell_Collection%2C_Glasgow%2C_UK.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/Head_of_Persephone._Earthenware._From_Sicily%2C_Centuripae%2C_c._420_BCE._The_Burrell_Collection%2C_Glasgow%2C_UK.jpg/440px-Head_of_Persephone._Earthenware._From_Sicily%2C_Centuripae%2C_c._420_BCE._The_Burrell_Collection%2C_Glasgow%2C_UK.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2848" data-file-height="4288" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Head_of_Persephone._Earthenware._From_Sicily,_Centuripae,_c._420_BCE._The_Burrell_Collection,_Glasgow,_UK.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>Head of Persephone. <UL><LI><UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Syracuse,_Sicily" title="Syracuse, Sicily">Syracuse</A>: There was a harvest festival of Demeter and Persephone at Syracuse when the grain was ripe (about May).<SUP id="cite_ref-103" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-103">[98]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI>A fest <I>Koris katagogi</I>, the descent of Persephone into the underworld.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Magna_Graecia" title="Magna Graecia">Magna Graecia</A>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Epizephyrian_Locri" class="mw-redirect" title="Epizephyrian Locri">Epizephyrian Locri</A>: A temple associated with childbirth; its treasure was looted by <A href="/wiki/Pyrrhus_of_Epirus" title="Pyrrhus of Epirus">Pyrrhus</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-104" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-104">[99]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI>Archaeological finds suggest that worship of Demeter and Persephone was widespread in Sicily and Greek Italy.</LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Libya" title="Libya">Libya</A>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Cyrene,_Libya" title="Cyrene, Libya">Cyrene</A>: Temple of Demeter and Kore<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI></UL>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Ancient_literary_references">Ancient literary references</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Persephone&action=edit&section=19" title="Edit section: Ancient literary references">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Homer" title="Homer">Homer</A>:
<UL><LI><B>Iliad</B>:
<UL><LI>"the gods fulfilled his curse, even Zeus of the nether world and dread Persephone." (9, line 457; A. T. Murray, trans)</LI>
<LI>"<A href="/wiki/Althea" title="Althea">Althea</A> prayed instantly to the gods, being grieved for her brother's slaying; and furthermore instantly beat with her hands upon the all-nurturing earth, calling upon Hades and dread Persephone" (9, 569)</LI></UL></LI>
<LI><B>Odyssey</B>:
<UL><LI>"And come to the house of Hades and dread Persephone to seek sooth saying of the spirit of Theban Teiresias. To him even in death Persephone has granted reason that ..." (book 10, card 473)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Hymn" title="Hymn">Hymns to</A> <A href="/wiki/Demeter" title="Demeter">Demeter</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>
<UL><LI><B>Hymn 2</B>:
<UL><LI>"Mistress Demeter goddess of heaven, which God or mortal man has rapt away Persephone and pierced with sorrow your dear heart?<I>(hymn 2, card 40)</I></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><B>Hymn 13</B>:
<UL><LI>"I start to sing for Demeter the lovely-faced goddess, for her and her daughter the most beautiful Persephone. Hail goddess keep this city safe!" (hymn 13, card 1)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Pindar" title="Pindar">Pindar</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>

<UL><LI>"Now go Echo, to the dark-walled home of Persephone."(book O, poem 14)</LI></UL></LI>
<LI><B>Isthmean</B>:
<UL><LI>"Aecus showed them the way to the house of Persephone and nymphs, one of them carrying a ball."(book 1, poem 8)</LI></UL></LI>
<LI><B>Nemean</B>:
<UL><LI>"Island which Zeus, the lord of Olympus gave to Persephone;he nodded descent with his flowers hair."(book N, poem 1)</LI></UL></LI>
<LI><B>Pythian</B>:
<UL><LI>"You splendor-loving city, most beautiful on earth, home of Persephone. You who inhabit the hill of well-built dwellings."(book P, poem 12)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Aeschylus" title="Aeschylus">Aeschylus</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>
<UL><LI><B>Libation bearers</B>:
<UL><LI>Electra:"O Persephone, grant us indeed a glorious victory!" (card 479)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Aristophanes" title="Aristophanes">Aristophanes</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>
<UL><LI><B>Thesmophoriazusae</B>:
<UL><LI>Mnesilochos:"Thou Mistress Demeter, the most valuable friend and thou Persephone, grant that I may be able to offer you!" (card 266)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Euripides" title="Euripides">Euripides</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>
<UL><LI><B>Alcestis</B>:
<UL><LI>"O you brave and best hail, sitting as attendand Beside's Hades bride Persephone!" (card 741)</LI></UL></LI>
<LI><B>Hecuba</B>:
<UL><LI>"It is said that any of the dead that stand beside Persephone, that the Danaids have left the plains to Troy." (card 130)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Bacchylides" title="Bacchylides">Bacchylides</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>
<UL><LI><B> Epinicians</B>:
<UL><LI>"Flashing thunderbolt went down to the halls of slender-ankled Persephone to bring up into the light of Hades." (book Ep. poem 5)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Vergil" class="mw-redirect" title="Vergil">Vergil</A><SUP id="cite_ref-106" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-106">[101]</A></SUP>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Modern_reception">Modern reception</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Persephone&action=edit&section=20" title="Edit section: Modern reception">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Persephone_in_popular_culture" title="Persephone in popular culture">Persephone in popular culture</A></DIV>
<P>In 1934, <A href="/wiki/Igor_Stravinsky" title="Igor Stravinsky">Igor Stravinsky</A> based his <A href="/wiki/Melodrama" title="Melodrama">melodrama</A> <I><A href="/wiki/Pers%C3%A9phone_(Stravinsky)" title="Perséphone (Stravinsky)">Perséphone</A></I> on Persephone's story. In 1961, Frederick Ashton of the Royal Ballet appropriated Stravinsky's score, to choreograph a ballet starring Svetlana Beriosova as Persephone.
</P><P>Persephone also appears many times in popular culture. Featured in a variety of young adult novels such as "Persephone"<SUP id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-107">[102]</A></SUP> by Kaitlin Bevis, "Persephone's Orchard"<SUP id="cite_ref-108" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-108">[103]</A></SUP> by Molly Ringle, "The Goddess Test" by Aimee Carter, "The Goddess Letters" by Carol Orlock, and "Abandon" by Meg Cabot, her story has also been treated by Suzanne Banay Santo in "Persephone Under the Earth" in the light of women's spirituality. Here Santo treats the mythic elements in terms of maternal sacrifice to the burgeoning sexuality of an adolescent daughter. Accompanied by the classic, sensual paintings of Frederic Lord Leighton and William-Adolphe Bouguereau, Santo portrays Persephone not as a victim but as a woman in quest of sexual depth and power, transcending the role of daughter, though ultimately returning to it as an awakened Queen.<SUP id="cite_ref-109" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-109">[104]</A></SUP>
</P>

<H1 id="firstHeading" class="firstHeading" lang="en">Colony (biology)</H1>			<DIV id="bodyContent" class="mw-body-content">
				<DIV id="siteSub" class="noprint">From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia</DIV>				<DIV id="contentSub"></DIV>
								<DIV id="jump-to-nav" class="mw-jump">

				<DIV id="mw-content-text" lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr"><DIV class="mw-parser-output"><P>In <A href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</A>, a <B>colony</B> is composed of two or more <A href="/wiki/Conspecific" class="mw-redirect" title="Conspecific">conspecific</A> individuals living in close association with, or connected to, one another. This association is usually for mutual benefit such as stronger defense or the ability to attack bigger prey.<SUP id="cite_ref-Jackson1977_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Jackson1977-1">[1]</A></SUP> It is a cluster of identical cells (clones) on the surface of (or within) a solid medium, usually derived from a single parent cell, as in bacterial colony.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> In contrast, a <A href="/wiki/Solitary_animal" title="Solitary animal">solitary organism</A> is one in which all individuals live independently and have all of the functions needed to survive and reproduce.</P>
<P>Colonies, in the context of development, may be composed of two or more unitary (or solitary) organisms or be <A href="/wiki/Modular" class="mw-redirect" title="Modular">modular</A> organisms. <B>Unitary organisms</B> have determinate development (set life stages) from <A href="/wiki/Zygote" title="Zygote">zygote</A> to adult form and individuals or groups of individuals (colonies) are visually distinct. <B>Modular organisms</B> have indeterminate growth forms (life stages not set) through repeated iteration of genetically identical modules (or individuals), and it can be difficult to distinguish between the colony as a whole and the modules within.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP> In the latter case, modules may have specific functions within the colony.</P>
<P>Some organisms are primarily independent and form <A href="/wiki/Facultative" title="Facultative">facultative</A> colonies in reply to environmental conditions while others must live in a colony to survive (<A href="/wiki/Obligate" title="Obligate">obligate</A>). For example, some <A href="/wiki/Carpenter_bee" title="Carpenter bee">carpenter bees</A> will form colonies when a dominant hierarchy is formed between two or more nest foundresses<SUP id="cite_ref-DunnRichards2003_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-DunnRichards2003-4">[4]</A></SUP> (facultative colony), while <A href="/wiki/Coral" title="Coral">corals</A> are animals that are physically connected by living tissue (the <A href="/wiki/Coenosarc" title="Coenosarc">coenosarc</A>) that contains a shared <A href="/wiki/Gastrovascular_cavity" title="Gastrovascular cavity">gastrovascular cavity</A>.</P>
<P></P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Social_colonies">Social colonies</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Colony_(biology)&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Social colonies">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg/220px-Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg/330px-Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg/440px-Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1248" data-file-height="830" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
A breeding colony of <A href="/wiki/Northern_gannet" title="Northern gannet">Northern gannets</A> on the <A href="/wiki/Heligoland" title="Heligoland">Heligoland</A> archipelago in the <A href="/wiki/North_Sea" title="North Sea">North Sea</A>.</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P><A href="/wiki/Unicellular" class="mw-redirect" title="Unicellular">Unicellular</A> and <A href="/wiki/Multicellular" class="mw-redirect" title="Multicellular">multicellular</A> unitary organisms may aggregate to form colonies. For example,</P>
<UL>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Protist" title="Protist">Protists</A> such as <A href="/wiki/Slime_mold" title="Slime mold">slime molds</A> are many unicellular organisms that aggregate to form colonies when food resources are hard to come by, as together they are more reactive to chemical cues released by preferred prey.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Eusociality" title="Eusociality">Eusocial</A> insects like <A href="/wiki/Ant" title="Ant">ants</A> and <A href="/wiki/Honey_bee" title="Honey bee">honey bees</A> are multicellular animals that live in colonies with a highly organized social structure. Colonies of some social insects may be deemed <A href="/wiki/Superorganism" title="Superorganism">superorganisms</A>.</LI>
<LI>Animals such as <A href="/wiki/Human" title="Human">humans</A> and <A href="/wiki/Rodent" title="Rodent">rodents</A> form breeding or <A href="/wiki/Bird_colony" title="Bird colony">nesting colonies</A>, potentially for more successful mating and to better protect offspring.
<UL>
<LI>The <A href="/wiki/Bracken_Cave" title="Bracken Cave">Bracken Cave</A> is the summer home to a colony of around 20 million <A href="/wiki/Mexican_free-tailed_bat" title="Mexican free-tailed bat">Mexican free-tailed bats</A> making it the largest known concentration of mammals.<SUP id="cite_ref-natgeo_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-natgeo-5">[5]</A></SUP></LI>
</UL>
</LI>
</UL>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Modular_organisms">Modular organisms</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Colony_(biology)&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Modular organisms">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Modular organisms are those in which a genet (or genetic individual formed from a <A href="/wiki/Sexual_reproduction" title="Sexual reproduction">sexually-produced</A> <A href="/wiki/Zygote" title="Zygote">zygote</A>) asexually reproduces to form genetically identical clones called <A href="/wiki/Ramet" class="mw-redirect" title="Ramet">ramets</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Winston2010_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Winston2010-6">[6]</A></SUP></P>
<P>A <B><A href="/wiki/Clonal_colony" title="Clonal colony">clonal colony</A></B> is when the ramets of a genet live in close proximity or are physically connected. Ramets may have all of the functions needed to survive on their own or be interdependent on other ramets. For example, some <A href="/wiki/Sea_anemone" title="Sea anemone">sea anemones</A> go through the process of pedal laceration in which a genetically identical individual is asexually produced from tissue broken off from the anemone's pedal disc. In plants, clonal colonies are created through the propagation of genetically identical trees by <A href="/wiki/Stolon" title="Stolon">stolons</A> or <A href="/wiki/Rhizome" title="Rhizome">rhizomes</A>.</P>
<P><B>Colonial organisms</B> are <A href="/wiki/Clonal_colonies" class="mw-redirect" title="Clonal colonies">clonal colonies</A> composed of many physically connected, interdependent individuals. Colonial organisms can be unicellular, as in the alga <I><A href="/wiki/Volvox" title="Volvox">Volvox</A></I> (a <A href="/wiki/Coenobium_(morphology)" title="Coenobium (morphology)">coenobium</A>), or <A href="/wiki/Multicellular_organism" title="Multicellular organism">multicellular</A>, as in the <A href="/wiki/Phylum" title="Phylum">phylum</A> <A href="/wiki/Bryozoa" title="Bryozoa">Bryozoa</A>. The former type may have been the first step toward multicellular <A href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organisms</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> Individuals within a multicellular colonial organism may be called <A href="/wiki/Ramet" class="mw-redirect" title="Ramet">ramets</A>, <A href="/wiki/Modularity_(biology)" title="Modularity (biology)">modules</A>, or <A href="/wiki/Zooid" title="Zooid">zooids</A>. Structural and functional variation (<A href="/wiki/Polymorphism_(biology)" title="Polymorphism (biology)">polymorphism</A>), when present, designates ramet responsibilities such as feeding, reproduction, and defense. To that end, being physically connected allows the colonial organism to distribute nutrients and energy obtained by feeding zooids throughout the colony. An example of colonial organisms that is well known are hydrozoans, like Portuguese man o' wars.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Microbial_colonies">Microbial colonies</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Colony_(biology)&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Microbial colonies">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>A <B>microbial colony</B> is defined as a visible cluster of <A href="/wiki/Microorganism" title="Microorganism">microorganisms</A> growing on the surface of or within a solid medium, presumably cultured from a single cell.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> Because the colony is <A href="/wiki/Clone_(cell_biology)" title="Clone (cell biology)">clonal</A>, with all organisms in it descending from a single ancestor (assuming no <A href="/wiki/Contamination" title="Contamination">contamination</A>), they are genetically identical, except for any <A href="/wiki/Mutation" title="Mutation">mutations</A> (which occur at low frequencies). Obtaining such genetically identical organisms (or pure <A href="/wiki/Strain_(biology)" title="Strain (biology)">strains</A>) can be useful; this is done by spreading organisms on a culture plate and starting a new stock from a single resulting colony.</P>
<P>A <B><A href="/wiki/Biofilm" title="Biofilm">biofilm</A></B> is a colony of <A href="/wiki/Microorganism" title="Microorganism">microorganisms</A> often comprising several species, with properties and capabilities greater than the aggregate of capabilities of the individual organisms.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Life_history">Life history</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Colony_(biology)&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Life history">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Individuals in social colonies and modular organisms receive benefit to such a lifestyle. For example, it may be easier to seek out food, defend a nesting site, or increase competitive ability against other species. Modular organisms' ability to reproduce asexually in addition to sexually allows them unique benefits that social colonies do not have.<SUP id="cite_ref-Winston2010_6-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Winston2010-6">[6]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The energy required for sexual reproduction varies based on the frequency and length of reproductive activity, number and size of offspring, and parental care.<SUP id="cite_ref-KunzOrrell_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-KunzOrrell-10">[10]</A></SUP> While solitary individuals bear all of those energy costs, individuals in some social colonies share a portion of those costs.</P>
<P>Modular organisms save energy by using asexual reproduction during their life. Energy reserved in this way allows them to put more energy towards colony growth, regenerating lost modules (due to predation or other cause of death), or response to environmental conditions.</P>

<P><I><B>The Man in the High Castle</B></I> is an American <A href="/wiki/Dystopia" title="Dystopia">dystopian</A> <A href="/wiki/Uchronia" title="Uchronia">alternative history</A> <A href="/wiki/Television" title="Television">television</A> series produced by <A href="/wiki/Amazon_Studios" title="Amazon Studios">Amazon Studios</A>, <A href="/wiki/Scott_Free_Productions" title="Scott Free Productions">Scott Free Productions</A>, <A href="/wiki/Headline_Pictures" title="Headline Pictures">Headline Pictures</A>, <A href="/wiki/Electric_Shepherd_Productions" class="mw-redirect" title="Electric Shepherd Productions">Electric Shepherd Productions</A> and <A href="/wiki/Big_Light_Productions" class="mw-redirect" title="Big Light Productions">Big Light Productions</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Variety_review_2015-11-18_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Variety_review_2015-11-18-1">[1]</A></SUP> The series is loosely based on the 1962 <A href="/wiki/The_Man_in_the_High_Castle" title="The Man in the High Castle">novel of the same name</A> by <A href="/wiki/Science_fiction" title="Science fiction">science fiction</A> author <A href="/wiki/Philip_K._Dick" title="Philip K. Dick">Philip K. Dick</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> In the series' <A href="/wiki/Alternate_history" title="Alternate history">alternate version</A> of 1962 America, <A href="/wiki/Hypothetical_Axis_victory_in_World_War_II" title="Hypothetical Axis victory in World War II">the Axis powers have won World War II</A> and divided the United States into two <A href="/wiki/Puppet_state" title="Puppet state">puppet states</A>: the Greater Nazi Reich and the Japanese Pacific States. The series follows characters whose destinies intertwine after coming into contact with a series of propaganda films that show a vastly different history from that of their own.</P>
<P>Premiering in January 2015, the pilot was Amazon's "most-watched since the original series development program began."<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP> The next month Amazon ordered episodes to fill out a ten-episode season,<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP> which was released in November, to positive reviews.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> A second season of ten episodes premiered in December 2016,<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> with a third season announced a few weeks later to be released in 2018.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP></P>
<P></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Synopsis">Synopsis</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Synopsis">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Season_one">Season one</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Season one">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The central characters are Juliana Crain, Frank Frink, Joe Blake, John Smith, Nobusuke Tagomi, and Takeshi Kido. The series takes place in an alternate 1962.</P>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_(Ridley_Scott%27s_series).svg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_%28Ridley_Scott%27s_series%29.svg/220px-The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_%28Ridley_Scott%27s_series%29.svg.png" width="220" height="116" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_%28Ridley_Scott%27s_series%29.svg/330px-The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_%28Ridley_Scott%27s_series%29.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_%28Ridley_Scott%27s_series%29.svg/440px-The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_%28Ridley_Scott%27s_series%29.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1235" data-file-height="650" /></A>

<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_(Ridley_Scott%27s_series).svg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
Flag of the Greater Nazi Reich in America</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:JPS_flag.svg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/JPS_flag.svg/220px-JPS_flag.svg.png" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/JPS_flag.svg/330px-JPS_flag.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/JPS_flag.svg/440px-JPS_flag.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="900" data-file-height="600" /></A>

Flag of the Japanese Pacific States</DIV>

<P>Juliana Crain is a <A href="/wiki/San_Francisco" title="San Francisco">San Francisco</A> woman who becomes entangled with the resistance when her half-sister Trudy is killed by the <SPAN lang="ja-Latn"><I><A href="/wiki/Kempeitai" class="mw-redirect" title="Kempeitai">Kempeitai</A></I></SPAN>, just after giving Juliana a film reel that contains newsreel-style footage depicting an alternate history in which the <A href="/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II" title="Allies of World War II">Allies</A> won <A href="/wiki/World_War_II" title="World War II">World War II</A> and Germany and Japan were defeated. The film is entitled <I>The Grasshopper Lies Heavy</I>, and is part of a series of similar newsreels being collected by someone referred to as "The Man in the High Castle". Juliana believes the newsreel reflects some sort of alternate reality and that it is part of some kind of larger truth about how the world should be. Her boyfriend, Frank Frink (who keeps his <A href="/wiki/Jews" title="Jews">Jewish</A> roots hidden in order to avoid extradition and death at the hands of the <A href="/wiki/Nazism" title="Nazism">Nazis</A>), believes that the newsreel has no relation to real-life events. Juliana learns Trudy was carrying the film to <A href="/wiki/Ca%C3%B1on_City,_Colorado" title="Cañon City, Colorado">Canon City</A>, <A href="/wiki/Colorado" title="Colorado">Colorado</A>, in the <A href="/wiki/Neutral_zone_(territorial_entity)" title="Neutral zone (territorial entity)">Neutral Zone</A>, where she was going to meet someone. Juliana decides to travel there in Trudy's place to find out what her half-sister's mission was. When she arrives in Canon City, she encounters Joe Blake.</P>
<P>Blake is a 27-year-old <A href="/wiki/New_York_City" title="New York City">New Yorker</A> who is a <A href="/wiki/Double_agent" title="Double agent">double agent</A> working for the Nazis under <SPAN lang="de"><A href="/wiki/Obergruppenf%C3%BChrer" title="Obergruppenführer">Obergruppenführer</A></SPAN> John Smith, a former <A href="/wiki/United_States_Army" title="United States Army">US Army</A> officer who joined the Nazis and rose through the ranks to become a senior officer in the <A href="/wiki/SS" class="mw-redirect" title="SS">SS</A>. Blake is pretending to be a member of the resistance while he searches for the resistance contact in Canon City, which is Juliana, substituting for Trudy.</P>
<P>Nobusuke Tagomi is a high-ranking Japanese official (the Trade Minister) in <A href="/wiki/San_Francisco" title="San Francisco">San Francisco</A>. He meets in secret with Nazi official Rudolph Wegener, who is traveling incognito as <A href="/wiki/Sweden" title="Sweden">Swedish</A> businessman Victore Baynes. Tagomi and Wegener are concerned about the power vacuum that will exist when the Reich's Führer <A href="/wiki/Adolf_Hitler" title="Adolf Hitler">Adolf Hitler</A> dies, or is forced to step down due to his worsening <A href="/wiki/Parkinson%27s_disease" title="Parkinson's disease">Parkinson's disease</A>. Wegener explains that Hitler's successor will want to use the Reich's nuclear bombs against Japan to gain control of the rest of the former United States. Currently, however, Japan and the Third Reich are engaged in a <A href="/wiki/Cold_war_(general_term)" title="Cold war (general term)">cold war</A> full of tension but no open warfare, with the Japanese lagging behind the Germans technologically.</P>
<P>Frank Frink ends up being arrested when the Japanese and the Nazis become suspicious of Juliana's activities. Not having the information they seek, he is unable to give the Japanese what they are looking for, and they kill Frink's sister and her two children in retaliation, using their Jewish heritage as an excuse for their executions. This leads Frink to plan to kill the visiting Japanese Crown Prince and Princess, but he ultimately decides against going through with his plan.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Season_two">Season two</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Season two">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Season Two of the show broadly encompasses Frank Frink deciding to forgo his hesitancy and relative pacifism and choosing to become a committed member of the American Resistance to the Japanese Empire inside the Pacific States, eventually participating in a successful terrorist bombing of a central-command building of the Pacific States government in downtown San Francisco. The attack kills many members of the Japanese military and other top-level leadership.</P>
<P>Juliana Crain claims asylum in the Nazi Reich using their San Francisco Embassy so she can escape Japanese soldiers who hold her responsible for at least one murder. John Smith, seeing that her asylum claim is unlikely to succeed, steps in to the interrogation room and assumes command of her claim himself, ensuring it goes through, and he takes her to New York without Joe Blake's knowledge. Joe Blake himself discovers he was a product of the <A href="/wiki/Lebensborn" title="Lebensborn">Lebensborn</A> programme, and also that he is the sole biological son of a top-ranking Nazi official in Berlin, Martin Heusmann. Eventually Blake reconciles with Heusmann on the personal level and, in so doing, becomes second-in-command of the Chancellorship after Adolf Hitler dies and the Nazi leadership in Berlin grants Heusmann the Reich's Acting Chancellor title, which they do quickly and almost by default.</P>
<P>Hitler's death is abruptly pinned upon Japanese spies, and Heusmann suddenly announces on television that the Japanese agents whom he claims assassinated the Führer will be brought to justice by any means necessary, including war. John Smith is the only high-ranking Nazi official to be suspicious of the nature of Heusmann's sudden announcement. To gain insight in to why it has happened, he interrogates another high-ranking Nazi, <A href="/wiki/Reinhard_Heydrich" title="Reinhard Heydrich">Reinhard Heydrich</A>, who reveals a far-reaching conspiracy led by Heusmann designed to result in a Nazi nuclear onslaught against the Japanese Empire that will kill tens of millions of Japanese, decimate their Empire, level <A href="/wiki/Tokyo" title="Tokyo">Tokyo</A>, kill their Emperor, and force the surviving Japanese to permanently absorb themselves in to a global Nazi Reich. John Smith undertakes carefully-calculated stealth actions to disrupt and dismantle the Heusmann conspiracy and, as a final act, travels to Berlin and informs <A href="/wiki/Heinrich_Himmler" title="Heinrich Himmler">Heinrich Himmler</A> — the Nazi <A href="/wiki/Reichsf%C3%BChrer-SS" title="Reichsführer-SS">Reichsführer</A> and not involved in the conspiracy — of the existence of the conspiracy. Audiotapes, together with physical and written evidence reaching too deep within the existing Reich's power structure to be dismissed as hearsay, are handed personally by John Smith over to the Reichsführer, who then angrily leads Smith and several of his closest Berlin subordinates in to the late Führer's office occupied by the Acting Chancellor. He arrests Heusmann for high treason and the murder of Adolf Hitler, detains Joe Blake along with Heusmann, and then addresses the <A href="/wiki/Volkshalle" title="Volkshalle">Volkshalle</A> packed with hundreds of thousands of Reich civilians and uniformed stormtroopers, nixing the war-declaration speech meant to have been delivered by Heusmann and instead informing the Reich of Heusmann's conspiracy and John Smith's exposing of it. Upon learning this, the entire Volkshalle erupts in to a celebratory mood marked by repeated mass Nazi salutes of Himmler's men in general and then John Smith in particular.</P>
<P>The second season ends with Himmler and John Smith implicitly assuming command of the Reich, and an implied new era of peace and tranquility between the Japanese Empire and the Greater Nazi Reich. Juliana Crain continues to live out her asylum claim inside New York Nazi territory, and the final few minutes of the final episode of the second season show Trudy (or an alternate-universe version of her) alive and well. In a basement somewhere, John Smith is given access to a room filled to bursting with reels of films watched by the late Führer.</P>

He is a natural-born American who previously served in the <A href="/wiki/Signal_Corps_(United_States_Army)" title="Signal Corps (United States Army)">U.S. Army Signal Corps</A> and lives a comfortable suburban life with a wife and three children. <TH scope="row" id="ep4" style="text-align:center">4</TH>
<TD>4</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Revelations"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Michael_Rymer" title="Michael Rymer">Michael Rymer</A></TD>
<TD>Thomas Schnauz and <A href="/wiki/Jace_Richdale" title="Jace Richdale">Jace Richdale</A></TD>
<TD>November 20, 2015<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2015-11-20</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #A12300">Joe quickly saves Juliana from the Marshal. Joe and Juliana confront Lemuel who leads them into the woods, where they are surrounded by resistance fighters, who force them to give them the films and leave. Joe and Juliana are attacked again by the Marshal, causing Joe to reveal to the Marshal that he is a Nazi agent. The Marshal pursues Juliana on the highway. When Juliana gets far enough, she burns her car and hides. When the Marshal reaches the car, he assumes that she has died. Back in the Reich, <A href="/wiki/SS" class="mw-redirect" title="SS">SS</A> Captain Connolly is suspected by Smith for telling the resistance members who attacked him, which route he was taking to work. In the Pacific States, Frank heads to the Crown Prince's speech with a gun to assassinate him, but hesitates to do so. The Crown Prince is then shot by an unseen gunman.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep5" style="text-align:center">5</TH>
<TD>5</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"The New Normal"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Bryan_Spicer" title="Bryan Spicer">Bryan Spicer</A></TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Rob_Williams_(filmmaker)" title="Rob Williams (filmmaker)">Rob Williams</A></TD>
<TD>November 20, 2015<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2015-11-20</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #A12300">The Crown Prince is rushed to the hospital after the attack, and the captain of the <A href="/wiki/Imperial_Guard_(Japan)" title="Imperial Guard (Japan)">Imperial Guard</A> is ordered to commit <A href="/wiki/Seppuku" title="Seppuku">seppuku</A>, for not protecting the Crown Prince. Kido then states that if he cannot find the gunman, he will do the same. Meanwhile, Juliana returns home to find an angry Frank, who alludes to his time in prison. Juliana visits her parents and learns the Japanese killed Frank's sister and children. When she later reports to the Japanese military, she is interrogated and asked about Trudy's partner Randall but is ultimately let go. She then visits Simone and meets an agent of the resistance who gives her a visitor's card to the government building. Joe returns to New York from the Neutral Zone and is kidnapped by <A href="/wiki/Gestapo" title="Gestapo">Gestapo</A> agents and brought to Smith's office. He is then forced to tell Smith what happened in Canon City. Smith tells Joe he has failed in his mission because the leader of the resistance escaped. Smith believes Joe is being truthful and invites him over for VA day (Victory in America day).</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep6" style="text-align:center">6</TH>
<TD>6</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Three Monkeys"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Nelson_McCormick_(director)" title="Nelson McCormick (director)">Nelson McCormick</A></TD>
<TD>Rob Williams</TD>
<TD>November 20, 2015<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2015-11-20</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #A12300">Joe celebrates VA day at Smith's house. Juliana accepts a job working for Tagomi as she continues her search for answers. Smith, who has received intelligence about Wegener's activities but also happens to be an old friend, intercepts him at the airport and invites him for dinner hoping to probe Wegener for answers. Smith has Wegener arrested. Smith catches Joe sneaking through his files.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep7" style="text-align:center">7</TH>
<TD>7</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Truth"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Brad_Anderson_(director)" title="Brad Anderson (director)">Brad Anderson</A></TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Emma_Frost_(screenwriter)" title="Emma Frost (screenwriter)">Emma Frost</A></TD>
<TD>November 20, 2015<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2015-11-20</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #A12300">Juliana makes a startling discovery about her sister's death. Frank reflects on recent events and makes an important decision about his future, and Tagomi gains greater insight into Juliana's past. Smith catches Joe in his home office and interrogates him about Juliana and <A href="/wiki/Canon_City" class="mw-redirect" title="Canon City">Canon City</A>.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep8" style="text-align:center">8</TH>
<TD>8</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"End of the World"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Karyn_Kusama" title="Karyn Kusama">Karyn Kusama</A></TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Walon_Green" title="Walon Green">Walon Green</A></TD>
<TD>November 20, 2015<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2015-11-20</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #A12300">Juliana and Frank make plans to escape the Pacific States, only to be dragged back into danger by Joe as he tries to retrieve a new film, and walks directly into the <A href="/wiki/Kempeitai" class="mw-redirect" title="Kempeitai">Kempeitai</A>'s ambush. Meanwhile, Smith's loyalty is put to the ultimate test when confronted with a startling family discovery. The episode is named after the <A href="/wiki/The_End_of_the_World_(Skeeter_Davis_song)" title="The End of the World (Skeeter Davis song)">song of the same name</A>, which is performed by <A href="/wiki/Lini_Evans" title="Lini Evans">Lini Evans</A> during the episode with Japanese lyrics she co-wrote.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep9" style="text-align:center">9</TH>
<TD>9</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Kindness"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Michael_Slovis" title="Michael Slovis">Michael Slovis</A></TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Jace_Richdale" title="Jace Richdale">Jace Richdale</A></TD>
<TD>November 20, 2015<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2015-11-20</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #A12300">With time running out, a desperate Frank is forced to put his life on the line to help Joe. The pieces finally fall into place for Smith as he uncovers who was behind the assassination attempt. Tagomi is devastated when he is confronted with the consequences of his scheming, and Kido's investigation takes a dramatic turn when he makes an important discovery. Meanwhile, Frank and Juliana, after taking possession of the new film, decide to watch it, but they are shocked to find out that the film describes, apparently in the near future, a nuclear-bombed San Francisco where the SS are rounding up and executing survivors; Frank is shown being executed by Joe, who is wearing an SS uniform.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep10" style="text-align:center">10</TH>
<TD>10</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"A Way Out"</TD>
<TD>Daniel Percival</TD>
<TD>Rob Williams</TD>
<TD>November 20, 2015<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2015-11-20</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #A12300">Frank and Juliana angrily confront Joe as a Nazi agent. He goes to the Nazi embassy with the film. Joe learns that Heydrich is preparing a trap. Kido acts on the information from the <SPAN lang="ja-Latn"><I>Yakuza</I></SPAN> and kills the Nazi sniper that shot the Crown Prince. Ed is caught with Frank's gun and is used as a scapegoat for the attempted assassination of the Crown Prince, averting the need for Kido to commit <SPAN lang="ja-Latn"><I><A href="/wiki/Seppuku" title="Seppuku">seppuku</A></I></SPAN>. Heydrich demands Smith's loyalty ahead of Wegener assassinating Hitler. Wegener says goodbye to his family and travels to Hitler's alpine castle (filmed at <A href="/wiki/Hohenwerfen_Castle" title="Hohenwerfen Castle">Hohenwerfen Castle</A>), but after confronting Hitler (who is watching the alternate newsreels in his huge film vault saying that he learns something every time he watches), kills himself instead. Smith captures the traitor Heydrich and reports such to Hitler. Joe evades Lem's ambush and boards a boat to Mexico in Juliana's place. Frank finds out that Ed has been arrested and returns to the <SPAN lang="ja-Latn"><I>Kempeitai</I></SPAN> headquarters to find him being detained. Tagomi goes to <A href="/wiki/Union_Square,_San_Francisco" title="Union Square, San Francisco">Union Square</A> to meditate with Juliana's charm and opens his eyes to find himself in an alternate 1962 where the Allies won World War II and America is in the midst of the <A href="/wiki/Cuban_Missile_Crisis" title="Cuban Missile Crisis">Cuban Missile Crisis</A>.</TD>
</TR>
</TBODY></TABLE>
<H3><SPAN id="Season_2_.282016.29"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Season_2_(2016)">Season 2 (2016)</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section: Season 2 (2016)">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The second season was released on December 16, 2016.<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP></P>
<TABLE class="wikitable plainrowheaders wikiepisodetable" style="width:100%">
<TBODY><TR style="color:white;text-align:center">
<TH scope="col" style="background:#424E5C;width:5%"><ABBR title="Number">No.</ABBR><BR />
overall</TH>
<TH scope="col" style="background:#424E5C;width:5%"><ABBR title="Number">No.</ABBR> in<BR />
season</TH>
<TH scope="col" style="background:#424E5C;width:25%">Title</TH>
<TH scope="col" style="background:#424E5C;width:18%">Directed by</TH>
<TH scope="col" style="background:#424E5C;width:24%">Written by</TH>
<TH scope="col" style="background:#424E5C;width:23%">Original release date</TH>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep11" style="text-align:center">11</TH>
<TD>1</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"The Tiger's Cave"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Daniel_Percival_(director)" title="Daniel Percival (director)">Daniel Percival</A></TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Frank_Spotnitz" title="Frank Spotnitz">Frank Spotnitz</A></TD>
<TD>December 16, 2016<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2016-12-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #424E5C">Joe returns to New York to hand over the film to Smith and request for his resignation, but Smith denies his request before delivering the film to Hitler. Karen and Lem confront Juliana for not shooting Joe before she is tranquilized. She wakes up in the home of Hawthorne Abendsen, The Man in the High Castle, and his vast film collection. Meanwhile, General Onoda reveals to Tagomi and his staff that the capsule Science Minister Shimada found in his pocket contains the plans for a nuclear weapon that the Empire intends to use to crush the Nazis, much to Tagomi's dismay. Frank confronts Arnold about spying over his own family. Desperate to clear Ed's name, Frank goes to Childan and asks for his help. Juliana attempts to get answers from an evasive Abendsen and receives a clue which may help to avert nuclear war. Gary Connell, leader of the West Coast Resistance, goes against orders and tries to kill Juliana, but she escapes at a Kempeitai checkpoint. A gunfight ensues between the Resistance members and the Japanese soldiers. Karen is killed in the crossfire.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep12" style="text-align:center">12</TH>
<TD>2</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"The Road Less Traveled"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Colin_Bucksey" title="Colin Bucksey">Colin Bucksey</A></TD>
<TD>Rob Williams</TD>
<TD>December 16, 2016<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2016-12-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #424E5C">Kido investigates the shootout at the checkpoint and suspects Juliana is involved. Frank decides to get Paul Kasoura, who is a defense lawyer, to help Ed. In desperation, he reveals to Kasoura that the antique goods he and Childan sold him are fake, leading the pair to be imprisoned by the Yakuza, to whom Kasoura has a connection. Frank is almost killed by Okamura, the Yakuza leader, in the previous incident with Joe. However, he manages to convince Okamura to allow him to repay his debt for the forgery, with a condition that Ed is to work with him as his assistant. Kido is forced by Okamura to release Ed. He later pins the assassination of the Crown Prince on the deceased Karen. Joe is ordered by Smith to visit his father, a Reichminister named Heusmann, in Berlin. Smith tells Joe that Juliana is possibly dead. Meanwhile, Juliana evades Gary and Lem and tries to convince her parents to leave San Francisco, to no avail. Using the clue on a mysterious man that Abendsen is fixated on, Juliana discovers the man is a family friend named George Dixon, who is Trudy's real father. Learning he may be in Brooklyn, Juliana risks her life to reach the Nazi embassy and request asylum, while leaving a letter to Frank.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep13" style="text-align:center">13</TH>
<TD>3</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Travelers"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Daniel_Sackheim" title="Daniel Sackheim">Daniel Sackheim</A></TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Erik_Oleson" title="Erik Oleson">Erik Oleson</A></TD>
<TD>December 16, 2016<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2016-12-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #424E5C">Smith is warned by Dr. Adler, the family physician, to end his son Thomas's life, as the boy's incurable illness prevents him from being accepted in the Reich. Juliana makes it to New York and is questioned by Smith, who is notified of her arrival and arranges her stay. He keeps this a secret from Joe. Frank learns of Juliana's defection to the Nazi states, though he does not believe Gary on her betrayal. While he works with Ed and Childan to create forgeries for the Yakuza to repay his debt, Frank is convinced by the Resistance to help them liberate innocent citizens from the Kempeitai in retaliation for the checkpoint murders. While saving a Resistance member named Sarah, Frank commits his first kill against the Japanese. Juliana looks for Joe but is told by his ex-lover that he has rejoined the Nazis, leading her to think he may have betrayed her. Joe travels to Berlin and meets with his father but is distant due to the latter's treatment of his mother. He crosses paths with Nicole Becker, a filmmaker. Smith is unable to kill his son when given the chance to do so. He meets with Dr. Adler and kills him to ensure his silence.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep14" style="text-align:center">14</TH>
<TD>4</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Escalation"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/David_Petrarca" title="David Petrarca">David Petrarca</A></TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Wesley_Strick" title="Wesley Strick">Wesley Strick</A></TD>
<TD>December 16, 2016<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2016-12-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #424E5C">Juliana adjusts to life in the Reich under the tutelage of Smith's wife Helen and Thomas. While looking for George Dixon at his old apartment, she is pursued by two unknown agents and almost killed. General Onoda has the Kempeitai execute numerous citizens for the murder of the Japanese soldiers during the Resistance rescue. Enraged, Frank starts to neglect his debt with the Yakuza and accepts a risky assignment to siphon materials from an unexploded Japanese bomb for a Resistance mission, much to Ed's dismay. Frank begins to get close with Sarah during the assignment. Smith reveals to a suspecting Helen that he killed Dr. Adler to keep their son's illness a secret. Kido gets Onoda drunk and tricks him into approving an unknown order. After escaping from her pursuers, Juliana is approached by Dixon. Tagomi travels to the alternate timeline once again and sees his still-living wife Michiko, who is deceased in his own timeline.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep15" style="text-align:center">15</TH>
<TD>5</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Duck and Cover"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/John_Fawcett_(director)" title="John Fawcett (director)">John Fawcett</A></TD>
<TD>Erik Oleson & <A href="/wiki/Rick_Cleveland" title="Rick Cleveland">Rick Cleveland</A></TD>
<TD>December 16, 2016<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2016-12-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #424E5C">Dixon is revealed to be a Resistance leader and meets up with Juliana after she tells him that the Man in the High Castle sent her. Juliana tells him he may be somehow involved in the possible San Francisco bombing as he has appeared several times in the films. Dixon forces Juliana to spy on Smith and his family to redeem her betrayal when she allowed Joe to escape with the film. Joe is upset when his father brings him to his place of birth and reveals he is one of the <A href="/wiki/Lebensborn" title="Lebensborn">Lebensborn</A>, an experiment to perfect racial purity. Despite this, he takes up his father's offer to remain in Berlin for a few more days. Kido attempts to use Onoda's approval to extradite Juliana from the Nazi states, though he fails and reveals his motive for visiting Smith for an unknown reason. Frank becomes further involved with the Resistance while Ed is revealed to be under the control of the Kempeitai to report on the Yakuza's counterfeiting activities in exchange for his and Frank's lives. Lem assists Abendsen in moving to a new location under the possibility the location of the High Castle is compromised and Abendsen destroys most of the films before leaving. Tagomi reveals himself to the alternate Michiko and his son Noriyuke, but discovers the alternate Tagomi's relationship with them is estranged. He is shocked to see Noriyuke married to an alternate Juliana with their son.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep16" style="text-align:center">16</TH>
<TD>6</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Kintsugi"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Paul_Holahan" title="Paul Holahan">Paul Holahan</A></TD>
<TD>Francesca Gardiner</TD>
<TD>December 16, 2016<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2016-12-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #424E5C">Juliana starts to socialize with the Ladies Committee as planned and gains the support of one of the members, Lucy. Helen discovers Thomas has been selected by the Hitler Youth group to go for an expedition in South America. She forbids her son to go until she finds out that Smith arranged to have their son disappear from society by staging a fake abduction and live a life of anonymity. Joe starts to get closer to Nicole, who reveals herself as one of the Lebensborn and brings him to meet with some of the others. After spending the night with Nicole, Joe begins to embrace his real heritage. Tagomi attempts to mend his alternate self's relationship with his family, and is dismayed by the alternate Noriyuke's foregoing of the Japanese culture. Kido is informed by his right hand man, Yoshida, that they have found Abendsen's burnt hideout and learns the Yakuza is also looking for the films.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep17" style="text-align:center">17</TH>
<TD>7</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Land O' Smiles"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Karyn_Kusama" title="Karyn Kusama">Karyn Kusama</A></TD>
<TD>Rob Williams</TD>
<TD>December 16, 2016<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2016-12-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #424E5C">Ed and Childan go to Okamura to repay their debt with the sale from Frank's forgery but are locked up in a storage room when Kido and his men pay a visit. Kido kills Okamura and the Yakuza members present for treason as he has deduced the Yakuza are working with the Nazis. Yoshida discovers Ed and Childan but lets them go. Frank is tasked to plant a bomb at the harbor where General Onoda is visiting. However, Frank aborts the mission when he discovers that the Japanese are secretly building an atomic bomb there and alerts the Resistance of this information. While at Adler's funeral, Smith is dismayed when Adler's wife Alice raises her suspicion on her husband's sudden death and plans to have an autopsy performed. Juliana also attends the funeral and while talking to Thomas, she notices he has a seizure and covers for him. Later, she promises Helen that she will not reveal Thomas's condition. Smith has further troubles when Heinrich Himmler informs him that Hitler has suffered a collapse.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep18" style="text-align:center">18</TH>
<TD>8</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Loose Lips"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Alex_Zakrzewski" title="Alex Zakrzewski">Alex Zakrzewski</A></TD>
<TD>Rick Cleveland</TD>
<TD>December 16, 2016<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2016-12-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #424E5C">Smith questions Juliana about Joe's film and learns of San Francisco's impending destruction. Lucy tells Juliana she knows that supposedly live footage of Hitler is actually archival because her husband manages the TV broadcast. Juliana shares with Dixon her belief that Hitler may be dead. The Resistance decide it is time to stage an uprising, leaving Juliana concerned that she may have caused the nuclear catastrophe she is trying to prevent. Heusmann is made Acting Chancellor while Joe decides to support his father. Frank learns from Arnold that Juliana has warned them to leave San Francisco and has not betrayed him. Enraged, he confronts Gary but the Resistance is determined to go ahead with the uprising. Armed with the knowledge from Juliana and Kido, Smith misleads a secretly imprisoned Heydrich into thinking Germany and Japan are already at war, leading Heydrich to confirm what Smith has suspected: a conspiracy to create a pretext for war with the Japanese exists among the Nazi ranks. Smith executes Heydrich, but not before learning he is not the mastermind behind the rush to war. Hitler passes away, leaving Heusmann in charge, and the new Chancellor is revealed to have orchestrated the looming conflict.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep19" style="text-align:center">19</TH>
<TD>9</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Detonation"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Chris_Long_(director)" title="Chris Long (director)">Chris Long</A></TD>
<TD>Wesley Strick</TD>
<TD>December 16, 2016<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2016-12-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #424E5C">Tagomi watches a film with his alternate family showing the <A href="/wiki/Nuclear_testing_at_Bikini_Atoll" title="Nuclear testing at Bikini Atoll">recent test detonation</A> of a hydrogen bomb at <A href="/wiki/Bikini_Atoll" title="Bikini Atoll">Bikini Atoll</A>. Finally resolved to stop war between Japan and the Nazis, Tagomi takes the film and returns to his reality. Thomas confides to Juliana about his condition, unaware that their conversation is being recorded. Smith later learns of the tape and takes it to protect Thomas' secret. In a televised address, Heusmann frames the Japanese for Hitler's death by poison and promises retaliation much to Joe's horror. Frank decides to assist the Resistance in assassinating Onoda using their homemade bombs. Before the operation, he convinces Ed and Childan to leave San Francisco. Frank and Sarah smuggle a car bomb into the Kempeitai HQ underground parking garage. They set the bomb timer and attempt to leave the building, but are spotted by Kido, which starts a gunfight in the lobby. Just as Tagomi arrives, the bomb detonates, killing General Onoda and his staff and collapsing most of the building. Frank and Sarah's fate is not shown.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep20" style="text-align:center">20</TH>
<TD>10</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Fallout"</TD>
<TD>Daniel Percival</TD>
<TD>Erik Oleson</TD>
<TD>December 16, 2016<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2016-12-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="6" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #424E5C">Tagomi and Kido, who survived the bombing, deal with the aftermath of the destruction of the Kempeitai HQ. Afterwards, Kido travels to New York and plays the film for Smith appearing to provide evidence that the Japanese possess a hydrogen bomb. The resistance attempts to avenge Karen's death by killing Juliana, but she escapes and kills Susan in the process. She then confronts and kills Dixon, who was threatening to expose Smith by broadcasting the tape of her conversation with Thomas. Smith travels to Berlin with the film to convince the Nazi higher-ups not to attack Japan out of fear of nuclear retaliation and meets privately with Himmler, exposing Heusmann as the traitor. After arresting Heusmann and Joe, Himmler addresses the worldwide public from the <A href="/wiki/Volkshalle" title="Volkshalle">Volkshalle</A>, possibly assuming control of the Reich, and rewards Smith for his service. The recognition Smith receives inspires Thomas to turn himself over to the Public Health Department to be euthanized. After traveling to the Neutral Zone, a bereft Juliana learns from Abendsen that hope remains and that her sister is alive. Finally, Lem hands over Abendsen's remaining films to Tagomi.</TD>
</TR>
