<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Production">Production</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14" title="Edit section: Production">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>In 2010, it was announced that the <A href="/wiki/BBC" title="BBC">BBC</A> would co-produce a four-part TV adaptation of <I>The Man in the High Castle</I> for <A href="/wiki/BBC_One" title="BBC One">BBC One</A> together with Headline Pictures, <A href="/wiki/FremantleMedia" title="FremantleMedia">FremantleMedia Enterprises</A> and <A href="/wiki/Scott_Free_Productions" title="Scott Free Productions">Scott Free Films</A>. Director <A href="/wiki/Ridley_Scott" title="Ridley Scott">Ridley Scott</A> was to act as <A href="/wiki/Executive_producer" title="Executive producer">executive producer</A> of the adaptation by <A href="/wiki/Howard_Brenton" title="Howard Brenton">Howard Brenton</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On February 11, 2013, <I><A href="/wiki/Variety_(magazine)" title="Variety (magazine)">Variety</A></I> reported that <A href="/wiki/Syfy" title="Syfy">Syfy</A> was adapting the book as a four-part miniseries, with Ridley Scott and Frank Spotnitz as executive producers, co-produced with Scott Free Prods., Headline Pictures and Electric Shepherd Prods.<SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On October 1, 2014, Amazon.com began filming the pilot episode in <A href="/wiki/Roslyn,_Washington" title="Roslyn, Washington">Roslyn, Washington</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-Muir2014_18-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Muir2014-18">[18]</A></SUP> for a new television drama to be aired on their Prime web video streaming service.<SUP id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-19">[19]</A></SUP> This has been adapted by Frank Spotnitz and is being produced for Amazon by Ridley Scott, David Zucker and Jordan Sheehan for Scott Free, Stewart Mackinnon and Christian Baute for Headline Pictures, Isa Hackett and Kalen Egan for Electric Shepherd and Spotnitz's Big Light Productions.<SUP id="cite_ref-Variety_review_2015-11-18_1-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Variety_review_2015-11-18-1">[1]</A></SUP> The pilot episode was released by <A href="/wiki/Amazon_Studios" title="Amazon Studios">Amazon Studios</A> on January 15, 2015.<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP> Amazon Studios' production process is somewhat different from those of other conventional television channels. They produce pilot episodes of a number of different prospective programs, then release them and gather data on their success. The most promising shows are then picked up as regular series. On February 18, 2015, Amazon.com announced that <I>The Man in the High Castle</I> was given the <A href="/wiki/Green-light" title="Green-light">green-light</A> along with four other series, and a full season would be produced.<SUP id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-21">[21]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Production for the pilot episode began in October 2014. Principal filming took place in <A href="/wiki/Seattle" title="Seattle">Seattle</A>, with the city standing in for <A href="/wiki/San_Francisco" title="San Francisco">San Francisco</A> and locations in <A href="/wiki/New_York_City" title="New York City">New York City</A>, as well as <A href="/wiki/Roslyn,_Washington" title="Roslyn, Washington">Roslyn, Washington</A>, which was the long-time shooting location for <I><A href="/wiki/Northern_Exposure" title="Northern Exposure">Northern Exposure</A></I>. Sites used in Seattle include the <A href="/wiki/Seattle_Center_Monorail" title="Seattle Center Monorail">Seattle Center Monorail</A>, the <A href="/wiki/Paramount_Theatre_(Seattle)" title="Paramount Theatre (Seattle)">Paramount Theatre</A>, a newspaper office in the <A href="/wiki/Pike_Place_Market" title="Pike Place Market">Pike Place Market</A> area, as well as various buildings in the city's <A href="/wiki/Capitol_Hill,_Seattle" class="mw-redirect" title="Capitol Hill, Seattle">Capitol Hill</A>, <A href="/wiki/Chinatown-International_District,_Seattle" title="Chinatown-International District, Seattle">International District</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Georgetown,_Seattle" title="Georgetown, Seattle">Georgetown</A> neighborhoods. In Roslyn, the production used external shots of the Roslyn Cafe which featured prominently in <I>Northern Exposure</I> along with several local businesses and scenery.<SUP id="cite_ref-Muir2014_18-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Muir2014-18">[18]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In April 2015, filming took place in <A href="/wiki/Vancouver" title="Vancouver">Vancouver</A>, <A href="/wiki/British_Columbia" title="British Columbia">British Columbia</A>, in the downtown area of <A href="/wiki/Georgia_Street" title="Georgia Street">West Georgia Street</A>, along the promenade of the <A href="/wiki/Coast_Capital_Savings" title="Coast Capital Savings">Coast Capital Savings</A> building.<SUP id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-23">[23]</A></SUP> In May and June 2015 filming also took place at the <A href="/wiki/University_of_British_Columbia" title="University of British Columbia">University of British Columbia</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-24">[24]</A></SUP> Exterior shots of <A href="/wiki/Hohenwerfen_Castle" title="Hohenwerfen Castle">Hohenwerfen Castle</A> in <A href="/wiki/Werfen" title="Werfen">Werfen</A>, <A href="/wiki/Austria" title="Austria">Austria</A>, were filmed in September 2015 for the tenth episode of the first season.<SUP id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-25">[25]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Amazon announced that they were bringing on new executive producer and showrunner <A href="/wiki/Eric_Overmyer" title="Eric Overmyer">Eric Overmyer</A> for season three to replace Frank Spotnitz after his sudden departure from the show during the middle of season two.<SUP id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-26">[26]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Reception">Reception</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=15" title="Edit section: Reception">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The first season of <I>The Man in the High Castle</I> received acclaim from critics. <A href="/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes" title="Rotten Tomatoes">Rotten Tomatoes</A> gives season 1 an approval rating of 95% based on reviews from 58 critics, with an average rating of 7.54 out of 10. The site's critical consensus states, "By executive producer Ridley Scott, <I>The Man in the High Castle</I> is unlike anything else on TV, with an immediately engrossing plot driven by quickly developed characters in a fully realized post-WWII dystopia."<SUP id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-27">[27]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Metacritic" title="Metacritic">Metacritic</A> gives the first season a score of 77 out of 100, based on reviews from 30 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<SUP id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-28">[28]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Meredith Woerner from <I><A href="/wiki/Io9" title="Io9">io9</A></I> wrote, "I can honestly say I loved this pilot. It's an impressive, streamlined undertaking of a fairly complicated and very beloved novel."<SUP id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-29">[29]</A></SUP> Matt Fowler from <A href="/wiki/IGN" title="IGN">IGN</A> gave 9.2 out of 10 and described the series as a "a superb, frightening experience filled with unexpected twists and (some sci-fi) turns."<SUP id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-30">[30]</A></SUP> Brian Moylan of <I><A href="/wiki/The_Guardian" title="The Guardian">The Guardian</A></I> was positive and praised the convincing depiction as well as the complex, and gripping, plot.<SUP id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-31">[31]</A></SUP> The <I><A href="/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times" title="Los Angeles Times">Los Angeles Times</A></I> described the pilot as "provocative" and "smartly adapted by The X-Files' Frank Spotnitz." <I><A href="/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph" title="The Daily Telegraph">The Daily Telegraph</A></I> said it was "absorbing" and <I><A href="/wiki/Wired_(magazine)" title="Wired (magazine)">Wired</A></I> called it "must-see viewing." <I><A href="/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly" title="Entertainment Weekly">Entertainment Weekly</A></I> said it was "engrossing" and "a triumph in world-building," cheering, "<I>The Man in the High Castle</I> is king."</P>
<P>After its first season, <I><A href="/wiki/Rolling_Stone" title="Rolling Stone">Rolling Stone</A></I> included it on a list of the forty best science fiction television shows of all time.<SUP id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-32">[32]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Amazon subsequently announced it was the service's most-streamed original series and had been renewed for a second season.<SUP id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-33">[33]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-34">[34]</A></SUP> Season 2 was met with mixed reviews. Rotten Tomatoes gives the second season an approval rating of 63% based on reviews from 19 critics, with an average rating of 6.86 out of 10. The site's critical consensus states, "Although its plot is admittedly unwieldy, <I>The Man in the High Castle</I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</SPAN>s second season expands its fascinating premise in powerful new directions, bolstered by stunning visuals, strong performances, and intriguing new possibilities."<SUP id="cite_ref-35" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-35">[35]</A></SUP> Metacritic gives season 2 a score of 62 out of 100, based on reviews from ten critics.<SUP id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-36">[36]</A></SUP></P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Advertising_controversy">Advertising controversy</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Man_in_the_High_Castle_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=17" title="Edit section: Advertising controversy">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>As part of an advertising campaign for the release of the first season, one entire <A href="/wiki/New_York_City_Subway" title="New York City Subway">New York City Subway</A> car was covered with Nazi and Imperial Japanese imagery as seen in the show, including multiple <A href="/wiki/Flag_of_the_United_States" title="Flag of the United States">American flags</A> with the <A href="/wiki/Nazi_symbolism" title="Nazi symbolism">Nazi eagle emblem</A> in place of the 50 stars and multiple flags of the fictional Pacific States.<SUP id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-51">[51]</A></SUP> In response to criticism from "state lawmakers and city leaders", the <A href="/wiki/Metropolitan_Transportation_Authority" title="Metropolitan Transportation Authority">Metropolitan Transportation Authority</A> (MTA) released a statement saying that there were no grounds to reject the ads due to the fact that neutral content subway ad standards only prohibit advertising that is a political advertisement or disparages an individual or group. MTA spokesperson Kevin Ortiz stated that, "The MTA is a government agency and can't accept or reject ads based on how we feel about them; we have to follow the standards approved by our board. Please note they're commercial ads." Spokesperson Adam Lisberg said, "This advertising, whether you find it distasteful or not, obviously they're not advertising Nazism; they're advertising a TV show." After complaints from <A href="/wiki/Governor_of_New_York" title="Governor of New York">New York State Governor</A> <A href="/wiki/Andrew_Cuomo" title="Andrew Cuomo">Andrew Cuomo</A> and <A href="/wiki/Mayor_of_New_York_City" title="Mayor of New York City">New York City Mayor</A> <A href="/wiki/Bill_de_Blasio" title="Bill de Blasio">Bill de Blasio</A>, initial reports indicated that Amazon pulled the advertisement from the subway. It was later announced that it was the MTA, not Amazon, that pulled the ad, due to pressure from Governor Cuomo.<SUP id="cite_ref-52" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-52">[52]</A></SUP></P>

<P>This is a list of the <B>heads of state of <A href="/wiki/Nigeria" title="Nigeria">Nigeria</A></B>, from independence in 1960 to the present day.</P>
<P>From 1960 to 1963 the head of state under the <A href="/w/index.php?title=Nigeria_Independence_Act_1960&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Nigeria Independence Act 1960 (page does not exist)">Nigeria Independence Act 1960</A> was the <A href="/wiki/Queen_of_Nigeria" title="Queen of Nigeria">Queen of Nigeria</A>, <A href="/wiki/Elizabeth_II" title="Elizabeth II">Elizabeth II</A>, who was also <A href="/wiki/Monarchy_of_the_United_Kingdom" title="Monarchy of the United Kingdom">monarch of the United Kingdom</A> and the other <A href="/wiki/Commonwealth_realm" title="Commonwealth realm">Commonwealth realms</A>. The Queen was represented in Nigeria by a <A href="/wiki/List_of_heads_of_state_of_Nigeria#Governors-General" title="List of heads of state of Nigeria">Governor-General</A>. Nigeria became a federal republic under the Constitution of 1963 and the monarch and Governor-General were replaced by a ceremonial <A href="/wiki/President_of_Nigeria" title="President of Nigeria">President</A>. In 1979, under the 1979 Constitution, the President gained executive powers, becoming head of both state and government. Since 1994, under the 1993 Constitution and the current 1999 Constitution, the head of state and government has been called the President.<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP></P>

<P>The <A href="/wiki/List_of_heads_of_state_of_Nigeria#Governors-General" title="List of heads of state of Nigeria">Governor-General</A> was the representative of the monarch in Nigeria and exercised most of the powers of the monarch. The Governor-General was appointed for an indefinite term, serving at the pleasure of the monarch. Since Nigeria was granted independence by the <A href="/w/index.php?title=Nigeria_Independence_Act_1960&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Nigeria Independence Act 1960 (page does not exist)">Nigeria Independence Act 1960</A>, rather than being first established as a semi-autonomous <A href="/wiki/Dominion" title="Dominion">Dominion</A> and later promoted to independence by the <A href="/wiki/Statute_of_Westminster_1931" title="Statute of Westminster 1931">Statute of Westminster 1931</A>, the Governor-General was appointed solely on the advice of the Nigerian cabinet without the involvement of the British government, with the sole of exception of James Robertson, the former colonial governor, who served as Governor-General temporarily until he was replaced by Nnamdi Azikiwe. In the event of a vacancy the <A href="/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_Nigeria" title="Chief Justice of Nigeria">Chief Justice</A> would have served as <A href="/wiki/Administrator_of_the_Government" title="Administrator of the Government">Officer Administering the Government</A>.</P>

<H2><SPAN id="First_Republic_(1963–1966)"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="First_Republic_.281963.E2.80.931966.29"><A href="/wiki/First_Nigerian_Republic" title="First Nigerian Republic">First Republic</A> (1963–1966)</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_heads_of_state_of_Nigeria&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: First Republic (1963–1966)">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>

<H2><SPAN id="Third_Republic_(1993)"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Third_Republic_.281993.29"><A href="/wiki/Third_Nigerian_Republic" title="Third Nigerian Republic">Third Republic</A> (1993)</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_heads_of_state_of_Nigeria&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Third Republic (1993)">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The Third Republic was the planned republican government of Nigeria in 1993 which was to be governed by the Third Republican constitution.</P>
<P>The constitution of the Third Republic was drafted in 1989, when General <A href="/wiki/Ibrahim_Babangida" title="Ibrahim Babangida">Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida</A> (IBB), the <A href="/wiki/President_of_Nigeria" title="President of Nigeria">military Head of State</A>, promised to terminate military rule by 1990 – a date which was subsequently pushed back to 1993. IBB lifted the ban on political activity in the spring of 1989, and his government established two political parties: the center-right <A href="/wiki/National_Republican_Convention" title="National Republican Convention">National Republican Convention</A> (NRC) and the center-left <A href="/wiki/Social_Democratic_Party_(Nigeria)" title="Social Democratic Party (Nigeria)">Social Democratic Party</A> (SDP). <A href="/wiki/Gubernatorial" class="mw-redirect" title="Gubernatorial">Gubernatorial</A> and state legislative elections were conducted in December 1991, while the presidential election was postponed till 12 June 1993 – due to political unrest. <A href="/wiki/Moshood_Kashimawo_Olawale_Abiola" class="mw-redirect" title="Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola">M. K. O. Abiola</A>, a wealthy <A href="/wiki/Yoruba_people" title="Yoruba people">Yoruba</A> businessman, won a decisive victory in the presidential elections on the SDP platm.</P>

<P><I><A href="/wiki/Game_of_Thrones" title="Game of Thrones">Game of Thrones</A></I> is an American <A href="/wiki/Fantasy" title="Fantasy">fantasy</A> <A href="/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)" title="Drama (film and television)">drama</A> television series created for <A href="/wiki/HBO" title="HBO">HBO</A> by <A href="/wiki/David_Benioff" title="David Benioff">David Benioff</A> and <A href="/wiki/D._B._Weiss" title="D. B. Weiss">D. B. Weiss</A>. It is an adaptation of <I><A href="/wiki/A_Song_of_Ice_and_Fire" title="A Song of Ice and Fire">A Song of Ice and Fire</A></I>, <A href="/wiki/George_R._R._Martin" title="George R. R. Martin">George R. R. Martin</A>'s series of fantasy novels.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[1]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[2]</A></SUP> The story takes place on the fictional continents of <A href="/wiki/World_of_A_Song_of_Ice_and_Fire" title="World of A Song of Ice and Fire">Westeros and Essos</A>, it has several plot lines and a large <A href="/wiki/Ensemble_cast" title="Ensemble cast">ensemble cast</A>. The first <A href="/wiki/Story_arc" title="Story arc">story arc</A> follows a dynastic conflict among competing claimants for succession to the <A href="/wiki/Iron_Throne_(A_Song_of_Ice_and_Fire)" title="Iron Throne (A Song of Ice and Fire)">Iron Throne</A> of the <A href="/wiki/World_of_A_Song_of_Ice_and_Fire#Westeros" title="World of A Song of Ice and Fire">Seven Kingdoms</A>, with other noble families fighting for independence from the throne. The second covers attempts to reclaim the throne by the exiled last <A href="/wiki/Lineal_descendant" title="Lineal descendant">scion</A> of the realm's deposed ruling dynasty; the third chronicles the threat of the impending winter and the legendary creatures and fierce peoples of the North.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[3]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The series, mostly written by Benioff, Weiss and Martin, has been nominated for many awards, including six <A href="/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award" title="Golden Globe Award">Golden Globe Awards</A> (one win),<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[4]</A></SUP> ten <A href="/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America_Award" title="Writers Guild of America Award">Writers Guild of America Awards</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[5]</A></SUP> seven <A href="/wiki/Producers_Guild_of_America_Award" title="Producers Guild of America Award">Producers Guild of America Awards</A> (one win), eight <A href="/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America_Award" title="Directors Guild of America Award">Directors Guild of America Awards</A> (two wins), eight <A href="/wiki/ADG_Excellence_in_Production_Design_Award" title="ADG Excellence in Production Design Award">Art Directors Guild Awards</A> (five wins), twenty one <A href="/wiki/Saturn_Award" title="Saturn Award">Saturn Awards</A> (two wins),<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[6]</A></SUP> fourteen <A href="/wiki/Satellite_Awards" title="Satellite Awards">Satellite Awards</A> (three wins), and one <A href="/wiki/Peabody_Award" title="Peabody Award">Peabody Award</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-peabody_8-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-peabody-8">[7]</A></SUP> The series has received 110 <A href="/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award" title="Primetime Emmy Award">Primetime Emmy Award</A> nominations, including six consecutive <A href="/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Drama_Series" title="Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series">Outstanding Drama Series</A> nominations, with 38 wins to date.<SUP id="cite_ref-ewrecord_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ewrecord-9">[8]</A></SUP> <I>Game of Thrones</I> received many nominations, with awards recognizing various aspects of the series such as directing, writing, cast, visual effects, or overall quality.</P>
<P><A href="/wiki/Peter_Dinklage" title="Peter Dinklage">Peter Dinklage</A> is the most rewarded member of the cast, with recognitions such as the <A href="/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Supporting_Actor_in_a_Drama_Series" title="Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series">Primetime Emmy Award</A><SUP id="cite_ref-2015EmmyPT_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2015EmmyPT-10">[9]</A></SUP> and <A href="/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_%E2%80%93_Series,_Miniseries_or_Television_Film" title="Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Series, Miniseries or Television Film">Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actor in a Series</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-goldenglobe_2011-12_11-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-goldenglobe_2011-12-11">[10]</A></SUP> In addition, cast members <A href="/wiki/Lena_Headey" title="Lena Headey">Lena Headey</A>, <A href="/wiki/Emilia_Clarke" title="Emilia Clarke">Emilia Clarke</A>, <A href="/wiki/Kit_Harington" title="Kit Harington">Kit Harington</A>, <A href="/wiki/Maisie_Williams" title="Maisie Williams">Maisie Williams</A>, <A href="/wiki/Diana_Rigg" title="Diana Rigg">Diana Rigg</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Max_von_Sydow" title="Max von Sydow">Max von Sydow</A> received Primetime Emmy Award nominations for their performances in the series.<SUP id="cite_ref-2011Emmy_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2011Emmy-12">[11]</A></SUP> The rest of the cast was also very praised, many receiving various awards nominations, including six <A href="/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_an_Ensemble_in_a_Drama_Series" title="Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series">Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series</A> nominations rewarding all of the main cast for seasons 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7.<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[12]</A></SUP> In 2015, it set a record for winning the most number of Primetime Emmy Awards for a series in a single year, with 12 wins out of 24 nominations.<SUP id="cite_ref-2015EmmyVar_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2015EmmyVar-14">[13]</A></SUP> In 2016, it became the most awarded series in Emmy Awards history, with a total of 38 wins.<SUP id="cite_ref-ewrecord_9-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ewrecord-9">[8]</A></SUP> To date, <I>Game of Thrones</I> has won 239 awards out of 682 nominations.</P>
<P><I>Game of Thrones</I> also holds six world records from the <A href="/wiki/Guinness_World_Records" title="Guinness World Records">Guinness Book of World Records</A>: "Most pirated TV program and Largest TV drama simulcast" among others.<SUP id="cite_ref-worldrecordone_15-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-worldrecordone-15">[14]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-worldrecordtwo_16-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-worldrecordtwo-16">[15]</A></SUP></P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="BAFTA_Awards">BAFTA Awards</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Game_of_Thrones&action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section: BAFTA Awards">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The <A href="/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Awards" title="British Academy Television Awards">British Academy Television Awards</A> are presented in an annual award show hosted by the <A href="/wiki/British_Academy_of_Film_and_Television_Arts" title="British Academy of Film and Television Arts">British Academy of Film and Television Arts</A> (BAFTA).<SUP id="cite_ref-64" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-64">[63]</A></SUP> They have been awarded annually since 1955. It is the British equivalent to the Emmy Awards in the <A href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</A>. <I>Game of Thrones</I> has won two out of eight nominations. British Academy Television Awards recognize outstanding work in British television programming, while the <A href="/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Craft_Awards" title="British Academy Television Craft Awards">British Academy Television Craft Awards</A> are presented to honor technical and creative achievements, and include categories recognising work of art directors, lighting and costume designers, cinematographers, casting directors, and other production-based personnel.<SUP id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-65">[64]</A></SUP></P>

<A href="/wiki/Lena_Headey" title="Lena Headey">Lena Headey</A> received her first Primetime Emmy Award nomination for her performance as <A href="/wiki/Cersei_Lannister" title="Cersei Lannister">Cersei Lannister</A> in 2014</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>The <A href="/wiki/Emmy_Award" title="Emmy Award">Emmy Awards</A> were established in 1949 in order to recognize excellence in the American television industry, and are bestowed by members of the <A href="/wiki/Academy_of_Television_Arts_%26_Sciences" title="Academy of Television Arts & Sciences">Academy of Television Arts & Sciences</A>. Emmy Awards are given in different ceremonies presented annually; <A href="/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award" title="Primetime Emmy Award">Primetime Emmy Awards</A> recognize outstanding work in American primetime television programming, while the <A href="/wiki/Creative_Arts_Emmy_Award" title="Creative Arts Emmy Award">Creative Arts Emmy Awards</A> are presented to honor technical and creative achievements, and include categories recognising work of art directors, lighting and costume designers, cinematographers, casting directors, and other production-based personnel.<SUP id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-100">[99]</A></SUP> The Emmy Award corresponds to the <A href="/wiki/Academy_Award" class="mw-redirect" title="Academy Award">Academy Award</A> (for film), the <A href="/wiki/Tony_Award" title="Tony Award">Tony Award</A> (for theatre), and the <A href="/wiki/Grammy_Award" title="Grammy Award">Grammy Award</A> (for music).<SUP id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-101">[100]</A></SUP></P>
<P><I>Game of Thrones</I> has won 38 out of 110 nominations.<SUP id="cite_ref-2011Emmy_12-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2011Emmy-12">[11]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Peter_Dinklage" title="Peter Dinklage">Peter Dinklage</A> has been nominated for the best supporting actor six times in a row for playing <A href="/wiki/Tyrion_Lannister" title="Tyrion Lannister">Tyrion Lannister</A>, with an win in 2011 and 2015. Showrunners <A href="/wiki/David_Benioff" title="David Benioff">David Benioff</A> and <A href="/wiki/D._B._Weiss" title="D. B. Weiss">D. B. Weiss</A> have won twice for writing. <I>Game of Thrones</I> has six nominations for the best drama series, winning two in 2015 and 2016. Both <A href="/wiki/David_Nutter" title="David Nutter">David Nutter</A> and <A href="/wiki/Miguel_Sapochnik" title="Miguel Sapochnik">Miguel Sapochnik</A> have won for directing. <I>Game of Thrones</I> holds the Emmy-award record for most wins for a scripted television series, ahead of <I><A href="/wiki/Frasier" title="Frasier">Frasier</A></I> (which received 37).<SUP id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-102">[101]</A></SUP></P>
<P>At the <A href="/wiki/67th_Primetime_Emmy_Awards" title="67th Primetime Emmy Awards">67th Primetime Emmy Awards</A> the show's fifth season was nominated for 24 awards. The show ultimately won twelve awards, setting a new record for most Emmy wins by a series in a single year, replacing the previous holder <I><A href="/wiki/The_West_Wing" title="The West Wing">The West Wing</A></I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</SPAN>s nine wins, and tying that show and <I><A href="/wiki/Hill_Street_Blues" title="Hill Street Blues">Hill Street Blues</A></I> for the most wins by a drama series throughout its run.<SUP id="cite_ref-2015EmmyVar_14-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2015EmmyVar-14">[13]</A></SUP> At the nominee announcement for the <A href="/wiki/68th_Primetime_Emmy_Awards" title="68th Primetime Emmy Awards">68th Primetime Emmy Awards</A>, the show's sixth season received the most nominations of any show with 23. The show yet again won twelve awards, setting the same record for most Emmy wins by a series in a single year.<SUP id="cite_ref-2011Emmy_12-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2011Emmy-12">[11]</A></SUP></P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Location_Managers_Guild_Awards">Location Managers Guild Awards</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Game_of_Thrones&action=edit&section=28" title="Edit section: Location Managers Guild Awards">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The <A href="/wiki/Location_Managers_Guild_Awards" title="Location Managers Guild Awards">Location Managers Guild Awards</A> are awarded annually by the <A href="/wiki/Location_Managers_Guild_International" title="Location Managers Guild International">Location Managers Guild International</A>. <I>Game of Thrones</I> took the most awards, two in total, and claimed the top TV award at the inaugural LMGA Awards in 2014.<SUP id="cite_ref-2014LMGuild_144-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2014LMGuild-144">[143]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In 2016 the show became the first series to win multiple LMGI Awards, with <A href="/wiki/Location_Manager" class="mw-redirect" title="Location Manager">Location Managers</A> Robert Boake and Tate Araez taking home the award for Outstanding Locations in a Period Television Series.<SUP id="cite_ref-2016LMGuild_145-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2016LMGuild-145">[144]</A></SUP> Nominated again in 2017 and 2018, <I>Game of Thrones</I> took back the period television throne from <I><A href="/wiki/The_Crown_(TV_series)" title="The Crown (TV series)">The Crown</A></I> in 2018, and currently holds a record 4 LMGI Award wins out of 5 nominations.</P>
<P>The <A href="/wiki/Filming_location" title="Filming location">film locations</A> featured in <I>Game of Thrones</I> have also proven to be winners themselves, as the show has been responsible for driving a significant increase in tourism to the host regions filmed by the series.<SUP id="cite_ref-146" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-146">[145]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-147" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-147">[146]</A></SUP></P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Society_of_Camera_Operators_Awards">Society of Camera Operators Awards</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Game_of_Thrones&action=edit&section=32" title="Edit section: Society of Camera Operators Awards">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The <A href="/wiki/Society_of_Operating_Cameramen" title="Society of Operating Cameramen">Society of Camera Operators Awards</A> are awarded annually to honor the creative contribution of the camera operator in the motion picture and television industries.<SUP id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-173">[172]</A></SUP> <I>Game of Thrones</I> has been nominated one time.</P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Visual_Effects_Society">Visual Effects Society</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Game_of_Thrones&action=edit&section=33" title="Edit section: Visual Effects Society">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P><A href="/wiki/Visual_Effects_Society" title="Visual Effects Society">Visual Effects Society</A> honors <A href="/wiki/Visual_effects" title="Visual effects">visual effects</A> in film, television, commercials, music videos and video games. At the <A href="/wiki/Visual_Effects_Society" title="Visual Effects Society">11th annual Visual Effects Society</A> awards, the show won four awards, the most of the TV shows nominated.<SUP id="cite_ref-2013VESociety_175-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2013VESociety-175">[174]</A></SUP> In 2014 the show was the most successful TV nominee at the <A href="/wiki/Visual_Effects_Society" title="Visual Effects Society">Visual Effects Society</A> awards for the second year in a row, winning three of its four nominations.<SUP id="cite_ref-2014VESWin_176-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2014VESWin-176">[175]</A></SUP> In 2015 <I>Game of Thrones</I> was the most successful TV nominee at the Visual Effects Society awards for the third consecutive year, winning three of its five nominations.<SUP id="cite_ref-2015VES_177-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2015VES-177">[176]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-2015VESGen_178-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2015VESGen-178">[177]</A></SUP> In 2016 the show was the most successful TV nominee at the Visual Effects Society awards for the fourth consecutive year, winning four of its nine nominations.<SUP id="cite_ref-auto1_179-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-auto1-179">[178]</A></SUP> <I>Game of Thrones</I> has received twenty six awards out of forty seven nominations.</P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Writers_Guild_of_America_Awards">Writers Guild of America Awards</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Game_of_Thrones&action=edit&section=34" title="Edit section: Writers Guild of America Awards">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>First presented in 1949, the <A href="/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America_Award" title="Writers Guild of America Award">Writers Guild of America Award</A> recognizes the work of film, television and radio screenwriters.<SUP id="cite_ref-186" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-186">[185]</A></SUP> <I>Game of Thrones</I> has been nominated ten times.</P>
<P>In June 2013, the show was placed at number 40 on the list of the 101 best written shows of all time by the <A href="/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America" title="Writers Guild of America">Writers Guild of America</A>, assessing series from the previous 70 years.<SUP id="cite_ref-2013WGABestever_187-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2013WGABestever-187">[186]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-188" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-188">[187]</A></SUP> HBO had attempted to submit the show for a third consecutive Writers Guild Award for Best Drama Series, but a technical error during the process meant it was not submitted and the fault was discovered too late for the show to be entered.<SUP id="cite_ref-2013WGA_189-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2013WGA-189">[188]</A></SUP></P>

<P>The <A href="/wiki/Peabody_Award" title="Peabody Award">Peabody Award</A> recognizes excellence in various platforms of the media, including film, television, and radio. The award "spotlight[s] instances of how electronic media can teach, expand our horizons, defend the public interest, or encourage empathy with others".<SUP id="cite_ref-242" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-242">[241]</A></SUP> <I>Game of Thrones</I> was honored with a <A href="/wiki/Peabody_Award" title="Peabody Award">Peabody Award</A> in 2011 for its first season. The award association gave the following description of the show:<SUP id="cite_ref-peabody_8-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-peabody-8">[7]</A></SUP></P>

<P>The <A href="/wiki/Satellite_Awards" title="Satellite Awards">Satellite Award</A> is given annually by the <A href="/wiki/International_Press_Academy" title="International Press Academy">International Press Academy</A> (IPA) to honor the best work in the entertainment industry.<SUP id="cite_ref-250" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-250">[249]</A></SUP> <I>Game of Thrones</I> has received three awards out of fourteen nominations.</P>
<P>In 2011, Dinklage received the <A href="/wiki/Satellite_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_%E2%80%93_Series,_Miniseries_or_Television_Film" title="Satellite Award for Best Supporting Actor – Series, Miniseries or Television Film">Satellite Award for Best Supporting Actor – Series, Miniseries, or Television Film</A>, and received three more nominations (2012, 2014–2015).<SUP id="cite_ref-2012Satellite_251-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2012Satellite-251">[250]</A></SUP> In 2014, <I>Game of Thrones</I> won the <A href="/wiki/Satellite_Award_for_Best_Television_Series_%E2%80%93_Genre" title="Satellite Award for Best Television Series – Genre">Satellite Award for Best Television Series – Genre</A>, while <A href="/wiki/Nikolaj_Coster-Waldau" title="Nikolaj Coster-Waldau">Nikolaj Coster-Waldau</A> and <A href="/wiki/Emilia_Clarke" title="Emilia Clarke">Emilia Clarke</A> received nominations for Best Supporting Actor and <A href="/wiki/Satellite_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress_%E2%80%93_Series,_Miniseries_or_Television_Film" title="Satellite Award for Best Supporting Actress – Series, Miniseries or Television Film">Best Supporting Actress</A>, respectively.<SUP id="cite_ref-2013Satellite_252-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2013Satellite-252">[251]</A></SUP></P>

<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/File:Star_of_David.svg" class="image"><IMG alt="Star of David.svg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Star_of_David.svg/14px-Star_of_David.svg.png" width="14" height="16" class="noviewer" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Star_of_David.svg/21px-Star_of_David.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Star_of_David.svg/28px-Star_of_David.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="260" data-file-height="300" /></A> <A href="/wiki/Portal:Judaism" title="Portal:Judaism">Judaism portal</A></LI></UL></TD></TR><TR><TD style="text-align:right;font-size:115%;padding-top: 0.6em;"><DIV class="plainlinks hlist navbar mini"><UL><LI class="nv-view"><A href="/wiki/Template:Judaism" title="Template:Judaism"><ABBR title="View this template">v</ABBR></A></LI><LI class="nv-talk"><A href="/wiki/Template_talk:Judaism" title="Template talk:Judaism"><ABBR title="Discuss this template">t</ABBR></A></LI><LI class="nv-edit"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:Judaism&action=edit"><ABBR title="Edit this template">e</ABBR></A></LI></UL></DIV></TD></TR></TBODY></TABLE>
<P><B>Judaism</B> (originally from <A href="/wiki/Hebrew_language" title="Hebrew language">Hebrew</A> <SPAN class="script-hebrew" style="font-size: 115%; font-family: 'Ezra SIL', 'Ezra SIL SR', 'Keter Aram Tsova', 'Taamey Ashkenaz', 'Taamey David CLM', 'Taamey Frank CLM', 'Frenk Ruehl CLM', 'Keter YG', 'Shofar', 'David CLM', 'Hadasim CLM', 'Simple CLM', 'Nachlieli', 'SBL BibLit', 'SBL Hebrew', Cardo, Alef, 'Noto Serif Hebrew', 'Noto Sans Hebrew', 'David Libre', David, 'Times New Roman', Gisha, Arial, FreeSerif, FreeSans;" dir="rtl">יהודה</SPAN>‬, <I>Yehudah</I>, "<A href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Judah" title="Kingdom of Judah">Judah</A>";<SUP id="cite_ref-bibleinterp_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-bibleinterp-1">[1]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-askoxford_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-askoxford-2">[2]</A></SUP> via <A href="/wiki/Latin" title="Latin">Latin</A> and <A href="/wiki/Ancient_Greek" title="Ancient Greek">Greek</A>) is the religion of the <A href="/wiki/Jews" title="Jews">Jewish people</A>. It is an ancient, <A href="/wiki/Monotheistic" class="mw-redirect" title="Monotheistic">monotheistic</A>, <A href="/wiki/Abrahamic_religion" class="mw-redirect" title="Abrahamic religion">Abrahamic religion</A> with the <A href="/wiki/Torah" title="Torah">Torah</A> as its foundational text.<SUP id="cite_ref-uncertainties_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-uncertainties-3">[3]</A></SUP> It encompasses the <A href="/wiki/Religion" title="Religion">religion</A>, <A href="/wiki/Philosophy" title="Philosophy">philosophy</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Culture" title="Culture">culture</A> of the <A href="/wiki/Jewish_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Jewish people">Jewish people</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Judaism_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Judaism-4">[4]</A></SUP> Judaism is considered by religious Jews to be the expression of the <A href="/wiki/Mosaic_covenant" title="Mosaic covenant">covenant</A> that <A href="/wiki/God_in_Judaism" title="God in Judaism">God</A> established with the <A href="/wiki/Children_of_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="Children of Israel">Children of Israel</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Knowledge_Resources:_Judaism_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Knowledge_Resources:_Judaism-5">[5]</A></SUP> Judaism encompasses a wide corpus of texts, practices, theological positions, and forms of organization. The Torah is part of the larger text known as the <A href="/wiki/Tanakh" class="mw-redirect" title="Tanakh">Tanakh</A> or the <A href="/wiki/Hebrew_Bible" title="Hebrew Bible">Hebrew Bible</A>, and supplemental oral tradition represented by later texts such as the <A href="/wiki/Midrash" title="Midrash">Midrash</A> and the <A href="/wiki/Talmud" title="Talmud">Talmud</A>. With between 14.5 and 17.4 million adherents worldwide,<SUP id="cite_ref-Population_of_Jews_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Population_of_Jews-6">[6]</A></SUP> Judaism is <A href="/wiki/Major_religious_groups#Religious_demographics" title="Major religious groups">the tenth largest religion in the world</A>.
</P><P>Within Judaism there are a variety of movements, most of which emerged from <A href="/wiki/Rabbinic_Judaism" title="Rabbinic Judaism">Rabbinic Judaism</A>, which holds that God revealed his laws and <A href="/wiki/613_Mitzvot" class="mw-redirect" title="613 Mitzvot">commandments</A> to <A href="/wiki/Moses" title="Moses">Moses</A> on <A href="/wiki/Biblical_Mount_Sinai" title="Biblical Mount Sinai">Mount Sinai</A> in the form of both the <A href="/wiki/Torah" title="Torah">Written</A> and <A href="/wiki/Oral_Torah" title="Oral Torah">Oral Torah</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-What_is_the_oral_Torah?_7-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-What_is_the_oral_Torah?-7">[7]</A></SUP> Historically, this assertion was challenged by various groups such as the <A href="/wiki/Sadducees#General" title="Sadducees">Sadducees</A> and <A href="/wiki/Hellenistic_Judaism" title="Hellenistic Judaism">Hellenistic Judaism</A> during the <A href="/wiki/Second_Temple_period" title="Second Temple period">Second Temple period</A>; the <A href="/wiki/Karaite_Judaism#Karaite_interpretations_of_the_Torah" title="Karaite Judaism">Karaites</A> and <A href="/wiki/Sabbateans" title="Sabbateans">Sabbateans</A> during the early and later medieval period;<SUP id="cite_ref-Karaite_Jewish_University_8-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Karaite_Jewish_University-8">[8]</A></SUP> and among segments of the modern non-Orthodox denominations. Modern branches of Judaism such as <A href="/wiki/Humanistic_Judaism" title="Humanistic Judaism">Humanistic Judaism</A> may be <A href="/wiki/Nontheistic" class="mw-redirect" title="Nontheistic">nontheistic</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Society_for_Humanistic_Judaism_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Society_for_Humanistic_Judaism-9">[9]</A></SUP> Today, the largest <A href="/wiki/Jewish_religious_movements" title="Jewish religious movements">Jewish religious movements</A> are <A href="/wiki/Orthodox_Judaism" title="Orthodox Judaism">Orthodox Judaism</A> (<A href="/wiki/Haredi_Judaism" title="Haredi Judaism">Haredi Judaism</A> and <A href="/wiki/Modern_Orthodox_Judaism" title="Modern Orthodox Judaism">Modern Orthodox Judaism</A>), <A href="/wiki/Conservative_Judaism" title="Conservative Judaism">Conservative Judaism</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Reform_Judaism" title="Reform Judaism">Reform Judaism</A>. Major sources of difference between these groups are their approaches to <A href="/wiki/Jewish_law" class="mw-redirect" title="Jewish law">Jewish law</A>, the authority of the <A href="/wiki/Rabbinic_tradition" class="mw-redirect" title="Rabbinic tradition">Rabbinic tradition</A>, and the significance of the <A href="/wiki/State_of_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="State of Israel">State of Israel</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Jewish_Denominations_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Jewish_Denominations-10">[10]</A></SUP> Orthodox Judaism maintains that the Torah and Jewish law are divine in origin, eternal and unalterable, and that they should be strictly followed. Conservative and Reform Judaism are more <A href="/wiki/Religious_liberalism" title="Religious liberalism">liberal</A>, with Conservative Judaism generally promoting a more traditionalist interpretation of Judaism's requirements than Reform Judaism. A typical Reform position is that Jewish law should be viewed as a set of general guidelines rather than as a set of restrictions and obligations whose observance is required of all Jews.<SUP id="cite_ref-Reform_Judaism_11-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Reform_Judaism-11">[11]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-What_is_Reform_Judaism?_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-What_is_Reform_Judaism?-12">[12]</A></SUP> Historically, <A href="/wiki/Beth_din" title="Beth din">special courts</A> enforced Jewish law; today, these courts still exist but the practice of Judaism is mostly voluntary.<SUP id="cite_ref-Britannica_Online_Encyclopedia:_Bet_Din_13-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Britannica_Online_Encyclopedia:_Bet_Din-13">[13]</A></SUP> Authority on theological and legal matters is not vested in any one person or organization, but in the sacred texts and the <A href="/wiki/Rabbis" class="mw-redirect" title="Rabbis">rabbis</A> and scholars who interpret them.<SUP id="cite_ref-religiousleadership_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-religiousleadership-14">[14]</A></SUP>
</P><P>The <A href="/wiki/History_of_Judaism" class="mw-redirect" title="History of Judaism">history of Judaism</A> spans more than 3,000 years.<SUP id="cite_ref-MINDELL2009_15-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-MINDELL2009-15">[15]</A></SUP> Judaism has its roots as an <A href="/wiki/Organized_religion" title="Organized religion">organized religion</A> in the <A href="/wiki/Middle_East" title="Middle East">Middle East</A> during the <A href="/wiki/Bronze_Age" title="Bronze Age">Bronze Age</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP> Judaism is considered one of the oldest monotheistic religions.<SUP id="cite_ref-Religion_&_Ethics_–_Judaism_17-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Religion_&_Ethics_–_Judaism-17">[17]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP> The <A href="/wiki/Hebrews" title="Hebrews">Hebrews</A> and <A href="/wiki/Israelites" title="Israelites">Israelites</A> were already referred to as "Jews" in later books of the Tanakh such as the <A href="/wiki/Book_of_Esther" title="Book of Esther">Book of Esther</A>, with the term Jews replacing the title "Children of Israel".<SUP id="cite_ref-google_19-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-google-19">[19]</A></SUP> Judaism's texts, traditions and values strongly influenced later <A href="/wiki/Abrahamic_religions" title="Abrahamic religions">Abrahamic religions</A>, including <A href="/wiki/Christianity" title="Christianity">Christianity</A>, <A href="/wiki/Islam" title="Islam">Islam</A> and the <A href="/wiki/Baha%27i_Faith" class="mw-redirect" title="Baha'i Faith">Baha'i Faith</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Islam,_Judaism,_and_Christianity:_Theological_and_Historical_Affiliations_20-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Islam,_Judaism,_and_Christianity:_Theological_and_Historical_Affiliations-20">[20]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-The_Historical_Muhammad_21-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-The_Historical_Muhammad-21">[21]</A></SUP> Many aspects of Judaism have also directly or indirectly influenced <A href="/wiki/Secular" class="mw-redirect" title="Secular">secular</A> <A href="/wiki/Western_world" title="Western world">Western</A> <A href="/wiki/Ethics" title="Ethics">ethics</A> and <A href="/wiki/Civil_law_(legal_system)" title="Civil law (legal system)">civil law</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-questia_22-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-questia-22">[22]</A></SUP><SUP class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources" title="Wikipedia:Citing sources"><SPAN title="This citation requires a reference to the specific page or range of pages in which the material appears. (July 2017)">page needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> <A href="/wiki/Hebraism" title="Hebraism">Hebraism</A> was just as important a factor in the ancient era development of <A href="/wiki/Western_civilization" class="mw-redirect" title="Western civilization">Western civilization</A> as <A href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Hellenism" class="extiw" title="wikt:Hellenism">Hellenism</A>, and Judaism, as the background of <A href="/wiki/Christianity" title="Christianity">Christianity</A>, has considerably shaped Western ideals and morality since <A href="/wiki/Early_Christianity" title="Early Christianity">Early Christianity</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Cambridge_University_Historical_Series_23-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Cambridge_University_Historical_Series-23">[23]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Jews are an <A href="/wiki/Ethnoreligious_group" title="Ethnoreligious group">ethnoreligious group</A><SUP id="cite_ref-Ethnoreligious_24-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Ethnoreligious-24">[24]</A></SUP> including those born Jewish, in addition to <A href="/wiki/Converts_to_Judaism" class="mw-redirect" title="Converts to Judaism">converts to Judaism</A>. In 2015, the <A href="/wiki/Jewish_population_by_country" title="Jewish population by country">world Jewish population</A> was estimated at about 14.3 million, or roughly 0.2% of the total world population.<SUP id="cite_ref-WJP2015_25-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-WJP2015-25">[25]</A></SUP> About 43% of all Jews reside in <A href="/wiki/Israel" title="Israel">Israel</A> and another 43% reside in the <A href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</A> and <A href="/wiki/Canada" title="Canada">Canada</A>, with most of the remainder living in <A href="/wiki/Europe" title="Europe">Europe</A>, and other minority groups spread throughout <A href="/wiki/Latin_America" title="Latin America">Latin America</A>, <A href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</A>, <A href="/wiki/Africa" title="Africa">Africa</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Australia" title="Australia">Australia</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-WJP2015_25-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-WJP2015-25">[25]</A></SUP>
</P>

<P>Unlike other ancient Near Eastern gods, the Hebrew God is portrayed as unitary and solitary; consequently, the Hebrew God's principal relationships are not with other gods, but with the world, and more specifically, with the people he created.<SUP id="cite_ref-understanding_26-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-understanding-26">[26]</A></SUP><SUP class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources" title="Wikipedia:Citing sources"><SPAN title="This citation requires a reference to the specific page or range of pages in which the material appears. (July 2017)">page needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> Judaism thus begins with ethical monotheism: the belief that God is one and is concerned with the actions of mankind.<SUP id="cite_ref-google1_27-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-google1-27">[27]</A></SUP> According to the <A href="/wiki/Tanakh" class="mw-redirect" title="Tanakh">Tanakh</A> (Hebrew Bible), God promised <A href="/wiki/Abraham" title="Abraham">Abraham</A> to make of his offspring a great nation.<SUP id="cite_ref-everlasting_28-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-everlasting-28">[28]</A></SUP> Many generations later, he commanded the nation of <A href="/wiki/Israelites" title="Israelites">Israel</A> to love and worship only one God; that is, the Jewish nation is to reciprocate God's concern for the world.<SUP id="cite_ref-deuteronomy_29-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-deuteronomy-29">[29]</A></SUP> He also commanded the Jewish people to love one another; that is, Jews are to imitate God's love for people.<SUP id="cite_ref-leviticus_30-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-leviticus-30">[30]</A></SUP> These commandments are but two of a large corpus of <A href="/wiki/613_mitzvot" class="mw-redirect" title="613 mitzvot">commandments</A> and <A href="/wiki/Halakha" title="Halakha">laws</A> that constitute this <A href="/wiki/Covenant_(biblical)" title="Covenant (biblical)">covenant</A>, which is the substance of Judaism.
</P><P>Thus, although there is an esoteric tradition in Judaism (<A href="/wiki/Kabbalah" title="Kabbalah">Kabbalah</A>), Rabbinic scholar <A href="/wiki/Max_Kadushin" title="Max Kadushin">Max Kadushin</A> has characterized normative Judaism as "normal mysticism", because it involves everyday personal experiences of God through ways or modes that are common to all Jews.<SUP id="cite_ref-publishing_31-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-publishing-31">[31]</A></SUP> This is played out through the observance of the <A href="/wiki/Halakha" title="Halakha">Halakha</A> (Jewish law) and given verbal expression in the <A href="/wiki/List_of_Jewish_prayers_and_blessings" title="List of Jewish prayers and blessings">Birkat Ha-Mizvot</A>, the short blessings that are spoken every time a positive commandment is to be fulfilled.
</P>
<DL><DD>The ordinary, familiar, everyday things and occurrences we have, constitute occasions for the experience of God. Such things as one's daily sustenance, the very day itself, are felt as manifestations of God's loving-kindness, calling for the <I>Berakhot</I>. <I>Kedushah</I>, holiness, which is nothing else than the imitation of God, is concerned with daily conduct, with being gracious and merciful, with keeping oneself from defilement by idolatry, adultery, and the shedding of blood. The <I>Birkat Ha-Mitzwot</I> evokes the consciousness of holiness at a rabbinic rite, but the objects employed in the majority of these rites are non-holy and of general character, while the several holy objects are <A href="/wiki/Theurgy" title="Theurgy">non-theurgic.</A> And not only do ordinary things and occurrences bring with them the experience of God. Everything that happens to a man evokes that experience, evil as well as good, for a <I>Berakah</I> is said also at evil tidings. Hence, although the experience of God is like none other, the <I>occasions</I> for experiencing Him, for having a consciousness of Him, are manifold, even if we consider only those that call for Berakot.<SUP id="cite_ref-publishing2_32-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-publishing2-32">[32]</A></SUP></DD></DL>
<P>Whereas <A href="/wiki/Jewish_philosophy" title="Jewish philosophy">Jewish philosophers</A> often debate whether God is <A href="/wiki/Immanence" title="Immanence">immanent</A> or <A href="/wiki/Transcendence_(religion)" title="Transcendence (religion)">transcendent</A>, and whether people have free will or their lives are determined, <A href="/wiki/Halakha" title="Halakha">Halakha</A> is a system through which any Jew acts to bring God into the world.
</P><P>Ethical monotheism is central in all sacred or normative texts of Judaism. However, monotheism has not always been followed in practice. The Jewish Bible (<A href="/wiki/Tanakh" class="mw-redirect" title="Tanakh">Tanakh</A>) records and repeatedly condemns the widespread worship of other gods in <A href="/wiki/Ancient_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="Ancient Israel">ancient Israel</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-mechon-mamre_33-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-mechon-mamre-33">[33]</A></SUP> In the Greco-Roman era, many different interpretations of monotheism existed in Judaism, including the interpretations that gave rise to Christianity.<SUP id="cite_ref-The_Jewish_roots_of_Christological_monotheism:_papers_from_the_St._Andrews_conference_on_the_historical_origins_of_the_worship_of_Jesus_34-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-The_Jewish_roots_of_Christological_monotheism:_papers_from_the_St._Andrews_conference_on_the_historical_origins_of_the_worship_of_Jesus-34">[34]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Moreover, some have argued that Judaism is a non-creedal religion that does not require one to believe in God.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (February 2016)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> For some, observance of Jewish law is more important than belief in God <I>per se</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-jovanovich_35-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-jovanovich-35">[35]</A></SUP> In modern times, some liberal Jewish movements do not accept the existence of a personified deity active in history.<SUP id="cite_ref-movements_36-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-movements-36">[36]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-37">[37]</A></SUP> The debate about whether one can speak of authentic or normative Judaism is not only a debate among religious Jews but also among historians.<SUP id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-38">[38]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Core_tenets">Core tenets</SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Jewish_principles_of_faith" title="Jewish principles of faith">Jewish principles of faith</A></DIV>
<DIV class="quotebox pullquote floatright" style="width:35%; ;"><STYLE data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r856303512">.mw-parser-output .quotebox{background-color:#F9F9F9;border:1px solid #aaa;box-sizing:border-box;padding:10px;font-size:88%}.mw-parser-output .quotebox.floatleft{margin:0.5em 1.4em 0.8em 0}.mw-parser-output .quotebox.floatright{margin:0.5em 0 0.8em 1.4em}.mw-parser-output .quotebox.centered{margin:0.5em auto 0.8em auto}.mw-parser-output .quotebox.floatleft p,.mw-parser-output .quotebox.floatright p{font-style:inherit}.mw-parser-output .quotebox-title{background-color:#F9F9F9;text-align:center;font-size:larger;font-weight:bold}.mw-parser-output .quotebox-quote.quoted:before{font-family:"Times New Roman",serif;font-weight:bold;font-size:large;color:gray;content:" “ ";vertical-align:-45%;line-height:0}.mw-parser-output .quotebox-quote.quoted:after{font-family:"Times New Roman",serif;font-weight:bold;font-size:large;color:gray;content:" ” ";line-height:0}.mw-parser-output .quotebox .left-aligned{text-align:left}.mw-parser-output .quotebox .right-aligned{text-align:right}.mw-parser-output .quotebox .center-aligned{text-align:center}.mw-parser-output .quotebox cite{display:block;font-style:normal}@media screen and (max-width:360px){.mw-parser-output .quotebox{min-width:100%;margin:0 0 0.8em!important;float:none!important}}</STYLE>
<DIV class="quotebox-quote left-aligned" style="">13 Principles of Faith:
<OL><LI>I believe with perfect faith that the Creator, Blessed be His Name, is the Creator and Guide of everything that has been created; He alone has made, does make, and will make all things.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that the Creator, Blessed be His Name, is One, and that there is no unity in any manner like His, and that He alone is our God, who was, and is, and will be.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that the Creator, Blessed be His Name, has no body, and that He is free from all the properties of matter, and that there can be no (physical) comparison to Him whatsoever.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that the Creator, Blessed be His Name, is the first and the last.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that to the Creator, Blessed be His Name, and to Him alone, it is right to pray, and that it is not right to pray to any being besides Him.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that all the words of the prophets are true.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that the prophecy of Moses our teacher, <A href="/wiki/Honorifics_for_the_dead_in_Judaism#Peace_be_upon_him/her" title="Honorifics for the dead in Judaism">peace be upon him</A>, was true, and that he was the chief of the prophets, both those who preceded him and those who followed him.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that the entire Torah that is now in our possession is the same that was given to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that this Torah will not be exchanged, and that there will never be any other Torah from the Creator, Blessed be His Name.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that the Creator, Blessed be His Name, knows all the deeds of human beings and all their thoughts, as it is written, "Who fashioned the hearts of them all, Who comprehends all their actions" (<A href="/wiki/Psalms" title="Psalms">Psalms</A> 33:15).</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that the Creator, Blessed be His Name, rewards those who keep His commandments and punishes those that transgress them.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith in the coming of the <A href="/wiki/Jewish_messianism" class="mw-redirect" title="Jewish messianism">Messiah</A>; and even though he may tarry, nonetheless, I wait every day for his coming.</LI>
<LI>I believe with perfect faith that there will be a revival of the dead at the time when it shall please the Creator, Blessed be His name, and His mention shall be exalted for ever and ever.</LI></OL></DIV>
<P><CITE class="left-aligned" style="">—<A href="/wiki/Maimonides" title="Maimonides">Maimonides</A></CITE>
</P>
</DIV>
<P>Scholars throughout <A href="/wiki/Jewish_history" title="Jewish history">Jewish history</A> have proposed numerous formulations of Judaism's core tenets, all of which have met with criticism.<SUP id="cite_ref-montpelier_39-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-montpelier-39">[39]</A></SUP> The most popular formulation is <A href="/wiki/Maimonides" title="Maimonides">Maimonides</A>' <A href="/wiki/13_principles_of_faith" class="mw-redirect" title="13 principles of faith">thirteen principles of faith</A>, developed in the 12th century. According to Maimonides, any Jew who rejects even one of these principles would be considered an apostate and a heretic.<SUP id="cite_ref-mesora_40-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-mesora-40">[40]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Maimonides,_13_Principles_of_Faith_41-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Maimonides,_13_Principles_of_Faith-41">[41]</A></SUP> Jewish scholars have held points of view diverging in various ways from Maimonides' principles.<SUP id="cite_ref-learning_42-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-learning-42">[42]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-The_JPS_guide_to_Jewish_traditions_43-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-The_JPS_guide_to_Jewish_traditions-43">[43]</A></SUP>
</P><P>In Maimonides' time, his list of tenets was criticized by <A href="/wiki/Hasdai_Crescas" title="Hasdai Crescas">Hasdai Crescas</A> and <A href="/wiki/Joseph_Albo" title="Joseph Albo">Joseph Albo</A>. Albo and <A href="/wiki/Abraham_ben_David" title="Abraham ben David">the Raavad</A> argued that Maimonides' principles contained too many items that, while true, were not fundamentals of the faith.
</P><P>Along these lines, the ancient historian <A href="/wiki/Josephus" title="Josephus">Josephus</A> emphasized practices and observances rather than religious beliefs, associating <A href="/wiki/Apostasy" title="Apostasy">apostasy</A> with a failure to observe Jewish law and maintaining that the requirements for conversion to Judaism included <A href="/wiki/Circumcision" title="Circumcision">circumcision</A> and adherence to traditional customs. Maimonides' principles were largely ignored over the next few centuries.<SUP id="cite_ref-medieval_44-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-medieval-44">[44]</A></SUP> Later, two poetic restatements of these principles ("<I><A href="/wiki/Ani_Ma%27amin" title="Ani Ma'amin">Ani Ma'amin</A></I>" and "<I><A href="/wiki/Yigdal" title="Yigdal">Yigdal</A></I>") became integrated into many Jewish liturgies,<SUP id="cite_ref-The_Thirteen_Principles_of_the_Jewish_Faith_45-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-The_Thirteen_Principles_of_the_Jewish_Faith-45">[45]</A></SUP> leading to their eventual near-universal acceptance.<SUP id="cite_ref-What_Do_Jews_Believe?_46-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-What_Do_Jews_Believe?-46">[46]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-traditions_47-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-traditions-47">[47]</A></SUP>
</P><P>In modern times, Judaism lacks a centralized authority that would dictate an exact religious dogma.<SUP id="cite_ref-religiousleadership_14-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-religiousleadership-14">[14]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-judaism101beliefs_48-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-judaism101beliefs-48">[48]</A></SUP> Because of this, many different variations on the basic beliefs are considered within the scope of Judaism.<SUP id="cite_ref-learning_42-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-learning-42">[42]</A></SUP> Even so, all <A href="/wiki/Jewish_religious_movements" title="Jewish religious movements">Jewish religious movements</A> are, to a greater or lesser extent, based on the principles of the <A href="/wiki/Hebrew_Bible" title="Hebrew Bible">Hebrew Bible</A> and various commentaries such as the <A href="/wiki/Talmud" title="Talmud">Talmud</A> and <A href="/wiki/Midrash" title="Midrash">Midrash</A>. Judaism also universally recognizes the Biblical <A href="/wiki/Covenant_(biblical)" title="Covenant (biblical)">Covenant</A> between God and the <A href="/wiki/Patriarchs_(Bible)" title="Patriarchs (Bible)">Patriarch</A> <A href="/wiki/Abraham" title="Abraham">Abraham</A> as well as the additional aspects of the Covenant revealed to <A href="/wiki/Moses" title="Moses">Moses</A>, who is considered Judaism's greatest <A href="/wiki/Prophet" title="Prophet">prophet</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-learning_42-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-learning-42">[42]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-ontario_49-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ontario-49">[49]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-patriarchscovenant_50-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-patriarchscovenant-50">[50]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-How_Do_You_Know_the_Exodus_Really_Happened?_51-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-How_Do_You_Know_the_Exodus_Really_Happened?-51">[51]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-sacredtexts_52-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-sacredtexts-52">[52]</A></SUP> In the <A href="/wiki/Mishnah" title="Mishnah">Mishnah</A>, a core text of <A href="/wiki/Rabbinic_Judaism" title="Rabbinic Judaism">Rabbinic Judaism</A>, acceptance of the Divine origins of this covenant is considered an essential aspect of Judaism and those who reject the Covenant forfeit their share in the <A href="/wiki/World_to_Come" class="mw-redirect" title="World to Come">World to Come</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-sacred-texts_53-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-sacred-texts-53">[53]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Establishing the core tenets of Judaism in the modern era is even more difficult, given the number and diversity of the contemporary <A href="/wiki/Jewish_religious_movements" title="Jewish religious movements">Jewish denominations</A>. Even if to restrict the problem to the most influential intellectual trends of the nineteenth and twentieth century, the matter remains complicated. Thus for instance, <A href="/wiki/Joseph_B._Soloveitchik" title="Joseph B. Soloveitchik">Joseph Soloveitchik's</A> (associated with the <A href="/wiki/Modern_Orthodox_Judaism" title="Modern Orthodox Judaism">Modern Orthodox movement</A>) answer to modernity is constituted upon the identification of Judaism with following the <A href="/wiki/Halakha" title="Halakha">halakha</A> whereas its ultimate goal is to bring the holiness down to the world. <A href="/wiki/Mordecai_Kaplan" title="Mordecai Kaplan">Mordecai Kaplan</A>, the founder of the <A href="/wiki/Reconstructionist_Judaism" title="Reconstructionist Judaism">Reconstructionist Judaism</A>, abandons the idea of religion for the sake of identifying Judaism with <A href="/wiki/Civilization" title="Civilization">civilization</A> and by means of the latter term and secular translation of the core ideas, he tries to embrace as many Jewish denominations as possible. In turn, <A href="/wiki/Solomon_Schechter" title="Solomon Schechter">Solomon Schechter</A>'s <A href="/wiki/Conservative_Judaism" title="Conservative Judaism">Conservative Judaism</A> was identical with the tradition understood as the interpretation of Torah, in itself being the history of the constant updates and adjustment of the Law performed by means of the creative interpretation. Finally, <A href="/wiki/David_Philipson" title="David Philipson">David Philipson</A> draws the outlines of the <A href="/wiki/Reform_Judaism" title="Reform Judaism">Reform movement</A> in Judaism by opposing it to the strict and traditional rabbinical approach and thus comes to the conclusions similar to that of the Conservative movement.<SUP id="cite_ref-54" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-54">[54]</A></SUP>
</P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Jewish_legal_literature">Jewish legal literature</SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Halakha" title="Halakha">Halakha</A></DIV>
<P>The basis of Jewish law and tradition (halakha) is the <A href="/wiki/Torah" title="Torah">Torah</A> (also known as the <A href="/wiki/Pentateuch" class="mw-redirect" title="Pentateuch">Pentateuch</A> or the Five Books of Moses). According to rabbinic tradition, there are <A href="/wiki/613_mitzvot" class="mw-redirect" title="613 mitzvot">613 commandments</A> in the Torah. Some of these laws are directed only to men or to women, some only to the ancient priestly groups, the <A href="/wiki/Kohen" title="Kohen">Kohanim</A> and <A href="/wiki/Levite" title="Levite">Leviyim</A> (members of the tribe of <A href="/wiki/Levi" title="Levi">Levi</A>), some only to farmers within the <A href="/wiki/Land_of_Israel" title="Land of Israel">Land of Israel</A>. Many laws were only applicable when the <A href="/wiki/Temple_in_Jerusalem" title="Temple in Jerusalem">Temple in Jerusalem</A> existed, and only 369 of these commandments are still applicable today.<SUP id="cite_ref-56" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-56">[56]</A></SUP>
</P><P>While there have been Jewish groups whose beliefs were based on the written text of the Torah alone (e.g., the <A href="/wiki/Sadducees" title="Sadducees">Sadducees</A>, and the <A href="/wiki/Karaite_Judaism" title="Karaite Judaism">Karaites</A>), most Jews believe in the <A href="/wiki/Oral_law#Oral_law_in_Judaism" title="Oral law">oral law</A>. These oral traditions were transmitted by the <A href="/wiki/Pharisees" title="Pharisees">Pharisee</A> school of thought of ancient Judaism and were later recorded in written form and expanded upon by the rabbis.
</P><P>According to Rabbinical Jewish tradition, God gave both the Written Law (the <A href="/wiki/Torah" title="Torah">Torah</A>) and the <A href="/wiki/Oral_law" title="Oral law">Oral law</A> to Moses on <A href="/wiki/Biblical_Mount_Sinai" title="Biblical Mount Sinai">Mount Sinai</A>. The Oral law is the oral tradition as relayed by God to Moses and from him, transmitted and taught to the sages (<A href="/wiki/Rabbi" title="Rabbi">rabbinic</A> leaders) of each subsequent generation.
</P><P>For centuries, the Torah appeared only as a written text transmitted in parallel with the oral tradition. Fearing that the oral teachings might be forgotten, Rabbi <A href="/wiki/Judah_haNasi" class="mw-redirect" title="Judah haNasi">Judah haNasi</A> undertook the mission of consolidating the various opinions into one body of law which became known as the <I>Mishnah</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-57">[57]</A></SUP>
</P><P>The Mishnah consists of 63 tractates codifying Jewish law, which are the basis of the <I>Talmud.</I> According to <A href="/wiki/Abraham_ben_David" title="Abraham ben David">Abraham ben David</A>, the <I><A href="/wiki/Mishnah" title="Mishnah">Mishnah</A></I> was compiled by Rabbi <A href="/wiki/Judah_the_Prince" class="mw-redirect" title="Judah the Prince">Judah haNasi</A> after the destruction of Jerusalem, in <A href="/wiki/Anno_mundi" class="mw-redirect" title="Anno mundi">anno mundi</A> 3949, which corresponds to 189 CE.<SUP id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-58">[58]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Over the next four centuries, the Mishnah underwent discussion and debate in both of the world's major Jewish communities (in Israel and <A href="/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Iraq" title="History of the Jews in Iraq">Babylonia</A>). The commentaries from each of these communities were eventually compiled into the two <A href="/wiki/Talmud" title="Talmud">Talmuds</A>, the Jerusalem Talmud (<I>Talmud Yerushalmi</I>) and the Babylonian Talmud (<I>Talmud Bavli</I>). These have been further expounded by commentaries of various Torah scholars during the ages.
</P><P>In the text of the Torah, many words are left undefined and many procedures are mentioned without explanation or instructions. Such phenomena are sometimes offered to validate the viewpoint that the Written Law has always been transmitted with a parallel oral tradition, illustrating the assumption that the reader is already familiar with the details from other, i.e., oral, sources.<SUP id="cite_ref-59" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-59">[59]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Halakha, the rabbinic Jewish way of life, then, is based on a combined reading of the Torah, and the oral tradition—the Mishnah, the halakhic <A href="/wiki/Midrash" title="Midrash">Midrash</A>, the Talmud and its commentaries. The Halakha has developed slowly, through a precedent-based system. The literature of questions to rabbis, and their considered answers, is referred to as <A href="/wiki/Responsa" title="Responsa">responsa</A> (in <A href="/wiki/Hebrew_language" title="Hebrew language">Hebrew</A>, <I>Sheelot U-Teshuvot</I>.) Over time, as practices develop, codes of Jewish law are written that are based on the responsa; the most important code, the <A href="/wiki/Shulchan_Aruch" title="Shulchan Aruch">Shulchan Aruch</A>, largely determines Orthodox religious practice today.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Jewish_philosophy">Jewish philosophy</SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Jewish_philosophy" title="Jewish philosophy">Jewish philosophy</A></DIV>
<P>Jewish philosophy refers to the conjunction between serious study of philosophy and Jewish theology. Major Jewish philosophers include <A href="/wiki/Solomon_ibn_Gabirol" title="Solomon ibn Gabirol">Solomon ibn Gabirol</A>, <A href="/wiki/Saadia_Gaon" title="Saadia Gaon">Saadia Gaon</A>, <A href="/wiki/Judah_Halevi" title="Judah Halevi">Judah Halevi</A>, <A href="/wiki/Maimonides" title="Maimonides">Maimonides</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Gersonides" title="Gersonides">Gersonides</A>. Major changes occurred in response to the <A href="/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment" title="Age of Enlightenment">Enlightenment</A> (late 18th to early 19th century) leading to the post-Enlightenment Jewish philosophers. Modern Jewish philosophy consists of both Orthodox and non-Orthodox oriented philosophy. Notable among Orthodox Jewish philosophers are <A href="/wiki/Eliyahu_Eliezer_Dessler" title="Eliyahu Eliezer Dessler">Eliyahu Eliezer Dessler</A>, <A href="/wiki/Joseph_B._Soloveitchik" title="Joseph B. Soloveitchik">Joseph B. Soloveitchik</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Yitzchok_Hutner" title="Yitzchok Hutner">Yitzchok Hutner</A>. Well-known non-Orthodox Jewish philosophers include <A href="/wiki/Martin_Buber" title="Martin Buber">Martin Buber</A>, <A href="/wiki/Franz_Rosenzweig" title="Franz Rosenzweig">Franz Rosenzweig</A>, <A href="/wiki/Mordecai_Kaplan" title="Mordecai Kaplan">Mordecai Kaplan</A>, <A href="/wiki/Abraham_Joshua_Heschel" title="Abraham Joshua Heschel">Abraham Joshua Heschel</A>, <A href="/wiki/Will_Herberg" title="Will Herberg">Will Herberg</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Emmanuel_L%C3%A9vinas" class="mw-redirect" title="Emmanuel Lévinas">Emmanuel Lévinas</A>.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Rabbinic_hermeneutics">Rabbinic hermeneutics</SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="quotebox pullquote floatright" style="width:35%; ;"><LINK rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r856303512" />
<DIV class="quotebox-quote left-aligned" style="">13 Principles of Hermeneutics:
<OL><LI>A law that operates under certain conditions will surely be operative in other situations where the same conditions are present in a more acute form</LI>
<LI>A law operating in one situation will also be operative in another situation if the text characterizes both situations in identical terms.</LI>
<LI>A law that clearly expresses the purpose it was meant to serve will also apply to other situations where the identical purpose may be served.</LI>
<LI>When a general rule is followed by illustrative particulars, only those particulars are to be embraced by it.</LI>
<LI>A law that begins with specifying particular cases, and then proceeds to an all-embracing generalization, is to be applied to particulars cases not specified but logically falling into the same generalization.</LI>
