<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Han_Lue">Han Lue</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section: Han Lue">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Han_Lue" title="Han Lue">Han Lue</A></DIV>
<P><SPAN id="Han_Seoul-Oh"></SPAN><SPAN id="Han_Lue"></SPAN> <B>Han Lue</B> (<A href="/wiki/Chinese_language" title="Chinese language">Chinese</A>: <SPAN lang="zh">韓哥</SPAN> <I>Hán Gē</I>), also known by the alias <B>Han Seoul-Oh</B><SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> is an aloof former gang member and street racer, a member of Dominic's crew in <I><A href="/wiki/Fast_%26_Furious_(2009_film)" title="Fast & Furious (2009 film)">Fast & Furious</A></I>, <I><A href="/wiki/Fast_Five" title="Fast Five">Fast Five</A></I> and <I><A href="/wiki/Fast_%26_Furious_6" title="Fast & Furious 6">Fast & Furious 6</A></I>, and Sean Boswell's mentor and friend in <I><A href="/wiki/The_Fast_and_the_Furious:_Tokyo_Drift" title="The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift">The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift</A></I>.</P>
<P>Chronologically, in <I>Fast & Furious</I> he steals fuel tankers with Dominic, while in <I>Fast Five</I> he joins Dom and Brian's heist team as a precision driver and a "chameleon". While planning the heist in <I>Fast Five</I>, Gisele attributes Han's constant need to occupy his hands to him being a former smoker. After the heist, Han and Gisele start a relationship and travel together through Europe, starting with <A href="/wiki/Berlin" title="Berlin">Berlin</A>. They assist Dom and his crew in taking down Owen Shaw.</P>
<P>In <I>Tokyo Drift</I>, Han hires Sean Boswell as a delivery driver and teaches him how to race against Takashi. During a climatic getaway, a silver Mercedes crashes into his car, causing it to flip over and then explode. In the post-credits scene of <I>Fast & Furious 6</I>, Deckard Shaw (portrayed by Jason Statham) is revealed to have driven the Mercedes after tracking the street racers on a police radio. Dominic goes to Japan to retrieve his body, he and his crew have a funeral for him in <I>Furious 7</I>.</P>
<P>Han is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Sung_Kang" title="Sung Kang">Sung Kang</A>. In the <I>Fast & Furious 6</I> production notes, his last name is listed as Lue,<SUP id="cite_ref-prod_notes_6_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-prod_notes_6-10">[10]</A></SUP> while in <I>Furious 7</I>, his name appears in the DSS files as Han Seoul-Oh, a nod to <A href="/wiki/Han_Solo" title="Han Solo">Han Solo</A> from <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars" title="Star Wars">Star Wars</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP> Director <A href="/wiki/Justin_Lin" title="Justin Lin">Justin Lin</A> has stated that Seoul-Oh is a fake ID.<SUP id="cite_ref-fake_id_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-fake_id-12">[12]</A></SUP></P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Gisele_Yashar">Gisele Yashar</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section: Gisele Yashar">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Gisele_Yashar" title="Gisele Yashar">Gisele Yashar</A></DIV>
<P><B>Gisele</B> was the liaison for Braga who developed feelings for Dominic, who does not reciprocate. She warns him of potential danger that awaits him after delivering Braga's heroin across the border. Dominic saves her life in the chaos surrounding the heroin exchange meant as a trap for Braga. She returns the favor by giving the location of Braga's hideout in Mexico. Gisele re-appears alongside Dominic's crew assisting him and Brian in their heist as their weapons expert, where it is revealed that she is a former <A href="/wiki/Mossad" title="Mossad">Mossad</A> agent. She and Han eventually start a relationship and take off to Europe together after the heist in Rio de Janeiro.</P>
<P>Gisele reappears in <I>Fast & Furious 6</I>, along with Han, and helps Dom and the gang take on a rival gang of hijacking, car criminals. In a <A href="/wiki/Running_gag" title="Running gag">running gag</A>, she takes pride in her ability to accomplish objectives on her own where men would fail, that is, using her attractiveness to infiltrate Herman Reyes's bodyguards and Owen Shaw's security. She falls from the roof of an airborne car to her death while shooting the man who would have shot Han. Her last name in the sixth film's production notes is Harabo,<SUP id="cite_ref-prod_notes_6_10-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-prod_notes_6-10">[10]</A></SUP> while her file in the fifth film presents it as Yashar. However, Lin has said that, like Han, she was not given a last name.<SUP id="cite_ref-fake_id_12-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-fake_id-12">[12]</A></SUP> She is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Gal_Gadot" title="Gal Gadot">Gal Gadot</A>.</P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Luke_Hobbs">Luke Hobbs</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section: Luke Hobbs">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P><B>Agent Luke Hobbs</B> is a <A href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</A> <A href="/wiki/Diplomatic_Security_Service" title="Diplomatic Security Service">Diplomatic Security Service</A> (DSS) agent and <A href="/wiki/Bounty_hunter" title="Bounty hunter">bounty hunter</A>.</P>
<P>In <I>Fast Five</I>, he is trying to bring down Toretto's crew which is his number one priority when he believes that Toretto's crew killed the DEA agents in the train. After outsmarting Toretto and ambushing him, Mia, Brian, and Vince in their base, he takes them into custody to take back to the United States for prosecution. When his team is killed in an ambush by Hernan Reyes en route to the airport to take the fugitives home, he joins Toretto's team to steal Reyes' money, and personally kills a badly-injured Reyes, avenging his team. Faced with the chance to arrest the team after Reyes' death, he instead offers them a 24-hour head start to get to safety before he will start the search again.</P>
<P>In <I>Fast & Furious 6</I>, he comes to Toretto for help to bring down Owen Shaw, the leader of an international crime syndicate, recognizing that Toretto's team are the best candidates to match Shaw's own skills. He partners up with DSS Agent, Riley Hicks, who turns out to be a double agent who double crossed Hobbs and Toretto's team. While Riley and Letty are fighting with each other in the airplane, Hobbs tosses a harpoon to Letty, who in return uses it to impale Riley off the airplane, killing her on impact. After the mission is completed, Hobbs grants amnesty to Toretto and his team, the two men publicly disagreeing on which of them was in charge during that mission but privately acknowledging that they trust each other.</P>
<P>In <I>Furious 7</I>, Shaw's older brother, Deckard, breaks into Hobbs' DSS office to extract profiles of Dom's crew. After revealing his identity, Shaw engages Hobbs in a fight and later escapes by detonating a bomb that sends Hobbs and his partner Elena, flying out of a window and onto a car parked below. He is injured by the fall, and rushed to the hospital by Elena. Dom later visits Hobbs in the hospital, where he learns that Shaw is a rogue British Special Forces assassin seeking to avenge his brother, Owen. During the final climactic scene, Hobbs, seeing that the team is being hunted by a Predator UAV drone, leaves the hospital- even breaking his own cast- and destroys the UAV drone by ramming it with an ambulance. Later, Hobbs plays a part in taking down Jakande when he shoots a belt of grenades that was slung onto Jakande's chopper by Toretto destroying the helicopter and killing Jakande. He later imprisons Shaw in a maximum security prison.</P>
<P>In <I>The Fate of the Furious</I>, Hobbs initially appears coaching his daughter Samantha's sports team, before being approached by a government contact to conduct an off-the-books mission to retrieve an EMP device from a facility in Berlin, and warned that he will be acting unofficially and will face arrest if captured. Although he claims the device with the aid of Dom's team, he is captured after Dom steals the device himself due to the blackmail of cyber-terrorist Cipher, resulting in Hobbs being sent to the same prison as Shaw. However, he is swiftly 'released' by Mr. Nobody to help Dom's team track down Dom and Cipher, learning that she is seeking to gain control of nuclear launch codes to appoint herself to a position of power over the world. Despite the odds against them, Hobbs and Dom's team manage to track Cipher while Dom sets plans in motion to escape her blackmail himself, culminating in the destruction of the converted Russian nuclear submarine Cipher was planning to use to launch her stolen missiles. Although offered reinstatement after the threat is over, Hobbs decides to remain officially retired to spend more time with his daughter and his new "family", being Dom's team.</P>
<P>Luke Hobbs is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Dwayne_Johnson" title="Dwayne Johnson">Dwayne Johnson</A>.</P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="The_Fast_and_the_Furious"><I>The Fast and the Furious</I></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=14" title="Edit section: The Fast and the Furious">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Vince">Vince</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=15" title="Edit section: Vince">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Vince</B> is a childhood friend and street racer under Dominic Toretto. He opposed O'Conner's inclusion into Dominic's crew especially since his sister favored O'Conner over him. During <A href="/wiki/Race_Wars" class="mw-redirect" title="Race Wars">Race Wars</A>, Johnny Tran blames Dominic for the SWAT forces that came into his house, disrespecting his whole family for being narced out by someone and they get into a fight. Vince then leads Dominic away telling him to chill out. Near the end of the first film, Vince is seriously injured when he is shot by a trucker whose shipments he attempted to hijack. He recovers from his injuries, escapes from the hospital, and goes to Rio de Janeiro. He is not present or mentioned in <I>Fast & Furious</I>, but can be seen in a picture with Letty and Dominic at Letty's funeral, although his face is not clear. Vince re-appears in <I>Fast Five</I> living in the favelas of Rio de Janeiro with his wife, Rosa and infant son, Nico (who is named after Dominic). He tries to steal one of three cars on a train he attempted to hijack in an earlier mission, but it goes awry. Dominic's trust in his longtime friend is strained for a time when he was caught hiding information from the team, but ultimately regains that trust after saving Mia from being killed and joins Dominic's heist team. Before the crew could perform their heist on Reyes, he is later captured by Hobbs along with Dominic, Brian and Mia, but is fatally wounded while saving the cop from Zizi's ambush on the convoy. Before he dies, Dominic promises Vince that he will watch over Rosa and Nico. After the successful heist on Reyes, Dominic gives Vince's share to Rosa and Nico, promising to visit soon. Vince is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Matt_Schulze_(actor)" class="mw-redirect" title="Matt Schulze (actor)">Matt Schulze</A>.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Jesse">Jesse</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=17" title="Edit section: Jesse">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Jesse</B> is a street racer and the brains of Dominic's operations, and he is a wheelman in the heists. Jesse admits to having <A href="/wiki/Attention_Deficit_Disorder" class="mw-redirect" title="Attention Deficit Disorder">ADD</A> and is shown often stuttering in his speeches and acting very nervous. Despite this setback, he is the <A href="/wiki/Computer_nerd" class="mw-redirect" title="Computer nerd">computer nerd</A> of the group as he is responsible for creating the designs, doing background checks on people, and hacking the engine characteristics of Toretto's race vehicles with precise calculations (a potential characteristic of those with ADD as they may at times have high IQs). He is somewhat reckless and irresponsible as he later raced Johnny Tran for <A href="/wiki/Pink_slip_(auto)" class="mw-redirect" title="Pink slip (auto)">pink slips</A> against the wishes of both Brian and Toretto who warned him that Tran had over $100,000 under the hood of his vehicle. This proved to be true as Jesse lost to Tran, later driving off and escaping his loss. An enraged Tran and an accomplice later pull a drive-by shooting at Toretto's house missing everyone but Jesse, who gets hit, killing him instantly. Brian and Dominic chase after Tran, shooting him dead and avenging Jesse's death. Jesse is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Chad_Lindberg" title="Chad Lindberg">Chad Lindberg</A>.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Hector">Hector</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=18" title="Edit section: Hector">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Hector</B> is a former street racer and organizer. He is a friend to both Dominic and Brian. In the first movie, Hector organizes and attends the original race in which Dominic and Brian participate, which is later interrupted by the police; he has a last name, but claims he "can't pronounce it". Brian begins investigating Hector and Tran's activities and is convinced that Tran is behind the hijackings, believing his suspicions are founded when he discovers an unusual purchase made by Hector in The Racer's Edge (the parts shop where Brian works). Hector later throws a party at El Gato Negro, but his whereabouts after this party are unknown. Hector returns in <I><A href="/wiki/Furious_7" title="Furious 7">Furious 7</A></I>, where he takes an accidental punch from Letty at the Race Wars after she has a traumatic flashback when the girl fans from the race wars pick on her, but Hector is not angry; Dominic jokes that he "never could take a punch". Hector is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Noel_Gugliemi" title="Noel Gugliemi">Noel Gugliemi</A>.</P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Fast_Five"><I>Fast Five</I></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=33" title="Edit section: Fast Five">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Elena_Neves">Elena Neves</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=34" title="Edit section: Elena Neves">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Officer Elena Neves</B> was a member of the Rio military police (PMERJ) assigned to Hobbs' DSS team to track down Dom and Brian for killing three DEA agents. She was chosen because of her knowledge of the favelas and the fact that she was the only incorruptible officer. Her police officer husband's death had motivated her to join the force, preventing her from being bribed by Reyes like the rest of the police.</P>
<P>When Dom saved her from a shootout in the favelas orchestrated by Reyes to prevent the theft of his drug money, she starts to believe they are innocent of killing the DEA agents. Elena later assisted Hobbs in aiding Dom and Brian in stealing Hernan Reyes cash supply and started a relationship with Dom after the job is done. Upon discovering that Dom's wife, Letty, was still alive and currently working for Owen Shaw, Elena encouraged Dom to find her by joining Hobbs. She assisted Mia when Shaw's crew attacks them and takes care of Jack during Mia's kidnapping.</P>
<P>After Letty was successfully convinced to rejoin Dom, Elena joined the DSS as Hobbs' new partner to let the couple live together. Elena was present at the DSS HQ to check on Hobbs, and as she headed home, Hobbs gave her a letter of recommendation for her request to join Interpol. When Deckard Shaw breaks into the HQ to hack Hobbs computer to find out who crippled his brother, she assist Hobbs in attempt to bring him. Hobbs is left injured, so Elena informs Dom to visit him as she takes care of Hobbs's daughter, Samantha.</P>
<P>She was later kidnapped by Cipher in order to blackmail Dom into abandoning his family and retrieve nuclear launch codes, after it was revealed that Dom had fathered a child with Elena in Letty's absence. After failing to retrieve the launch codes from Letty after an encounter in New York City, Dom returned to the base of operations to find Elena tied to a chair, with Cipher holding Dom's son. As punishment for Dom being unable to shoot Letty to retrieve the launch codes, Cipher ordered one of her henchmen, Rhodes, to execute Elena by shooting her head and body in cold blood. Dom later avenges Elena's death by killing Rhodes and promises to her that their son will always be safe. She is a main character in Fast Five and a supporting character in Fast & Furious 6, Furious 7 and The Fate of the Furious.</P>
<P>Despite the fact she was a Rio police officer, she didn't work for the regular Rio de Janeiro police department because they were owned by the corrupt Hernan Reyes, shown by the fact that she takes out one of the officers in the climax of the movie. Elena is portrayed by Elsa Pataky.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Ramsey">Ramsey</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=36" title="Edit section: Ramsey">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Ramsey</B> is a British computer hacker and the creator of God's Eye, a program capable of tracking a specific person through digital services and coveted by mercenary Mose Jakande. Ramsey was a prisoner of Jakande, until Dom and his crew rescue her. Subsequently, she assists Dom and his crew in collecting the God's Eye, stating that she trusts them more than her previous captors as the team is clearly brought together by respect and trust rather than the fear that kept her captors loyal. When she makes contact with her associate Safar, she learns that the hard drive has been sold away to a Jordanian prince despite her previous warning to keep it safe. When they lose the program to Jakande, Ramsey helps the crew to hack and regain control of it, then shuts it down.</P>
<P>Ramsey returns in <I>The Fate of the Furious</I>, having joined Dom's team as secondary technical advisor to Tej. Due to being the newest member, she was the one who doubted Dom the most after his betrayal. Throughout the film, she is constantly in the middle of Roman and Tej's respective advances towards her: after Cipher is defeated, she admits she likes both of them but would only choose one of them if they figured out what her last name is. Ramsey is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Nathalie_Emmanuel" title="Nathalie Emmanuel">Nathalie Emmanuel</A>.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Johnny_Tran">Johnny Tran</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=43" title="Edit section: Johnny Tran">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Johnny Tran</B> is the head of an opposing race crew to Dominic Toretto's, and implied to be involved in some form of organized crime. He is first seen blowing up Brian O'Conner's car, originally owned by Sgt. Tanner, with his gang's machine guns near the beginning of the film. It is soon revealed that their business deal went sour when Johnny found his sister sleeping with Dominic. Later, as O'Conner and Dominic spy on Tran at his garage, he is seen with his accomplice (and cousin) Lance interrogating a man named Ted Gassner regarding engines in his vehicles, which is also where they spot several boxes of merchandise in his garage (the kind being robbed in the film from truckers). This leads Brian O'Conner to organize a large SWAT assault team to invade Tran's house, only to find a few minor weapons charges and other minor issues. Tran gets slapped by his father for this and learned he destroyed Sgt. Tanner's car and pays $80,000 of the car. After being bailed out, Tran is later seen at the Race Wars, racing Jesse for pink slips. Both Dominic and Brian warn Jesse about Tran's vehicle having over $100,000 worth of upgrades, but Jesse ignores them and races Tran anyway. After Tran wins, he then confronts Dominic, accusing him of the SWAT team invasion of his home, which disrespected him in front of his entire family (unaware that the man responsible, Brian O'Conner, is right there in front of him; he soon becomes aware of this near the end). Dominic then delivers a right hook to Tran's face, and the two men scuffle on the ground before being broken up by the crowd. After Tran and Lance kill Jesse in a drive-by shooting while driving motorcycles, Brian and Dominic chase after the two, ending with Brian shooting Tran in the side while Tran is fleeing on his motorcycle, sending Tran head-first into a curbside, breaking his neck. Johnny Tran is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Rick_Yune" title="Rick Yune">Rick Yune</A>.</P>

It is unknown what happened to him after the race, but in a deleted scene, he was apprehended by his uncle's henchmen. During a botched sting operation, it is revealed that "Campos" is Arturo Braga himself and he escapes to Mexico. Brian and Dominic capture him and bring him back to the USA. Arturo Braga is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/John_Ortiz" title="John Ortiz">John Ortiz</A>. He returns making a cameo appearance in the sixth film being in jail having a connection with Shaw and O'Conner returns in the U.S. as a prisoner to gain access to Braga, who discloses how Letty survived the explosion that was thought to have killed her.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Hernan_Reyes">Hernan Reyes</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=58" title="Edit section: Hernan Reyes">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Hernan Reyes</B> is a corrupt businessman and ruthless Brazilian drug lord who provides resources to the <A href="/wiki/Favela" title="Favela">favelas</A> in Rio de Janeiro to gain control over them. He also has most of the Rio <A href="/wiki/Civil_Police_of_Rio_de_Janeiro_State" title="Civil Police of Rio de Janeiro State">civil</A> and <A href="/wiki/Military_Police_of_Rio_de_Janeiro_State" title="Military Police of Rio de Janeiro State">military</A> police and local division of the <A href="/wiki/Federal_Highway_Police" title="Federal Highway Police">Brazilian federal highway police (PRF)</A> on his payroll, which allows him to hide his money inside a vault in their evidence room. He wants Toretto and O'Conner dead when they plot to steal his money. He has Hobbs' team and Vince killed on his orders, forcing a vengeful Hobbs to join Toretto. After, Dom crashed the vault to Reyes in a car accident, leaving Hernan badly injured. Reyes was subsequently shot and killed by Hobbs in revenge for murdering Hobbs' team and Vince, ending his reign of terror. Hernan Reyes is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Joaquim_de_Almeida" title="Joaquim de Almeida">Joaquim de Almeida</A>.</P>

<P><B>Zizi</B> is a lead henchman for Hernan Reyes. He enlists Vince, who brings Brian, Mia, and Dominic, to help him steal three confiscated cars off a moving train. However, when Mia drives the GT40 away from the intended destination, he turns on Dominic and Brian, shooting the DEA agents in the process. He also leads the ambush on Hobbs' convoy, killing most of Hobbs' team before his hit squad is wiped out by Toretto, Brian, and Vince, allowing them, Hobbs, Mia, and Elena to escape. Towards the end of the film, he is shot and killed by Brian when he tries to kill Dominic after surviving having Reyes' money vault slammed into the vehicle he was driving with Reyes in the back. Zizi is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Michael_Irby" title="Michael Irby">Michael Irby</A>.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Owen_Shaw">Owen Shaw</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=61" title="Edit section: Owen Shaw">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Owen Shaw</B> is a paramilitary-trained criminal mastermind.<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP> Formerly with the <A href="/wiki/Special_Air_Service" title="Special Air Service">Special Air Service</A>, (the <A href="/wiki/Special_ops" class="mw-redirect" title="Special ops">special ops</A> of the British Army), Shaw has assembled a team of mercenaries to rob high-tech devices worth billions in the black market. While trying to escape the plane with the chip, Dom stops him and Shaw is thrown out of the car and plane falling to the ground. Lin describes him as "an antagonist that's worthy of Dominic Toretto" and "that had the opposite philosophy to Dom. Dom often goes with trusting his gut, whereas Shaw is more about the analytics where there is no room for weakness."<SUP id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14">[14]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In <I><A href="/wiki/Furious_7" title="Furious 7">Furious 7</A></I>, it is revealed that Shaw survived his injuries from <I>Fast & Furious 6</I> but is still in a coma. In <I><A href="/wiki/The_Fate_of_the_Furious" title="The Fate of the Furious">The Fate of the Furious</A></I>, Shaw is shown to have fully recovered, and is shown aiding his older brother in saving Dominic's baby son from the terrorist Cipher. Shaw is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Luke_Evans_(actor)" title="Luke Evans (actor)">Luke Evans</A>. Originally the role was earmarked for <A href="/wiki/Jason_Statham" title="Jason Statham">Jason Statham</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP> who would later join the franchise in the sequel as Owen's older brother Deckard Shaw.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Deckard_Shaw">Deckard Shaw</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=72" title="Edit section: Deckard Shaw">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Deckard Shaw</B> is a <A href="/wiki/United_Kingdom_Special_Forces" title="United Kingdom Special Forces">UKSF</A> assassin and the older brother of Owen Shaw, who was injured and put into a critical condition by Dominic in <I><A href="/wiki/Fast_%26_Furious_6" title="Fast & Furious 6">Fast & Furious 6</A></I>. Seeking to avenge his comatose brother, he meets him in London, in a secure hospital. Shaw sends a message to Dominic by killing Han during <A href="/wiki/The_Fast_and_the_Furious:_Tokyo_Drift" title="The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift"><I>Tokyo Drift</I></A> in a car chase in Tokyo, Japan and blowing up Dominic's old house in Los Angeles in <A href="/wiki/Furious_7" title="Furious 7">the seventh film</A>. By the climactic ending, Deckard is captured and put into a CIA Detention Black Site prison, promising to escape and continue his revenge though Hobbs expresses doubts about it. In <I><A href="/wiki/The_Fate_of_the_Furious" title="The Fate of the Furious">The Fate of the Furious</A></I>, Shaw is recruited into the crew by Mr. Nobody as an ally, as part of the quest to figure out why Dominic has betrayed them. Shaw has his own motives to destroy Cipher who has blackmailed Dom and admitted his past conflict with her when the former tried to recruit him in her plans, which started the chain of events that led to the Shaw brothers' feud with Dom and his crew. He is seemingly shot by Dom before Letty grabs the briefcase and tries to escape. As the film goes on, Shaw ultimately redeems himself, and in the climax, along with the recovered Owen, he saves Dominic's baby son from Cipher, although Cipher manages to escape to parts unknown. Shaw is last seen attending the crew's celebratory lunch in the end, where he makes peace with Dominic by presenting to him his son and joins the team. Shaw is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Jason_Statham" title="Jason Statham">Jason Statham</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP></P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Mose_Jakande">Mose Jakande</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=73" title="Edit section: Mose Jakande">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Mose Jakande</B> was a Somalian terrorist who led a Private Military Base that allies to Shaw. He is powerful and violent with no allegiance to anyone. He wants the hacker known as "Ramsey", who has created a device called <I>God's Eye</I>, which can find anyone on Earth, for use as a personal toy. He teams up with Deckard Shaw in order to take on Dominic and his team after they rescue Ramsey from his henchmen, but soon turns on Shaw when faced with a chance to take out Toretto during a fight between the two men on top of a car park. He is killed in the ending climactic scene after Dom plants Deckard Shaw's bag of grenades on his helicopter, which Hobbs shoots, destroying the helicopter with Jakande still inside. In the Fate of the Furious, it was revealed Jakande was working for Cipher for information on Toretto. Mose Jakande is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Djimon_Hounsou" title="Djimon Hounsou">Djimon Hounsou</A>.</P>

Kiet is portrayed by martial artist and stunt coordinator <A href="/wiki/Tony_Jaa" title="Tony Jaa">Tony Jaa</A>.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Cipher">Cipher</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=77" title="Edit section: Cipher">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Cipher</B> is a criminal mastermind and <A href="/wiki/Cyberterrorist" class="mw-redirect" title="Cyberterrorist">cyberterrorist</A> who blackmails Dom into working against his allies by kidnapping Dom's son and Elena. It is revealed that she was the one who hired Owen Shaw to steal the Nightshade device after his brother Deckard Shaw refused to do the work himself and she also hired Mose Jakande to steal the God's Eye. She plans to hijack a Russian nuclear submarine and then fire one of its missiles into the air, claiming that by doing this, she will let the world's superpowers that she'll hold them "accountable" should any one of them "cross the line." She survives by jumping out of a flying plane before Deckard can kill her, though her plans are foiled by Dom and his crew, and Dom's son is saved by Deckard. It is mentioned at the end by Mr. Nobody that Cipher is still at large and is rumored to be hiding in Athens, though thanks to Dom and his crew, she won't have the power to nuke any cities anytime soon. She is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Charlize_Theron" title="Charlize Theron">Charlize Theron</A>.</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Connor_Rhodes">Connor Rhodes</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=78" title="Edit section: Connor Rhodes">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Connor Rhodes</B> is the ruthless henchmen of Cipher and a former teammate of Owen Shaw. He kills Elena under Cipher's orders after Dom disobeyed her during the heist in New York. When he tries to shoot Letty from afar, Dom rebels against Cipher and kills Rhodes by breaking his neck, stating this was for Elena. He is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Kristofer_Hivju" title="Kristofer Hivju">Kristofer Hivju</A>.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Agent_Bilkins">Agent Bilkins</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=81" title="Edit section: Agent Bilkins">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Bilkins</B> is an <A href="/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation" title="Federal Bureau of Investigation">FBI</A> agent who was seen in <I>The Fast and the Furious</I> and <I>2 Fast 2 Furious</I>. He is Brian's former boss while he was in the <A href="/wiki/Los_Angeles_Police_Department" title="Los Angeles Police Department">LAPD</A>. Bilkins is shown to have doubts about Brian in <I>The Fast and the Furious</I>. He also complained at Brian's car being destroyed at the hands of Johnny Tran and Lance Nguyen. In <I>2 Fast 2 Furious</I>, Bilkins showed more sympathy towards Brian than Markham. When he came to Barstow with Brian, Bilkins manages to convince Roman to help Customs catch Verone in exchange of their criminal record being cleaned. He is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Thom_Barry" title="Thom Barry">Thom Barry</A>.</P>

Markham initially opposes the inclusion of Brian and his partner Roman Pearce in the undercover sting operation. During the film, Markham shows no trust in Brian and Roman to the point of nearly blowing their cover during the first part of their mission. However, the duo gain his trust after stopping Verone from fleeing the country. Markham is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/James_Remar" title="James Remar">James Remar</A>.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Monica_Fuentes">Monica Fuentes</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=85" title="Edit section: Monica Fuentes">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Agent Monica Fuentes</B> is a U.S. Customs (<A href="/wiki/U.S._Immigration_and_Customs_Enforcement" title="U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement">U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement</A> or <A href="/wiki/U.S._Immigration_and_Customs_Enforcement" title="U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement">ICE</A> in <I>Fast Five</I>) federal agent. Monica has been working undercover as an assistant for drug kingpin Carter Verone for nearly a year when Brian and Roman are brought in. She falls in love with Brian, but earns Roman's mistrust. Monica later warns Brian that after the mission Verone has assigned them, he intends to kill them. She blows her cover by telling Brian about the airstrip, being the only person Verone notified about it. She is then taken captive aboard his private yacht, but Brian and Roman jump their <A href="/wiki/Chevrolet_Camaro_(first_generation)" title="Chevrolet Camaro (first generation)">Camaro</A> onto the boat, saving Monica and capturing Verone. In the mid-credits scene of <I>Fast Five</I>, Hobbs receives a file from Monica regarding a robbery, in which Letty's photograph is attached, revealing that she is still alive, and is involved with the military convoy robbery in Berlin. Monica is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Eva_Mendes" title="Eva Mendes">Eva Mendes</A>.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Agent_Wilkes">Agent Wilkes</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=91" title="Edit section: Agent Wilkes">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Wilkes</B> was a <A href="/wiki/Diplomatic_Security_Service" title="Diplomatic Security Service">DSS</A> federal agent. He was on Luke Hobbs' team whose job was to capture Dominic Toretto and Brian O'Conner in Fast Five. After apprehending Dom, Brian, Mia and Vince, the convoy is ambushed by Hernan Reyes' henchmen, led by Zizi. One of them fires a rocket at Wilkes' vehicle, killing him and Macroy; every DSS agent is taken out with the exception of Hobbs. Agent Wilkes is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Fernando_Chien" title="Fernando Chien">Fernando Chien</A>.</P>

<P><B>Macroy</B> was a DSS federal agent and a part of Luke Hobbs' team tasked with apprehending Dominic Toretto and Brian O'Conner. He was also tasked with reassembling a <A href="/wiki/Ford_GT40" title="Ford GT40">Ford GT40</A>. He met his end when Zizi along with Reyes' other henchmen killed him in an ambush by blowing up Wilkes' vehicle. The other agents were gunned down as well, Hobbs being the only DSS agent to survive. Agent Macroy is portrayed by Geoff Meed.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Fusco">Fusco</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=93" title="Edit section: Fusco">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Fusco</B> is a member of Hobbs team and helps disassemble and consequently reassemble the stolen car in the hope of finding what is missing and finding a lead on the whereabouts of Dominic and his team. Fusco is present during the subsequent chase and kills Reyes' hit men alongside his fellow agents. He accompanies Hobbs to the 'meeting' with Toretto and after being threatened by Dom's fellow Brazilian street racers he and the team leave, but not before Tej places a tracking device on the agents' truck. After the tracking signal is reversed Fusco and the rest of Hobbs team turn up at the garage to arrest Dom, Mia, Brian and Vince.</P>
<P>On their way to the airport, however, they were suddenly ambushed by Reyes men, led by Zizi. One of them fires a rocket-propelled projectile at Fusco's vehicle, sending it hurling off the road. As he lies injured, three grenades are suddenly thrown aside him as Hobbs watches on helplessly. He casts a final glare at his boss before they explode, killing him in the blasts. Agent Fusco is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Alimi_Ballard" title="Alimi Ballard">Alimi Ballard</A>.</P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Mr._Nobody">Mr. Nobody</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=96" title="Edit section: Mr. Nobody">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><SPAN id="Frank_Petty"></SPAN> <B>Mr. Nobody</B> is a government agent and the leader of an unknown covert ops team wanting to capture Mose Jakande, a mercenary coveting the God's Eye, a program capable of tracking a specific individual using anything on a digital network. He approaches and convinces Dom to assist him in collecting the God's Eye and rescuing its creator, Ramsey, in return for using the program to locate Deckard Shaw. He assembles Dom's crew upon the latter's agreement on the deal. While fighting Deckard and Jakande along with his mercenaries, he is shot by Kiet but tells Dom to move on without him and stop Jakande and Deckard while he is evacuated for medical treatment. Mr. Nobody is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/Kurt_Russell" title="Kurt Russell">Kurt Russell</A>. Originally referred to as Frank Petty several weeks before the premiere,<SUP id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-19">[19]</A></SUP> he was later noted to just be Mr. Nobody when Russell interviewed on <I><A href="/wiki/Jimmy_Kimmel_Live" class="mw-redirect" title="Jimmy Kimmel Live">Jimmy Kimmel Live</A></I>. His real name is unknown.<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP></P>

<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Agent_Sheppard">Agent Sheppard</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Fast_and_the_Furious_characters&action=edit&section=97" title="Edit section: Agent Sheppard">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Sheppard</B> is Mr. Nobody's assistant and a tactical leader and member of his ops team. He was first seen when they attempt to attack Deckard causing him to flee and believe Dom is actually a criminal causing Dom to put him on chokehold, but Mr. Nobody stops him when they see Dom as an ally, leaving him passed out and later helps plan out Dom and his crew for their rescue of Ramsey and also participates in the infiltration to capture Deckard Shaw. Sheppard is killed by Mose Jakande during a shootout, leaving the God's Eye to be taken by Jakande. Mr. Nobody avenges his death by killing several of Jakande's men, although Hobbs would be the one who truly avenges Sheppard's death by killing Jakande himself in the film's climax. Sheppard is portrayed by <A href="/wiki/John_Brotherton" title="John Brotherton">John Brotherton</A>.</P>

<P><B>Thomas Eugene "Tom" Paris</B>, played by <A href="/wiki/Robert_Duncan_McNeill" title="Robert Duncan McNeill">Robert Duncan McNeill</A>, is a character in the American <A href="/wiki/Science_fiction" title="Science fiction">science fiction</A> television series <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Trek:_Voyager" title="Star Trek: Voyager">Star Trek: Voyager</A></I>. Paris serves as the chief <A href="/wiki/Helmsman" title="Helmsman">helmsman</A> and an auxiliary medic aboard the <A href="/wiki/USS_Voyager_(Star_Trek)" title="USS Voyager (Star Trek)">USS <I>Voyager</I></A>. The character's middle name, "Eugene", is a tribute to <I>Star Trek</I> creator <A href="/wiki/Gene_Roddenberry" title="Gene Roddenberry">Gene Roddenberry</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP></P>
<P></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Biography">Biography</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Tom_Paris&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Biography">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Tom Paris is the son of <A href="/wiki/Starfleet" title="Starfleet">Starfleet</A> Admiral <A href="/wiki/Owen_Paris" class="mw-redirect" title="Owen Paris">Owen Paris</A> and a scion of a family with a long history of illustrious service in Starfleet. Following in his family's tradition, Paris attended <A href="/wiki/Starfleet_Academy" title="Starfleet Academy">Starfleet Academy</A> sometime in the 2350s and majored in astrophysics. A gifted pilot, Paris earned an assignment to the Academy's honor squadron.</P>
<P>His relationship with his father was not a good one; while Tom wanted to join the <A href="/wiki/United_Federation_of_Planets" title="United Federation of Planets">Federation</A> Naval Patrol, Owen wanted him to enlist at Starfleet Academy. Admiral Paris often disapproved of his son's tendency to get into fights and his resulting punishments.</P>
<P>Soon after his graduation from Starfleet Academy, Tom crashed a shuttle he was piloting near Caldik Prime, killing three other Starfleet officers. Afraid he would lose his commission, Paris falsified records that would later reveal the cause of the accident as pilot error. His efforts to cover up the error succeeded, yet still, overwhelmed by guilt and regret, he confessed. He was court martialed for his actions and was dishonorably discharged from Starfleet. This caused a major rift between Paris and his father.</P>
<P>Following his discharge, Paris left <A href="/wiki/San_Francisco" title="San Francisco">San Francisco</A> for <A href="/wiki/Marseille" title="Marseille">Marseille</A>, where he started spending his time drinking and playing pool in Sandrine's, a waterfront bar. There, <A href="/wiki/Chakotay" title="Chakotay">Chakotay</A>, a former Starfleet officer now serving with the <A href="/wiki/Maquis_(Star_Trek)" title="Maquis (Star Trek)">Maquis</A>, recruited him to serve as a mercenary pilot for the Maquis Rebellion against the Federation. This adventure went no better than his earlier stint in Starfleet as Paris was captured by Starfleet while piloting his first mission for the Maquis.</P>
<P>Tried and convicted of treason for aiding the Maquis Rebellion, Paris was sentenced to serve time in the Federation penal settlement near <A href="/wiki/Auckland" title="Auckland">Auckland</A>, New Zealand. <A href="/wiki/Kathryn_Janeway" title="Kathryn Janeway">Kathryn Janeway</A>, captain of the starship <A href="/wiki/USS_Voyager_(Star_Trek)" title="USS Voyager (Star Trek)">USS <I>Voyager</I></A>, obtained Paris' temporary release from the penal colony. Janeway, charged with finding and capturing the Maquis ship commanded by Chakotay, offered Paris early parole in exchange for serving as her informant on Chakotay and the Maquis.</P>
<P>Janeway and the crew of <I>Voyager</I>, while searching for the Maquis ship, were thrown into the <A href="/wiki/Delta_Quadrant" class="mw-redirect" title="Delta Quadrant">Delta Quadrant</A> by a massive energy wave created by an alien known as the Caretaker. Once there, they successfully located the Maquis ship docked at the Caretaker's array. The survivors of the incident became stranded about 70,000 light-years away from Earth. The Maquis ship was destroyed and its crew joined the Federation crew on <I>Voyager</I>.</P>
<P>The marooning of <I>Voyager</I> in the Delta Quadrant provided Paris with a new beginning. Janeway gave Paris a field commission as a Starfleet lieutenant and made him chief helmsman of <I>Voyager</I>. He had a rough start, however, as Starfleet and Maquis alike viewed Paris with suspicion. Paris worked hard to earn his crewmates' respect. During this time, he became best friends with Ensign <A href="/wiki/Harry_Kim_(Star_Trek)" title="Harry Kim (Star Trek)">Harry Kim</A>, a young officer on his first mission who defied his crewmates to befriend Paris. Eventually, Paris was accepted by the crew and became one of Janeway's valued officers.</P>
<P>Paris' duties were not limited to piloting <I>Voyager</I>. On Janeway's orders, he trained as a field medic and assisted <A href="/wiki/Doctor_(Star_Trek:_Voyager)" class="mw-redirect" title="Doctor (Star Trek: Voyager)">The Doctor</A> until the Doctor recruited <A href="/wiki/Kes_(Star_Trek)" title="Kes (Star Trek)">Kes</A> as his primary assistant. Following Kes's departure ("<A href="/wiki/The_Gift_(Star_Trek:_Voyager)" title="The Gift (Star Trek: Voyager)">The Gift</A>") Paris once again served regular duty shifts in sickbay.</P>
<P>In the episode "<A href="/wiki/Thirty_Days_(Star_Trek:_Voyager)" title="Thirty Days (Star Trek: Voyager)">Thirty Days</A>", while disobeying direct orders in order to do what he felt was morally right, he was reduced to ensign and thrown in <I>Voyager</I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</SPAN>s brig for a period of 30 days. About a year later, after working diligently at his duties, he regained his former rank. This occurred just before the events of "<A href="/wiki/Unimatrix_Zero" title="Unimatrix Zero">Unimatrix Zero</A>", during which it is revealed that he is fourth in the chain of command.</P>
<P>While serving on <I>Voyager</I>, Paris nurtured a long-hidden talent for holo-programming, devising several programs for the entertainment of his fellow crewmembers. His most popular programs included a re-creation of Sandrine's bar, an Irish town called Fair Haven, and a 1930s-era sci-fi movie serial entitled <I><A href="/wiki/Captain_Proton" class="mw-redirect" title="Captain Proton">Captain Proton</A></I>.</P>
<P>Paris married Lieutenant <A href="/wiki/B%27Elanna_Torres" title="B'Elanna Torres">B'Elanna Torres</A>, <I>Voyager</I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</SPAN>s half-Klingon chief engineer, in 2377. Torres gave birth to their daughter Miral Paris during the events that led to <I>Voyager</I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</SPAN>s return to the <A href="/wiki/Alpha_Quadrant" class="mw-redirect" title="Alpha Quadrant">Alpha Quadrant</A> and Earth.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Personality">Personality</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Tom_Paris&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Personality">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Tom Paris at times displayed resentment toward his father, Owen Paris. This situation improved substantially over the course of the journey, due to Janeway's willingness to offer him redemption, and later to his relationship with <A href="/wiki/B%27Elanna_Torres" title="B'Elanna Torres">B'Elanna Torres</A>.</P>
<P>Paris also has a deep interest in 20th-century Earth <A href="/wiki/Pop-culture" class="mw-redirect" title="Pop-culture">pop-culture</A>, often utilizing such in his holo-programs. The knowledge helped the crew during time-travel incidents.</P>
<P>He became good friends with Harry Kim from the start and at times displayed protectiveness in the face of Harry's customary naiveté. In the first episode he rescues the ensign from <A href="/wiki/Quark_(Star_Trek)" title="Quark (Star Trek)">Quark</A>, a manipulative <A href="/wiki/Ferengi" title="Ferengi">Ferengi</A>. The only member of the crew with whom Paris initially had a somewhat difficult relationship was Chakotay because of their history in the <A href="/wiki/Maquis_(Star_Trek)" title="Maquis (Star Trek)">Maquis</A>. However, throughout <I>Voyager</I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</SPAN>s seven-year journey home, Paris and Chakotay reconciled (in part due to Paris having earned Chakotay's trust) and became good friends.</P>
<P>Tom was a full lieutenant at the very beginning of the series, then a lieutenant junior grade in the first-season episode "<A href="/wiki/Faces_(Star_Trek:_Voyager)" title="Faces (Star Trek: Voyager)">Faces</A>".</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Character_background">Character background</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Tom_Paris&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Character background">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The writers planned to use the character of Nicolas Locarno as a template for Tom Paris, who was played by McNeill in the <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Trek:_The_Next_Generation" title="Star Trek: The Next Generation">Next Generation</A></I> episode "<A href="/wiki/The_First_Duty" title="The First Duty">The First Duty</A>". As a result, <I>Voyager</I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</SPAN>s writers created an entirely new character sharing many of Locarno's attributes. <SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The Tom Paris character has two backstories. The original backstory, and the only one acknowledged onscreen, cast Paris as a disgraced officer dishonorably discharged from Starfleet for covering up pilot error following a shuttle accident on Caldik Prime. In her published novel, <I>Pathways</I>, <I>Voyager</I> producer <A href="/wiki/Jeri_Taylor" title="Jeri Taylor">Jeri Taylor</A> provided an alternative story much more similar to Locarno's, moving the accident to Paris' Starfleet Academy years and making his fellow cadets the victims of his recklessness.</P>
<P>An unproduced <I>Voyager</I> script was to have had a flashback to his time attending Starfleet Academy, and shown that <A href="/wiki/Ro_Laren" title="Ro Laren">Ro Laren</A>, the <A href="/wiki/Bajoran" title="Bajoran">Bajoran</A> character from <I>Star Trek: The Next Generation</I> was among his classmates.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Voyager_relaunch_novels"><I>Voyager</I> relaunch novels</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Tom_Paris&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Voyager relaunch novels">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>In the non-canonical <I>Voyager</I> relaunch novels, written by <A href="/wiki/Christie_Golden" title="Christie Golden">Christie Golden</A>, Paris was promoted two steps in rank, like many of the <I>Voyager</I> crew, and is now a <A href="/wiki/Lieutenant_commander" title="Lieutenant commander">lieutenant commander</A>. He serves as First Officer of <I>Voyager</I>, under the command of now-Captain <A href="/wiki/Chakotay" title="Chakotay">Chakotay</A>.</P>

<P><B>Roger Dean Miller, Sr.</B> (January 2, 1936 – October 25, 1992) was an American singer-songwriter, musician, and actor, best known for his <A href="/wiki/Honky-tonk" title="Honky-tonk">honky-tonk</A>-influenced <A href="/wiki/Novelty_song" title="Novelty song">novelty songs</A>. His most recognized tunes included the chart-topping <A href="/wiki/Country_music" title="Country music">country</A> and pop hits "<A href="/wiki/King_of_the_Road_(song)" title="King of the Road (song)">King of the Road</A>", "<A href="/wiki/Dang_Me" title="Dang Me">Dang Me</A>", and "<A href="/wiki/England_Swings" title="England Swings">England Swings</A>", all from the mid-1960s <A href="/wiki/Nashville_sound" title="Nashville sound">Nashville sound</A> era.</P>
<P>After growing up in <A href="/wiki/Oklahoma" title="Oklahoma">Oklahoma</A> and serving in the <A href="/wiki/United_States_Army" title="United States Army">United States Army</A>, Miller began his musical career as a songwriter in the late 1950s, writing such hits as "<A href="/wiki/Billy_Bayou" title="Billy Bayou">Billy Bayou</A>" and "Home" for <A href="/wiki/Jim_Reeves" title="Jim Reeves">Jim Reeves</A> and "<A href="/w/index.php?title=Invitation_to_the_Blues&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Invitation to the Blues (page does not exist)">Invitation to the Blues</A>" for <A href="/wiki/Ray_Price_(musician)" title="Ray Price (musician)">Ray Price</A>. He later began a recording career and reached the peak of his fame in the mid-1960s, continuing to record and tour into the 1990s, charting his final top 20 country hit "<A href="/w/index.php?title=Old_Friends_(Willie_Nelson_album)&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Old Friends (Willie Nelson album) (page does not exist)">Old Friends</A>" with <A href="/wiki/Willie_Nelson" title="Willie Nelson">Willie Nelson</A> in 1982. He also wrote and performed several of the songs for the 1973 Disney animated film <I><A href="/wiki/Robin_Hood_(1973_film)" title="Robin Hood (1973 film)">Robin Hood</A></I>. Later in his life, he wrote the music and lyrics for the 1985 <A href="/wiki/Tony_Award" title="Tony Award">Tony</A>-award winning Broadway musical <I><A href="/wiki/Big_River_(musical)" title="Big River (musical)">Big River</A></I>, in which he acted.</P>
<P>Miller died from lung cancer in 1992 and was inducted into the <A href="/wiki/Country_Music_Hall_of_Fame" class="mw-redirect" title="Country Music Hall of Fame">Country Music Hall of Fame</A> three years later. His songs continued to be recorded by other singers, with covers of "<A href="/wiki/Tall,_Tall_Trees" title="Tall, Tall Trees">Tall, Tall Trees</A>" by <A href="/wiki/Alan_Jackson" title="Alan Jackson">Alan Jackson</A> and "<A href="/wiki/Husbands_and_Wives_(song)" title="Husbands and Wives (song)">Husbands and Wives</A>" by <A href="/wiki/Brooks_%26_Dunn" title="Brooks & Dunn">Brooks & Dunn</A>; both reached the number one spot on country charts in the 1990s. The <A href="/wiki/Roger_Miller_Museum" title="Roger Miller Museum">Roger Miller Museum</A> in his home town of <A href="/wiki/Erick,_Oklahoma" title="Erick, Oklahoma">Erick, Oklahoma</A>, was a tribute to Miller.</P>
