<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Durandal">Durandal</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Song_of_Roland&action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section: Durandal">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>According to the Song of Roland, the legendary sword called <A href="/wiki/Durandal" class="mw-redirect" title="Durandal">Durandal</A> was first given to <A href="/wiki/Charlemagne" title="Charlemagne">Charlemagne</A> by an angel.  It contained one tooth of <A href="/wiki/Saint_Peter" title="Saint Peter">Saint Peter</A>, blood of <A href="/wiki/Saint_Basil" class="mw-redirect" title="Saint Basil">Saint Basil</A>, hair of <A href="/wiki/Denis" title="Denis">Saint Denis</A>, and a piece of the raiment of the Blessed <A href="/wiki/Virgin_Mary" class="mw-redirect" title="Virgin Mary">Virgin Mary</A>, and was supposedly the sharpest sword in all existence. In the story of the Song of Roland, the weapon is given to Roland, and he uses it to defend himself single-handedly against thousands of Muslim attackers.  According to one 12th-century legend from the French town of <A href="/wiki/Rocamadour" title="Rocamadour">Rocamadour</A>, Roland threw the sword into a cliffside.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2018)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> You can still see a sword there, allegedly Durandal, embedded into the cliff-face.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2018)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Historical_adaptations">Historical adaptations</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Song_of_Roland&action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section: Historical adaptations">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>A Latin poem, <I><A href="/wiki/Carmen_de_Prodicione_Guenonis" title="Carmen de Prodicione Guenonis">Carmen de Prodicione Guenonis</A></I>, was composed around 1120, and a Latin prose version, <I><A href="/wiki/Historia_Caroli_Magni" title="Historia Caroli Magni">Historia Caroli Magni</A></I> (often known as "The Pseudo-Turpin") even earlier. Around 1170, a version of the French poem was translated into the <A href="/wiki/Middle_High_German" title="Middle High German">Middle High German</A> <I>Rolandslied</I> by <A href="/wiki/Konrad_der_Pfaffe" title="Konrad der Pfaffe">Konrad der Pfaffe</A><SUP id="cite_ref-Brault_8-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Brault-8">[8]</A></SUP> (formerly thought to have been the author of the <A href="/wiki/Kaiserchronik" title="Kaiserchronik">Kaiserchronik</A>). In his translation Konrad replaces French topics with generically Christian ones. The work was translated into <A href="/wiki/Middle_Dutch" title="Middle Dutch">Middle Dutch</A> in the 13th century.
</P><P>It was also rendered into <A href="/wiki/Occitan_language" title="Occitan language">Occitan</A> verse in the 14th- or 15th-century poem of <I>Ronsasvals</I>, which incorporates the later, southern aesthetic into the story. An <A href="/wiki/Old_Norse" title="Old Norse">Old Norse</A> version of the <I>Song of Roland</I> exists as <I><A href="/wiki/Karlamagn%C3%BAs_saga" title="Karlamagnús saga">Karlamagnús saga</A></I>, and a translation into the artificial literary language of <A href="/wiki/Venetian_language" title="Venetian language">Franco-Venetian</A> is also known; such translations contributed to the awareness of the story in <A href="/wiki/Italy" title="Italy">Italy</A>. In 1516 <A href="/wiki/Ludovico_Ariosto" title="Ludovico Ariosto">Ludovico Ariosto</A> published his epic <I><A href="/wiki/Orlando_Furioso" title="Orlando Furioso">Orlando Furioso</A></I>, which deals largely with characters first described in the <I>Song of Roland</I>.
</P><P>There is also <A href="/wiki/Faroese_language" title="Faroese language">Faroese</A> adoption of this ballad named "Runtsivalstríðið" (Battle of Roncevaux).<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> The ballad is one of many sung during the <A href="/wiki/Faroese_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Faroese people">Faroese</A> folkdance tradition of chain dancing.
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Modern_adaptations">Modern adaptations</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Song_of_Roland&action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section: Modern adaptations">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The <I>Chanson de Roland</I> has an important place in the background of <A href="/wiki/Graham_Greene" title="Graham Greene">Graham Greene</A>'s <I><A href="/wiki/The_Confidential_Agent" title="The Confidential Agent">The Confidential Agent</A></I>, published in 1939. The book's protagonist had been a Medieval scholar specialising in this work, until the outbreak of the <A href="/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War" title="Spanish Civil War">Spanish Civil War</A> forced him to become a soldier and secret agent. Throughout the book, he repeatedly compares himself and other characters with the characters of "Roland". Particularly, the book includes a full two pages of specific commentary, which is relevant to its 20th-century plot line: "Oliver, when he saw the Saracens coming, urged Roland to blow his horn and fetch back Charlemagne – but Roland wouldn't blow. A big brave fool. In war one always chooses the wrong hero. Oliver should have been the hero of that song, instead of being given second place with the blood-thirsty Bishop Turpin.(...) In the Oxford version Oliver is reconciled in the end, he gives Roland his death-blow by accident, his eyes blinded by wounds. [But] the story had been tidied up. In truth, Oliver strikes his friend down in full knowledge – because of what he has done to his men, all the wasted lives. Oliver dies hating the man he loves – the big boasting courageous fool who was more concerned with his own glory than with the victory of his faith. This makes the story tragedy, not just heroics".<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP>
</P><P>It is also adapted by Stephen King, in the <A href="/wiki/The_Dark_Tower_(series)" title="The Dark Tower (series)"><I>Dark Tower</I></A> series in which Roland Deschain wishes to save the Dark Tower from the  Crimson King.
</P><P><I>The Song of Roland</I> is part of the <A href="/wiki/Matter_of_France" title="Matter of France">Matter of France</A> (the Continental counterpart to the Arthurian legendarium known as the <A href="/wiki/Matter_of_Britain" title="Matter of Britain">Matter of Britain</A>), and related to <I>Orlando Furioso</I>. The names Roland and Orlando are cognates.
</P><P>Emanuelle Luzzati's animated short film, <I>I paladini di Francia</I>, together with <I>Giulio Gianini</I>, in 1960, was turned into the children's picture-story book, with verse narrative, <I>I Paladini de Francia ovvero il tradimento di Gano di Maganz</I>, which translates literally as “The Paladins of France or the treachery of Gano of Maganz” (Ugo Mursia Editore, 1962). This was then republished, in English, as <I>Ronald and the Wizard Calico</I> (1969). The Picture Lion paperback edition (William Collins, London, 1973) is a paperback imprint of the Hutchinson Junior Books edition (1969), which credits the English translation to Hutchinson Junior Books.
</P><P>Luzatti's original verse story in Italian is about the plight of a beautiful maiden called Biancofiore – White Flower, or Blanchefleur – and her brave hero, Captain Rinaldo, and Ricardo and his paladins – the term used for Christian knights engaged in Crusades against the Saracens and Moors. Battling with these good people are the wicked Moors – North African Muslims and Arabs – and their Sultan, in Jerusalem. With the assistance of the wicked and treacherous magician, Gano of Maganz, Biancofiore is stolen from her fortress castle, and taken to become the reluctant wife of the Sultan. The catalyst for victory is the good magician, Urlubulu, who lives in a lake, and flies through the air on the back of his magic blue bird. The English translators, using the original illustrations, and the basic rhyme patterns, slightly simplify the plot, changing the Christians-versus-Muslim-Moors conflict into a battle between good and bad magicians and between golden knights and green knights. The French traitor in The Song of Roland, who is actually Roland's cowardly step-father, is Ganelon – very likely the inspiration for Luzzati's traitor and wicked magician, Gano. Orlando Furioso (literally, Furious or Enraged Orlando, or Roland), includes Orlando's cousin, the paladin Rinaldo, who, like Orlando, is also in love with Angelica, a pagan princess. Rinaldo is, of course, the Italian equivalent of Ronald. Flying through the air on the back of a magic bird is equivalent to flying on a magic <A href="/wiki/Hippogriff" title="Hippogriff">hippogriff</A>.
</P><P>On July 22, 2017, Michael Eging and Steve Arnold released a novel ″The Silver Horn Echoes: A Song of Roland," inspired by the La Chanson de Roland. This work is more closely based on a screenplay written by Michael Eging in 2008, simply known as "Song of Roland" and first optioned to Alan Kaplan at Cine LA that same year. The book explores the untold story of how Roland finds himself at Ronceveaux, betrayed by Ganelon and facing the expansive Saragossan host. Primary characters in the novel include Charles (Charlemagne), Ganelon, Bishop Turpin, Oliver, Aude, Marsilion, Blancandarin and others recognizable from the poem. Introduced in this tale are additional characters that inject intrigue and danger to the story, including Charles oldest son, Pepin, Marsilion's treacherous son, Saleem, and the scheming Byzantine emissary, Honorius. The cover artwork was hand painted by Jordan Raskin. The authors determined when writing both the screenplay and the novel to remain in the world created by the poem; thus Charles remains an older man near the end of his long reign rather than in 778 when the attack on the rearguard actually occurred. Further, this novel bookends the story with <A href="/wiki/William_the_Conqueror" title="William the Conqueror">William the Conqueror</A>'s use of the poem as a motivator for Norman forces prior to the <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Hastings" title="Battle of Hastings">Battle of Hastings</A> in 1066.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP>

<P><B>Power Rangers</B> is an American entertainment and merchandising <A href="/wiki/Media_franchise" title="Media franchise">franchise</A> built around a live action superhero television series. Produced first by <A href="/wiki/Saban_Entertainment" title="Saban Entertainment">Saban Entertainment</A>, later by <A href="/wiki/BVS_Entertainment" class="mw-redirect" title="BVS Entertainment">BVS Entertainment</A>, and today by <A href="/wiki/SCG_Power_Rangers" class="mw-redirect" title="SCG Power Rangers">SCG Power Rangers</A>, the television series takes much of its <A href="/wiki/Footage" title="Footage">footage</A> from the Japanese <A href="/wiki/Tokusatsu" title="Tokusatsu">tokusatsu</A> <I><A href="/wiki/Super_Sentai" title="Super Sentai">Super Sentai</A></I>, produced by <A href="/wiki/Toei_Company" title="Toei Company">Toei Company</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP> The first <I>Power Rangers</I> entry, <I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers">Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</A></I>, debuted on August 28, 1993, and helped launch the <A href="/wiki/Fox_Kids" title="Fox Kids">Fox Kids</A> programming block of the 1990s, during which it catapulted into <A href="/wiki/Popular_culture" title="Popular culture">popular culture</A> along with a line of <A href="/wiki/Action_figure" title="Action figure">action figures</A> and other toys by <A href="/wiki/Bandai" title="Bandai">Bandai</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> As of 2001<SUP class="plainlinks noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Power_Rangers&action=edit">[update]</A></SUP>, the media franchise has generated over $6 billion in retail sales worldwide.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Despite initial <A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers#Reception_and_controversy" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers">criticism</A> that its action violence targeted child audiences, the franchise has continued, and as of 2017<SUP class="plainlinks noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Power_Rangers&action=edit">[update]</A></SUP> the show consists of 24 television seasons of 20 different themed series and three theatrical films released in 1995, 1997 and 2017. In 2010, <A href="/wiki/Haim_Saban" title="Haim Saban">Haim Saban</A>, creator of the series, regained ownership of the franchise after seven years under <A href="/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company" title="The Walt Disney Company">The Walt Disney Company</A>.</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Premise">Premise</SPAN></H2>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <A href="/wiki/List_of_Power_Rangers_characters" title="List of Power Rangers characters">List of Power Rangers characters</A> and <A href="/wiki/List_of_Power_Rangers_villains" title="List of Power Rangers villains">List of Power Rangers villains</A></DIV>
<P>Since <I>Power Rangers</I> derives most of its footage from the <I><A href="/wiki/Super_Sentai" title="Super Sentai">Super Sentai</A></I> series, it features many <A href="/wiki/Super_Sentai#Common_elements" title="Super Sentai">hallmarks</A> that distinguish it from other superhero series. Each series revolves around a team of youths recruited and trained by a mentor to morph into the eponymous Power Rangers, able to utilize special powers and pilot immense assault machines, called Zords, to overcome the periodic antagonists. In the original series <I>Mighty Morphin</I>, the wizard <A href="/wiki/Zordon" title="Zordon">Zordon</A> recruits "<A href="/wiki/Teenagers" class="mw-redirect" title="Teenagers">teenagers</A> with attitude" against <A href="/wiki/Rita_Repulsa" title="Rita Repulsa">Rita Repulsa</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP></P>
<P>When "morphed," the rangers become powerful <A href="/wiki/Superhero" title="Superhero">superheroes</A> wearing color-coded skin-tight <A href="/wiki/Spandex" title="Spandex">spandex</A> suits and helmets with <A href="/wiki/Opacity_(optics)" title="Opacity (optics)">opaque</A> <A href="/wiki/Visor" title="Visor">visors</A>; identical except in individual rangers' color and helmet design. Morphed Rangers generally possess enhanced strength, durability, agility and combat prowess. Some possess superhuman or <A href="/wiki/Psychic" title="Psychic">psychic</A> abilities such as super-speed, element manipulation, <A href="/wiki/Extra-sensory_perception" class="mw-redirect" title="Extra-sensory perception">extra-sensory perception</A> or <A href="/wiki/Invisibility" title="Invisibility">invisibility</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP> In addition, each individual ranger has a unique <A href="/wiki/Weapon" title="Weapon">weapon</A>, as well as common weaponry used for ground fighting.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[note 1]</A></SUP> When enemies grow to incredible size (as nearly all do), Rangers utilize individual Zords that combine into a larger Megazord.</P>
<P>Rangers teams operate in teams of five or three, with more Rangers joining the team later. Each team of Rangers, with a few exceptions, obeys a general set of conventions, outlined at the beginning of <I>Mighty Morphin</I> and implied by mentors throughout many of the other series: Power Rangers may not use their Ranger powers for personal gain or for escalating a fight (unless the enemy does so), nor may the Power Rangers disclose their identities to the general public.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[note 2]</A></SUP> The penalty for disobeying these rules, in <I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers">Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</A></I>, is the loss of their power.</P>
<P>As in <I>Super Sentai</I>, the color palette of each <I>Power Rangers</I> team changes every series.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[note 3]</A></SUP> Only Red and Blue appear in every Ranger team, while a Yellow Ranger has been present in every season except <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Dino_Charge" title="Power Rangers Dino Charge">Power Rangers Dino Charge</A></I>. Other colors and designations also appear throughout the series.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[note 4]</A></SUP> A Rangers' color designation also influences their wardrobe throughout the series: civilian clothing often matches Ranger color.<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[note 5]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="History">History</SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Adapting_the_Super_Sentai_series">Adapting the <I>Super Sentai</I> series</SPAN></H3>
<TABLE class="plainlinks metadata ambox mbox-small-left ambox-content" role="presentation">
<TBODY><TR>
<TD class="mbox-image"><A href="/wiki/File:Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg" class="image"><IMG alt="[icon]" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg/20px-Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg.png" width="20" height="14" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg/30px-Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg/40px-Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="44" data-file-height="31" /></A></TD>

</TD>

</TBODY></TABLE>
<P>Production of <I>Power Rangers</I> episodes involves extensive localization of and revision of original <I>Super Sentai</I> source material in order to incorporate American culture and conform to American television standards. Rather than making an English <A href="/wiki/Dubbing_(filmmaking)" title="Dubbing (filmmaking)">dub</A> or <A href="/wiki/Translation" title="Translation">translation</A> of the Japanese footage, <I>Power Rangers</I> programs consist of scenes featuring <A href="/wiki/English_Language" class="mw-redirect" title="English Language">English-speaking</A> actors (either from the <A href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</A>, <A href="/wiki/Canada" title="Canada">Canada</A>, <A href="/wiki/Australia" title="Australia">Australia</A>, <A href="/wiki/New_Zealand" title="New Zealand">New Zealand</A>, or the <A href="/wiki/United_Kingdom" title="United Kingdom">United Kingdom</A>) spliced with scenes featuring either Japanese actors dubbed into English or the action scenes from the Super Sentai Series featuring the Rangers fighting <A href="/wiki/Kaiju" title="Kaiju">monsters</A> or the <A href="/wiki/Mecha" title="Mecha">giant robot</A> (Zord and Megazord) battles with English dubbing. In some series, original fight scenes are filmed to incorporate characters or items unique to the <I>Power Rangers</I> production.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[6]</A></SUP> Like many of <A href="/wiki/Saban_Entertainment" title="Saban Entertainment">Saban Entertainment</A> previous ventures in <A href="/wiki/Language_localisation" title="Language localisation">localizing</A> Japanese television for a <A href="/wiki/Western_culture" title="Western culture">Western</A> audience, the plot, character names, and other names usually differ greatly from the source footage, though a few seasons have stayed close to the story of the original Super Sentai season.</P>
<P>Along with adapting the villains from the Super Sentai counterparts, most <I>Power Rangers</I> series also feature villains with no Sentai counterpart. Generally, the primary antagonist of a <I>Power Rangers</I> series (for example, Lord Zedd, Divatox, etc.) are not adapted from the Sentai. Exceptions to this includes <I>Mighty Morphin</I>, <I>Zeo</I>, <I>Lightspeed Rescue</I> and a few others which only use villains adapted from the Japanese shows.</P>
<P>The series that began the <A href="/wiki/Media_franchise" title="Media franchise">franchise</A>, <I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers">Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</A></I> (an American adaptation of the 1992 Japanese <A href="/wiki/Super_Sentai" title="Super Sentai">Super Sentai</A> Series, <I><A href="/wiki/Ky%C5%8Dry%C5%AB_Sentai_Zyuranger" title="Kyōryū Sentai Zyuranger">Kyōryū Sentai Zyuranger</A></I>), began broadcasting as part of the <A href="/wiki/Fox_Kids" title="Fox Kids">Fox Kids</A> block of programing that aired on the <A href="/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company" title="Fox Broadcasting Company">FOX</A> network. It lasted for three seasons (from 1993 to 1996).<SUP id="cite_ref-MMPR2010_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-MMPR2010-12">[7]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Broadcast_history">Broadcast history</SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:252px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Power_rangers.png" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/0/01/Power_rangers.png/250px-Power_rangers.png" width="250" height="125" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/0/01/Power_rangers.png/375px-Power_rangers.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/0/01/Power_rangers.png/500px-Power_rangers.png 2x" data-file-width="565" data-file-height="283" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Power_rangers.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
The Saban Entertainment run of the franchise—beginning with <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_in_Space" title="Power Rangers in Space">Power Rangers in Space</A></I>—used this version of the <I>Power Rangers</I> logo (1998–2001).</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P><A href="/wiki/Saban_Entertainment" title="Saban Entertainment">Saban Entertainment</A> distributed the <I>Power Rangers</I> series from 1993 until the end of 2001, and Fox broadcast it until the <A href="/wiki/Autumn" title="Autumn">fall</A> of 2002. <A href="/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company" title="The Walt Disney Company">The Walt Disney Company</A> purchased the franchise as part of a buyout that took place in 2001.<SUP id="cite_ref-MMPR2010_12-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-MMPR2010-12">[7]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-HaimSaban_13-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-HaimSaban-13">[8]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14">[9]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-buyout_15-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-buyout-15">[10]</A></SUP> This resulted in Fox Family Worldwide becoming <A href="/wiki/ABC_Family_Worldwide_Inc." class="mw-redirect" title="ABC Family Worldwide Inc.">ABC Family Worldwide Inc.</A><SUP id="cite_ref-buyout_15-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-buyout-15">[10]</A></SUP> This buyout also saw Saban Entertainment becoming BVS Entertainment in 2002, from <A href="/wiki/News_Corporation" title="News Corporation">News Corporation</A>, Fox's parent company, and <A href="/wiki/Haim_Saban" title="Haim Saban">Haim Saban</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-buyout_15-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-buyout-15">[10]</A></SUP> The show continued to air on Fox until the company replaced its <A href="/wiki/Fox_Kids" title="Fox Kids">Fox Kids</A> package with "FoxBox" in the United States. Since September 2002, all <I>Power Rangers</I> shows had aired on various Disney-owned networks (<A href="/wiki/ABC_Kids_(United_States)" title="ABC Kids (United States)">ABC Kids</A>, <A href="/wiki/Toon_Disney" title="Toon Disney">Toon Disney</A> and <A href="/wiki/Jetix" title="Jetix">Jetix</A> channels worldwide).<SUP id="cite_ref-MMPR2010_12-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-MMPR2010-12">[7]</A></SUP> When <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Wild_Force" title="Power Rangers Wild Force">Wild Force</A></I> ended, Disney moved production of the franchise from Los Angeles to New Zealand. This resulted in the closure of MMPR Productions and the dismissal of many members of the production. From <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Ninja_Storm" title="Power Rangers Ninja Storm">Ninja Storm</A></I> to date, <I>Power Rangers</I> is produced in New Zealand. ABC Family, another Disney-owned network, also used to air <I>Power Rangers</I> until it did away with its Jetix timeslot after August 31, 2006. On February 12, 2009, Toon Disney ended in the wake of <A href="/wiki/Disney_XD" title="Disney XD">Disney XD</A>, ending cable airings of <I>Power Rangers</I> in certain areas of the United States. Several ABC affiliate broadcasting groups declined to air most of the <I>Power Rangers</I> series since 2006 due to the lack of FCC-compliant <A href="/wiki/E/I" title="E/I">educational and informational content</A> in the programs.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[11]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The Saban era seasons, starting with <I>In Space</I>, have gone under the "Saban's Power Rangers" moniker, up until <I>Time Force</I>. Since the re-acquisition of <I>Power Rangers</I> by Saban in 2010, this practice has continued once again starting with <I>Samurai</I>.</P>
<P>Starting in 2005, up until 2007, during its run on Jetix, <I>Power Rangers</I> reruns were aired under the moniker <I>Power Rangers Generations</I>, showcasing select episodes from <I>Mighty Morphin</I> through <I>Dino Thunder</I>.</P>
<P>An article in <I><A href="/wiki/The_New_Zealand_Herald" title="The New Zealand Herald">The New Zealand Herald</A></I> published on March 7, 2009, identified <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_RPM" title="Power Rangers RPM">Power Rangers RPM</A></I> as the last season of the <I>Power Rangers</I> run. Production manager Sally Campbell stated in an interview, "...at this stage we will not be shooting another season."<SUP id="cite_ref-lightsout_17-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-lightsout-17">[12]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[13]</A></SUP> A September 1, 2009, revision to <I><A href="/wiki/Disney_A_to_Z:_The_Official_Encyclopedia" class="mw-redirect" title="Disney A to Z: The Official Encyclopedia">Disney A to Z: The Official Encyclopedia</A></I> by Disney's head archivist <A href="/wiki/Dave_Smith_(archivist)" title="Dave Smith (archivist)">Dave Smith</A> states that "production of new episodes [of <I>Power Rangers</I>] ceased in 2009".<SUP id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-19">[14]</A></SUP> Production of <I>Power Rangers</I> ceased and the last<SUP class="plainlinks noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Power_Rangers&action=edit">[update]</A></SUP> series by BVS Entertainment, <I>RPM</I>, ended on December 26, 2009.<SUP id="cite_ref-lightsout_17-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-lightsout-17">[12]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On October 1, 2009, Bandai released a press release that Disney would re-broadcast <I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers">Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</A></I> starting in January 2010 on <A href="/wiki/ABC_Kids_(United_States)" title="ABC Kids (United States)">ABC Kids</A> in lieu of a new series utilizing footage from the <A href="/wiki/Samurai_Sentai_Shinkenger" title="Samurai Sentai Shinkenger">2009 <I>Super Sentai</I> television series</A>. A new toy line accompanied the series and appeared in stores in the later part of 2009.<SUP id="cite_ref-MMPR2010_12-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-MMPR2010-12">[7]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Bandai_MMPR_20-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Bandai_MMPR-20">[15]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-businesswire_21-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-businesswire-21">[16]</A></SUP> ABC's over-the air telecasts ended on August 28, 2010, and turned the hour back to affiliates.</P>
<P>On May 12, 2010, <A href="/wiki/Haim_Saban" title="Haim Saban">Haim Saban</A> bought back the <I>Power Rangers</I> franchise from Disney for $43 million and announced plans to produce a new season of the television series.<SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[17]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-buy_back_23-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-buy_back-23">[18]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-24">[19]</A></SUP> The eighteenth season, <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Samurai" title="Power Rangers Samurai">Samurai</A></I>, began airing on <A href="/wiki/Nickelodeon" title="Nickelodeon">Nickelodeon</A> on February 7, 2011,<SUP id="cite_ref-buy_back_23-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-buy_back-23">[18]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-cast_and_premiere_25-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-cast_and_premiere-25">[20]</A></SUP> with the previous episodes beginning rebroadcast on <A href="/wiki/Nicktoons_(TV_channel)" title="Nicktoons (TV channel)">Nicktoons</A> later that year.<SUP id="cite_ref-cast_and_premiere_25-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-cast_and_premiere-25">[20]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-26">[21]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-27">[22]</A></SUP> It was also announced that Saban plans to make a new Power Rangers movie.<SUP id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-28">[23]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On July 2, 2012, it was announced that <A href="/wiki/Saban_Capital_Group" title="Saban Capital Group">Saban Brands</A> would launch a <A href="/wiki/Saturday_morning_cartoon" class="mw-redirect" title="Saturday morning cartoon">Saturday morning cartoon</A> block on <A href="/wiki/The_CW_Television_Network" class="mw-redirect" title="The CW Television Network">The CW</A>, called <A href="/wiki/Vortexx" title="Vortexx">Vortexx</A>, on August 25, 2012, that would air <I>Power Rangers Lost Galaxy</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-29">[24]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-30">[25]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-31">[26]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-32">[27]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-33">[28]</A></SUP> To commemorate the series' 20th anniversary, Nickelodeon began airing <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Megaforce" title="Power Rangers Megaforce">Power Rangers Megaforce</A></I> on February 2, 2013, featuring all of the past rangers from the series' 20-year history. On October 1, 2013, Saban Brands announced that it had extended agreements with Nickelodeon and Bandai America Incorporated through 2016 for its globally recognized Power Rangers franchise.<SUP id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-34">[29]</A></SUP> In January 2016, Saban and Nickelodeon extended their broadcast partnership through 2018.<SUP id="cite_ref-35" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-35">[30]</A></SUP></P>
<P><A href="/wiki/The_90s_Are_All_That" class="mw-redirect" title="The 90s Are All That">The 90s Are All That</A> aired <I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers">Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</A></I> as part of Mighty Morphin Weekend in 2013.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Television_series">Television series</SPAN></H2>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/List_of_Power_Rangers_episodes" title="List of Power Rangers episodes">List of Power Rangers episodes</A></DIV>

Variations of Power Rangers throughout the franchise unite.</DIV>

<P>The first series <I>Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</I> through <I>In Space</I> followed a <A href="/wiki/Story_arc" title="Story arc">story arc</A> called "The Zordon Era" with a gradually changing cast and characters over six years. Beginning with <I>Lost Galaxy</I>, although it had ties with the previous story arc, each <I>Power Rangers</I> series had its own self-contained <A href="/wiki/Plot_(narrative)" title="Plot (narrative)">storylines</A>, independent of previous series. <A href="/wiki/Fictional_crossover" class="mw-redirect" title="Fictional crossover">Crossover</A> episodes between different series featuring rangers, villains, and other characters from past seasons also began with <I>Lost Galaxy</I>, with a few exceptions.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="The_Saban_Era">The Saban Era</SPAN></H3>
<P>The Saban Era is seasons 1-10 that includes <I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers">Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</A></I> (1993-1996) to <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Wild_Force" title="Power Rangers Wild Force">Power Rangers Wild Force</A></I> (2002). These series aired on <A href="/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company" title="Fox Broadcasting Company">Fox</A> during the <A href="/wiki/Fox_Kids" title="Fox Kids">Fox Kids</A> programming block. The Zordon Era is <I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers">Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</A></I> to <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_in_Space" title="Power Rangers in Space">Power Rangers in Space</A></I>.</P>
<UL>
<LI><SPAN id="Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers"></SPAN><I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers">Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</A></I> (1993–1996)
<UL>
<LI>Season 1: When the evil witch <A href="/wiki/Rita_Repulsa" title="Rita Repulsa">Rita Repulsa</A> and her minions <A href="/wiki/Goldar" class="mw-redirect" title="Goldar">Goldar</A>, Squatt, Baboo, and Finster, are freed from their imprisonment on the Moon, the wizard <A href="/wiki/Zordon" title="Zordon">Zordon</A>, with the help of his assistant <A href="/wiki/Alpha_5_(Power_Rangers)" class="mw-redirect" title="Alpha 5 (Power Rangers)">Alpha 5</A>, enlists five teenagers—<A href="/wiki/Jason_Lee_Scott" title="Jason Lee Scott">Jason Lee Scott</A>, <A href="/wiki/Trini_Kwan" title="Trini Kwan">Trini Kwan</A>, <A href="/wiki/Billy_Cranston" title="Billy Cranston">Billy Cranston</A>, <A href="/wiki/Kimberly_Hart" title="Kimberly Hart">Kimberly Hart</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Zack_Taylor" title="Zack Taylor">Zack Taylor</A>—to become the Mighty Morphin Power Rangers to battle Rita's invasion of the Earth, using their Power Coins and Dinozords to combat her monsters. Rita soon creates her own evil Power Ranger by brainwashing a recent transfer student <A href="/wiki/Tommy_Oliver" title="Tommy Oliver">Tommy Oliver</A>, but the Power Rangers are able to free him from her control and he joins their side. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Ky%C5%8Dryu_Sentai_Zyuranger" class="mw-redirect" title="Kyōryu Sentai Zyuranger">Kyōryu Sentai Zyuranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI>Season 2: Rita's superior <A href="/wiki/Lord_Zedd" class="mw-redirect" title="Lord Zedd">Lord Zedd</A> returns to the Earth to take over for Rita's incompetence, imprisoning her once more. His new monsters prove too powerful for the Dinozords, leading Zordon to empower them into the Thunderzords. Jason, Trini, and Zack leave to join a youth conference in Switzerland, and are replaced by Rocky DeSantos, Aisha Campbell, and <A href="/wiki/Adam_Park" title="Adam Park">Adam Park</A>, respectively, and Rita returns and marries Lord Zedd. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Gosei_Sentai_Dairanger" title="Gosei Sentai Dairanger">Gosei Sentai Dairanger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers:_The_Movie" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie">Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie</A></I> (1995): When the evil wizard <A href="/wiki/Ivan_Ooze" class="mw-redirect" title="Ivan Ooze">Ivan Ooze</A> is freed by construction work, he takes revenge against Zordon for imprisoning him. As his powers are too strong for the Power Rangers, Alpha 5 uses the last of the Command Center's power to send them to the planet Phaedos to learn the ways of the Ninjetti from the warrior Dulcea to stop Ooze before he can conquer the universe. The movie, which does not fall into the canon of the TV series, drew inspiration from <I><A href="/wiki/Ninja_Sentai_Kakuranger" title="Ninja Sentai Kakuranger">Ninja Sentai Kakuranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI>Season 3: Rita's brother <A href="/wiki/Rito_Revolto" class="mw-redirect" title="Rito Revolto">Rito Revolto</A> comes to Earth and destroys the Power Rangers' Power Coins and Thunderzords. The Power Rangers seek out <A href="/wiki/Ninjor_(Power_Rangers)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ninjor (Power Rangers)">Ninjor</A>, creator of the Power Coins, for new Power Coins giving them new ninja powers and the Ninjazords, and later the Shogunzords. Rita also enchants a new Australian exchange student Kat Hillard into slowly draining Kimberly of her Ranger powers, until the spell is broken; when Kimberly ultimately leaves to train for the Olympics, she entrusts Kat to be her replacement amongst the Power Rangers. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Ninja_Sentai_Kakuranger" title="Ninja Sentai Kakuranger">Ninja Sentai Kakuranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Alien_Rangers" title="Mighty Morphin Alien Rangers">Mighty Morphin Alien Rangers</A></I> (1996): When Rita's father Master Vile comes to Earth, he turns back time, turning the Power Rangers, and many of their friends, into children. Zordon calls upon his proteges the Alien Rangers of Aquitar to protect the Earth from Master Vile's monsters and to help work on a machine that would return the child rangers to their proper ages. Unfortunately, Only Billy returns to normal as the machine which required the power coins as a power source is stolen by Rito & Goldar allowing Rita & Zedd to destroy the coins. The child rangers then travel throughout time to gather the fragments of the Zeo Crystal to bring time back to normal. During her journey in Africa, Aisha meets Tanya Sloan and realizes that she can do more help to stop the sickness plaguing the wildlife and sends Tanya back with her Zeo Crystal. This series also uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Ninja_Sentai_Kakuranger" title="Ninja Sentai Kakuranger">Ninja Sentai Kakuranger</A></I>.</LI>
</UL>
</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Zeo" title="Power Rangers Zeo">Power Rangers Zeo</A></I> (1996): With the Zeo Crystal restored, time brought back to normal, and Master Vile defeated, the Rangers are caught off guard when Goldar and Rito destroy their headquarters. Although Zordon reveals he is fine, he warns the Rangers that the <A href="/wiki/Machine_Empire" title="Machine Empire">Machine Empire</A> is planning on conquering the Earth, and the Rangers must use the power of the Zeo Crystal to become the Zeo Rangers to battle them. Billy, who used his scientific prowess to return to his original age during <I>Alien Rangers</I>, decides to work on the Zeo Zords and other machinery, and his presence in the destruction of the previous Command Center leaves him unable to receive the powers of the Gold Ranger, <A href="/wiki/Trey_of_Triforia" class="mw-redirect" title="Trey of Triforia">Trey of Triforia</A>, but Jason returns instead. Billy soon begins to age rapidly, a side effect from the regenerator, he used to return to his normal age, and leaves Earth to be healed on Aquitar. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Ch%C5%8Driki_Sentai_Ohranger" class="mw-redirect" title="Chōriki Sentai Ohranger">Chōriki Sentai Ohranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Turbo:_A_Power_Rangers_Movie" title="Turbo: A Power Rangers Movie">Turbo: A Power Rangers Movie</A></I> (1997): The intergalactic pirate <A href="/wiki/Divatox" class="mw-redirect" title="Divatox">Divatox</A> kidnaps the wizard Lerigot to open a dimensional barrier so she can wed the demon Maligore. To stop her, Zordon gives the Rangers their new Turbo Ranger powers to stop her. Rocky, however, has been hurt, and in his stead Zordon sends <A href="/wiki/Justin_Stewart" class="mw-redirect" title="Justin Stewart">Justin Stewart</A>, a young boy who inadvertently discovers the Rangers' identities. This film drew inspiration from <I><A href="/wiki/Gekisou_Sentai_Carranger" title="Gekisou Sentai Carranger">Gekisou Sentai Carranger</A></I> and serves as a bridge to the subsequent TV season.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Turbo" title="Power Rangers Turbo">Power Rangers Turbo</A></I> (1997): After Divatox's plans are foiled, she sets her sights on conquering the Earth, with the Turbo Rangers and eventually the intergalactic police officer the <A href="/wiki/Blue_Senturion" class="mw-redirect" title="Blue Senturion">Blue Senturion</A> combatting her monsters. Tommy, Adam, Tanya, and Kat soon retire from being Power Rangers, choosing <A href="/wiki/T.J._Johnson" class="mw-redirect" title="T.J. Johnson">T.J. Johnson</A>, <A href="/wiki/Carlos_Vallerte" class="mw-redirect" title="Carlos Vallerte">Carlos Vallerte</A>, <A href="/wiki/Ashley_Hammond" class="mw-redirect" title="Ashley Hammond">Ashley Hammond</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Cassie_Chan" class="mw-redirect" title="Cassie Chan">Cassie Chan</A> as their replacements, who are also assisted by the <A href="/wiki/Phantom_Ranger" class="mw-redirect" title="Phantom Ranger">Phantom Ranger</A>. Zordon also leaves, putting <A href="/wiki/Dimitria" class="mw-redirect" title="Dimitria">Dimitria</A> in his place. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Gekisou_Sentai_Carranger" title="Gekisou Sentai Carranger">Gekisou Sentai Carranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_in_Space" title="Power Rangers in Space">Power Rangers in Space</A></I> (1998): After Divatox succeeds in destroying the Command Center, she is called off planet to participate in Dark Specter's evil alliance in conquering the universe. T.J., Carlos, Ashley, and Cassie travel into outer space to try to stop him, and meet up with <A href="/wiki/Andros_(Power_Rangers)" class="mw-redirect" title="Andros (Power Rangers)">Andros</A>, who they join to become the Space Rangers to stop Dark Specter and his protege <A href="/wiki/Astronema" class="mw-redirect" title="Astronema">Astronema</A>. They eventually awaken Andros' friend Zhane, the Silver Ranger, and free Andros' sister <A href="/wiki/Karone" class="mw-redirect" title="Karone">Karone</A> (Astronema) from Dark Specter's control and ultimately use Zordon, captured by Dark Specter, to defeat Dark Specter's armies and free the universe from his control. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Denji_Sentai_Megaranger" title="Denji Sentai Megaranger">Denji Sentai Megaranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Lost_Galaxy" title="Power Rangers Lost Galaxy">Power Rangers Lost Galaxy</A></I> (1999): The governments of the Earth decide to send out an experimental space colony Terra Venture, on which Leo Corbett stows away to join his brother Mike on the journey to find new planets. When it encounters a wormhole on the Moon, Leo, Mike, Kai Chen, and Kendrix Morgan go through it and encounter Maya and her planet Mirinoi which is under attack from Scorpius and his minions, led by Trakeena. After Leo, Mike, and Kendrix are stranded, Kai commandeers the Astro Megaship along with its mechanic Damon Henderson to save them. Mike, Kai, Damon, Maya, and Kendrix are chosen by the Quasar Sabers to fight Scorpius, but Mike seemingly falls to his death, leaving Leo to act as the leader of the Galaxy Rangers in his stead back on Terra Venture. Mike later returns after it is revealed the <A href="/wiki/Magna_Defender" class="mw-redirect" title="Magna Defender">Magna Defender</A> has been using his body as a vessel to fight Scorpius' monsters along with the Galaxy Rangers. Mid-season, Deviot revives the Psycho Rangers and the space rangers come to help. Kendrix ultimately dies while saving the Pink Space Ranger, Cassie and is replaced by Karone. They later must fight Captain Mutiny and his space pirates after they are transported to the Lost Galaxy. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Seijuu_Sentai_Gingaman" title="Seijuu Sentai Gingaman">Seijuu Sentai Gingaman</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Lightspeed_Rescue" title="Power Rangers Lightspeed Rescue">Power Rangers Lightspeed Rescue</A></I> (2000): Carter Grayson, Chad Lee, Joel Rawlings, Kelsey Winslow, and Dana Mitchell are hired by Operation Lightspeed to protect Mariner Bay from a group of evil demons led by Queen Bansheera from taking over the world by fighting as the Lightspeed Rangers. They are later joined by Dana's long lost brother Ryan. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Kyuukyuu_Sentai_GoGoFive" title="Kyuukyuu Sentai GoGoFive">Kyuukyuu Sentai GoGoFive</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Time_Force" title="Power Rangers Time Force">Power Rangers Time Force</A></I> (2001): When the mutant Ransik and his daughter Nadira escape custody of the Time Force police in the year 3000 by stealing the very prison, they travel back in time to 2001, but not before seemingly killing the Red Time Force Ranger Alex. His subordinates Jen Scotts, Lucas Kendall, Katie Walker, and Trip travel back in time to 2001 and seek out Alex's ancestor Wes Collins, as his DNA unlocks the Time Force Morphers, allowing all of them to become the Time Force Power Rangers to recapture the mutants Ransik uses to thwart them and stop the Bio-Lab who ended up creating him. They are ultimately joined by Eric Myers, who uses the Quantum Morpher and Q-Rex to fight. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Mirai_Sentai_Timeranger" title="Mirai Sentai Timeranger">Mirai Sentai Timeranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Wild_Force" title="Power Rangers Wild Force">Power Rangers Wild Force</A></I> (2002): Jungle man Cole Evans, Air Force pilot Taylor Earhardt, would-be pro-bowler Max Cooper, florist Danny Delgado, and martial artist Alyssa Enrilé are chosen by Princess Shayla of the floating island Animaria to be the Wild Force Power Rangers to fight the evil Orgs. They are later joined by Merrick Baliton, one of the original Wild Force Power Rangers who used a forbidden power to defeat the Master Org 3,000 years in the past, after he is freed from the power in the present. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Hyakujuu_Sentai_Gaoranger" title="Hyakujuu Sentai Gaoranger">Hyakujuu Sentai Gaoranger</A></I>. <I>Wild Force</I> featured an anniversary commemoration episode in "<A href="/wiki/Forever_Red" class="mw-redirect" title="Forever Red">Forever Red</A>", featuring the return of nearly every Red Ranger.
<UL>
<LI><I>Wild Force</I> marked a shift from <A href="/wiki/Saban_Entertainment" title="Saban Entertainment">Saban Entertainment</A> to <A href="/wiki/BVS_Entertainment" class="mw-redirect" title="BVS Entertainment">BVS Entertainment</A> in production and distribution and was the last season to be filmed in the United States.</LI>
</UL>
</LI>
</UL>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="The_Disney_Era">The Disney Era</SPAN></H3>
<P>The Disney Era is seasons 11-17 that includes <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Ninja_Storm" title="Power Rangers Ninja Storm">Power Rangers Ninja Storm</A></I> (2003) to <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_RPM" title="Power Rangers RPM">Power Rangers RPM</A></I> (2009). These series aired on various <A href="/wiki/Disney" class="mw-redirect" title="Disney">Disney</A> television networks.</P>
<UL>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Ninja_Storm" title="Power Rangers Ninja Storm">Power Rangers Ninja Storm</A></I> (2003): Shane Clarke, Tori Hanson, and Dustin Brooks are bumbling students of Kanoi Watanabe's Wind Ninja Academy, but when Lothor kidnaps the other students, they are all that remain to protect the Earth from Lothor's evil space ninjas as the Wind Rangers. They are also joined in battle by adopted brothers Hunter and Blake Bradley of the rival Thunder Ninja Academy as the Thunder Rangers and Kanoi's son Cam as the Samurai Ranger. aired in 2003. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Ninpuu_Sentai_Hurricaneger" title="Ninpuu Sentai Hurricaneger">Ninpuu Sentai Hurricaneger</A></I>.
<UL>
<LI><I>Ninja Storm</I> is the first season to be filmed in <A href="/wiki/New_Zealand" title="New Zealand">New Zealand</A>.</LI>
</UL>
</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Dino_Thunder" title="Power Rangers Dino Thunder">Power Rangers Dino Thunder</A></I> (2004): When the evil Mesogog appears to bring the Earth back to the Mesozoic age, Dr. Tommy Oliver of Reefside reluctantly enlists his students Conner McKnight, Ethan James, and Kira Ford to battle him as the Dino Rangers. Tommy later joins them as a Ranger, once more, as well as Trent Fernandez-Mercer, adopted son of Tommy's once colleague Dr. Anton Mercer, who is Mesogog's alterego. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Bakuryuu_Sentai_Abaranger" class="mw-redirect" title="Bakuryuu Sentai Abaranger">Bakuryuu Sentai Abaranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_S.P.D." title="Power Rangers S.P.D.">Power Rangers S.P.D.</A></I> (2005): In the year 2025, the Space Patrol Delta police force protects the galaxy from the Troobian Empire's forces. When their A-Squad of Power Rangers fall in battle, B-Squad members Sky Tate, Bridge Carson, and Syd Drew are joined by rookies Jack Landors and Z Delgado under the direction of Commander Anubis Cruger to be the S.P.D. Power Rangers. They are later joined by Sam, a young boy they save from the Troobian Empire who in the future becomes the Omega Ranger, as well as Cmdr. Cruger as the Shadow Ranger and technical expert Dr. Kat Manx as the Kat Ranger. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Tokusou_Sentai_Dekaranger" title="Tokusou Sentai Dekaranger">Tokusou Sentai Dekaranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Mystic_Force" title="Power Rangers Mystic Force">Power Rangers Mystic Force</A></I> (2006): The sorceress Udonna enlists the help of Chip Thorn, Madison Rocca, Vida Rocca, Xander Bly, and new guy in town Nick Russell to become the Mystic Rangers to protect Briarwood and its nearby magical forest from the evil forces of Morticon, who plans on taking over both the magical and human worlds. They are eventually joined by Udonna's old friend Daggeron and his genie Jenji, and Udonna and her long lost husband Leanbow, who has been trapped as the evil Koragg since falling in battle 20 years prior. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Mahou_Sentai_Magiranger" title="Mahou Sentai Magiranger">Mahou Sentai Magiranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Operation_Overdrive" title="Power Rangers Operation Overdrive">Power Rangers Operation Overdrive</A></I> (2007): Wealthy adventurer Andrew Hartford tasks Will Aston, Dax Lo, Ronny Robinson, Rose Ortiz, and reluctantly his own son Mack to act as the Overdrive Rangers, searching for the jewels of the Corona Aurora before either Flurious or Moltor, and later Kamdor and the Fearcats can. They are later joined by Tyzonn, member of a search and rescue team from the planet Mercuria, who has a past with the Fearcats. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/GoGo_Sentai_Boukenger" title="GoGo Sentai Boukenger">GoGo Sentai Boukenger</A></I>. <I>Operation Overdrive</I> also featured an anniversary episode in "<A href="/wiki/Once_a_Ranger" class="mw-redirect" title="Once a Ranger">Once a Ranger</A>", bringing back several characters from previous seasons.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Jungle_Fury" title="Power Rangers Jungle Fury">Power Rangers Jungle Fury</A></I> (2008): The Pai Zhua, or "Order of the Claw", has protected the world from the evil spirit of Dai Shi for nearly ten thousand years. When Jarrod, Lily Chilman, and Theo Martin are chosen by Master Mao to guard the container of Dai Shi's spirit, Jarrod is deemed unworthy and replaced by rookie or "cub" member Casey Rhodes. Angered by this slight, Jarrod attempts to steal Dai Shi's vessel, only to become possessed by his spirit. Mao, who falls in battle, entrusts in best student R.J. to lead the others as the Jungle Fury Power Rangers to stop Dai Shi from taking over the world. R.J. later joins them in battle, as does Dom Hargan, a former Pai Zhua student who went to find his path in life. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Juken_Sentai_Gekiranger" title="Juken Sentai Gekiranger">Juken Sentai Gekiranger</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_RPM" title="Power Rangers RPM">Power Rangers RPM</A></I> (2009): A malicious and rapidly evolving computer virus known as Venjix has ravaged the Earth, leaving the surviving members of humanity to huddle for safety in the force field protected city of Corinth. To stop Venjix's attacks, led by his humanoid warrior Tenaya, the mysterious Doctor K enlists Scott Truman, Flynn McAllistair, Summer Landsdown, and reluctantly Ziggy Grover and the apparent cyborg Dillon as the RPM Ranger Operators. They are later joined by Gem and Gemma, Doctor K's old friends. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Engine_Sentai_Go-onger" title="Engine Sentai Go-onger">Engine Sentai Go-onger</A></I>.
<UL>
<LI><I>RPM</I> was the last season to be produced by BVS Entertainment.</LI>
</UL>
</LI>
<LI>In 2010, a re-versioned edit of <I>Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</I> aired. During this year, <A href="/wiki/Saban_Brands" class="mw-redirect" title="Saban Brands">Saban Brands</A> bought back the rights to <I>Power Rangers</I>.</LI>
</UL>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="The_Neo-Saban_Era">The Neo-Saban Era</SPAN></H3>
<P>The Neo-Saban Era began in season 18 and continues to present starting with <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Samurai" title="Power Rangers Samurai">Power Rangers Samurai</A></I>. These series aired on <A href="/wiki/Nickelodeon" title="Nickelodeon">Nickelodeon</A>.</P>
<UL>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Samurai" title="Power Rangers Samurai">Power Rangers Samurai</A></I> and <I><A href="/wiki/List_of_Power_Rangers_Super_Samurai_episodes" title="List of Power Rangers Super Samurai episodes">Super Samurai</A></I> (2011–2012): In order to prevent Master Xandred's Nighlok forces from taking over the Earth, Mentor Ji of the Shiba House trains Jayden, Kevin, Mia, Mike, and Emily in the ways of the samurai to fight as the Samurai Power Rangers. They are later joined by Jayden's childhood friend Antonio as the Gold Ranger, who is instrumental in unlocking the group's Super Mode. These two seasons use footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Samurai_Sentai_Shinkenger" title="Samurai Sentai Shinkenger">Samurai Sentai Shinkenger</A></I>.
<UL>
<LI><I>Samurai</I> is the first season back under the ownership of Saban and the first season produced by SCG Power Rangers. <I>Power Rangers</I> continues to be produced and filmed in New Zealand.</LI>
</UL>
</LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Megaforce" title="Power Rangers Megaforce">Power Rangers Megaforce</A></I> (2013): Zordon's protege Gosei calls on high school students Troy Burrows, Noah Carver, Jake Holling, Emma Goodall, and Gia Moran to become the Megaforce Power Rangers to battle the invasion of the Warstar Empire. They are later joined by the Robo Knight in his fight against the Toxic Mutants. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Tensou_Sentai_Goseiger" title="Tensou Sentai Goseiger">Tensou Sentai Goseiger</A></I>.
<UL>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/List_of_Power_Rangers_Super_Megaforce_episodes" title="List of Power Rangers Super Megaforce episodes">Super Megaforce</A></I> (2014): With the Warstar Empire's forces increasing their invasion, Gosei gives the Rangers new morphers to assume Super Mega Mode, allowing them to call on the powers of all of the previous Power Rangers. They are joined by Orion, a citizen from the planet Andresia. <I>Super Megaforce</I> also features the return of several previous characters. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Kaizoku_Sentai_Gokaiger" title="Kaizoku Sentai Gokaiger">Kaizoku Sentai Gokaiger</A></I>.</LI>
</UL>
</LI>
<LI><SPAN id="Dino_Charge"></SPAN><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Dino_Charge" title="Power Rangers Dino Charge">Power Rangers Dino Charge</A></I> and <I><A href="/wiki/List_of_Power_Rangers_Dino_Super_Charge_episodes" title="List of Power Rangers Dino Super Charge episodes">Dino Super Charge</A></I> (2015–2016): When an intergalactic bounty hunter comes to Earth looking for the Energems, entrusted to an alien who lost them during the asteroid bombardment that resulted in the <A href="/wiki/Extinction_of_the_dinosaurs" class="mw-redirect" title="Extinction of the dinosaurs">extinction of the dinosaurs</A>, the Dino Charge Power Rangers are formed to find the Energems first. These two seasons use footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Zyuden_Sentai_Kyoryuger" title="Zyuden Sentai Kyoryuger">Zyuden Sentai Kyoryuger</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-USA_Today_36-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-USA_Today-36">[31]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Ninja_Steel" title="Power Rangers Ninja Steel">Power Rangers Ninja Steel</A></I> and <I>Super Ninja Steel</I> (2017-2018): The Power Rangers are protecting an item called the Ninja Nexus Prism from the forces of Galvanax, the champion of the universe's most popular intergalactic game show, who wants the Prism, which contains six magical Ninja Power Throwing Stars, to become invincible. The Rangers must master the arsenal of throwing stars, Zords, and Megazords, all made from the titular legendary "ninja steel", to stop Galvanax's warrior contestants sent to Earth to retrieve the Prism, the Steel and the Power Stars for him. This season uses footage from <I><A href="/wiki/Shuriken_Sentai_Ninninger" title="Shuriken Sentai Ninninger">Shuriken Sentai Ninninger</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-37">[32]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-38">[33]</A></SUP></LI>
</UL>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Distribution">Distribution</SPAN></H2>
<P><I>Power Rangers</I> has long had success in international markets and continues to air in many countries, with the exception of New Zealand, where the series filming takes place as of 2009<SUP class="plainlinks noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Power_Rangers&action=edit">[update]</A></SUP>. As of 2006, <I>Power Rangers</I> aired at least 65 times a week in more than 40 worldwide markets.<SUP id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-42">[37]</A></SUP> Many markets carry or have carried the series on their respective <A href="/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company" title="Fox Broadcasting Company">Fox</A> or later <A href="/wiki/Jetix" title="Jetix">Jetix</A>/<A href="/wiki/Disney_XD" title="Disney XD">Disney XD</A> channels or have syndicated the program on regional children's channels or blocks, either dubbed into the local language or broadcast in the original English. Since the 2010 acquisition by Saban Brands, international television distribution rights for Power Rangers have been managed by <A href="/wiki/MarVista_Entertainment" title="MarVista Entertainment">MarVista Entertainment</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-43">[38]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-44">[39]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-45" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-45">[40]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Broadcast in East Asian territories has been treated differently from in other international markets due to the prevalence and familiarity of 'the <I>Super Sentai</I> brand originating in Japan. <I>Power Rangers</I> was briefly banned in Malaysia for supposedly encouraging the use of drugs because it contained the word "Morphin'" in its title, which could be associated with <A href="/wiki/Morphine" title="Morphine">morphine</A>. The show eventually aired without the offending word.<SUP id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-46">[41]</A></SUP> In Japan, many <I>Power Rangers</I> television seasons and movies were dubbed into Japanese for television and video with the voice actors often pulled from past <I>Super Sentai</I> casts, leading to the English-dubbed <A href="/wiki/Stage_combat" title="Stage combat">action sequences</A> being "re-dubbed" or "restored" back to Japanese as well. <I>Power Rangers Mystic Force</I> is the latest season to be broadcast in Japan on <A href="/w/index.php?title=Toei_Channel&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Toei Channel (page does not exist)">Toei Channel</A> in January 2014, with the <I>Magiranger</I> cast voicing their counterparts. After broadcast of <I>Power Rangers</I> ended in South Korea with <I>Wild Force</I>, Bandai of Korea started airing <A href="/wiki/Super_Sentai#South_Korea" title="Super Sentai">dubbed <I>Super Sentai</I> series</A> under the <I>파워레인저</I> <I>(Power Ranger)</I> brand on <A href="/w/index.php?title=JEI_TV&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="JEI TV (page does not exist)">JEI TV</A>. Some seasons of <I>Super Sentai</I> broadcast in South Korea have similarly named titles as their American counterparts, such as <I>Power Ranger Dino Thunder</I><SUP id="cite_ref-47" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-47">[42]</A></SUP> for <I>Abaranger</I> in 2007 and <I>Power Ranger S.P.D.</I><SUP id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-48">[43]</A></SUP> in place of <I>Dekaranger</I>.</P>

<P>Internationally, additional DVD releases have occurred (such as <I>Lightspeed Rescue</I>, <I>Time Force</I> and <I>Wild Force</I> in Germany) and as free DVDs attached to the <I>Jetix</I> magazine, published in the UK. <I>Mighty Morphin Power Rangers Season 1</I>, <I>Season 2</I>, and <I>Season 3</I>, <I>Power Rangers Zeo</I>, <I>Power Rangers Turbo</I>, and <I>Power Rangers In Space</I> have id="cite_ref-56" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-56">[51]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-57">[52]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><A complete boxset releases in the UK.<SUP id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-62">[57]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-63">[58]</A></SUP><SUP 3</I> were released in May 2008.<SUP id="cite_ref-67" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-67">[62]</A></SUP> In Italy, <I>Mighty Morphin</I>, <I>Zeo</I>, <I>Dino Thunder</I> and <I>S.P.D.</I> have appeared in their entirety. <I>Zeo</I> and <I>S.P.D.</I> were made available as commercial DVDs, while <I>Mighty Morphin</I> and <I>Dino Thunder</I> were issued as bi-weekly volumes at newsstands.</P>
<P>The <A href="/wiki/ITunes_Store" title="ITunes Store">iTunes Store</A> previously made Power Rangers episodes available: part of <I><A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers">Mighty Morphin Power Rangers</A></I>, all of <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_S.P.D." title="Power Rangers S.P.D.">Power Rangers S.P.D.</A></I>, and the first 26 episodes of <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Mystic_Force" title="Power Rangers Mystic Force">Power Rangers Mystic Force</A></I>. Subsequent seasons and episodes of the program also made their appearances in the iTunes Store, but as of July 2009<SUP class="plainlinks noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Power_Rangers&action=edit">[update]</A></SUP>, <I><A href="/wiki/Turbo:_A_Power_Rangers_Movie" title="Turbo: A Power Rangers Movie">Turbo: A Power Rangers Movie</A></I> is the only Power Rangers film available. In 2012, Mighty Morphin Power Rangers Season 1 volumes 1 & 2 were released on iTunes to coincide with the DVD releases. As of February 2013, all 3 seasons of <I>MMPR</I> were released on iTunes.</P>
<P>On June 15, 2011, all episodes of Power Rangers from <A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers_(season_1)" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers (season 1)"><I>Mighty Morphin Power Rangers Season 1</I></A> to <A href="/wiki/Mighty_Morphin_Power_Rangers_(re-version)" title="Mighty Morphin Power Rangers (re-version)"><I>Mighty Morphin Power Rangers re-version</I></A> were made available for instant streaming on Netflix.<SUP id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-68">[63]</A></SUP> As of 2017, all seasons through <I>Dino Super Charge</I> have been made available on Netflix.</P>
<P>On March 12, 2012, <A href="/wiki/Shout!_Factory" title="Shout! Factory">Shout! Factory</A> announced a home video distribution deal with Saban, which includes the first 17 series of Power Rangers. Shout! Factory released the first seven seasons on DVD in August 2012,<SUP id="cite_ref-69" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-69">[64]</A></SUP> seasons 8-12 on November 2013,<SUP id="cite_ref-70" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-70">[65]</A></SUP> a 20-year collection on December 2013,<SUP id="cite_ref-71" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-71">[66]</A></SUP> and seasons 13-17 on April 2014.<SUP id="cite_ref-72" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-72">[67]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On March 22, 2012 <A href="/wiki/Lionsgate_Home_Entertainment" title="Lionsgate Home Entertainment">Lionsgate Home Entertainment</A> reached a home media distribution deal with Saban to release <I><A href="/wiki/Power_Rangers_Samurai" title="Power Rangers Samurai">Power Rangers Samurai</A></I> to DVD and Blu-ray.<SUP id="cite_ref-73" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-73">[68]</A></SUP></P>
<P>As of April 2015<SUP class="plainlinks noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Power_Rangers&action=edit">[update]</A></SUP>, all series through <I>Super Megaforce</I> are available on the <A href="/wiki/ITunes_Store" title="ITunes Store">iTunes Store</A>.</P>
<P>As of 2016<SUP class="plainlinks noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Power_Rangers&action=edit">[update]</A></SUP>, <I>Dino Charge</I> became available on iTunes.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Broadcast">Broadcast</SPAN></H2>
<P>The series originally aired on <A href="/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company" title="Fox Broadcasting Company">Fox</A>'s children block, <A href="/wiki/Fox_Kids" title="Fox Kids">Fox Kids</A> from 1993-2002. When Disney bought the rights to Power Rangers, it moved to <A href="/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company" title="American Broadcasting Company">ABC</A>'s Saturday morning block, <A href="/wiki/ABC_Kids_(US)" class="mw-redirect" title="ABC Kids (US)">ABC Kids</A> from 2002-2010. During that time, all seasons aired on the <A href="/wiki/Freeform_(TV_channel)" title="Freeform (TV channel)">ABC Family</A> (now Freeform) and <A href="/wiki/Toon_Disney" title="Toon Disney">Toon Disney</A>'s block <A href="/wiki/Jetix" title="Jetix">Jetix</A>. When Saban bought Power Rangers back, the series aired new episodes on <A href="/wiki/Nickelodeon" title="Nickelodeon">Nickelodeon</A>, while previous seasons aired on <A href="/wiki/Nicktoons_(TV_channel)" title="Nicktoons (TV channel)">Nicktoons</A>.</P>

For other uses, see <A href="/wiki/ABO_(disambiguation)" class="mw-redirect mw-disambig" title="ABO (disambiguation)">ABO (disambiguation)</A>.</DIV>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">"H substance" redirects here. For use in inflammation, see <A href="/wiki/Histamine" title="Histamine">histamine</A>. For hydrogen atom, see <A href="/wiki/Hydrogen" title="Hydrogen">hydrogen</A>.</DIV>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:412px;"><A href="/wiki/File:ABO_blood_type.svg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/ABO_blood_type.svg/410px-ABO_blood_type.svg.png" width="410" height="264" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/ABO_blood_type.svg/615px-ABO_blood_type.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/ABO_blood_type.svg/820px-ABO_blood_type.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="824" data-file-height="530" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:ABO_blood_type.svg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
ABO blood group <A href="/wiki/Antigen" title="Antigen">antigens</A> present on <A href="/wiki/Red_blood_cell" title="Red blood cell">red blood cells</A> and <A href="/wiki/IgM" class="mw-redirect" title="IgM">IgM</A> <A href="/wiki/Antibodies" class="mw-redirect" title="Antibodies">antibodies</A> present in the <A href="/wiki/Blood_serum" class="mw-redirect" title="Blood serum">serum</A></DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>The <B>ABO blood group system</B> is used to denote the presence of one, both, or neither of the A and B <A href="/wiki/Antigen" title="Antigen">antigens</A> on <A href="/wiki/Erythrocyte" class="mw-redirect" title="Erythrocyte">erythrocytes</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-britannica_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-britannica-1">[1]</A></SUP> In human <A href="/wiki/Blood_transfusion" title="Blood transfusion">blood transfusions</A> it is the most important of the 35 different <A href="/wiki/Blood_type" title="Blood type">blood type</A> (or group) classification systems currently recognized.<SUP id="cite_ref-ISBT4.0_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ISBT4.0-2">[2]</A></SUP> A very rare (in modern medicine) mismatch in this, or any other <A href="/wiki/Serotype" title="Serotype">serotype</A>, can cause a serious, potentially fatal, <A href="/wiki/Blood_transfusion#Adverse_effects" title="Blood transfusion">adverse reaction</A> after a transfusion, or a contra-indicated immune response to an <A href="/wiki/Organ_transplantation" title="Organ transplantation">organ transplant</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid11532188_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid11532188-3">[3]</A></SUP> The associated anti-A and anti-B <A href="/wiki/Antibodies" class="mw-redirect" title="Antibodies">antibodies</A> are usually <A href="/wiki/IgM" class="mw-redirect" title="IgM">IgM</A> antibodies, which are produced in the first years of life by sensitization to environmental substances, such as food, bacteria, and viruses. ABO blood types are also present in some other <A href="/wiki/Blood_type_(non-human)" title="Blood type (non-human)">animals</A>, for example <A href="/wiki/Rodents" class="mw-redirect" title="Rodents">rodents</A> and <A href="/wiki/Ape" title="Ape">apes</A>, such as <A href="/wiki/Chimpanzee" title="Chimpanzee">chimpanzees</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bonobo" title="Bonobo">bonobos</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Gorilla" title="Gorilla">gorillas</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="History_of_discoveries_of_the_blood_types">History of discoveries of the blood types</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: History of discoveries of the blood types">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Jan_Jansk%C3%BD,_1902.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Jan_Jansk%C3%BD%2C_1902.jpg/170px-Jan_Jansk%C3%BD%2C_1902.jpg" width="170" height="244" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Jan_Jansk%C3%BD%2C_1902.jpg/255px-Jan_Jansk%C3%BD%2C_1902.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a2/Jan_Jansk%C3%BD%2C_1902.jpg 2x" data-file-width="258" data-file-height="370" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Jan_Jansk%C3%BD,_1902.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
<A href="/wiki/Czechs" title="Czechs">Czech</A> serologist <A href="/wiki/Jan_Jansk%C3%BD" title="Jan Janský">Jan Janský</A> is credited with the first classification of blood into the four types (I, II, III, IV)</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>The ABO blood group system is widely credited to have been discovered by the Austrian scientist <A href="/wiki/Karl_Landsteiner" title="Karl Landsteiner">Karl Landsteiner</A>, who identified the O, A, and B blood types in 1900.<SUP id="cite_ref-Tan_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Tan-5">[5]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Landsteiner_1900_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Landsteiner_1900-6">[6]</A></SUP> Landsteiner originally described the O blood type as type "C", and in parts of Europe it is rendered as "0" (zero), signifying the lack of A or B antigen. Landsteiner was awarded the <A href="/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine" title="Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine">Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine</A> in 1930 for his work.<SUP id="cite_ref-Tan_5-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Tan-5">[5]</A></SUP> <A href="/w/index.php?title=Alfred_von_Decastello&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Alfred von Decastello (page does not exist)">Alfred von Decastello</A> and <A href="/w/index.php?title=Adriano_Sturli&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Adriano Sturli (page does not exist)">Adriano Sturli</A> discovered the fourth type, AB, in 1902.<SUP id="cite_ref-von_Decastello_1902_7-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-von_Decastello_1902-7">[7]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP></P>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:UkrArmyBloodGroupIII%2B2000s.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/UkrArmyBloodGroupIII%2B2000s.jpg/220px-UkrArmyBloodGroupIII%2B2000s.jpg" width="220" height="57" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/UkrArmyBloodGroupIII%2B2000s.jpg/330px-UkrArmyBloodGroupIII%2B2000s.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/UkrArmyBloodGroupIII%2B2000s.jpg/440px-UkrArmyBloodGroupIII%2B2000s.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5952" data-file-height="1536" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:UkrArmyBloodGroupIII%2B2000s.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
<A href="/wiki/Ukraine" title="Ukraine">Ukraine</A> marine uniform imprint, showing the wearer's blood type as "B (III) Rh+"</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>It was subsequently found that the Czech serologist <A href="/wiki/Jan_Jansk%C3%BD" title="Jan Janský">Jan Janský</A> had independently pioneered the classification of human blood into four groups in 1907,<SUP id="cite_ref-Janský_1907_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Janský_1907-9">[9]</A></SUP> but Landsteiner's independent discovery had been accepted by the scientific world while Janský remained then in relative obscurity. However, in 1921 an American medical commission acknowledged Janský's classification. Jan Janský is nowadays credited with the first classification of blood into the four types (I, II, III, IV).</P>
<P>Janský's classification remains in use today. In Russia and states of the former <A href="/wiki/USSR" class="mw-redirect" title="USSR">USSR</A>, blood types O, A, B, and AB are respectively designated I, II, III, and IV.<SUP id="cite_ref-Erb_1940_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Erb_1940-10">[10]</A></SUP> The designation A and B with reference to blood groups was proposed by <A href="/wiki/Ludwik_Hirszfeld" title="Ludwik Hirszfeld">Ludwik Hirszfeld</A>.</P>
<P>In America, W.L. Moss published his own (very similar) work in 1910.<SUP id="cite_ref-Moss_1910_11-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Moss_1910-11">[11]</A></SUP></P>
<P><A href="/wiki/Ludwik_Hirszfeld" title="Ludwik Hirszfeld">Ludwik Hirszfeld</A> and <A href="/wiki/Emil_Freiherr_von_Dungern" class="mw-redirect" title="Emil Freiherr von Dungern">E. von Dungern</A> discovered the heritability of ABO blood groups in 1910–11. <A href="/wiki/Felix_Bernstein_(mathematician)" title="Felix Bernstein (mathematician)">Felix Bernstein</A> demonstrated the correct blood group inheritance pattern of multiple <A href="/wiki/Allele" title="Allele">alleles</A> at one locus in 1924.<SUP id="cite_ref-Crow_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Crow-12">[12]</A></SUP> Watkins and Morgan, in England, discovered that the ABO <A href="/wiki/Epitope" title="Epitope">epitopes</A> were conferred by sugars, to be specific, N-acetylgalactosamine for the A-type and galactose for the B-type.<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14">[14]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP> After much published literature claiming that the ABH substances were all attached to glycosphingolipids, Finne et al. (1978) found that the human erythrocyte glycoproteins contain polylactosamine chains<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP> that contains ABH substances attached and represent the majority of the antigens.<SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-19">[19]</A></SUP> The main glycoproteins carrying the ABH antigens were identified to be the Band 3 and Band 4.5 proteins and glycophorin.<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP> Later, Yamamoto's group showed the precise glycosyl transferase set that confers the A, B and O epitopes.<SUP id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-21">[21]</A></SUP></P>
