<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Alteration_of_ABO_antigens_for_transfusion">Alteration of ABO antigens for transfusion</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Alteration of ABO antigens for transfusion">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>In April 2007, an international team of researchers announced in the journal <I><A href="/wiki/Nature_Biotechnology" title="Nature Biotechnology">Nature Biotechnology</A></I> an inexpensive and efficient way to convert types A, B, and AB blood into type O.<SUP id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-23">[23]</A></SUP> This is done by using <A href="/wiki/Glycoside_hydrolase" title="Glycoside hydrolase">glycosidase</A> enzymes from specific bacteria to strip the blood group antigens from <A href="/wiki/Red_blood_cell" title="Red blood cell">red blood cells</A>. The removal of A and B antigens still does not address the problem of the <A href="/wiki/Rh_blood_group_system" title="Rh blood group system">Rh</A> blood group antigen on the blood cells of Rh positive individuals, and so blood from Rh negative donors must be used. Patient trials will be conducted before the method can be relied on in live situations.</P>
<P>Another approach to the blood antigen problem is the manufacture of <A href="/wiki/Artificial_blood" class="mw-redirect" title="Artificial blood">artificial blood</A>, which could act as a substitute in emergencies.<SUP id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-24">[24]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Genetics">Genetics</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Genetics">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV class="thumb tleft">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:282px;"><A href="/wiki/File:ABO_system_codominance.svg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/ABO_system_codominance.svg/280px-ABO_system_codominance.svg.png" width="280" height="279" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/ABO_system_codominance.svg/420px-ABO_system_codominance.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/ABO_system_codominance.svg/560px-ABO_system_codominance.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="942" data-file-height="938" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:ABO_system_codominance.svg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
A and B are <A href="/wiki/Dominance_relationship#Co-dominance" class="mw-redirect" title="Dominance relationship">codominant</A>, giving the AB <A href="/wiki/Phenotype" title="Phenotype">phenotype</A>.</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>Blood groups are inherited from both parents. The ABO blood type is controlled by a single <A href="/wiki/Gene" title="Gene">gene</A> (the <A href="/wiki/ABO_(gene)" title="ABO (gene)">ABO gene</A>) with three types of <A href="/wiki/Allele" title="Allele">alleles</A> inferred from <A href="/wiki/Classical_genetics" title="Classical genetics">classical genetics</A>: <I>i</I>, <I>I<SUP>A</SUP></I>, and <I>I<SUP>B</SUP></I>. The <I>I</I> designation stands for <B>isoagglutinogen</B>, another term for <A href="/wiki/Antigen" title="Antigen">antigen</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-25">[25]</A></SUP> The gene encodes a <A href="/wiki/Glycosyltransferase" title="Glycosyltransferase">glycosyltransferase</A>—that is, an <A href="/wiki/Enzyme" title="Enzyme">enzyme</A> that modifies the <A href="/wiki/Carbohydrate" title="Carbohydrate">carbohydrate</A> content of the <A href="/wiki/Red_blood_cell" title="Red blood cell">red blood cell</A> antigens. The gene is located on the long arm of the <A href="/wiki/Chromosome_9_(human)" title="Chromosome 9 (human)">ninth chromosome</A> (9q34).</P>
<P>The <I>I<SUP>A</SUP></I> allele gives type A, <I>I<SUP>B</SUP></I> gives type B, and <I>i</I> gives type O. As both <I>I<SUP>A</SUP></I> and <I>I<SUP>B</SUP></I> are dominant over <I>i</I>, only <I>ii</I> people have type O blood. Individuals with <I>I<SUP>A</SUP>I<SUP>A</SUP></I> or <I>I<SUP>A</SUP>i</I> have type A blood, and individuals with <I>I<SUP>B</SUP>I<SUP>B</SUP></I> or <I>I<SUP>B</SUP>i</I> have type B. <I>I<SUP>A</SUP>I<SUP>B</SUP></I> people have both <A href="/wiki/Phenotype" title="Phenotype">phenotypes</A>, because A and B express a special dominance relationship: <A href="/wiki/Dominance_relationship#Co-dominance" class="mw-redirect" title="Dominance relationship">codominance</A>, which means that type A and B parents can have an AB child. A couple with type A and type B can also have a type O child if they are both heterozygous (<I>I<SUP>B</SUP>i</I>,<I>I<SUP>A</SUP>i</I>) The <I><A href="/wiki/Cis_AB" title="Cis AB">cis-AB</A></I> phenotype has a single enzyme that creates both A and B antigens. The resulting red blood cells do not usually express A or B antigen at the same level that would be expected on common group A<SUB>1</SUB> or B red blood cells, which can help solve the problem of an apparently genetically impossible blood group.<SUP id="cite_ref-Yazer=2006_26-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Yazer=2006-26">[26]</A></SUP></P>

<P>Historically, ABO blood tests were used in <A href="/wiki/DNA_paternity_testing" title="DNA paternity testing">paternity testing</A>, but in 1957 only 50% of American men falsely accused were able to use them as evidence against paternity.<SUP id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-29">[29]</A></SUP> Occasionally, the blood types of children are not consistent with expectations—for example, a type O child can be born to an AB parent—due to rare situations, such as <A href="/wiki/Bombay_phenotype" class="mw-redirect" title="Bombay phenotype">Bombay phenotype</A> and <A href="/wiki/Cis_AB" title="Cis AB">cis AB</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-30">[30]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Subgroups">Subgroups</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Subgroups">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The A blood type contains about 20 subgroups, of which A1 and A2 are the most common (over 99%). A1 makes up about 80% of all A-type blood, with A2 making up almost all of the rest.<SUP id="cite_ref-atype_31-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-atype-31">[31]</A></SUP> These two subgroups are not always interchangeable as far as transfusion is concerned, as some A2 individuals produce antibodies against the A1 antigen. Complications can sometimes arise in rare cases when typing the blood.<SUP id="cite_ref-atype_31-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-atype-31">[31]</A></SUP></P>
<P>With the development of <A href="/wiki/DNA_sequencing" title="DNA sequencing">DNA sequencing</A>, it has been possible to identify a much larger number of alleles at the ABO locus, each of which can be categorized as A, B, or O in terms of the reaction to transfusion, but which can be distinguished by variations in the <A href="/wiki/DNA" title="DNA">DNA</A> sequence. There are six common <A href="/wiki/Allele" title="Allele">alleles</A> in white individuals of the <A href="/wiki/ABO_gene" class="mw-redirect" title="ABO gene">ABO gene</A> that produce one's blood type:<SUP id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-32">[32]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-33">[33]</A></SUP></P>

<P>The same study also identified 18 rare alleles, which generally have a weaker glycosylation activity. People with weak alleles of A can sometimes express anti-A antibodies, though these are usually not clinically significant as they do not stably interact with the antigen at body temperature.<SUP id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-34">[34]</A></SUP></P>
<P><A href="/wiki/Cis_AB" title="Cis AB">Cis AB</A> is another rare variant, in which A and B genes are transmitted together from a single parent.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Distribution_and_evolutionary_history">Distribution and evolutionary history</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Distribution and evolutionary history">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Blood_type_distribution_by_country" title="Blood type distribution by country">Blood type distribution by country</A></DIV>
<P>The distribution of the blood groups A, B, O and AB varies across the world according to the population. There are also variations in blood type distribution within human subpopulations.</P>
<P>In the UK, the distribution of blood type frequencies through the population still shows some correlation to the distribution of <A href="/wiki/Toponymy" title="Toponymy">placenames</A> and to the successive invasions and migrations including <A href="/wiki/Norsemen" title="Norsemen">Norsemen</A>, <A href="/wiki/Danes_(Germanic_tribe)" title="Danes (Germanic tribe)">Danes</A>, <A href="/wiki/Saxons" title="Saxons">Saxons</A>, <A href="/wiki/Celts" title="Celts">Celts</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Normans" title="Normans">Normans</A> who contributed the <A href="/wiki/Morpheme" title="Morpheme">morphemes</A> to the placenames and the <A href="/wiki/Gene" title="Gene">genes</A> to the population.<SUP id="cite_ref-Potts_1979_35-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Potts_1979-35">[35]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The two common O alleles, O01 and O02, share their first 261 <A href="/wiki/Nucleotide" title="Nucleotide">nucleotides</A> with the group A allele A01.<SUP id="cite_ref-Cserti2007_36-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Cserti2007-36">[36]</A></SUP> However, unlike the group A allele, a <A href="/wiki/Guanosine" title="Guanosine">guanosine</A> base is subsequently deleted. A premature <A href="/wiki/Stop_codon" title="Stop codon">stop codon</A> results from this <A href="/wiki/Frame-shift_mutation" class="mw-redirect" title="Frame-shift mutation">frame-shift mutation</A>. This variant is found worldwide, and likely predates human migration from <A href="/wiki/Africa" title="Africa">Africa</A>. The O01 allele is considered to predate the O02 allele.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (November 2013)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP></P>
<P>Some evolutionary biologists theorize that there are four main lineages of the ABO gene and that mutations creating type O have occurred at least three times in humans.<SUP id="cite_ref-calafell_37-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-calafell-37">[37]</A></SUP> From oldest to youngest, these lineages comprise the following alleles: <I>A101/A201/O09</I>, <I>B101</I>, <I>O02</I> and <I>O01</I>. The continued presence of the O alleles is hypothesized to be the result of <A href="/wiki/Balancing_selection" title="Balancing selection">balancing selection</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-calafell_37-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-calafell-37">[37]</A></SUP> Both theories contradict the previously held theory that type O blood evolved first.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (November 2013)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Origin_theories">Origin theories</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Origin theories">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>It is possible that food and environmental antigens (bacterial, viral, or plant antigens) have <A href="/wiki/Epitope" title="Epitope">epitopes</A> similar enough to A and B glycoprotein antigens. The antibodies created against these environmental antigens in the first years of life can cross-react with ABO-incompatible red blood cells that it comes in contact with during blood transfusion later in life. Anti-A antibodies are hypothesized to originate from immune response towards <A href="/wiki/Influenza_virus" class="mw-redirect" title="Influenza virus">influenza virus</A>, whose epitopes are similar enough to the α-D-N-galactosamine on the A glycoprotein to be able to elicit a cross-reaction. Anti-B antibodies are hypothesized to originate from antibodies produced against <A href="/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria" title="Gram-negative bacteria">Gram-negative bacteria</A>, such as <I><A href="/wiki/Escherichia_coli" title="Escherichia coli">E. coli</A></I>, cross-reacting with the α-D-galactose on the B glycoprotein.<SUP id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<P>However, it is more likely that the force driving evolution of allele diversity is simply negative frequency-dependent selection; cells with rare variants of membrane antigens are more easily distinguished by the immune system from pathogens carrying antigens from other hosts. Thus, individuals possessing rare types are better equipped to detect pathogens. The high within-population diversity observed in human populations would, then, be a consequence of natural selection on individuals.<SUP id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-39">[39]</A></SUP></P>
<P>HIV can be neutralized in <I>in vitro</I> experiments using antibodies against blood group antigens specifically expressed on the HIV-producing cell lines.<SUP id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-40">[40]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-41">[41]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Clinical_relevance">Clinical relevance</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Clinical relevance">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The carbohydrate molecules on the surfaces of red blood cells have roles in <A href="/wiki/Cell_membrane" title="Cell membrane">cell membrane</A> integrity, <A href="/wiki/Cell_adhesion" title="Cell adhesion">cell adhesion</A>, membrane transportation of molecules, and acting as receptors for extracellular ligands, and enzymes. ABO antigens are found having similar roles on <A href="/wiki/Epithelial_cell" class="mw-redirect" title="Epithelial cell">epithelial cells</A> as well as red blood cells.<SUP id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-42">[42]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-43">[43]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN id="Bleeding_and_thrombosis_.28von_Willebrand_factor.29"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Bleeding_and_thrombosis_(von_Willebrand_factor)">Bleeding and thrombosis (von Willebrand factor)</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Bleeding and thrombosis (von Willebrand factor)">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The ABO antigen is also expressed on the <A href="/wiki/Von_Willebrand_factor" title="Von Willebrand factor">von Willebrand factor</A> (vWF) <A href="/wiki/Glycoprotein" title="Glycoprotein">glycoprotein</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-44">[44]</A></SUP> which participates in <A href="/wiki/Hemostasis" title="Hemostasis">hemostasis</A> (control of bleeding). In fact, having type O blood predisposes to bleeding,<SUP id="cite_ref-45" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-45">[45]</A></SUP> as 30% of the total genetic variation observed in plasma vWF is explained by the effect of the ABO blood group,<SUP id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-46">[46]</A></SUP> and individuals with group O blood normally have significantly lower plasma levels of vWF (and <A href="/wiki/Factor_VIII" title="Factor VIII">Factor VIII</A>) than do non-O individuals.<SUP id="cite_ref-47" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-47">[47]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-48">[48]</A></SUP> In addition, vWF is degraded more rapidly due to the higher prevalence of blood group O with the Cys1584 variant of vWF (an amino acid <A href="/wiki/Polymorphism_(biology)" title="Polymorphism (biology)">polymorphism</A> in VWF):<SUP id="cite_ref-49" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-49">[49]</A></SUP> the gene for <A href="/wiki/ADAMTS13" title="ADAMTS13">ADAMTS13</A> (vWF-cleaving <A href="/wiki/Protease" title="Protease">protease</A>) maps to the <A href="/wiki/Chromosome_9_(human)" title="Chromosome 9 (human)">ninth chromosome</A> (9q34), the same <A href="/wiki/Locus_(genetics)" title="Locus (genetics)">locus</A> as ABO blood type. Higher levels of vWF are more common amongst people who have had <A href="/wiki/Ischemic_stroke" class="mw-redirect" title="Ischemic stroke">ischemic stroke</A> (from blood clotting) for the first time.<SUP id="cite_ref-50" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-50">[50]</A></SUP> The results of this study found that the occurrence was not affected by ADAMTS13 polymorphism, and the only significant genetic factor was the person's blood group.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Disease_risks">Disease risks</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section: Disease risks">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Compared to O group individuals, non-O group (A, AB, and B) individuals have a 14% reduced risk of <A href="/wiki/Squamous_cell_carcinoma" title="Squamous cell carcinoma">squamous cell carcinoma</A> and 4% reduced risk of <A href="/wiki/Basal_cell_carcinoma" class="mw-redirect" title="Basal cell carcinoma">basal cell carcinoma</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-51">[51]</A></SUP> Conversely, type O blood is associated with a reduced risk of <A href="/wiki/Pancreatic_cancer" title="Pancreatic cancer">pancreatic cancer</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-52" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-52">[52]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-53" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-53">[53]</A></SUP> The B antigen links with increased risk of <A href="/wiki/Ovarian_cancer" title="Ovarian cancer">ovarian cancer</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-54" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-54">[54]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Gastric_cancer" class="mw-redirect" title="Gastric cancer">Gastric cancer</A> has reported to be more common in blood group A and least in group O.<SUP id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-55">[55]</A></SUP></P>
<P>According to Glass, Holmgren, et al., those in the O blood group have an increased risk of infection with <A href="/wiki/Cholera" title="Cholera">cholera</A>, and those O-group individuals who are infected have more severe infections. The mechanisms behind this association with cholera are unclear in the literature.<SUP id="cite_ref-glass_et_al_56-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-glass_et_al-56">[56]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="ABO_hemolytic_disease_of_the_newborn">ABO hemolytic disease of the newborn</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section: ABO hemolytic disease of the newborn">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Hemolytic_disease_of_the_newborn_(ABO)" title="Hemolytic disease of the newborn (ABO)">Hemolytic disease of the newborn (ABO)</A></DIV>
<P>ABO blood group incompatibilities between the mother and child does not usually cause <A href="/wiki/Hemolytic_disease_of_the_newborn" title="Hemolytic disease of the newborn">hemolytic disease of the newborn</A> (HDN) because antibodies to the ABO blood groups are usually of the <A href="/wiki/IgM" class="mw-redirect" title="IgM">IgM</A> type, which do not cross the placenta. However, in an O-type mother, <B>IgG</B> ABO antibodies are produced and the baby can potentially develop <A href="/wiki/ABO_hemolytic_disease_of_the_newborn" class="mw-redirect" title="ABO hemolytic disease of the newborn">ABO hemolytic disease of the newborn</A>.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Clinical_applications">Clinical applications</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section: Clinical applications">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>In human cells, the ABO alleles and their encoded glycosyltransferases have been described in several oncologic conditions.<SUP id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-57">[57]</A></SUP> Using anti-GTA/GTB monoclonal antibodies, it was demonstrated that a loss of these enzymes was correlated to malignant bladder and oral epithelia.<SUP id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-58">[58]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-59" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-59">[59]</A></SUP> Furthermore, the expression of ABO blood group antigens in normal human tissues is dependent the type of differentiation of the epithelium. In most human carcinomas, including oral carcinoma, a significant event as part of the underlying mechanism is decreased expression of the A and B antigens.<SUP id="cite_ref-Dabelsteen_21–28_60-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Dabelsteen_21–28-60">[60]</A></SUP> Several studies have observed that a relative down-regulation of GTA and GTB occurs in oral carcinomas in association with tumor development.<SUP id="cite_ref-Dabelsteen_21–28_60-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Dabelsteen_21–28-60">[60]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-61" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-61">[61]</A></SUP> More recently, a genome wide association study (GWAS) has identified variants in the ABO locus associated with susceptibility to pancreatic cancer.<SUP id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-62">[62]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Clinical_marker">Clinical marker</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section: Clinical marker">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>A multi-locus genetic risk score study based on a combination of 27 loci, including the ABO gene, identified individuals at increased risk for both incident and recurrent coronary artery disease events, as well as an enhanced clinical benefit from statin therapy. The study was based on a community cohort study (the Malmo Diet and Cancer study) and four additional randomized controlled trials of primary prevention cohorts (JUPITER and ASCOT) and secondary prevention cohorts (CARE and PROVE IT-TIMI 22).<SUP id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-63">[63]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Pseudoscience">Pseudoscience</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=ABO_blood_group_system&action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section: Pseudoscience">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>During the 1930s, connecting <A href="/wiki/Blood_types_in_Japanese_culture" class="mw-redirect" title="Blood types in Japanese culture">blood groups to personality types</A> became popular in Japan and other areas of the world.<SUP id="cite_ref-64" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-64">[64]</A></SUP> Studies of this association have yet to confirm its existence definitively.<SUP id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-65">[65]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-66" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-66">[66]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Other popular but unsupported ideas include the use of a <A href="/wiki/Blood_type_diet" title="Blood type diet">blood type diet</A>, claims that group A causes severe <A href="/wiki/Hangover" title="Hangover">hangovers</A>, group O is associated with perfect teeth, and those with blood group A2 have the highest <A href="/wiki/IQ" class="mw-redirect" title="IQ">IQs</A>. Scientific evidence in support of these concepts is nonexistent.<SUP id="cite_ref-67" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-67">[67]</A></SUP></P>

<P><I><B>Beverly Hills Cop</B></I> is a series of American <A href="/wiki/Action_film" title="Action film">action</A> <A href="/wiki/Comedy_films" class="mw-redirect" title="Comedy films">comedy films</A> and an unaired <A href="/wiki/Television_pilot" title="Television pilot">television pilot</A> based on characters created by <A href="/wiki/Daniel_Petrie,_Jr." class="mw-redirect" title="Daniel Petrie, Jr.">Daniel Petrie, Jr.</A> and <A href="/wiki/Danilo_Bach" title="Danilo Bach">Danilo Bach</A>. The films star <A href="/wiki/Eddie_Murphy" title="Eddie Murphy">Eddie Murphy</A> as <A href="/wiki/Axel_Foley" title="Axel Foley">Axel Foley</A>, a street-smart <A href="/wiki/Detroit" title="Detroit">Detroit</A> cop who travels to <A href="/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California" title="Beverly Hills, California">Beverly Hills, California</A> to investigate crimes, even though it is out of his jurisdiction. There, he meets Detective Billy Rosewood (<A href="/wiki/Judge_Reinhold" title="Judge Reinhold">Judge Reinhold</A>), Sergeant John Taggart (<A href="/wiki/John_Ashton_(actor)" title="John Ashton (actor)">John Ashton</A>), and Lieutenant Andrew Bogomil (<A href="/wiki/Ronny_Cox" title="Ronny Cox">Ronny Cox</A>). Ashton and Cox do not appear in <I><A href="/wiki/Beverly_Hills_Cop_III" title="Beverly Hills Cop III">Beverly Hills Cop III</A></I>. Murphy, Reinhold, and <A href="/wiki/Gil_Hill" title="Gil Hill">Gil Hill</A>, who plays Axel's boss, Inspector Todd, are the only actors who appear in all three films. <A href="/wiki/Harold_Faltermeyer" title="Harold Faltermeyer">Harold Faltermeyer</A> produced the now famous "<A href="/wiki/Axel_F" title="Axel F">Axel F</A>" theme song heard throughout the series. The series as a whole have been distributed by <A href="/wiki/Paramount_Pictures" title="Paramount Pictures">Paramount Pictures</A>. The films have made a total of <A href="/wiki/United_States_dollar" title="United States dollar">$</A>735,534,503<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (June 2013)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> at the worldwide box office.</P>
<P>Following a failed attempt at a television series based on the films, Paramount decided to produce another film with a currently unknown release date.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Ditzian_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Ditzian-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>
<P></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Films">Films</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Beverly_Hills_Cop_(film_series)&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Films">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Overview">Overview</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Beverly_Hills_Cop_(film_series)&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Overview">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<UL>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Beverly_Hills_Cop" title="Beverly Hills Cop">Beverly Hills Cop</A></I> (1984)<BR />
<A href="/wiki/Axel_Foley" title="Axel Foley">Axel Foley</A> (<A href="/wiki/Eddie_Murphy" title="Eddie Murphy">Eddie Murphy</A>) is introduced as a <A href="/wiki/Detroit" title="Detroit">Detroit</A> cop who, after the murder of his friend, travels to California to investigate and track down the killer(s), who he believes operate an arts dealership as a cover in <A href="/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California" title="Beverly Hills, California">Beverly Hills</A>. He teams up with two reluctant detectives, Billy Rosewood (<A href="/wiki/Judge_Reinhold" title="Judge Reinhold">Judge Reinhold</A>) and John Taggart (<A href="/wiki/John_Ashton_(actor)" title="John Ashton (actor)">John Ashton</A>), from the Beverly Hills police department who were supposed to keep a watch on him, especially after seeing Foley's different approach to tackling the situations which were considered unacceptable by the chief of police.</LI>
</UL>
<UL>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Beverly_Hills_Cop_II" title="Beverly Hills Cop II">Beverly Hills Cop II</A></I> (1987)<BR />
Axel returns to Beverly Hills, after finding out that Captain Andrew Bogomil (<A href="/wiki/Ronny_Cox" title="Ronny Cox">Ronny Cox</A>) was shot. He once again teams up with Detective Billy Rosewood and Sgt. John Taggart, who, reluctantly and against incompetent and verbally abusive Police Chief Harold Lutz's (<A href="/wiki/Allen_Garfield" title="Allen Garfield">Allen Garfield</A>) orders, help Foley to find out the person responsible for Bogomil's shooting. Axel, Billy, and John soon discover that the alphabet crimes, a series of felonies (robberies and Bogomil's shooting) that have been going on in the area, are masterminded by weapons kingpin Maxwell Dent (<A href="/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Prochnow" title="Jürgen Prochnow">Jürgen Prochnow</A>). With this information, Axel, Billy, and Taggart try to find Dent and his lover, Karla Fry (<A href="/wiki/Brigitte_Nielsen" title="Brigitte Nielsen">Brigitte Nielsen</A>), (who had shot Bogomil).</LI>
</UL>
<UL>
<LI><I><A href="/wiki/Beverly_Hills_Cop_III" title="Beverly Hills Cop III">Beverly Hills Cop III</A></I> (1994)<BR />
Axel returns to Beverly Hills once again. During an assignment, his boss, Inspector Todd (<A href="/wiki/Gil_Hill" title="Gil Hill">Gil Hill</A>) is killed, and certain evidence points towards an amusement park called "Wonderworld". Upon arriving in Beverly Hills, Axel looks up his old friend Billy Rosewood who has attained the title of DDOJSIOC (Deputy Director of Joint Special Inter Operational Command). Bogomil and Taggart have retired and a new detective called Jon Flint (<A href="/wiki/Hector_Elizondo" class="mw-redirect" title="Hector Elizondo">Hector Elizondo</A>) is Rosewood's new partner.</LI>
</UL>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Unaired_television_pilot">Unaired television pilot</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Beverly_Hills_Cop_(film_series)&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Unaired television pilot">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P><A href="/wiki/CBS" title="CBS">CBS</A> ordered a pilot with <A href="/wiki/Brandon_T._Jackson" title="Brandon T. Jackson">Brandon T. Jackson</A> starring as Axel Foley's son, Aaron.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> The hour long crime drama was produced by the critically acclaimed writer <A href="/wiki/Shawn_Ryan" title="Shawn Ryan">Shawn Ryan</A> who created <I><A href="/wiki/The_Shield" title="The Shield">The Shield</A></I> and <I><A href="/wiki/The_Chicago_Code" title="The Chicago Code">The Chicago Code</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In January 2013, Ryan stated, "It's going to be a CBS procedural. We're going to solve a case every week, but we're going to do it with a lot of humor and a lot of fun. And I would say the stealth thing I would like to get in is, in a day and age when income inequality and class inequities dominate a lot of the country, this is going to be an opportunity to put a young working-class kid in Detroit in the middle of Beverly Hills, you can do a lot of stealth social commentary. My approach is to update it and make it feel modern and 2013. The pilot opens with a 4-5 minute sequence which I think is really harrowing and really dangerous, that would be something that you might have seen on <I>Chicago Code</I> or <I>The Shield</I>. I want it to feel grounded in that way. There'll be some opportunities for laughs after that. It's not a laughs come first show."<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In February 2013, <A href="/wiki/Kevin_Pollak" title="Kevin Pollak">Kevin Pollak</A> was cast as Rodney Daloof, an irritating and incredibly risk-averse in-house attorney for the Beverly Hills Police Department.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/David_Denman" title="David Denman">David Denman</A> was cast as Brad, an honest and likable but socially awkward detective, formerly a baseball player and a musician.<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP> Director <A href="/wiki/Barry_Sonnenfeld" title="Barry Sonnenfeld">Barry Sonnenfeld</A> agreed to both direct the <I>Beverly Hills Cop</I> pilot and serve as an executive producer.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP> In May 2013, CBS decided to pass on the <I>Beverly Hills Cop</I> TV series.<SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP> In August 2013, Brandon T. Jackson give his reason about the pass:</P>
<BLOCKQUOTE>
<P>I think we were very edgy for CBS. I think we were the edgiest as you could've went for CBS. It would have been like a '<A href="/wiki/The_Fresh_Prince_of_Bel-Air" title="The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air">Fresh Prince</A>' thing on CBS, like the edgiest you can go on network TV. But it doesn't agree to our franchise man."<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP></P>
</BLOCKQUOTE>
<P>In February 2015, Eddie Murphy stated that his cameo appearance in the pilot ironically doomed the show's chances: "I was gonna be in the pilot, and they thought I should be recurring. I’m not gonna do Beverly Hills Cop on TV. I remember when they tested it — they had this little knob that you turn if you like it or you don’t like it. So when Axel shows up in the pilot, some people turned the knob so much, they broke it. So the network decided 'if he isn’t recurring, then this isn’t gonna happen.' So it didn’t happen."<SUP id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14">[14]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In a January 2016 interview, Shawn Ryan blamed personality clashes with the network: "The official answer is they decided they liked other pilots better. If you look at what pilots they picked up that year, I think that's kind of incredible. I would say there were a lot of 400 lb. gorillas involved in the show and sometimes the gorillas don’t always get along.". He also said that he was very proud of the pilot and loved working with Murphy.<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP></P>
<P>During late Summer 2013, after CBS decided to pass on the TV series, Paramount decided to move forward with the fourth film.</P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Music">Music</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Beverly_Hills_Cop_(film_series)&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Music">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>There is a recurring instrumental theme throughout the film series called "<A href="/wiki/Axel_F" title="Axel F">Axel F</A>", which was composed by <A href="/wiki/Harold_Faltermeyer" title="Harold Faltermeyer">Harold Faltermeyer</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP> The theme became popular with audiences, and has been <A href="/wiki/Crazy_Frog_song" class="mw-redirect" title="Crazy Frog song">remixed</A> by <A href="/wiki/Crazy_Frog" title="Crazy Frog">Crazy Frog</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP> A new version of the theme was created for <I><A href="/wiki/Beverly_Hills_Cop_III" title="Beverly Hills Cop III">Beverly Hills Cop III</A></I>, with Faltermeyer not returning for the film.<SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Future">Future</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Beverly_Hills_Cop_(film_series)&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Future">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>A fourth entry in the series was initially announced for release in the mid-1990s, under the production of Eddie Murphy's own production company "Eddie Murphy Productions", though production later fizzled out.<SUP id="cite_ref-BHC4_19-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-BHC4-19">[19]</A></SUP> It was re-announced in 2006, when producer <A href="/wiki/Jerry_Bruckheimer" title="Jerry Bruckheimer">Jerry Bruckheimer</A> announced his intention to resurrect the film series, though he eventually gave up his option to produce the film, instead passing production duties to <A href="/wiki/Lorenzo_di_Bonaventura" title="Lorenzo di Bonaventura">Lorenzo di Bonaventura</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-variety_21-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-variety-21">[21]</A></SUP> In September 2006 a script, an amalgamation of several earlier drafts, was presented to Murphy who was reported to be "very happy" with the outline which was described as an attempt to recapture the "feel of the original".<SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-23">[23]</A></SUP> Murphy admitted one of his motivations for making a fourth <I>Beverly Hills Cop</I> film was to make up for the fact that the third film was "horrible" and that "he didn't want to leave (the series) like that".<SUP id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-24">[24]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-25">[25]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In May 2008, <I><A href="/wiki/Rush_Hour_(1998_film)" title="Rush Hour (1998 film)">Rush Hour</A></I> director <A href="/wiki/Brett_Ratner" title="Brett Ratner">Brett Ratner</A> was officially named director, who promised the film would return under the series' standard "R" rating, rather than as a rumored watered down PG-13.<SUP id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-26">[26]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-27">[27]</A></SUP> Michael Brandt and Derek Haas were hired as screenwriters to improve on the existing script in July 2008<SUP id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-28">[28]</A></SUP> and completed a new script, under the working title <I>Beverly Hills Cop 2009</I>, which would see Foley return to Beverly Hills to investigate the murder of his friend <A href="/wiki/Billy_Rosewood" class="mw-redirect" title="Billy Rosewood">Billy Rosewood</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-BHC4_19-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-BHC4-19">[19]</A></SUP> The script was eventually rejected, leaving Ratner to work on a new idea. In an interview with <I><A href="/wiki/Empire_(film_magazine)" title="Empire (film magazine)">Empire</A></I> magazine, Ratner stated "I'm working very hard on the fourth. It's very difficult, especially since there were three before. We're trying to figure out some important things, like where do we start? Is Axel retired? Is he in Beverly Hills? Is he on vacation? Does Judge Reinhold return as the loveable Billy Rosewood? Many questions to figure out, but I'm hoping to have a script before film disappears from our existence."<SUP id="cite_ref-BHC4_19-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-BHC4-19">[19]</A></SUP> Although Murphy himself committed to the project, it was unconfirmed whether the series' other principal actors, <A href="/wiki/Judge_Reinhold" title="Judge Reinhold">Judge Reinhold</A>, <A href="/wiki/John_Ashton_(actor)" title="John Ashton (actor)">John Ashton</A>, <A href="/wiki/Ronny_Cox" title="Ronny Cox">Ronny Cox</A> or <A href="/wiki/Bronson_Pinchot" title="Bronson Pinchot">Bronson Pinchot</A> would also return,<SUP id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-29">[29]</A></SUP> though Ratner stated in late 2009 that he was trying to convince Reinhold and Ashton to reprise their roles.<SUP id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-30">[30]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Harold_Faltermeyer" title="Harold Faltermeyer">Harold Faltermeyer</A>'s "<A href="/wiki/Axel_F" title="Axel F">Axel F</A>", however, would definitely be returning for the proposed fourth installment, with Ratner quoted as saying "It'll be back but it'll be a whole new interpretation."<SUP id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-31">[31]</A></SUP> On November 15, 2010, Ratner stated in an interview with MTV that there was still a possibility that they will make a fourth film, but that it wouldn't be "anytime soon."<SUP id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-32">[32]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In October 2011, Murphy discussed a possible fourth film, stating, "They're not doing it. What I'm trying to do now is produce a TV show starring Axel Foley's son, and Axel is the chief of police now in Detroit. I'd do the pilot, show up here and there. None of the movie scripts were right; it was trying to force the premise. If you have to force something, you shouldn't be doing it. It was always a rehash of the old thing. It was always wrong."<SUP id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-33">[33]</A></SUP></P>
<P>During late Summer 2013, after CBS decided to pass on the TV series, Paramount decided to move forward with the fourth film. On September 13, 2013, Jerry Bruckheimer, stated he was in talks to produce. On December 6, 2013, it was announced that Eddie Murphy will again reprise the role of Axel Foley and Brett Ratner will direct.<SUP id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-34">[34]</A></SUP> On May 2, 2014, Deadline announced that screenwriters <A href="/wiki/Josh_Appelbaum" title="Josh Appelbaum">Josh Appelbaum</A> and <A href="/wiki/Andre_Nemec" class="mw-redirect" title="Andre Nemec">Andre Nemec</A> would be penning the screenplay.<SUP id="cite_ref-Ditzian_5-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Ditzian-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On June 27, 2014, in an interview with <I><A href="/wiki/Rolling_Stone" title="Rolling Stone">Rolling Stone</A></I>, Murphy discussed returning to the edgier type character of Axel Foley after years of making family friendly films. "I haven't done a street guy, working class, blue-collar character in ages so maybe it's like, 'Oh, wow, I didn't remember he was able to do that,'" Murphy said. According to studio reports on the film's plot, Foley will return to Detroit after leaving his job in Beverly Hills and he will be faced with the coldest winter on record to navigate the new rules and old enemies of one of America's most tenacious cities. The state of Michigan approved $13.5 million in film incentives, based on an estimated $56.6 million of filmmaker spending in the state. The film will be shot in and around Detroit and is estimated to provide jobs for 352 workers. The film was originally scheduled for a March 25, 2016 release,<SUP id="cite_ref-35" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-35">[35]</A></SUP> but on May 6, 2015, Paramount Pictures pulled <I>Beverly Hills Cop IV</I> from its release schedule, due to script concerns.<SUP id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-36">[36]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-37">[37]</A></SUP> On June 14, 2016, <A href="/wiki/Deadline.com" class="mw-redirect" title="Deadline.com">Deadline.com</A> reported that Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah, directors of the Belgian drama <I><A href="/wiki/Black_(2015_Belgian_film)" title="Black (2015 Belgian film)">Black</A></I>, would direct the film.<SUP id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In January 2017, it was revealed that a new entry in the franchise will commence filming in June 2017 with Eddie Murphy reprising his role as Axel Foley, and Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah as directors.<SUP id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-39">[39]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-40">[40]</A></SUP></P>

<P><A href="/wiki/The_Championships,_Wimbledon" title="The Championships, Wimbledon">The Championships, Wimbledon</A> is an annual <A href="/wiki/Tennis" title="Tennis">tennis</A> tournament first contested in <A href="/wiki/1877_Wimbledon_Championship" title="1877 Wimbledon Championship">1877</A> and played on <A href="/wiki/Grass_court" title="Grass court">outdoor grass courts</A><SUP class="reference" id="ref_Indoora"><A href="#endnote_Indoora">[a]</A></SUP><SUP class="reference" id="ref_OpenErab"><A href="#endnote_OpenErab">[b]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcGrass_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcGrass-1">[1]</A></SUP> at the <A href="/wiki/All_England_Lawn_Tennis_and_Croquet_Club" title="All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club">All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club</A> (AELTC) in the <A href="/wiki/Wimbledon,_London" title="Wimbledon, London">Wimbledon</A> suburb of London, United Kingdom.<SUP id="cite_ref-WProfile_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-WProfile-2">[2]</A></SUP> The Ladies' Singles was started in <A href="/wiki/1884_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1884 Wimbledon Championships">1884</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcHistory_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcHistory-3">[3]</A></SUP>
</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="History">History</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Wimbledon_ladies%27_singles_champions&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: History">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Wimbledon has historically been played in the last week of June and the first week of July (though changed to the first two weeks of July in 2017), and has been chronologically the third of the four <A href="/wiki/Grand_Slam_(tennis)" title="Grand Slam (tennis)">Grand Slam</A> tournaments of the tennis <A href="/wiki/Season_(sports)" title="Season (sports)">season</A> since 1987.<SUP id="cite_ref-WProfile_2-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-WProfile-2">[2]</A></SUP> The event was not held from 1915 to 1918 because of <A href="/wiki/World_War_I" title="World War I">World War I</A> and again from 1940 to 1945 because of <A href="/wiki/World_War_II" title="World War II">World War II</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcFinals_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcFinals-4">[4]</A></SUP>
</P><P>The Ladies' Singles' rules have undergone several changes since the first edition. From <A href="/wiki/1886_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1886 Wimbledon Championships">1886</A> until <A href="/wiki/1921_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1921 Wimbledon Championships">1921</A>, the event started with a <A href="/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament" title="Single-elimination tournament">knockout</A> phase, the All Comers' Singles, whose winner then faced the defending champion in a <A href="/wiki/Glossary_of_tennis#Challenge_Round" class="mw-redirect" title="Glossary of tennis">challenge round</A>. The All Comers' winner was automatically awarded the title six times (<A href="/wiki/1887_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1887 Wimbledon Championships">1887</A>, <A href="/wiki/1891_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1891 Wimbledon Championships">1891</A>, <A href="/wiki/1895_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1895 Wimbledon Championships">1895</A>, <A href="/wiki/1907_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1907 Wimbledon Championships">1907</A>, <A href="/wiki/1908_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1908 Wimbledon Championships">1908</A>) in the absence of the previous year's champion. The challenge round system was abolished with the <A href="/wiki/1922_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1922 Wimbledon Championships">1922</A> edition.<SUP id="cite_ref-Barrett_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Barrett-5">[5]</A></SUP> Since the first championships, all matches have been played at the <A href="/wiki/Tennis_score#Scoring_a_set" class="mw-redirect" title="Tennis score">best-of-three sets</A>. Between 1877 and <A href="/wiki/1883_Wimbledon_Championship" title="1883 Wimbledon Championship">1883</A>, the winner of the next game at five games<A href="/wiki/Glossary_of_tennis#All" class="mw-redirect" title="Glossary of tennis">-all</A> took the set in every match except the All Comers' final, and the challenge round, which were won with six games and a two games advantage. All sets were decided in two-game <A href="/wiki/Glossary_of_tennis#Advantage_format" class="mw-redirect" title="Glossary of tennis">advantage format</A> from <A href="/wiki/1884_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1884 Wimbledon Championships">1884</A> to <A href="/wiki/1970_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1970 Wimbledon Championships">1970</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Barrett_5-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Barrett-5">[5]</A></SUP> The <A href="/wiki/Glossary_of_tennis#Lingering_death" class="mw-redirect" title="Glossary of tennis">lingering death</A> best-of-12 points <A href="/wiki/Tennis_score#Scoring_a_tiebreak_game" class="mw-redirect" title="Tennis score">tie-break</A> was introduced in <A href="/wiki/1971_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1971 Wimbledon Championships">1971</A> for the first two sets, played at eight games-all until <A href="/wiki/1978_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1978 Wimbledon Championships">1978</A> and at six games-all since <A href="/wiki/1979_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1979 Wimbledon Championships">1979</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Barrett_5-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Barrett-5">[5]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Tie-break_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Tie-break-6">[6]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-SuddenLingering_7-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-SuddenLingering-7">[7]</A></SUP>
</P><P>The Ladies' Singles champion receives a sterling silver salver commonly known as the "<A href="/wiki/Venus_Rosewater_Dish" title="Venus Rosewater Dish">Venus Rosewater Dish</A>", or simply the "Rosewater Dish". The salver, which is 18.75 inches (about 48 cm) in diameter, is decorated with figures from mythology.<SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcTrophy_8-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcTrophy-8">[8]</A></SUP> New singles champions are traditionally elected honorary members of the AELTC by the club's committee.<SUP class="reference" id="ref_McEnroeMembershipc"><A href="#endnote_McEnroeMembershipc">[c]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcClub_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcClub-9">[9]</A></SUP> In 2012, the Ladies' Singles winner received <A href="/wiki/Prize_money" title="Prize money">prize money</A> of <A href="/wiki/Pound_sterling" title="Pound sterling">£</A>1,150,000.<SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcPrize_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcPrize-10">[10]</A></SUP>
</P><P>These records include the Amateur Era only, <A href="/wiki/Dorothea_Lambert_Chambers" class="mw-redirect" title="Dorothea Lambert Chambers">Dorothea Lambert Chambers</A> (1903–1904, 1906, 1910–1911, 1913–1914) holds the record for most titles, with seven, and <A href="/wiki/Lottie_Dod" title="Lottie Dod">Lottie Dod</A> (1891–1893) and <A href="/wiki/Suzanne_Lenglen" title="Suzanne Lenglen">Suzanne Lenglen</A> (1919–1921) holds the record for most consecutive wins in the Ladies' Singles during the challenge round era, with three victories each. The record for most consecutive and most wins post challenge round during the Amateur Era is <A href="/wiki/Helen_Wills_Moody" class="mw-redirect" title="Helen Wills Moody">Helen Wills Moody</A> (1927–1930), with four straight wins, and Moody holds the record for most victories in this era with eight (1927–1930, 1932–1933, 1935, 1938).<SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcFinals_4-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcFinals-4">[4]</A></SUP>
</P><P>These records only include the Open Era, since the inclusion of the professional tennis players, <A href="/wiki/Martina_Navratilova" title="Martina Navratilova">Martina Navratilova</A> (1978–1979, 1982–1987, 1990) holds the record for most victories with nine. Navratilova holds the record for most consecutive victories with six (1982–1987).<SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcFinals_4-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcFinals-4">[4]</A></SUP>
</P><P>This event has been won without the loss of a set, during the Open Era of Tennis, by the following players: <A href="/wiki/Billie_Jean_King" title="Billie Jean King">Billie Jean King</A> in 1968, 1972, 1973 and 1975, <A href="/wiki/Margaret_Court" title="Margaret Court">Margaret Court</A> in 1970, <A href="/wiki/Evonne_Goolagong_Cawley" title="Evonne Goolagong Cawley">Evonne Goolagong Cawley</A> in 1971 and 1980, <A href="/wiki/Chris_Evert" title="Chris Evert">Chris Evert</A> in 1974 and 1981, <A href="/wiki/Martina_Navratilova" title="Martina Navratilova">Martina Navratilova</A> in 1979, 1983, 1984, 1986, 1987, and 1990, <A href="/wiki/Steffi_Graf" title="Steffi Graf">Steffi Graf</A> in 1992 and 1996, <A href="/wiki/Jana_Novotn%C3%A1" title="Jana Novotná">Jana Novotná</A> in 1998, <A href="/wiki/Lindsay_Davenport" title="Lindsay Davenport">Lindsay Davenport</A> in 1999, <A href="/wiki/Venus_Williams" title="Venus Williams">Venus Williams</A> in 2000, 2007 and 2008, <A href="/wiki/Serena_Williams" title="Serena Williams">Serena Williams</A> in 2002, 2009, 2010, 2015 and 2016, <A href="/wiki/Maria_Sharapova" title="Maria Sharapova">Maria Sharapova</A> in 2004, <A href="/wiki/Petra_Kvitov%C3%A1" title="Petra Kvitová">Petra Kvitová</A> in 2011 and 2014 and <A href="/wiki/Marion_Bartoli" title="Marion Bartoli">Marion Bartoli</A> in 2013.
</P>

<UL><LI><SPAN class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_Indoora"><A href="#ref_Indoora"><B><SUP>a</SUP></B></A></SPAN>  Since 2009, <A href="/wiki/Centre_Court" title="Centre Court">Centre Court</A> features a <A href="/wiki/Retractable_roof" title="Retractable roof">retractable roof</A>, allowing <A href="/wiki/Tennis_court#Indoor_courts" title="Tennis court">indoor</A> and night-time play.<SUP id="cite_ref-Indoor_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Indoor-12">[12]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><SPAN class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_OpenErab"><A href="#ref_OpenErab"><B><SUP>b</SUP></B></A></SPAN>  Wimbledon entered the <A href="/wiki/History_of_tennis#Open_Era" title="History of tennis">Open Era</A> with the <A href="/wiki/1968_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1968 Wimbledon Championships">1968</A> edition, allowing <A href="/wiki/Professional" title="Professional">professional</A> players to compete alongside <A href="/wiki/Amateur" title="Amateur">amateurs</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcHistory_3-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcHistory-3">[3]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><SPAN class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_McEnroeMembershipc"><A href="#ref_McEnroeMembershipc"><B><SUP>c</SUP></B></A></SPAN>  <A href="/wiki/John_McEnroe" title="John McEnroe">John McEnroe</A> is the only player to have been denied membership in <A href="/wiki/1981_Wimbledon_Championships" title="1981 Wimbledon Championships">1981</A>, because of his on-court behaviour during the championships.<SUP id="cite_ref-McEnroeMembership1_13-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-McEnroeMembership1-13">[13]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-McEnroeMembership2_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-McEnroeMembership2-14">[14]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><SPAN class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_Yeard"><A href="#ref_Yeard"><B><SUP>d</SUP></B></A></SPAN>  Each year is linked to an article about that particular year's draws, but pre-1922 they did not have draws due to the challenge round system.  In 1922 till the present they do have draws, but the years of 1925–1939 do not have draw pages with links, so it is linked to the year's articles instead.</LI>
<LI><SPAN class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_BRIe"><A href="#ref_BRIe"><B><SUP>e</SUP></B></A></SPAN>  "British Isles" (BRI) is used for players from the <A href="/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland" title="United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland">United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland</A> (1801–1922), distinct from "Great Britain" (GBR) used for players from the <A href="/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Northern_Ireland" class="mw-redirect" title="United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland">United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland</A> (1922–present).<SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcFinals_4-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcFinals-4">[4]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcCountries_15-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcCountries-15">[15]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><SPAN class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_WWIf"><A href="#ref_WWIf"><B><SUP>f</SUP></B></A></SPAN>  The tournament was not held from 1915 to 1918 because of World War I.<SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcFinals_4-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcFinals-4">[4]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><SPAN class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_WWIIg"><A href="#ref_WWIIg"><B><SUP>g</SUP></B></A></SPAN>  The tournament was not held from 1940 to 1945 because of World War II.<SUP id="cite_ref-2009aetlcFinals_4-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2009aetlcFinals-4">[4]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><SPAN class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_TCHh"><A href="#ref_TCHh"><B><SUP>h</SUP></B></A></SPAN>  <A href="/wiki/Czechoslovakia" title="Czechoslovakia">Czechoslovakia</A> (TCH, 1918–1992) split into the <A href="/wiki/Czech_Republic" title="Czech Republic">Czech Republic</A> (CZE, 1992–present) and <A href="/wiki/Slovakia" title="Slovakia">Slovakia</A> (SVK, 1992–present).</LI>
<LI><SPAN class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_NAVUSAi"><A href="#ref_NAVUSAi"><B><SUP>i</SUP></B></A></SPAN>  <A href="/wiki/Martina_Navratilova" title="Martina Navratilova">Martina Navratilova</A> was born in Czechoslovakia, but was stripped of her citizenship in 1975 when she defected to the United States. She became a US citizen in 1981.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><SPAN class="citation wikicite" id="endnote_FRGGERj"><A href="#ref_FRGGERj"><B><SUP>j</SUP></B></A></SPAN>  FRG is West Germany, but after unification became just Germany (GER) after 1990.</LI></UL>
</DIV>

<P><B>Dualism</B> (from the <A href="/wiki/Latin" title="Latin">Latin</A> word <I>duo</I> meaning "two")<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP> denotes the state of two parts. The term <I>dualism</I> was originally coined to denote co-eternal<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template" style="margin-left:0.1em; white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify" title="Wikipedia:Please clarify"><SPAN title="The text near this tag may need clarification or removal of jargon. (December 2016)">clarification needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> <A href="/wiki/Binary_opposition" title="Binary opposition">binary opposition</A>, a meaning that is preserved in <A href="/wiki/Metaphysics" title="Metaphysics">metaphysical</A> and <A href="/wiki/Philosophy" title="Philosophy">philosophical</A> <A href="/wiki/Dualism_(philosophy_of_mind)" class="mw-redirect" title="Dualism (philosophy of mind)">duality</A> discourse but has been more generalized in other usages to indicate a system which contains two essential parts.</P>
<P>Moral dualism is the belief of the great complement of or conflict between the benevolent and the malevolent. It simply implies that there are two moral opposites at work, independent of any interpretation of what might be "moral" and independent of how these may be represented. Moral opposites might, for example, exist in a worldview which has one god, more than one god, or none. By contrast, ditheism or bi-theism implies (at least) two gods. While bi-theism implies harmony, <A href="/wiki/Ditheism" class="mw-redirect" title="Ditheism">ditheism</A> implies rivalry and opposition, such as between good and evil, or light and dark, or summer and winter. For example, a ditheistic system would be one in which one god is a creator, and the other a destroyer.</P>
<P>Alternatively, in ontological dualism, the world is divided into two overarching categories. The opposition and combination of the universe's two basic principles of <A href="/wiki/Yin_and_yang" title="Yin and yang">yin and yang</A> is a large part of Chinese philosophy, and is an important feature of <A href="/wiki/Taoism" title="Taoism">Taoism</A>. It is also discussed in <A href="/wiki/Confucianism" title="Confucianism">Confucianism</A>.</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Moral_dualism">Moral dualism</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Dualism&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Moral dualism">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<TABLE class="plainlinks metadata ambox ambox-content ambox-Unreferenced" role="presentation">
<TBODY><TR>
<TD class="mbox-image">

<DIV class="mbox-text-span">This section <B>does not <A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources" title="Wikipedia:Citing sources">cite</A> any <A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability">sources</A></B>. <SPAN class="hide-when-compact">Please help <A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dualism&action=edit">improve this section</A> by <A href="/wiki/Help:Introduction_to_referencing_with_Wiki_Markup/1" title="Help:Introduction to referencing with Wiki Markup/1">adding citations to reliable sources</A>.
