<P>Maggie is first introduced in the penultimate episode of the <A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_10)" title="Grey's Anatomy (season 10)">tenth season</A>. <A href="/wiki/Cristina_Yang" title="Cristina Yang">Cristina Yang</A> (<A href="/wiki/Sandra_Oh" title="Sandra Oh">Sandra Oh</A>) interviews various different candidates to replace her as the head of her department in Cardiothoracic surgery. Maggie, having finished high school and medical school early, becomes head of her department at 31 years old. It is revealed in the season 10 finale "<A href="/wiki/Fear_(of_the_Unknown)_(Grey%27s_Anatomy)" class="mw-redirect" title="Fear (of the Unknown) (Grey's Anatomy)">Fear (of the Unknown)</A>", Maggie's biological mother was Ellis Grey.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Richard_Webber" title="Richard Webber">Richard Webber</A> is shocked by this, knowing he is her biological father. Throughout the eleventh season, Webber struggles to deal with the revelation and keeps it from Maggie. Maggie explains that 2 years prior, she looked for her birth mom and needed to go to the court for the records. She found out that she was dead, but got her name, and discovered that she was an amazing surgeon that worked at the Seattle Grace Hospital. She stated that that's not why she took the job, but it's "a little bit" why she took the interview.</P>
<P>When Maggie identifies <A href="/wiki/Meredith_Grey" title="Meredith Grey">Meredith Grey</A>, her half-sister, she attempts to bond with her. However, Meredith attempts to take charge and conflicts with her on a case. After several arguments, Maggie tells Meredith that she is her half-sister. Meredith, in disbelief, points out that she would know that her mother would be pregnant when she was five years old, as Maggie is five years younger than her. Meredith works with <A href="/wiki/Alex_Karev" title="Alex Karev">Alex Karev</A> (<A href="/wiki/Justin_Chambers" title="Justin Chambers">Justin Chambers</A>) to decide whether Maggie is lying or if she is wrong. They discover she is correct. Meredith gets flashes back to the time of her mother's crisis at five years old, and remembers being at a hospital and hearing a screaming baby. After several weeks, Webber admits to Maggie that he is her father. Maggie is angry at him. Later, when he comes to apologize for not being there as a father, Maggie corrects him and says he is not her father, as she has adoptive parents she loves, and that she is only angry because of his dishonesty and making her look foolish and naive for weeks. Derek and Meredith decide to have Maggie come over to their house for dinner, to get to know Maggie better. After Maggie says yes, Derek decides it is a good idea to ask Richard as well. Richard reluctantly agrees. The night of the dinner, Maggie and Richard show up, but no-one answers. Maggie leaves him after that. Maggie develops a relationship with radiologist, Ethan Boyd. She admits her awkwardness in relationships, having ended her previous engagement to Dean, who she was unable to sleep in the same bed with. Meredith ends up in a bind with no one to watch her kids, so Maggie offers to watch them. Richard and Maggie eventually come to good terms, and Maggie's helping with Meredith's kids help her integrate into her family home more. Maggie learns about the histories of Meredith, Alex and <A href="/wiki/Callie_Torres" title="Callie Torres">Callie Torres</A> (<A href="/wiki/Sara_Ramirez" title="Sara Ramirez">Sara Ramirez</A>) as they commemorate their dead friend, <A href="/wiki/George_O%27Malley" title="George O'Malley">George O'Malley</A> (<A href="/wiki/TR_Knight" class="mw-redirect" title="TR Knight">TR Knight</A>).</P>
<P>After Derek's death, Meredith abandons Seattle for a year, leaving Maggie a note. Maggie is shocked by this, and admits she felt abandoned by Meredith right when they were starting to become a family. She invites Webber to a Christmas party, noticing his loneliness. Meredith eventually returns home, hugging Maggie and re-integrating into her old family home. While Maggie and her colleagues are busy dealing with Keith Gardner after a tunnel collapse, Maggie gets a phone call that her parents are getting a divorce. Her mother confesses to her that she'd been having an affair with their car serviceman for eleven years and they had only stayed together for her sake, but were getting a divorce now that she was out on her own. Maggie is emotional about this, but she doesn't want to bother her colleagues about it. Later, she confides in Meredith over the issue, but feels it is silly in comparison to her husband's death. Meredith, however, says she can tell her anything and she should come to her whenever she is having a problem. After Meredith buys her house back from Alex, she invites Maggie and <A href="/wiki/Amelia_Shepherd" title="Amelia Shepherd">Amelia Shepherd</A> (<A href="/wiki/Caterina_Scorsone" title="Caterina Scorsone">Caterina Scorsone</A>) to move in with her. They assist Meredith in caring for her kids. Maggie also often mediates between Meredith and Amelia, who frequently get into fights over little things. She often helps with Meredith's three kids, with each "sister" in charge of getting one kid ready for the day.</P>
<P>In the twelfth season, Maggie develops a relationship with intern Andrew DeLuca. Maggie sleeps with DeLuca after a short conversation and a couple of drinks at Joe's. They agree it is a one-time thing, before they have sex again. Maggie and DeLuca keep their relationship private to avoid difficulties at work. DeLuca grows frustrated with their secrecy, so Maggie abruptly decides to go public. When this happens, DeLuca becomes uncomfortable with the way he is viewed by others because he is dating an attending, and doesn't want others to think he is getting special treatment. He also feels intimidated by her authority. When she confronts him, he ends things with her. Maggie attempts to move on and develops an interest in Nathan Riggs (<A href="/wiki/Martin_Henderson" title="Martin Henderson">Martin Henderson</A>). However, she is unaware Meredith has a sexual relationship with him. She confides in Meredith about this at Amelia's wedding to <A href="/wiki/Owen_Hunt" title="Owen Hunt">Owen Hunt</A> (<A href="/wiki/Kevin_McKidd" title="Kevin McKidd">Kevin McKidd</A>). In the thirteenth season, Maggie is personally hurt by Meredith lying to her about Alex's actions assaulting DeLuca. She tells her to never lie to her again, but she does so immediately afterwards about Riggs. Riggs tells Meredith she needs to tell Maggie. Maggie works up the courage to ask Riggs out, but he rejects her.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Development">Development</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Maggie_Pierce&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Development">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Casting_and_creation">Casting and creation</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Maggie_Pierce&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Casting and creation">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="quotebox" style="float: right; clear: right; margin: 0.5em 0 0.8em 1.4em; width:22em; padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #aaa; font-size: 88%; background-color: #F9F9F9;">
<DIV class="" style="background-color: #F9F9F9; color: black; text-align: center; font-size: larger; font-weight: bold;">McCreary on the role</DIV>
<DIV class="" style="position: relative; text-align: left;">
<DIV style="margin:0px 2em;">When I auditioned, all they told me was that the character might recur a little bit into Season 11; they did not tell me it was Meredith’s sister and there was long-term potential. I had no idea the scope of it in terms of how [she] fit into the mythology of the series. Her character ties into a lot of things that have already occurred in these people’s lives.</DIV>
<DIV style="position: absolute; left: 0px; top: 0px; text-align: left; font-family:'Times New Roman',serif; font-weight:bold; font-size: large; color: gray;">“</DIV>
<DIV style="position: absolute; right: 0px; bottom: 0px; text-align: left; font-family:'Times New Roman',serif; font-weight:bold; font-size: large; color: gray;">”</DIV>
</DIV>
<CITE style="display: block; text-align: left;">Benjamin Lindsay, <A href="/wiki/Backstage_(magazine)" title="Backstage (magazine)">Backstage</A> <SMALL>2015</SMALL><SUP id="cite_ref-Backstage120815_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Backstage120815-3">[3]</A></SUP></CITE></DIV>
<P>On April 5, 2014, <I><A href="/wiki/TVLine" title="TVLine">TVLine</A></I> reported that <A href="/wiki/Kelly_McCreary" title="Kelly McCreary">Kelly McCreary</A> best known for her series regular role on <A href="/wiki/The_CW" title="The CW">The CW</A>'s short lived medical drama <I><A href="/wiki/Emily_Owens,_M.D." title="Emily Owens, M.D.">Emily Owens, M.D.</A></I> and recent guest appearances on <I><A href="/wiki/Scandal_(TV_series)" title="Scandal (TV series)">Scandal</A></I> had been cast in a guest star role. McCeary was slated to debut on the May 8, 2015 episode.<SUP id="cite_ref-TVLine040514_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TVLine040514-4">[4]</A></SUP> On October 23, 2014, it was announced that McCreary was promoted to series regular after being credited as guest-starring until the eleventh episode.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> It was a couple of months after McCreary wrapped her stint on <I>Scandal</I> that she was invited to audition for <I>Grey's</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Cosmo100914_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Cosmo100914-9">[9]</A></SUP> McCeary revealed that she originally auditioned for the character of "Claudette" with dummy sides, unbeknownst to her. The only information McCeary had about the character was "that she was adopted, that she would recur, and she was going to be a very important storyline." Just before the script reading for the season 10 finale, Rhimes summoned McCeary to inform her of Maggie's true identity.<SUP id="cite_ref-BF012915_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-BF012915-10">[10]</A></SUP> "I was really psyched" McCeary revealed when Rhimes informed her of Maggie's lineage. "I felt really honored to be the one to accept the challenge."<SUP id="cite_ref-TTVA101614_11-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TTVA101614-11">[11]</A></SUP> However, it wasn't until McCeary experienced the reactions to Maggie's existence from her fellow cast mates that McCeary realized just how big of a deal the character would be.<SUP id="cite_ref-THR100214_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-THR100214-12">[12]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The character's potential existence was first referenced in the press in February 2009 when <A href="/wiki/Michael_Ausiello" title="Michael Ausiello">Michael Ausiello</A> hinted at the possibility of Meredith having a half-sibling, the product of her mother's affair with Richard.<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP> Initial speculation pointed to <A href="/wiki/Jesse_Williams_(actor)" title="Jesse Williams (actor)">Jesse Williams</A>' <A href="/wiki/Jackson_Avery" title="Jackson Avery">Jackson Avery</A> as the child, but the actor refuted those rumors.<SUP id="cite_ref-Fancast120809_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Fancast120809-14">[14]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Shonda_Rhimes" title="Shonda Rhimes">Shonda Rhimes</A> revealed that the character had always been a part of the original story plans, but the character's existence was not set in stone until season 4.<SUP id="cite_ref-TVG071514_15-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TVG071514-15">[15]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Characterization">Characterization</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Maggie_Pierce&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Characterization">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Kelly McCeary expressed her excitement about how special Maggie in an interview with <A href="/wiki/BuddyTV" title="BuddyTV">BuddyTV</A>. "I just feel like it's a rare opportunity to be able to play somebody that is so complex and fully realized and smart and fierce and compassionate and awkward and the whole thing."<SUP id="cite_ref-Buddy100114_16-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Buddy100114-16">[16]</A></SUP> Maggie is very good at her job so she can find a place in a professional capacity, but in her personal life, she "gets more than she bargained for" McCreary said.<SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP> "I think she's a really good doctor" McCeary said of Maggie. "She's obviously super-bright. She's very young to be as high in her field as she is." McCeary further described Maggie as a "really great problem-solver." Maggie is "very compassionate" and at the same time can "keep a clear head and do the right thing medically all the time."<SUP id="cite_ref-Buddy100114_16-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Buddy100114-16">[16]</A></SUP> McCeary further described Maggie as "so dynamic."<SUP id="cite_ref-TTVA101614_11-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TTVA101614-11">[11]</A></SUP> While Maggie initially "came across as all business," Kelly McCeary relishes in playing "Maggie's neurotic, existential, meltdown side."<SUP id="cite_ref-Backstage120815_3-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Backstage120815-3">[3]</A></SUP> "Maggie also won't really back down from a fight; she's very decisive."<SUP id="cite_ref-THR100214_12-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-THR100214-12">[12]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Introduction">Introduction</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Maggie_Pierce&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Introduction">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <A href="/wiki/Puzzle_With_a_Piece_Missing" title="Puzzle With a Piece Missing">Puzzle With a Piece Missing</A> and <A href="/wiki/Got_to_Be_Real_(Grey%27s_Anatomy)" title="Got to Be Real (Grey's Anatomy)">Got to Be Real (Grey's Anatomy)</A></DIV>
<P>Kate Aurthur noted that until Maggie's introduction, <I>Grey's</I> was not "known for dropping in stories that it planted seasons before -- it's never been filled with twisty mythology."<SUP id="cite_ref-BF012915_10-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-BF012915-10">[10]</A></SUP> Rhimes insisted that the timing wasn't right for Maggie's introduction in previous seasons. In season 3, the series introduced Meredith's paternal half-sister <A href="/wiki/Lexie_Grey" title="Lexie Grey">Lexie Grey</A> (<A href="/wiki/Chyler_Leigh" title="Chyler Leigh">Chyler Leigh</A>) and it was at that time that Maggie became a serious topic of discussion. Though Lexie was killed off in the season 8 finale, "<A href="/wiki/Flight_(Grey%27s_Anatomy)" title="Flight (Grey's Anatomy)">Flight</A>," Rhimes felt it was still too soon for Maggie's arrival.<SUP id="cite_ref-Cosmo100914_9-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Cosmo100914-9">[9]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-THR071614_18-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-THR071614-18">[18]</A></SUP> The scribe even thought the show might end without the character ever being introduced. "Then we hit this moment in time and I remember walking into the writers' room and going, 'You guys, it's time.'"<SUP id="cite_ref-TVG071514_15-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TVG071514-15">[15]</A></SUP></P>
<P>When Maggie makes the sudden revelation that she is Ellis' child to Richard, viewers are left to wonder about her history. The second episode of the season puts Maggie front and center. The episode appropriately titled "<A href="/wiki/Puzzle_With_a_Piece_Missing" title="Puzzle With a Piece Missing">Puzzle With a Piece Missing</A>," focuses on Maggie's struggle to fit in throughout her life, even with her own adoptive parents whom she is very different from.<SUP id="cite_ref-EW093014_19-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-EW093014-19">[19]</A></SUP> Though she is very close with her parents, and they get along very well, she's grown up "still feeling like something's missing." Kelly McCreary said "That's what's really compelling to me about Maggie: that sort of dark underbelly of this person who seems to really have it all together."<SUP id="cite_ref-TVGM100114_20-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TVGM100114-20">[20]</A></SUP> Maggie struggles to build relationships with her colleagues. She unknowingly shares confidential information about <A href="/wiki/Alex_Karev" title="Alex Karev">Alex Karev</A> (<A href="/wiki/Justin_Chambers" title="Justin Chambers">Justin Chambers</A>) and she gets she also insults the hospital board when she tries to prop up <A href="/wiki/Miranda_Bailey" title="Miranda Bailey">Miranda Bailey</A> (<A href="/wiki/Chandra_Wilson" title="Chandra Wilson">Chandra Wilson</A>). Though she's got the "best intentions," things backfire.<SUP id="cite_ref-EW093014_19-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-EW093014-19">[19]</A></SUP> Maggie also serves as a "mentor" to <A href="/wiki/Jo_Wilson" class="mw-redirect" title="Jo Wilson">Jo Wilson</A> (<A href="/wiki/Camilla_Luddington" title="Camilla Luddington">Camilla Luddington</A>).<SUP id="cite_ref-ENetwork100214_21-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ENetwork100214-21">[21]</A></SUP> As Maggie discovers she has several things in common with Richard, the stage is set for Maggie to learn that Richard is her father.<SUP id="cite_ref-TVGM100114_20-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TVGM100114-20">[20]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-EW093014_19-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-EW093014-19">[19]</A></SUP></P>
<P>"I think people will relate to the awkwardness of being the new kid at school" McCeary said of the episode's comedic tone.<SUP id="cite_ref-TVGM100114_20-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TVGM100114-20">[20]</A></SUP> Despite so many different interactions, the episode highlights "Maggie's loneliness."<SUP id="cite_ref-ENetwork100214_21-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ENetwork100214-21">[21]</A></SUP> The Maggie-centric episode also featured Kelly McCreary stepping into the coveted role of narrator for the episode, which was usually reserved for <A href="/wiki/Ellen_Pompeo" title="Ellen Pompeo">Ellen Pompeo</A>'s Meredith, and on occasion other veteran cast members.<SUP id="cite_ref-THR100214Post_22-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-THR100214Post-22">[22]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-BuddyTV100214_23-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-BuddyTV100214-23">[23]</A></SUP> "It was overwhelming and very surprising" McCeary said of being the center of attention so early into her <I>Grey's</I> tenure. She continued, "I felt terrified and also really grateful that they trusted me with the institution about of <I>Grey's Anatomy</I> for a whole episode." McCeary relished in finally learning the character's history. "[It] was a huge gift to have 65 pages worth of material telling me exactly who she is. It was great!"<SUP id="cite_ref-ENetwork100214_21-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ENetwork100214-21">[21]</A></SUP></P>

<P>Critics responded positively to the development of Pierce in her centric episode "<A href="/wiki/Puzzle_With_a_Piece_Missing" title="Puzzle With a Piece Missing">Puzzle With a Piece Missing</A>". <I>Fempop</I> gave a largely positive review writing, "<I>Puzzle With a Piece Missing</I> is a funny and insightful look both into this latest interloper and the established characters of Grey’s." praising the new addition, "Thankfully she’s (Pierce) her own person, confident and happy to bring the thunder and put everyone, from interns to the chief of surgery, into their places."<SUP id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-24">[24]</A></SUP></P>
<P><I><A href="/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly" title="Entertainment Weekly">Entertainment Weekly</A></I> lauded the episode stating, "Coming into the second week without <A href="/wiki/Cristina_Yang" title="Cristina Yang">Cristina Yang</A>, Grey’s was smart to focus all of its attention on the newcomer. With most other main characters only making occasional cameos, it made it more difficult to feel Yang’s absence. And by showing Maggie’s side of the story, it made her more relatable. It was a win-win." adding on McCreary's character, " this episode is about how Maggie is her own, very likable person."<SUP id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-25">[25]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On her character <I>TV Fanatic</I> wrote, Overall, we got to know Maggie a little better and it's nice to see that she's made some friends. It was a fair episode that showed Maggie's basically a work in progress. Maybe she'll grow on us eventually."<SUP id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-26">[26]</A></SUP></P>
<P>For the thirteenth season, <I><A href="/wiki/Vulture" title="Vulture">Vulture</A></I> writer, Maggie Fremont spoke positively about the character: "It’s never easy for a long-running series to introduce a new character, especially when that character is meant to immediately fit in with the rest of the ensemble. But when Maggie Pierce arrived in season ten, that’s exactly what Grey’s Anatomy did. It could’ve been easy to dislike her — she showed up to take over cardio as Cristina Yang was leaving, for chrissakes! She was yet another one of Meredith’s long-lost sisters. The cards were really stacked against Maggie Pierce. Yet, thanks to the writers and Kelly McCreary’s terrific performance, Maggie was immediately endearing. She is weird and neurotic and cheerful. She is nothing like Cristina, but she fills a void that Meredith needs filled in order to function. Can you really imagine Grey’s without Maggie Pierce?"<SUP id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-27">[27]</A></SUP></P>

<P>"<B>I'll Be There for You</B>" is a song recorded by the American duo <A href="/wiki/The_Rembrandts" title="The Rembrandts">The Rembrandts</A>. It is best known as the <A href="/wiki/Theme_song" class="mw-redirect" title="Theme song">theme song</A> to the American <A href="/wiki/Sitcom" title="Sitcom">sitcom</A> <I><A href="/wiki/Friends" title="Friends">Friends</A></I>, which premiered during 1994 and ended in 2004.<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP> The song was also released as the first single from the group's third studio album <I><A href="/wiki/LP_(The_Rembrandts_album)" class="mw-redirect" title="LP (The Rembrandts album)">LP</A></I>.</P>
<P></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Song_information">Song information</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=I%27ll_Be_There_for_You_(The_Rembrandts_song)&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Song information">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>"I'll Be There for You" was co-written by <I>Friends</I> producers <A href="/wiki/David_Crane_(producer)" title="David Crane (producer)">David Crane</A> and <A href="/wiki/Marta_Kauffman" title="Marta Kauffman">Marta Kauffman</A>, Kauffman's husband, composer Michael Skloff, and songwriter <A href="/wiki/Allee_Willis" title="Allee Willis">Allee Willis</A>, along with Phil Sōlem and Danny Wilde, both of the Rembrandts. It is strongly influenced by <A href="/wiki/The_Beatles" title="The Beatles">The Beatles</A>, especially reminiscent of the "<A href="/wiki/I_Feel_Fine" title="I Feel Fine">I Feel Fine</A>" guitar riff, and is also highly reminiscent of <A href="/wiki/The_Monkees" title="The Monkees">The Monkees</A>' "<A href="/wiki/Pleasant_Valley_Sunday" title="Pleasant Valley Sunday">Pleasant Valley Sunday</A>."</P>
<P>The original theme, which is under one minute long, was later re-recorded as a three-minute pop song.<SUP id="cite_ref-Buzzefeed-story-of-song_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Buzzefeed-story-of-song-2">[2]</A></SUP> After <A href="/wiki/Nashville" class="mw-redirect" title="Nashville">Nashville</A> program director Charlie Quinn, along with radio announcer and music director Tom Peace, <A href="/wiki/Music_loop" class="mw-redirect" title="Music loop">looped</A> the original short version into a full-length track and broadcast it on radio station <A href="/wiki/WRVW" title="WRVW">WYHY</A>, it became so popular that they had to re-record it. "Our record label said we had to finish the song and record it. There was no way to get out of it," lead singer Phil Sōlem said.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Music_video">Music video</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=I%27ll_Be_There_for_You_(The_Rembrandts_song)&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Music video">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The music video of the song featured the six main stars of <I>Friends</I>, taking the singing and dancing roles of the band after, amusingly<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (August 2017)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>, attacking them all and bemusing everyone else on the set with their daft behaviour. The video was included as a bonus feature on several of the show's Complete Season DVD Boxsets.</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Chart_performance">Chart performance</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=I%27ll_Be_There_for_You_(The_Rembrandts_song)&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Chart performance">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>In the United States, the song topped the <I>Billboard</I> <A href="/wiki/Hot_100_Airplay" class="mw-redirect" title="Hot 100 Airplay">Hot 100 Airplay</A> chart for eight weeks. When the single was released 1995, it peaked at #3 on the <A href="/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart" title="UK Singles Chart">UK Singles Chart</A> in the United Kingdom and at #17 on the <A href="/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100" title="Billboard Hot 100"><I>Billboard</I> Hot 100</A> in the United States as the <A href="/wiki/A-side_and_B-side" title="A-side and B-side">flipside</A> to "This House Is Not a Home". It also peaked at #1 on the U.S. <A href="/wiki/Top_40_Mainstream" class="mw-redirect" title="Top 40 Mainstream">Top 40 Mainstream</A> and <A href="/wiki/Hot_Adult_Contemporary_Tracks" class="mw-redirect" title="Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks">Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks</A> charts.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The song was the most successful in Canada where it peaked at number 1 for 5 consecutive weeks.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In April 2004, the song was ranked at #15 on <I><A href="/wiki/Blender_(magazine)" title="Blender (magazine)">Blender</A></I> magazine's list of the "50 Worst Songs Ever".<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Compilation_usage">Compilation usage</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=I%27ll_Be_There_for_You_(The_Rembrandts_song)&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Compilation usage">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>

<UL>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Cover_versions">Cover versions</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=I%27ll_Be_There_for_You_(The_Rembrandts_song)&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Cover versions">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<UL>
<LI>American pop rock band <A href="/wiki/The_Goo_Goo_Dolls" class="mw-redirect" title="The Goo Goo Dolls">The Goo Goo Dolls</A> recorded their own version of this song which contained slightly altered lyrics, and a more upbeat tempo, rockier sound, as well as a <A href="/wiki/Glockenspiel" title="Glockenspiel">glockenspiel</A> in the rhythm track.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Yakko,_Wakko,_and_Dot" class="mw-redirect" title="Yakko, Wakko, and Dot">Yakko, Wakko, and Dot</A> of <I><A href="/wiki/Animaniacs" title="Animaniacs">Animaniacs</A></I> parodied the theme song as "We Won't Ever Leave" during a 1997 episode entitled "Acquaintances" (which is itself a spoof of <I>Friends</I>).</LI>
<LI>American punk rock band <A href="/wiki/Pink_Lincolns" title="Pink Lincolns">Pink Lincolns</A> covered this song under the title "Friends" for a 1997 compilation album titled <I>Show & Tell</I>.</LI>
<LI>Fictional American band <A href="/wiki/Alvin_and_the_Chipmunks" title="Alvin and the Chipmunks">Alvin and the Chipmunks</A> covered this song for their 2007 video game <I><A href="/wiki/Alvin_and_the_Chipmunks_(video_game)" title="Alvin and the Chipmunks (video game)">Alvin and the Chipmunks</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/%22Weird_Al%22_Yankovic" title=""Weird Al" Yankovic">"Weird Al" Yankovic</A> had planned to record a parody for his <I>Bad Hair Day</I> album called "Theme for Home Improvement or I'll Repair For You". Although the Rembrandts were fine with the parody idea, the producers of <I>Friends</I> were not, fearing that the show's theme would be overexposed. "Theme for Home Improvement" is nevertheless a concert favorite.</LI>
</UL>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="In_popular_culture">In popular culture</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=I%27ll_Be_There_for_You_(The_Rembrandts_song)&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: In popular culture">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<UL>
<LI>The 2013 comedy film <I><A href="/wiki/We%27re_the_Millers" title="We're the Millers">We're the Millers</A></I>, which stars <A href="/wiki/Jennifer_Aniston" title="Jennifer Aniston">Jennifer Aniston</A>, features a blooper during the credits where <A href="/wiki/Jason_Sudeikis" title="Jason Sudeikis">Jason Sudeikis</A> flips through radio stations and ends up on "I'll Be There for You". Sudeikis, <A href="/wiki/Emma_Roberts" title="Emma Roberts">Emma Roberts</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Will_Poulter" title="Will Poulter">Will Poulter</A> begin singing the song as Aniston covers her face laughing.</LI>
</UL>

<H1 id="firstHeading" class="firstHeading" lang="en">Transient lingual papillitis</H1>			<DIV id="bodyContent" class="mw-body-content">
				<DIV id="siteSub" class="noprint">From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia</DIV>				<DIV id="contentSub"></DIV>
								<DIV id="jump-to-nav" class="mw-jump">
					Jump to:					<A href="#mw-head">navigation</A>, 					<A href="#p-search">search</A>
				</DIV>
				<DIV id="mw-content-text" lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr"><DIV class="mw-parser-output"><TABLE class="plainlinks metadata ambox ambox-content ambox-Weasel" role="presentation">
<TBODY><TR>
<TD class="mbox-image">
<DIV style="width:52px"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Ambox_important.svg/40px-Ambox_important.svg.png" width="40" height="40" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Ambox_important.svg/60px-Ambox_important.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Ambox_important.svg/80px-Ambox_important.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="40" data-file-height="40" /></DIV>
</TD>
<TD class="mbox-text">
<DIV class="mbox-text-span">This article <B>contains <A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Unsupported_attributions" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch">weasel words</A>: vague phrasing that often accompanies <A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Neutral_point_of_view" title="Wikipedia:Neutral point of view">biased</A> or <A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability">unverifiable</A> information</B>. <SPAN class="hide-when-compact">Such statements should be <A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Improving_weasel-worded_statements" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch">clarified or removed</A>.</SPAN> <SMALL><I>(January 2014)</I></SMALL></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TBODY></TABLE>
<P><B>Transient lingual papillitis</B> (also termed <B>fungiform papillary glossitis</B>,<SUP id="cite_ref-Marks_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Marks-1">[1]</A></SUP> <B>eruptive lingual papillitis</B>,<SUP id="cite_ref-Roux_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Roux-2">[2]</A></SUP> or colloquially, <B>lie bumps</B>),<SUP id="cite_ref-Roux_2-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Roux-2">[2]</A></SUP> are painful, <A href="/wiki/Hypertrophic" class="mw-redirect" title="Hypertrophic">hypertrophic</A>, red and white <A href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Papillae" class="extiw" title="wiktionary:Papillae">papillae</A> on the <A href="/wiki/Tongue" title="Tongue">tongue</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Roux_2-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Roux-2">[2]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Cause">Cause</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Transient_lingual_papillitis&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Cause">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The name "lie bumps" is a result of a myth that telling lies would cause them. However, very little has been written about this condition in scientific articles or textbooks and scientific studies have failed to produce a definite cause.<SUP id="cite_ref-Roux_2-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Roux-2">[2]</A></SUP> Possible causes include: "stress, gastrointestinal upset, menstruation, acidic or sour food, smoking, and local trauma" (direct physical irritation) of the tongue. Lie bumps are often caused by the taste bud(s) splitting.</P>
<P>These bumps are small, white bumps on the base of the tongue. They are likely to be the result of transient lingual papillitis (TLP). This condition is limited to the upper (dorsal) surface of the tongue, affecting some of the tiny bumps on the tongue known as the fungiform papillae, what we commonly call the "taste buds."</P>
<P>TLP is a harmless problem.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (March 2018)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> These bumps can become notably red or white and are quite tender for up to several days. While the cause of TLP is not known with certainty, most experts<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Unsupported_attributions" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch"><SPAN title="The material near this tag possibly uses too-vague attribution or weasel words. (January 2014)">who?</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> feel that local accidental trauma (rubbing, scraping or biting) is a major factor; however, contact reactions to things like certain foods have also been suggested. Lie bumps are not contagious and the discomfort is relatively minor. Typically these lesions heal within a few days with no treatment, though a doctor may refer a patient to an oral pathologist in prolonged cases.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Treatments">Treatments</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Transient_lingual_papillitis&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Treatments">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>There are no specific treatments for this problem, other than using ice or numbing medicines to ease the pain.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2018)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP></P>

<P><B>Greatest Royal Rumble</B><SUP id="cite_ref-GRR_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GRR-3">[3]</A></SUP> was a <A href="/wiki/Professional_wrestling" title="Professional wrestling">professional wrestling</A> <A href="/wiki/Pay-per-view" title="Pay-per-view">pay-per-view</A> <A href="/wiki/List_of_WWE_pay-per-view_events" title="List of WWE pay-per-view events">event</A><SUP id="cite_ref-SkyPPV_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-SkyPPV-4">[4]</A></SUP> and <A href="/wiki/WWE_Network" title="WWE Network">WWE Network</A> <A href="/wiki/List_of_WWE_Network_events" title="List of WWE Network events">event</A><SUP id="cite_ref-Fedwork_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Fedwork-5">[5]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-GRRNetwork_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GRRNetwork-6">[6]</A></SUP> promoted by <A href="/wiki/WWE" title="WWE">WWE</A> for their <A href="/wiki/Raw_(WWE_brand)" title="Raw (WWE brand)">Raw</A> and <A href="/wiki/SmackDown_(WWE_brand)" title="SmackDown (WWE brand)">SmackDown</A> <A href="/wiki/WWE_brand_extension" title="WWE brand extension">brands</A>. The event was held on April 27, 2018 at the <A href="/wiki/King_Abdullah_Sports_City" title="King Abdullah Sports City">King Abdullah Sports City</A>'s King Abdullah International Stadium in <A href="/wiki/Jeddah" title="Jeddah">Jeddah</A>, <A href="/wiki/Saudi_Arabia" title="Saudi Arabia">Saudi Arabia</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-GRR_3-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GRR-3">[3]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> The event was scheduled for 7:00 p.m. local time. It aired live in the <A href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</A> at noon <A href="/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone" title="Eastern Time Zone">EDT</A>, with a pre-show starting at 11 a.m. EDT.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> At the event, all men's main roster championships were defended, in addition to a 50-man <A href="/wiki/Royal_Rumble_match" title="Royal Rumble match">Royal Rumble match</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-matchListing_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-matchListing-9">[9]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The card featured ten matches. In the main event, <A href="/wiki/Braun_Strowman" title="Braun Strowman">Braun Strowman</A> won the titular Greatest Royal Rumble match to become the inaugural <A href="#WWE_Greatest_Royal_Rumble_Championship">Greatest Royal Rumble Champion</A>. In the penultimate match, <A href="/wiki/Brock_Lesnar" title="Brock Lesnar">Brock Lesnar</A> retained the <A href="/wiki/WWE_Universal_Championship" title="WWE Universal Championship">Universal Championship</A> in a <A href="/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#Steel_Cage_match" title="Professional wrestling match types">steel cage match</A> against <A href="/wiki/Roman_Reigns" title="Roman Reigns">Roman Reigns</A>. On the undercard, the <A href="/wiki/WWE_Championship" title="WWE Championship">WWE Championship</A> match between <A href="/wiki/A.J._Styles" title="A.J. Styles">AJ Styles</A> and <A href="/wiki/Shinsuke_Nakamura" title="Shinsuke Nakamura">Shinsuke Nakamura</A> resulted in a double countout, <A href="/wiki/The_Undertaker" title="The Undertaker">The Undertaker</A> defeated <A href="/wiki/Rusev_(wrestler)" title="Rusev (wrestler)">Rusev</A> in a casket match, and <A href="/wiki/John_Cena" title="John Cena">John Cena</A> defeated <A href="/wiki/Triple_H" title="Triple H">Triple H</A> in the opening match.</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Production">Production</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=WWE_Greatest_Royal_Rumble&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Production">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Background">Background</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=WWE_Greatest_Royal_Rumble&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Background">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Since 1988, the Royal Rumble has been an annual event held by WWE and is typically shown on <A href="/wiki/Pay-per-view" title="Pay-per-view">pay-per-view</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-wwematch_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-wwematch-10">[10]</A></SUP> The event is highlighted by the Royal Rumble match, a <A href="/wiki/Battle_royal_(professional_wrestling)" title="Battle royal (professional wrestling)">battle royal</A> whose participants enter at timed intervals.<SUP id="cite_ref-stats_11-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-stats-11">[11]</A></SUP> The Greatest Royal Rumble included the largest version of the match to date, having a total of 50 participants.</P>
<P>On March 5, 2018, WWE and the <A href="/wiki/General_Sports_Authority" title="General Sports Authority">Saudi General Sports Authority</A> advertised the Greatest Royal Rumble, a live event to be held on April 27, 2018, at King Abdullah International Stadium, part of the King Abdullah Sports City, in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.<SUP id="cite_ref-auto_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-auto-12">[12]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-auto1_13-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-auto1-13">[13]</A></SUP> The event is a part of a 10-year strategic multi-platform partnership between WWE and the Saudi General Sports Authority in support of <A href="/wiki/Saudi_Vision_2030" title="Saudi Vision 2030">Saudi Vision 2030</A>, Saudi Arabia's social and economic reform program.<SUP id="cite_ref-GRR_3-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GRR-3">[3]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-auto2_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-auto2-14">[14]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On March 19, 2018, WWE scheduled seven championship matches for the event: the <A href="/wiki/WWE_Championship" title="WWE Championship">WWE Championship</A>, <A href="/wiki/WWE_Universal_Championship" title="WWE Universal Championship">Universal Championship</A>, <A href="/wiki/WWE_United_States_Championship" title="WWE United States Championship">United States Championship</A>, <A href="/wiki/WWE_Intercontinental_Championship" title="WWE Intercontinental Championship">Intercontinental Championship</A>, <A href="/wiki/WWE_SmackDown_Tag_Team_Championship" title="WWE SmackDown Tag Team Championship">SmackDown Tag Team Championship</A>, <A href="/wiki/WWE_Raw_Tag_Team_Championship" title="WWE Raw Tag Team Championship">Raw Tag Team Championship</A> and <A href="/wiki/WWE_Cruiserweight_Championship" title="WWE Cruiserweight Championship">Cruiserweight Championship</A> were to be defended at the event.</P>
<P>As revealed on March 22, 2018, the event was streamed live on the WWE Network.<SUP id="cite_ref-GRRNetwork_6-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GRRNetwork-6">[6]</A></SUP> It also aired on traditional pay-per-view in the United States<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP> and internationally.<SUP id="cite_ref-SkyPPV_4-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-SkyPPV-4">[4]</A></SUP> The event was also the first WWE pay-per-view to feature <A href="/wiki/Modern_Standard_Arabic" title="Modern Standard Arabic">Arabic</A> commentary.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In the weeks leading up to the event, the WWE held tryouts in Saudi Arabia. From these tryouts, eight were selected to receive training by WWE, which would include an opportunity to earn a spot at the Greatest Royal Rumble event itself.<SUP id="cite_ref-tryouts_17-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-tryouts-17">[17]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Storylines">Storylines</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=WWE_Greatest_Royal_Rumble&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Storylines">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The card comprised ten matches that resulted from scripted storylines and had results predetermined by <A href="/wiki/WWE" title="WWE">WWE</A> on the <A href="/wiki/Raw_(WWE_brand)" title="Raw (WWE brand)">Raw</A> and <A href="/wiki/SmackDown_(WWE_brand)" title="SmackDown (WWE brand)">SmackDown</A> <A href="/wiki/WWE_brand_extension" title="WWE brand extension">brands</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-HSW_18-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-HSW-18">[18]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-WWEnt_19-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-WWEnt-19">[19]</A></SUP> Storylines were produced on WWE's weekly television shows, <I><A href="/wiki/WWE_Raw" title="WWE Raw">Monday Night Raw</A></I>, <I><A href="/wiki/WWE_SmackDown" title="WWE SmackDown">SmackDown Live</A></I>,<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP> and the <A href="/wiki/Cruiserweight_(professional_wrestling)" title="Cruiserweight (professional wrestling)">cruiserweight</A>-exclusive <I><A href="/wiki/WWE_205_Live" title="WWE 205 Live">205 Live</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-21">[21]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On April 9, <A href="/wiki/Brock_Lesnar" title="Brock Lesnar">Brock Lesnar</A>, who had renewed his WWE contract, was scheduled to defend the Universal Championship against <A href="/wiki/Roman_Reigns" title="Roman Reigns">Roman Reigns</A> in a <A href="/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#Steel_cage_match" title="Professional wrestling match types">steel cage match</A> as a rematch from <A href="/wiki/WrestleMania_34" title="WrestleMania 34">WrestleMania 34</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-23">[23]</A></SUP> On <I>Raw</I> following WrestleMania, Reigns expressed frustration about not being told about his future matches and opponents, singling out the steel cage match with Lesnar. Reigns alleged that there was a conspiracy against him. <A href="/wiki/Samoa_Joe" title="Samoa Joe">Samoa Joe</A>, who had been out with an injury since January, came out and warned Reigns that Lesnar would beat him again.<SUP id="cite_ref-Raw04092018_24-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Raw04092018-24">[24]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On March 26, WWE scheduled a <A href="/wiki/Ladder_match" title="Ladder match">ladder match</A> between then-champion <A href="/wiki/The_Miz" title="The Miz">The Miz</A>, <A href="/wiki/Seth_Rollins" title="Seth Rollins">Seth Rollins</A>, <A href="/wiki/Finn_B%C3%A1lor" title="Finn Bálor">Finn Bálor</A>, and Samoa Joe for the Intercontinental Championship.<SUP id="cite_ref-326matches_25-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-326matches-25">[25]</A></SUP> At WrestleMania 34, The Miz lost the Intercontinental Championship to Rollins, thus making Rollins the defending champion.<SUP id="cite_ref-WM34_26-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-WM34-26">[26]</A></SUP> Both Miz and Joe were <A href="/wiki/2018_WWE_Superstar_Shake-up" title="2018 WWE Superstar Shake-up">traded to</A> SmackDown while Rollins and Bálor remained on Raw.<SUP id="cite_ref-Raw04162018_27-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Raw04162018-27">[27]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-SmackDown04172018_28-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-SmackDown04172018-28">[28]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On March 26, <A href="/wiki/Cesaro_and_Sheamus" title="Cesaro and Sheamus">Cesaro and Sheamus</A> were scheduled to defend the Raw Tag Team Championship against <A href="/wiki/The_Hardy_Boyz" title="The Hardy Boyz">The Hardy Boyz</A> (<A href="/wiki/Jeff_Hardy" title="Jeff Hardy">Jeff</A> and <A href="/wiki/Matt_Hardy" title="Matt Hardy">Matt Hardy</A>).<SUP id="cite_ref-326matches_25-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-326matches-25">[25]</A></SUP> At WrestleMania 34, however, Cesaro and Sheamus lost the titles to <A href="/wiki/Braun_Strowman" title="Braun Strowman">Braun Strowman</A> and 10-year-old Nicholas.<SUP id="cite_ref-WM34_26-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-WM34-26">[26]</A></SUP> The following night on <I>Raw</I>, Strowman and Nicholas relinquished the titles due to Nicholas being a fourth grader. Cesaro and Sheamus demanded their titles back, but Raw General Manager <A href="/wiki/Kurt_Angle" title="Kurt Angle">Kurt Angle</A> instead scheduled them to face the winner of the four-team Tag Team Eliminator tournament for the vacant titles at the Greatest Royal Rumble.<SUP id="cite_ref-Raw04092018_24-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Raw04092018-24">[24]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Matt_Hardy" title="Matt Hardy">"Woken" Matt Hardy</A> and <A href="/wiki/Bray_Wyatt" title="Bray Wyatt">Bray Wyatt</A> won the tournament by defeating Titus Worldwide (<A href="/wiki/Apollo_Crews" title="Apollo Crews">Apollo Crews</A> and <A href="/wiki/Titus_O%27Neil" title="Titus O'Neil">Titus O'Neil</A>) and <A href="/wiki/The_Revival_(professional_wrestling)" title="The Revival (professional wrestling)">The Revival</A> (<A href="/wiki/Dash_Wilder" title="Dash Wilder">Dash Wilder</A> and <A href="/wiki/Scott_Dawson_(wrestler)" title="Scott Dawson (wrestler)">Scott Dawson</A>).<SUP id="cite_ref-Raw04162018_27-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Raw04162018-27">[27]</A></SUP> Cesaro and Sheamus were then traded to SmackDown during the Superstar Shake-up.<SUP id="cite_ref-SmackDown04172018_28-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-SmackDown04172018-28">[28]</A></SUP></P>
<P>At WrestleMania 34, <A href="/wiki/The_Bludgeon_Brothers" title="The Bludgeon Brothers">The Bludgeon Brothers</A> (<A href="/wiki/Luke_Harper" title="Luke Harper">Harper</A> and <A href="/wiki/Erick_Rowan" title="Erick Rowan">Rowan</A>) defeated <A href="/wiki/The_Usos" title="The Usos">The Usos</A> (Jey and Jimmy Uso) and <A href="/wiki/The_New_Day_(professional_wrestling)" title="The New Day (professional wrestling)">The New Day's</A> <A href="/wiki/Big_E_(wrestler)" title="Big E (wrestler)">Big E</A> and <A href="/wiki/Kofi_Kingston" title="Kofi Kingston">Kofi Kingston</A> in a triple threat tag team match to win the SmackDown Tag Team Championship.<SUP id="cite_ref-WM34_26-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-WM34-26">[26]</A></SUP> On the following <I>SmackDown</I>, The Usos defeated The New Day to earn a title match at Greatest Royal Rumble.<SUP id="cite_ref-SmackDown04102018_29-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-SmackDown04102018-29">[29]</A></SUP></P>
<P>A match between <A href="/wiki/John_Cena" title="John Cena">John Cena</A> and <A href="/wiki/Triple_H" title="Triple H">Triple H</A> was scheduled on March 26.<SUP id="cite_ref-326matches_25-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-326matches-25">[25]</A></SUP></P>
<P><A href="/wiki/The_Undertaker" title="The Undertaker">The Undertaker</A>, was originally scheduled to face <A href="/wiki/Rusev_(wrestler)" title="Rusev (wrestler)">Rusev</A> in a <A href="/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#Casket_match" title="Professional wrestling match types">casket match</A>, the first match of its kind in three years.<SUP id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-30">[30]</A></SUP> Due to reasons not entirely clear, Rusev was temporarily replaced by <A href="/wiki/Chris_Jericho" title="Chris Jericho">Chris Jericho</A><SUP id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-31">[31]</A></SUP> — this was explained with Rusev's wife <A href="/wiki/Lana_(wrestling)" title="Lana (wrestling)">Lana</A> complaining about her husband competing in a casket match<SUP id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-32">[32]</A></SUP> — but eventually reinserted back into the match. Jericho was restored to his original participation in the Greatest Royal Rumble match.<SUP id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-33">[33]</A></SUP></P>
<P>At WrestleMania 34, <A href="/wiki/Jinder_Mahal" title="Jinder Mahal">Jinder Mahal</A> defeated <A href="/wiki/Randy_Orton" title="Randy Orton">Randy Orton</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bobby_Roode" title="Bobby Roode">Bobby Roode</A>, and Rusev in a fatal-four way match to win the United States Championship.<SUP id="cite_ref-WM34_26-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-WM34-26">[26]</A></SUP> Mahal was then traded to Raw and lost the championship to <A href="/wiki/Jeff_Hardy" title="Jeff Hardy">Jeff Hardy</A> and Mahal invoked his rematch clause for the Greatest Royal Rumble.<SUP id="cite_ref-Raw04162018_27-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Raw04162018-27">[27]</A></SUP> Hardy was then traded to SmackDown the following night.<SUP id="cite_ref-SmackDown04172018_28-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-SmackDown04172018-28">[28]</A></SUP></P>
<P>At WrestleMania 34, <A href="/wiki/A.J._Styles" title="A.J. Styles">AJ Styles</A> successfully defended the WWE Championship against <A href="/wiki/Shinsuke_Nakamura" title="Shinsuke Nakamura">Shinsuke Nakamura</A>. After the match, showed his respect to Styles but then attacked him with a low blow and a <I>Kinshasa</I>, turning <A href="/wiki/Heel_(professional_wrestling)" title="Heel (professional wrestling)">heel</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-WM34_26-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-WM34-26">[26]</A></SUP> On April 17, after repeated attacks on Styles by Nakamura, a rematch between the two was scheduled for the Greatest Royal Rumble.<SUP id="cite_ref-SmackDown04172018_28-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-SmackDown04172018-28">[28]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On the WrestleMania 34 pre-show, <A href="/wiki/Cedric_Alexander" title="Cedric Alexander">Cedric Alexander</A> defeated <A href="/wiki/Mustafa_Ali_(wrestler)" title="Mustafa Ali (wrestler)">Mustafa Ali</A> in the <A href="/wiki/WWE_tournaments#WWE_Cruiserweight_Championship_Tournament_(2018)" title="WWE tournaments">WWE Cruiserweight Championship tournament final</A> to win the vacant title.<SUP id="cite_ref-preWM34_34-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-preWM34-34">[34]</A></SUP> Two nights later on <I>205 Live</I>, <A href="/wiki/Buddy_Murphy" title="Buddy Murphy">Buddy Murphy</A> attacked the new champion during his celebration.<SUP id="cite_ref-205Live04112018_35-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-205Live04112018-35">[35]</A></SUP> Murphy was then scheduled to face Alexander for the title at the Greatest Royal Rumble, but he failed his mandatory weigh-in when he weighed 207 pounds, 2 pounds over the 205 pound weight limit. He was then removed from the match and banned from competing on <I>205 Live</I> until he met the weight requirement.<SUP id="cite_ref-205Live04172018_36-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-205Live04172018-36">[36]</A></SUP> The following week, <A href="/wiki/Kalisto_(wrestler)" title="Kalisto (wrestler)">Kalisto</A> earned a Cruiserweight Championship match at the Greatest Royal Rumble by winning a gauntlet match.<SUP id="cite_ref-205Live04242018_37-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-205Live04242018-37">[37]</A></SUP></P>

<P>The actual pay-per-view opened with John Cena facing Triple H. During the match, after trading finishers, and reversing each other's finishers, Cena performed an <I>Attitude Adjustment</I> on Triple H, a springboard into the corner turnbuckle, followed and another <I>Attitude Adjustment</I> to pick up the victory. Following the match Cena thanked the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for their hospitality, and expressed excitement over the event.<SUP id="cite_ref-GreatestRR_38-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreatestRR-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In the following match, Cedric Alexander defended the Cruiserweight Championship against Kalisto. The match ended when Alexander countered a <I>Salida Del Sol</I> attempt into a <I>Lumbar Check</I> to retain the title.<SUP id="cite_ref-GreatestRR_38-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreatestRR-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Next, the vacant Raw Tag Team Championship was contested between the team of Bray Wyatt and Matt Hardy and the former champions, Cesaro and Sheamus. In the end, Hardy distracted Sheamus, allowing Wyatt to perform a <I>Sister Abigail</I> on him. Hardy and Wyatt then performed a <I>wheelbarrow Twist of Fate</I> on Sheamus to win the title.<SUP id="cite_ref-GreatestRR_38-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreatestRR-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Jeff Hardy then defended the United States Championship against Jinder Mahal. In the end, Hardy performed a <I>Swanton Bomb</I> on Mahal to retain the title.<SUP id="cite_ref-GreatestRR_38-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreatestRR-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<P>After that, The Bludgeons Brothers defended the SmackDown Tag Team Championship against The Usos. Harper and Rowan retained their titles after performing a <I>Double Crucifix Powerbomb</I> on Jimmy Uso.<SUP id="cite_ref-GreatestRR_38-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreatestRR-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Next, Seth Rollins defended the Intercontinental Championship against Finn Balor, Samoa Joe and The Miz in a Ladder match. Near the end of the match, Finn Balor climbed the ladder to unhook the championship, only for Rollins to leap from the top rope onto the ladder and managed to retrieve the title belt before Balor, thus retaining his championship.<SUP id="cite_ref-GreatestRR_38-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreatestRR-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Later, AJ Styles defended the WWE Championship against Shinsuke Nakamura. During the match, Nakamura resorted to various illegal tactics, such as a <I>Low Blow</I>, increasingly frustrating Styles. In the end, both Nakamura and Styles brawled outside of the ring only for the match to end in a double countout. Post-match Styles performed a <I>Phenomenal Forearm</I> over the top rope on Nakamura.<SUP id="cite_ref-GreatestRR_38-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreatestRR-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<P>After that, The Undertaker fought Rusev (who was accompanied by Aiden English) in a Casket match. At the end of the match, Undertaker performed a Chokeslam on Rusev and rolled him into the casket. Before he could close the lid, English attacked the Undertaker, who retailiated with another Chokeslam and a Tombstone Piledriver before putting English into the casket alongside Rusev and closing it for the victory.<SUP id="cite_ref-GreatestRR_38-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreatestRR-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In the penultimate match, Brock Lesnar (accompanied by Paul Heyman) defended the Universal Championship against Roman Reigns in a steel cage match. Lesnar delivered multiple <I>German Suplexes</I> during the match, and both men kicked out of each other's finishing moves. At one point in the match, Reigns tried to escape the cage through the door only for Heyman to slam the door on Reigns. The match ended after Reigns put Lesnar through the cage wall with a <I>Spear</I>, sending it onto the floor. Despite Reigns touching the floor with both feet first, the referee awarded the win to Lesnar, thereby retaining the Universal Championship.<SUP id="cite_ref-GreatestRR_38-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreatestRR-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Main_event">Main event</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=WWE_Greatest_Royal_Rumble&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Main event">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P><A href="/wiki/Daniel_Bryan" title="Daniel Bryan">Daniel Bryan</A> and <A href="/wiki/Dolph_Ziggler" title="Dolph Ziggler">Dolph Ziggler</A> began the 50-man Royal Rumble match as the first two entrants. Bryan survived until the final 3, beating out <A href="/wiki/Rey_Mysterio" title="Rey Mysterio">Rey Mysterio</A> for the longest time spent in a single Royal Rumble match of all time at an hour and sixteen minutes. At the end of the match, <A href="/wiki/Big_Cass" title="Big Cass">Big Cass</A> eliminated Bryan only for Cass to then attempt a <I>Big Boot</I> on <A href="/wiki/Braun_Strowman" title="Braun Strowman">Braun Strowman</A>, who ducked and knocked Cass over the top rope to win the match. Strowman also achieved the most eliminations of a single Royal Rumble match at 13, beating out a record previously held by Roman Reigns with 12.<SUP id="cite_ref-ViewReport_39-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ViewReport-39">[39]</A></SUP> Post-match, Strowman received a trophy and the Greatest Royal Rumble Championship.<SUP id="cite_ref-GreatestRR_38-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreatestRR-38">[38]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Controversy">Controversy</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=WWE_Greatest_Royal_Rumble&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Controversy">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <A href="/wiki/Women_in_WWE" title="Women in WWE">Women in WWE</A></DIV>
<P>WWE had been criticized for holding the event without female wrestlers, who were unable to perform at the event due to the <A href="/wiki/Women%27s_rights_in_Saudi_Arabia" title="Women's rights in Saudi Arabia">limited rights women have in Saudi Arabia</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Independent_40-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Independent-40">[40]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Uproxx_41-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Uproxx-41">[41]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Triple_H" title="Triple H">Triple H</A>, WWE's Executive Vice President of Talent, Live Events and Creative, responded to the criticism: "I understand that people are questioning it, but you have to understand that every culture is different and just because you don’t agree with a certain aspect of it, it doesn’t mean it’s not a relevant culture...You can’t dictate to a country or a religion about how they handle things but, having said that, WWE is at the forefront of a women’s evolution in the world and what you can’t do is effect change anywhere by staying away from it....While women are not competing in the event, we have had discussions about that and hope that, in the next few years they will be".<SUP id="cite_ref-Independent_40-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Independent-40">[40]</A></SUP> Women were in attendance for the event, though only if <A href="/wiki/Women%27s_rights_in_Saudi_Arabia#Male_guardians" title="Women's rights in Saudi Arabia">accompanied by a male guardian</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Independent_40-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Independent-40">[40]</A></SUP> This was a major change from previous events, which were only open to men. <A href="/wiki/Associated_Press" title="Associated Press">Associated Press</A> noted that this is due to "a series of social changes" by the Crown Prince <A href="/wiki/Mohammad_bin_Salman" title="Mohammad bin Salman">Mohammad bin Salman</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-42">[42]</A></SUP> During the event, WWE aired a promotional video, which included WWE female wrestlers. The Saudi General Sports Authority issued an apology for "indecent material" that aired at the event.<SUP id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-43">[43]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In addition to the women, wrestler <A href="/wiki/Sami_Zayn" title="Sami Zayn">Sami Zayn</A> did not participate in the event as Zayn is of <A href="/wiki/Syrian_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Syrian people">Syrian</A> descent, and Saudi Arabia has strained relations with Syria.<SUP id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-44">[44]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Another subject of criticism was the situation of <A href="/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Saudi_Arabia" title="LGBT rights in Saudi Arabia">LGBT rights in Saudi Arabia</A>, as in Saudi Arabia homosexual intercourse is illegal and can be punished by death.<SUP id="cite_ref-45" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-45">[45]</A></SUP></P>

<P>The <B>WWE Greatest Royal Rumble Championship</B>, also known as the <B>Belt Kingdom Championship</B> (<A href="/wiki/Arabic" title="Arabic">Arabic</A>: <B>حزام بطولة المملكة</B>), is a <A href="/wiki/Professional_wrestling_championship" title="Professional wrestling championship">professional wrestling championship</A> created and promoted by American <A href="/wiki/Professional_wrestling_promotion" title="Professional wrestling promotion">professional wrestling promotion</A> <A href="/wiki/WWE" title="WWE">WWE</A> and sanctioned by the <A href="/wiki/General_Sports_Authority" title="General Sports Authority">Saudi General Sports Authority</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-58">[58]</A></SUP> The current and inaugural champion is <A href="/wiki/Braun_Strowman" title="Braun Strowman">Braun Strowman</A>, who was awarded the championship for winning the 50-man Greatest Royal Rumble match at the namesake event.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="History">History</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=WWE_Greatest_Royal_Rumble&action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section: History">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>On March 5, 2018, WWE and the <A href="/wiki/General_Sports_Authority" title="General Sports Authority">Saudi General Sports Authority</A> advertised the Greatest Royal Rumble, a live event to be held on April 27, 2018, at King Abdullah International Stadium, part of the King Abdullah Sports City, in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.<SUP id="cite_ref-auto_12-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-auto-12">[12]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-auto1_13-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-auto1-13">[13]</A></SUP> The event was part of a 10-year strategic multi-platform partnership between WWE and the Saudi General Sports Authority in support of <A href="/wiki/Saudi_Vision_2030" title="Saudi Vision 2030">Saudi Vision 2030</A>, Saudi Arabia's social and economic reform program.<SUP id="cite_ref-GRR_3-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GRR-3">[3]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-auto2_14-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-auto2-14">[14]</A></SUP> The Greatest Royal Rumble Championship was unveiled by WWE on April 27, 2018 during the Greatest Royal Rumble event.<SUP id="cite_ref-59" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-59">[59]</A></SUP> The championship was announced on the official website of the <A href="/wiki/General_Sports_Authority" title="General Sports Authority">Saudi General Sports Authority</A> as the Belt Kingdom Championship.<SUP id="cite_ref-60" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-60">[60]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Braun_Strowman" title="Braun Strowman">Braun Strowman</A>, the 41st entrant of the 50-man <A href="/wiki/Royal_Rumble_match" title="Royal Rumble match">Greatest Royal Rumble match</A>, became the inaugural Greatest Royal Rumble Champion by lastly eliminating <A href="/wiki/Big_Cass" title="Big Cass">Big Cass</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-61" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-61">[61]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-62">[62]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-63">[63]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Championship_belt_design">Championship belt design</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=WWE_Greatest_Royal_Rumble&action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section: Championship belt design">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>As with some other championship belts unveiled in 2016, the base design is <A href="/wiki/WWE_Championship#Current_design" title="WWE Championship">similar</A> to the <A href="/wiki/WWE_Championship" title="WWE Championship">WWE Championship</A>, with notable differences.<SUP id="cite_ref-64" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-64">[64]</A></SUP> Instead of a large cut out of the WWE logo, the center plate is modeled with Arabic pattern with the WWE logo in the center. Like the WWE Championship belt and other belts introduced in 2016 and 2017, the Greatest Royal Rumble Championship belt features two side plates, both separated by gold divider bars, with removable round sections that can be replaced with the current champion's logo; the default plates feature the official logo of <A href="/wiki/General_Sports_Authority" title="General Sports Authority">Saudi General Sports Authority</A> which is identical to the <A href="/wiki/Emblem_of_Saudi_Arabia" title="Emblem of Saudi Arabia">national emblem of Saudi Arabia</A>. The plates are on a green leather strap resembling the color of the <A href="/wiki/Flag_of_Saudi_Arabia" title="Flag of Saudi Arabia">national flag of Saudi Arabia</A>.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Reigns">Reigns</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=WWE_Greatest_Royal_Rumble&action=edit&section=14" title="Edit section: Reigns">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>As of May 28, 2018, there has been one reign, which is the inaugural and current champion, <A href="/wiki/Braun_Strowman" title="Braun Strowman">Braun Strowman</A>.</P>

<P><I><B>Bugsy Malone</B></I> is a 1976 American-British <A href="/wiki/Musical_film" title="Musical film">musical</A> <A href="/wiki/Mob_film" class="mw-redirect" title="Mob film">gangster</A> <A href="/wiki/Comedy_film" title="Comedy film">comedy film</A>, directed by <A href="/wiki/Alan_Parker" title="Alan Parker">Alan Parker</A> and featuring only <A href="/wiki/Child_actor" title="Child actor">child actors</A>. Set in <A href="/wiki/New_York_City" title="New York City">New York City</A>, the film is loosely based on events in New York and Chicago from the early 1920s to 1931 during <A href="/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States" title="Prohibition in the United States">Prohibition</A>, specifically the exploits of real-life <A href="/wiki/Gangster" title="Gangster">gangsters</A> like <A href="/wiki/Al_Capone" title="Al Capone">Al Capone</A> and <A href="/wiki/Bugs_Moran" title="Bugs Moran">Bugs Moran</A>, as dramatized in cinema. Parker lightened the subject matter considerably for the children's market; in the U.S. the film received a <A href="/wiki/MPAA_rating" class="mw-redirect" title="MPAA rating">G rating</A>.</P>
<P>The film was Parker's feature-length <A href="/wiki/Directorial_debut" class="mw-redirect" title="Directorial debut">directorial debut</A>, introduced actor <A href="/wiki/Scott_Baio" title="Scott Baio">Scott Baio</A>, and featured a 13-year old <A href="/wiki/Jodie_Foster" title="Jodie Foster">Jodie Foster</A>.</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Plot">Plot</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Bugsy_Malone&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Plot">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>A mobster named Roxy Robinson is "splurged" by members of a gang, using rapid-fire cream-shooting "splurge guns". Once splurged, a kid is "all washed up... finished". <A href="/wiki/Speakeasy" title="Speakeasy">Speakeasy</A> boss Fat Sam introduces himself and Bugsy Malone, a boxing promoter with no money ("Bugsy Malone").</P>
<P>At Fat Sam's <A href="/wiki/Speakeasy" title="Speakeasy">speakeasy</A>, there is much dancing and singing ("Fat Sam's Grand Slam"). Fat Sam is worried that his rival Dandy Dan will try to take control of the speakeasy. Blousey Brown, an aspiring singer, has come for an audition, but Sam is too distracted to see her. Bugsy meets Blousey when he trips over her luggage. He is smitten and flirts with her. Fat Sam's is raided by Dandy Dan's men, who shoot up the place. Dandy Dan's men continue to attack Fat Sam's empire, eventually taking away rackets and splurging members of Fat Sam's gang. Fat Sam sends all his available men to see if they can track down the guns. They are trapped at a laundry and all are splurged by Dandy Dan's gang.</P>
<P>Bugsy returns to Fat Sam's to arrange a new audition for Blousey. Fat Sam's girlfriend, the chanteuse Tallulah, makes a pass at him. Although Bugsy rejects her flirtation, Tallulah plants a big kiss on Bugsy's forehead when Blousey enters; Blousey is jealous. Fat Sam hires Blousey after her audition, but she refuses to speak to Bugsy ("I'm Feelin' Fine").</P>
<P>Fat Sam hires Bugsy to accompany him to a meeting with Dandy Dan. The meeting is a trap, but Bugsy helps Fat Sam escape. Gratefully, Fat Sam pays him $200. Bugsy and Blousey reconcile and have a romantic outing on a lake; Bugsy promises to take her to Hollywood. When he returns Sam's car to the garage, he is attacked and his money is stolen. Bugsy is saved by Leroy Smith, who assaults the attackers and drives them away. Bugsy realizes that Leroy has the potential to be a great boxer. Bugsy introduces Leroy to Cagey Joe and helps him train ("So You Wanna Be a Boxer?"). Fat Sam again seeks Bugsy's aid after his assistant Knuckles is unintentionally killed. Bugsy resists, but Fat Sam offers $400, enough money to keep his promise to Blousey. Blousey is disappointed when she learns that Bugsy hasn't bought the tickets to California yet ("Ordinary Fool"). Bugsy and Leroy follow Dandy Dan's men to a warehouse, where the guns are being stashed. The two of them can't take the place alone, so Bugsy recruits a large group of down-and-out workers at a soup kitchen ("Down and Out").</P>
<P>They steal the crates of guns and take them to Fat Sam's, arriving just as Dandy Dan's gang arrives. Chaos ensues as a massive splurge gun fight erupts, covering everyone (except Bugsy and Blousey) with cream. Unarmed patrons throw cream pies. The piano player is hit from behind and falls onto the keys, striking a single bass note. The tone silences the room, and the cream-covered crowd performs in a final number ("You Give a Little Love"). They realize they can all be friends, and Bugsy and Blousey leave for Hollywood.</P>
