<H3><SPAN id="Bonnie.27s_toys"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Bonnie's_toys">Bonnie's toys</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=32" title="Edit section: Bonnie's toys">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>These characters are the toys owned by <A href="#Bonnie_Anderson">Bonnie</A> in <I>Toy Story 3</I> and the short films.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Chuckles">Chuckles</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=33" title="Edit section: Chuckles">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by:
</P>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Bud_Luckey" title="Bud Luckey">Bud Luckey</A> (2010–2011)</LI></UL>
<P><B>Chuckles</B> is a brokenhearted toy <A href="/wiki/Clown" title="Clown">clown</A> who was once owned by Daisy (along with Lotso and Big Baby), and is later owned by Bonnie. He is first seen mournfully looking out the kitchen window in Bonnie's house, where he tells Woody about Lotso's past, stating that Lotso used to be a good friend. Chuckles explains that he, Lotso, and Big Baby were accidentally left behind on a trip with Daisy's family, and when they finally made it back to Daisy's house, both him and Lotso discovered that Lotso had been replaced, which caused Lotso to snap. Chuckles objected when Lotso claimed all three had been replaced, but Lotso silenced him, and lied to Big Baby, saying that Daisy did not love him anymore. After the three found their way to Sunnyside and Lotso took over, running it like a prison, Chuckles was damaged and Bonnie found him and took him home. He still feels sorry for what happened to Lotso, but knows that what Lotso is doing at Sunnyside is wrong. He gives Woody a pendant (which formerly belonged to Big Baby) that says <I>My heart belongs to Daisy,</I> which later leads Big Baby to discover Lotso's deception and rebel against him. In one of the end credits sequences, Chuckles sees a crayon-drawn picture of him, and Dolly says that "Bonnie really got your smile," making Chuckles happy again, for the first time in many years.
</P><P>Chuckles returns in the short film <I><A href="/wiki/Hawaiian_Vacation" title="Hawaiian Vacation">Hawaiian Vacation</A></I> and he sings a Hawaiian love song while playing a <A href="/wiki/Ukulele" title="Ukulele">ukulele</A> when Barbie and Ken get their recreated Hawaiian adventures. He also appears in <I><A href="/wiki/Small_Fry_(film)" title="Small Fry (film)">Small Fry</A>.</I>
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Dolly">Dolly</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=34" title="Edit section: Dolly">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Bonnie_Hunt" title="Bonnie Hunt">Bonnie Hunt</A>
</P><P><B>Dolly</B> is a soft dress-up rag doll with purple hair, <A href="/wiki/Googly_eyes" title="Googly eyes">googly-eyes</A>, an orange dress with buttons sewn on, and gently blushing cheeks. She helps Woody get back to Sunnyside Daycare Center with the rest of Andy's toys. In the <A href="/wiki/Toy_Story_3_(video_game)" class="mw-redirect" title="Toy Story 3 (video game)"><I>Toy Story 3</I> video game</A>, she is seen as a witch. It's indicated that she is the leader of Bonnie's toys.
</P><P>Dolly appears in the theatrical short films <I><A href="/wiki/Hawaiian_Vacation" title="Hawaiian Vacation">Hawaiian Vacation</A></I>, <I><A href="/wiki/Small_Fry_(film)" title="Small Fry (film)">Small Fry</A></I>, and <I><A href="/wiki/Partysaurus_Rex" title="Partysaurus Rex">Partysaurus Rex</A></I>.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Mr._Pricklepants">Mr. Pricklepants</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=35" title="Edit section: Mr. Pricklepants">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Timothy_Dalton" title="Timothy Dalton">Timothy Dalton</A>
</P><P><B>Mr. Pricklepants</B> is a stuffed <A href="/wiki/Hedgehog" title="Hedgehog">hedgehog</A>. He wears <A href="/wiki/Lederhosen" title="Lederhosen">lederhosen</A> and a <A href="/wiki/Tyrolean_hat" title="Tyrolean hat">Tyrolean hat</A>, and views himself as a <A href="/wiki/Actor" title="Actor">thespian</A>. Mr. Pricklepants was made in <A href="/wiki/Germany" title="Germany">Germany</A> (although he speaks with an English accent and actor's diction) and is from the Waldfreunde (Forest Friends) collection of premium imported plush toys. Throughout <I>Toy Story 3</I>, he expresses great interest in <A href="/wiki/Theater_arts" class="mw-redirect" title="Theater arts">theater arts</A> and in the same respect, takes the art of role playing as a child's toy very seriously. Buttercup refers to him sarcastically as "Baron von Shush" due to his habit of "shushing" the other toys when they break character. During the credits, he plays <A href="/wiki/Romeo_Montague" class="mw-redirect" title="Romeo Montague">Romeo</A>, with one of the aliens playing <A href="/wiki/Juliet_Capulet" class="mw-redirect" title="Juliet Capulet">Juliet</A>.
</P><P>Mr. Pricklepants reappears in the short films <I><A href="/wiki/Hawaiian_Vacation" title="Hawaiian Vacation">Hawaiian Vacation</A></I>, <I><A href="/wiki/Small_Fry_(film)" title="Small Fry (film)">Small Fry</A></I>, and <I><A href="/wiki/Partysaurus_Rex" title="Partysaurus Rex">Partysaurus Rex</A></I>, and appeared in the TV specials <I>Toy Story of Terror!</I> and <I>Toy Story That Time Forgot</I>.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Trixie">Trixie</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=36" title="Edit section: Trixie">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Kristen_Schaal" title="Kristen Schaal">Kristen Schaal</A>
</P><P><B>Trixie</B> is a blue toy <I><A href="/wiki/Triceratops" title="Triceratops">Triceratops</A></I>. She chats online with "a dinosaur toy down the street" who goes by the name "Velocistar237." She becomes best friends with Rex during the credits, playing cooperatively on a computer.
</P><P>Trixie reappears in the short films <I>Hawaiian Vacation</I>, <I>Small Fry,</I> and <I>Partysaurus Rex</I>, and appears in the TV specials <I>Toy Story of Terror!</I> and <I>Toy Story That Time Forgot</I>.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Buttercup">Buttercup</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=37" title="Edit section: Buttercup">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Jeff_Garlin" title="Jeff Garlin">Jeff Garlin</A>
</P><P><B>Buttercup</B>  is a white <A href="/wiki/Unicorn" title="Unicorn">unicorn</A> with a yellow mane and a pink nose. Despite his appearance, he has a very gruff voice and sarcastic personality. He is the first to introduce himself to Woody when Bonnie brings him home. He later appears at the end of the movie, now very close friends with Hamm.
</P><P>He also appears in <I><A href="/wiki/Small_Fry_(film)" title="Small Fry (film)">Small Fry</A></I>, <I><A href="/wiki/Hawaiian_Vacation" title="Hawaiian Vacation">Hawaiian Vacation</A></I>, and <I><A href="/wiki/Partysaurus_Rex" title="Partysaurus Rex">Partysaurus Rex</A></I>.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Peas-in-a-Pod">Peas-in-a-Pod</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=38" title="Edit section: Peas-in-a-Pod">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by
</P>
<UL><LI>Charlie Bright, Amber Kroner, and Brianna Maiwand in <I>Toy Story 3</I></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Zoe_Levin" title="Zoe Levin">Zoe Levin</A> in <I>Hawaiian Vacation</I> and <I>Small Fry</I></LI></UL>
<P><B>Peas-in-a-Pod</B> are three soft, plush green balls in a green zip-up case that looks like a <A href="/wiki/Pea_pod" class="mw-redirect" title="Pea pod">pea pod</A>. They have the personalities of small children, and their names are Peaty, Peatrice, and Peanelope.
</P><P>The Peas-in-a-Pod reappear in the short film <I>Hawaiian Vacation</I>. They also appear in <I>Small Fry</I>.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Angel_Kitty">Angel Kitty</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=39" title="Edit section: Angel Kitty">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by Emma Hudak
</P><P><B>Angel Kitty</B> is a Christmas ornament that only appears in <I>Toy Story That Time Forgot</I>. A running gag in the film is Angel Kitty giving a moral about Christmas much to other toys' (mostly Trixie) dismay and joy. She is mostly seen with a trumpet giving morals. She was last seen in Toy Story That Time Forgot giving one last moral and "vanishes".
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Totoro">Totoro</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=40" title="Edit section: Totoro">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Totoro</B>, the title character from <I><A href="/wiki/My_Neighbor_Totoro" title="My Neighbor Totoro">My Neighbor Totoro</A></I>, who is also the <A href="/wiki/Mascot" title="Mascot">mascot</A> of <A href="/wiki/Studio_Ghibli" title="Studio Ghibli">Studio Ghibli</A>, appears as one of Bonnie's toys. He is a big plush toy and does not speak at all during the film, nor is he spoken to by anyone by his name. He does however display his famous grin during the credit scenes, and at the end of the film, he is seen juggling the alien triplets, while Mr. and Mrs. Potato Head watch. According to the tie-in book, <I>The Art of Toy Story 3</I>,<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (June 2011)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> Totoro's appearance in the film was intended as a tribute to <A href="/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki" title="Hayao Miyazaki">Hayao Miyazaki</A>, who is a close friend of Pixar executive <A href="/wiki/John_Lasseter" title="John Lasseter">John Lasseter</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP> In addition to Lasseter's relationship to Miyazaki, another factor that contributed to Totoro's appearance was Disney's role in dubbing <A href="/wiki/Studio_Ghibli" title="Studio Ghibli">Studio Ghibli</A> films for their English-language releases.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H3><SPAN id="Sid_and_Hannah.27s_toys"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Sid_and_Hannah's_toys">Sid and Hannah's toys</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=41" title="Edit section: Sid and Hannah's toys">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The following toys are only seen in the first film.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Combat_Carl">Combat Carl</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=42" title="Edit section: Combat Carl">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Combat Carl</B> is a <A href="/wiki/G.I._Joe" title="G.I. Joe">G.I. Joe</A>-type toy character. He first appears as a toy of Sid's that Sid blows up with an <A href="/wiki/M-80_(explosive)" title="M-80 (explosive)">M-80</A> explosive in his first scene in <I>Toy Story</I>. Pieces of him are later seen coming to life during Woody's plan to frighten Sid into altering his behavior near the end of the film.
</P><P>A <A href="/wiki/List_of_Toy_Story_characters#Sleep_Well_Toys" title="List of Toy Story characters">different character with the same name</A> appears in <I>Toy Story of Terror!</I>
</P>
<H4><SPAN id="Hannah.27s_dolls"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Hannah's_dolls">Hannah's dolls</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=43" title="Edit section: Hannah's dolls">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<UL><LI><I>For Janie, see "Janie and Pterodactyl" under "Mutant toys."</I></LI>
<LI><B>Sally</B>—Sally is Hannah's replacement doll for Janie. Sally has brown hair and a yellow dress. After Sid is attacked by the toys, Sid sees Sally, then runs off in fright, thinking that Sally will come to life.</LI></UL>
<UL><LI><B>Marie Antoinette and her little sister</B>—Marie Antoinette and her little sister are a company of two headless dolls from Hannah's tea party. One is <A href="/wiki/Barbie" title="Barbie">Barbie</A> without her original legs (she has spare legs from a rag doll body), and the second is rag doll in violet bloom dress. A dark brown headless <A href="/wiki/Teddy_bear" title="Teddy bear">teddy bear</A> is also seen with the dolls. It is because Sid tortured Hannah's toys. Yet, she is able to play with them. "<A href="/wiki/Marie_Antoinette" title="Marie Antoinette">Marie Antoinette</A>" is probably a nickname (given by Buzz), based on their headlessness rather than the actual name of one of the toys.</LI></UL>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Mutant_toys">Mutant toys</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=44" title="Edit section: Mutant toys">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>The <B>Mutant Toys</B> are mutilated toys who live their unhappy lives in the darkest corners of Sid's room. They are assembled by Sid from mixed pieces of several toys that belong to him and Hannah (hence the baby doll's parts). They do not speak, though it is revealed they know Morse Code. Woody and Buzz initially think that they are <A href="/wiki/Cannibal" class="mw-redirect" title="Cannibal">cannibals</A> who are going to eat them, before they learn that the toys are actually friendly and compassionate. They fix Buzz's broken arm, Janie and the Pterodactyl, and also help Woody implement his plan to save Buzz from Sid. They close in on Sid as Woody tells Sid how much they hate being mutilated, and they all rejoice in victory after Woody frightens Sid away with his own voice. In <I>Toy Story Treats</I>, the Mutant Toys appear in Andy's house.
</P>
<UL><LI><B>Baby Face</B> – The leader of the mutant toys, he is a one-eyed baby doll head staked on top of a <A href="/wiki/Spider" title="Spider">spider</A>-like body with <A href="/wiki/Crab" title="Crab">crab</A>-like pincers made of <A href="/wiki/Erector_set" class="mw-redirect" title="Erector set">Erector set</A> pieces. Baby Face lives in the shadows under Sid's bed. One way Baby Face communicates with the other toys is by banging in <A href="/wiki/Morse_code" title="Morse code">Morse code</A> on the side of Sid's metal bedpost with his big claw. This method is used when he signals the other mutant toys to gather around to listen to Woody as he formulates his plan to rescue Buzz from Sid. When the mutant toys gain on Sid, Baby Face, suspended by Legs, lands on Sid's head, scaring him. Baby Face is a playable character in the <I>Toy Story Racer</I> video game.</LI>
<LI><B>Legs</B> – A toy <A href="/wiki/Fishing_rod" title="Fishing rod">fishing rod</A> with <A href="/wiki/Barbie" title="Barbie">Barbie</A> doll legs. She is shown to be very strong, being able to hold Ducky's and Baby Face's weight. When Woody formulates his plan to save Buzz from Sid, he assigns Legs to partner up with Ducky. Legs opens the vent grating so she and Ducky can go to the front porch, where Legs lowers Ducky through the hole Ducky created so Ducky can swing toward the doorbell. After Ducky catches the Frog, Legs pulls both toys up to safety. Later, when the mutant toys advance on Sid, Legs lowers Baby Face onto Sid's head, scaring him.</LI>
<LI><B>Hand-in-the-Box</B> – Hand-in-the-box is based on the character <A href="/wiki/Thing_(The_Addams_Family)" title="Thing (The Addams Family)">Thing</A> from the 1960s TV horror spoof <I><A href="/wiki/The_Addams_Family" title="The Addams Family">The Addams Family</A></I>. A green rubber arm that emerges from a black box, it appears to be based on the electro-mechanical coin-bank that was marketed as part of the show's merchandising. During Woody's plan to save Buzz from Sid, Hand-in-the-box, held by Rockmobile mounted on Babyface's head, extends its hand to the doorknob, ready to open the door when the signal comes. After the Frog is let out the room to distract Scud, Hand-in-the-box mounts Roller Bob (held by Rockmobile) and extends its hand to pull Jingle Joe (carrying Janie and the Pterodactyl) when Woody motions the other mutant toys to go down to Sid's backyard. The Hand also grabs Sid's leg when the mutant toys surround him.</LI>
<LI><B>Roller Bob</B> – A <A href="/wiki/Jet_plane" class="mw-redirect" title="Jet plane">jet pilot</A> action figure, whose torso has been attached to an old-school mini-<A href="/wiki/Skateboard" title="Skateboard">skateboard</A>. After the Frog is let out of Sid's room to distract Scud, Roller Bob ferries Woody and the other mutant toys outside the house to Sid's yard.</LI>
<LI><B>The Frog</B> – The speediest toy of all. A tin wind-up <A href="/wiki/Frog" title="Frog">frog</A> with two different wheels (left is from an erector set and right is from a <A href="/wiki/Monster_truck" title="Monster truck">monster truck</A>) instead of back legs. The Frog is missing his left front foot. As part of Woody's plot to rescue Buzz from Sid, Woody orders, "Wind the Frog!", and the Walking Car twists the wind-up key on the Frog's back to provide energy. When Ducky rings the doorbell, the Frog is let out of Sid's room, allowing Scud to chase him down the stairs and out to the front porch, where he is caught by Ducky, and Legs reels both toys up to safety.</LI>
<LI><B>Jingle Joe</B> – The result of a triple toy combination. He is a <I>Combat Carl</I> head staked on top of a Melody Push Chime toddler toy with an arm which is missing from a <A href="/wiki/Mickey_Mouse" title="Mickey Mouse">Mickey Mouse</A> figure. He appears at the part when he turns Woody's flashlight off by pressing the button. He helps in the plan to save Buzz by supplying motion for Janie and the Pterodactyl when there is no room on Roller Bob.</LI>
<LI><B>Ducky</B> – Another triple toy combination: a <A href="/wiki/Duck" title="Duck">duck</A>-headed <A href="/wiki/Pez" title="Pez">Pez</A> dispenser with a baby doll torso and plunger base. Other than Rockmobile, he is the only one of Sid's toys that can communicate orally. He and Legs go to the front porch via the vent, and Ducky, suspended from the porch ceiling by Legs, swings toward the doorbell until he finally activates it, giving Woody the signal to release the Frog. Ducky catches the Frog as Legs reels both toys up to safety.</LI>
<LI><B>Rockmobile</B> – A figure with an <A href="/wiki/Insect" title="Insect">insect</A>'s head who sits in a headless upper torso of <I>Rocky Gibraltar</I>, in which is a steering wheel from a toy car. Rockmobile also walks on the Rocky doll's hands.</LI>
<LI><B>Walking Car</B> – A yellow 1957 <A href="/wiki/Austin-Healey_3000" title="Austin-Healey 3000">Austin-Healey 3000</A> car with small baby doll arms. He can run and climb very quickly. As part of Woody's plot to save Buzz from Sid, when Woody orders to wind the Frog, the Walking Car twists the screw on the Frog's back, giving the Frog enough energy to speed from Sid's room to the porch.</LI>
<LI><B>Janie and Pterodactyl</B> – Hannah's beloved <A href="/wiki/Rag_doll" title="Rag doll">rag doll</A>, Janie, and Sid's creepy toy, a small plastic <A href="/wiki/Pterodactylus" title="Pterodactylus">Pterodactyl</A>, are the subjects of Sid's last "operation", called a "double bypass brain transplant" (he ripped off their heads and replaced Janie's head with a pterodactyl's). The mutant toys later put their heads on the correct bodies. After the Frog is released from Sid's room for Scud to chase after, Janie and the Pterodactyl ride Jingle Joe (since Roller Bob has run out of capacity) as Woody motions the toys to go down to Sid's back yard. Janie has yellow hair and a striped dress.</LI>
<LI><B>Red <A href="/wiki/Pickup_Truck" class="mw-redirect" title="Pickup Truck">Pickup Truck</A></B> – a toy <A href="/wiki/Toyota_Hilux" title="Toyota Hilux">Toyota Hilux</A>. It is a broken red pickup truck with crooked parts, missing ear windows and is covered in sand because it was abused and buried in the sandbox. It helps Woody and the other mutant toys rescue Buzz Lightyear from being blown up with a rocket by emerging from the sandbox along with Burned Rag Doll and Walking Car.</LI>
<LI><B>Burned Rag Doll</B> – a one eyed rag doll that was possibly burnt in an explosion or fire. It repeatedly utters "Mama!", which signifies that it talks. It helps Woody and the mutant toys rescue Buzz Lightyear by coming out of the sandbox along with Walking Car and Red Pickup Truck.</LI></UL>
<H3><SPAN id="Mason.27s_toys"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Mason's_toys">Mason's toys</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=45" title="Edit section: Mason's toys">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Appearing in <I>Toy Story That Time Forgot</I>, these are the toys of Bonnie's best friend Mason.
</P>
<UL><LI><B>Battlesaurs</B> – A group of mostly humanoid dinosaur toys who initially believe themselves to be real beings rather than playthings (like Buzz in the first and third films, and Buzz 2 in the second film). This illusion is encouraged by Mason's greater interest in a new videogame system that he received for Christmas, and they become hostile to Mason's other toys and to Bonnie's when they are brought over for a playdate. However, Trixie is eventually able to convince them that being played with brings its own joy, and they happily embrace their life as toys.
<UL><LI><B>Reptillus Maximus</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Kevin_McKidd" title="Kevin McKidd">Kevin McKidd</A>) – The <A href="/wiki/Carcharodontosaurus" title="Carcharodontosaurus">Carcharodontosaurus</A>-like Champion of the Battlesaurs, who is fascinated by Trixie after meeting her. Initially, Reptillus is resistant to the idea of being a plaything, feeling that to submit to the will of his child would be surrender and dishonorable. However, Trixie later helps him to see that being there for Mason is honorable, and he helps her divert Mason's attention to his new toys. Near at the end of <I>Toy Story That Time Forgot</I> it's implied that he has a crush on Trixie.</LI>
<LI><B>The Cleric</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Steve_Purcell" title="Steve Purcell">Steve Purcell</A>) – An anthropomorphic <A href="/wiki/Ludodactylus" title="Ludodactylus">Ludodactylus</A> and the "spiritual" leader of the Battlesaurs. The Cleric is the first Battlesaur shown to be aware of their status as toys, but conceals it from the others so that he can rule over them and Mason's other toys. However, his plans are thwarted when Reptillus sides with Trixie; he is later shown apparently enjoying his new role as Mason's plaything.</LI>
<LI><B>Ray-Gon</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Jonathan_Kydd_(actor)" title="Jonathan Kydd (actor)">Jonathan Kydd</A>) – A <A href="/wiki/Scelidosaurus" title="Scelidosaurus">Scelidosaurus</A> who serves as the armorer of the Battlesaurs, his main contribution is providing Trixie and Rex with battle armor, with the latter featuring remote-control arms that the Cleric uses to manipulate Rex.</LI>
<LI><B>Goliathon</B> – An <A href="/wiki/Erythrosuchus" title="Erythrosuchus">Erythrosuchus</A> that is kept as a pet by the other Battlesaurs and used to imprison their enemies in its belly.</LI>
<LI><B>Guards</B> – Various guards are part of the Battlesaur collections, with raptor-like males and <A href="/wiki/Parasaurolophus" title="Parasaurolophus">Parasaurolophus</A>-like females amongst others.</LI></UL></LI></UL>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Toy_characters_by_location">Toy characters by location</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=46" title="Edit section: Toy characters by location">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN id="Al.27s_Toy_Barn_and_apartment"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Al's_Toy_Barn_and_apartment">Al's Toy Barn and apartment</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=47" title="Edit section: Al's Toy Barn and apartment">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Shown in a Buzz Lightyear commercial in <I>Toy Story</I>, this section contains characters from <I>Toy Story 2</I>. Al's Toy Barn appears in <I>Toy Story 3: The Video Game</I>.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Stinky_Pete_the_Prospector">Stinky Pete the Prospector</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=48" title="Edit section: Stinky Pete the Prospector">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by:
</P>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Kelsey_Grammer" title="Kelsey Grammer">Kelsey Grammer</A> (<I>Toy Story 2</I>)</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Stephen_Stanton" title="Stephen Stanton">Stephen Stanton</A> (<I>Toy Story 3: The Video Game</I>)</LI></UL>
<P><B>Stinky Pete,</B> also known as <B>Prospector,</B> is a <A href="/wiki/Prospecting" title="Prospecting">prospector</A> doll and the primary antagonist of <I>Toy Story 2</I>. He is a toy modeled after a character on the fictional television show, <I><A href="/wiki/Woody%27s_Roundup" class="mw-redirect" title="Woody's Roundup">Woody's Roundup</A></I>, where the characters consists of <A href="/wiki/Sheriff_Woody" title="Sheriff Woody">Sheriff Woody</A>, <A href="/wiki/Jessie_(Toy_Story)" title="Jessie (Toy Story)">Jessie</A>, Stinky Pete, and Bullseye. The Prospector doll seen in the film had never been opened and was still <A href="/wiki/Mint_condition" title="Mint condition">"Mint in the Box"</A> making him sought after by thousands of collectors.
</P><P>In contrast to the character on the show, Stinky Pete is quite intelligent, manipulative, and well-spoken and, when he first appears, he seems to be a grandfather figure and mentor. However, he becomes embittered because he has never been sold or played with until <A href="#Al_McWhiggin">Al McWhiggin</A> eventually found him. Stinky Pete makes no secret of his hatred for space toys like Buzz Lightyear, whom he blames for causing the show to be canceled after the launch of <A href="/wiki/Sputnik" class="mw-redirect" title="Sputnik">Sputnik</A>, causing children all over America to lose their interest in cowboy toys, shifting their interest to space adventures instead.
</P><P>Years after being purchased, Stinky Pete would spend years in storage while Al bought more toys and advertisements from <I>Woody's Roundup.</I> After Al had stolen Woody, Stinky Pete and Jessie were excited because now they could go to the Konishi Toy Museum in Japan, where they will be treated with respect. Woody reveals that he has an owner named Andy Davis, which infuriates Jessie and leads the Prospector to become determined to make sure Woody doesn't go back to Andy at any cost, despite the fact that he is now aware that Al actually has stolen Woody because he still belongs to Andy.
</P><P>When Al accidentally rips off Woody's arm, Stinky Pete secretly leaves his box and he sabotages Woody's attempt to recover his arm and return to Andy by turning on the TV. He then frames Jessie for this by putting the TV remote near her before returning to his box and pretending that he "doesn't know" how the TV turned on after Woody falls for his trick. He later convinces Woody to wait until his arm is supposed to be fixed in the morning, which is done after Al calls in a cleaner. After Woody's arm is fixed, Stinky Pete convinces Woody after a story that Jessie tells him about her old owner, that Andy won't play with him anymore by the time he goes to college, but in Japan, Woody will be treasured forever. Woody agrees to stay with them instead of going back to Andy, much to Stinky Pete, Jessie and Bullseye's delight.
</P><P>However, Woody's friends arrive during a celebration of going to Japan and they demand that Woody returns to Andy, but Woody angrily refuses, resulting in the toys sadly saying goodbye and leaving without him. However, before leaving, Buzz says an upset goodbye to Woody by saying that he'll be staying behind glass forever and not being loved again if he chooses to go to Japan, leaving Woody to think over his choice. However, Woody has a change of heart and tells Buzz that he is coming with them, and invites his friends to come with him to Andy's house. However, Stinky Pete is very angry with Woody for attempting to leave with Jessie and Bullseye back to Andy's house, and once again he sabotages Woody's attempt to escape by tightening the bolt to the vent (as well as revealing to the others that he can actually get out of his box whenever he wants) and uses his pick axe to turn off the TV, causing Woody to realize that it was the Prospector who foiled his escape the previous night by turning on the TV and framing Jessie for it. He sees unpopular toys like him and the Roundup Gang doomed to either always ending up in storage or "spending a lifetime on a dime store shelf watching every other toy be sold," similar to his fate before Al found him, and does not want Woody, Jessie, and Bullseye to suffer the same fate. He also sees children as destroyers of toys whose ultimate fate will be "spending eternity rotting in some <A href="/wiki/Landfill" title="Landfill">landfill</A>". This makes him all the more determined to go to the Tokyo museum and become an exhibit for the rest of his life, unlike Woody and Jessie. When Slinky attempts to get Woody out of Al's suitcase, Stinky Pete quickly stops them and yanks Woody back in.
</P><P>When an angry Stinky Pete punches Buzz off the ramp at the airport to prevent Woody's rescue, Woody confronts and fights Stinky Pete for harming his friend. Stinky Pete manages to overpower him, ripping his right arm in the process. He then attempts to finish Woody off after he refuses to get back in the case as told, assuring him that he will be fixed again in Japan while saying that going home will eventually end up with him being in pieces. The other toys blind and stun Stinky Pete with flash cameras that the toys found after they confused and mistook another green luggage case for Woody's. Buzz, surviving the fall, captures Stinky Pete and Woody instructs Buzz and the other toys to dump Stinky Pete into a Barbie doll backpack that belongs to a little girl named Amy (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Debi_Derryberry" title="Debi Derryberry">Debi Derryberry</A>), who enjoys decorating her dolls' faces with tattoos, as punishment and revenge for his betrayal, knowing it will make him learn the true meaning of playtime. Upon learning of Amy's occupations of decorating her dolls, Stinky Pete starts to weep as he is taken to his new owner's home. Ironically, this fate is a rectification of a past injustice done to Stinky Pete. Since much of his anger came from never being sold, opened or played with; now he is finally being owned by a child after waiting 50 years.
</P><P>However, after the film's release, the film's website featured interviews with the characters. In Stinky Pete's interview, he has reformed and said that he has become accustomed to Amy decorating him, as well of being fond of Amy herself.
</P><P>Despite his appearance, Stinky Pete does not appear in the third film, because he was no longer mentioned, though he seems to accurately predict the events of <I>Toy Story 3</I> (as what he had said after his defeat started to come true in the film). He asks Woody if Andy will take him to college, and later tells the rest of the toys that children destroy toys, which occurs in the Sunnyside Daycare, and that they will be forgotten and end up in a landfill permanently, where the toys are narrowly rescued from the incinerator after an escape attempt and return to Andy's. The last part of his prediction did not come true.
</P><P>According to his box, Stinky Pete had a total of 9 sayings. In one outtake, Stinky Pete is seen talking to two Barbie dolls in the box, promising them a role in the third film. In another outtake, Stinky Pete gives Woody a choice to go back to Andy's home or stay, until he suffers a bout of flatulence, which he later implies is the reason for his nickname.
</P><P>Despite the fact that he does not appear in the third film, Stinky Pete does appear in the Toy Box Mode of <I>Toy Story 3: The Video Game.</I>
</P><P>According to the DVD commentary, the Pixar team had deliberated for a while what the proper comeuppance for the Prospector would be before it was decided for him to be placed in a Barbie bag with a face-painted Barbie.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Utility_Belt_Buzz_Lightyear">Utility Belt Buzz Lightyear</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=49" title="Edit section: Utility Belt Buzz Lightyear">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Tim_Allen" title="Tim Allen">Tim Allen</A>
</P><P>When searching for Woody at Al's Toy Barn, Buzz comes across the Buzz Lightyear aisle, causing him to stare in awe. While looking around, Buzz notices that there is a display case labeled "New Utility Belt." Buzz then climbs up the display case to find a newer Buzz Lightyear with a Utility Belt. When Buzz tries to take the belt, the newer Buzz (who thinks he is a real Space Ranger, similar to Andy's Buzz in the <A href="/wiki/Toy_Story" title="Toy Story">original film</A>) springs to life and grabs him, believing him to be an AWOL Space Ranger. Buzz finds himself wondering out loud if he was this deluded, which Utility Belt Buzz mistakes for talking back and threatens to use his laser on him. Buzz tries to prove to him that he is not an actual Space Ranger by showing him that his laser is actually a light bulb. This doesn't work however and Utility Belt Buzz jumps out of the way and tells him that he could've killed him. Buzz then decides that he's had enough and tries to leave, only for Utility Belt Buzz to jump out and attack him. After trapping Buzz in a box similar to the one he came in, he is mistaken for the original Buzz by the gang. When Rex mentions that he knows how to defeat Emperor Zurg—having recently acquired a walkthrough guide for the <I>Buzz Lightyear</I> video game that he's been stuck on, Utility Belt Buzz quickly decides to tag along thinking that the toys are trying to find Zurg. While the gang search Al's Toy Barn and through the vents of Al's apartment with Utility Belt Buzz, they become increasingly suspicious of his cocky attitude ("I'm Buzz Lightyear! I'm always sure!") and strange actions (such as thinking that he is flying up the elevator shift and is unaware that he's standing on the elevator, which is helping him fly) until they are finally reunited with Andy's Buzz, who defuses his counterpart's confusion by claiming that the situation is a 'Code 546' (Precisely what this involves is unknown, but it prompted Utility Belt Buzz to refer to Woody as "Your Majesty").
</P><P>Heading to the elevator on the way down, they encounter a savage Emperor Zurg toy and Utility Belt Buzz engages him in battle. When Utility Belt Buzz claims Zurg killed his father, Zurg responds he <I>is</I> his father, causing Utility Belt Buzz to scream in dismay (a parody of <I><A href="/wiki/The_Empire_Strikes_Back" title="The Empire Strikes Back">The Empire Strikes Back</A></I>). Rex defeats Zurg by accident, sending him falling off the elevator to his apparent doom by knocking him off-balance with his tail when he turns away as Zurg prepares to shoot Utility Belt Buzz, upsetting him. He is last seen playing catch with his "father," the Zurg toy, whose attitude towards Utility Belt Buzz has changed after the fall.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Evil_Emperor_Zurg">Evil Emperor Zurg</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=50" title="Edit section: Evil Emperor Zurg">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by:
</P>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Andrew_Stanton" title="Andrew Stanton">Andrew Stanton</A> (1999–present)</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Wayne_Knight" title="Wayne Knight">Wayne Knight</A> (<I>Buzz Lightyear of Star Command</I> and <I>Buzz Lightyear of Star Command: The Adventure Begins</I>)</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Jess_Harnell" title="Jess Harnell">Jess Harnell</A> (mini counterpart)</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/James_Patrick_Stuart" title="James Patrick Stuart">James Patrick Stuart</A> (<I>Disney Magic Kingdoms</I>)<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP></LI></UL>
<P><B>Evil Emperor Zurg</B> is a space villain action figure and Buzz Lightyear's <A href="/wiki/Archenemy" title="Archenemy">archenemy</A>. He has red evil eyes with neon gritting teeth, silver horns on his head, a purple tunic with a black cape on it and his weapon, a gun (which has a power control that, as a homage to <I><A href="/wiki/This_is_Spinal_Tap" class="mw-redirect" title="This is Spinal Tap">This is Spinal Tap</A></I>, goes to 11). In some cases, he does not have a gun but a hand like the one on his other arm. 
</P><P>In the first film, Zurg is a referenced character, and does not appear at all. However, Zurg is first seen in the opening sequence of the second film when Buzz is trying to take his main power away from him (Zurg's main power is from an <A href="/wiki/AA_battery" title="AA battery">AA battery</A> which is actually revealed to be a hologram). In the ensuing battle, Zurg vaporizes the top half of Buzz Lightyear's body with his gun, killing him. The sequence then cuts showing that the opening sequence was actually a video game played by <A href="/wiki/Rex_(Toy_Story)" class="mw-redirect" title="Rex (Toy Story)">Rex</A>. 
</P><P>As the story progresses, a Zurg toy in Al's Toy Barn bursts out from its box and follows Andy's Buzz Lightyear, who is on the way to rescue <A href="/wiki/Sheriff_Woody" title="Sheriff Woody">Woody</A> from <A href="/wiki/List_of_Toy_Story_characters#Al_McWhiggin" title="List of Toy Story characters">Al McWhiggin</A>. Zurg is deluded, similar to Andy's Buzz in the first film. In the second film, <A href="/wiki/List_of_Toy_Story_characters#Utility_Belt_Buzz" title="List of Toy Story characters">another copy of Buzz Lightyear</A>, deluded in the same way as Andy's Buzz in the first film, escapes from Al's Toy Barn and battles with Zurg on top of an elevator. In a reference to the relationship of <A href="/wiki/Luke_Skywalker" title="Luke Skywalker">Luke Skywalker</A> and <A href="/wiki/Darth_Vader" title="Darth Vader">Darth Vader</A>, the principal hero and villain respectively of the original <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars" title="Star Wars">Star Wars</A></I> trilogy, Evil Emperor Zurg claims he is in fact the father of Buzz, in an almost word-for-word parody of the scene in <I><A href="/wiki/The_Empire_Strikes_Back" title="The Empire Strikes Back">The Empire Strikes Back</A></I>. As Zurg attempts to finish off Buzz at point-blank range, <A href="/wiki/List_of_Toy_Story_characters#Rex" title="List of Toy Story characters">Rex</A> accidentally hits Zurg with his large tail and sends him falling down the elevator shaft. The second Buzz looks down the shaft in despair, thinking he has lost his father, while Rex is excited that he has finally managed to defeat Zurg in real life. Near the end of the film, Zurg is seen to have survived his fall with a bent horn and is now playing catch with the second Buzz. He supposedly bumped his head so hard that he forgot he was Buzz Lightyear's worst enemy. In the novelisation, however, Zurg is killed by the fall, and Buzz finds him and takes him back to Al's Toy Barn to bury him.
</P><P>Zurg is mentioned in the third film by Buzz in his bad guy character after Lotso resets him to Demo mode. Zurg appears briefly during a sequence in the end credits, where he is donated to Sunnyside Daycare center and greeted by the resident toys.
</P><P>Zurg also appears as in <I>Buzz Lightyear of Star Command</I> and its direct-to-video movie <I>Buzz Lightyear of Star Command: The Adventure Begins</I>. Zurg says he is Lightyear's father during a fight in order to shock Lightyear, before regaining the advantage during the fight and then denying the truth of that previous claim. Whether or not this is actually true, Buzz definitely does not know who his father is. This version of Zurg is also severely lightened up, going from the movie's Darth Vader-esque version to a far less intimidating one; in the TV series Zurg is a flamboyant villain who is just as much a comic relief character as he is a formidable opponent, similar to <A href="/wiki/Skeletor" title="Skeletor">Skeletor</A>. This Zurg is known for videotaping Buzz's speeches, maintaining a troll doll collection, and various other comedic habits. He is shown to have a bit of a British accent throughout the series. It is revealed in the first episode that there is a Nana Zurg, but she is never seen at all (although he claims that she's "plenty evil"). Zurg would appear to be a cyborg of some description, also much like <A href="/wiki/Darth_Vader" title="Darth Vader">Darth Vader</A>. However, it has also been discussed amongst fans that his "cybernetic" traits could also very well be because of advanced technology. There is yet to be a clear answer. In the TV series, he is the warlord-like ruler of an evil empire and is in command of an army of Hornet robots, as well of a minion workforce consisting of Grubs and Brainpods. The seat of which is the hellish Planet Z (standing for Xrghthung). In various media surrounding the film, his planet is said to be called Xrghthung. However, because this is unpronounceable in the TV series it is changed to simply "Z." It is unknown whether Zurg rules over any other worlds, but, if he does, they have not been revealed. Planet Z evidently possesses vast resources and forces enabling Zurg to be a serious threat to the Galactic Alliance. Despite being frequently gullible and bungling, Zurg is evidently highly intelligent, able to concoct sound military tactics and <A href="/wiki/Machiavelli" class="mw-redirect" title="Machiavelli">Machiavellian</A> evil schemes. Additionally, he occasionally references stereotypes of typical evil villains and intentionally violates them, showing how aware he is of his similarity to them. For example, when designing a vast prison on Planet Z, he declines building an execution arena, for it simply "gives the captives more time to get away." When he was designing a schematic for a new base, he expressly forbade for air vents that allow "hero-sized objects" into the control room. "And, may I remind you, no giant trash compactor! When heroes fall in, they always have enough time to figure a way out. Make it—an incinerator!"
</P><P>Despite his camp nature, he is just as fearsome and ruthless as his movie counterpart. Zurg is frequently mentioned to be the most evil villain in the galaxy and appears to possess authority over all other villains. In fact, he would appear to be a physical manifestation of pure evil. He is particularly proud of this and frequently brags of how "evil" he is. He is a parody of <A href="/wiki/Darth_Vader" title="Darth Vader">Darth Vader</A> on <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars" title="Star Wars">Star Wars</A></I>, <A href="/wiki/Darkseid" title="Darkseid">Darkseid</A> on <A href="/wiki/DC_Comics" title="DC Comics">DC Comics</A>,<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2012)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> <A href="/wiki/Ming_the_Merciless" title="Ming the Merciless">Ming the Merciless</A> on <A href="/wiki/Flash_Gordon" title="Flash Gordon">Flash Gordon</A>, <A href="/wiki/Megatron_(Transformers)" class="mw-redirect" title="Megatron (Transformers)">Megatron</A> on <A href="/wiki/Transformers" title="Transformers">Transformers</A>, <A href="/wiki/Doctor_Doom" title="Doctor Doom">Doctor Doom</A> on <A href="/wiki/Marvel_Comics" title="Marvel Comics">Marvel Comics</A> as well as <A href="/wiki/The_Six_Million_Dollar_Man" title="The Six Million Dollar Man">The Six Million Dollar Man</A>.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2012)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>
</P><P>Zurg appears as a playable character in <I>Toy Story 3: The Video Game</I> on the <A href="/wiki/PlayStation_3" title="PlayStation 3">PlayStation 3</A> in Toy Box Mode after completing several missions. He also has a <A href="/wiki/Convertible" title="Convertible">convertible</A> (the ZurgsMobile) that matches his personality. His mini counterpart is featured in the short <I>Small Fry</I>.
</P><P>Zurg appears in the 2015 live-action Disney movie, <I><A href="/wiki/Tomorrowland_(film)" title="Tomorrowland (film)">Tomorrowland</A></I>.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Tour_Guide_Barbie">Tour Guide Barbie</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=51" title="Edit section: Tour Guide Barbie">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Jodi_Benson" title="Jodi Benson">Jodi Benson</A>
</P><P><B>Tour Guide Barbie</B> is a <A href="/wiki/Barbie" title="Barbie">Barbie</A> doll initially from Al's Toy Barn in <I>Toy Story 2</I>. When Hamm, Slinky Dog, Rex and Mr. Potato Head come upon the Barbie aisle at Al's Toy Barn while searching for <A href="/wiki/Sheriff_Woody" title="Sheriff Woody">Woody</A>, Tour Guide Barbie hops into the toy car they are driving. She gives the toys a tour in the toy barn and helps them locate <A href="/wiki/Buzz_Lightyear" title="Buzz Lightyear">Buzz Lightyear</A> (they actually find a different, 'limited-edition' Buzz). After the outtakes of the film, Tour Guide Barbie waves goodbye to the audience until her face hurts from smiling. She then leaves for a break.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Sunnyside_Daycare">Sunnyside Daycare</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=52" title="Edit section: Sunnyside Daycare">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>These characters live at Sunnyside Daycare Centre. All appear in <I>Toy Story 3</I> only.
</P>
<H4><SPAN id="Lots-O.27-Huggin.27_Bear"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Lots-O'-Huggin'_Bear">Lots-O'-Huggin' Bear</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=53" title="Edit section: Lots-O'-Huggin' Bear">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Ned_Beatty" title="Ned Beatty">Ned Beatty</A>
</P><P><B>Lots-O'-Huggin' Bear</B> (<B>Lotso</B> for short)  is a plush, hot pink <A href="/wiki/Teddy_bear" title="Teddy bear">teddy bear</A> with a big plum nose, a sweet strawberry scent and a <A href="/wiki/Southern_American_English" title="Southern American English">southern accent</A>, who uses a wooden toy <A href="/wiki/Mallet" title="Mallet">mallet</A> as an <A href="/wiki/Assistive_cane" title="Assistive cane">assistive cane</A> (although he is still able to walk even without it). He is the self-proclaimed leader of the toys at the Sunnyside Daycare Center. He initially acts like a kind-hearted and wise caretaker, but is eventually revealed to be a ruthless <A href="/wiki/Prison_warden" title="Prison warden">prison warden</A>, although his <A href="/wiki/Backstory" title="Backstory">backstory</A> makes him more of a tragic villain.
</P><P>In <I>Toy Story 3</I>, he welcomes Andy's toys to Sunnyside and assigns them to the Caterpillar Room. Woody tries to escape from Sunnyside so he could go back to Andy, but is instead found and taken by a little girl named Bonnie.  Woody learns from Chuckles, one of Bonnie's toys, that Lotso was once owned and loved by a girl named Daisy, having become Daisy's favorite toy when she obtained it for <A href="/wiki/Christmas" title="Christmas">Christmas</A>. Lotso became friends with Chuckles and Big Baby. One day, Daisy and her family had a picnic in the countryside. When she fell asleep, her parents drove her home, inadvertently leaving the toys behind. Not wanting to give up, Lotso led his two friends on a long trek back to Daisy's house, only to discover that Daisy had gotten another Lots-O'-Huggin' Bear. Lotso became embittered and convinced Big Baby that they had been replaced, leaving Daisy's home with Chuckles. Lotso eventually discovered Sunnyside Daycare Center and turned it into an <A href="/wiki/Internment_camp" class="mw-redirect" title="Internment camp">internment camp</A> for toys. Big Baby took on the role of Lotso's enforcer, while Chuckles was broken, and was discovered by Bonnie and taken home.
</P><P>Meanwhile, Lotso realizes that Buzz is actually requesting a transfer of himself and the rest of Andy's toys to the Butterfly Room. Thinking of Buzz to be useful to him, Lotso only approves the transfer to him. When Buzz refuses Lotso's offer to stay in the Caterpillar Room, Lotso reverses Buzz to demo mode and manipulates him into imprisoning Andy's other toys.
</P><P>When Woody and Andy's toys attempt to flee from the daycare center. Lotso catches the group and once again offers them to stay at Sunnyside when a garbage truck arrives, but the toys refuse and Lotso instructs Stretch to push the toys into the dumpster. Woody argues with Lotso over his wrongdoings and reveals to him what he knows about Daisy and tosses Daisy's ownership tag to him; Lotso destroys it and says that toys are supposed to be discarded. His henchmen then turn on him and Big Baby throws him into the dumpster. As the toys attempt to flee, a vengeful Lotso pulls Woody into the dumpster just as the truck collects it to get the other toys to be sent to the dump.
</P><P>At the landfill, the toys end up on a conveyor belt leading to a shredder. Finding Lotso stuck under a large golf bag, Woody and Buzz rescue him and escape the shredder, only to realize that it leads to an <A href="/wiki/Incineration" title="Incineration">incinerator</A>. As they are about to reach the incinerator, Lotso sees an emergency stop button, and with Woody and Buzz's help, manages to reach it. However, instead of pushing the button, he chooses to leave them behind, as he is still evil and selfish on the inside and still believes that all toys are meant to be at the dump. When Woody and the toys are rescued by the aliens, Hamm and Slinky want to get back at Lotso for leaving them to die, but Woody talks them out of it, claiming that "he's not worth it" and that the dump is the right place for him. Lotso (who is unaware the Andy's toys are still alive) is eventually found by a garbage man who recalls that he once had a Lots-O'-Huggin' Bear as a child, and straps Lotso to the grill of a garbage truck with three other toys before driving away.
</P><P>Lotso was intended to be in the first film (originally for a sequel to <A href="/wiki/Tin_Toy" title="Tin Toy">Tin Toy</A>), but the technology to design the fur to the proper consistency had yet to exist until <I><A href="/wiki/Monsters,_Inc." title="Monsters, Inc.">Monsters, Inc.</A></I> in 2001, so he was saved for the third film. However, an early version of Lotso can be seen in the first film when Woody says "Everybody hear me? Up on the shelf, can you hear me? Great!" and can be seen in the second film during the first Al's Toy Barn Commercial.
</P><P>Test audiences who had sympathized with Lotso for his backstory had wanted him to push the button in the incinerator scene to redeem himself. However, according to the DVD commentary, director Lee Unkrich explained that Lotso not pushing the button to save the toys was intended for the audience to really care about the characters after three films of getting to know them when it looked like it was the end for them in the incinerator. The Pixar team took note of the people's concerns and made Lotso to be an outright, selfish liar.
</P><P>Lotso also makes a cameo appearance in Pixar's 2009 movie <I><A href="/wiki/Up_(2009_film)" title="Up (2009 film)">Up</A></I> in a little girl's room in the city where Mr. Fredricksen's house goes by in the bottom left corner in the shadow of the bed.
</P><P>Ned Beatty was nominated for an <A href="/wiki/MTV_Movie_Award_for_Best_Villain" title="MTV Movie Award for Best Villain">MTV Movie Award for Best Villain</A> for his performance as Lotso, and Pixar and he received widespread praise for the character's back story and Beatty's performance. <A href="/wiki/IGN" title="IGN">IGN</A> named Lotso the best villain of the summer of 2010.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Ken">Ken</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=54" title="Edit section: Ken">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Michael_Keaton" title="Michael Keaton">Michael Keaton</A>
</P><P><B><A href="/wiki/Ken_(doll)" title="Ken (doll)">Ken</A></B> is a smooth-talking doll who falls in love with Barbie. He first appears wearing light blue pleated and cuffed shorts, and a tucked-in leopard-print shirt with short sleeves. His accessories include matching ascot, sensible loafers and a fashion-forward gold belt. He lives in Ken's Dreamhouse, a big yellow doll house with three stories, a large wardrobe room, and an elevator. Barbie originally breaks up with Ken when she finds him, Lotso, his other henchmen, and a reset Buzz Lightyear locking up her friends and discovering their ulterior motive. Piqued, Ken orders her locked up as well.
</P><P>However, as part of a plan to escape, she pretends to forgive Ken, gaining access to his dream house. Barbie then ties Ken hostage to try to get him to reveal how to reset Buzz back to normal. As a provocation, she entangles him in an ironing board and rips his clothing apart. Ken reveals the truth after she begins to sabotage his prized <A href="/wiki/Nehru_jacket" title="Nehru jacket">Nehru jacket</A>. He is not seen again until Lotso has the toys cornered at the dumpster, where he is the first to turn on Lotso. Ken comes to Barbie's help by trying to stop Lotso, having realized Barbie through her understanding of civics. Lotso tells Ken "there's 100,000,000 just like her", but Ken insists that for him, there is no one else like her, and wins back her affections.
</P><P>In the end credits of the film, he and Barbie are seen greeting new toys at Sunnyside as Barbie becomes his girlfriend again, and with Lotso gone, they both take charge of the Sunnyside toys as the new leaders. He resembles a real doll from 1988 called Animal Lovin' Ken.<SUP id="cite_ref-Slashfilm_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Slashfilm-9">[9]</A></SUP> Due to being called a "girl's toy," it is often joked about his femininity: such as his large selection and obsession with clothes, him wearing Barbie's scarf, his rather feminine boxer-shorts, Bookworm not being suspicious seeing who he believed being Ken (Barbie in a spacesuit outfit) in <A href="/wiki/High_heels" class="mw-redirect" title="High heels">high heels</A>, as well as at the end Buzz believing Barbie wrote them the fancy note, only to discover Ken's signature at the end.
</P><P>Ken, along with Barbie, appears in the theatrical short, <I>Hawaiian Vacation</I>, in which the two embark on a journey to Hawaii, but ends up in Bonnie's room, where Woody and the other toys reenact various Hawaiian scenes.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Big_Baby">Big Baby</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=55" title="Edit section: Big Baby">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by Woody Smith (2010–present)
</P><P><B>Big Baby</B> is a <A href="/wiki/Bitty_Baby" title="Bitty Baby">Bitty Baby</A> doll with a <A href="/wiki/Strabismus" title="Strabismus">lazy eye</A> who carries around a bottle and is adorned with childlike scribbling that resembles ferocious <A href="/wiki/Tattoos" class="mw-redirect" title="Tattoos">tattoos</A>. He normally does not speak, instead communicating through baby sounds, with the exception of one spoken line after the toys escape Sunnyside.
Big Baby was once one of Daisy's toys before he, Lotso, and Chuckles were lost at a rest area. After returning home, Lotso lied to Big Baby, claiming that Daisy replaced and no longer loved them. They eventually took over Sunnyside Daycare, where Big Baby became Lotso's third-in-command. Eventually, Woody reveals to Lotso that Daisy still cared about them and gives Big Baby his pendant, sparking his memory of his former owner, whom he called "Mama". Lotso derides Big Baby for his attachment to Daisy and smashes the pendant with his mallet. Big Baby turns against Lotso and throws him in the dumpster (a parody of a scene from <A href="/wiki/Return_of_the_Jedi" title="Return of the Jedi">Return of the Jedi</A>), <A href="/wiki/Blowing_a_raspberry" title="Blowing a raspberry">blows him a raspberry</A>, and helps Woody and his friends escape Sunnyside.
</P><P>In the credits, Big Baby is much happier at Sunnyside under Barbie and Ken's care, and even wears gold diapers to match their outfits at a party at the daycare. 
</P><P>The baby who provided the voice for Big Baby is named "Woody," according to <A href="/wiki/Lee_Unkrich" title="Lee Unkrich">Lee Unkrich</A>'s Twitter account,<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP> and the film's credits confirm it as being Woody Smith (listed under Additional voices).
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Twitch">Twitch</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=56" title="Edit section: Twitch">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/John_Cygan" title="John Cygan">John Cygan</A>
</P><P><B>Twitch</B> is a green "insectaloid warrior" action figure with a bug's head, orange eyes with ferocious chomping mandibles, wings, and two muscular arms. He is one of the toy thugs working for Lotso. He helps to reprogram Buzz, and later apprehends Andy's other toys. He keeps a search light working in the playground. He and Sparks "break" the Chatter telephone before he is convinced of Lotso's evil by Woody and Ken. Because of how Lotso abused Big Baby, Twitch turns on Lotso, along with the other gang members. During the credits, he is seen living in a happier Sunnyside and is shown taking a turn to endure playtime with the young children in the Caterpillar Room, switching with Chunk so he can rest.
</P><P>Twitch is reminiscent of the 1980s "<A href="/wiki/He-Man" title="He-Man">He-Man</A> and the <A href="/wiki/Masters_of_the_Universe" title="Masters of the Universe">Masters of the Universe</A>" toy line, and other similar lines.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Stretch">Stretch</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=57" title="Edit section: Stretch">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg" title="Whoopi Goldberg">Whoopi Goldberg</A>
</P><P><B>Stretch</B> is a toy rubber <A href="/wiki/Octopus" title="Octopus">octopus</A> with sticky suckers on her eight long arms and a glittery, purple body. She is the sole female member of Lotso's gang, and at first welcomes the toys, but later helps capture them with her elastic tentacles. With her cohorts, she later catches Woody and his friends, and was eager to push them into the dumpster, should they not admit defeat. However, Stretch was also seen to be the first toy to doubt Lotso's leadership and motives, as she was seen to visibly cringe at Lotso's true character being revealed. After Lotso destroys Big Baby's locket, he angrily orders Stretch to push Woody and his friends into the dumpster, which Stretch is now reluctant to do, causing Lotso to reveal his true feelings about all toys. Eventually, Lotso is thrown into the dumpster by Big Baby for his lies and treachery, and Stretch immediately leaves the area, shocked at what had happened but relieved. In the credits, she welcomes new toys happily without Lotso and is later seen sneaking a message to Woody and the gang in Bonnie's backpack. She is based on a purple <A href="/wiki/Wacky_WallWalker" title="Wacky WallWalker">Wacky WallWalker</A> toy from the 1980s.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Chunk">Chunk</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=58" title="Edit section: Chunk">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Jack_Angel" title="Jack Angel">Jack Angel</A>
</P><P><B>Chunk</B> is an orange muscular rock monster toy. He has two red eyes when fierce, blue eyes when he's friendly, huge fists, and a face that you can change by rolling it up or down to a different facial expression or pressing a button at the top of his head. He welcomes the toys to Sunnyside, but later helps Lotso and Buzz imprison them. He is then convinced of Lotso's deception when he abuses Big Baby, and is seen helping Woody and his friends climb to safety. In the credits, he is seen taking the abuse of the younger children, later taking a rest while Twitch takes his place. He is based on the short lived <A href="/wiki/Rock_Lords" title="Rock Lords">Rock Lords</A> toyline.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2012)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>
</P><P>Chunk has a very low level of intelligence: During a gambling scene, he describes Buzz as "He ain't the sharpest knife in the.....place...where they...keep the knives". He enjoys teasing Ken during the gambling scene since he called him a "girl's toy."
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Sparks">Sparks</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=59" title="Edit section: Sparks">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Jan_Rabson" title="Jan Rabson">Jan Rabson</A>
</P><P>Sparks is a robot toy at Sunnyside Daycare. He has shown to be both blunt and sarcastic. Sparks' retro design has flashing red LED eyes and a blaster cavity in his chest that spits out real sparks when he's rolling around on his wheels, but is completely safe for children. He sports telescoping arms with working pincers and he can also elevate his body to make himself taller. He starts out as one of Lotso's henchmen, but in the dumpster scene, when Ken states that Lotso put all of the toys in Sunnyside Daycare into a pyramid and placed himself on the top, he and Twitch (and likely Chunk as well) start to doubt Lotso's leadership as both of them look at each other. Both of them are also in shock when Lotso shows his true colors and pokes Big Baby angrily in the stomach. They also witness Big Baby who retaliates by throwing Lotso into the dumpster, and he and the rest of his fellow henchmen let Andy's toys escape. In the end, he and the rest of Lotso's former henchmen reform for the better and become nicer.
</P><P>Sparks has only one line, when he points out Chunk's low intelligence, he says, "Neither are you, Chunk" after Chunk gives his opinion on Buzz.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Chatter_Telephone">Chatter Telephone</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=60" title="Edit section: Chatter Telephone">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Teddy_Newton" title="Teddy Newton">Teddy Newton</A>
</P><P><B><A href="/wiki/Chatter_Telephone" title="Chatter Telephone">Chatter Telephone</A></B> is a character based on the real-life toy of the same name. He can only speak when his receiver is lifted from its cradle. He lives in the Caterpillar Room. He is the oldest toy at Sunnyside, and becomes an ally to Woody. When Woody returns to Sunnyside, he immediately says that coming back was a mistake because Lotso had rigged his security after he left and that the best action would be to just lay low. He reluctantly gives him instructions on how to escape Sunnyside. For this, he is later brutally beaten and broken for helping Woody and his group escape, and eventually rats Woody out when convinced that Woody and the other toys had already escaped, but are caught just before they can do so. He sadly apologizes to Woody who fortunately shows sympathy for the broken toy. In the credits, he has been repaired and now lives a happier life there at Sunnyside Daycare without Lotso, having been invited into the Butterfly Room. When Woody talked to him, he called him Ol' Timer.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Bookworm">Bookworm</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=61" title="Edit section: Bookworm">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Richard_Kind" title="Richard Kind">Richard Kind</A>
</P><P><B>The Bookworm</B> is a green toy worm with a built-in flashlight who wears glasses. He is a genius who loves reading books. He keeps a library of instruction manuals in a closet at Sunnyside, and gives Lotso the instruction manual for Buzz Lightyear. He later gives the same manual to Barbie (who he thinks is Ken since she is disguised in his spacesuit outfit). It is unknown if he is in allegiance with Lotso but is most likely not, since he is never seen with him very often. In the credits, he is happy without Lotso, and is seen using his flashlight to light a disco ball during a party at Sunnyside. He is based on the <A href="/wiki/Glo_Worm" title="Glo Worm">Glo Worm</A> toys from the 1980s. He only has two lines in the film.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Cymbal-banging_monkey">Cymbal-banging monkey</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=62" title="Edit section: Cymbal-banging monkey">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>The <A href="/wiki/Cymbal-banging_monkey_toy" title="Cymbal-banging monkey toy">cymbal-banging monkey</A></B> is a monkey toy based on the Musical Jolly Chimp toy from the 1960s. he monitors the Sunnyside Daycare <A href="/wiki/Security_cameras" class="mw-redirect" title="Security cameras">security cameras</A> at night, and can alert Lotso and the gang of any toys attempting to escape by screeching into a microphone to broadcast over the <A href="/wiki/Intercom" title="Intercom">intercom</A>. Chatter Telephone tells Woody that he must get rid of the monkey before he and his friends can escape. Woody and Slinky manage to succeed in taking him down by wrapping him up in <A href="/wiki/Scotch_Tape" title="Scotch Tape">Scotch Tape</A> and shutting him in a <A href="/wiki/Filing_cabinet" title="Filing cabinet">filing cabinet</A>. In the credits, he is seen in a much happier situation, gently playing his <A href="/wiki/Clash_cymbals" title="Clash cymbals">clash cymbals</A> while wearing star-shaped sunglasses.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Toys_in_other_projects">Toys in other projects</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=63" title="Edit section: Toys in other projects">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The following toy characters were seen in other Toy Story projects:
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Discarded_Fun_Meal_Toys">Discarded Fun Meal Toys</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=64" title="Edit section: Discarded Fun Meal Toys">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Appearing in <I><A href="/wiki/Small_Fry_(film)" title="Small Fry (film)">Small Fry</A></I>, the <B>Discarded Fun Meal Toys</B> are toys that were discarded by children and have formed a support group in a storage room at Poultry Palace. Buzz Lightyear came across them at the time when he was replaced by the Fun Meal Toy version of Buzz. Among the Fun Meal Toys are:
</P>
<UL><LI><B><A href="/wiki/Queen_regnant" title="Queen regnant">Queen</A> Neptuna</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Jane_Lynch" title="Jane Lynch">Jane Lynch</A>) — Queen Neptuna is a <A href="/wiki/Mermaid" title="Mermaid">mermaid</A> toy who is leader of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. She was from the "Mermaid Battle Squadron" line where the Mermaid Battle Squadron's duties are to protect the oceans from pollution and exploitation.</LI>
<LI><B>T-Bone</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Angus_MacLane" title="Angus MacLane">Angus MacLane</A>) — T-Bone is a steak-like <A href="/wiki/Transformers" title="Transformers">Transformer</A> who is Queen Neptuna's second-in-command of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He was from the "Steak Force" line where they fight the Vegetenarians.</LI>
<LI><B><A href="/wiki/Disc_jockey" title="Disc jockey">DJ</A> Blu-Jay</B> (voiced by Bret Parker) — DJ Blu-Jay is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a small <A href="/wiki/Blue_jay" title="Blue jay">blue jay</A> toy wearing a set of headphones with a disco player with a tree trunk to stand it up.</LI>
<LI><B><A href="/wiki/Lizard" title="Lizard">Lizard</A> <A href="/wiki/Magician_(fantasy)" title="Magician (fantasy)">Wizard</A></B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Josh_Cooley" title="Josh Cooley">Josh Cooley</A>) — Lizard Wizard is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a small lime green lizard toy with a beard, a violet wizard hat and a wizard robe.</LI>
<LI><B>Bozu the <A href="/wiki/Ninja" title="Ninja">Ninja</A> <A href="/wiki/Clown" title="Clown">Clown</A></B> — Bozu is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a circus clown by day, 15th century ninja from <A href="/wiki/History_of_Japan#Medieval_Japan_(1185–1573/1600)" title="History of Japan">Feudal Japan</A> by night.</LI>
<LI><B>Vlad the Engineer</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Jess_Harnell" title="Jess Harnell">Jess Harnell</A> in a Transylvanian accent) — Vlad the Engineer is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. Vlad is a <A href="/wiki/Vampire" title="Vampire">vampire</A> in a <A href="/wiki/Conductor_(rail)" title="Conductor (rail)">conductor</A>'s hat that rides in a purple steam engine. Vlad got discarded because "nobody wanted to board the Vampire Express."</LI>
<LI><B>Gary <A href="/wiki/Grappling_hook" title="Grappling hook">Grappling Hook</A></B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Angus_MacLane" title="Angus MacLane">Angus MacLane</A>) — Gary Grappling Hook is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a green toy gun with hands and legs and a blue grappling hook for a face. Buzz uses him to escape the toy psychotherapy meeting when he was paired up with Lizard Wizard.</LI>
<LI><B>Tae-Kwon Doe</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Lori_Alan" title="Lori Alan">Lori Alan</A>) — Tae-Kwon Doe is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. She is an anthropomorphic karate <A href="/wiki/Deer" title="Deer">deer</A> toy that can chop through the boards that are part of her toy. At one point, Queen Neptuna sees her hand up and thinks she is raising her hand. When Neptuna calls on her, Tae-Kwon Doe explains that it's simply her play feature at which point her left hoof goes down hitting the plastic boards and "breaking" it. Her name is a play on "<A href="/wiki/Taekwondo" title="Taekwondo">Taekwondo</A>".</LI>
<LI><B>Super Pirate</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Angus_MacLane" title="Angus MacLane">Angus MacLane</A>) — Super Pirate is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a pirate-themed <A href="/wiki/Superhero" title="Superhero">superhero</A> with an eyepatch on his left eye and a peg leg in place of the lower part of the left leg.</LI>
<LI><B>Beef <A href="/wiki/Flight_attendant" title="Flight attendant">Stewardess</A></B> — Beef Stewardess is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. She is an anthropomorphic <A href="/wiki/Cattle" title="Cattle">cow</A> that is dressed as a stewardess.</LI>
<LI><B>Nervous Sys-Tim</B> (voiced by Kitt Hiraski) — Nervous Sys-Tim is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a clear plastic human that shows many body parts such as the brain, the eyes, and the nervous system. Nervous Sys-Tim mentioned that nobody wanted him because he is an accurate depiction of the human nervous system and that would seem gross when kids were eating.</LI>
<LI><B><A href="/wiki/Ghost" title="Ghost">Ghost</A> Burger</B> (voiced by Jason Topolski) — Ghost Burger is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a normal <A href="/wiki/Hamburger" title="Hamburger">hamburger</A> dressed in a ghost sheet.</LI>
<LI><B><A href="/wiki/Koala" title="Koala">Koala</A> Kopter</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Carlos_Alazraqui" title="Carlos Alazraqui">Carlos Alazraqui</A> in an Australian accent) — Koala Kopter is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a plastic koala on a helicopter that has a propeller on the top of his hat that is part of the "Down Undermals" set. Koala Kopter stated that he was switched out for a Kangaroo Kanoe.</LI>
<LI><B>Roxy Boxy</B> (voiced by Emily Forbes) — Roxy Boxy is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. She is a <A href="/wiki/Boxing" title="Boxing">boxing</A>-themed <A href="/wiki/Turtle" title="Turtle">turtle</A>. Roxy Boxy mentioned that she was recalled because her boxing glove hands will come out and could hurt kids. This has happened during the meeting where it hit Lizard Wizard twice.</LI>
<LI><B>Recycle Bin</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Peter_Sohn" title="Peter Sohn">Peter Sohn</A>) — Recycle Bin is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a blue <A href="/wiki/Recycling_bin" title="Recycling bin">recycling bin</A> with arms. Recycle Ben claimed that "he was recycled."</LI>
<LI><B>Funky <A href="/wiki/Monk" title="Monk">Monk</A></B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Angus_MacLane" title="Angus MacLane">Angus MacLane</A>) — Funky Monk is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a monk with sunglasses and a gold chain with his initials around his neck.</LI>
<LI><B><A href="/wiki/Condorman" title="Condorman">Condorman</A></B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Bob_Bergen" title="Bob Bergen">Bob Bergen</A>) — Condorman is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a <A href="/wiki/Condor" title="Condor">condor</A>-themed superhero in his vehicle. Condorman is an allusion to the live-action 1981 Disney film of the same name.</LI>
<LI><B>Franklin</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Jim_Ward_(voice_actor)" title="Jim Ward (voice actor)">Jim Ward</A>) — Franklin is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a <A href="/wiki/Bald_eagle" title="Bald eagle">bald eagle</A> sitting on a rolled-up version of the <A href="/wiki/Constitution" title="Constitution">constitution</A> that supports a feather pen on the back of it and the wheels are made up of quarters. Franklin didn't understand why kids disliked him because "he is history, but on wheels."</LI>
<LI><B>Pizza-Bot</B> (voiced by Jason Topolski) — Pizza-Bot is a member of the Discarded Fun Meal Toys. He is a blue pizza box-headed robot whose right hand holds a pizza and his left hand is a pizza cutter. It reads PIZZABOT5000 on his chest. His chest is possibly a pizza-carrying chest, such as the ones that you see when someone brings you pizza or the boxes that carry the pizzas at baseball games. Kids do not like Pizza-Bot for some reason which makes him sad.</LI></UL>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Sleep_Well_Toys">Sleep Well Toys</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=65" title="Edit section: Sleep Well Toys">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>A set of toys who were stolen from their owners during their stay at the Sleep Well roadside motel by Manager Ron's pet iguana, Mr. Jones, so that Ron could sell them online. They appear in <I>Toy Story of Terror!</I>, where they are held along with Bonnie's toys while Ron auctions them off on the Internet. They eventually escape with help from Jessie, and depart the Sleep Well on a mail truck.
</P>
<UL><LI><B>Combat Carl</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Carl_Weathers" title="Carl Weathers">Carl Weathers</A>) – A <A href="/wiki/G.I._Joe" title="G.I. Joe">G.I. Joe</A>-esque action figure.
