He is African-American in appearance, unlike the Caucasian <A href="/wiki/List_of_Toy_Story_characters#Combat_Carl" title="List of Toy Story characters">character of the same name</A> who briefly appeared in the first film. He is encountered by Jessie after all of her friends have been captured, having eluded Mr. Jones though losing a hand in the process. Carl is extremely paranoid and refers to himself in the third person, but later helps Jessie overcome her fears to save everyone. He was owned by a boy named Billy, to whom he is determined to return.</LI>
<LI><B>Combat Carl Jr.</B> (voiced by Carl Weathers in a high-pitched voice) – A miniature version of Combat Carl who has a close relationship with his larger self.</LI>
<LI><B>Pocketeer</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Ken_Marino" title="Ken Marino">Ken Marino</A>) – Part of an action figure line known as the "Fastener Four," the Pocketeer has an outfit covered in pockets in which he keeps various helpful items. His fellows Zipper Man, Snaps, and Speed Lacer were sold by Ron prior to the capture of Bonnie's toys.</LI>
<LI><B>Pez Cat</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Kate_McKinnon" title="Kate McKinnon">Kate McKinnon</A>) – a <A href="/wiki/Pez_dispenser" class="mw-redirect" title="Pez dispenser">Pez dispenser</A> whose head is that of a cat wearing glasses, and who serves as the lookout for the trapped toys in the Sleep Well motel.</LI>
<LI><B>Transitron</B> (voiced by <A href="/wiki/Peter_Sohn" title="Peter Sohn">Peter Sohn</A>) – a <A href="/wiki/Transformers" title="Transformers">Transformers</A>-esque transforming robot who splits into five vehicle components. Jessie freed Transitron from a box he was to be shipped in and then had him seal her inside so she could rescue Woody; Transitron later joined up with the other stolen toys and departed the Sleep Well.</LI></UL>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Non-toy_characters">Non-toy characters</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=66" title="Edit section: Non-toy characters">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Humans">Humans</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=67" title="Edit section: Humans">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Andy_Davis">Andy Davis</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=68" title="Edit section: Andy Davis">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by:
</P>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/John_Morris_(actor)" title="John Morris (actor)">John Morris</A> — <I>Toy Story</I>, <I>Toy Story 2</I>, <I>Toy Story 3</I></LI>
<LI>Charlie Bright — <I>Toy Story 3</I> (young)</LI></UL>
<P><B>Andrew "Andy" Davis Jr.</B><SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP> is the owner of Woody, Buzz and the other toys in each of the three films. He lived with his mother and sister Molly, but left to go to <A href="/wiki/College" title="College">college</A> when he was 17. However, his father is never seen or mentioned in the films. <I>Toy Story 2</I> implies that Woody might be a hand-me-down toy, and when introducing the 2009 set of Toy Story collectibles, John Lasseter said "We always imagined he was a hand-me-down to Andy from his father."
</P><P>In <I>Toy Story</I>, Andy receives a Buzz Lightyear action figure for his 6th birthday party. Tension erupts between Buzz and Woody, who has always prided himself on being Andy's favorite. Andy initially spends much more time with his new toy, but still has a special place in his heart for Woody. Thus, he becomes concerned when both toys go missing for a time, fearing they would be lost during his family's move to a new house.
</P><P>In <I>Toy Story 2</I>, Andy is only seen in the beginning and for a short while in the ending. During his appearances, it is clear that he still loves his toys very much. At the end of the film, Andy is pleased to have five new toys – Jessie, Bullseye, and the three Squeeze Toy Aliens – added into his collection. He marks them, as he has all his toys, with his name on the soles of their feet, or in Bullseye's case, one letter of his name on each hoof.
</P><P>In <I>Toy Story 3</I>, Andy is 17 and preparing to go off to college, intending to put most of his toys in the attic except for Woody, whom he initially plans to take with him. While he apparently has not played with his toys for some years and has given many of them away, he is still resistant to his mother's suggestion to either donate or sell his remaining toys, referring to them as "junk" (which the toys believe is what he truly thinks). When they go missing, however, he becomes upset and confused when he cannot find them. Before he goes to college, Woody secretly puts the address of Bonnie (the young daughter of a family friend) on the box with the toys in it, causing Andy to come around to the idea of donating them. He passes them on to young Bonnie, who he realizes will look after his childhood playthings and gives them each their own introduction, stating the qualities that make each of them special. When Bonnie finds Woody in the box as well, Andy shows great reluctance to pass on his favorite toy, but ultimately relents, allowing the toys to stay together in an environment where they will be loved and played with. He spends time with Bonnie and the toys one last time before departing for college, and is noticeably sad when Bonnie has Woody "wave" to him. He then responds with a quiet "Thanks, guys".
</P><P>According to <I>Toy Story</I> producer Ralph Guggenheim in a December 1995 Animation Magazine article, John Lasseter and the story team for <I>Toy Story</I> reviewed the names of Pixar employees' children, looking for the right name for Woody's owner. Davis was ultimately named after and based on <A href="/wiki/Andy_Luckey" title="Andy Luckey">Andy Luckey</A>, the son of legendary animator <A href="/wiki/Bud_Luckey" title="Bud Luckey">Bud Luckey</A>, Pixar's fifth employee and the creator of Woody. Luckey has declined to publicly comment on the connection.
</P><P>In the DVD feature for <I>Toy Story 3</I> on the voice cast, the Pixar crew remark that they weren't sure if Morris would want to do it or would sound right, and were ecstatic when they heard his voice on an answering machine, Morris was perfect for teenage Andy.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Bonnie_Anderson">Bonnie Anderson</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=69" title="Edit section: Bonnie Anderson">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Emily_Hahn_(actress)" title="Emily Hahn (actress)">Emily Hahn</A>
</P><P><B>Bonnie Anderson</B> appears in <I>Toy Story 3</I> as one of the children who goes to Sunnyside Daycare. She becomes the owner of Woody, Buzz and the other toys at the end of the film. Although she has an active imagination and boisterous manner when playing with her toys, she is shy and withdrawn when she is around adults, but she quickly warms up to Andy, when he donates his toys to her. She finds Woody, who was trying to escape Sunnyside, takes him home, and plays with him. Woody is impressed by what he sees at her house and ultimately gets himself (and all of Andy's other toys) donated to her. Andy briefly plays with her after handing over his toys, and tells her he needs someone "very special" to take care of them for him.
</P><P>In the short film <I><A href="/wiki/Hawaiian_Vacation" title="Hawaiian Vacation">Hawaiian Vacation</A></I>, Bonnie goes on a vacation to Hawaii and leaves Barbie and Ken in her room.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Molly_Davis">Molly Davis</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=70" title="Edit section: Molly Davis">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by:
</P>
<UL><LI>Hannah Unkrich—<I>Toy Story</I>, <I>Toy Story 2</I></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Bea_Miller" title="Bea Miller">Bea Miller</A>—<I>Toy Story 3</I></LI></UL>
<P><B>Molly Davis</B> is Andy's younger sister, seen as an infant in the first film, a toddler in the second film, and as a preteen in the third film. Andy uses her crib as the town jail during playtime at the beginning of the first film, implying they are sharing a room. When the family moves later in the film, Andy and Molly get separate rooms, though Molly has plans to move into Andy's presumably larger room once he leaves for college. In the first film, she slobbers on Mr. Potato Head and throws him from the crib, causing his parts to scatter and earning her the nickname "Princess Drool" from him. At the end of the film, she receives a Mrs. Potato Head toy for Christmas. In <I>Toy Story 3</I>, she also owned a Barbie doll, which she donates to the daycare center as she was less interested in dolls and toys by that time and is now a preteen.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Mrs._Davis">Mrs. Davis</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=71" title="Edit section: Mrs. Davis">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Laurie_Metcalf" title="Laurie Metcalf">Laurie Metcalf</A> (1995–present)
</P><P><B>Mrs. Davis</B> is Andy and Molly's single mother. In the first film, she has brown hair and ties it in a ponytail. In the other two films, her physical appearance is noticeably different and instead of brown, she has blonde hair and leaves it down. Though presented as a loving mother to Andy and Molly, Mrs. Davis is actually a major (though indirect) threat to the toys, as she frequently asks Andy to throw out the toys he no longer wants. Mrs. Davis’ actions regarding the toys sets the plot in motion in all three films, though they are not malicious. In the first film, she purchases a Buzz Lightyear toy for Andy on his birthday, prompting the rivalry between Buzz and Woody which leads to them being lost and forced to find their way home. In the second film, she puts Wheezy up for sale at a yard sale (due to a broken squeaker), prompting Woody's rescue attempt where he is subsequently stolen by Al. In the third film, she orders Andy to clean out his room before going to college and mistakenly throws away the bag of toys Andy was putting in the attic, causing them to be donated to a daycare center. Despite this, in the second film, she is overly protective of Woody, describing him as an old family toy. At the end of the third film, she breaks down and weeps at the departure of her first son, but Andy reassures her that she will always be with him even if they are apart. This moment between mother and son plays a major factor in Woody deciding to have Andy donate his toys to Bonnie, thus giving them a new lease on their lives.
</P><P>Some 2014 articles explore the possibility that Mrs. Davis is Jessie's original owner, Emily from her flashback memories. The evidence cited references the flashbacks of Jessie and Emily from <I>Toy Story 2</I>. The flashback sequence shows Emily as a child in the 1960s, which is when she would have been a child. The sequence also shows that the cowboy hat that Emily had is very similar to Andy's hat but with an additional white lace area, and Emily's hair was brown, just like Mrs. Davis's hair in the first film.<SUP id="cite_ref-Hernandez_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Hernandez-12">[12]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Negroni_13-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Negroni-13">[13]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Sid_Phillips">Sid Phillips</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=72" title="Edit section: Sid Phillips">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Erik_von_Detten" title="Erik von Detten">Erik von Detten</A>
</P><P><B>Sid Phillips</B> is Andy's neighbor until Andy moves, but it is unknown if he and Andy know each other. Sid is known for torturing and destroying toys. Many of his toys are either destroyed, have missing pieces, or replaced with parts from other toys, even Sid "torturing" Woody by burning his forehead with a magnifying glass. He is also shown tormenting his sister and destroying her toys by certain methods such as exploding, burning, and decapitating them. He also enjoys <A href="/wiki/Skateboard" title="Skateboard">skateboarding</A>, and his shirt depicts the logo for <A href="/wiki/Zero_Skateboards" title="Zero Skateboards">Zero Skateboards</A>. The toys mention that he was consistently kicked out of summer camp; and in the audio commentary on the tenth anniversary DVD, the directors mention that he is a bully but also the "most creative character in the movie". It is also implied that he does not have the best home life. His parents do not make any major appearances: his mother's voice is only heard briefly several times in the film, and his father is only seen briefly asleep on a chair in front of the TV in the living room.
</P><P>He also seems to be the only human depicted in the film to observe toys actually coming to life. At the end of the first film, Woody and Sid's mutant toys decide to rescue Buzz by scaring Sid, which causes him to become very frightened of toys. The last straw is Woody coming alive and telling him to take good care of his toys or else. This causes Sid to panic and run back into his house screaming, and then to his room when his sister scares him with her toy doll.
</P><P>Sid does not appear in the second film, although he is mentioned once by Buzz during the toys' mission to rescue Woody from the greedy toy collector Al McWhiggin. Sid also appears in the four-issue <I><A href="/wiki/Monsters,_Inc." title="Monsters, Inc.">Monsters, Inc.</A></I> comic mini-series produced by <A href="/wiki/Boom!_Comics" class="mw-redirect" title="Boom! Comics">Boom! Comics</A>.
</P><P>In the third film, Sid (now an adult) makes brief appearances in two scenes once again voiced by Erik von Detten. He is shown to be a garbageman with a small beard, recognizable by his characteristic T-shirt. His only dialogue in this movie involves humming guitar riffs, and he is depicted listening to <A href="/wiki/Heavy_metal_music" title="Heavy metal music">heavy metal music</A> through a pair of large headphones.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Hannah_Phillips">Hannah Phillips</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=73" title="Edit section: Hannah Phillips">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Sarah_Freeman_(actress)" title="Sarah Freeman (actress)">Sarah Freeman</A>
</P><P><B>Hannah Phillips</B> is Sid's sweet-natured, younger sister who appears a few times in the first film. In <I>Toy Story,</I> Hannah has adjusted to her toys being <A href="/wiki/Mutilate" class="mw-redirect" title="Mutilate">mutilated</A> by Sid. Most of her dolls either have different heads or altered body parts, and at the end of the film she finds enjoyment in scaring her brother after he has been horrified by Woody and the other toys. She spends most of the time during the movie playing with her altered dolls.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Al_McWhiggin">Al McWhiggin</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=74" title="Edit section: Al McWhiggin">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Wayne_Knight" title="Wayne Knight">Wayne Knight</A>
</P><P><B>Al McWhiggin</B> – nicknamed "The Chicken Man" by Andy's toys – is the owner of a chain of local toy stores and also an obsessive collector of all things related to the old <I>Woody's Roundup</I> TV series. He steals Woody from a yard sale held by Andy's mother in hopes of selling him to a toy museum in Tokyo, Japan. He is unscrupulously obsessive, overweight, very impatient, and lazy, as he complains of having to "drive all the way to work on a Saturday", despite his apartment only being across the street from the store. He is partially inspired by his voice actor <A href="/wiki/Wayne_Knight" title="Wayne Knight">Wayne Knight</A>; during the production of <I>Toy Story 2,</I> Knight had a goatee like Al in the movie. Cartoonist and animator <A href="/wiki/Scott_Shaw_(artist)" title="Scott Shaw (artist)">Scott Shaw</A> has also been acknowledged as another model and inspiration for Al.
</P><P>Al is the owner of a large toy store called "Al's Toy Barn". The store is mentioned in the first <I>Toy Story</I> in an advertisement for Buzz Lightyear toys, but Al did not appear. He is first seen in <I>Toy Story 2</I> during an advertisement on TV in which he is dressed up in a chicken suit of which Hamm remarks "I despise that chicken" after turning off the TV. He later is seen trying to buy <A href="/wiki/Sheriff_Woody" title="Sheriff Woody">Woody</A> in a yard sale held by Andy's mom. After Andy's mother refuses to hand over the doll and locks him in a box, Al steals Woody with the intent of selling him, along with the rest of his collection of <I>Woody's Roundup</I> toys and memorabilia, to a Japanese toy museum for a large sum of money. Andy's toys arrived at his apartment to rescue Woody but Stinky Pete's interference allow Al to leave for the airport with the Roundup Gang. Andy's toys follow him there on a stolen pizza planet truck. (In the original script, Andy's toys steal Al's car and Al steals the pizza planet truck and gives chase) As Al's plane is about to fly off to Japan with the Roundup Gang packed in the luggage, Andy's toys are able to save Woody, Jessie and Bullseye, getting Jessie off of the plane at the last second, while the Prospector is placed in a little girl's backpack for his betrayal. During his latest commercial soon after, Al is unable to control himself from hysterically sobbing over his losses as a result, which Hamm responded to by saying "Well, I guess crime doesn't pay."
</P><P>Al was originally conceived to appear in the first <I>Toy Story</I> film, but was cut in the final screenplay.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (October 2017)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> However, Al's Toy Barn makes an appearance in the first film during a television advertisement for Buzz Lightyear toys.
</P><P>Al's last name was revealed on the nameplate on his office desk; also, when he is done taking pictures, he answers his cellphone and Mr. Konishi can be heard saying his full name. According to <I><A href="/wiki/Disney_Adventures" title="Disney Adventures">Disney Adventures</A></I> magazine, Al was not permitted to play with his toys when he was a kid, which led to his toy-collecting niche. It is implied that Al's full name is actually Carl McWhiggin since Mr. Konishi is heard calling him that on the phone.
</P><P>His car's license plate reads LZTYBRN, which is "Al's Toy Barn" (minus the <A href="/wiki/Vowel" title="Vowel">vowel</A> letters). It is also the actual license plate of Ash Brannon, co-director of <I>Toy Story 2,</I> according to the <I>Toy Story 2: Special Edition</I> commentary.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Mrs._Anderson">Mrs. Anderson</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=75" title="Edit section: Mrs. Anderson">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Lori_Alan" title="Lori Alan">Lori Alan</A>
</P><P><B>Mrs. Anderson</B> is the mother of Bonnie. She wears purple glasses. In Toy Story 3, she is the receptionist at Sunnyside Daycare. When Andy comes to return his toys to Bonnie, Mrs. Anderson is amazed to see a grown-up college student donating his childhood toys to her daughter. During the credits scene, she carries another box of donation toys into the Butterfly Room at Sunnyside that contains Emperor Zurg.
</P><P>In <I>Toy Story of Terror</I>, she and Bonnie are driving in the countryside at nighttime when the car tire punctures. In the morning, the curtain behind the manager's desk fell down revealing all her missing toys. Mrs. Anderson calls the police to arrest the manager who stole the toys.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Geri_the_Cleaner">Geri the Cleaner</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=76" title="Edit section: Geri the Cleaner">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Jonathan_Harris" title="Jonathan Harris">Jonathan Harris</A>
</P><P><B>Geri</B>, an elderly specialist in toy restoration and repair with a fully loaded toy repair kit, comes to Al's apartment in <I>Toy Story 2</I> to fix Woody up in preparation for his trip to <A href="/wiki/Japan" title="Japan">Japan</A>. He insists that Al let him take his time with the work and views it as more than a simple job, asserting, "You can't rush art."
</P><P>Geri previously appeared in Pixar's 1997 short, <I><A href="/wiki/Geri%27s_Game" title="Geri's Game">Geri's Game</A></I>, where he plays a chess game against himself. In that short, he is voiced by <A href="/wiki/Bob_Peterson_(filmmaker)" title="Bob Peterson (filmmaker)">Bob Peterson</A>. One of the drawers in his carrying case contains chess pieces, a reference to the short.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Emily">Emily</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=77" title="Edit section: Emily">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Emily</B> was the name of Jessie's former owner and is mentioned by her in the second film. She appears in a flashback musical sequence while "When She Loved Me" by <A href="/wiki/Sarah_McLachlan" title="Sarah McLachlan">Sarah McLachlan</A> is played. During this sequence, Jessie tells Woody of her first experience with an owner who was Emily and why she resented being a child's toy. As a young child she was a fan of the Wild West and horses, along with the <I>Woody's Roundup</I> TV show, apparent through her love of Jessie. As she became a teenager, her interest began to shift towards makeup, pop culture of the time and gossip with her friends which led to Jessie being neglected then thrown away through a donation box. She is mentioned by Jessie for the second time in the third film, when she fears of being thrown away by Andy, saying "I should've seen this coming! It's Emily all over again!".
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Daisy">Daisy</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=78" title="Edit section: Daisy">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Daisy</B> is a little girl who appears in <A href="/wiki/Flashback_(narrative)" title="Flashback (narrative)">flashbacks</A> in <I>Toy Story 3</I>. She owned Lotso, Big Baby and Chuckles in the beginning, but accidentally left them behind at a rest area along the road. In order to pacify her, Daisy's parents bought her another Lots-O'-Huggin' Bear rather than finding Lotso and the rest of her toys, which made Lotso think he had been replaced and forgotten about, and changed him into a sinister, ruthless toy.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Ron">Ron</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=79" title="Edit section: Ron">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Stephen_Tobolowsky" title="Stephen Tobolowsky">Stephen Tobolowsky</A>
</P><P><B>Ron</B> is the greedy manager of the Sleep Well Motel, appearing in <I>Toy Story of Terror</I>. He has a habit of stealing toys from customers in his motel and selling them on the Internet, with the help from his pet iguana, Mr. Jones. When Bonnie and her mother went to Sleep Well after their car got a flat tire, Mr. Jones steals a number of Bonnie's toys, including Woody, Buzz, and Jessie. Ron then takes pictures of the toys and puts them on his bidding sale, awaiting buyers. Jessie manages to trick Mr. Jones into tearing off the curtain, revealing the toys' location and Ron's scheme to Bonnie and her mother, who then calls the police.
</P><P>Two police officers later arrive to question Ron, who attempts to escape by stealing their car but is forced to flee on foot after immediately crashing it into the motel sign. The police officers initiate a manhunt for him.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Mason">Mason</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=80" title="Edit section: Mason">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by R.C. Cope
</P><P><B>Mason</B> is Bonnie's best friend, and a post-Christmas playdate between the pair serves as the setting for <I>Toy Story That Time Forgot</I>. Mason receives an entire Battlesaurs collection for Christmas but is distracted from them by a new video game system. However, due to Trixie and Reptillus' efforts he abandons the video game and plays with his new toys. He is later shown to write his name on his toys in similar fashion to Andy and Bonnie.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Animals">Animals</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=81" title="Edit section: Animals">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Scud">Scud</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=82" title="Edit section: Scud">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Frank_Welker" title="Frank Welker">Frank Welker</A>
</P><P><B>Scud</B> is Sid's aggressive <A href="/wiki/Bull_Terrier" title="Bull Terrier">Bull Terrier</A>. His viciousness is first demonstrated when Sid sets a Squeeze Toy Alien on his nose and commands him to maul it mercilessly. Scud serves as an obstacle for Woody and Buzz as they try to escape Sid's house. First, as Woody tries to run off when Sid leaves the bedroom door open he encounters Scud sleeping and accidentally wakes him, forcing him and Buzz to hide. When Sid takes Buzz to the backyard to blow him up with a rocket, Woody tries to save him but Scud traps him in Sid's room. The mutant toys help Woody distract Scud so they can rescue Buzz. Scud later spots Woody and Buzz trying to escape on the moving van and pursues them, but is eluded when he runs after them into the middle of a traffic intersection and is trapped by the cars as they crash while trying to avoid him.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Buster">Buster</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=83" title="Edit section: Buster">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by Frank Welker
</P><P><B>Buster</B> is Andy's pet <A href="/wiki/Dachshund" title="Dachshund">dachshund</A>, whom he receives at the end of <I>Toy Story</I>. Buster appears in <I>Toy Story 2</I> and <I>Toy Story 3.</I> In <I>Toy Story 2,</I> he is depicted as being very energetic. Buster is considered to be nice to the toys in Andy's room and is the only one in Andy's house who knows that the toys are alive, and is fiercely loyal to Woody, obeying all commands given to him by Woody: when Wheezy is taken by Andy's mother to be sold at a yard sale, Woody is able to command Buster to carry him down to the yard sale so he can rescue Wheezy. However, he does not respond to commands from Andy whatsoever. Slinky is also able to communicate with him due to the fact they are both dogs. At the beginning of <I>Toy Story 2,</I> Buster finds Woody in a record of 13.5 seconds.
</P><P>In <I>Toy Story 3</I>, Buster is now older and looks very aged, with mixed brown and gray fur, a gray-white snout, overweight, and too old to help Woody save the other toys (in a direct parody of the rescue scene from <I>Toy Story 2</I>), although he remains nice and loyal to them. He tends to fall asleep as well.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Crazy_Critters">Crazy Critters</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=84" title="Edit section: Crazy Critters">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Crazy Critters</B> are a bunch of 2-dimensional animal puppets from the <I><A href="/wiki/Woody%27s_Roundup" class="mw-redirect" title="Woody's Roundup">Woody's Roundup</A></I> show including an <A href="/wiki/Armadillo" title="Armadillo">armadillo</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bat" title="Bat">bat</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bear" title="Bear">bear</A>, <A href="/wiki/Beaver" title="Beaver">beaver</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bird" title="Bird">bird</A>, <A href="/wiki/Deer" title="Deer">deer</A>, <A href="/wiki/Vulture" title="Vulture">vulture</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bear" title="Bear">bear</A> cub, <A href="/wiki/Porcupine" title="Porcupine">porcupine</A>, <A href="/wiki/Flying_squirrel" title="Flying squirrel">flying squirrel</A>, <A href="/wiki/Rabbit" title="Rabbit">rabbit</A>, <A href="/wiki/Skunk" title="Skunk">skunk</A>, <A href="/wiki/Snake" title="Snake">snake</A>, <A href="/wiki/Fox" title="Fox">fox</A>, <A href="/wiki/Raccoon" title="Raccoon">raccoon</A>, <A href="/wiki/Tortoise" title="Tortoise">tortoise</A> and <A href="/wiki/Bobcat" title="Bobcat">bobcat</A>. They come quickly when Jessie calls them, with the tortoise falling slightly behind the others. Woody understands them in the <I>Woody's Roundup</I> show. The Crazy Critters make cameo appearances as prizes determined by the score of players in <I>Toy Story Midway Mania!,</I> and in the <A href="/wiki/Toy_Story_2_(video_game)" class="mw-redirect" title="Toy Story 2 (video game)"><I>Toy Story 2</I> video game</A> on the <A href="/wiki/Nintendo_64" title="Nintendo 64">Nintendo 64</A>.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Mr._Jones">Mr. Jones</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_Toy_Story_characters&action=edit&section=85" title="Edit section: Mr. Jones">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>Voiced by <A href="/wiki/Dee_Bradley_Baker" title="Dee Bradley Baker">Dee Bradley Baker</A>
</P><P><B>Mr. Jones</B> is an <A href="/wiki/Iguana" title="Iguana">iguana</A> appearing in <I><A href="/wiki/Toy_Story_of_Terror!" title="Toy Story of Terror!">Toy Story of Terror!</A></I>, owned by the manager of Sleep Well Motel, Ron. He is loyal to his master and is trained to secretly steal toys from customers so that his master can sell the toys off the Internet. During the majority of the special, he is seen snatching most of Bonnie's toys away in a flash through the air shafts and ventilation systems. Eventually, he accidentally swallowed Mr. Potato Head's left arm and Combat Carl's right hand. However, he is forced to regurgitate them out after Jessie tricks him into ripping off the curtain, revealing Ron's scheme to Bonnie and her mother. It is unknown what happens to him afterwards, although it is implied that he will be sent to Animal Control.
</P>

<P>"<B>It Wasn't Me</B>" is the first single from <A href="/wiki/Jamaican-American" class="mw-redirect" title="Jamaican-American">Jamaican-American</A> <A href="/wiki/Reggae" title="Reggae">reggae</A> artist <A href="/wiki/Shaggy_(musician)" title="Shaggy (musician)">Shaggy</A>'s multi-Platinum studio album <I><A href="/wiki/Hot_Shot_(album)" class="mw-redirect" title="Hot Shot (album)">Hot Shot</A></I> (2000). The song features vocals from English-Jamaican singer <A href="/wiki/Rikrok" title="Rikrok">Rikrok</A>.</P>
<P>The <A href="/wiki/Lyrics" title="Lyrics">lyrics</A> of the song depict one man asking his friend what to do after his girlfriend caught him <A href="/wiki/Infidelity" title="Infidelity">having sex with another woman</A>. His friend's advice is to deny everything, despite clear evidence to the contrary, with the phrase "It wasn't me."</P>
<P>"It Wasn't Me" has been regarded as Shaggy's breakthrough in the pop market, and is his highest-charting song to date, topping the charts in <A href="/wiki/Australia" title="Australia">Australia</A>, <A href="/wiki/Austria" title="Austria">Austria</A>, <A href="/wiki/France" title="France">France</A>, <A href="/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland" title="Republic of Ireland">Ireland</A>, the <A href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</A>, the <A href="/wiki/Netherlands" title="Netherlands">Netherlands</A>, and the <A href="/wiki/United_Kingdom" title="United Kingdom">United Kingdom</A>. It was the best-selling single of 2001 in the United Kingdom, selling over 1.15 million copies that year<SUP id="cite_ref-UK_year-end_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-UK_year-end-2">[2]</A></SUP> and over 1.42 million as of 2017. The song was also featured on the 2001 compilation album <I><A href="/wiki/Now_That%27s_What_I_Call_Music!_6_(U.S._series)" title="Now That's What I Call Music! 6 (U.S. series)">Now That's What I Call Music! 6</A></I>.</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Background">Background</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=It_Wasn%27t_Me&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Background">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The <A href="/wiki/Lyrics" title="Lyrics">lyrics</A> of "It Wasn't Me" depict one man asking his friend what to do after his girlfriend catches him having sex with another woman. His friend's advice is to deny everything, despite clear evidence to the contrary, with the phrase "It wasn't me." Ultimately, the narrator says that the advice "makes no sense at all". The song was inspired by a bit called "No Loyal Men," performed by <A href="/wiki/Eddie_Murphy" title="Eddie Murphy">Eddie Murphy</A> in his 1987 comedy special <I><A href="/wiki/Eddie_Murphy_Raw" title="Eddie Murphy Raw">Raw</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP> In a 2016 interview, Shaggy acknowledged similarities with the <A href="/wiki/War_(band)" title="War (band)">War</A> song "Smile Happy".<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP> The connection is further supported by <A href="/wiki/Liam_Payne" title="Liam Payne">Liam Payne</A>'s 2017 debut single "<A href="/wiki/Strip_That_Down" title="Strip That Down">Strip That Down</A>", itself based on "It Wasn't Me", which credited both Shaggy (as Orville Burrell) and members of War as co-songwriters.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The clean version of the song replaces the lyric <I>"Picture this: we were both butt-naked banging on the bathroom floor"</I> with <I>"Picture this: we were both caught making love on the bathroom floor"</I> and <I>"Saw me banging on the sofa"</I> with <I>"Saw me kissing on the sofa"</I>. "It Wasn't Me" was originally never intended to be released as a single.</P>
<P>Before the original version of <I>Hot Shot</I> was released in August 2000, Hawaiian DJ Pablo Sato downloaded the album from "a <A href="/wiki/Napster" title="Napster">Napster</A>-like MP3 site he won't name" and discovered that "It Wasn't Me" was "the album's standout cut." He played the song on American radio the next day, and in an interview, claimed, "The phone lines lit up right away. Within a couple of days, it was our number-one requested song."<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> The song was then released as the album's first single in September 2000, following its radio success. The song is written in the key of C, in the <A href="/wiki/Mixolydian_mode" title="Mixolydian mode">Mixolydian mode</A>.</P>
<P>The song was spoofed by <A href="/wiki/Bob_Rivers" title="Bob Rivers">Bob Rivers</A>, as <I>Shaggy One Handed</I>, making a reference to the <I><A href="/wiki/Scooby-Doo" title="Scooby-Doo">Scooby-Doo</A></I> character, <A href="/wiki/Shaggy_Rogers" title="Shaggy Rogers">Shaggy Rogers</A>. The video focused on him being caught <A href="/wiki/Masturbating" class="mw-redirect" title="Masturbating">masturbating</A> (about the girl next door) by his mother.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> The song was also spoofed on <I><A href="/wiki/Svengoolie" title="Svengoolie">Svengoolie</A></I>. On <I><A href="/wiki/The_Chris_Moyles_Show" title="The Chris Moyles Show">The Chris Moyles Show</A></I>, the song was used as a prank call with Shaggy trying to book a taxi, with the final line being "Can you drop me off at <I>The Chris Moyles Show</I> on <A href="/wiki/BBC_Radio_1" title="BBC Radio 1">BBC Radio 1</A>?, 97 to 99 FM".<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Chart_performance">Chart performance</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=It_Wasn%27t_Me&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Chart performance">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>"It Wasn't Me" was Shaggy's first number-one hit in the United States. The song peaked at number two for two weeks from December 16, 2000<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP> to December 23, 2000.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP> On December 30, 2000, it was bumped down one position to number three.<SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP> It moved back up to the number two spot on January 4, 2001.<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The song also reached number one on the <A href="/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart" title="UK Singles Chart">UK Singles Chart</A> on March 4, 2001, selling 345,000 copies, making the song a transatlantic chart-topper.<SUP id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14">[14]</A></SUP> It also reached number one in <A href="/wiki/Australia" title="Australia">Australia</A> on April 1, 2001. It is also the <A href="/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles_of_the_2000s_(century)_in_the_United_Kingdom" title="List of best-selling singles of the 2000s (century) in the United Kingdom">11th biggest selling single of the 21st century in the United Kingdom</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-UK_sales_15-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-UK_sales-15">[15]</A></SUP> with sales of over 1.42 million as of September 2017.<SUP id="cite_ref-UK_sales_15-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-UK_sales-15">[15]</A></SUP></P>
<P>As of August 2014, it is the 49th best-selling single of the 21st century in France, with 399,500 units sold.<SUP id="cite_ref-CIF_16-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-CIF-16">[16]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Music_video">Music video</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=It_Wasn%27t_Me&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Music video">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The music video was directed by Stephen Scott.</P>
<P>It starts out with Rikrok running to Shaggy's mansion to explain to him what has just happened. Rikrok tells him that he cheated on his girlfriend and got caught. Shaggy tells him to tell her that "It wasn't me." The video then cuts into a flashback to earlier that day. Rikrok has been caught sleeping with another woman, and his girlfriend is outside the apartment in her convertible when two women pull up next to her on their motorcycles (sport bikes).</P>
<P>Then, the three women go into the building. He then sneaks out the window, takes the motorcycle of one of his girlfriends accomplices and leaves. The women come out and the girlfriend and one of the accomplices get in the convertible and the other gets on her motorcycle and they chase after him. From his mansion, Shaggy, using his futuristic technology, tracks down where Rikrok is going and prepares an escape for him. Rikrok then gets on a bridge over the highway when the accomplice rode on the bridge in front of him.</P>
<P>He then hits the brakes to stop while she stops her motorcycle. Rikrok then hears a noise behind him and it's the other accomplices and the girlfriend driving the convertible on the other side of the bridge with the highway down below. An eighteen-wheeler drives by, and Shaggy leaves Rikrok a text message telling him to look behind and he notices the truck and jumps off the side of overhead and lands on the truck. He is then dropped off at Shaggy's mansion, showing the same scene from the start of the video.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Legacy">Legacy</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=It_Wasn%27t_Me&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Legacy">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The lyrics of "It Wasn't Me" inspired <I><A href="/wiki/Slate_(magazine)" title="Slate (magazine)">Slate</A></I> writer <A href="/wiki/Josh_Levin" title="Josh Levin">Josh Levin</A> to coin the term the "<A href="/wiki/Shaggy_defense" title="Shaggy defense">Shaggy defense</A>" to describe <A href="/wiki/R._Kelly" title="R. Kelly">R. Kelly</A>'s defence at his child pornography trial stemming from the production of a sex tape: "I predict that in the decades to come, law schools will teach this as the 'Shaggy defense'. You allege that I was caught on camera, butt naked, banging on the log cabin floor? It wasn't me."<SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Levin repeated the term on <A href="/wiki/NPR" title="NPR">NPR</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP> The term describes a strategy of flatly denying guilt and refusing to engage with the evidence against the defendant, no matter how overwhelming. R. Kelly was ultimately found not guilty on all charges.<SUP id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-19">[19]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The song is referenced by <A href="/wiki/Trevor_Noah" title="Trevor Noah">Trevor Noah</A> on an episode of <I><A href="/wiki/The_Daily_Show_with_Trevor_Noah" class="mw-redirect" title="The Daily Show with Trevor Noah">The Daily Show with Trevor Noah</A></I> when he covered the vice-presidential debate between <A href="/wiki/Mike_Pence" title="Mike Pence">Mike Pence</A> and <A href="/wiki/Tim_Kaine" title="Tim Kaine">Tim Kaine</A>, as Pence vehemently kept denying his running mate <A href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</A>'s claims, despite the fact that the claims have been proved to be said by Trump on camera or through his Twitter account.<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP></P>

<P>The <B>cat o' nine tails</B>, commonly shortened to <B>the cat</B>, is a type of multi-tailed <A href="/wiki/Whip" title="Whip">whip</A> that originated as an implement for severe <A href="/wiki/Physical_punishment" class="mw-redirect" title="Physical punishment">physical punishment</A>, notably in the <A href="/wiki/Royal_Navy" title="Royal Navy">Royal Navy</A> and Army of the United Kingdom, and also as a <A href="/wiki/Judicial_corporal_punishment" title="Judicial corporal punishment">judicial punishment</A> in Britain and some other countries.</P>
<P></P>

<P></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Etymology">Etymology</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Etymology">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The term first appears in 1695,<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP> although the design is much older. It was probably so called in reference to its "<A href="/wiki/Claw" title="Claw">claws</A>", which inflict parallel wounds. There are equivalent terms in many languages, usually strictly translating, and also some analogous terms referring to a similar instrument's number of tails (cord or leather), such as the Dutch <I>zevenstaart</I> (seven tail[s]), <I>negenstaart</I> (nine tail[s]), the Spanish <I>gato de nueve colas</I> or the Italian <I>gatto a nove code</I>.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Description">Description</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Description">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The cat is made up of nine <A href="/wiki/Knot" title="Knot">knotted</A> <A href="/wiki/Leather" title="Leather">thongs</A> of <A href="/wiki/Cotton" title="Cotton">cotton</A> <A href="/wiki/Rope" title="Rope">cord</A>, about ​<SPAN class="frac nowrap">2<SPAN class="visualhide"> </SPAN><SUP>1</SUP>⁄<SUB>2</SUB></SPAN> feet or 76 cm long, designed to lacerate the skin and cause intense pain.</P>
<P>It traditionally has nine thongs as a result of the manner in which rope is <A href="/wiki/Braid" title="Braid">plaited</A>. Thinner rope is made from three strands of <A href="/wiki/Yarn" title="Yarn">yarn</A> plaited together, and thicker rope from three strands of thinner rope plaited together. To make a cat o' nine tails, a rope is unravelled into three small ropes, each of which is unravelled again.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Variations">Variations</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Variations">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Variations exist, either named cat (of x tails) or not, such as the whip used on adult <A href="/wiki/Egypt" title="Egypt">Egyptian</A> prisoners which had a cord on a cudgel branching into seven tails, each with six knots, used only on adult men, with boys being subject to <A href="/wiki/Caning" title="Caning">caning</A>, until Egypt banned the use of the device in 2001.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Sometimes the term "cat" is used incorrectly to describe various other punitive <A href="/wiki/Flogging" class="mw-redirect" title="Flogging">flogging</A> devices with multiple tails in any number, even one made from 80 twigs (so rather a limp <A href="/wiki/Birching" title="Birching">birch</A>) to flog a drunk or other offender instead of 80 lashes normally applicable under <A href="/wiki/Shariah" class="mw-redirect" title="Shariah">shariah</A> law. The closed cat, one without tails, was called a starter.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Historical_punishments">Historical punishments</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Historical punishments">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Naval_types_and_use">Naval types and use</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Naval types and use">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The naval cat, also known as the "captain's daughter" (which in principle was used under his authority) weighed about 13 ounces (370 grams) and was composed of a handle connected to nine thinner pieces of line, with each line knotted several times along its length.<SUP id="cite_ref-Lavery218_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Lavery218-3">[3]</A></SUP> Formal floggings — those ordered by captain or <A href="/wiki/Court_martial" class="mw-redirect" title="Court martial">court martial</A> — were administered ceremonially on deck, the crew being summoned to "witness punishment" and the prisoner being brought forward by marines with fixed bayonets.<SUP id="cite_ref-Lavery218_3-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Lavery218-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>
<P>During the period of the <A href="/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars" title="Napoleonic Wars">Napoleonic Wars</A>, the naval cat's handle was made of rope about 2 feet (0.61 m) long and about 1 inch (25 mm) in diameter, and was traditionally covered with red <A href="/wiki/Baize" title="Baize">baize</A> cloth. The tails were made of cord about a quarter inch (6 mm) in diameter and typically 2 feet long.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2011)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> Drunkenness or striking an officer might incur a dozen lashes, which could be administered on the authority of the ship's captain. Greater punishments were generally administered following a formal <A href="/wiki/Court_martial" class="mw-redirect" title="Court martial">court martial</A>, with Royal Navy records reflecting some standard penalties of two hundred lashes for desertion, three hundred for mutiny, and up to five hundred for theft. The offence of <A href="/wiki/Sodomy" title="Sodomy">sodomy</A> generally drew the death penalty, though one eighteenth century court martial awarded a punishment of one thousand lashes - a roughly equivalent sentence as there was no likelihood of survival.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP></P>
<P>A new cat was made for each flogging by a <A href="/wiki/Bosun" class="mw-redirect" title="Bosun">bosun</A>'s mate and kept in a red baize bag until use. If several dozen lashes were awarded, each could be administered by a fresh bosun's mate—a left-handed one could be included to assure extra painful crisscrossing of the wounds. One dozen was usually awarded as a highly sensitizing prelude to <A href="/wiki/Running_the_gauntlet" title="Running the gauntlet">running the gauntlet</A>.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (June 2015)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP></P>
<P>For summary punishment of Royal Navy <I>boys</I>, a lighter model was made, the reduced cat, also known as boy's cat, boy's pussy or just pussy, that had only five tails of smooth whip cord. If formally convicted by a court martial, however, even boys would suffer the punishment of the adult cat. While adult sailors received their lashes on the back, they were administered to boys on the bare posterior, usually while "kissing the gunner's daughter" (bending over a gun barrel), just as boys' lighter "daily" chastisement was usually over their (often naked) rear-end (mainly with a cane – this could be applied to the hand, but captains generally refused such impractical disablement – or a rope's end). Bare-bottom discipline was a tradition of the English upper and middle classes, who frequented public schools,<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP> so <A href="/wiki/Midshipmen" class="mw-redirect" title="Midshipmen">midshipmen</A> (trainee officers, usually from 'good families', getting a cheaper equivalent education by enlisting) were not spared, at best sometimes allowed to receive their lashes inside a cabin. Still, it is reported that the 'infantile' embarrassment of bare-bottom punishment was believed essential for optimal deterrence; cocky miscreants might brave the pain of the adult cat in the macho spirit of "taking it like a man" or even as a "badge of honour".</P>
<P>On board <A href="/wiki/Training_ship" title="Training ship">training ships</A>, where most of the crew were boys, the cat was never introduced, but their bare bottoms risked, as in other naval establishments on land, "the sting of the <A href="/wiki/Birching" title="Birching">birch</A>", another favourite in public schools.</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Flogging_round_the_fleet">Flogging round the fleet</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Flogging round the fleet">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>"The severest form of flogging was a flogging round the fleet. The number of lashes was divided by the number of ships in port and the offender was rowed between ships for each ship's company to witness the punishment."<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> Penalties of hundreds of lashes were imposed for the gravest offences, including <A href="/wiki/Sedition" title="Sedition">sedition</A> and <A href="/wiki/Mutiny" title="Mutiny">mutiny</A>. The prisoner was rowed around the fleet in an open boat and received a number of his lashes at each ship in turn, for as long as the surgeon allowed. Sentences often took months or years to complete, depending on how much a man was expected to bear at a time. Normally 250–500 lashes would kill a man, as infections would spread."<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> After the flogging was completed, the sailor's lacerated back was frequently rinsed with <A href="/wiki/Brine" title="Brine">brine</A> or <A href="/wiki/Seawater" title="Seawater">seawater</A>, which was thought to serve as a crude <A href="/wiki/Antiseptic" title="Antiseptic">antiseptic</A> (now known <A href="/wiki/Seawater#Microbial_components" title="Seawater">not to be the case</A>). Although the purpose was to control infection, it caused the sailor to endure additional pain, and gave rise to the expression, "rubbing salt into his wounds," which came to mean vindictively or gratuitously increasing a punishment or injury already imposed.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="British_Army">British Army</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: British Army">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The <A href="/wiki/British_Army" title="British Army">British Army</A> had a similar multiple whip, though much lighter in construction, made of a drumstick with attached strings. The flogger was usually a <A href="/wiki/Drummer" title="Drummer">drummer</A> rather than a strong bosun's mate. Flogging with the cat o' nine tails fell into disuse around 1870.</P>
<P>Whereas the British naval cat rarely cut (contrary to graphic films) but rather abraded the skin, the falls (tresses) of the British Army cat were lighter (around 1/8th of an inch) and the string was in fact codline - a very dense material akin to tarred string. Although the total whip would weigh only a fraction of a naval rope cat, the thin, dense codline tresses were far more likely to cut the skin.</P>
<P>It was also used elsewhere in the empire, notably at the penal colonies in <A href="/wiki/Australia" title="Australia">Australia</A>, and also in <A href="/wiki/Canada" title="Canada">Canada</A> (a dominion in 1867) where it was used until 1881. An 1812 drawing<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> shows a drummer apparently lashing the buttocks of a naked soldier who is tied with spread legs on an A-frame made from sergeants' half pikes. In many places, soldiers were generally flogged stripped to the waist.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Prison_usage">Prison usage</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Prison usage">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The cat-o'-nine-tails was also used on adult <A href="/wiki/Convict" title="Convict">convicts</A> in prisons; a 1951 memorandum<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> (possibly confirming earlier practice) ordered all UK male prisons to use only cat o' nine tails (and birches) from a national stock at <A href="/wiki/Wandsworth" title="Wandsworth">Wandsworth</A> prison, where they were to be 'thoroughly' tested before being supplied in triplicate to a prison whenever a flogging was pending for use as prison discipline. In the 20th century, this use was confined to very serious cases involving violence against a prison officer, and each flogging had to be confirmed by central government.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Penal_colonies_in_Australia">Penal colonies in Australia</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section: Penal colonies in Australia">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Especially harsh floggings were given with it in secondary <A href="/wiki/Penal_colony" title="Penal colony">penal colonies</A> of early colonial Australia, particularly at such places as <A href="/wiki/Norfolk_Island" title="Norfolk Island">Norfolk Island</A> (apparently this had 9 leather thongs, each with a lead weight, meant as the ultimate deterrent for hardened life-convicts), <A href="/wiki/Port_Arthur,_Tasmania" title="Port Arthur, Tasmania">Port Arthur</A> and <A href="/wiki/Moreton_Bay" title="Moreton Bay">Moreton Bay</A> (now <A href="/wiki/Brisbane" title="Brisbane">Brisbane</A>).<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2011)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP></P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Slavery">Slavery</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section: Slavery">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>It was used on slave trade ships to punish the slaves.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2017)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Modern_uses_and_types">Modern uses and types</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Cat_o%27_nine_tails&action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section: Modern uses and types">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Judicial_corporal_punishment" title="Judicial corporal punishment">Judicial corporal punishment</A></DIV>
<P>Judicial corporal punishment was removed from the statute book in Great Britain in 1948. The cat was still being used in Australia in 1957 and is still in use in a few Commonwealth countries, although the cane is used in more countries.</P>
<P>Judicial corporal punishment has been abolished or declared unconstitutional since 1997 in <A href="/wiki/Jamaica" title="Jamaica">Jamaica</A>, <A href="/wiki/St._Vincent_and_the_Grenadines" class="mw-redirect" title="St. Vincent and the Grenadines">St. Vincent and the Grenadines</A>, <A href="/wiki/South_Africa" title="South Africa">South Africa</A>, <A href="/wiki/Zambia" title="Zambia">Zambia</A>, <A href="/wiki/Uganda" title="Uganda">Uganda</A> (in 2001) and <A href="/wiki/Fiji" title="Fiji">Fiji</A> (in 2002).</P>
<P>However, some former colonies in the <A href="/wiki/Caribbean" title="Caribbean">Caribbean</A> have reinstated flogging with the cat. <A href="/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda" title="Antigua and Barbuda">Antigua and Barbuda</A> reinstated it in 1990, followed by the <A href="/wiki/Bahamas" class="mw-redirect" title="Bahamas">Bahamas</A> in 1991 (where, however, it was subsequently banned by law)<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP> and <A href="/wiki/Barbados" title="Barbados">Barbados</A> in 1993 (only to be formally declared inhumane and thus unconstitutional by the Barbados Supreme Court).</P>
<P><A href="/wiki/Trinidad_%26_Tobago" class="mw-redirect" title="Trinidad & Tobago">Trinidad & Tobago</A> never banned the "Cat". Under the Corporal Punishment (Offenders over Sixteen) Act 1953, use of the "Cat" was limited to male offenders over the age of 16. The age limit was raised in 2000 to 18.</P>
<P>The Government of Trinidad & Tobago has been accused of torture and "cruel, inhuman and degrading" treatment of prisoners, and in 2005 was ordered by the <A href="/wiki/Inter-American_Court_of_Human_Rights" title="Inter-American Court of Human Rights">Inter-American Court of Human Rights</A> to pay US $50,000 for "moral damages" to a prisoner who had received 15 strokes of the "Cat" plus expenses for his medical and psychological care; it is unclear whether the Court's decisions were implemented. Trinidad & Tobago did not acknowledge the Court's jurisdiction, since it had denounced the American Convention on Human Rights several years before the Court started hearing this case.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP></P>

<P><B>St. Francis Preparatory School</B>, commonly known as <B>St. Francis Prep</B>, is a private, independent <A href="/wiki/Roman_Catholicism" class="mw-redirect" title="Roman Catholicism">Catholic</A> <A href="/wiki/College_preparatory_school" class="mw-redirect" title="College preparatory school">college preparatory school</A> in the <A href="/wiki/Fresh_Meadows,_Queens" title="Fresh Meadows, Queens">Fresh Meadows</A> neighborhood of the <A href="/wiki/New_York_City" title="New York City">New York City</A> <A href="/wiki/Borough" title="Borough">Borough</A> of <A href="/wiki/Queens" title="Queens">Queens</A>, in the State of <A href="/wiki/New_York_(state)" title="New York (state)">New York</A>. It is the largest non-diocesan Catholic high school in the United States.<SUP id="cite_ref-150_Years_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-150_Years-3">[3]</A></SUP> St. Francis is run by the <A href="/wiki/Franciscan_Brothers_of_Brooklyn" title="Franciscan Brothers of Brooklyn">Franciscan Brothers of Brooklyn</A>, who maintain a residence on the top floor of the school. The school has a student body of about 2,750 students and graduates between 600 and 700 students annually.</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="History">History</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=St._Francis_Preparatory_School&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: History">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>St. Francis Preparatory originated as St. Francis Academy, a small all-boys high school on 300 Baltic Street in <A href="/wiki/Brooklyn,_New_York" class="mw-redirect" title="Brooklyn, New York">Brooklyn, New York</A>, founded by the Franciscans Brothers of Brooklyn (O.S.F.).<SUP id="cite_ref-150_Years_3-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-150_Years-3">[3]</A></SUP> The college section became <A href="/wiki/St._Francis_College" title="St. Francis College">St. Francis College</A>, a private predominantly undergraduate college in <A href="/wiki/Brooklyn_Heights" title="Brooklyn Heights">Brooklyn Heights</A>. It took its current name in 1935, then moved to a larger facility in <A href="/wiki/Williamsburg,_Brooklyn" title="Williamsburg, Brooklyn">Williamsburg, Brooklyn</A> in 1952.<SUP id="cite_ref-location_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-location-4">[4]</A></SUP> The school moved to its current location in <A href="/wiki/Fresh_Meadows,_Queens" title="Fresh Meadows, Queens">Fresh Meadows, Queens</A> in 1974 when it acquired the facility that formerly housed Bishop Reilly High School, a co-educational Catholic high school. The school began admitting female students that same year.<SUP id="cite_ref-location_4-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-location-4">[4]</A></SUP> A fitness center was added recently and the science labs are being updated.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2016)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> There are currently plans to add a three-story addition to the rear of the existing building.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2016)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> The upgrades to the art rooms will support students in the studio, digital and the performing arts.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Co-curricular_activities_and_athletics">Co-curricular activities and athletics</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=St._Francis_Preparatory_School&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Co-curricular activities and athletics">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>St. Francis Prep has a rivalry with <A href="/wiki/Holy_Cross_High_School_(Queens)" title="Holy Cross High School (Queens)">Holy Cross High School</A>, fueled particularly by their <A href="/wiki/American_football" title="American football">football</A> teams. Known as the "Battle of the Boulevard" due to the two schools being located only 2 miles apart on <A href="/wiki/Francis_Lewis_Boulevard" title="Francis Lewis Boulevard">Francis Lewis Boulevard</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-Daily_News_Battle_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Daily_News_Battle-6">[6]</A></SUP> the rivalry between the Prep Terriers and the Holy Cross Knights has been called "arguably the greatest rivalry in New York City football."<SUP id="cite_ref-FiveBoroSports_7-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FiveBoroSports-7">[7]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The St. Francis Prep girls tennis team has been undefeated for 17 consecutive years, making them 17 time CHSAA champions.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2016)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> In 2015 the St. Francis Prep Varsity Handball team won their 13th consecutive CHSAA championship (with an undefeated season).<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2016)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP></P>

<P>The <B>history of the <A href="/wiki/China" title="China">People's Republic of China</A></B> details the history of <A href="/wiki/Mainland_China" title="Mainland China">mainland China</A> since October 1, 1949, when, after a near complete victory by the <A href="/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party" class="mw-redirect" title="Chinese Communist Party">Chinese Communist Party</A> (CCP) in the <A href="/wiki/Chinese_Civil_War" title="Chinese Civil War">Chinese Civil War</A>, <A href="/wiki/Mao_Zedong" title="Mao Zedong">Mao Zedong</A> proclaimed the People's Republic of China (PRC) from atop <A href="/wiki/Tiananmen" title="Tiananmen">Tiananmen</A>. The PRC has for several decades been synonymous with <A href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</A>, but it is only the most recent political entity to govern mainland China, preceded by the <A href="/wiki/Republic_of_China_(1912%E2%80%931949)" title="Republic of China (1912–1949)">Republic of China</A> (ROC) and thousands of years of <A href="/wiki/Dynasties_in_Chinese_history" title="Dynasties in Chinese history">imperial dynasties</A>.</P>
