<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Biography">Biography</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Biography">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Early_life">Early life</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Early life">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Percy Fawcett was born on 18 August 1867 in <A href="/wiki/Torquay" title="Torquay">Torquay</A>, <A href="/wiki/Devon" title="Devon">Devon</A>, England, to <A href="/wiki/Edward_Fawcett" title="Edward Fawcett">Edward Boyd Fawcett</A> and Myra Elizabeth (née MacDougall).<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> He received his education at <A href="/wiki/Newton_Abbot" title="Newton Abbot">Newton Abbot</A> Proprietary College along with <A href="/wiki/Bertram_Fletcher_Robinson" title="Bertram Fletcher Robinson">Bertram Fletcher Robinson</A>. Percy Fawcett's <A href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</A>-born father was a Fellow of the <A href="/wiki/Royal_Geographical_Society" title="Royal Geographical Society">Royal Geographical Society</A> (RGS). His elder brother <A href="/w/index.php?title=Edward_Douglas_Fawcett&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Edward Douglas Fawcett (page does not exist)">Edward Douglas Fawcett</A> (1866–1960) was a mountain climber, Eastern occultist and author of philosophical books and popular <A href="/wiki/Adventure_fiction" title="Adventure fiction">adventure novels</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Fawcett attended the <A href="/wiki/Royal_Military_Academy,_Woolwich" title="Royal Military Academy, Woolwich">Royal Military Academy, Woolwich</A> as a cadet, being commissioned as a lieutenant of the <A href="/wiki/Royal_Artillery" title="Royal Artillery">Royal Artillery</A> on 24 July 1886.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP> On 13 January 1896 he was appointed <A href="/wiki/Adjutant" title="Adjutant">adjutant</A><SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP> of the <A href="/wiki/1st_Cornwall_(Duke_of_Cornwall%27s)_Artillery_Volunteers" title="1st Cornwall (Duke of Cornwall's) Artillery Volunteers">1st Cornwall (Duke of Cornwall's) Artillery Volunteers</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> and was promoted to captain on 15 June 1897.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> He later served in <A href="/wiki/Trincomalee" title="Trincomalee">Trincomalee</A>, <A href="/wiki/Sri_Lanka" title="Sri Lanka">Ceylon</A>, where he also met his future wife Nina Agnes Paterson, whom he married in January 1901 after having previously ended their engagement. They had two sons, Jack (born 1903) and Brian (1906–1984), and one daughter, Joan (1910–2005). He joined the RGS himself in 1901 in order to study surveying and mapmaking. Later, he worked for the <A href="/wiki/Secret_Intelligence_Service" title="Secret Intelligence Service">British Secret Service</A> in <A href="/wiki/North_Africa" title="North Africa">North Africa</A> while pursuing the surveyor's craft. He served for the war office on <A href="/wiki/Spike_Island,_County_Cork" title="Spike Island, County Cork">Spike Island, County Cork</A> from 1903 to 1906, where he was promoted to major on 11 January 1905.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> He became friends with authors <A href="/wiki/H._Rider_Haggard" title="H. Rider Haggard">H. Rider Haggard</A> and <A href="/wiki/Arthur_Conan_Doyle" title="Arthur Conan Doyle">Arthur Conan Doyle</A>; the latter used Fawcett's <A href="/wiki/Amazon_basin" title="Amazon basin">Amazonian</A> field reports as an inspiration for his novel <I><A href="/wiki/The_Lost_World_(Conan_Doyle_novel)" title="The Lost World (Conan Doyle novel)">The Lost World</A></I>.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Early_expeditions">Early expeditions</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Early expeditions">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Fawcett's first expedition to South America was in 1906 (being seconded for service there on 2 May<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP>) when at the age of 39 he travelled to Brazil to map a jungle area at the border of Brazil and Bolivia at the behest of the Royal Geographical Society. The Society had been commissioned to map the area as a third party unbiased by local <A href="/wiki/Nationalism" title="Nationalism">national interests</A>. He arrived in <A href="/wiki/La_Paz" title="La Paz">La Paz</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bolivia" title="Bolivia">Bolivia</A> in June. Whilst on the expedition in 1907, Fawcett claimed to have seen and shot a 62 foot long <A href="/wiki/Giant_anaconda" title="Giant anaconda">giant anaconda</A>, a claim for which he was ridiculed by scientists. He reported other mysterious animals unknown to zoology, such as a small <A href="/wiki/Mitla_(cryptid)" title="Mitla (cryptid)">cat-like dog</A> about the size of a <A href="/wiki/Foxhound" title="Foxhound">foxhound</A>, which he claimed to have seen twice, or the giant Apazauca spider which was said to have poisoned a number of locals.<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Fawcett made seven expeditions between 1906 and 1924. He was mostly amicable with the locals through gifts, patience and courteous behaviour. In 1908, he traced the source of the <A href="/wiki/Verde_River_(Guapor%C3%A9_River)" class="mw-redirect" title="Verde River (Guaporé River)">Rio Verde</A> (Brazil) and in 1910 made a journey to <A href="/wiki/Heath_River" title="Heath River">Heath River</A> (on the border between <A href="/wiki/Peru" title="Peru">Peru</A> and Bolivia) to find its source, having retired from the British army on 19 January.<SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP> After a 1913 expedition, he supposedly claimed to have seen dogs with double noses. These may have been <A href="/wiki/Double-nosed_Andean_tiger_hound" title="Double-nosed Andean tiger hound">Double-nosed Andean tiger hounds</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Based on documentary research, Fawcett had by 1914 formulated ideas about a "lost city" he named "Z" somewhere in the <A href="/wiki/Mato_Grosso" title="Mato Grosso">Mato Grosso</A> region of Brazil. He theorized that a complex civilization once existed in the Amazon region and that isolated ruins may have survived.<SUP id="cite_ref-Yorker_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Yorker-14">[14]</A></SUP> Fawcett also found a document known as <A href="/wiki/Manuscript_512" class="mw-redirect" title="Manuscript 512">Manuscript 512</A><SPAN class="noprint" style="font-size:85%; font-style: normal;"> (<A href="https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuscrito_512" class="extiw" title="pt:Manuscrito 512">pt</A>)</SPAN>, written after explorations made in the <A href="/wiki/Sert%C3%A3o" title="Sertão">sertão</A> of the state of <A href="/wiki/Bahia" title="Bahia">Bahia</A>, and housed at the National Library of <A href="/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro" title="Rio de Janeiro">Rio de Janeiro</A>. It is believed to be by Portuguese <A href="/wiki/Bandeirante" class="mw-redirect" title="Bandeirante">bandeirante</A> <A href="/w/index.php?title=Jo%C3%A3o_da_Silva_Guimar%C3%A3es&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="João da Silva Guimarães (page does not exist)">João da Silva Guimarães</A><SPAN class="noprint" style="font-size:85%; font-style: normal;"> (<A href="https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo%C3%A3o_da_Silva_Guimar%C3%A3es" class="extiw" title="pt:João da Silva Guimarães">pt</A>)</SPAN>, who wrote that in 1753 he'd discovered the ruins of an ancient city that contained arches, a statue, and a temple with hieroglyphics; the city is described in great detail without providing a specific location. This city became a secondary destination for Fawcett, after "Z". (See Fawcett's own book <I>Exploration Fawcett</I>.)</P>
<P>At the beginning of the <A href="/wiki/First_World_War" class="mw-redirect" title="First World War">First World War</A> Fawcett returned to Britain to serve with the Army as a Reserve Officer in the Royal Artillery, volunteering for duty in <A href="/wiki/Flanders" title="Flanders">Flanders</A>, and commanding an <A href="/wiki/Artillery_brigade" title="Artillery brigade">artillery brigade</A> despite the fact that he was nearly fifty years of age. He was promoted from major to lieutenant-colonel on 1 March 1918,<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP> and received three <A href="/wiki/Mentions_in_despatches" class="mw-redirect" title="Mentions in despatches">mentions in despatches</A> from <A href="/wiki/Douglas_Haig,_1st_Earl_Haig" title="Douglas Haig, 1st Earl Haig">Douglas Haig</A>, in November 1916,<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP> November 1917,<SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP> and November 1918,<SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP> and was also awarded the <A href="/wiki/Distinguished_Service_Order" title="Distinguished Service Order">Distinguished Service Order</A> in June 1917.<SUP id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-19">[19]</A></SUP></P>
<P>After the war Fawcett returned to Brazil to study local wildlife and <A href="/wiki/Archaeology" title="Archaeology">archaeology</A>. In 1920, he made a solo attempt to search for "Z", but ended after suffering from a fever and shooting his pack animal.<SUP id="cite_ref-Yorker_14-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Yorker-14">[14]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Final_expedition">Final expedition</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Final expedition">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>In 1925, with funding from a London-based group of financiers known as the Glove,<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP> Fawcett returned to Brazil with his eldest son Jack and Jack's best and longtime friend, Raleigh Rimell, for an exploratory expedition to find "Z". Fawcett left instructions stating that if the expedition did not return, no rescue expedition should be sent lest the rescuers suffer his fate.</P>
<P>Fawcett was a man with years of experience travelling, and had brought equipment such as canned foods, powdered milk, guns, flares, a <A href="/wiki/Sextant" title="Sextant">sextant</A>, and a <A href="/wiki/Marine_chronometer" title="Marine chronometer">chronometer</A>. His travel companions were both chosen for their health, ability and loyalty to each other; Fawcett chose only two companions in order to travel lighter and with less notice to native tribes, as some were hostile towards outsiders.</P>
<P>On 20 April 1925 his final expedition departed from <A href="/wiki/Cuiab%C3%A1" title="Cuiabá">Cuiabá</A>. In addition to his two principal companions, Fawcett was accompanied by two Brazilian labourers, two horses, eight mules, and a pair of dogs. The last communication from the expedition was on 29 May 1925 when Fawcett wrote, in a letter to his wife delivered by a native runner, that he was ready to go into unexplored territory with only Jack and Raleigh. They were reported to be crossing the <A href="/wiki/Xingu_River" title="Xingu River">Upper Xingu</A>, a <A href="/wiki/Ordinal_directions" class="mw-redirect" title="Ordinal directions">southeastern</A> <A href="/wiki/Tributary" title="Tributary">tributary</A> river of the <A href="/wiki/Amazon_River" title="Amazon River">River Amazon</A>. The final letter, written from <A href="/wiki/Dead_Horse_Camp" class="mw-redirect" title="Dead Horse Camp">Dead Horse Camp</A>, gave their location and was generally optimistic.</P>
<P>Many people assumed that local <A href="/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_in_Brazil" title="Indigenous peoples in Brazil">Indians</A> killed them, as several tribes were nearby at the time: the <A href="/wiki/Kalapalo" title="Kalapalo">Kalapalos</A>, the last tribe to have seen them, the Arumás, <A href="/wiki/Suy%C3%A1" title="Suyá">Suyás</A>, and the <A href="/wiki/Xavante_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Xavante people">Xavantes</A> whose territory they were entering. The Kalapalo have an oral story of the arrival of three explorers which states that the three went east, and after five days the Kalapalo noticed that the group no longer made camp fires. The Kalapalo say that a very violent tribe most likely killed them. However, both of the younger men were lame and ill when last seen, and there is not any proof that they were murdered. It is plausible that they died of natural causes in the Brazilian jungle.</P>
<P>In 1927, a name-plate of Fawcett was found with an Indian tribe. In June 1933, a <A href="/wiki/Theodolite" title="Theodolite">theodolite</A> compass belonging to Fawcett was found near the Baciary Indians of <A href="/wiki/Mato_Grosso" title="Mato Grosso">Mato Grosso</A> by Colonel Aniceto Botelho. However, the name-plate was from Fawcett's expedition five years earlier and had most likely been given as a gift to the chief of that Indian tribe. The compass was proved to have been left behind before he entered the jungle on his final journey.<SUP id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-21">[21]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-23">[23]</A></SUP></P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Dead_Horse_Camp">Dead Horse Camp</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Dead Horse Camp">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P><B>Dead Horse Camp</B>, or <B>Fawcett’s camp</B>, is one of the major camps that Fawcett made on his final journey. This encampment was his last known location.<SUP id="cite_ref-last_words_24-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-last_words-24">[24]</A></SUP></P>
<P>From Dead Horse Camp, Fawcett wrote to his wife about the hardships that he and his companions had faced, his coordinates, his doubts in Raleigh Rimmel, and of his plans for the near future. He concludes his message with, “You need have no fear of any failure...”<SUP id="cite_ref-last_words_24-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-last_words-24">[24]</A></SUP></P>
<P>One question remaining about Dead Horse Camp concerns a discrepancy in the coordinates Fawcett gave for the camp. In the letter to his wife, he wrote: "Here we are at Dead Horse Camp, latitude 11 degrees 43' South and longitude 54 degrees 35' West, the spot where my horse died in 1920" (<SPAN class="plainlinks nourlexpansion"><A class="external text" href="//tools.wmflabs.org/geohack/geohack.php?pagename=Percy_Fawcett&params=11_43_S_54_35_W_"><SPAN class="geo-default"><SPAN class="geo-dms" title="Maps, aerial photos, and other data for this location"><SPAN class="latitude">11°43′S</SPAN> <SPAN class="longitude">54°35′W</SPAN></SPAN></SPAN><SPAN class="geo-multi-punct">﻿ / ﻿</SPAN><SPAN class="geo-nondefault"><SPAN class="geo-dec" title="Maps, aerial photos, and other data for this location">11.717°S 54.583°W</SPAN><SPAN style="display:none">﻿ / <SPAN class="geo">-11.717; -54.583</SPAN></SPAN></SPAN></A></SPAN>). However, in a report to the <A href="/wiki/North_American_Newspaper_Alliance" title="North American Newspaper Alliance">North American Newspaper Alliance</A> he gave the coordinates as <SPAN class="plainlinks nourlexpansion"><A class="external text" href="//tools.wmflabs.org/geohack/geohack.php?pagename=Percy_Fawcett&params=13_43_S_54_35_W_"><SPAN class="geo-default"><SPAN class="geo-dms" title="Maps, aerial photos, and other data for this location"><SPAN class="latitude">13°43′S</SPAN> <SPAN class="longitude">54°35′W</SPAN></SPAN></SPAN><SPAN class="geo-multi-punct">﻿ / ﻿</SPAN><SPAN class="geo-nondefault"><SPAN class="geo-dec" title="Maps, aerial photos, and other data for this location">13.717°S 54.583°W</SPAN><SPAN style="display:none">﻿ / <SPAN class="geo">-13.717; -54.583</SPAN></SPAN></SPAN></A></SPAN>.<SUP id="cite_ref-camp_location_25-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-camp_location-25">[25]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The discrepancy may have been a <A href="/wiki/Typographical" class="mw-redirect" title="Typographical">typographical</A> error. However, he may have intentionally concealed the location to prevent others from using his notes to find the lost city.<SUP id="cite_ref-chronicles_26-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-chronicles-26">[26]</A></SUP> It may have also been an attempt to dissuade any rescue attempts; Fawcett had stated that if he disappeared, no <A href="/wiki/Search_and_rescue" title="Search and rescue">rescue party</A> should be sent because the danger was too great.<SUP id="cite_ref-camp_location_25-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-camp_location-25">[25]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Posthumous_controversy_and_speculations">Posthumous controversy and speculations</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Posthumous controversy and speculations">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Rumours_and_unverified_reports">Rumours and unverified reports</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Rumours and unverified reports">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>During the ensuing decades, various groups mounted several rescue expeditions, without success. They heard only various rumours that could not be verified. In addition to reports that Fawcett had been killed by Indians or wild animals, there was a tale that Fawcett had <A href="/wiki/Amnesia" title="Amnesia">lost his memory</A> and lived out his life as the chief of a tribe of <A href="/wiki/Cannibalism" class="mw-redirect" title="Cannibalism">cannibals</A>.</P>
<P>While a fictitious tale estimated that 100 would-be-rescuers died on several expeditions attempting to discover Fawcett's fate<SUP id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-27">[27]</A></SUP>, the actual toll was only one - a sole man who ventured after him alone.<SUP id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-28">[28]</A></SUP> One of the earliest expeditions was commanded by American explorer <A href="/wiki/George_Miller_Dyott" title="George Miller Dyott">George Miller Dyott</A>. In 1927 he claimed to have found evidence of Fawcett's death at the hands of the <A href="/w/index.php?title=Aloique&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Aloique (page does not exist)">Aloique</A> Indians, but his story was unconvincing. From 1930–31, <A href="/wiki/Aloha_Wanderwell#Brazil" title="Aloha Wanderwell">Aloha Wanderwell</A> used her seaplane to try to land on the Amazon River in the Matto Grosso to find him. After an emergency landing and living with the Bororo Tribe for 6 weeks, Aloha and Walter Flew back to Brazil, with no luck. A 1951 expedition unearthed human bones that were found later to be unrelated to Fawcett or his companions.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Villas-B.C3.B4as_story">Villas-Bôas story</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Villas-Bôas story">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Danish explorer <A href="/wiki/Arne_Falk-R%C3%B8nne" title="Arne Falk-Rønne">Arne Falk-Rønne</A> journeyed to the <A href="/wiki/Mato_Grosso" title="Mato Grosso">Mato Grosso</A> during the 1960s. In a 1991 book, he wrote that he learned of Fawcett's fate from <A href="/wiki/Villas-B%C3%B4as_brothers" title="Villas-Bôas brothers">Orlando Villas-Bôas</A><SUP id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-29">[29]</A></SUP>, who had heard it from one of Fawcett's murderers. Allegedly, Fawcett and his companions had a mishap on the river and lost most of the gifts they'd brought along for the Indian tribes. Continuing without gifts was a serious breach of protocol; since the expedition members were all more or less seriously ill at the time, the Kalapalo tribe they encountered decided to kill them. The bodies of Jack Fawcett and Raleigh Rimell were thrown into the river; Colonel Fawcett, considered an old man and therefore distinguished, received a proper burial. Falk-Rønne visited the Kalapalo tribe and reported that one of the tribesmen confirmed Villas-Bôas's story about how and why Fawcett had been killed.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Fawcett.27s_Bones">Fawcett's Bones</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section: Fawcett's Bones">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>In 1951, <A href="/wiki/Villas-B%C3%B4as_brothers" title="Villas-Bôas brothers">Orlando Villas-Bôas</A>, activist for indigenous peoples, supposedly received the actual remaining skeletal bones of Fawcett and had them analysed scientifically. The analysis allegedly confirmed the bones to be Fawcett's, but his son Brian Fawcett (1906–1984) refused to accept this. Villas-Bôas claimed that Brian was too interested in making money from books about his father's disappearance. Later scientific analysis confirmed that the bones were not Fawcett's.<SUP id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-30">[30]</A></SUP> As of 1965, the bones reportedly rested in a box in the flat of one of the Villas-Bôas brothers in <A href="/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo" title="São Paulo">São Paulo</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-31">[31]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In 1998, English explorer <A href="/wiki/Benedict_Allen" title="Benedict Allen">Benedict Allen</A> went to talk to the Kalapalo Indians, said by Villas-Bôas to have confessed to having killed the three Fawcett expedition members. An elder of the Kalapalo, Vajuvi, claimed during a filmed BBC interview with Allen that the bones found by Villas-Bôas some 45 years before were not really Fawcett's.<SUP id="cite_ref-Orcutt_32-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Orcutt-32">[32]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-33">[33]</A></SUP> Vajuvi also denied that his tribe had any part in the Fawcetts' disappearance. No conclusive evidence supports either statement.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Russian_documentary">Russian documentary</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section: Russian documentary">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>In 2003, a Russian documentary film, "Проклятье золота инков / Экспедиция Перси Фоссета в Амазонку" (<I>The Curse of the Incas' Gold / Expedition of Percy Fawcett to the Amazon</I>), was released as a part of the television series "Тайны века" (<I>Mysteries of the Century</I>). Among other things, the film emphasizes the recent expedition of Oleg Aliyev to the presumed approximate place of Fawcett's last whereabouts and Aliyev's findings, impressions and presumptions about Fawcett's fate.<SUP id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-34">[34]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Commune_in_the_jungle">Commune in the jungle</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section: Commune in the jungle">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>On 21 March 2004, the British newspaper <I><A href="/wiki/The_Observer" title="The Observer">The Observer</A></I> reported that television director Misha Williams, who had studied Fawcett's private papers, believed that Fawcett had not intended to return to Britain but rather meant to found a <A href="/wiki/Commune_(intentional_community)" class="mw-redirect" title="Commune (intentional community)">commune</A> in the jungle based on <A href="/wiki/Theosophy" title="Theosophy">theosophical</A> principles and the worship of his son Jack.<SUP id="cite_ref-35" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-35">[35]</A></SUP> Williams explained his research in some detail in the preface to his play <I>AmaZonia</I>, first performed in April 2004.<SUP id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-36">[36]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Grann.27s_Lost_City_of_Z">Grann's <I>Lost City of Z</I></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Percy_Fawcett&action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section: Grann's Lost City of Z">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/The_Lost_City_of_Z_(book)" title="The Lost City of Z (book)"><I>The Lost City of Z</I> (book)</A></DIV>
<P>In 2005, <I><A href="/wiki/The_New_Yorker" title="The New Yorker">The New Yorker</A></I> staff writer <A href="/wiki/David_Grann" title="David Grann">David Grann</A> visited the Kalapalo tribe and reported that it had apparently preserved an oral history about Fawcett, among the first Europeans the tribe had ever seen. The oral account said that Fawcett and his party had stayed at their village and then left, heading eastward. The Kalapalos warned Fawcett and his companions that if they went that way they would be killed by the "fierce Indians" who occupied that territory, but Fawcett insisted on going. The Kalapalos observed smoke from the expedition’s campfire each evening for five days before it disappeared. The Kalapalos said they were sure the fierce Indians had killed them.<SUP id="cite_ref-Yorker_14-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Yorker-14">[14]</A></SUP> The article also reports that a monumental civilisation known as <A href="/wiki/Kuhikugu" title="Kuhikugu">Kuhikugu</A> may have actually existed near where Fawcett was searching, as discovered recently by archaeologist <A href="/wiki/Michael_Heckenberger" class="mw-redirect" title="Michael Heckenberger">Michael Heckenberger</A> and others.<SUP id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-37">[37]</A></SUP> Grann's findings are further detailed in his book <I><A href="/wiki/The_Lost_City_of_Z_(book)" title="The Lost City of Z (book)">The Lost City of Z</A></I> (2009).</P>

<UL>
<LI>Was the subject of an episode of <I><A href="/wiki/Digging_for_the_Truth" title="Digging for the Truth">Digging for the Truth</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Arthur_Conan_Doyle" title="Arthur Conan Doyle">Arthur Conan Doyle</A> based his <A href="/wiki/Professor_Challenger" title="Professor Challenger">Professor Challenger</A> character partly on Fawcett, and stories of the "Lost City of Z" became the basis for his novel <I><A href="/wiki/The_Lost_World_(Conan_Doyle_novel)" title="The Lost World (Conan Doyle novel)">The Lost World</A>.</I><SUP id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-38">[38]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI>A contemporary reviewer of <A href="/wiki/Evelyn_Waugh" title="Evelyn Waugh">Evelyn Waugh</A>'s novel <I><A href="/wiki/A_Handful_of_Dust" title="A Handful of Dust">A Handful of Dust</A></I> suggested he may have derived the plot partly from Fawcett's disappearance.<SUP id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-39">[39]</A></SUP> The novel's hero vanishes into the Brazilian jungle and is kept prisoner there.</LI>
<LI>Fawcett has been proposed as a possible inspiration for <A href="/wiki/Indiana_Jones" title="Indiana Jones">Indiana Jones</A>, the fictional archaeologist/adventurer.<SUP id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-40">[40]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-41">[41]</A></SUP> A fictionalised version of Fawcett aids Jones in the novel <I><A href="/wiki/Indiana_Jones_and_the_Seven_Veils" title="Indiana Jones and the Seven Veils">Indiana Jones and the Seven Veils</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-42">[42]</A></SUP>)</LI>
<LI>Fawcett was a prototype of Percy Foster, fictional explorer in the Russian-language novel <I><A href="https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9C%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%B8%D0%BB%D0%B0_%D0%A2%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B5-%D0%A2%D1%83%D0%BD%D0%B3%D0%B0" class="extiw" title="ru:Могила Таме-Тунга">The grave of Tame-Tung</A></I>. There, Foster and his son became obsessed with riches of Indians and were killed by their former friend Raleigh Rimer (based on Raleigh Rimmel) to prevent pillaging.</LI>
<LI>According to an article in <I>Comics Scene</I> No. 45, Fawcett was the inspiration of Kent Allard, an alter ego of <A href="/wiki/The_Shadow_(fictional_character)" class="mw-redirect" title="The Shadow (fictional character)">the Shadow</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Orcutt_32-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Orcutt-32">[32]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI>Director <A href="/wiki/Pete_Docter" title="Pete Docter">Pete Docter</A> named Fawcett as one of the inspirations for the character Charles F. Muntz, the antagonist of the <A href="/wiki/Pixar" title="Pixar">Pixar</A> film <I><A href="/wiki/Up_(2009_film)" title="Up (2009 film)">Up</A></I>.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/David_Grann" title="David Grann">David Grann</A>'s <I><A href="/wiki/The_Lost_City_of_Z_(book)" title="The Lost City of Z (book)">The Lost City of Z</A></I> was optioned by <A href="/wiki/Brad_Pitt" title="Brad Pitt">Brad Pitt</A>'s <A href="/wiki/Plan_B_Entertainment" title="Plan B Entertainment">Plan B</A> production company and <A href="/wiki/Paramount_Pictures" title="Paramount Pictures">Paramount Pictures</A>. <A href="/wiki/James_Gray_(film_director)" title="James Gray (film director)">James Gray</A> directed <A href="/wiki/The_Lost_City_of_Z_(film)" title="The Lost City of Z (film)">the film</A>, which stars <A href="/wiki/Charlie_Hunnam" title="Charlie Hunnam">Charlie Hunnam</A> as Fawcett and was released in April 2017.</LI>
<LI><I>The Cruise of the Condor</I> (1933), one of <A href="/wiki/W._E._Johns" title="W. E. Johns">W. E. Johns</A>' "<A href="/wiki/Biggles" title="Biggles">Biggles</A>" stories, is inspired by Fawcett's search for "Z".</LI>
<LI>Writers <A href="/wiki/Douglas_Preston" title="Douglas Preston">Douglas Preston</A> and <A href="/wiki/Lincoln_Child" title="Lincoln Child">Lincoln Child</A> mentioned in their books that Percy Fawcett was a great-great uncle of <A href="/wiki/Aloysius_Pendergast" title="Aloysius Pendergast">Aloysius Pendergast</A> on his mother’s side.</LI>
<LI>The plot of the first episode of the television programme <I><A href="/wiki/Hooten_%26_the_Lady" title="Hooten & the Lady">Hooten & the Lady</A></I> was about the search for Fawcett's camp.</LI>
<LI>In <A href="/wiki/Herg%C3%A9" title="Hergé">Hergé</A>'s adventure of <A href="/wiki/Tintin_(character)" title="Tintin (character)">Tintin</A> <I><A href="/wiki/The_Broken_Ear" title="The Broken Ear">L'Oreille Cassée</A></I>, Fawcett is believed to be the model for Ridgewell, an explorer disappeared for ten years who has become known as "the white old man" a member of the Arumbaya tribe.</LI>
<LI>Peter Fleming's book Brazilian Adventure is the story of his part in an expedition to find Fawcett. Fleming's book was first published in 1933. Peter was the brother of Ian who wrote the James Bond books.</LI>
<LI>The 2017 <A href="/wiki/Osprey_Publishing" title="Osprey Publishing">Osprey Games</A> <A href="/wiki/Eurogame" title="Eurogame">Eurogame</A> <I>The Lost Expedition</I>, designed by Peer Sylvester, with artwork by <A href="/wiki/Garen_Ewing" title="Garen Ewing">Garen Ewing</A>, is based on Percy Fawcett's expeditions.<SUP id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-43">[43]</A></SUP></LI>

<P><B>Meredith Grey</B>, <A href="/wiki/Doctor_of_Medicine" title="Doctor of Medicine">M.D.</A> is a <A href="/wiki/Fictional_character" class="mw-redirect" title="Fictional character">fictional character</A> from the <A href="/wiki/Medical_drama" title="Medical drama">medical drama</A> television series <I><A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy" title="Grey's Anatomy">Grey's Anatomy</A></I>, which airs on the <A href="/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company" title="American Broadcasting Company">American Broadcasting Company</A> (ABC) in the <A href="/wiki/Television_in_the_United_States" title="Television in the United States">United States</A>. The character was created by series' producer <A href="/wiki/Shonda_Rhimes" title="Shonda Rhimes">Shonda Rhimes</A>, and is portrayed by actress <A href="/wiki/Ellen_Pompeo" title="Ellen Pompeo">Ellen Pompeo</A>. Meredith is the series' <A href="/wiki/Protagonist" title="Protagonist">protagonist</A>, and was introduced as a <A href="/wiki/Internship_(medicine)" title="Internship (medicine)">surgical intern</A> at the fictional Seattle Grace Hospital (later Seattle Grace-Mercy West, and afterwards Grey Sloan Memorial), eventually obtaining the position of a <A href="/wiki/Residency_(medicine)" title="Residency (medicine)">resident</A>, and later the position of an <A href="/wiki/Attending_physician" title="Attending physician">attending</A>, and in 2015, attaining the Chief of General Surgery position. As the daughter of world-renowned surgeon <A href="/wiki/List_of_Grey%27s_Anatomy_characters" title="List of Grey's Anatomy characters">Ellis Grey</A>, Meredith struggles with the everyday life of being in a competitive profession, maintaining the relationship with her <A href="/wiki/One-night_stand" title="One-night stand">one-night stand</A> and eventual husband <A href="/wiki/Derek_Shepherd" title="Derek Shepherd">Derek Shepherd</A> (deceased), her motherhood, and her friendships with her colleagues.</P>
<P>Meredith is the narrator of the show and serves as the focal point for most episodes. Pompeo's connection with <A href="/wiki/Patrick_Dempsey" title="Patrick Dempsey">Patrick Dempsey</A> (Derek Shepherd) is acclaimed as a high point of the series. Rhimes has characterized Meredith as not believing in good or bad, but instead doing what she thinks is right. Grey has been positively received by television critics, with Alessandra Stanley of <I><A href="/wiki/The_New_York_Times" title="The New York Times">The New York Times</A></I> referring to her as "the heroine of <I>Grey's Anatomy</I>". News of Pompeo leaving arose when it was made clear that her contract ended after the eighth season, and whether or not she would return to the series after her contract expires has been the centre of media speculation ever since. In 2016, Pompeo re-negotiated her contract and signed up for the thirteenth season of the show.</P>
<P>Pompeo's performance has been well received throughout the show and the character has gained widespread popularity worldwide. Pompeo has been nominated for multiple awards for her portrayal of the character in the long running <A href="/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company" title="American Broadcasting Company">ABC</A> <A href="/wiki/Medical_drama" title="Medical drama">medical drama</A> including <A href="/wiki/Satellite_Award_for_Best_Actress_%E2%80%93_Television_Series_Drama" title="Satellite Award for Best Actress – Television Series Drama">Satellite Award for Best Actress</A> and multiple nominations at the <A href="/wiki/People%27s_Choice_Awards" title="People's Choice Awards">People's Choice Awards</A> for Best Actress winning at <A href="/wiki/39th_People%27s_Choice_Awards" title="39th People's Choice Awards">39th People's Choice Awards</A> in 2013 and again in 2015 at <A href="/wiki/41st_People%27s_Choice_Awards" title="41st People's Choice Awards">41st People's Choice Awards</A>, Pompeo has also received a <A href="/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_%E2%80%93_Television_Series_Drama" title="Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Television Series Drama">Best Performance by an Actress in a Drama Series</A> nomination at the <A href="/wiki/64th_Golden_Globe_Awards" title="64th Golden Globe Awards">64th Golden Globe Awards</A>.</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Storylines_and_Characteristics">Storylines and Characteristics</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Meredith_Grey&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Storylines and Characteristics">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Dr. Meredith Grey is the daughter of world-renowned surgeon Ellis Grey, and grew up in her shadow. Ellis was a deeply flawed, emotionally and verbally abusive, neglectful mother towards her. Meredith is described as a "dark and twisty," damaged person who sees the world in varying shades of gray morality. Because of this, she is an emotionally complex person capable of empathizing with others when they're at their lowest points, and a sensitive observer of the people around her. Meredith is a graduate of <A href="/wiki/Dartmouth_College" title="Dartmouth College">Dartmouth College</A> and nearly did not attend med school due to conflicts with her mother. Meredith was directionless after obtaining her undergrad and had plans to sleep and party her way through Europe. After a month abroad, Meredith was called back to care for Ellis, who had developed early-onset <A href="/wiki/Alzheimer%27s_disease" title="Alzheimer's disease">Alzheimer's disease</A>, and Meredith obtained her M.D.</P>
<P>The night before Meredith's <A href="/wiki/Internship_(medicine)" title="Internship (medicine)">internship</A> begins, she has a <A href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/one-night_stand" class="extiw" title="wiktionary:one-night stand">one-night stand</A> with <A href="/wiki/Derek_Shepherd" title="Derek Shepherd">Derek Shepherd</A> (<A href="/wiki/Patrick_Dempsey" title="Patrick Dempsey">Patrick Dempsey</A>), a stranger she meets at a bar. She discovers the next day that he is the recently-hired <A href="/wiki/Attending_physician" title="Attending physician">attending</A> and new head of <A href="/wiki/Neurosurgery" title="Neurosurgery">neurosurgery</A> at her new workplace, Seattle Grace Hospital. Meredith is assigned to work under resident <A href="/wiki/Miranda_Bailey" title="Miranda Bailey">Miranda Bailey</A> (<A href="/wiki/Chandra_Wilson" title="Chandra Wilson">Chandra Wilson</A>), and befriends her fellow interns, <A href="/wiki/George_O%27Malley" title="George O'Malley">George O'Malley</A> (<A href="/wiki/T.R._Knight" class="mw-redirect" title="T.R. Knight">T.R. Knight</A>), <A href="/wiki/Izzie_Stevens" title="Izzie Stevens">Izzie Stevens</A> (<A href="/wiki/Katherine_Heigl" title="Katherine Heigl">Katherine Heigl</A>), <A href="/wiki/Cristina_Yang" title="Cristina Yang">Cristina Yang</A> (<A href="/wiki/Sandra_Oh" title="Sandra Oh">Sandra Oh</A>) and <A href="/wiki/Alex_Karev" title="Alex Karev">Alex Karev</A> (<A href="/wiki/Justin_Chambers" title="Justin Chambers">Justin Chambers</A>).</P>
<P>She is particularly close with Cristina Yang, who becomes her best friend and "person". Though she initially thinks poorly of him, Alex Karev also evolves into Meredith's "person" and the two assume a sibling-esque familial relationship. Meredith has a conflicted relationship with <A href="/wiki/Richard_Webber" title="Richard Webber">Richard Webber</A> (<A href="/wiki/James_Pickens_Jr." title="James Pickens Jr.">James Pickens Jr.</A>), the Chief of Surgery at Seattle Grace. Richard was very close to Ellis when Meredith was a child, which inclines him to save or mentor Grey and make exceptions for her. Meredith has a habit of "collecting strays", allowing her friends and coworkers to live in the house her mother left her and become her pseudo-family. Meredith is endlessly loyal to those she deems her family, and bends traditional morality as needed in order to keep them safe.</P>
<P>Having grown up in a hospital, Meredith shows immense natural talent. She possesses a steadfast, calm ease during medical procedures and emergencies, and is a natural observer of people. She exhibits a knack for catching subtle hints and accurately determining difficult-to-catch diagnoses. Her placid, non-judgmental bedside manner often causes people to open up and trust her. Her surgical skills are solidly impressive and she shows a talent and patience for medical research trials and dealing with psychologically damaged patients.</P>
<P>Meredith resists Derek's advances throughout her internship, but is eventually charmed into starting a relationship with him despite misgivings about an intern dating an attending. She is therefore shocked by the arrival of <A href="/wiki/Addison_Montgomery" title="Addison Montgomery">Addison Montgomery</A> (<A href="/wiki/Kate_Walsh_(actress)" title="Kate Walsh (actress)">Kate Walsh</A>), Derek's wife, unaware that he was married. Derek struggles to choose between the two, but ultimately returns to Addison, despite Meredith begging to be chosen instead.</P>
<P>Meredith is devastated and turns to multiple, self-destructive means of coping. Initially she falls on old habits of self-medicating with tequila and sex, and buys a dog. She also tries to resolve some issues by searching for her long-absent father, Thatcher. <SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP> She learns that her father, who left when she was five and she has not seen since, remarried and had two more daughters. The two do not become close, but Grey becomes fond of her stepmother.</P>
<P>Meredith spirals further when Ellis is admitted to the hospital, revealing Ellis' diagnosis of early-onset Alzheimer's and her verbally abusive tendencies. Meredith self-destructive behavior increases when she saves a patient with a bomb in their chest by impulsively inserting her hand to hold it until the bomb squad can remove it. Mereidth has a series of one-night stands, including one with George, who is in love with her. When she cries in the middle of their encounter, their friendship temporarily ends. Meredith swears off her behavior, agrees to be friends only with Shepherd, and embarks on a relationship with veterinarian <A href="/wiki/Finn_Dandridge" class="mw-redirect" title="Finn Dandridge">Finn Dandridge</A> (<A href="/wiki/Chris_O%27Donnell" title="Chris O'Donnell">Chris O'Donnell</A>).</P>
<P>Derek regrets his decision to return to his wife and Meredith must decide whether to continue a relationship with Finn, or allow Derek a second chance.</P>
<P>When Ellis experiences a rare, completely <A href="/wiki/Sanity" title="Sanity">lucid</A> day, and expresses her immense disappointment at how ordinary Meredith has turned out to be, she becomes depressed and possibly suicidal. During a ferryboat accident, Meredith is knocked into the water and chooses to give up and drown, rather than fight and swim. She <A href="/wiki/Flatline" title="Flatline">flatlines</A> at the hospital, and awakens in an "afterlife", where she interacts with deceased former acquaintances. Ellis dies in the interim, and Meredith meets with her mother, who tells her that she is anything but ordinary. She is subsequently <A href="/wiki/Cardiopulmonary_resuscitation" title="Cardiopulmonary resuscitation">resuscitated</A> at the insistence of Cristina. Derek distances himself from Meredith as the result of her self recklessness, prompting her to seek <A href="/wiki/Therapy" title="Therapy">therapy</A> to address her problems. Meredith sees a therapist, Dr. Wyatt (<A href="/wiki/Amy_Madigan" title="Amy Madigan">Amy Madigan</A>), to seek happiness and begins to successfully tackle her issues. Meredith found her mother's diaries, dredging up old memories and secrets for her to work through. Meanwhile, Meredith nearly fails her intern exam after a drunken Thatcher publicly blames Meredith for the death of his wife, Susan, a distraught Grey sits through her entire test without writing a single answer. Dr. Webber gives her a second chance, saving her from destroying her career.</P>
<P>After Meredith is promoted to a resident, her younger half-sister <A href="/wiki/Lexie_Grey" title="Lexie Grey">Lexie Grey</A> (<A href="/wiki/Chyler_Leigh" title="Chyler Leigh">Chyler Leigh</A>) begins working at Seattle Grace as an intern. Meredith initially rejects Lexie's attempts to form a relationship, but slowly softens towards her. The sisters are very different people with different childhoods. Lexie had an idealistic family life and often has difficulty understanding her much darker sister, who does not have the same positive associations with family as Lexie.</P>
<P>She later initiates a neurosurgical clinical trial, enlisting Derek as a consulting neurosurgeon. The trial fails repeatedly, but the final patient they treat survives, which leads them to reuniting and moving in together. Their relationship is healthier than before, but still experiences snags as the two attempt to understand each other and navigate what they now look on as a permanent, long-term relationship. Meredith relies heavily on Cristina for emotional support and guidance. Eventually, Derek and Meredith decide to marry, but on their wedding day, the pair give their "perfect" wedding ceremony to Izzie and Alex, to marry each other during the planned ceremony instead.</P>

<P>Meredith and Derek marry by writing their wedding vows on a <A href="/wiki/Post-it_note" title="Post-it note">post-it note</A>. Meredith spends the majority of a season out of commission after donating part of her liver to Thatcher and supporting Cristina's new relationship with Owen Hunt, an army doctor with worrisome <A href="/wiki/PTSD" class="mw-redirect" title="PTSD">PTSD</A>.</P>
<P>Mereduth experiences another immense trauma after the hospital is put under a lockdown from an active mass-shooter seeking revenge against Derek. Meredith offers her own life in exchange for his and <A href="/wiki/Miscarriage" title="Miscarriage">miscarries</A> her baby during the crisis. She goes through this traumatic experience with Cristina, who operates on Derek while threatened at gunpoint. Meredith hides her loss and the trauma psychiatrist refuses to clear neither Cristina nor Meredith for their return to surgery. Meredith is able to work through her issues and become cleared, but Cristina remains deeply traumatized. Meredith covers for and supports her friend through her dark time, but is ultimately unable to fully help her return to surgery.</P>
<P>Meredith decides to actively try to become pregnant, but learns that she has a "<A href="/wiki/Female_infertility" title="Female infertility">hostile uterus</A>", which leads her to consider her other possible genetic flaws. Derek, who is constantly worried about the possibility that she will develop Alzheimer's, initiates a clinical trial hoping to cure the disease. Meredith opts to work on the trial and appears to be leaning towards a neuro specialty.</P>
<P>When the chief of surgery, <A href="/wiki/Richard_Webber" title="Richard Webber">Richard Webber</A> (<A href="/wiki/James_Pickens_Jr." title="James Pickens Jr.">James Pickens Jr.</A>)'s wife, Adele, is diagnosed with Alzheimer's, she receives a spot on the trial. Meredith tampers with the drugs so that Adele does not receive the <A href="/wiki/Placebo" title="Placebo">placebo</A>. She and Derek decide to adopt Zola, an orphaned baby from <A href="/wiki/Malawi" title="Malawi">Malawi</A>, and make their marriage legal. When the truth about the tampering comes out, however, a furious Derek tells her he cannot raise a child with her because of her moral ambiguity. Meredith is fired, and tries to conceal both this and her marital separation from the <A href="/wiki/Adoption" title="Adoption">adoption counselor</A> in order to keep Zola. Although Dr. Webber steps down as chief of surgery and takes the blame for the trial tampering to protect Meredith, Zola is taken away. She and Derek reconcile. Meredith chooses a general specialty over neuro, and they successfully fight to get Zola back.</P>
<P>As her last year of residency is coming to a close, the residents travel around the country, searching for the best jobs in their <A href="/wiki/Specialty_(medicine)" title="Specialty (medicine)">specialties</A>. In order to finish their residency, the residents must take the <A href="/wiki/United_States_Medical_Licensing_Examination" title="United States Medical Licensing Examination">medical boards</A>. Meredith takes the exam while sick with the flu. She decides to take a job offer at The <A href="/wiki/Brigham_and_Women%27s_Hospital" title="Brigham and Women's Hospital">Brigham and Women's Hospital</A> as the next step in her career. During a medical flight to undertake a prestigious surgery involving conjoined twins, Meredith, Derek, Cristina, and Lexie, among others, are involved in an <A href="/wiki/Aviation_accident" class="mw-redirect" title="Aviation accident">aviation accident</A>. The plane crash kills Lexie, and the survivors are trapped in the wooded wilderness for days waiting for help. Following their rescue, Merdith becomes an <A href="/wiki/Attending_physician" title="Attending physician">attending</A> <A href="/wiki/General_surgery" title="General surgery">general surgeon</A> at Seattle Grace, now Seattle Grace-Mercy West. While Cristina flees Seattle for her fellowship, Meredith, afraid of flying and change, declines her job offer, and clings to what remains in Seattle. Cristina and Meredith begin calling the hospital Seattle Grace Mercy Death in light of the immense amount of trauma, death, and pain they have experienced there.</P>
<P>Meredith's newfound attitude and sarcasm leads to her being dubbed "<A href="/wiki/Medusa" title="Medusa">Medusa</A>" by the hospital's new batch of interns. In the aftermath of the plane accident, the hospital is sued and eventually found guilty of negligence. Each victim including Derek, Cristina, <A href="/wiki/Arizona_Robbins" title="Arizona Robbins">Arizona Robbins</A> (<A href="/wiki/Jessica_Capshaw" title="Jessica Capshaw">Jessica Capshaw</A>) and herself must receive $15 million of compensation, which leads the hospital to a near bankruptcy as the insurance company refuses to pay due to a loophole. The doctors along with <A href="/wiki/Callie_Torres" title="Callie Torres">Callie Torres</A> (<A href="/wiki/Sara_Ramirez" title="Sara Ramirez">Sara Ramirez</A>) buy the hospital with the help of the Harper Avery Foundation to prevent it from closing and become new members of the directing board.</P>
<P>Meredith asks Dr. Bailey to perform <A href="/wiki/Gene_mapping" title="Gene mapping">gene mapping</A> on her to finally know whether she has Alzheimer's genes like her mother. She tests positive for more than one of the genetic markers for the disease.</P>
<P>Meredith moves to the completed dream home and sells her house to Alex, who purchases it as the only true home he's ever known. He continues Meredith's tradition of keeping the house open to any "strays" needing a home. Meredith discovers she is pregnant and gives birth to a son. The baby is delivered via <A href="/wiki/C-section" class="mw-redirect" title="C-section">C-section</A>. While stitching Meredith up, the obstetrician who operated on her is called away to another patient and intern Shane Ross completes the stitching. When blood begins to appear from everywhere, Meredith diagnoses herself in as being in <A href="/wiki/Disseminated_intravascular_coagulation" title="Disseminated intravascular coagulation">DIC</A>. Dr. Bailey performs a <A href="/wiki/Spleen_removal" class="mw-redirect" title="Spleen removal">spleen removal</A>, which saves her life. In return, Derek and Meredith name their son Bailey.</P>
<P>As a spouse, surgeon, and mother, Meredith has cited a number times that she did not want to be like either of her parents: her father had followed her mother around pathetically before leaving to be happy, while her mother valued her career over her family. Meredith is frequently conflicted trying to balance between the two, and fears her family are hindering her medical aspirations, as much as she fears becoming like her mother whenever she's tempted to choose surgery over family. Meredith and Cristina have a huge rift when Cristina confirms Meredith's fears by stating that Meredith's skills have fallen behind Cristina's due to her familial obligations taking her away from OR time.</P>
<P>Meredith and Derek come to an agreement that he, already established in his career and reputation, would take a step back to take care of the children and allow her to shine. Meredith attempts to regain some ground by starting a promising research trial 3-D printing portal veins. The conflict between Cristina and Meredith widens when Cristina commandeers Meredith's resources for her own trial, ultimately garnering a Harper Avery nomination for Cristina. Cristina and Meredith repair their relationship when Meredith confesses that Cristina was correct, her skills have surpassed Meredith's. Cristina moves to Switzerland take up a job offer from <A href="/wiki/Preston_Burke" title="Preston Burke">Dr. Preston Burke</A>, her former attending, mentor and fiancé, who was looking for a replacement at a research hospital he was running, thus leaving Alex in charge of being Meredith's "person" in her place, an honor he gladly accepts.</P>
<P>Meredith and Derek's marriage becomes strained when Derek goes against his promise and accepts an offer from the U.S. President to participate in the Brain Mapping Initiative, which consumes his time and eclipses Meredith, who is feeling increasingly left behind and mommy-tracked. He receives an offer to head the project itself in <A href="/wiki/Washington_D.C." class="mw-redirect" title="Washington D.C.">Washington D.C.</A>, meaning that he would have to be based there permanently. Meredith puts her foot down as she does not want to uproot their young family to move across the country for his career at the sacrifice of her own. They begin a series of on-and-off arguments and "cold wars" over their careers. Derek accepts the job in the heat of the moment and promptly leaves for Washington. During a phone call with Meredith, they agree to work things out after she tells him that she did not want them to become "one of those couples" and he reciprocates, saying that he missed her. She privately admits to Alex that she has realized that she could live independently of Derek, but chooses not to.</P>
<P>Meredith finds out she has a maternal half sister named Maggie Pierce who is now working in Grey Sloan Memorial. Meredith is in denial and rejects Maggie, thinking she would have remembered if her mother was pregnant until she finds a hospital document confirming the revelation. Meredith tries to piece together her relationship with her mother and half sister by going through old videos of her mother. She eventually recovers her repressed memories of the pregnancy when she views her mother's diary and has a change of heart, choosing to accept Maggie and begin building a relationship.</P>
<P>Meredith is widowed when Derek is killed in a car accident and was taken to an understaffed hospital. The doctors failed to recognize his head injury in time and allowed personal conflicts to interfere. Derek is declared brain dead, and Meredith must go to the medical center to consent to remove him from life support, shortly before she's hit with the first waves of morning sickness. She tells Penny, the intern who was assigned to Derek that every doctor has "that one" patient who dies on their watch and haunts them forever and "that one will make you work harder, and they make you better."</P>
<P>After Derek's death, Meredith returns to Grey Sloan Memorial to inform the others of his passing. Following the funeral service, Meredith impulsively packs up her belongings and leaves with the children to San Diego. Months pass by while her friends and family are unaware of her whereabouts. Eventually, parallels show similarities in Meredith's and Ellis' lives: Both have lost the love of their life, both run away from Seattle following their loss, and both eventually give birth to a daughter. Meredith names her newborn daughter after her mother. Although still grieving over Derek, Meredith returns to Seattle with the children and later becomes chief of general surgery. She sells the "dream house" and moves back to her mother's house, having purchased it back from Alex, and now lives there with Maggie and <A href="/wiki/Amelia_Shepherd" title="Amelia Shepherd">Amelia Shepherd</A>, her sister-in-law.</P>
<P>Meredith hosts a dinner party and at the party Callie brings Penny as a date. Later at the event Meredith finds out Penny will be joining her at Grey Sloan Memorial. Meredith eventually forgives Penny, who becomes her favorite resident over Alex's girlfriend, Jo. Alex and Meredith continue their close, sibling-like relationship of being each other's "person", despite Jo's displeasure and inability to understand their closeness. He supports her when she is violently attacked by a disoriented patient, and she supports him through his legal difficulties. Alex initiates a weekly family waffle day where he makes waffles for everyone in the house.</P>
<P>Meredith recovers enough to start seeing <A href="/wiki/Nathan_Riggs" class="mw-redirect" title="Nathan Riggs">Nathan Riggs</A>, Owen Hunt's former best friend, by season 13, although their relationship is complicated by the fact that Maggie confesses to Meredith that she has feelings for Riggs and Meredith is not ready to declare their relationship formally or publicly. Eventually she accepts her relationship with Riggs, but it's complicated by the unexpected return of Owen's sister, Megan Hunt, Riggs' fiancée. Meredith finds herself in another love triangle when Megan rejects Riggs because he is still in love with Meredith, but Meredith pushes them to be together. After her relationship with Riggs ends, Meredith is nominated for a Harper Avery Award for her groundbreaking surgery on Megan.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Development">Development</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Meredith_Grey&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Development">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Casting_and_creation">Casting and creation</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Meredith_Grey&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Casting and creation">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Pompeo discovered <I>Grey's Anatomy</I> after an extended period of doing nothing in the acting profession. Her agent suggested she audition amongst other projects. <SUP id="cite_ref-search_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-search-2">[2]</A></SUP> While casting actresses for the part of Meredith Grey, series' creator <A href="/wiki/Shonda_Rhimes" title="Shonda Rhimes">Shonda Rhimes</A> said: "I kept saying we need a girl like that girl from <A href="/wiki/Moonlight_Mile_(film)" title="Moonlight Mile (film)">Moonlight Mile</A>, and after a while, they were like, 'We think we can get that girl from Moonlight Mile.' I spent time with her and got to know her, and then we started casting for the men." She reported that Grey was not an easy role to cast because of the strong verbal possibilities. <SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP> Rhimes was informed that the actress in question was Pompeo, who had a deal in place with <A href="/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company" title="American Broadcasting Company">ABC</A>, having previously tested for a pilot show on the network.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP> It has been speculated that Pompeo was the first character to be cast, but when asked, she said she did not know of this.<SUP id="cite_ref-fanbolt_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-fanbolt-5">[5]</A></SUP> When asked of how she created Pompeo's character, Rhimes said:</P>
<TABLE class="cquote" role="presentation" style="margin:auto; border-collapse: collapse; border: none; background-color: transparent; width: auto;">
<TBODY><TR>
<TD style="width: 20px; vertical-align: top; border: none; color: #B2B7F2; font-size: 40px; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-weight: bold; line-height: .6em; text-align: left; padding: 10px 10px;">“</TD>
<TD style="vertical-align: top; border: none; padding: 4px 10px;">"[I was] in my pajamas at home, which is where I spent a lot of time writing. I kept asking myself, 'What kind of woman should the heroine be?' I thought she should be someone who had made some big mistakes. As it turns out, Meredith also has another problem: She is trying to live up to her mother's renowned career in surgery. Meredith is the daughter of a mother who basically never spent any time with her—the daughter of a mother who now has Alzheimer's and doesn't even remember her."<SUP id="cite_ref-oprah_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-oprah-6">[6]</A></SUP></TD>
<TD style="width: 20px; vertical-align: bottom; border: none; color: #B2B7F2; font-size: 40px; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-weight: bold; line-height: .6em; text-align: right; padding: 10px 10px;">”</TD>
</TR>
</TBODY></TABLE>
<P>Pompeo was cast as the program's titular character, described by Mary McNamara of the <I><A href="/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times" title="Los Angeles Times">Los Angeles Times</A></I> as "a prickly, independent sort whose ambition, and ambivalence, is fueled by the fact that her mother was a gifted surgeon and now suffers from Alzheimer's."<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> Grey also serves as the show's narrator, and as such was likened in early reviews to <A href="/wiki/Carrie_Bradshaw" title="Carrie Bradshaw">Carrie Bradshaw</A> (<A href="/wiki/Sarah_Jessica_Parker" title="Sarah Jessica Parker">Sarah Jessica Parker</A>), the narrator and protagonist of <I><A href="/wiki/Sex_and_the_City" title="Sex and the City">Sex and the City</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> After her initial contract with <I>Grey's Anatomy</I> expired, Pompeo negotiated a new one, in which she would be paid US$200,000 per episode, making her and Dempsey the highest-paid cast members on the show.<SUP id="cite_ref-PayRaise_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-PayRaise-10">[10]</A></SUP> In 2012, <I><A href="/wiki/Forbes" title="Forbes">Forbes</A></I> recognized Pompeo as the eighth highest-paid actress on television, with a salary of US$275,000 per episode for her role on <I>Grey's Anatomy</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-forbes_11-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-forbes-11">[11]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Pompeo's second contract with <I>Grey's Anatomy</I> expired after the <A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_8)" title="Grey's Anatomy (season 8)">eighth season</A>, and speculation arose that she would be leaving subsequently. <SUP id="cite_ref-mercontract_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-mercontract-12">[12]</A></SUP> In September 2011, Pompeo reported that she is open to the idea of extending her contract, if invited. She told <I><A href="/wiki/TV_Guide" title="TV Guide">TV Guide</A></I>: "I would never turn up my nose at [<I>Grey's Anatomy</I>]. As long as the stories are honest and truthful, and Patrick [Dempsey] and I feel there is material for us to be passionate about, it still beats a 9-to-5 job any day. If I hear from the fans that they want us to keep going, then I would continue because we owe them everything." <I><A href="/wiki/E!_Online" class="mw-redirect" title="E! Online">E! Online</A></I> reported in May 2012, that Pompeo, as well as all original cast members have signed on for two more years.<SUP id="cite_ref-return_13-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-return-13">[13]</A></SUP> With the <I><A href="/wiki/Huffington_Post" class="mw-redirect" title="Huffington Post">Huffington Post</A></I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'s</SPAN> announcement of season nine having officially been renewed, the contract is set into place for Pompeo to return.<SUP id="cite_ref-renewed_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-renewed-14">[14]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Pompeo's contract expired again at the end of the twelfth season. She signed a new contract to keep her in the starring role on the series for thirteenth season.<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP> According to a report in <A href="/wiki/Deadline.com" title="Deadline.com">Deadline.com</A>, Pompeo was earning $300,000 per episode under the new deal.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Characterization">Characterization</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Meredith_Grey&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Characterization">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="quotebox" style="float: left; clear: left; margin: 0.5em 1.4em 0.8em 0; width:30em; padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #aaa; font-size: 88%; background-color: #F9F9F9;">
<DIV class="" style="position: relative; text-align: left;">
<DIV>Whatever I come up with, [Pompeo] is always game to play. She's been so good at what she's done that I've just let the character do what I've wanted the character to do, which has been wonderful. She's managed to sell every single thing because she's really believed it. The incredible thing is that you can have no fear to write what you think because she is always able to deliver.</DIV>
</DIV>
<CITE style="display: block; text-align: left;">Executive producer <A href="/wiki/Betsy_Beers" title="Betsy Beers">Betsy Beers</A> on developing Pompeo's character<SUP id="cite_ref-prod_17-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-prod-17">[17]</A></SUP></CITE></DIV>
<P>Grey is the protagonist and focal point of the series. She has been called "intelligent, compassionate, hard-working, oftentimes outspoken, easily distracted, and indecisive" by <I>Grey's Anatomy</I> executives.<SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP> Pompeo says she is unaware if her character knows how to have fun, adding: "All of my scenes with [Dempsey] are the same—we're either breaking up or having sex."<SUP id="cite_ref-fun_19-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-fun-19">[19]</A></SUP> Her personality has evolved over the past few seasons from depressed, to happy and "fixed". Pompeo said to <I><A href="/wiki/Good_Morning_America" title="Good Morning America">Good Morning America</A></I>, "I am so incredibly lucky to have Patrick [Dempsey], to have the chemistry that we do, we have an amazing relationship, and it's like any other relationship, you have your ups and downs. But we work it out, and we've found a way to do this for this long and still get along, and make it work and believe in what we're doing." Pompeo told <I><A href="/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly" title="Entertainment Weekly">Entertainment Weekly</A></I>: "It's awkward with Patrick [Dempsey] because he's like my brother. As soon as the camera is off, I'm like, 'Is your hand on my butt?' But there are millions of girls who have been waiting for this, so I feel an obligation to the fans."<SUP id="cite_ref-chem_20-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-chem-20">[20]</A></SUP> Rhimes used the dog "Doc", which Meredith and Derek shared, as a metaphor of their relationship during the <A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_2)" title="Grey's Anatomy (season 2)">second season</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-21">[21]</A></SUP> She characterizes Grey as doing what she thinks is right:</P>
<TABLE class="cquote" role="presentation" style="margin:auto; border-collapse: collapse; border: none; background-color: transparent; width: auto;">
<TBODY><TR>
<TD style="width: 20px; vertical-align: top; border: none; color: #B2B7F2; font-size: 40px; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-weight: bold; line-height: .6em; text-align: left; padding: 10px 10px;">“</TD>
<TD style="vertical-align: top; border: none; padding: 4px 10px;">Meredith is the girl who put her hand on a bomb in a body cavity. Meredith is the girl who tried to help a serial killer kill himself, so that he could donate his organs. Meredith—and this is obvious—has a compass that has always led her to shades of grey. She does not believe in black-and-white, she does not believe in good or bad, she does what she thinks is right.<SUP id="cite_ref-shonda_22-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-shonda-22">[22]</A></SUP></TD>
<TD style="width: 20px; vertical-align: bottom; border: none; color: #B2B7F2; font-size: 40px; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-weight: bold; line-height: .6em; text-align: right; padding: 10px 10px;">”</TD>
</TR>
