<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:TR_Knight_cropped.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/TR_Knight_cropped.jpg/220px-TR_Knight_cropped.jpg" width="220" height="221" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/TR_Knight_cropped.jpg/330px-TR_Knight_cropped.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d2/TR_Knight_cropped.jpg 2x" data-file-width="341" data-file-height="342" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:TR_Knight_cropped.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
McKee deemed Grey and O'Malley's sexual encounter irreversible.</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>The character had a one-night stand with George O'Malley, in the second season. Series writer Stacy McKee, said of the sexual encounter: "There’s no turning back. There’s nothing George and Meredith can do. The damage is done – things will never be the same. They’ve just changed something important in their lives FOREVER and…they are freaking out."<SUP id="cite_ref-GMSex_23-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GMSex-23">[23]</A></SUP> Grey's character development has also been known as an influence on the creation of her half-sister, Lexie Grey. Particularly, it has been made clear that they both share the same motives. McKee offered her thoughts: "Meredith and Lexie both want to succeed. They want to be strong. They want to feel normal. They want, so much, to be whole. But it’s a struggle – a genuine struggle for them. Being hardcore doesn’t come naturally. Sometimes, they have to fake it."<SUP id="cite_ref-MerLex_24-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-MerLex-24">[24]</A></SUP> Grey's personality has been compared with that of Alex Karev's. Rhimes offered the insight:</P>
<BLOCKQUOTE class="templatequote">
<P>"I like to create moments for him and Meredith. Because, in my head, they are very similar people. Even though Karev can be such an ass, even though he’s arrogant, even though he gave O'Malley the Syph. He and Meredith are both lost, both lonely, both former screw-ups who got their acts together. In another lifetime, they would be really good friends. So throughout the season, we watch them pause from time to time to look at each other and see that they are mirrors of one another.</P>
<DIV class="templatequotecite">— <CITE>Shonda Rhimes, Grey Matter<SUP id="cite_ref-AlexS_25-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-AlexS-25">[25]</A></SUP></CITE></DIV>
</BLOCKQUOTE>
<P>Pompeo fights for a truthful storyline for her character—she wants it to be realistic and says you can't always wrap it up in a neat little package.<SUP id="cite_ref-spark_26-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-spark-26">[26]</A></SUP> Referring to Grey's tampering with Shepherd's trial, Pompeo said: "Listen, what Meredith did clearly crossed a line. Derek has a right to be pissed."<SUP id="cite_ref-pissed_27-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pissed-27">[27]</A></SUP> Following the tampering, Rhimes said she believes that Grey and Shepherd are meant to be together and that it in the end, they will end up with each other.<SUP id="cite_ref-shonda_22-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-shonda-22">[22]</A></SUP> Grey's relationship with Cristina Yang, has been looked upon as "sisterhood", and Yang has repeatedly referred to Grey as "her person". This led to the two being dubbed "the twisted sisters". At the conclusion of season three, the duo went on a "honeymoon" together, and Rhimes called it her favorite detail of the finale.<SUP id="cite_ref-ChangeC_28-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ChangeC-28">[28]</A></SUP> Grey has been characterized, by some, as "whiny". Rhimes offered her insight:</P>
<TABLE class="cquote" role="presentation" style="margin:auto; border-collapse: collapse; border: none; background-color: transparent; width: auto;">
<TBODY><TR>
<TD style="width: 20px; vertical-align: top; border: none; color: #B2B7F2; font-size: 40px; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-weight: bold; line-height: .6em; text-align: left; padding: 10px 10px;">“</TD>
<TD style="vertical-align: top; border: none; padding: 4px 10px;">I've heard a lot of talk about Meredith being whiny but the truth is, she's got a mom [who died of] Alzheimer's, no other family to speak of, and the man she loves is married. She's pretty freaking lonely, people. She's got a right to get her whine on. So, when she falters, it's partly because she's got nothing to hang on to. As she says in the first episode, she needs a reason to go on, she needs some hope.<SUP id="cite_ref-Whiny_29-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Whiny-29">[29]</A></SUP></TD>
<TD style="width: 20px; vertical-align: bottom; border: none; color: #B2B7F2; font-size: 40px; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-weight: bold; line-height: .6em; text-align: right; padding: 10px 10px;">”</TD>
</TR>
</TBODY></TABLE>
<P>Rhimes felt that the <A href="/wiki/What_a_Difference_a_Day_Makes_(Grey%27s_Anatomy)" title="What a Difference a Day Makes (Grey's Anatomy)">100th episode</A> showed well Meredith's evolution throughout the show from a "dark and twisty girl" to a "happy woman". She said: "She is the thing her mother wished for her. She is extraordinary. Because, to get past the crap of your past? To move on? To let the past go and change? That is extraordinary. To love? Without fear? Without screwing it up? That is extraordinary. It makes me happy to see her happy."<SUP id="cite_ref-GreyMatter_30-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-GreyMatter-30">[30]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Following the departure of Patrick Dempsey's character, Rhimes was quoted as saying that "...Meredith and the entire Grey’s Anatomy family are about to enter uncharted territory as we head into this new chapter of her life. The possibilities for what may come are endless." <SUP id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-31">[31]</A></SUP> With at least a year left in Pompeo's contract with the show, viewers are sure to witness some of the most difficult times of Meredith's life yet.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Reception">Reception</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Meredith_Grey&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Reception">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Reviews">Reviews</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Meredith_Grey&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Reviews">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The character has received both overwhelmingly positive reviews to weary response from television critics throughout the course of the show. The initial response to the character was positive but as the series progressed Meredith Grey became immensely popular and Pompeo established the character as a critic and fan favorite featuring on a number of Top TV Character lists. The development of the character has been deemed as the highlight of the show. Grey has constantly been defined as "the heroine of <I>Grey's Anatomy</I>".<SUP id="cite_ref-heroine_32-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-heroine-32">[32]</A></SUP> At the time of inception <I><A href="/wiki/Newsday" title="Newsday">Newsday</A>'</I>s Diane Werts praised the character stating, "Like <A href="/wiki/Hugh_Laurie" title="Hugh Laurie">Hugh Laurie</A>'s irascible "House" title character, star <A href="/wiki/Ellen_Pompeo" title="Ellen Pompeo">Ellen Pompeo</A>'s newly minted Dr. Grey conveys such substance that you simply can't stop watching."<SUP id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-33">[33]</A></SUP> Ellen A. Kim of After Pompeo not receiving an Emmy nomination for her work as Grey, McNamara of the <I><A href="/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times" title="Los Angeles Times">Los Angeles Times</A></I> suggested that Pompeo, "who has worked very hard and against all narrative odds to make Meredith Grey an interesting character at last" should have received a nomination at the <A href="/wiki/61st_Primetime_Emmy_Awards" title="61st Primetime Emmy Awards">61st Primetime Emmy Awards</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-34">[34]</A></SUP> Later, during the twelfth season <I><A href="/wiki/Western_Gazette" title="Western Gazette">Western Gazette</A></I> gave <A href="/wiki/Ellen_Pompeo" title="Ellen Pompeo">Ellen Pompeo</A> the credit for carrying the show and re-ittirated." (It's) time for Pompeo to finally win an <A href="/wiki/Emmy_Award" title="Emmy Award">Emmy Award</A>."<SUP id="cite_ref-35" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-35">[35]</A></SUP> Tanner Stransky of <I><A href="/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly" title="Entertainment Weekly">Entertainment Weekly</A></I> referred to Grey as the "trusty voice over master" of <I>Grey's Anatomy</I>.</P>
<DIV class="thumb tleft">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:192px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Patrick_Dempsey_2011_(cropped).jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Patrick_Dempsey_2011_%28cropped%29.jpg/190px-Patrick_Dempsey_2011_%28cropped%29.jpg" width="190" height="253" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Patrick_Dempsey_2011_%28cropped%29.jpg/285px-Patrick_Dempsey_2011_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Patrick_Dempsey_2011_%28cropped%29.jpg/380px-Patrick_Dempsey_2011_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="888" data-file-height="1184" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Patrick_Dempsey_2011_(cropped).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
Pompeo's connection with <A href="/wiki/Patrick_Dempsey" title="Patrick Dempsey">Patrick Dempsey</A> (<A href="/wiki/Derek_Shepherd" title="Derek Shepherd">Derek Shepherd</A>) is acclaimed as a high point of the series.</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>Former television columnist for <I><A href="/wiki/The_Star-Ledger" title="The Star-Ledger">The Star-Ledger</A></I> <A href="/wiki/Alan_Sepinwall" title="Alan Sepinwall">Alan Sepinwall</A> expressed his boredom on the focus given on Grey's relationships storylines while reviewing the <A href="/wiki/Losing_My_Religion_(Grey%27s_Anatomy)" title="Losing My Religion (Grey's Anatomy)">second season's finale</A>: "On those occasions when Meredith's not involved in a plot about her love life, I do kind of like her, but those moments are so infrequent compared to her constant angsting over McDreamy -- not to mention all those seemingly unrelated storylines that always turn into a metaphor for that relationship -- that I really, really can't stand her."<SUP id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-36">[36]</A></SUP> During the show's <A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_3)" title="Grey's Anatomy (season 3)">third season</A>, the development of the character received negative reviews, with Cristopher Monfette of <I>IGN</I> stating that her storyline has become "some bizarrely under-developed sub-plot about depression and giving Derek a season's worth of reconsidering to do."<SUP id="cite_ref-ignga3_37-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ignga3-37">[37]</A></SUP> Also during the third season, Robert Rorke of the <I><A href="/wiki/New_York_Post" title="New York Post">New York Post</A></I> noted the decline in Meredith's role in the show, expressing disappointment: "She used to be the queen of the romantic dilemmas, but lately, she's been a little dopey, what with the endless McDreamy soliloquies."<SUP id="cite_ref-nypgreys_38-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-nypgreys-38">[38]</A></SUP> Similarly, <A href="/wiki/Maclean%27s" title="Maclean's">Macleans.ca</A> found their storyline in the <A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_4)" title="Grey's Anatomy (season 4)">fourth season</A> overused, "This whole 'Oh I need more time,' but 'Oh, I'm jealous if you look at someone else' angst was tired in the second season, frustrating in the third and now a total channel changer. The will-they-or-won't-they plot doesn't work because they've already been in and out of that relationship too many times. Meredith is a nag and McDreamy is henpecked."<SUP id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-39">[39]</A></SUP> On a more positive note, her relationship with Shepherd was included in <A href="/wiki/AOL_TV" title="AOL TV">AOL TV</A>'s list of the "Best TV Couples of All Time" and in the same list by <I><A href="/wiki/TV_Guide" title="TV Guide">TV Guide</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-40">[40]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-41">[41]</A></SUP> During the <A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_6)" title="Grey's Anatomy (season 6)">sixth season</A> the development of the character was praised, Glenn Diaz of <I><A href="/wiki/BuddyTV" title="BuddyTV">BuddyTV</A></I> commented that "You gotta love Mer when she's gloomy.", in addition to praising Pompeo's performance. In her review of the episode <A href="/wiki/Tainted_Obligation" title="Tainted Obligation">Tainted Obligation</A> she wrote "I felt for Meredith, but after Lexie's heartfelt begging and pleading, I was happy that Mere finally grows up and casts her selfishness aside. Three seasons ago Meredith would never have dreamed of putting Lexie first, and I was proud of her for giving up part of her liver—her offer to get to know her dad was an even bigger milestone."<SUP id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-42">[42]</A></SUP> Reviewing the first part of the <A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_8)" title="Grey's Anatomy (season 8)">eighth season</A>, TV Fanatic lauded the character and wrote: "this season belongs to Meredith Grey. She is the <I>heart and soul of the show</I> and has been outstanding. This is a character that used to be so dark and twisty and has now grown into a more mature woman. <A href="/wiki/Ellen_Pompeo" title="Ellen Pompeo">Ellen Pompeo</A> has been at the top of her game this season."<SUP id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-43">[43]</A></SUP></P>
<P><I>Wit & Fancy</I> praised the transformation of the character and stated, "Of course Meredith will still make rash decisions like when she took off with Zola, or tampered with the trial but she does things out of love and the kindness of her heart now and not because she is dark and twisty. Considering where Meredith was at the beginning and where she is now, I think she went through a remarkable journey and did more than just growing up, she finally became “all whole and healed“."<SUP id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-44">[44]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Maura O'Malley of <I><A href="/wiki/Bustle_(magazine)" title="Bustle (magazine)">Bustle</A></I> also lauded the development of the character ahead of season 12 saying, "When the series began, Meredith was just a girl sitting in a bar celebrating the exciting next phase of her life. She had graduated medical school, she was starting her residency at a prestigious hospital, and she was simply looking for a no-strings attached, one night stand. What she got instead was a complicated romantic relationship that rivals Romeo and Juliet — but the key is, she wasn't searching for love. Working and learning were — and continue to be — her priorities, while McDreamy was simply an added perk. Hopefully, the new season of Grey's Anatomy will reflect this change in tone, because Meredith is a strong, independent woman — and she will be just fine."<SUP id="cite_ref-bustle.com_45-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-bustle.com-45">[45]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Later in the series, <A href="/wiki/Ellen_Pompeo" title="Ellen Pompeo">Ellen Pompeo</A> received critical acclaim with numerous critics lauding her portrayal of the character. Reviewing the episode <A href="/wiki/She%27s_Leaving_Home_(Grey%27s_Anatomy)" title="She's Leaving Home (Grey's Anatomy)">She's Leaving Home</A> <I>CarterMatt</I> called her the "anchor" for Grey's saying, "Throughout, this was an episode completely anchored by <A href="/wiki/Ellen_Pompeo" title="Ellen Pompeo">Ellen Pompeo</A>, who has done some of her best work ever on the show the past couple of weeks. Tonight, she cried, she fought, and she learned that she was carrying his child."<SUP id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-46">[46]</A></SUP> and added that Pompeo is often "ovelooked" saying, "Her subtlety is probably why she is often overlooked."<SUP id="cite_ref-47" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-47">[47]</A></SUP> Rick Porter of <I><A href="/wiki/Zap2it" class="mw-redirect" title="Zap2it">Zap2it</A></I> reviewing "<A href="/wiki/How_to_Save_a_Life_(Grey%27s_Anatomy)" title="How to Save a Life (Grey's Anatomy)">How to Save a Life</A>" wrote, "Without Meredith, and without one of Pompeo's strongest performances in her long time on the show, "How to Save a Life" would have run the risk of coming across as a baldly manipulative death episode, the likes of which the show has done several times before. He added. "How to Save a Life" may not be the ideal <A href="/wiki/Emmy_Award" title="Emmy Award">Emmy-submission</A> episode for Pompeo, considering Meredith is off screen for more than half of it. But it's among the best work she's ever done on the show."<SUP id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-48">[48]</A></SUP> <I><A href="/wiki/USA_Today" title="USA Today">USA Today</A></I> also lauded Pompeo saying, " In some ways, the episode (<A href="/wiki/How_to_Save_a_Life_(Grey%27s_Anatomy)" title="How to Save a Life (Grey's Anatomy)">How to Save a Life</A>) was even more of a showcase for Pompeo. She had some of the more memorable and well-played scenes, from her angry response to the doctor who tries to tell her what her choices are, to her resignation when she realizes she has to comfort and motivate the young doctor whose mistakes cost Derek his life."<SUP id="cite_ref-49" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-49">[49]</A></SUP></P>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:202px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Sandra_Oh_2016.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Sandra_Oh_2016.jpg/200px-Sandra_Oh_2016.jpg" width="200" height="262" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Sandra_Oh_2016.jpg/300px-Sandra_Oh_2016.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Sandra_Oh_2016.jpg/400px-Sandra_Oh_2016.jpg 2x" data-file-width="662" data-file-height="868" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Sandra_Oh_2016.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
Mark Perigard of the <A href="/wiki/Boston_Herald" title="Boston Herald">Boston Herald</A> considered Meredith's friendship with Cristina (<A href="/wiki/Sandra_Oh" title="Sandra Oh">Sandra Oh</A>) to be "the secret core of Grey's".</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>The relation between Meredith and Cristina has been acclaimed and been a highlight of the show. Mark Perigard of the <A href="/wiki/Boston_Herald" title="Boston Herald">Boston Herald</A> considered the friendship to be "the secret core of Grey's". Aisha Harris of <I><A href="/wiki/Slate_(magazine)" title="Slate (magazine)">Slate</A></I> called their relation <I>The Best Female Friendship on TV</I> adding that "With those two characters, showrunner Shonda Rhimes and her team of writers created one of the most nuanced and realistic portrayals of female friendship on television."<SUP id="cite_ref-50" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-50">[50]</A></SUP> Samantha Highfill of <I><A href="/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly" title="Entertainment Weekly">Entertainment Weekly</A></I> called Cristina and Meredith the best female friends on TV because "they don’t try to be". There’s nothing fake about them, which is a rarity in how female friends are portrayed on television. She further went on to call them 'soulmates', " And even though they’d never dare get sappy enough to say it, they’re soul mates.<SUP id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-51">[51]</A></SUP> Margaret Lyons of <A href="/wiki/Vulture" title="Vulture">Vulture (magazine)</A> called the friendship " dream BFF relationship." and the primary focus of the show, "One of the series' calling cards has been its depiction of female friendship and particularly the primacy that friendship enjoyed over romantic relationships." <SUP id="cite_ref-52" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-52">[52]</A></SUP></P>
<TABLE class="cquote" role="presentation" style="margin:auto; border-collapse: collapse; border: none; background-color: transparent; width: auto;">
<TBODY><TR>
<TD style="width: 20px; vertical-align: top; border: none; color: #B2B7F2; font-size: 40px; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-weight: bold; line-height: .6em; text-align: left; padding: 10px 10px;">“</TD>
<TD style="vertical-align: top; border: none; padding: 4px 10px;">"I wanted to create a world in which you felt as if you were watching very real women. Most of the women I saw on TV didn't seem like people I actually knew. They felt like ideas of what women are. They never got to be nasty or competitive or hungry or angry. They were often just the loving wife or the nice friend. But who gets to be the bitch? Who gets to be the three-dimensional woman?" - <A href="/wiki/Shonda_Rhimes" title="Shonda Rhimes">Rhimes</A> on Cristina-Meredith friendship.<SUP id="cite_ref-53" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-53">[53]</A></SUP></TD>
<TD style="width: 20px; vertical-align: bottom; border: none; color: #B2B7F2; font-size: 40px; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-weight: bold; line-height: .6em; text-align: right; padding: 10px 10px;">”</TD>
</TR>
</TBODY></TABLE>
<P><I><A href="/wiki/E!" title="E!">E!</A></I> at the time of <A href="/wiki/Sandra_Oh" title="Sandra Oh">Sandra Oh</A>'s exit wrote, "In <A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy" title="Grey's Anatomy">Grey's Anatomy</A>'s 10-year history, the doctor duo has been through a lot together: weddings, deaths, plane crashes, bomb threats, shooting, you name it, they've lived (and danced) through it. " and added, "And with the three words, <I>"You're my person."</I> <A href="/wiki/Cristina_Yang" title="Cristina Yang">Cristina Yang</A> and Meredith Grey solidified their status as the small screen's best best friends ever."<SUP id="cite_ref-54" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-54">[54]</A></SUP> Marama Whyte of <I>Hypable</I> wrote, "Critically, the key relationship in Meredith’s life was not her romance with <A href="/wiki/Derek_Shepherd" title="Derek Shepherd">Derek Shepherd</A>, but her passionate, indestructible, absolutely enviable friendship with Cristina. Talk about relationship goals; who wants McDreamy when Cristina Yang could be your person. These two were the real powerhouse, and <A href="/wiki/Shonda_Rhimes" title="Shonda Rhimes">Shonda Rhimes</A> didn’t shy away from making the audience remember this. Derek was the love of her life, but Cristina was her soul mate. More than anyone else, Cristina challenged Meredith, was honest with her, and inspired her. For these reasons, it was Cristina who was constantly the source of Meredith’s character development, not Derek."<SUP id="cite_ref-hypable.com_55-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-hypable.com-55">[55]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Pompeo's character has also been used to define the image a strong woman, <I><A href="/wiki/Bustle_(magazine)" title="Bustle (magazine)">Bustle</A></I> previewing the 12th season wrote, "Meredith Grey has always been capable of being on her own. Grey's Anatomy is about Meredith's journey. Men and romantic interests are a part of her life, but they are not the priority. She doesn't need McDreamy. Grey's Anatomy doesn't need McDreamy. So even if the writers do decide to create a new love interest for Ms. Grey (<A href="/wiki/Martin_Henderson" title="Martin Henderson">Martin Henderson</A>, perhaps?), it wouldn't matter. I have faith that the show's writers will do this storyline justice, because TV needs more strong single women — and Meredith seems like the perfect candidate." The site added, "This past season was almost a trial run for a McDreamy-less Grey's Anatomy. When Derek left for Washington D.C. to pursue his research, Meredith stayed behind and focused on her own career. She didn't chase him. Her priority were her children and the Grey Sloan Memorial Hospital. Meredith showed that she would never put aside her own dreams and aspirations for a man, and I believe that this won't change after Derek's death."<SUP id="cite_ref-bustle.com_45-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-bustle.com-45">[45]</A></SUP></P>

Pompeo's failure to garner an <A href="/wiki/Emmy_Award" title="Emmy Award">Emmy Award</A> nomination has been called a "snub" on multiple occasions.</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>Pompeo has won and has been nominated for multiple awards for her portrayal of Grey. She and the <I>Grey's Anatomy</I> cast won <A href="/wiki/Satellite_Award_for_Best_Cast_%E2%80%93_Television_Series" title="Satellite Award for Best Cast – Television Series">Best Ensemble in a Television Series</A> at the <A href="/wiki/Satellite_Awards_2006" class="mw-redirect" title="Satellite Awards 2006">2006 Satellite Awards</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-56" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-56">[56]</A></SUP> During <A href="/wiki/Satellite_Awards_2007" class="mw-redirect" title="Satellite Awards 2007">the following year's ceremony</A>, she was named <A href="/wiki/Satellite_Award_for_Best_Actress_%E2%80%93_Television_Series_Drama" title="Satellite Award for Best Actress – Television Series Drama">Best Actress in a Television Drama Series</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-57">[57]</A></SUP> She was among the <I>Grey's Anatomy</I> cast members awarded the <A href="/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_an_Ensemble_in_a_Drama_Series" title="Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series">Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series</A> accolade at the <A href="/wiki/13th_Screen_Actors_Guild_Awards" title="13th Screen Actors Guild Awards">13th Screen Actors Guild Awards</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-58">[58]</A></SUP> and received nominations in the same category in 2006<SUP id="cite_ref-59" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-59">[59]</A></SUP> and 2008.<SUP id="cite_ref-60" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-60">[60]</A></SUP> Pompeo received a <A href="/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_%E2%80%93_Television_Series_Drama" title="Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Television Series Drama">Best Performance by an Actress in a Drama Series</A> nomination at the <A href="/wiki/64th_Golden_Globe_Awards" title="64th Golden Globe Awards">64th Golden Globe Awards</A> – the program won <A href="/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Television_Series_%E2%80%93_Drama" title="Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Drama">Best Drama Series</A> at the same ceremony.<SUP id="cite_ref-61" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-61">[61]</A></SUP> Also in 2007, Pompeo and the female cast and crew of <I>Grey's Anatomy</I> received the <A href="/wiki/Women_in_Film_Crystal_%2B_Lucy_Awards" title="Women in Film Crystal + Lucy Awards">Women in Film Lucy Award</A>, which honors those "whose work in television has positively influenced attitudes toward women."<SUP id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-62">[62]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Pompeo's performance has garnered her multiple <A href="/wiki/People%27s_Choice_Award" class="mw-redirect" title="People's Choice Award">People's Choice Awards</A>. At the <A href="/wiki/37th_People%27s_Choice_Awards" title="37th People's Choice Awards">37th People's Choice Awards</A>, she was nominated against Dempsey and Oh in the Favorite TV Doctor category,<SUP id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-63">[63]</A></SUP> and <A href="/wiki/38th_People%27s_Choice_Awards" title="38th People's Choice Awards">the following year</A>, she was a contender in the Favorite TV Drama Actress category.<SUP id="cite_ref-64" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-64">[64]</A></SUP> Since 2012 Pompeo has received nomination at the <A href="/wiki/People%27s_Choice_Awards" title="People's Choice Awards">People's Choice Awards</A> every year in two categories at <A href="/wiki/40th_People%27s_Choice_Awards" title="40th People's Choice Awards">40th People's Choice Awards</A> alongside <A href="/wiki/Patrick_Dempsey" title="Patrick Dempsey">Patrick Dempsey</A> and <A href="/wiki/Sandra_Oh" title="Sandra Oh">Sandra Oh</A> respectively. She won the <A href="/wiki/People%27s_Choice_Awards" title="People's Choice Awards">Best Drama Actress Award</A> at both the <A href="/wiki/39th_People%27s_Choice_Awards" title="39th People's Choice Awards">39th People's Choice Awards</A><SUP id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-65">[65]</A></SUP> and the <A href="/wiki/41st_People%27s_Choice_Awards" title="41st People's Choice Awards">41st People's Choice Awards</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-66" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-66">[66]</A></SUP> In 2007, show-business awards reporter Tom O'Neil commented that Pompeo was overdue an <A href="/wiki/Emmy_Award" title="Emmy Award">Emmy Award</A> nomination for her role in <I>Grey's Anatomy</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-67" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-67">[67]</A></SUP> Readers of O'Neil's awards website, <I>The Envelope</I>, included Pompeo in their 2009 nominations for Best Drama Actress in the site's Gold Derby TV Awards.<SUP id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-68">[68]</A></SUP> <I>Entertainment Weekly</I> launched the <A href="/wiki/EWwy_Awards" class="mw-redirect" title="EWwy Awards">EWwy Awards</A> in 2008, to honor actors who have not received Emmy nominations. Pompeo was nominated in the Best Actress in a Drama Series category, and placed fourth, with 19 percent of readers' votes.<SUP id="cite_ref-69" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-69">[69]</A></SUP></P>

<P><I><B>The Longest Yard</B></I> is a 2005 American <A href="/wiki/Sports_film" title="Sports film">sports</A> <A href="/wiki/Prison_film" title="Prison film">prison</A> <A href="/wiki/Comedy_film" title="Comedy film">comedy film</A> and a <A href="/wiki/Remake" title="Remake">remake</A> of the 1974 <A href="/wiki/The_Longest_Yard_(1974_film)" title="The Longest Yard (1974 film)">film of the same name</A>. <A href="/wiki/Adam_Sandler" title="Adam Sandler">Adam Sandler</A> plays the protagonist Paul Crewe, a disgraced former professional quarterback for the <A href="/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers" title="Pittsburgh Steelers">Pittsburgh Steelers</A>, who is forced to form a team from the prison inmates to play <A href="/wiki/American_football" title="American football">football</A> against their guards.
</P><P><A href="/wiki/Burt_Reynolds" title="Burt Reynolds">Burt Reynolds</A>, who played Sandler's role in the original, co-stars as Nate Scarborough, the inmates' coach. <A href="/wiki/Chris_Rock" title="Chris Rock">Chris Rock</A> plays Crewe's friend, known as Caretaker. The cast includes <A href="/wiki/James_Cromwell" title="James Cromwell">James Cromwell</A>, <A href="/wiki/Nelly" title="Nelly">Nelly</A>, <A href="/wiki/William_Fichtner" title="William Fichtner">William Fichtner</A> and several former and current professional athletes such as <A href="/wiki/Terry_Crews" title="Terry Crews">Terry Crews</A>, <A href="/wiki/Michael_Irvin" title="Michael Irvin">Michael Irvin</A>, <A href="/wiki/Brian_Bosworth" title="Brian Bosworth">Brian Bosworth</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bill_Romanowski" title="Bill Romanowski">Bill Romanowski</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bill_Goldberg" title="Bill Goldberg">Bill Goldberg</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bob_Sapp" title="Bob Sapp">Bob Sapp</A>, <A href="/wiki/Kevin_Nash" title="Kevin Nash">Kevin Nash</A>, <A href="/wiki/Stone_Cold_Steve_Austin" title="Stone Cold Steve Austin">Stone Cold Steve Austin</A>, and <A href="/wiki/The_Great_Khali" title="The Great Khali">Dalip "The Great Khali" Singh Rana</A>. The film was produced by <A href="/wiki/MTV_Films" title="MTV Films">MTV Films</A> and <A href="/wiki/Happy_Madison_Productions" title="Happy Madison Productions">Happy Madison Productions</A> and distributed by <A href="/wiki/Paramount_Pictures" title="Paramount Pictures">Paramount Pictures</A> and <A href="/wiki/Columbia_Pictures" title="Columbia Pictures">Columbia Pictures</A>, and was released on May 27, 2005.
</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Plot">Plot</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Longest_Yard_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Plot">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<TABLE class="plainlinks metadata ambox ambox-style ambox-Plot" role="presentation"><TBODY><TR><TD class="mbox-image"><DIV style="width:52px"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/f/f2/Edit-clear.svg/40px-Edit-clear.svg.png" width="40" height="40" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/f/f2/Edit-clear.svg/60px-Edit-clear.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/f/f2/Edit-clear.svg/80px-Edit-clear.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="48" data-file-height="48" /></DIV></TD><TD class="mbox-text"><DIV class="mbox-text-span">This article's plot summary <B>may be <A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:How_to_write_a_plot_summary" title="Wikipedia:How to write a plot summary">too long or excessively detailed</A>.</B><SPAN class="hide-when-compact"> Please <A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Longest_Yard_(2005_film)&action=edit">help improve it</A> by removing unnecessary details and making it more concise.</SPAN>  <SMALL><I>(September 2015)</I></SMALL><SMALL class="hide-when-compact"><I> (<A href="/wiki/Help:Maintenance_template_removal" title="Help:Maintenance template removal">Learn how and when to remove this template message</A>)</I></SMALL></DIV></TD></TR></TBODY></TABLE>
<P>Paul Crewe is a former <A href="/wiki/National_Football_League" title="National Football League">NFL</A> player who, one night, gets drunk and goes <A href="/wiki/Joyride_(crime)" title="Joyride (crime)">joyriding</A> in the <A href="/wiki/Bentley" title="Bentley">Bentley</A> of his girlfriend Lena, crashing it. It is revealed that he was accused of <A href="/wiki/Shaving_points" class="mw-redirect" title="Shaving points">shaving points</A> in a big game, although it was never proven.
</P><P>In prison, Warden Rudolph Hazen, wishing to boost his prison's reputation for future elections as State Governor, uses threats and confinement in a <A href="/wiki/Box_(torture)" title="Box (torture)">hot box</A> to coerce Crewe into helping the prison guards' football team, led by the hostile Captain Knauer. Crewe informs Hazen that what Hazen's team needs is a tune-up game to boost the guards' confidence, and is therefore coerced to form an inmate team to play against the guards. He does so with the help of a newfound friend, Caretaker. They start off with a poorly organized team, before being noticed by another prisoner, former college football star Nate Scarborough, who decides to help coach the team by gathering several intimidating inmates as a boost to the team's strength.
</P><P>Caretaker tells Crewe that they need more <A href="/wiki/African_American" class="mw-redirect" title="African American">"brothers"</A> on the team. When Crewe goes to the basketball court to ask the black inmates to join the team, their leader, Deacon Moss rebuffs him. Crewe challenges Deacon to a one-on-one basketball game, saying that if he wins, the brothers will join the team, and if Deacon wins, Crewe will leave them alone. Deacon accepts, and despite Deacon's undisguised <A href="/wiki/Personal_foul_(basketball)" title="Personal foul (basketball)">personal fouls</A> in which he elbows, punches or grabs Crewe, Crewe continues without complaint. On the game-winning shot, Crewe cleanly steals the ball from Deacon and scores, but Deacon calls a foul. Realizing he won't be allowed to win, Crewe lets Deacon score the final shot. Although Deacon beats Crewe, one of the brothers, a fast runner named Earl Megget, impressed with Crewe's decision to take the beating, joins the football team as its <A href="/wiki/Running_back" title="Running back">running back</A>. When the guards learn of this, they confront Earl in an attempt to provoke an assault by him by saying the racial epithet "<A href="/wiki/Nigger" title="Nigger">nigger</A>", but Earl does not allow himself to be provoked despite intimidation and minor abuse. Having witnessed this, the other "brothers", including Deacon, decide to join the team too.
</P><P>Hazen and the guards continue attempts to hinder Crewe's team by flooding their field, but the team decides to practice in the mud anyway.
</P><P>Inmate Unger spies on the activities of the inmates and after being pressured by the guards, rigs Crewe’s radio with an explosive. Caretaker unknowingly enters the cell to give a photo gift to Crewe, but is killed when he tries to turn the dial on the radio.
</P><P>On game day, the inmates are revitalized in the wake of Caretaker's murder when Crewe reveals Caretaker's last gift to the team, quality gear and uniforms from his cousin at <A href="/wiki/Reebok" title="Reebok">Reebok</A> with the team name "Mean Machine" on the uniforms. The Mean Machine overcomes a rough start, due to individual inmates' attempts to retaliate against guards for the abuse they've suffered. Crewe angrily tells the inmates that winning the game is more important and will damage the guards more than their personal grudges, and gets them to play as a team. The first half ends with the score tied. The angered Hazen informs Crewe in private that if he does not lose he will be charged for Caretaker's murder. Crewe acquiesces to Hazen's threat, asking that the guards refrain from using excessive force on the field after getting a comfortable lead, to which Hazen agrees to do so after they obtain a two touchdown lead. After Crewe fakes an injury in order to leave the field, his teammates voice their displeasure over his obvious deserting of the team.
</P><P>After seeing that Hazen has broken his promise and two members of the Mean Machine are injured, Crewe asks Skitchy if the time spent in jail for punching the warden was worth it. Skitchy replies, "It was worth every goddamn second," and inspired Crewe returns to the field. The team initially doubts Crewe’s resolve and allows him to be sacked twice. After running for a first down on 4th and Long, Crewe, realizing that his inmates are still not protecting him due to his prior actions, calls a huddle, admits to the point shaving that disgraced him, the injury that he faked as a result of Hazen's threat, and sabotage to the other inmates, and asks for their forgiveness, putting his hands in the middle of all of them. Moss puts his hand in, followed by the rest of the team.
</P><P>The Mean Machine, united again as a team, quickly scores two touchdowns to cut the guards' lead to 35–28. After Megget is injured following a long run, Scarborough comes in for one play as replacement and scores a touchdown off a trick play involving a fumble called a <A href="/wiki/Fumblerooski" title="Fumblerooski">Fumblerooski</A>. Mean Machine decides to go for the two-point conversion and the win. As they get up to the line they seem to be confused, and Crewe and Scarborough start arguing in order to trick the guards. Moss gets the snap and passes it to Crewe, who scores the winning conversion, winning the game. Knauer, with a newfound respect for Crewe, tells him that he showed extraordinary nerve, and lets him know that he will vouch that Crewe had nothing to do with Caretaker's death.
</P><P>Hazen admonishes Knauer for losing a fixed game and notices that Crewe is heading towards the exit. Eagerly implying Crewe is trying to escape, Hazen orders that Crewe be shot for attempting to escape. Knauer hesitates and at the last moment realizes (and scornfully tells Hazen) that Crewe is only picking up the game football. Crewe returns it to Hazen, telling him to "stick it in [his] trophy case." Moss and Joey Battle give Hazen a <A href="/wiki/Gatorade_shower" title="Gatorade shower">Gatorade shower</A>, and when he tells them that this has earned them a week in the hot box, Battle defiantly yells "Who gives a shit?!"
</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Production">Production</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Longest_Yard_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Production">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The movie was filmed at the <A href="/wiki/Penitentiary_of_New_Mexico" title="Penitentiary of New Mexico">New Mexico State Penitentiary</A> on Route 14, <A href="/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico" title="Santa Fe, New Mexico">Santa Fe, New Mexico</A>. The football game at the end of the film was filmed at <A href="/wiki/El_Camino_College#Murdock_Stadium" title="El Camino College">Murdock Stadium</A> at the El Camino College in <A href="/wiki/Torrance,_California" title="Torrance, California">Torrance, California</A>. The car chase scene was filmed whereabouts in <A href="/wiki/Long_Beach,_California" title="Long Beach, California">Long Beach, California</A>. Other parts of the film were filmed in Los Angeles and <A href="/wiki/New_Mexico" title="New Mexico">New Mexico</A>.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2014)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> The golf course scene was filmed at Lost Canyons Golf Club in <A href="/wiki/Simi_Valley,_California" title="Simi Valley, California">Simi Valley, California</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Reception">Reception</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Longest_Yard_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Reception">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Box_office">Box office</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Longest_Yard_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Box office">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The film did well at the box office. Its $47.6 million opening weekend was the largest of Sandler's career and only second to <I><A href="/wiki/The_Day_After_Tomorrow" title="The Day After Tomorrow">The Day After Tomorrow</A></I> as the largest opening by a movie that was not #1. The film would go on to gross $158.1 million in the United States and Canada and $190 million worldwide. It was the highest-grossing film produced by <A href="/wiki/MTV_Films" title="MTV Films">MTV Films</A>, until it was surpassed by <I><A href="/wiki/Hansel_and_Gretel:_Witch_Hunters" class="mw-redirect" title="Hansel and Gretel: Witch Hunters">Hansel and Gretel: Witch Hunters</A></I>. Despite the large number of remakes released at the theaters, it's worth noting that <I>The Longest Yard</I> is the highest grossing comedy remake of the modern box office era (from 1980 on).<SUP id="cite_ref-mojo-remake_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-mojo-remake-3">[3]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Critical_response">Critical response <SPAN id="Critics"></SPAN></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Longest_Yard_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Critical response">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>On <A href="/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes" title="Rotten Tomatoes">Rotten Tomatoes</A>, the film has an approval rating of 32% based on 165 reviews, with an average rating of 4.8/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "This <I>Yard</I> has some laughs but missing from this remake is the edginess of the original." On <A href="/wiki/Metacritic" title="Metacritic">Metacritic</A>, the film has a weighted average score of 48 out of 100, based on 35 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews". According to <A href="/wiki/CinemaScore" title="CinemaScore">CinemaScore</A>, audiences gave the film a grade of "A−" on an A+ to F scale.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP>
</P><P><A href="/wiki/Roger_Ebert" title="Roger Ebert">Roger Ebert</A>, in the critical minority with this title, gave it a "Thumbs Up", defending it later in his <I><A href="/wiki/Chicago_Sun-Times" title="Chicago Sun-Times">Chicago Sun-Times</A></I> review as a film that "...more or less achieves what most of the people attending it will expect." In the print review, Ebert beseeches his readers to "...seek out a movie you could have an interesting conversation about", citing films not in wide release such as <I><A href="/wiki/Dominion:_Prequel_to_the_Exorcist" title="Dominion: Prequel to the Exorcist">Dominion: Prequel to the Exorcist</A></I> and <I><A href="/wiki/Kontroll" title="Kontroll">Kontroll</A></I>, until finally encouraging his readers to "drop any thought of seeing anything else instead" if they can see <I><A href="/wiki/Crash_(2004_film)" title="Crash (2004 film)">Crash</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-ebert_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ebert-5">[5]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Awards">Awards</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Longest_Yard_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Awards">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The film earned Chris Rock a <A href="/wiki/BET" title="BET">BET</A> Comedy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Theatrical Film.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (November 2014)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>
</P><P>Burt Reynolds earned a <A href="/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Award" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden Raspberry Award">Golden Raspberry Award</A> nomination for Worst Supporting Actor for his performance in the film.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (November 2014)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Soundtrack">Soundtrack</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Longest_Yard_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Soundtrack">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/The_Longest_Yard_(soundtrack)" title="The Longest Yard (soundtrack)">The Longest Yard (soundtrack)</A></DIV>
<P>The official soundtrack, which consisted entirely of hip-hop music, was released on May 24, 2005 by <A href="/wiki/Universal_Records" class="mw-redirect" title="Universal Records">Universal Records</A>. It peaked at 11 on the <A href="/wiki/Billboard_200" title="Billboard 200"><I>Billboard</I> 200</A> and 10 on the <A href="/wiki/Top_R%26B/Hip-Hop_Albums" title="Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums">Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums</A>.
</P><P>The film itself contains a mixture of hip hop and rock music, featuring music by <A href="/wiki/Creedence_Clearwater_Revival" title="Creedence Clearwater Revival">Creedence Clearwater Revival</A>, <A href="/wiki/Norman_Greenbaum" title="Norman Greenbaum">Norman Greenbaum</A> and <A href="/wiki/AC/DC" title="AC/DC">AC/DC</A> among others.
</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Early_life">Early life</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Joanna_Going&action=edit&section=1&editintro=Template:BLP_editintro" title="Edit section: Early life">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>She was born in Washington, DC, the oldest of six children of a lawyer/state assemblyman father and a police dispatcher mother.<SUP id="cite_ref-filmr_1-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-filmr-1">[1]</A></SUP> Raised in <A href="/wiki/Newport,_Rhode_Island" title="Newport, Rhode Island">Newport, Rhode Island</A>, she graduated from <A href="/wiki/Rogers_High_School_(Newport,_Rhode_Island)" class="mw-redirect" title="Rogers High School (Newport, Rhode Island)">Rogers High School</A> in 1981, then attended <A href="/wiki/Emerson_College" title="Emerson College">Emerson College</A> for two years before studying at the <A href="/wiki/American_Academy_of_Dramatic_Arts" title="American Academy of Dramatic Arts">American Academy of Dramatic Arts</A>.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2012)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Career">Career</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Joanna_Going&action=edit&section=2&editintro=Template:BLP_editintro" title="Edit section: Career">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Going appeared in soap opera roles in the late 1980s, most notably as Lisa Grady on <I><A href="/wiki/Another_World_(TV_series)" title="Another World (TV series)">Another World</A></I> from 1987 to 1989.<SUP id="cite_ref-yah_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-yah-2">[2]</A></SUP> She went on to portray lead character <A href="/wiki/Victoria_Winters" title="Victoria Winters">Victoria Winters</A> in the 1991 primetime series <I><A href="/wiki/Dark_Shadows_(1991_TV_series)" title="Dark Shadows (1991 TV series)">Dark Shadows</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-yah_2-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-yah-2">[2]</A></SUP> Going later starred in short-lived television series <I><A href="/wiki/Going_to_Extremes" title="Going to Extremes">Going to Extremes</A></I> and guest-starred on <I><A href="/wiki/Columbo" title="Columbo">Columbo</A></I>, <I><A href="/wiki/Spin_City" title="Spin City">Spin City</A></I>, <I><A href="/wiki/The_Outer_Limits_(1995_TV_series)" title="The Outer Limits (1995 TV series)">The Outer Limits</A></I>, and <I><A href="/wiki/Law_%26_Order" title="Law & Order">Law & Order</A></I>.</P>
<P>Going starred in a number of feature films. She made her film debut in <I><A href="/wiki/Wyatt_Earp_(film)" title="Wyatt Earp (film)">Wyatt Earp</A></I> (1994) as <A href="/wiki/Josephine_Earp" title="Josephine Earp">Josephine Marcus</A>, and later had major roles in <I>Eden</I>, <I><A href="/wiki/Keys_to_Tulsa" title="Keys to Tulsa">Keys to Tulsa</A></I>, <I><A href="/wiki/Inventing_the_Abbotts" title="Inventing the Abbotts">Inventing the Abbotts</A></I>, and <I><A href="/wiki/Still_Breathing_(film)" title="Still Breathing (film)">Still Breathing</A></I>. Her biggest role may be in the 1998 film version of <I><A href="/wiki/Phantoms_(film)" title="Phantoms (film)">Phantoms</A></I>. In the 2000s, she starred in several television films and guest-starred on <I><A href="/wiki/CSI:_Crime_Scene_Investigation" title="CSI: Crime Scene Investigation">CSI: Crime Scene Investigation</A></I>, <I><A href="/wiki/Criminal_Minds" title="Criminal Minds">Criminal Minds</A></I>, and <I><A href="/wiki/Mad_Men" title="Mad Men">Mad Men</A></I>. She also appeared opposite <A href="/wiki/Sean_Penn" title="Sean Penn">Sean Penn</A> in the 2011 film <I><A href="/wiki/The_Tree_of_Life_(film)" title="The Tree of Life (film)">The Tree of Life</A></I>, her first role in a major motion picture since 2003's <I><A href="/wiki/Runaway_Jury" title="Runaway Jury">Runaway Jury</A></I>. In 2014, Going starred as First Lady Tricia Walker in the second season of <A href="/wiki/Netflix" title="Netflix">Netflix</A> political series <I><A href="/wiki/House_of_Cards_(U.S._TV_series)" title="House of Cards (U.S. TV series)">House of Cards</A></I>. She later was cast in the <A href="/wiki/DirecTV" title="DirecTV">DirecTV</A> series <I><A href="/wiki/Kingdom_(2014_TV_series)" class="mw-redirect" title="Kingdom (2014 TV series)">Kingdom</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Going appeared on <A href="/wiki/Ken_Reid_(comedian)" title="Ken Reid (comedian)">Ken Reid</A>'s <I>TV Guidance Counselor</I> podcast on March 25, 2016.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Personal_life">Personal life</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Joanna_Going&action=edit&section=3&editintro=Template:BLP_editintro" title="Edit section: Personal life">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Going married actor <A href="/wiki/Dylan_Walsh" title="Dylan Walsh">Dylan Walsh</A> on October 10, 2004. They have a daughter, Stella Haven. On December 15, 2010, Walsh announced he had filed for divorce.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> The divorce was finalized in December 2012.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP></P>

<P>"<B>Can't Take My Eyes Off You</B>" is a <A href="/wiki/1967_in_music" title="1967 in music">1967</A> single credited to <A href="/wiki/Frankie_Valli" title="Frankie Valli">Frankie Valli</A>. The song was among his biggest hits, earning a <A href="/wiki/Music_recording_sales_certification" title="Music recording sales certification">gold record</A> and reaching No. 2 on the <A href="/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100" title="Billboard Hot 100"><I>Billboard</I> Hot 100</A> for a week, stuck behind "<A href="/wiki/Windy" title="Windy">Windy</A>" by <A href="/wiki/The_Association" title="The Association">The Association</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> It was co-written by <A href="/wiki/Bob_Gaudio" title="Bob Gaudio">Bob Gaudio</A>, a bandmate of Valli's in <A href="/wiki/The_Four_Seasons_(band)" title="The Four Seasons (band)">The Four Seasons</A>. It was Valli's biggest solo hit until he hit #1 in 1974 with "<A href="/wiki/My_Eyes_Adored_You" title="My Eyes Adored You">My Eyes Adored You</A>".<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>
<P>"Can't Take My Eyes Off You" has had hundreds of <A href="/wiki/Cover_version" title="Cover version">cover versions</A>, many of which have been on the charts in different countries. The song is a staple of television and film soundtracks, even being featured as part of the plot of some films, such as when the lead characters sing or arrange their own version of the song. Its chorus has also become a popular <A href="/wiki/Football_chant" title="Football chant">football chant</A>, with supporters of various teams inserting their club's name or a popular player's name into the beat (for instance, <A href="/wiki/A.S._Roma" title="A.S. Roma">A.S. Roma</A> fans sing "<A href="/wiki/Francesco_Totti" title="Francesco Totti">Francesco Totti</A>, la la, la la la la!"). The Valli version was also used by <A href="/wiki/NASA" title="NASA">NASA</A> as a wake-up song for <A href="/wiki/STS-126#Wake-up_calls" title="STS-126">a mission of the Space Shuttle</A>, on the anniversary of astronaut <A href="/wiki/Christopher_Ferguson" title="Christopher Ferguson">Christopher Ferguson</A>.</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Credits">Credits</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Can%27t_Take_My_Eyes_Off_You&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Credits">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The song was written by <A href="/wiki/Bob_Crewe" title="Bob Crewe">Bob Crewe</A> and <A href="/wiki/Bob_Gaudio" title="Bob Gaudio">Bob Gaudio</A>. Arrangement was done by <A href="/wiki/Artie_Schroeck" title="Artie Schroeck">Artie Schroeck</A> and Gaudio.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP> The original recording was made at A&R Recording Studios at 799 7th Avenue, with Bob Crewe producing and <A href="/wiki/Phil_Ramone" title="Phil Ramone">Phil Ramone</A> as the engineer.</P>
