<P>Following the end of the Cold War, the <A href="/wiki/European_Economic_Community" title="European Economic Community">European Economic Community</A> pushed for closer integration, co-operation in foreign and home affairs, and started to increase its membership into the neutral and former communist countries. In 1993, the <A href="/wiki/Maastricht_Treaty" title="Maastricht Treaty">Maastricht Treaty</A> established the <A href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</A>, succeeding the EEC and furthering political co-operation. The neutral countries of Austria, Finland and Sweden acceded to the EU, and those that didn't join were tied into the EU's economic market via the <A href="/wiki/European_Economic_Area" title="European Economic Area">European Economic Area</A>. These countries also entered the <A href="/wiki/Schengen_Agreement" title="Schengen Agreement">Schengen Agreement</A> which lifted border controls between member states.<SUP id="cite_ref-Europa_History_90-99_138-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Europa_History_90-99-138">[138]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The Maastricht Treaty created a single currency for most EU members. The <I><A href="/wiki/Euro" title="Euro">euro</A></I> was created in 1999 and replaced all previous currencies in participating states in 2002. The most notable exception to the currency union, or <I><A href="/wiki/Eurozone" title="Eurozone">eurozone</A></I>, was the United Kingdom, which also did not sign the Schengen Agreement.</P>
<P>EU did not participate in the <A href="/wiki/Yugoslav_Wars" title="Yugoslav Wars">Yugoslav Wars</A>, and was divided on supporting the United States in the 2003–2011 <A href="/wiki/Iraq_War" title="Iraq War">Iraq War</A>. NATO has been part of the <A href="/wiki/War_in_Afghanistan_(2001%E2%80%93present)" title="War in Afghanistan (2001–present)">war in Afghanistan</A>, but at a much lower level of involvement than the United States.</P>
<P>In 2004, the EU <A href="/wiki/2004_enlargement_of_the_European_Union" title="2004 enlargement of the European Union">gained 10 new members</A>. (<A href="/wiki/Estonia" title="Estonia">Estonia</A>, <A href="/wiki/Latvia" title="Latvia">Latvia</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Lithuania" title="Lithuania">Lithuania</A>, which had been part of the Soviet Union; <A href="/wiki/Czech_Republic" title="Czech Republic">Czech Republic</A>, <A href="/wiki/Hungary" title="Hungary">Hungary</A>, <A href="/wiki/Poland" title="Poland">Poland</A>, <A href="/wiki/Slovakia" title="Slovakia">Slovakia</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Slovenia" title="Slovenia">Slovenia</A>, five former-communist countries; <A href="/wiki/Malta" title="Malta">Malta</A>, and the divided island of <A href="/wiki/Cyprus" title="Cyprus">Cyprus</A>.) These were followed by <A href="/wiki/2007_enlargement_of_the_European_Union" title="2007 enlargement of the European Union">Bulgaria and Romania in 2007</A>. Russia's regime had interpreted these expansions as violations against NATO's promise to not expand "one inch to the east" in 1990.<SUP id="cite_ref-139" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-139">[139]</A></SUP> Russia engaged in a number of bilateral disputes about gas supplies with <A href="/wiki/Belarus" title="Belarus">Belarus</A> and <A href="/wiki/Ukraine" title="Ukraine">Ukraine</A> which endangered gas supplies to Europe. Russia also engaged in a <A href="/wiki/Russo-Georgian_War" title="Russo-Georgian War">minor war with Georgia</A> in 2008.</P>
<P>Supported by the United States and some European countries, <A href="/wiki/Kosovo" title="Kosovo">Kosovo</A>'s government <A href="/wiki/2008_Kosovo_declaration_of_independence" title="2008 Kosovo declaration of independence">unilaterally declared independence</A> from Serbia on 17 February 2008.</P>
<P>Public opinion in the EU turned against enlargement, partially due to what was seen as over-eager expansion including Turkey gaining candidate status. The <A href="/wiki/Treaty_establishing_a_Constitution_for_Europe" title="Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe">European Constitution</A> was rejected <A href="/wiki/Referendums_related_to_the_European_Union" title="Referendums related to the European Union">in France and the Netherlands</A>, and then (as the <A href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Lisbon" title="Treaty of Lisbon">Treaty of Lisbon</A>) in Ireland, although a second vote passed in Ireland in 2009.</P>
<P>The <A href="/wiki/Financial_crisis_of_2007%E2%80%9308" class="mw-redirect" title="Financial crisis of 2007–08">financial crisis of 2007–08</A> <A href="/wiki/Great_Recession" title="Great Recession">effected</A> Europe, and government responded with <A href="/wiki/Anti-austerity_movement" title="Anti-austerity movement">austerity measures</A>. Limited <A href="/wiki/National_accounts" title="National accounts">ability</A> of the smaller EU nations (most notably <A href="/wiki/Economy_of_Greece#2010–present_government_debt_crisis" title="Economy of Greece">Greece</A>) to handle their debts led to social unrest, government liquidation, and financial insolvency. In May 2010, the German parliament agreed to loan 22.4 billion euros to Greece over three years, with the stipulation that Greece follow strict austerity measures. See <A href="/wiki/European_sovereign-debt_crisis" class="mw-redirect" title="European sovereign-debt crisis">European sovereign-debt crisis</A>.</P>
<P>Beginning in 2014, <A href="/wiki/Ukraine" title="Ukraine">Ukraine</A> has been in a <A href="/wiki/2014_Ukrainian_revolution" title="2014 Ukrainian revolution">state of revolution</A> and unrest with two breakaway regions (<A href="/wiki/Donetsk" title="Donetsk">Donetsk</A> and <A href="/wiki/Lugansk" class="mw-redirect" title="Lugansk">Lugansk</A>) attempting to join <A href="/wiki/Russia" title="Russia">Russia</A> as full <A href="/wiki/Federal_subjects_of_Russia" title="Federal subjects of Russia">federal subjects</A>. (<I>See <A href="/wiki/War_in_Donbass" title="War in Donbass">War in Donbass</A>.</I>) On 16 March, a <A href="/wiki/Crimean_status_referendum,_2014" title="Crimean status referendum, 2014">referendum</A> was held in <A href="/wiki/Crimea" title="Crimea">Crimea</A> leading to the <I><A href="/wiki/De_facto" title="De facto">de facto</A></I> secession of Crimea and its largely internationally unrecognized <A href="/wiki/Annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Federation" title="Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation">annexation</A> to the Russian Federation as the <A href="/wiki/Republic_of_Crimea" title="Republic of Crimea">Republic of Crimea</A>.</P>
<P>The future of the EU was plunged into doubt in June 2016 when a <A href="/wiki/United_Kingdom_European_Union_membership_referendum,_2016" title="United Kingdom European Union membership referendum, 2016">United Kingdom membership referendum</A> resulted in the country's <A href="/wiki/Brexit" title="Brexit">intended withdrawal</A>. 52% of the British voters voted to leave the EU, leading into a complex separation process implying <A href="/wiki/Aftermath_of_the_United_Kingdom_European_Union_membership_referendum,_2016" title="Aftermath of the United Kingdom European Union membership referendum, 2016">political and economic changes</A> for both the UK and the remaining European Union countries.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Chronology">Chronology</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=History_of_Europe&action=edit&section=58" title="Edit section: Chronology">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV class="div-col columns column-count column-count-2" style="-moz-column-count: 2; -webkit-column-count: 2; column-count: 2;">
<UL>
<LI>700 BC: <A href="/wiki/Homer" title="Homer">Homer</A> composes <I><A href="/wiki/Iliad" title="Iliad">The Iliad</A></I>, an epic poem that represents the first piece of European literature.</LI>
<LI>440 BC: <A href="/wiki/Herodotus" title="Herodotus">Herodotus</A> defends Athenian <A href="/wiki/Political_freedom" title="Political freedom">political freedom</A> in the <I><A href="/wiki/Histories_(Herodotus)" title="Histories (Herodotus)">Histories</A></I>.</LI>
<LI>323 BC: <A href="/wiki/Alexander_the_Great" title="Alexander the Great">Alexander the Great</A> dies and his <A href="/wiki/Macedonian_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Macedonian Empire">Macedonian Empire</A> fragments.</LI>
<LI>44 BC: <A href="/wiki/Julius_Caesar" title="Julius Caesar">Julius Caesar</A> is murdered. The <A href="/wiki/Roman_Republic" title="Roman Republic">Roman Republic</A> enters its terminal crisis.</LI>
<LI>27 BC: Establishment of the <A href="/wiki/Roman_Empire" title="Roman Empire">Roman Empire</A> under <A href="/wiki/Octavian" class="mw-redirect" title="Octavian">Octavian</A>.</LI>
</UL>
<P><B>AD</B></P>
<UL>
<LI>45–55 (ca): First <A href="/wiki/Christianity" title="Christianity">Christian</A> congregations in mainland Greece and in Rome.</LI>
<LI>293: <A href="/wiki/Diocletian" title="Diocletian">Diocletian</A> reorganizes the Empire by creating the <A href="/wiki/Tetrarchy" title="Tetrarchy">Tetrarchy</A>.</LI>
<LI>330: <A href="/wiki/Constantine_the_Great" title="Constantine the Great">Constantine</A> makes <A href="/wiki/Constantinople" title="Constantinople">Constantinople</A> into his capital, a <A href="/wiki/New_Rome" title="New Rome">new Rome</A>.</LI>
<LI>395: Following the death of <A href="/wiki/Theodosius_I" title="Theodosius I">Theodosius I</A>, the Empire is permanently split into the <A href="/wiki/Eastern_Roman_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Eastern Roman Empire">Eastern Roman Empire</A> (later Byzantium) and the <A href="/wiki/Western_Roman_Empire" title="Western Roman Empire">Western Roman Empire</A>.</LI>
<LI>476: <A href="/wiki/Odoacer" title="Odoacer">Odoacer</A> captures <A href="/wiki/Ravenna" title="Ravenna">Ravenna</A> and deposes the last Roman emperor in the west: traditionally seen as the end date of the <A href="/wiki/Western_Roman_Empire" title="Western Roman Empire">Western Roman Empire</A>.</LI>
<LI>527: <A href="/wiki/Justinian_I" title="Justinian I">Justinian I</A> is <A href="/wiki/Coronation" title="Coronation">crowned</A> emperor of <A href="/wiki/Byzantine_Empire" title="Byzantine Empire">Byzantium</A>. Orders the editing of <I><A href="/wiki/Corpus_Juris_Civilis" title="Corpus Juris Civilis">Corpus Juris Civilis</A></I>, <A href="/wiki/Digest_(Roman_law)" title="Digest (Roman law)">Digest (Roman law)</A>.</LI>
<LI>597: Beginning of Roman Catholic <A href="/wiki/Christianization_of_Anglo-Saxon_England" class="mw-redirect" title="Christianization of Anglo-Saxon England">Christianization of Anglo-Saxon England</A> (missions and churches had been in existence well before this date, but their contacts with Rome had been loose or nonexistent)</LI>
<LI>600: <A href="/wiki/Saint_Columbanus" class="mw-redirect" title="Saint Columbanus">Saint Columbanus</A> uses the term "Europe" in a letter.</LI>
<LI>655: <A href="/wiki/Jus_patronatus" title="Jus patronatus">Jus patronatus</A>.</LI>
<LI>681: <A href="/wiki/Khan_Asparukh" class="mw-redirect" title="Khan Asparukh">Khan Asparukh</A> leads the Bulgars and invades the <A href="/wiki/Byzantine_empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Byzantine empire">Byzantine empire</A> in the <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Ongal" title="Battle of Ongal">Battle of Ongal</A>, and creates <A href="/wiki/Bulgaria" title="Bulgaria">Bulgaria</A>.</LI>
<LI>718: <A href="/wiki/Tervel_of_Bulgaria" title="Tervel of Bulgaria">Tervel of Bulgaria</A> helps the <A href="/wiki/Byzantine_Empire" title="Byzantine Empire">Byzantine Empire</A> stop the Arabic invasion of <A href="/wiki/Europe" title="Europe">Europe</A>, and breaks the <A href="/wiki/Siege_of_Constantinople_(717%E2%80%93718)" title="Siege of Constantinople (717–718)">siege of Constantinople</A>.</LI>
<LI>722: <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Covadonga" title="Battle of Covadonga">Battle of Covadonga</A> in the Iberian Peninsula. <A href="/wiki/Pelagius_of_Asturias" title="Pelagius of Asturias">Pelayo</A>, a noble Visigoth, defeats a Muslim army that tried to conquer the Cantabrian coast. This helps establish the Christian <A href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Asturias" title="Kingdom of Asturias">Kingdom of Asturias</A>, and marks the beginning of the Reconquista.</LI>
<LI>732: At the <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Tours" title="Battle of Tours">Battle of Tours</A>, the Franks stop the advance of the Arabs into Europe.</LI>

<LI>813: Third Council of Tours: Priests are ordered to preach in the <A href="/wiki/Vernacular" title="Vernacular">native language of the population</A>.</LI>

<LI>872: <A href="/wiki/Unification_of_Norway" title="Unification of Norway">Unification of Norway</A>.</LI>

The <A href="/wiki/Cyrillic_alphabet" class="mw-redirect" title="Cyrillic alphabet">Cyrillic alphabet</A> becomes the official <A href="/wiki/Bulgarian_alphabet" title="Bulgarian alphabet">Bulgarian alphabet</A>.</LI>

<LI>1315–1317: The <A href="/wiki/Great_Famine_of_1315%E2%80%931317" class="mw-redirect" title="Great Famine of 1315–1317">Great Famine of 1315–1317</A> in Northern Europe</LI>
<LI>1341: <A href="/wiki/Petrarch" title="Petrarch">Petrarch</A>, the "Father of <A href="/wiki/Renaissance_Humanism" class="mw-redirect" title="Renaissance Humanism">Humanism</A>", becomes the first <A href="/wiki/Poet_laureate" title="Poet laureate">poet laureate</A> since antiquity.</LI>
<LI>1337–1453: The <A href="/wiki/Hundred_Years%27_War" title="Hundred Years' War">Hundred Years' War</A> between England and France.</LI>
<LI>1348–1351: <A href="/wiki/Black_Death" title="Black Death">Black Death</A> kills about one-third of Europe's population.</LI>
<LI>1439: <A href="/wiki/Johannes_Gutenberg" title="Johannes Gutenberg">Johannes Gutenberg</A> invents first <A href="/wiki/Movable_type" title="Movable type">movable type</A> and the first <A href="/wiki/Printing_press" title="Printing press">printing press</A> for books, starting the <A href="/wiki/Printing_Revolution" class="mw-redirect" title="Printing Revolution">Printing Revolution</A>.</LI>
<LI>1453: <A href="/wiki/Fall_of_Constantinople" title="Fall of Constantinople">Fall of Constantinople</A> to the <A href="/wiki/Ottoman_Turks" title="Ottoman Turks">Ottoman Turks</A>.</LI>
<LI>1492: The <A href="/wiki/Reconquista" title="Reconquista">Reconquista</A> ends in the <A href="/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula" title="Iberian Peninsula">Iberian Peninsula</A>. A Spanish expeditionary group, commanded by <A href="/wiki/Christopher_Columbus" title="Christopher Columbus">Christopher Columbus</A>, lands in the <A href="/wiki/New_World" title="New World">New World</A>.</LI>
<LI>1497: <A href="/wiki/Vasco_da_Gama" title="Vasco da Gama">Vasco da Gama</A> departs to India starting direct trade with Asia.</LI>
<LI>1498: <A href="/wiki/Leonardo_da_Vinci" title="Leonardo da Vinci">Leonardo da Vinci</A> paints <I><A href="/wiki/The_Last_Supper_(Leonardo_da_Vinci)" title="The Last Supper (Leonardo da Vinci)">The Last Supper</A></I> in Milan as the <A href="/wiki/Renaissance" title="Renaissance">Renaissance</A> flourishes.</LI>
<LI>1508: <A href="/wiki/Maximilian_I,_Holy_Roman_Emperor" title="Maximilian I, Holy Roman Emperor">Maximilian I</A> the last ruling "<A href="/wiki/King_of_the_Romans" title="King of the Romans">King of the Romans</A>" and the first "elected Emperor of the Romans".</LI>
<LI>1517: <A href="/wiki/Martin_Luther" title="Martin Luther">Martin Luther</A> nails his 95 theses on indulgences to the door of the <A href="/wiki/All_Saints%27_Church,_Wittenberg" title="All Saints' Church, Wittenberg">church</A> in <A href="/wiki/Wittenberg" title="Wittenberg">Wittenberg</A>, triggering discussions which would soon lead to the <A href="/wiki/Protestant_Reformation" class="mw-redirect" title="Protestant Reformation">Reformation</A></LI>
<LI>1519: <A href="/wiki/Ferdinand_Magellan" title="Ferdinand Magellan">Ferdinand Magellan</A> and <A href="/wiki/Juan_Sebasti%C3%A1n_Elcano" title="Juan Sebastián Elcano">Juan Sebastián Elcano</A> begin first global circumnavigation. Their expedition returns in 1522.</LI>
<LI>1519: <A href="/wiki/Hern%C3%A1n_Cort%C3%A9s" title="Hernán Cortés">Hernán Cortés</A> begins conquest of Mexico for Spain.</LI>
<LI>1532: <A href="/wiki/Francisco_Pizarro" title="Francisco Pizarro">Francisco Pizarro</A> begins the conquest of Peru (the <A href="/wiki/Inca_Empire" title="Inca Empire">Inca Empire</A>) for Spain.</LI>
<LI>1543: <A href="/wiki/Nicolaus_Copernicus" title="Nicolaus Copernicus">Nicolaus Copernicus</A> publishes <I><A href="/wiki/De_revolutionibus_orbium_coelestium" title="De revolutionibus orbium coelestium">De revolutionibus orbium coelestium</A> (On the Revolutions of the Celestial Spheres)</I>.</LI>
<LI>1547: The <A href="/wiki/Grand_Duchy_of_Moscow" title="Grand Duchy of Moscow">Grand Duchy of Moscow</A> becomes the <A href="/wiki/Tsardom_of_Russia" title="Tsardom of Russia">Tsardom of Russia</A>.</LI>
<LI>1582: The introduction of the <A href="/wiki/Gregorian_calendar" title="Gregorian calendar">Gregorian calendar</A>; Russia refuses to adopt it until 1918.</LI>
<LI>1610: <A href="/wiki/Galileo_Galilei" title="Galileo Galilei">Galileo Galilei</A> uses his telescope to discover the moons of Jupiter.</LI>
<LI>1618: The <A href="/wiki/Thirty_Years%27_War" title="Thirty Years' War">Thirty Years' War</A> brings massive devastation to central Europe.</LI>
<LI>1648: The <A href="/wiki/Peace_of_Westphalia" title="Peace of Westphalia">Peace of Westphalia</A> ends the Thirty Years' War, and introduces the principle of the integrity of the nation state.</LI>
<LI>1687: <A href="/wiki/Isaac_Newton" title="Isaac Newton">Isaac Newton</A> publishes <I><A href="/wiki/Philosophi%C3%A6_Naturalis_Principia_Mathematica" title="Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica">Principia Mathematica</A></I>, having a profound impact on <A href="/wiki/The_Enlightenment" class="mw-redirect" title="The Enlightenment">The Enlightenment</A>.</LI>
<LI>1699: <A href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Karlowitz" title="Treaty of Karlowitz">Treaty of Karlowitz</A> concludes the <A href="/wiki/Great_Turkish_War" title="Great Turkish War">Austro-Ottoman War</A>. This marks the end of Ottoman control of Central Europe and the beginning of Ottoman stagnation, establishing the Habsburg Monarchy as the dominant power in Central and Southeastern Europe.</LI>
<LI>1700: Outbreak of the <A href="/wiki/War_of_the_Spanish_Succession" title="War of the Spanish Succession">War of the Spanish Succession</A> and the <A href="/wiki/Great_Northern_War" title="Great Northern War">Great Northern War</A>. The first would check the aspirations of <A href="/wiki/Louis_XIV" class="mw-redirect" title="Louis XIV">Louis XIV</A>, king of France to dominate European affairs; the second would lead to Russia's emergence as a great power and a recognizably European state.</LI>
<LI>18th century: <A href="/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment" title="Age of Enlightenment">Age of Enlightenment</A> spurs an intellectual renaissance across Europe.</LI>
<LI>1707: The <A href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Great_Britain" title="Kingdom of Great Britain">Kingdom of Great Britain</A> is formed by the union of the <A href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_England" title="Kingdom of England">Kingdom of England</A> and the <A href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Scotland" title="Kingdom of Scotland">Kingdom of Scotland</A>.</LI>
<LI>1712: <A href="/wiki/Thomas_Newcomen" title="Thomas Newcomen">Thomas Newcomen</A> invents first practical steam engine which begins <A href="/wiki/Industrial_Revolution" title="Industrial Revolution">Industrial Revolution</A> in Britain.</LI>
<LI>1721: Foundation of the <A href="/wiki/Russian_Empire" title="Russian Empire">Russian Empire</A>.</LI>
<LI>1775: <A href="/wiki/James_Watt" title="James Watt">James Watt</A> invents a new efficient steam engine accelerating the <A href="/wiki/Industrial_Revolution" title="Industrial Revolution">Industrial Revolution</A> in Britain.</LI>
<LI>1784: <A href="/wiki/Immanuel_Kant" title="Immanuel Kant">Immanuel Kant</A> publishes <I><A href="/wiki/Answering_the_Question:_What_Is_Enlightenment%3F" class="mw-redirect" title="Answering the Question: What Is Enlightenment?">Answering the Question: What Is Enlightenment?</A></I>.</LI>
<LI>1789: Beginning of the <A href="/wiki/French_Revolution" title="French Revolution">French Revolution</A> and end of the absolute monarchy in France.</LI>
<LI>1792–1802: <A href="/wiki/French_Revolutionary_Wars" title="French Revolutionary Wars">French Revolutionary Wars</A>.</LI>
<LI>1799: <A href="/wiki/Napoleon" title="Napoleon">Napoleon</A> comes to power as dictator of France.</LI>
<LI>1803–1815: <A href="/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars" title="Napoleonic Wars">Napoleonic Wars</A> end in defeat of Napoleon.</LI>
<LI>1806: Napoleon abolishes the <A href="/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire" title="Holy Roman Empire">Holy Roman Empire</A>.</LI>
<LI>1814–15: <A href="/wiki/Congress_of_Vienna" title="Congress of Vienna">Congress of Vienna</A>; Treaty of Vienna; France is reduced to 1789 boundaries; Reactionary forces dominate across Europe.</LI>
<LI>1825: <A href="/wiki/George_Stephenson" title="George Stephenson">George Stephenson</A> opens the <A href="/wiki/Stockton_and_Darlington_Railway" title="Stockton and Darlington Railway">Stockton and Darlington Railway</A> the first steam train railway for passenger traffic in the world.</LI>
<LI>1836: <A href="/wiki/Louis_Daguerre" title="Louis Daguerre">Louis Daguerre</A> invents first practical photographic method, in effect the first camera.</LI>
<LI>1838: <A href="/wiki/SS_Great_Western" title="SS Great Western">SS <I>Great Western</I></A>, the first steamship built for regularly scheduled transatlantic crossings enters service.</LI>
<LI>1848: <A href="/wiki/Revolutions_of_1848" title="Revolutions of 1848">Revolutions of 1848</A> and publication of <I><A href="/wiki/The_Communist_Manifesto" title="The Communist Manifesto">The Communist Manifesto</A></I>.</LI>
<LI>1852: Start of the <A href="/wiki/Crimean_War" title="Crimean War">Crimean War</A>, which ends in 1855 in a defeat for Russia.</LI>
<LI>1859: <A href="/wiki/Charles_Darwin" title="Charles Darwin">Charles Darwin</A> publishes <I>On the Origin of Species</I>.</LI>
<LI>1861: <A href="/wiki/Unification_of_Italy" class="mw-redirect" title="Unification of Italy">Unification of Italy</A> after victories by <A href="/wiki/Giuseppe_Garibaldi" title="Giuseppe Garibaldi">Giuseppe Garibaldi</A>.</LI>
<LI>1866: First commercially successful <A href="/wiki/Transatlantic_telegraph_cable" title="Transatlantic telegraph cable">transatlantic telegraph cable</A> is completed.</LI>
<LI>1860s: Russia <A href="/wiki/Emancipation_reform_of_1861" title="Emancipation reform of 1861">emancipates its serfs</A> and <A href="/wiki/Karl_Marx" title="Karl Marx">Karl Marx</A> completes the first volume of <I><A href="/wiki/Das_Kapital" class="mw-redirect" title="Das Kapital">Das Kapital</A></I>.</LI>
<LI>1870: <A href="/wiki/Franco-Prussian_War" title="Franco-Prussian War">Franco-Prussian War</A> and the fall of the <A href="/wiki/Second_French_Empire" title="Second French Empire">Second French Empire</A>.</LI>
<LI>1871: <A href="/wiki/Unification_of_Germany" title="Unification of Germany">Unification of Germany</A> under the direction of <A href="/wiki/Otto_von_Bismarck" title="Otto von Bismarck">Otto von Bismarck</A>.</LI>
<LI>1873: <A href="/wiki/Panic_of_1873" title="Panic of 1873">Panic of 1873</A> occurs. The <A href="/wiki/Long_Depression" title="Long Depression">Long Depression</A> begins.</LI>
<LI>1885: <A href="/wiki/Karl_Benz" title="Karl Benz">Karl Benz</A> invents <A href="/wiki/Benz_Patent-Motorwagen" title="Benz Patent-Motorwagen">Benz Patent-Motorwagen</A>, the world's first automobile.</LI>
<LI>1885: First permanent citywide <A href="/wiki/Tram" title="Tram">electrical tram</A> system in Europe (in <A href="/wiki/Sarajevo" title="Sarajevo">Sarajevo</A>).</LI>
<LI>1895: <A href="/wiki/Auguste_and_Louis_Lumi%C3%A8re" title="Auguste and Louis Lumière">Auguste and Louis Lumière</A> begin exhibitions of projected films before the paying public with their <A href="/wiki/Cinematograph" title="Cinematograph">cinematograph</A>, a portable camera, printer, and projector.</LI>
<LI>1902: <A href="/wiki/Guglielmo_Marconi" title="Guglielmo Marconi">Guglielmo Marconi</A> sends first transatlantic radio transmission.</LI>
<LI>1914: <A href="/wiki/Archduke_Franz_Ferdinand_of_Austria" title="Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria">Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria</A> is assassinated; <A href="/wiki/World_War_I" title="World War I">World War I</A> begins.</LI>
<LI>1917: <A href="/wiki/Vladimir_Lenin" title="Vladimir Lenin">Vladimir Lenin</A> and the <A href="/wiki/Bolshevik" class="mw-redirect" title="Bolshevik">Bolsheviks</A> seize power in the <A href="/wiki/Russian_Revolution" title="Russian Revolution">Russian Revolution</A>. The ensuing <A href="/wiki/Russian_Civil_War" title="Russian Civil War">Russian Civil War</A> lasts until 1922.</LI>
<LI>1918: World War I ends with the defeat of Germany and the Central Powers. Ten million soldiers killed; collapse of Russian, German, Austrian, and Ottoman empires.</LI>
<LI>1918: Collapse of the German Empire and monarchic system; founding of <A href="/wiki/Weimar_Republic" title="Weimar Republic">Weimar Republic</A>.</LI>
<LI>1918: Worldwide Spanish flu epidemic kills millions in Europe.</LI>
<LI>1918: Austro-Hungarian Empire dissolves.</LI>
<LI>1919: <A href="/wiki/Versailles_Treaty" class="mw-redirect" title="Versailles Treaty">Versailles Treaty</A> strips Germany of its colonies, several provinces and its navy and air force; limits army; Allies occupy western areas; reparations ordered.</LI>
<LI>1920: <A href="/wiki/League_of_Nations" title="League of Nations">League of Nations</A> begins operations; largely ineffective; defunct by 1939.</LI>
<LI>1921–22: Ireland divided; Irish Free State becomes independent and civil war erupts.</LI>
<LI>1922: <A href="/wiki/Benito_Mussolini" title="Benito Mussolini">Benito Mussolini</A> and the <A href="/wiki/National_Fascist_Party" title="National Fascist Party">Fascists</A> take power in Italy.</LI>
<LI>1929: Worldwide <A href="/wiki/Great_Depression" title="Great Depression">Great Depression</A> begins with <A href="/wiki/Wall_Street_Crash_of_1929" title="Wall Street Crash of 1929">stock market crash</A> in <A href="/wiki/New_York_City" title="New York City">New York City</A>.</LI>
<LI>1933: <A href="/wiki/Adolf_Hitler" title="Adolf Hitler">Adolf Hitler</A> and the <A href="/wiki/Nazis" class="mw-redirect" title="Nazis">Nazis</A> take power in Germany.</LI>
<LI>1935: Italy conquers Ethiopia; League sanctions are ineffective.</LI>
<LI>1936: Start of the <A href="/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War" title="Spanish Civil War">Spanish Civil War</A>; ends in 1939 with victory of Nationalists who are aided by Germany and Italy.</LI>
<LI>1938: Germany escalates the persecution of Jews with <A href="/wiki/Kristallnacht" title="Kristallnacht">Kristallnacht</A>.</LI>
<LI>1938: Appeasement of Germany by Britain and France; <A href="/wiki/Munich_agreement" class="mw-redirect" title="Munich agreement">Munich agreement</A> splits <A href="/wiki/Czechoslovakia" title="Czechoslovakia">Czechoslovakia</A>; Germany seized the remainder in 1939.</LI>
<LI>1939: Britain and France hurriedly rearm; failed to arrange treaty with USSR.</LI>
<LI>1939: <A href="/wiki/Adolf_Hitler" title="Adolf Hitler">Adolf Hitler</A> and <A href="/wiki/Joseph_Stalin" title="Joseph Stalin">Joseph Stalin</A> agree partition of <A href="/wiki/Eastern_Europe" title="Eastern Europe">Eastern Europe</A> in <A href="/wiki/Molotov%E2%80%93Ribbentrop_Pact" title="Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact">Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact</A>.</LI>
<LI>1939: Germany <A href="/wiki/Invasion_of_Poland" title="Invasion of Poland">invades</A> <A href="/wiki/Second_Polish_Republic" title="Second Polish Republic">Poland</A>, starting the <A href="/wiki/World_War_II" title="World War II">Second World War</A>.</LI>
<LI>1940: Great Britain under <A href="/wiki/Winston_Churchill" title="Winston Churchill">Winston Churchill</A> becomes the last nation to hold out against the Nazis after winning the <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Britain" title="Battle of Britain">Battle of Britain</A>.</LI>
<LI>1941: U.S. begins large-scale <A href="/wiki/Lend-lease" class="mw-redirect" title="Lend-lease">lend-lease</A> aid to Britain, Free France, the USSR and other <A href="/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II" title="Allies of World War II">Allies</A>; Canada also provides financial aid.</LI>
<LI>1941: Germany invades the Soviet Union in <A href="/wiki/Operation_Barbarossa" title="Operation Barbarossa">Operation Barbarossa</A>; fails to capture <A href="/wiki/Moscow" title="Moscow">Moscow</A> or Leningrad.</LI>
<LI>1942: <A href="/wiki/Nazi_Germany" title="Nazi Germany">Nazi Germany</A> commences the Holocaust — a <A href="/wiki/Final_Solution" title="Final Solution">Final Solution</A>, with the murder of 6 million Jews.</LI>
<LI>1943: After <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Stalingrad" title="Battle of Stalingrad">Stalingrad</A> and <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Kursk" title="Battle of Kursk">Kursk</A>, Soviet forces begin recapturing Nazi-occupied territory in the East.</LI>
<LI>1944: U.S., British and Canadian armed forces <A href="/wiki/Normandy_landings" title="Normandy landings">invade Nazi-occupied France</A> at <A href="/wiki/Normandy" title="Normandy">Normandy</A>.</LI>
<LI>1945: Hitler commits suicide, Mussolini is murdered. World War II ends with Europe in ruins and Germany defeated.</LI>
<LI>1945: <A href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</A> formed.</LI>
<LI>1947: The <A href="/wiki/British_Empire" title="British Empire">British Empire</A> begins a process of voluntarily dismantling with the granting of independence to <A href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</A> and <A href="/wiki/Pakistan" title="Pakistan">Pakistan</A>.</LI>
<LI>1947: <A href="/wiki/Cold_War" title="Cold War">Cold War</A> begins as Europe is polarized East versus West.</LI>
<LI>1948–51: U.S. provides large sums to rebuild Western Europe through the <A href="/wiki/Marshall_Plan" title="Marshall Plan">Marshall Plan</A>; stimulates large-scale modernization of European industries and reduction of trade restrictions.</LI>
<LI>1949: The <A href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</A> alliance is established.</LI>
<LI>1955: USSR creates a rival military coalition, the <A href="/wiki/Warsaw_Pact" title="Warsaw Pact">Warsaw Pact</A>.</LI>
<LI>1950: The <A href="/wiki/Schuman_Declaration" title="Schuman Declaration">Schuman Declaration</A> begins the process of <A href="/wiki/European_integration" title="European integration">European integration</A>.</LI>
<LI>1954: The <A href="/wiki/French_colonial_empire" title="French colonial empire">French Empire</A> begins to be dismantled; Withdraws from Vietnam.</LI>
<LI>1956: <A href="/wiki/Suez_Crisis" title="Suez Crisis">Suez Crisis</A> signals the end of the effective power of the British Empire.</LI>
<LI>1956: <A href="/wiki/Hungarian_Revolution_of_1956" title="Hungarian Revolution of 1956">Hungarian Uprising</A> defeated by Soviet military forces.</LI>
<LI>1957: <A href="/wiki/Treaties_of_Rome" class="mw-redirect" title="Treaties of Rome">Treaties of Rome</A> establish the <A href="/wiki/European_Economic_Community" title="European Economic Community">European Economic Community</A> from 1958.</LI>
<LI>1968: The <A href="/wiki/May_1968_events_in_France" title="May 1968 events in France">May 1968 events in France</A> lead France to the brink of revolution.</LI>
<LI>1968: The <A href="/wiki/Prague_Spring" title="Prague Spring">Prague Spring</A> is defeated by <A href="/wiki/Warsaw_Pact_invasion_of_Czechoslovakia" title="Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia">Warsaw Pact military forces</A>. The <A href="/wiki/Club_of_Rome" title="Club of Rome">Club of Rome</A> is founded.</LI>
<LI>1980: The <A href="/wiki/Solidarity_(Polish_trade_union)" title="Solidarity (Polish trade union)">Solidarność</A> movement under <A href="/wiki/Lech_Wa%C5%82%C4%99sa" title="Lech Wałęsa">Lech Wałęsa</A> begins open, overground opposition to the Communist rule in Poland.</LI>
<LI>1985: <A href="/wiki/Mikhail_Gorbachev" title="Mikhail Gorbachev">Mikhail Gorbachev</A> becomes leader of the Soviet Union and <A href="/wiki/Perestroika" title="Perestroika">begins reforms</A> which inadvertently leads to the fall of Communism and the Soviet Union.</LI>
<LI>1986: <A href="/wiki/Chernobyl_disaster" title="Chernobyl disaster">Chernobyl disaster</A> occurs, the worst nuclear disaster in history.</LI>
<LI>1989: <A href="/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989" title="Revolutions of 1989">Communism overthrown</A> in all the <A href="/wiki/Warsaw_Pact" title="Warsaw Pact">Warsaw Pact</A> countries except the Soviet Union. Fall of the <A href="/wiki/Berlin_Wall" title="Berlin Wall">Berlin Wall</A> (opening of unrestrained border crossings between east and west, which effectively deprived the wall of any relevance).</LI>
<LI>1990: <A href="/wiki/German_reunification" title="German reunification">Reunification of Germany</A>.</LI>
<LI>1991: <A href="/wiki/Breakup_of_Yugoslavia" title="Breakup of Yugoslavia">Breakup of Yugoslavia</A> and the beginning of the <A href="/wiki/Yugoslav_Wars" title="Yugoslav Wars">Yugoslav Wars</A>.</LI>
<LI>1991: <A href="/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="Dissolution of the Soviet Union">Dissolution of the Soviet Union</A> and the creation of the <A href="/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Independent_States" title="Commonwealth of Independent States">Commonwealth of Independent States</A>.</LI>
<LI>1993: <A href="/wiki/Maastricht_Treaty" title="Maastricht Treaty">Maastricht Treaty</A> establishes the <A href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</A>.</LI>
<LI>2002: End of European <A href="/wiki/Colonial_empire" title="Colonial empire">colonial empires</A> with the independence of <A href="/wiki/East_Timor" title="East Timor">East Timor</A>, formerly <A href="/wiki/Portuguese_Timor" title="Portuguese Timor">Portuguese Timor</A>.</LI>
<LI>2004: Slovenia, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Cyprus and Malta <A href="/wiki/2004_enlargement_of_the_European_Union" title="2004 enlargement of the European Union">join the European Union</A>.</LI>
<LI>2007: Romania and Bulgaria <A href="/wiki/2007_enlargement_of_the_European_Union" title="2007 enlargement of the European Union">join the European Union</A>.</LI>
<LI>2008: The <A href="/wiki/Great_Recession#Effects_on_Europe" title="Great Recession">Great Recession</A> begins. Unemployment rises in some parts of Europe.</LI>
<LI>2013: Croatia <A href="/wiki/2013_enlargement_of_the_European_Union" title="2013 enlargement of the European Union">joins</A> the European Union.</LI>
<LI>2014: <A href="/wiki/2014_Ukrainian_revolution" title="2014 Ukrainian revolution">Revolution in Ukraine</A> and serious tensions between Russia, Ukraine and the European Union.</LI>
<LI>2015: <A href="/wiki/European_migrant_crisis" title="European migrant crisis">European migrant crisis</A> starts.</LI>
<LI>2016: United Kingdom <A href="/wiki/United_Kingdom_European_Union_membership_referendum,_2016" title="United Kingdom European Union membership referendum, 2016">votes</A> to <A href="/wiki/Brexit" title="Brexit">leave the European Union</A>.</LI>
</UL>

<P>The <B>fourteenth season</B> of the American television medical drama <I><A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy" title="Grey's Anatomy">Grey's Anatomy</A></I> was ordered on February 10, 2017, by <A href="/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company" title="American Broadcasting Company">American Broadcasting Company</A> (ABC), and premiered on September 28, 2017 with a special two-hour premiere.<SUP id="cite_ref-premiere_date_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-premiere_date-1">[1]</A></SUP> The season will consist of 24 episodes,<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-renewed_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-renewed-3">[3]</A></SUP> with the season's seventh episode marking the 300th episode for the series overall. The season is produced by <A href="/wiki/ABC_Studios" title="ABC Studios">ABC Studios</A>, in association with <A href="/wiki/Shondaland" title="Shondaland">Shondaland</A> Production Company and The Mark Gordon Company; the <A href="/wiki/Showrunners" class="mw-redirect" title="Showrunners">showrunners</A> being <A href="/wiki/Krista_Vernoff" title="Krista Vernoff">Krista Vernoff</A> and William Harper.</P>
<P>This season is the first not to feature <A href="/wiki/Jerrika_Hinton" title="Jerrika Hinton">Jerrika Hinton</A> as Dr. Stephanie Edwards since her introduction in the <A href="/wiki/Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_9)" title="Grey's Anatomy (season 9)">ninth season</A>, following her departure at the conclusion of the previous season.<SUP id="cite_ref-edwards_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-edwards-4">[4]</A></SUP> The season also marked the last appearance for <A href="/wiki/Martin_Henderson" title="Martin Henderson">Martin Henderson</A> as a series regular.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Plots">Plots</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_14)&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Plots">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The season follows the story of <A href="/wiki/Surgery" title="Surgery">surgical</A> <A href="/wiki/Residency_(medicine)" title="Residency (medicine)">residents</A>, <A href="/wiki/Fellowship_(medicine)" title="Fellowship (medicine)">fellows</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Attending_physician" title="Attending physician">attendings</A> as they experience the difficulties of the competitive careers they have chosen. It is set in the surgical wing of the fictional Grey Sloan Memorial Hospital, located in <A href="/wiki/Seattle,_Washington" class="mw-redirect" title="Seattle, Washington">Seattle, Washington</A>.</P>
<P>The season picks up right where it left off after the fire in the previous season finale. Grey-Sloan takes on a new, improved appearance after it is repaired of the damages from the fire. <A href="/wiki/Meredith_Grey" title="Meredith Grey">Meredith Grey</A> (<A href="/wiki/Ellen_Pompeo" title="Ellen Pompeo">Ellen Pompeo</A>) finds herself in another love triangle with Nathan Riggs (<A href="/wiki/Martin_Henderson" title="Martin Henderson">Martin Henderson</A>) and his long-lost fiancée, Megan Hunt (<A href="/wiki/Abigail_Spencer" title="Abigail Spencer">Abigail Spencer</A>), though she encourages Riggs to resume his relationship with Megan over her. Meredith performs a ground-breaking surgery on Megan, landing her a Harper Avery Award. <A href="/wiki/Jackson_Avery" title="Jackson Avery">Jackson Avery</A> (<A href="/wiki/Jesse_Williams_(actor)" title="Jesse Williams (actor)">Jesse Williams</A>) and <A href="/wiki/Maggie_Pierce" title="Maggie Pierce">Maggie Pierce</A> (<A href="/wiki/Kelly_McCreary" title="Kelly McCreary">Kelly McCreary</A>) fiddle with the idea of a relationship after Jackson and <A href="/wiki/April_Kepner" title="April Kepner">April Kepner</A> (<A href="/wiki/Sarah_Drew" title="Sarah Drew">Sarah Drew</A>) decide to live apart.</P>
<P><A href="/wiki/Teddy_Altman" title="Teddy Altman">Teddy Altman</A> (<A href="/wiki/Kim_Raver" title="Kim Raver">Kim Raver</A>) returns to Seattle to assist with Megan's reappearance and notices the tension in Owen and Amelia's relationship. With the help of DeLuca's sister, visiting doctor Carina DeLuca (Stefania Spampinato), <A href="/wiki/Amelia_Shepherd" title="Amelia Shepherd">Amelia Shepherd</A> (<A href="/wiki/Caterina_Scorsone" title="Caterina Scorsone">Caterina Scorsone</A>) discovers she has a brain tumor that has been impairing her judgment for the last 10 years. After it is removed by her former professor Tom Koracick (<A href="/wiki/Greg_Germann" title="Greg Germann">Greg Germann</A>), Amelia and <A href="/wiki/Owen_Hunt" title="Owen Hunt">Owen Hunt</A> (<A href="/wiki/Kevin_McKidd" title="Kevin McKidd">Kevin McKidd</A>) decide to end their marriage. Meanwhile, after <A href="/wiki/Alex_Karev" title="Alex Karev">Alex Karev</A> (<A href="/wiki/Justin_Chambers" title="Justin Chambers">Justin Chambers</A>) reveals to Jo Wilson (<A href="/wiki/Camilla_Luddington" title="Camilla Luddington">Camilla Luddington</A>) that he tracked down her husband, Alex and Jo reconcile their relationship, with Jo declaring that she will divorce Paul (<A href="/wiki/Matthew_Morrison" title="Matthew Morrison">Matthew Morrison</A>).</P>
<P>A new class of interns is introduced, one of which has a history with Andrew DeLuca (<A href="/wiki/Giacomo_Gianniotti" title="Giacomo Gianniotti">Giacomo Gianniotti</A>). Ben Warren (<A href="/wiki/Jason_Winston_George" title="Jason Winston George">Jason George</A>) joins to Fire Academy but has trouble telling his wife, <A href="/wiki/Miranda_Bailey" title="Miranda Bailey">Miranda Bailey</A> (<A href="/wiki/Chandra_Wilson" title="Chandra Wilson">Chandra Wilson</A>). Harper Avery (<A href="/wiki/Chelcie_Ross" title="Chelcie Ross">Chelcie Ross</A>) threatens to pull funding from Grey-Sloan and fires Bailey as Chief, but he soon after passes away, reinstating Bailey in the position. After Eliza Minnick (<A href="/wiki/Marika_Domi%C5%84czyk" title="Marika Domińczyk">Marika Domińczyk</A>) is fired from Grey-Sloan, she <A href="/wiki/Ghosting_(relationships)" title="Ghosting (relationships)">ghosts</A> <A href="/wiki/Arizona_Robbins" title="Arizona Robbins">Arizona Robbins</A> (<A href="/wiki/Jessica_Capshaw" title="Jessica Capshaw">Jessica Capshaw</A>), who subsequently begins dating Carina. Their relationship is short-lived, however, as Arizona inadvertently ends it while preparing for Sofia to return home from New York. Carina begins a sexual relationship with the newly single Owen.</P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Casting">Casting</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_14)&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Casting">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Series regular <A href="/wiki/Jerrika_Hinton" title="Jerrika Hinton">Jerrika Hinton</A> does not appear for the first time since her introduction at the start of the 9th season, after it was announced she landed a starring role in <A href="/wiki/Alan_Ball_(screenwriter)" title="Alan Ball (screenwriter)">Alan Ball</A>'s new <A href="/wiki/HBO" title="HBO">HBO</A> drama series <I><A href="/wiki/Here,_Now" class="mw-redirect" title="Here, Now">Here, Now</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-edwards_4-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-edwards-4">[4]</A></SUP> Hinton had previously been in talks of leaving the show at the end of the 12th season when she was cast in the Shondaland comedy pilot <I>Toast</I>, but ABC passed on the project.<SUP id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14">[14]</A></SUP> Renewing her contract for another three seasons as Dr. <A href="/wiki/Arizona_Robbins" title="Arizona Robbins">Arizona Robbins</A> after the eleventh season, <A href="/wiki/Jessica_Capshaw" title="Jessica Capshaw">Jessica Capshaw</A> will return for the 14th season.<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP> On June 20, 2017, it was announced that <A href="/wiki/Kim_Raver" title="Kim Raver">Kim Raver</A> is set to reprise her role as Dr. <A href="/wiki/Teddy_Altman" title="Teddy Altman">Teddy Altman</A> for a guest arc.<SUP id="cite_ref-TeddyReturns_6-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TeddyReturns-6">[6]</A></SUP> In August 2017, it was announced that <A href="/wiki/Abigail_Spencer" title="Abigail Spencer">Abigail Spencer</A> would replace <A href="/wiki/Bridget_Regan" title="Bridget Regan">Bridget Regan</A> as Megan Hunt for a multi-episode arc this season.<SUP id="cite_ref-MeganRecast_7-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-MeganRecast-7">[7]</A></SUP> After recurring in the previous season as the controversial character, Eliza Minnick, it was announced in August 2017 that Marika Dominczyk would not return to the show. On September 13, 2017, another special guest star was announced in <A href="/wiki/Greg_Germann" title="Greg Germann">Greg Germann</A> (<A href="/wiki/Ally_McBeal" title="Ally McBeal">Ally McBeal</A>); though details of his role were not disclosed, it was revealed that his character's name would be Tom Koracick and he'd been seen in the episode "Go Big or Go Home."<SUP id="cite_ref-Germann_8-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Germann-8">[8]</A></SUP> His character turned out to be Amelia's neurosurgery mentor and he re-appeared in the subsequent episode entitled "Ain't That a Kick in the Head."</P>
<P>On October 26, 2017, it was announced that <A href="/wiki/Martin_Henderson" title="Martin Henderson">Martin Henderson</A>'s appearance in the fifth episode of the season would be his last.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On October 9, 2017, the new group of interns to join the cast as of the fourth episode,"Ain't That a Kick in the Head," was announced to include <A href="/wiki/Jeanine_Mason" title="Jeanine Mason">Jeanine Mason</A> (<A href="/wiki/So_You_Think_You_Can_Dance_(U.S._TV_series)" title="So You Think You Can Dance (U.S. TV series)">So You Think You Can Dance</A>) as Sam, Alex Blue Davis as Casey, Rushi Kota as Vik, Jaicy Elliot as Taryn, Sophia Taylor Ali as Dahlia, and Jake Borelli as Levi.<SUP id="cite_ref-interns_11-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-interns-11">[11]</A></SUP></P>
<P>On January 31, 2018, it was announced that <A href="/wiki/Candis_Cayne" title="Candis Cayne">Candis Cayne</A> would be joining the show as Dr. Michelle Velez for a multi-episode arc revolving around a transgender character receiving a ground breaking surgery. <SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Production">Production</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_14)&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Production">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Development">Development</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Grey%27s_Anatomy_(season_14)&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Development">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P><I>Grey's Anatomy</I> was renewed for a 14th season on February 10, 2017.<SUP id="cite_ref-renewed_3-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-renewed-3">[3]</A></SUP> It premiered on September 28, 2017, with a two-hour premiere.<SUP id="cite_ref-premiere_date_1-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-premiere_date-1">[1]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Ellen_Pompeo" title="Ellen Pompeo">Ellen Pompeo</A> announced that she would be directing several episodes in the 14th season.<SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP> On April 28, 2017, veteran writer <A href="/wiki/Krista_Vernoff" title="Krista Vernoff">Krista Vernoff</A> announced that she would return to the show as a writer after leaving the show after the seventh season.<SUP id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-19">[19]</A></SUP> On January 11, 2018, ABC released a six-episode web series following the new surgical interns at Grey Sloan Memorial Hospital. The web series was written by Barbara Kaye Friend and directed by series regular <A href="/wiki/Sarah_Drew" title="Sarah Drew">Sarah Drew</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP></P>

<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep294" style="text-align:center">294</TH>
<TD>1</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Break Down the House"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Debbie_Allen" title="Debbie Allen">Debbie Allen</A></TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Krista_Vernoff" title="Krista Vernoff">Krista Vernoff</A></TD>
<TD>September 28, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-09-28</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.07<SUP id="cite_ref-house_21-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-house-21">[21]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">In a whirlwind of reunions and a Grey Sloan "major uplift," Meredith finds herself in a complicated love triangle between Nathan and Megan, Owen’s sister who was recently revealed to still be alive after a ten year absence in a hostage camp overseas. With Megan’s reappearance, Teddy Altman comes back to Seattle to support Owen and his mom, which leads to awkward interactions with Amelia. With Stephanie now in Texas at a burn unit, Jo eagerly tries to make Ben her new person. After being “ghosted” by Eliza, Arizona hits it off with an Italian girl in a bar whom she takes home with her. When DeLuca comes home, he finds his sister half-naked on his couch with Arizona.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep295" style="text-align:center">295</TH>
<TD>2</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Get Off on the Pain"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Kevin_McKidd" title="Kevin McKidd">Kevin McKidd</A></TD>
<TD>Krista Vernoff</TD>
<TD>September 28, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-09-28</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.07<SUP id="cite_ref-house_21-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-house-21">[21]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">Carina, DeLuca’s sister, asks to be introduced to Bailey in order to get approval to study the controversial topic of female masturbation and orgasms at her hospital; Bailey obliges due to society's double standard. Meredith works to get everyone to agree that an abdominal wall transplant is the best tactic to treat Megan’s wounds; she even gets Teddy to scrub in to erase any doubts of Meredith’s intentions of being Megan’s surgeon. Jo tries to mend her relationship with Alex, after it’s revealed that Jo slept with one of the new sub-interns. Owen gets called out on his marital status with Amelia, who seems to be avoiding him and his family. Even without the support of Jackson, Amelia fights to remove a patient’s mastoid tumor. She later takes part in Carina's study which leads to her finding a huge tumor in her own brain.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep296" style="text-align:center">296</TH>
<TD>3</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Go Big or Go Home"</TD>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Chandra_Wilson" title="Chandra Wilson">Chandra Wilson</A></TD>
<TD>Meg Marinis</TD>
<TD>October 5, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-10-05</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.06<SUP id="cite_ref-go_big_22-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-go_big-22">[22]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">Amelia brings in one of her former professors and current head of Neurology at <A href="/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University" title="Johns Hopkins University">Johns Hopkins</A>, Dr. Tom Koracik to help her come up with a treatment plan for her tumor. Much to her chagrin, Dr Koracik brings to light how impaired her judgment has been over the last ten years; Richard makes sure to let Amelia know that her judgment hasn’t been all that bad and encourages her to come clean to those with whom she’s closest. Bailey is confronted by Harper Avery about all the changes that have been made to the hospital and threatens to withdraw all funding from the foundation; when Bailey stands up to him, Avery fires her. In the end of the episode Avery passes away with a sudden cardiac arrest and then Jackson and Catherine Avery reinstate Bailey back as the chief. Ben and Arizona resort to advice delivered by Carina when one of their patients gets stuck in labor. Meredith turns to her former psychiatrist, who winds up as a patient, to sort out her mood towards everyone instigated by the love triangle involving Nathan and Megan. Jo asks Alex to move back home.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep297" style="text-align:center">297</TH>
<TD>4</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Ain't That a Kick in the Head?"</TD>
<TD>Geary McLeod</TD>
<TD>Marlana Hope</TD>
<TD>October 12, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-10-12</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.08<SUP id="cite_ref-kick_head_23-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-kick_head-23">[23]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">Amelia has her brain tumor removed, but in the days following, she experiences some complications, such as speaking only French, and memory loss. Richard unexpectedly brings Maggie to attend a family dinner hosted by Catherine, which turns awkward when Catherine discloses to Avery his inheritance from Harper’s passing, a quarter billion dollars. Bailey and Richard host interviews with prospective new interns but fail to find a decent candidate. Using her research to justify his entry into the country, Meredith and Nathan team up to bring Megan’s adopted son to America. Amelia and Owen face their fear that their marriage is based on a version of Amelia created by her illness. Arizona learns that Sofia wants to move home. Jo confesses that she hates how much control her ex-husband has over her.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep298" style="text-align:center">298</TH>
<TD>5</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"<A href="/wiki/Danger_Zone_(Grey%27s_Anatomy)" title="Danger Zone (Grey's Anatomy)">Danger Zone</A>"</TD>
<TD>Cecilie Mosli</TD>
<TD>Jalysa Conway</TD>
<TD>October 26, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-10-26</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>7.67<SUP id="cite_ref-zone_24-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-zone-24">[24]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">As Owen helps Megan make the trip to California where she’ll start her new life with Nathan and her son, Farouk, they reminisce on their time spent in <A href="/wiki/Fallujah" title="Fallujah">Fallujah, Iraq</A>. During their time overseas, Nathan proposed to Megan by recycling a necklace that wasn’t initially intended for her. Teddy quickly recognized the necklace and the fact that Nathan cheated and pushed him to come clean. Despite the good news of the engagement, Megan dealt with heartbreak of not making strat, which is later revealed to her as Owen’s own doing. Distraught over her brother's betrayal, she gets on a helicopter with one of the shooters who attacked their troops, leading to her disappearance. While Nathan awaits the arrival of Megan and Owen, he bonds with Farouk, who is having trouble acclimating to the free world. He also officially ends his relationship with Meredith, as does Owen with Amelia when he comes to terms with the notion that neither of them are truly happy.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep299" style="text-align:center">299</TH>
<TD>6</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Come On Down to My Boat, Baby"</TD>
<TD>Lisa Leone</TD>
<TD>Kiley Donovan</TD>
<TD>November 2, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-11-02</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>7.38<SUP id="cite_ref-boat_25-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-boat-25">[25]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">As the new surgeon on the cover page of the medical journal, JSA, Meredith performs a rare surgical procedure, made possible by Jo’s persuasion, to try and save a judge from his progressive cancer diagnosis. The men of Grey Sloan take a “sick day” and hang out on a Jackson’s newly purchased boat, whereas the women swipe for dates on <A href="/wiki/Tinder_(app)" title="Tinder (app)">Tinder</A>. Arizona has broken up with Carina in preparation of Sofia moving back home. Amelia heads back to surgery but struggles with her confidence, recruiting the help of Dr. Koracik and seeking the encouragement of Richard. While Arizona and April repair a woman’s injuries caused by an accidental firing of a gun that was hidden inside her vagina, Bailey and Maggie take care of a hypochondriac who was a victim of the accidental shooting. At the surgeon-intern mixer, Meredith learns that she's been nominated for the annual Harper Avery award; however, the news is overshadowed by the loss of her patient. Jackson gives half his inheritance to Bailey to fund a research competition. Jo learns she's in the running for chief resident and decides to file for divorce from Paul after confiding her situation to the judge. DeLuca recognizes one of the new interns from his past, while Owen and Carina are caught kissing.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep300" style="text-align:center">300</TH>
<TD>7</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Who Lives, Who Dies, Who Tells Your Story"</TD>
<TD>Debbie Allen</TD>
<TD>Krista Vernoff</TD>
<TD>November 9, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-11-09</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.13<SUP id="cite_ref-story_26-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-story-26">[26]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">When a roller coaster car derails off its tracks, Meredith’s plans to attend the Harper Avery award ceremony are put on hold. Three patients visiting the ER look like former doctors of the hospital: Drs. Cristina Yang, George O’Malley, and Izzie Stevens. Amelia and Owen learn to co-exist in the OR, after Amelia orders a surprise CT which shows a large hematoma that she is able to repair. As Arizona performs surgery on Liza, Izzie’s look-a-like, she reflects on her relationship with Callie and Mark in preparation for Sofia’s return to Seattle. Jo probes Alex to call Izzie and see how she is, to which Alex says he knows how she is: a happily married surgeon with three children. As they wait on Meredith to leave for Boston, Maggie bonds with Zola as they rehearse medical knowledge and talk about Derek. Bailey and Ben fight over his announcement to join the fire department, due to Bailey’s fear that he has commitment issues. Unable to fly out to Boston, in an OR—in front of her friends and colleagues—Meredith is announced the winner of the 2017 Harper Avery award.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep301" style="text-align:center">301</TH>
<TD>8</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Out of Nowhere"</TD>
<TD>Kevin McKidd</TD>
<TD>William Harper</TD>
<TD>November 16, 2017<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2017-11-16</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>7.52<SUP id="cite_ref-nowhere_27-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-nowhere-27">[27]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">As the interns struggle to find their stride as surgeons, Jo begins her reign as chief resident. Things take a turn for the worse when the computer system gets hacked at Grey Sloan Memorial, as all of the patients’ records get held hostage for $20 million. Unable to understand why the ransom is so large and unprecedented, Bailey realizes it’s due to the recently announced competition funded by Jackson’s inheritance. Without the use of the technological advancements to which the doctors have become accustomed, they must rely on their instincts to treat their patients; Richard teaches his younger colleagues about how they worked in the “Stone Age.” One patient is transported to another hospital by a helicopter which encounters bad turbulence, causing a line to loosen and squirt blood everywhere. Jo gets the scariest surprise of her life when she runs into her abusive husband, Paul, on her way to stop Alex from inadvertently killing their patient.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep302" style="text-align:center">302</TH>
<TD>9</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"1-800-799-7233"</TD>
<TD>Bill D'Elia</TD>
<TD>Andy Reaser</TD>
<TD>January 18, 2018<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2018-01-18</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.27<SUP id="cite_ref-14x09_28-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14x09-28">[28]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">
<P>While the staff of the hospital fawns over Dr. Paul Stadler and his legendary work as a surgeon, Jo tries to steer clear of him. Alex and Meredith team up to do their best to protect Jo during the process of filing for divorce. Drenched in blood, Jackson and Maggie save their patient’s life, and then bond in the locker room after showers; April and Owen use their trauma skills to work on patients in less than ideal and extremely hot conditions, very similar to when they were overseas. Bailey works with an exceptionally computer-savvy intern to take back the power against those who hacked the hospital; this intern later outs himself as "a proud trans man." After Paul’s fiancée, Jenny, tells him about her secret exchange with Jo, Meredith has to pretend to call in security to remove Paul from the hospital. However, he soon winds back up in the ER as a victim of a hit-and-run.</P>
<HR />
The episode was followed by a PSA of <A href="/wiki/Camilla_Luddington" title="Camilla Luddington">Camilla Luddington</A> reminding viewers that psychological abuse is a form of domestic violence and providing the number of the <A href="/wiki/National_Domestic_Violence_Hotline" title="National Domestic Violence Hotline">National Domestic Violence Hotline</A>: 1-800-799-7233, the episode's title.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep303" style="text-align:center">303</TH>
<TD>10</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"<A href="/wiki/Personal_Jesus_(Grey%27s_Anatomy)" title="Personal Jesus (Grey's Anatomy)">Personal Jesus</A>"</TD>
<TD>Kevin Sullivan</TD>
<TD>Zoanne Clack</TD>
<TD>January 25, 2018<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2018-01-25</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.62<SUP id="cite_ref-personal_29-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-personal-29">[29]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">With Paul recovering from surgery, Meredith questions the alibi that Alex and Jo provide her. Believing that it’s his fiancée, Jenny, who ran him over, Jo feels the need to consult her. April’s patient turns out to be the pregnant wife of her ex-fiancé, Matthew, proving to be more than an awkward situation, as she helps deliver their baby, and then watches him deal with his wife’s unexpected death. Jackson, Bailey, and April are confronted with racial profiling when police show up with a handcuffed 12-year-old boy whom they shot when he was seen trying to enter his own home by a window. Police officers continue to treat him like a criminal in the ER, prompting Bailey and Ben to give Tucker “the talk.” When Jo and Jenny go to Paul’s room to announce they are taking him to court, he gets in a bout of rage and falls out of his bed, knocking himself out and becoming brain dead. Still legally his wife, Jo decides to take him off life support and have his organs donated. April ends up in the shower with Roy, an intern, after she finds herself questioning her faith.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep304" style="text-align:center">304</TH>
<TD>11</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"(Don't Fear) the Reaper"</TD>
<TD>Nicole Rubio</TD>
<TD>Elisabeth R. Finch</TD>
<TD>February 1, 2018<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2018-02-01</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>8.93<SUP id="cite_ref-reaper_30-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-reaper-30">[30]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">With her intuition and the more subtle signs of a heart attack, Bailey winds up in the ER at Seattle Presbyterian; however, after her doctors treat her condescendingly, assuming she's imagining the heart attack and really just suffering from her OCD, she calls on Maggie to come save her. When Maggie arrives, she runs into Richard who found his way there based on Bailey’s record of attendance. With her life flashing before her eyes, Bailey reflects on her upbringing and her past as a surgeon with all the stressful fights and struggles she’s gone through to get to this point in her life. Right before she goes under for emergency surgery to save her life, Bailey asks Maggie to call Ben who is able to get there before she wakes up. Ben announces that he’s quit being a firefighter, but Bailey demands that he go back and never do anything other than what he truly loves.</TD>
</TR>
<TR class="vevent" style="text-align:center;background:#F2F2F2">
<TH scope="row" id="ep305" style="text-align:center">305</TH>
<TD>12</TD>
<TD class="summary" style="text-align:left">"Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger"</TD>
<TD>Jeannot Szwarc</TD>
<TD>Kiley Donovan</TD>
<TD>February 8, 2018<SPAN style="display:none"> (<SPAN class="bday dtstart published updated">2018-02-08</SPAN>)</SPAN></TD>
<TD>7.32<SUP id="cite_ref-harder_31-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-harder-31">[31]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD class="description" colspan="7" style="border-bottom:solid 3px #D6D7D9">As the contest draws near, a competitive edge and tension arise between the doctors and their selected interns vying for millions of dollars. In preparation to surprise Catherine on her birthday, Richard takes salsa dancing lessons with Maggie, who is struggling with the one year anniversary of her mother’s death. Amelia and Alex tag team a pediatric case, in order to save their patient’s ability to sing, as well as retain all mental capabilities. Meredith gets a visit from an old splenectomy patient, who’s back with multiple miniature spleens, which guides Meredith to her idea for the competition, and Jackson gets pulled into his mother’s gender confirmation proposal, despite his wishes.</TD>
</TR>

			<H1 id="firstHeading" class="firstHeading" lang="en">Blood gas tension</H1>
									<DIV id="bodyContent" class="mw-body-content">
									<DIV id="siteSub" class="noprint">From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia</DIV>
								<DIV id="contentSub"></DIV>
												<DIV id="jump-to-nav" class="mw-jump">
					Jump to:					<A href="#mw-head">navigation</A>, 					<A href="#p-search">search</A>
				</DIV>
				<DIV id="mw-content-text" lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr"><DIV class="mw-parser-output"><P><B>Blood gas tension</B> refers to the <A href="/wiki/Partial_pressure" title="Partial pressure">partial pressure</A> of <A href="/wiki/Gas" title="Gas">gases</A> in <A href="/wiki/Blood" title="Blood">blood</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid9563770_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid9563770-1">[1]</A></SUP> There are several significant purposes for measuring gas tension;<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid16215371_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid16215371-2">[2]</A></SUP> the most common gas tensions measured are <A href="/wiki/Oxygen" title="Oxygen">oxygen</A> tension<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid14736638_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid14736638-3">[3]</A></SUP> (P<SUB>x</SUB>O<SUB>2</SUB>), the <A href="/wiki/Carbon_dioxide" title="Carbon dioxide">carbon dioxide</A> tension<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid14736638_3-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid14736638-3">[3]</A></SUP> (P<SUB>x</SUB>CO<SUB>2</SUB>) and <A href="/wiki/Carbon_monoxide" title="Carbon monoxide">carbon monoxide</A> tension<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid14736638_3-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid14736638-3">[3]</A></SUP> (P<SUB>x</SUB>CO). The subscript <I>x</I> in each symbol represents the source of the gas being measured; "<I>a</I>" meaning <A href="/wiki/Artery" title="Artery">arterial</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid14736638_3-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid14736638-3">[3]</A></SUP> "<I>A</I>" being <A href="/wiki/Pulmonary_alveolus" title="Pulmonary alveolus">alveolar</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid14736638_3-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid14736638-3">[3]</A></SUP> "<I>v</I>" being <A href="/wiki/Vein" title="Vein">venous</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid14736638_3-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid14736638-3">[3]</A></SUP> "<I>c</I>" being <A href="/wiki/Capillary" title="Capillary">capillary</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid14736638_3-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid14736638-3">[3]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Blood_gas_test" title="Blood gas test">Blood gas tests</A> (such as <A href="/wiki/Arterial_blood_gas" class="mw-redirect" title="Arterial blood gas">arterial blood gas</A> tests) measure these partial pressures.</P>
<P></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Oxygen_tension">Oxygen tension</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Blood_gas_tension&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Oxygen tension">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DL>
<DT>Arterial blood oxygen tension (normal)</DT>
</DL>
<P><B>P<SUB>a</SUB>O<SUB>2</SUB></B> – Partial pressure of oxygen at sea level (765 <A href="/wiki/MmHg" class="mw-redirect" title="MmHg">mmHg</A>) in <A href="/wiki/Arterial_blood" title="Arterial blood">arterial blood</A> is between 75 mmHg and 100 mmHg.<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid9390851_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid9390851-4">[4]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-pmid17652681_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid17652681-5">[5]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-pmid14569318_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid14569318-6">[6]</A></SUP></P>
<DL>
<DT>Venous blood oxygen tension (normal)</DT>
</DL>
<P><B>P<SUB>v</SUB>O<SUB>2</SUB></B> – Oxygen tension in <A href="/wiki/Venous_blood" title="Venous blood">venous blood</A> at sea level is between 30 mmHg and 40 mmHg.<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid14569318_6-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid14569318-6">[6]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-pmid20018607_7-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid20018607-7">[7]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Carbon_dioxide_tension">Carbon dioxide tension</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Blood_gas_tension&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Carbon dioxide tension">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Carbon dioxide is a by-product of food metabolism and in high amounts has toxic effects including: <A href="/wiki/Dyspnea" class="mw-redirect" title="Dyspnea">dyspnea</A>, <A href="/wiki/Acidosis" title="Acidosis">acidosis</A> and <A href="/wiki/Altered_consciousness" class="mw-redirect" title="Altered consciousness">altered consciousness</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid2535633_8-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid2535633-8">[8]</A></SUP></P>
<DL>
<DT>Arterial blood carbon dioxide tension</DT>
</DL>
<P><B><A href="/wiki/PCO2" title="PCO2">P<SUB>a</SUB>CO<SUB>2</SUB></A></B> – Partial pressure of carbon dioxide at sea level (765 mmHg) in arterial blood is between 35 mmHg and 45 mmHg.<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid9794863_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid9794863-9">[9]</A></SUP></P>
<DL>
<DT>Venous blood carbon dioxide tension</DT>
</DL>
<P><B>P<SUB>v</SUB>CO<SUB>2</SUB></B> – Partial pressure of carbon dioxide at sea level in venous blood is between 40 mmHg and 50 mmHg.<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid9794863_9-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid9794863-9">[9]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Carbon_monoxide_tension">Carbon monoxide tension</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Blood_gas_tension&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Carbon monoxide tension">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DL>
<DT>Arterial carbon monoxide tension (normal)</DT>
</DL>
<P><B>P<SUB>a</SUB>CO</B> – Partial pressure of CO at sea level (765 mmHg) in arterial blood is approximately 0.02. It can be slightly higher in smokers and people living in dense urban areas.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Significance">Significance</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Blood_gas_tension&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Significance">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The partial pressure of gas in blood is significant because it is directly related to ventilation and oxygenation.<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid2661120_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid2661120-10">[10]</A></SUP> When used alongside the pH balance of the blood, the P<SUB>a</SUB>CO<SUB>2</SUB> and HCO<SUB>3</SUB> (and Lactate) suggest to the health care practitioner which interventions, if any, should be made.<SUP id="cite_ref-pmid2661120_10-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid2661120-10">[10]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-pmid3144222_11-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pmid3144222-11">[11]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Equations">Equations</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Blood_gas_tension&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Equations">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Oxygen_content">Oxygen content</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Blood_gas_tension&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Oxygen content">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DL>
<DD><SPAN class="mwe-math-element"><SPAN class="mwe-math-mathml-inline mwe-math-mathml-a11y" style="display: none;"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">

<P>The constant, 1.36, is the amount of oxygen (ml at 1 atmosphere) bound per gram of <A href="/wiki/Hemoglobin" title="Hemoglobin">hemoglobin</A>. The exact value of this constant varies from 1.34 to 1.39, depending on the reference and the way it is derived. The constant 0.0031 represents the amount of oxygen dissolved in plasma. The dissolved-oxygen term is generally small relative to the term for hemoglobin-bound oxygen, but becomes significant at very high P<SUB>a</SUB>O<SUB>2</SUB> (as in a <A href="/wiki/Hyperbaric_chamber" class="mw-redirect" title="Hyperbaric chamber">hyperbaric chamber</A>) or in severe <A href="/wiki/Anemia" title="Anemia">anemia</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP></P>
