<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Plot">Plot</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Perfect_Mate&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Plot">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Kriosian ambassador Briam (<A href="/wiki/Tim_O%27Connor_(actor)" title="Tim O'Connor (actor)">Tim O'Connor</A>) comes on board the <I><A href="/wiki/USS_Enterprise_(NCC-1701-D)" title="USS Enterprise (NCC-1701-D)">Enterprise</A></I> with some cargo, ready for a peace ceremony with the Valtian. As the ship heads to the rendezvous, they save two <A href="/wiki/Ferengi" title="Ferengi">Ferengi</A> from a failing ship. Despite security being assigned, the Ferengi enter the cargo bay and deactivate the stasis field on Briam's cargo, revealing a young Kriosian woman named Kamala (<A href="/wiki/Famke_Janssen" title="Famke Janssen">Famke Janssen</A>). With the Ferengi secured, it is revealed that she is an empathic metamorph who can sense what males around her desire and react appropriately. She was being brought as an arranged marriage to the Valtian representative. Kamala is generating <A href="/wiki/Pheromone" title="Pheromone">pheromones</A> that can affect males around her, which was why she was kept in stasis until the ceremony.</P>
<P>Briam tells Kamala to stay in her quarters, but Captain Picard allows her to travel throughout the ship, with the unaffected Lt. Commander <A href="/wiki/Data_(Star_Trek)" title="Data (Star Trek)">Data</A> (<A href="/wiki/Brent_Spiner" title="Brent Spiner">Brent Spiner</A>) as her escort. This results in a fight nearly breaking out in Ten Forward, when Kamala begins to interact with several miners. The Ferengi seek to bribe Briam to turn Kamala over to them, but he rejects their offer. As he leaves, they attack him, causing him to fall, hit his head, and lose consciousness. The <I>Enterprise</I> turns the Ferengi over to the nearest <A href="/wiki/Starbase" title="Starbase">starbase</A> to stand trial, but Briam is unable to participate in the ceremony. Kamala helps Picard to take on Briam's role, and the two become close. He seeks to resist her abilities and tells her to be herself, and she explains that the woman he wants her to be is who she actually is.</P>
<P>They meet with the Valtian ambassador, Chancellor Alrik (Mickey Cottrell), who is uninterested in the marriage and wants to pursue trade agreements. With the arrangements made, Picard visits Kamala to say goodbye; she tells him that she has permanently bonded with him instead of Alrik. Kamala explains that he has changed her for the better, and will continue in her duty for her people to marry Alrik. At the wedding ceremony, Picard escorts Kamala down the aisle and watches as she marries another. After the newlyweds have returned to the planet, Picard says goodbye to Briam in the <A href="/wiki/Transporter_(Star_Trek)" title="Transporter (Star Trek)">transporter</A> room. When asked how he resisted Kamala, the expression on Picard's face reveals how much of a struggle it has been and how much he feels he has lost.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Production">Production</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Perfect_Mate&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Production">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Writing">Writing</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Perfect_Mate&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Writing">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The story for "The Perfect Mate" was created by <A href="/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Echevarria" title="René Echevarria">René Echevarria</A> and Rueben Leder and then written as a teleplay by Leder and executive producer <A href="/wiki/Michael_Piller" title="Michael Piller">Michael Piller</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENemecek2003199_1-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENemecek2003199-1">[1]</A></SUP> A great deal of edits were made to the script by a number of staff members, and Piller felt that it was a difficult one due to the subject matter. As Piller explained to Echevarria in a memo, he felt that Kamala had to be a well-rounded character which would be loved by the viewer in order for the episode to work.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGrossAltman1993245_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrossAltman1993245-2">[2]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Fellow executive producer <A href="/wiki/Rick_Berman" title="Rick Berman">Rick Berman</A> recalled heated discussions over the content of the script,<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGrossAltman1993245_2-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrossAltman1993245-2">[2]</A></SUP> and following re-writes to the draft, Leder elected to be credited only under the <A href="/wiki/Pseudonym" title="Pseudonym">pseudonym</A> Gary Percante. This was the only time during Piller's tenure as executive producer that a writer chose to be credited under a pseudonym. Piller subsequently praised the episode, saying "We have Beverly argue the point that Kamala's mission amounts to prostitution, and we have Picard taking the other tack; that whether or not we approve, we can't change or interfere with the way these people are. And if you accept <A href="/wiki/Gene_Roddenberry" title="Gene Roddenberry">[Gene] Roddenberry</A>'s vision, which we are built on, you have to respect that."<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENemecek2003200_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENemecek2003200-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Two of the scenes seen in "The Perfect Mate" built upon references in earlier episodes. The morning meeting over tea between Picard and Crusher seen here was previously mentioned in "<A href="/wiki/Qpid" title="Qpid">Qpid</A>", while in "<A href="/wiki/Family_(Star_Trek:_The_Next_Generation)" title="Family (Star Trek: The Next Generation)">Family</A>" there was the mention of Picard taking <A href="/wiki/Piano" title="Piano">piano</A> lessons as a child. In "The Perfect Mate", he relates that these were only briefly taken because his mother wanted him to.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENemecek2003200_3-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENemecek2003200-3">[3]</A></SUP> Four endings were written for the episode, with two filmed. Piller preferred a "trick ending" in which Picard daydreamed of objecting to the wedding, but ultimately with Kamala rejecting both him and Alrik having been enlightened by Picard's influence.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGrossAltman1993245_2-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrossAltman1993245-2">[2]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Casting">Casting</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Perfect_Mate&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Casting">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Famke_Janssen_WonderCon_2013.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="A headshot of a Caucasian woman with brown hair." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/Famke_Janssen_WonderCon_2013.jpg/220px-Famke_Janssen_WonderCon_2013.jpg" width="220" height="275" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/Famke_Janssen_WonderCon_2013.jpg/330px-Famke_Janssen_WonderCon_2013.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/Famke_Janssen_WonderCon_2013.jpg/440px-Famke_Janssen_WonderCon_2013.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1777" data-file-height="2218" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Famke_Janssen_WonderCon_2013.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
Famke Janssen had worked as a model before appearing in "The Perfect Mate".</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>Prior to working on <I>The Next Generation</I>, <A href="/wiki/Famke_Janssen" title="Famke Janssen">Famke Janssen</A> had worked as a model in Europe for seven years.<SUP id="cite_ref-starlog197_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-starlog197-4">[4]</A></SUP> Her first acting role was on the television series <I><A href="/wiki/Fathers_and_Sons_(1986_TV_series)" title="Fathers and Sons (1986 TV series)">Fathers and Sons</A></I>, with <I>Star Trek</I> representing her second acting performance.<SUP id="cite_ref-2016interview_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2016interview-5">[5]</A></SUP> Two days after auditioning for the role of Kamala, she was on set filming the episode.<SUP id="cite_ref-starlog197_4-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-starlog197-4">[4]</A></SUP> She later described how this did not give a great deal of time to prepare for the role, and that new script pages would be delivered on a daily basis through the seven day shoot which she found difficult due to her lack of fluency in English at the time.<SUP id="cite_ref-starlog197_4-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-starlog197-4">[4]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-2016interview_5-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2016interview-5">[5]</A></SUP> However, she said the cast were friendly and described them as a "family". Regarding the make-up, she said that on the first day they created a stencil through which they applied the spots on the following six days. Janssen said that Kamala was "very intelligent and educated".<SUP id="cite_ref-starlog197_4-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-starlog197-4">[4]</A></SUP> Berman described Janssen as "about as beautiful as any woman any of us have ever seen and she gave a delightful performance".<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGrossAltman1993245_2-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrossAltman1993245-2">[2]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Following her appearance in the episode, Janssen was offered a five-year contract to appear in the main cast as <A href="/wiki/Jadzia_Dax" title="Jadzia Dax">Jadzia Dax</A> on <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Trek:_Deep_Space_Nine" title="Star Trek: Deep Space Nine">Star Trek: Deep Space Nine</A></I> but turned it down as she did not want to be tied to a long term series contract,<SUP id="cite_ref-starlog197_4-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-starlog197-4">[4]</A></SUP> and felt it would have made her lazy as an actor. The makeup worn by Janssen was used on the actress cast in that part, <A href="/wiki/Terry_Farrell_(actress)" title="Terry Farrell (actress)">Terry Farrell</A>, although without stencilling.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEErdmannBlock2000245_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErdmannBlock2000245-6">[6]</A></SUP> This was as a result of Berman's rejection of the original <A href="/wiki/Trill_(Star_Trek)" class="mw-redirect" title="Trill (Star Trek)">Trill</A> makeup from "<A href="/wiki/The_Host_(Star_Trek:_The_Next_Generation)" title="The Host (Star Trek: The Next Generation)">The Host</A>", with Kamala's makeup suggested as a replacement.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEWestmore2000133_7-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWestmore2000133-7">[7]</A></SUP> At the time of an interview with <I><A href="/wiki/Starlog" title="Starlog">Starlog</A></I> magazine in 1993, Janssen said that she would be happy to return to <I>The Next Generation</I> to portray Kamala once again.<SUP id="cite_ref-starlog197_4-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-starlog197-4">[4]</A></SUP> She did not return to the series, but went on to appear as <A href="/wiki/Jean_Grey" title="Jean Grey">Jean Grey</A> alongside Stewart in the 2000 film <I><A href="/wiki/X-Men_(film)" title="X-Men (film)">X-Men</A></I> and subsequent films in the <A href="/wiki/X-Men_(film_series)" title="X-Men (film series)">series</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> She found working with Stewart easy when they were reunited, because of their previous work on "The Perfect Mate".<SUP id="cite_ref-2016interview_5-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2016interview-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>
<P>"The Perfect Mate" was one of several episodes of <I>The Next Generation</I> where <A href="/wiki/Max_Grod%C3%A9nchik" title="Max Grodénchik">Max Grodénchik</A> portrayed a Ferengi. He would subsequently audition for the role of <A href="/wiki/Quark_(Star_Trek)" title="Quark (Star Trek)">Quark</A> on <I>Deep Space Nine</I>, but this went to <A href="/wiki/Armin_Shimerman" title="Armin Shimerman">Armin Shimerman</A>. Grodénchik then portrayed "Ferengi Pit Boss" in the pilot of <I>Deep Space Nine</I>, "<A href="/wiki/Emissary_(Star_Trek:_Deep_Space_Nine)" title="Emissary (Star Trek: Deep Space Nine)">Emissary</A>", who was subsequently written to become the brother of Quark, <A href="/wiki/Rom_(Star_Trek)" title="Rom (Star Trek)">Rom</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEReeves-StevensReeves-Stevens19949_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves-StevensReeves-Stevens19949-9">[9]</A></SUP> Michael Snyder went on to appear as another Ferengi in <I>The Next Generation</I> episode "<A href="/wiki/Rascals_(Star_Trek:_The_Next_Generation)" title="Rascals (Star Trek: The Next Generation)">Rascals</A>".<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENemecek2003224_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENemecek2003224-10">[10]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Themes">Themes</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Perfect_Mate&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Themes">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Robin Roberts discussed "The Perfect Mate" in his 1999 book <I>Sexual Generations</I>. He explained that the premise of a perfect mate had been seen elsewhere in science fiction, such as in <I><A href="/wiki/The_Stepford_Wives" title="The Stepford Wives">The Stepford Wives</A></I>, and said that he found it disturbing when works of the genre depicted this as a role model for women.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERoberts199966_11-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoberts199966-11">[11]</A></SUP> He called "The Perfect Mate" the exemplification of the "depiction of woman as a passive reflection of a male partner".<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERoberts199973_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoberts199973-12">[12]</A></SUP> He compared the <A href="/wiki/Federation_(Star_Trek)" class="mw-redirect" title="Federation (Star Trek)">Federation</A> non-interference in a people who treat women as gifts to the involvement of the United States in the <A href="/wiki/Gulf_War" title="Gulf War">Gulf War</A> in defence of Kuwait, a country which limits rights for women.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERoberts199974–75_13-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoberts199974–75-13">[13]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In Chris Gregory's 2000 book <I>Star Trek: Parallel Narratives</I>, he compared "The Perfect Mate" to the <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Trek:_The_Original_Series" title="Star Trek: The Original Series">Star Trek: The Original Series</A></I> episode "<A href="/wiki/Elaan_of_Troyius" title="Elaan of Troyius">Elaan of Troyius</A>" to the <A href="/wiki/Ancient_Greek" title="Ancient Greek">ancient Greek</A> poem the <I><A href="/wiki/Iliad" title="Iliad">Iliad</A></I>. He said that the influence of Picard caused Kamala to abandon any potential sense of happiness and replace it with an increased sense of self-awareness and remove the ability for her to legitimately love Arik.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGregory2000186_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGregory2000186-14">[14]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Reception">Reception</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Perfect_Mate&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Reception">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>"The Perfect Mate" aired during the week commencing May 10, 1992, in <A href="/wiki/Broadcast_syndication" title="Broadcast syndication">broadcast syndication</A>. According to <A href="/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research" title="Nielsen Media Research">Nielsen Media Research</A>, it received ratings of 10.8 percent. This means that it was watched by 10.8 percent of all households watching television during its timeslot. This was the lowest first run episode of the season.<SUP id="cite_ref-ratings_15-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ratings-15">[15]</A></SUP> It was the lowest rating since "<A href="/wiki/In_Theory_(Star_Trek:_The_Next_Generation)" title="In Theory (Star Trek: The Next Generation)">In Theory</A>", broadcast during the <A href="/wiki/Star_Trek:_The_Next_Generation_(season_4)" title="Star Trek: The Next Generation (season 4)">fourth season</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP> and no episode broadcast afterwards during the course of the season received ratings equal or lower.<SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP></P>
<P><I><A href="/wiki/Starlog" title="Starlog">Starlog</A></I> magazine reported in 1993 that the reception from female fans of <I>Star Trek</I> was mostly negative due to the manner in which Kamala was presented,<SUP id="cite_ref-starlog197_4-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-starlog197-4">[4]</A></SUP> while some reviewers offered a similar opinion. Michelle Erica Green, in her review for <A href="/wiki/TrekNation" title="TrekNation">TrekNation</A> in 2013, praised the chemistry between Stewart and Janssen but called it "a terrible episode, an enormous setback in terms of how Next Gen presents women in the 24th century, and the fact that I appreciate several of the performances doesn't mean I don't wish it had never been produced." She questioned that if Kamala's gender was switched about whether the arguments presented in the episode would have remained, and felt it was a missed opportunity to tackle social issues.<SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Keith_DeCandido" title="Keith DeCandido">Keith DeCandido</A> hated the episode in his review for <A href="/wiki/Tor_Books" title="Tor Books">Tor.com</A> in 2012, giving it a score of 2 out of 10, and said that when he first watched it, the episode had left him "seething". He explained that he would "expect a storyline rooted in tiresomely traditional gender roles from a show airing in the late 1960s. Not so much the early 1990s." He said that Janssen was "flat", and did not have any chemistry with Stewart. DeCandido also criticized the Ferengi "at their absolute worst" and the absence of <A href="/wiki/Deanna_Troi" title="Deanna Troi">Deanna Troi</A> from the episode.<SUP id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-19">[19]</A></SUP></P>
<P>However, other reviewers received the episode more positively. Zack Handlen gave the episode a rating of a "B+" in his 2011 review for <I><A href="/wiki/The_A.V._Club" title="The A.V. Club">The A.V. Club</A></I>. He called the Ferengi "as awful as ever", but otherwise praised the episode. He said that Janssen was one of the reasons why it worked, with the evolution of Kamala through "The Perfect Mate" showing "a sense of someone coming into their own as a sexually aware, potentially powerful individual." Handlen compared the situation to the "Elaan of Troyius", and found the imprinting of Kamala on Picard an unexpected twist.<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP> It was ranked in 47th place out of the top 100 of the entire franchise in <A href="/wiki/Charlie_Jane_Anders" title="Charlie Jane Anders">Charlie Jane Anders</A>' list for <A href="/wiki/Io9" title="Io9">io9</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-21">[21]</A></SUP> In the <I><A href="/wiki/Toronto_Sun" title="Toronto Sun">Toronto Sun</A></I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</SPAN>s list of the 50 top moments of the franchise, Janssen's appearance as Kamala was placed 13th.<SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Home_media_release">Home media release</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Perfect_Mate&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Home media release">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>"The Perfect Mate" was first released on <A href="/wiki/VHS" title="VHS">VHS</A> cassette in the United States and Canada on October 7, 1997.<SUP id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-23">[23]</A></SUP> The episode was later released in the United States on November 5, 2002, as part of the season five <A href="/wiki/DVD" title="DVD">DVD</A> box set.<SUP id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-24">[24]</A></SUP> The first <A href="/wiki/Blu_Ray" class="mw-redirect" title="Blu Ray">Blu Ray</A> release was in the United States on November 19, 2013,<SUP id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-25">[25]</A></SUP> followed by the United Kingdom on November 18.<SUP id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-26">[26]</A></SUP></P>

<P>This is a list of the characters from the American television <A href="/wiki/Sitcom" title="Sitcom">sitcom</A> <I><A href="/wiki/Full_House" title="Full House">Full House</A></I> and its sequel series <I><A href="/wiki/Fuller_House_(TV_series)" title="Fuller House (TV series)">Fuller House</A></I>. The former ran for eight seasons on ABC from September 22, 1987 to May 23, 1995. <I>Fuller House</I> followed 21 years later, airing on <A href="/wiki/Netflix" title="Netflix">Netflix</A> beginning February 26, 2016. The first nine episodes of the third season were released on September 22, 2017, and the back nine was released on December 22, 2017.</P>
