<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Early_life">Early life</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Samuel_Prescott&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Early life">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Jonathan_Prescott,_Chester,_Nova_Scotia.png" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Jonathan_Prescott%2C_Chester%2C_Nova_Scotia.png/220px-Jonathan_Prescott%2C_Chester%2C_Nova_Scotia.png" width="220" height="265" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f5/Jonathan_Prescott%2C_Chester%2C_Nova_Scotia.png 1.5x" data-file-width="315" data-file-height="379" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Jonathan_Prescott,_Chester,_Nova_Scotia.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>Samuel Prescott's uncle <A href="/wiki/Jonathan_Prescott_(military_officer)" title="Jonathan Prescott (military officer)">Jonathan Prescott</A></DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>Dr. Samuel Prescott was born August 19, 1751.  He lived in colonial <A href="/wiki/Concord,_Massachusetts" title="Concord, Massachusetts">Concord, Massachusetts</A>, among his large extended family. (His uncle was <A href="/wiki/Jonathan_Prescott_(military_officer)" title="Jonathan Prescott (military officer)">Jonathan Prescott</A>.)  Much of this history was probably passed on to the family by his grand uncle Samuel Prescott, who knew many of the early Prescotts, and was even old enough to remember the first ancestor of the Concord branch of the family, John Prescott,<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> founder of <A href="/wiki/Lancaster,_Massachusetts" title="Lancaster, Massachusetts">Lancaster, Massachusetts</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP> Indeed, the Prescotts and their extended family played an important and often heroic role in colonial history.  These include settling Concord, fighting in colonial wars, and negotiating for the ransom of <A href="/wiki/Mary_Rowlandson" title="Mary Rowlandson">Mary Rowlandson</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Prescott followed in the footsteps of his older brother Benjamin and apprenticed under his father, Abel Prescott, for about seven years.  He appears to have kept an extremely low profile during pre-revolutionary times as well as afterward, as best can be attained.  He did open a practice in Concord, just before or after which time he began to court Lydia Mulliken, daughter of a well-respected Lexington clockmaker who had died in 1767.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP>
</P><P>During the latter part of his <A href="/wiki/Apprenticeship" title="Apprenticeship">apprenticeship</A> or shortly after he began his medical practice, he became an active member in the <A href="/wiki/Patriot_(American_Revolution)" title="Patriot (American Revolution)">patriot movement</A>. There is strong circumstantial evidence that he was an express courier for the <A href="/wiki/Sons_of_Liberty" title="Sons of Liberty">Sons of Liberty</A> and the <A href="/wiki/Committees_of_Correspondence" class="mw-redirect" title="Committees of Correspondence">Committees of Correspondence</A>, and that he was an important liaison between the Concord Defense Committee and <A href="/wiki/John_Hancock" title="John Hancock">John Hancock</A> and other leaders of the patriots.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="The_Ride">The Ride</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Samuel_Prescott&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: The Ride">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>On the evening of April 18, 1775, <A href="/wiki/Paul_Revere" title="Paul Revere">Paul Revere</A> and <A href="/wiki/William_Dawes" title="William Dawes">William Dawes</A> were dispatched by <A href="/wiki/Joseph_Warren" title="Joseph Warren">Joseph Warren</A> to warn the countryside that the British were coming. Prescott was in Lexington at the time to visit with his fiancée, Lydia Mulliken.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> He was also there to report on Concord's readiness, its status in hiding supplies and munitions from the British, and its success in moving cannon to Groton lest it fall into British hands.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> The British wanted the military stores at Concord and had hoped to capture <A href="/wiki/Samuel_Adams" title="Samuel Adams">Samuel Adams</A> and John Hancock in the process.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (April 2017)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>
</P><P>When Prescott left Lexington, it was about 1 a.m. the next morning, April 19.  On his way back to Concord he met Paul Revere and William Dawes, who had just left Lexington shortly before him and were also on their way to Concord—to warn the town that the Redcoats were on the march.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP>
</P><P>When the three continued on to Hartwell's tavern in the lower bounds of Lincoln, they were cut off by four British horseman who were part of a larger scouting party sent out the preceding evening.  Revere was captured but both Prescott and Dawes succeeded in making a run for it.  Prescott did so with a show of artful horsemanship and knowledge of the forest.  Finally losing his pursuers, he circled about and headed quickly to Concord, carrying Revere's warning to his townsmen.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (April 2011)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>
</P><P>Dawes also escaped from his pursuers, but it was after a close chase, a frantic ruse on his part, and a bit of luck. Once he was safe, he considered circling around the patrol and racing on to Concord much as Prescott had, but he heard the Concord town house bell and knew Prescott had made it there, and so he continued on his special mission, for he was only assigned to accompany Revere to Concord.<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP> Prescott, meanwhile, continued west to warn Acton, Massachusetts while his brother <A href="/wiki/Abel_Prescott,_Jr." class="mw-redirect" title="Abel Prescott, Jr.">Abel Prescott, Jr.</A> rode south to warn <A href="/wiki/Sudbury,_Massachusetts" title="Sudbury, Massachusetts">Sudbury</A> and <A href="/wiki/Framingham,_Massachusetts" title="Framingham, Massachusetts">Framingham</A>.  By this time, countless riders were also dispatched from other towns to spread the warning—while bells and cannon were rung or fired to punctuate the danger at hand.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (April 2011)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>
</P><P>Because of  the "midnight" rides of Revere, Dawes, Prescott, and many other expresses (couriers), <A href="/wiki/Minutemen" title="Minutemen">minutemen</A> and <A href="/wiki/Militia" title="Militia">militia</A> everywhere were on the ready, many marching to Concord to effectively engage the British Army at the Battles of Lexington and Concord. Prescott was there to witness the <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Concord" class="mw-redirect" title="Battle of Concord">Battle of Concord</A>, then tried to beat the British back to Lexington to see Lydia Mulliken and her family and to help with the wounded.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP>  He remained at Lexington as a volunteer surgeon for about two weeks, then seems to have disappeared into the war.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (April 2011)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>
</P>
<DIV class="center"><DIV class="thumb tnone"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:802px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Concord_Expedition_and_Patriot_Messengers.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Concord_Expedition_and_Patriot_Messengers.jpg/800px-Concord_Expedition_and_Patriot_Messengers.jpg" width="800" height="341" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/da/Concord_Expedition_and_Patriot_Messengers.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1000" data-file-height="426" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Concord_Expedition_and_Patriot_Messengers.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>A <A href="/wiki/National_Park_Service" title="National Park Service">National Park Service</A> map showing the route of the initial <A href="/wiki/Patriot_(American_Revolution)" title="Patriot (American Revolution)">Patriot</A> messengers including Prescott (purple trail)</DIV></DIV></DIV></DIV>
<H2><SPAN id="Prescott.27s_life_following_.22The_Ride.22"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Prescott's_life_following_"The_Ride"">Prescott's life following "The Ride"</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Samuel_Prescott&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Prescott's life following "The Ride"">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>There is evidence that Prescott went on to serve as a surgeon in the <A href="/wiki/Continental_Army" title="Continental Army">Continental Army</A>, a tradition that he joined the crew of a New England <A href="/wiki/Privateer" title="Privateer">privateer</A>, and a report that he was in prison in <A href="/wiki/City_of_Halifax" class="mw-redirect" title="City of Halifax">Halifax, Nova Scotia</A>, where he may have died between  November 23, 1776 and December 26 (1777?).<SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP>  There is also circumstantial evidence that he served in some medical support capacity out of <A href="/wiki/Fort_Ticonderoga" title="Fort Ticonderoga">Fort Ticonderoga</A> during the invasion attempts against Canada and until about the time of <A href="/wiki/Benedict_Arnold" title="Benedict Arnold">Benedict Arnold</A>'s failed attempts against <A href="/wiki/Sir_Guy_Carleton" class="mw-redirect" title="Sir Guy Carleton">Sir Guy Carleton</A> on <A href="/wiki/Lake_Champlain" title="Lake Champlain">Lake Champlain</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Legacy">Legacy</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Samuel_Prescott&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Legacy">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Prescott's ride is re-enacted every <A href="/wiki/Patriots%27_Day" title="Patriots' Day">Patriots' Day</A> eve (observed) in the Town of Acton. The re-enactment begins in East Acton, continues through Acton Center, and ends at Liberty Tree Farm, where once was the home of a minuteman named Simon Hunt. The distance is approximately five miles (8 km).
</P><P>There are also re-enactments on Patriots' Day (usually the third Monday of April) of the rides of William Dawes and Paul Revere, to commemorate the famous "midnight" ride that began in the evening hours of April 18 and continued on April 19.
</P><P>Prescott's ride is re-enacted every year at midnight April 18–19 at Concord's First Parish Church. The re-enactment is preceded by a Patriots' Ball.  The Minute Men march with fife and drum leading the attendees from the armory to the church. The Captain of the Concord Minute Men reads a message handed him by "Prescott" on horseback.
</P><P>A memorial plaque to Prescott is at his former home in Concord, Massachusetts.<SUP id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14">[14]</A></SUP>
</P>

<P><I><B>Alone</B></I> is an American <A href="/wiki/Reality_television_series" class="mw-redirect" title="Reality television series">reality television series</A> on <A href="/wiki/History_(U.S._TV_channel)" class="mw-redirect" title="History (U.S. TV channel)">the History channel</A>. The first, second and fourth seasons were filmed on northern <A href="/wiki/Vancouver_Island" title="Vancouver Island">Vancouver Island, British Columbia</A>, and the third near <A href="/wiki/Nahuel_Huapi_National_Park" title="Nahuel Huapi National Park">Nahuel Huapi National Park</A> in <A href="/wiki/Patagonia" title="Patagonia">Patagonia</A>, <A href="/wiki/Argentina" title="Argentina">Argentina</A>. It follows the self-documented daily struggles of 10 individuals (7 paired teams in season 4) as they survive in the <A href="/wiki/Wilderness" title="Wilderness">wilderness</A> for as long as possible using a limited amount of survival equipment. With the exception of medical check-ins, the participants are isolated from each other and all other humans. They may "tap out" at any time, or be removed due to failing a medical check-in. The contestant (or team in Season 4) who remains the longest wins a grand prize of $500,000.
</P><P>The series premiered on June 18, 2015. On August 19, before the finale of season 1, it was announced that the series had been renewed for a second season, which would begin production in the fall of 2015 on Vancouver Island, Canada.<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP> Season 2 premiered on April 21, 2016. Season 3 was filmed in the second quarter of 2016 in Patagonia, Argentina and premiered on December 8.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> One day before the season 3 premiere, History announced that casting had begun for season 4.
</P><P>In January 2017, a Danish version of the series premiered with the name <I>Alone in the Wilderness</I> (<A href="/wiki/Danish_language" title="Danish language">Danish</A>: <I lang="da">Alene i vildmarken</I>) on <A href="/wiki/DR3" title="DR3">DR3</A>. It featured ten contestants and was filmed in <A href="/wiki/Northern_Norway" title="Northern Norway">northern Norway</A>. Participants chose 12 items from a list of 18.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP>
</P><P>In the fall of 2017, a Norwegian version aired with 10 contestants spread around a lake with fish. It was near the tree line, so the few, small, mostly birch trees left few land resources. The last contestant tapped out after a little more than a month.
</P><P>The fifth season premiered on June 7, 2018.<SUP id="cite_ref-AloneS5_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-AloneS5-4">[4]</A></SUP>
</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Format_and_rules">Format and rules</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Alone_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Format and rules">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="General_rules_-_all_seasons">General rules - all seasons</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Alone_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: General rules - all seasons">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Contestants are dropped off in remote areas of Northern Vancouver Island (seasons 1-2,4), Patagonia (season 3) and Northern Mongolia (season 5), far enough apart to ensure that they will not come in contact with one another.<SUP id="cite_ref-:0_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-:0-5">[5]</A></SUP> The process begins in mid to late autumn; this adds time pressure to the survival experience as the approaching winter causes temperatures to drop and food to become scarce. Although terrains may differ in each contestant's location, the drop-off zones are assessed in advance to ensure a similar distribution of local resources is available to each contestant.
</P><P>Contestants each select 10 items of survival gear from a pre-approved list of 40, and are issued a kit of standard equipment, clothing and first aid/emergency supplies.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> They are also given a set of cameras to document their daily experiences and emotions. Attempting to live in the wild for as long as possible, the contestants must find food, build shelters, and endure extreme isolation and psychological distress.
</P><P>Contestants who wish to withdraw from the competition for any reason (referred to as "tapping out") may signal a rescue crew using a provided satellite telephone. In addition, medical professionals conduct periodic health checks on the contestants and may, at their discretion, disqualify and evacuate anyone they feel is unable to continue participating safely. The last remaining contestant wins a $500,000 cash prize.<SUP id="cite_ref-:0_5-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-:0-5">[5]</A></SUP> Contestants are warned that the show might last for up to a year.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Season_4">Season 4</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Alone_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Season 4">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Season 4 was also filmed in Northern Vancouver Island but included a team dynamic. Fourteen contestants, consisting of seven family-member pairs, were individually dropped off in remote areas of Northern Vancouver Island. The two members of each team chose 10 items of survival gear to be equally divided between them. The team chose one member to be taken to a campsite; the other began approximately 10 mi (16.09 km) away and was required to hike to the site, using only a <A href="/wiki/Compass" title="Compass">compass</A> and <A href="/wiki/Bearing_(navigation)" title="Bearing (navigation)">bearing</A> to find the way. Either member may tap out at any time, but doing so removed both of them from the competition; in addition, if either member of a team was medically evacuated, both were disqualified. The last remaining team won the $500,000 prize.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Season_5">Season 5</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Alone_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Season 5">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Season 5 contestants were selected from non-winning contestants from Seasons 1 through 4. The rules were otherwise similar to Seasons 1 through 3. 
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Reception">Reception</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Alone_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Reception">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>The series received positive reviews in its first season and outstanding reviews for its third season, and earned a respectable 2.5 million total viewers, placing it in the top three new nonfictional cable series of 2015.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP><SUP class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability"><SPAN title="Verification of this source citation failed to find it supporting or even relevant to the material that cites it (July 2016)">irrelevant citation</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP>
</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Series_overview">Series overview</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Alone_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Series overview">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Season_1">Season 1</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Alone_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Season 1">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The first season premiered on June 18, 2015. It was won by Alan Kay, who lost over 60 pounds during the course of the season. His staple foods were limpets and seaweed. He also consumed mussels, crab, fish and slugs.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> Lucas Miller enjoyed his time on the show and was selected based on his work as a wilderness therapist. His most difficult experience with the show was making honest confessions to the camera.<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP> Sam Larson described his time on the show as "playing in the woods". He set a goal for himself to last 50 days. After he reached his goal, a large storm hit the island, which Larson described as being larger than any he had seen and prompting his decision to leave the island. Larson said that the loneliness and solitude took the most time to adjust to, and that his preparation for the show mostly consisted of mental preparation.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP>
</P>

<DIV class="noviewer thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:202px"><DIV style="position:relative;width:200px;border:1px solid lightgray"><A href="/wiki/File:Canada_British_Columbia_location_map_2.svg" class="image" title="Quatsino is located in British Columbia"><IMG alt="Quatsino is located in British Columbia" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Canada_British_Columbia_location_map_2.svg/200px-Canada_British_Columbia_location_map_2.svg.png" width="200" height="162" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Canada_British_Columbia_location_map_2.svg/300px-Canada_British_Columbia_location_map_2.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Canada_British_Columbia_location_map_2.svg/400px-Canada_British_Columbia_location_map_2.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="2419" data-file-height="1960" /></A><DIV style="position:absolute;top:81.802%;left:46.508%"><DIV style="position:absolute;left:-4px;top:-4px;line-height:0"><IMG alt="Quatsino" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Red_pog.svg/8px-Red_pog.svg.png" title="Quatsino" width="8" height="8" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Red_pog.svg/12px-Red_pog.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Red_pog.svg/16px-Red_pog.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="64" data-file-height="64" /></DIV><DIV style="font-size:90%;line-height:110%;position:absolute;width:6em;top:-0.75em;left:5px;text-align:left"><DIV style="display:inline;padding:1px;float:left">Quatsino</DIV></DIV></DIV></DIV><DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Canada_British_Columbia_location_map_2.svg" title="File:Canada British Columbia location map 2.svg"> </A></DIV>Location of Quatsino in <A href="/wiki/British_Columbia" title="British Columbia">British Columbia</A></DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>The season was shot in <A href="/wiki/Quatsino" title="Quatsino">Quatsino</A> Territory, located near <A href="/wiki/Port_Hardy,_British_Columbia" class="mw-redirect" title="Port Hardy, British Columbia">Port Hardy, British Columbia</A>.
</P><P>Quatsino is a <A href="/wiki/Hamlet_(place)" title="Hamlet (place)">small hamlet</A> of 91 people located on <A href="/wiki/Quatsino_Sound" title="Quatsino Sound">Quatsino Sound</A> in <A href="/wiki/Vancouver_Island" title="Vancouver Island">Northern Vancouver Island, Canada</A>, only accessible by boat or float plane. Its nearest neighbour is <A href="/wiki/Coal_Harbour,_British_Columbia" class="mw-redirect" title="Coal Harbour, British Columbia">Coal Harbour</A>, to the east, about 20 minutes away by boat, and <A href="/wiki/Port_Alice,_British_Columbia" class="mw-redirect" title="Port Alice, British Columbia">Port Alice</A>, to the south, about 40 minutes away by boat. The largest town in the region, Port Hardy, is located about an hour northeast by boat and vehicle.
</P>

<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Season_3">Season 3</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Alone_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=14" title="Edit section: Season 3">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>The third season premiered on December 8, 2016.<SUP id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-21">[21]</A></SUP>  The winner, Zachary Fowler, had lost 70 lbs (a third of his starting body weight) before the end of his stay. The person who stayed the second-longest, Carleigh Fairchild, was pulled out because, at 101 lbs, she had lost nearly 30% of her starting body weight and had a BMI of 16.8. Participants were automatically "pulled" at a BMI of 17 or less. The fourth longest stayer, Dave Nessia, was pulled out when, due to inadequate caloric intake, his <A href="/wiki/Systole" title="Systole">systolic pressure</A> barely exceeded his <A href="/wiki/Diastole" title="Diastole">diastolic pressure</A> (80/60 mmHg), putting him in danger of death due to inadequate perfusion of the internal organs.
</P>

<DIV class="noviewer thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:202px"><DIV style="position:relative;width:200px;border:1px solid lightgray"><A href="/wiki/File:Argentina_location_map.svg" class="image" title="Alone (TV series) is located in Argentina"><IMG alt="Alone (TV series) is located in Argentina" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Argentina_location_map.svg/200px-Argentina_location_map.svg.png" width="200" height="340" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Argentina_location_map.svg/300px-Argentina_location_map.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Argentina_location_map.svg/400px-Argentina_location_map.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1418" data-file-height="2412" /></A><DIV style="position:absolute;top:58.282%;left:20.125%"><DIV style="position:absolute;left:-4px;top:-4px;line-height:0"><IMG alt="Alone (TV series)" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Red_pog.svg/8px-Red_pog.svg.png" title="Alone (TV series)" width="8" height="8" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Red_pog.svg/12px-Red_pog.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Red_pog.svg/16px-Red_pog.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="64" data-file-height="64" /></DIV></DIV></DIV><DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Argentina_location_map.svg" title="File:Argentina location map.svg"> </A></DIV>Location of Lakes Soberania, Montes and Escondido in <A href="/wiki/Patagonia" title="Patagonia">Patagonia</A>, <A href="/wiki/Argentina" title="Argentina">Argentina</A><SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP></DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>The third season was set in Patagonia, Argentina, in South America. The contestants were spread across multiple lakes in the foothills of the Andes mountain range. Unlike in seasons 1 and 2, which were located on the Pacific Ocean, season 3's food resources were mostly limited to brook and rainbow trout, forage, small birds, and the possibility of wild boar. Contestants also were at a disadvantage because they had no access to the flotsam and jetsam that washes up on the Pacific Coast. They also had no salt source.
</P><P>The weather in Patagonia is comparable to that of Vancouver Island, with rainfall averaging 78 inches a year. However, unlike Vancouver Island, snowfall is extremely common in the winter.
</P><P>Predators in Patagonia include wild boar and puma.
</P>

<IMG alt="Portal" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/f/fd/Portal-puzzle.svg/16px-Portal-puzzle.svg.png" title="Portal" width="16" height="14" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/f/fd/Portal-puzzle.svg/24px-Portal-puzzle.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/f/fd/Portal-puzzle.svg/32px-Portal-puzzle.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="32" data-file-height="28" /> <A href="/wiki/Portal:Business_and_economics" title="Portal:Business and economics">Business portal</A></TD></TR><TR><TD style="text-align:right;font-size:115%;padding-top: 0.6em;"><DIV class="plainlinks hlist navbar mini"><UL><LI class="nv-view"><A href="/wiki/Template:Accounting" title="Template:Accounting"><ABBR title="View this template">v</ABBR></A></LI><LI class="nv-talk"><A href="/wiki/Template_talk:Accounting" title="Template talk:Accounting"><ABBR title="Discuss this template">t</ABBR></A></LI><LI class="nv-edit"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:Accounting&action=edit"><ABBR title="Edit this template">e</ABBR></A></LI></UL></DIV></TD></TR></TBODY></TABLE>
<P>In <A href="/wiki/Financial_accountancy" class="mw-redirect" title="Financial accountancy">financial accounting</A>, an <B>asset</B> is an economic <A href="/wiki/Resource" title="Resource">resource</A>. Anything tangible or intangible that can be owned or controlled to produce value and that is held by a company to produce positive <A href="/wiki/Economic_value" class="mw-redirect" title="Economic value">economic value</A> is an asset. Simply stated, assets represent value of <A href="/wiki/Ownership" title="Ownership">ownership</A> that can be converted into <A href="/wiki/Cash" title="Cash">cash</A> (although cash itself is also considered an asset).<SUP id="cite_ref-O'Sullivan_2003_272_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-O'Sullivan_2003_272-1">[1]</A></SUP>
</P><P>The <A href="/wiki/Balance_sheet" title="Balance sheet">balance sheet</A> of a firm records the monetary<SUP id="cite_ref-CPA_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-CPA-2">[2]</A></SUP> value of the assets owned by that firm. It covers money and other valuables belonging to an individual or to a <A href="/wiki/Business" title="Business">business</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-O'Sullivan_2003_272_1-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-O'Sullivan_2003_272-1">[1]</A></SUP> One can classify assets into two major asset classes:  <A href="/wiki/Tangible_property" title="Tangible property">tangible assets</A> and <A href="/wiki/Intangible_assets" class="mw-redirect" title="Intangible assets">intangible assets</A>. Tangible assets contain various subclasses, including <A href="/wiki/Current_asset" title="Current asset">current assets</A> and <A href="/wiki/Fixed_asset" title="Fixed asset">fixed assets</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-FinanceDict_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FinanceDict-3">[3]</A></SUP> Current assets include <A href="/wiki/Inventory" title="Inventory">inventory</A>, while fixed assets include such items as <A href="/wiki/Buildings" class="mw-redirect" title="Buildings">buildings</A> and <A href="/wiki/Capital_equipment" class="mw-redirect" title="Capital equipment">equipment</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-CPA_Finance_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-CPA_Finance-4">[4]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Intangible assets are nonphysical resources and rights that have a value to the firm because they give the firm some kind of advantage in the marketplace. Examples of intangible assets include <A href="/wiki/Goodwill_(accounting)" title="Goodwill (accounting)">goodwill</A>, <A href="/wiki/Copyrights" class="mw-redirect" title="Copyrights">copyrights</A>, <A href="/wiki/Trademarks" class="mw-redirect" title="Trademarks">trademarks</A>, <A href="/wiki/Patents" class="mw-redirect" title="Patents">patents</A> and <A href="/wiki/Computer_program" title="Computer program">computer programs</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-CPA_Finance_4-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-CPA_Finance-4">[4]</A></SUP> and financial assets, including such items as <A href="/wiki/Accounts_receivable" title="Accounts receivable">accounts receivable</A>, <A href="/wiki/Bond_(finance)" title="Bond (finance)">bonds</A> and <A href="/wiki/Stock" title="Stock">stocks</A>.
</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Formal_definition">Formal definition</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Asset&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Formal definition">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>An asset is a resource controlled by the entity as a result of past events and from which future economic benefits are expected to flow to the entity<SUP id="cite_ref-IFRS_for_SMEs_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-IFRS_for_SMEs-5">[5]</A></SUP> (Framework Par 49a).
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Characteristics">Characteristics</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Asset&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Characteristics">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>One of the most widely accepted accounting definitions of asset is the one used by the <A href="/wiki/International_Accounting_Standards_Board" title="International Accounting Standards Board">International Accounting Standards Board</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> The following is a quotation from the IFRS Framework: "An asset is a resource controlled by the enterprise as a result of past events and from which future economic benefits are expected to flow to the enterprise."<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP>
</P><P>This means that:
</P>
<UL><LI>The probable present benefit involve a capacity, singly or in combination with other assets, in the case of profit oriented enterprises, to contribute directly or indirectly to future net <A href="/wiki/Cash_flows" class="mw-redirect" title="Cash flows">cash flows</A>, and, in the case of <A href="/wiki/Nonprofit_organization" title="Nonprofit organization">nonprofit organizations</A>, to provide services;</LI>
<LI>The entity can control access to the benefit;</LI>
<LI>The transaction or event giving rise to the entity's right to, or control of, the benefit has already occurred.</LI></UL>
<P>Employees are not considered assets like machinery is, even though they can generate future economic benefits. This is because an entity does not have sufficient control over its employees to satisfy the Framework's definition of an asset. Resources that are expected to yield benefits only for a short time can also be considered not to be assets, for example in the USA the <A href="/wiki/12_month_rule" title="12 month rule">12 month rule</A> excludes items with a useful life of less than a year.
</P><P>Similarly, in <A href="/wiki/Economics" title="Economics">economics</A> an asset is any form in which <A href="/wiki/Wealth" title="Wealth">wealth</A> can be held.
</P><P>There is a growing analytical interest in assets and asset forms in other <A href="/wiki/Social_science" title="Social science">social sciences</A> too, especially in terms of how a variety of things (e.g. personality, personal data, ecosystems, etc.) can be turned into an asset.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> 
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Accounting">Accounting</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Asset&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Accounting">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>In the <A href="/wiki/Financial_accounting" title="Financial accounting">financial accounting</A> sense of the term, it is not necessary to be able to legally enforce the asset's benefit for qualifying a resource as being an asset, provided the entity can control its use by other means.
</P><P>The <A href="/wiki/Accounting_equation" title="Accounting equation">accounting equation</A> is the mathematical structure of the <A href="/wiki/Balance_sheet" title="Balance sheet">balance sheet</A>. It relates assets, liabilities, and <A href="/wiki/Ownership_equity" class="mw-redirect" title="Ownership equity">owner's equity</A>:
</P>
<DL><DD><A href="/wiki/Assets" class="mw-redirect" title="Assets">Assets</A> = <A href="/wiki/Liability_(financial_accounting)" title="Liability (financial accounting)">Liabilities</A> + Capital (which for a corporation equals <I>owner's equity</I>)</DD>
<DD>Liabilities = Assets − Capital</DD>
<DD><A href="/wiki/Equity_(finance)" title="Equity (finance)">Equity</A> = Assets − Liabilities</DD></DL>
<P>Assets are listed on the <A href="/wiki/Balance_sheet" title="Balance sheet">balance sheet</A>. On a company's balance sheet certain divisions are required by <A href="/wiki/Generally_accepted_accounting_principles" class="mw-redirect" title="Generally accepted accounting principles">generally accepted accounting principles</A> (GAAP), which vary from country to country.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> Assets can be divided into e.g. current assets and fixed assets, often with further subdivisions such as cash, receivables and inventory.
</P><P>Assets are formally controlled and managed within larger organizations via the use of asset tracking tools. These monitor the purchasing, upgrading, servicing, licensing, disposal etc., of both physical and non-physical assets.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Current_assets">Current assets</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Asset&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Current assets">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Current_asset" title="Current asset">Current asset</A></DIV>
<P>Current assets are cash and other assets expected to be converted to cash or consumed either in a year or in the operating cycle (whichever is longer), without disturbing the normal operations of a business. These assets are continually turned over in the course of a business during normal business activity. There are 5 major items included into current assets:
</P>
<OL><LI><B><A href="/wiki/Cash_and_cash_equivalents" title="Cash and cash equivalents">Cash and cash equivalents</A></B> – it is the most <A href="/wiki/Market_liquidity" title="Market liquidity">liquid asset</A>, which includes <A href="/wiki/Currency" title="Currency">currency</A>, <A href="/wiki/Deposit_account" title="Deposit account">deposit accounts</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Negotiable_instrument" title="Negotiable instrument">negotiable instruments</A> (e.g., money orders, cheque, bank drafts).</LI>
<LI><B><A href="/wiki/Investment" title="Investment">Short-term investments</A></B> – include securities bought and held for sale in the near future to generate income on short-term price differences (trading securities).</LI>
<LI><B><A href="/wiki/Receivable" class="mw-redirect" title="Receivable">Receivables</A></B> – usually reported as net of allowance for non-collectable accounts.</LI>
<LI><B><A href="/wiki/Inventory" title="Inventory">Inventory</A></B> – trading these assets is a normal business of a company. The inventory value reported on the <A href="/wiki/Balance_sheet" title="Balance sheet">balance sheet</A> is usually the historical cost or fair market value, whichever is lower. This is known as the "<A href="/wiki/Lower_of_cost_or_market" title="Lower of cost or market">lower of cost or market</A>" rule.</LI>
<LI><B><A href="/wiki/Prepaid_expense" class="mw-redirect" title="Prepaid expense">Prepaid expenses</A></B> – these are expenses paid in cash and recorded as assets before they are used or consumed (common examples are insurance or office supplies). See also <A href="/wiki/Adjusting_entries" title="Adjusting entries">adjusting entries</A>.</LI></OL>
<P><A href="/wiki/Marketable_securities" class="mw-redirect" title="Marketable securities">Marketable securities</A>: Securities that can be converted into cash quickly at a reasonable price.
</P><P>The phrase <I>net current assets</I> (also called <I><A href="/wiki/Working_capital" title="Working capital">working capital</A></I>) is often used and refers to the total of current assets less the total of current <A href="/wiki/Liability_(accounting)" class="mw-redirect" title="Liability (accounting)">liabilities</A>.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Long-term_investments">Long-term investments</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Asset&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Long-term investments">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Often referred to simply as "investments". Long-term investments are to be held for many years and are not intended to be disposed of in the near future. This group usually consists of three types of investments:
</P>
<OL><LI>Investments in securities such as bonds, common stock, or long-term notes.</LI>
<LI>Investments in fixed assets not used in operations (e.g., land held for sale).</LI>
<LI>Investments in special funds (e.g. sinking funds or pension funds).</LI></OL>
<P>Different forms of <A href="/wiki/Insurance" title="Insurance">insurance</A> may also be treated as long term investments.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Fixed_assets">Fixed assets</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Asset&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Fixed assets">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Fixed_asset" title="Fixed asset">Fixed asset</A></DIV>
<P>Also referred to as PPE (property, plant, and equipment), these are purchased for continued and long-term use in earning <A href="/wiki/Profit_(economics)" title="Profit (economics)">profit</A> in a business. This group includes as an asset <A href="/wiki/Land_(economics)" title="Land (economics)">land</A>, <A href="/wiki/Building" title="Building">buildings</A>, <A href="/wiki/Machinery" class="mw-redirect" title="Machinery">machinery</A>, <A href="/wiki/Furniture" title="Furniture">furniture</A>, <A href="/wiki/Tool" title="Tool">tools</A>, <A href="/wiki/Information_technology" title="Information technology">IT</A> equipment, e.g., laptops, and certain wasting resources e.g., timberland and <A href="/wiki/Mineral" title="Mineral">minerals</A>. They are written off against <A href="/wiki/Profit_(accounting)" title="Profit (accounting)">profits</A> over their anticipated life by charging <A href="/wiki/Depreciation" title="Depreciation">depreciation</A> expenses (with exception of land assets). Accumulated depreciation is shown in the face of the balance sheet or in the notes. An asset is an important factor in a balance sheet.
</P><P>These are also called <A href="/wiki/Capital_asset" title="Capital asset">capital assets</A> in <A href="/wiki/Management_accounting" title="Management accounting">management accounting</A>.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Intangible_assets">Intangible assets</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Asset&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Intangible assets">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Intangible_asset" title="Intangible asset">Intangible asset</A></DIV>
<P>Intangible assets lack of physical substance and usually are very hard to evaluate. They include <A href="/wiki/Patent" title="Patent">patents</A>, <A href="/wiki/Copyright" title="Copyright">copyrights</A>, <A href="/wiki/Franchising" title="Franchising">franchises</A>, <A href="/wiki/Goodwill_(accounting)" title="Goodwill (accounting)">goodwill</A>, <A href="/wiki/Trademark" title="Trademark">trademarks</A>, <A href="/wiki/Trade_name" title="Trade name">trade names</A>, etc. These assets are (according to US GAAP) amortized to expense over 5 to 40 years with the exception of goodwill.
</P><P><A href="/wiki/Website" title="Website">Websites</A> are treated differently in different countries and may fall under either tangible or intangible assets.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Tangible_assets">Tangible assets</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Asset&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Tangible assets">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Tangible assets are those that have a physical substance, such as <A href="/wiki/Currency" title="Currency">currencies</A>, <A href="/wiki/Buildings" class="mw-redirect" title="Buildings">buildings</A>, <A href="/wiki/Real_estate" title="Real estate">real estate</A>, <A href="/wiki/Vehicles" class="mw-redirect" title="Vehicles">vehicles</A>, <A href="/wiki/Inventory" title="Inventory">inventories</A>, <A href="/wiki/Capital_equipment" class="mw-redirect" title="Capital equipment">equipment</A>, <A href="/wiki/Private_collection" title="Private collection">art collections</A>, <A href="/wiki/Precious_metals" class="mw-redirect" title="Precious metals">precious metals</A>, <A href="/wiki/Rare-earth_metals" class="mw-redirect" title="Rare-earth metals">rare-earth metals</A>, Industrial metals, and crops.
</P><P><A href="/wiki/Depreciation" title="Depreciation">Depreciation</A> is applied to tangible assets when those assets have an anticipated lifespan of more than one year. This process of depreciation is used instead of allocating the entire expense to one year.<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Tangible assets such as art, furniture, stamps, gold, wine, toys and books have become recognized as an asset class in their own right<SUP id="cite_ref-ReferenceA_11-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ReferenceA-11">[11]</A></SUP> and many high-net-worth individuals will seek to include these tangible assets as part of their overall asset portfolio. This has created a need for <A href="/wiki/Tangible_asset_managers" class="mw-redirect" title="Tangible asset managers">tangible asset managers</A>.
</P>

<P>The <B>Medical University of Vienna</B> (<A href="/wiki/German_language" title="German language">German</A>: <I>Medizinische Universität Wien</I>) is a public <A href="/wiki/University" title="University">university</A> located in <A href="/wiki/Vienna" title="Vienna">Vienna</A>, <A href="/wiki/Austria" title="Austria">Austria</A>. It is the direct successor to the <A href="/wiki/Faculty_of_medicine" class="mw-redirect" title="Faculty of medicine">faculty of medicine</A> at the <A href="/wiki/University_of_Vienna" title="University of Vienna">University of Vienna</A>, founded in 1365 by <A href="/wiki/Rudolf_IV,_Duke_of_Austria" title="Rudolf IV, Duke of Austria">Rudolf IV, Duke of Austria</A>. As one of the <A href="/wiki/List_of_oldest_universities_in_continuous_operation" title="List of oldest universities in continuous operation">oldest medical schools in the world</A>, it is the oldest in the German-speaking countries, and was the second medical faculty in the <A href="/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire" title="Holy Roman Empire">Holy Roman Empire</A>, after the <A href="/wiki/Charles_University_of_Prague" class="mw-redirect" title="Charles University of Prague">Charles University of Prague</A>.
</P><P>The Medical University of Vienna is the largest medical organisation in Austria, as well as one of the top-level research institutions in <A href="/wiki/Europe" title="Europe">Europe</A> and provides Europe's largest hospital, the <A href="/wiki/Vienna_General_Hospital" title="Vienna General Hospital">Vienna General Hospital</A>, with all of its medical staff.<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP>
It consists of 31 university clinics and clinical institutes, and 12 medical-theoretical departments, which perform around 48,000 <A href="/wiki/Surgery" title="Surgery">operations</A> each year. The Vienna General Hospital has about 100,000 <A href="/wiki/Patients" class="mw-redirect" title="Patients">patients</A> treated as inpatients and 605,000 treated as outpatients each year.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP>
</P><P>There have been seven <A href="/wiki/Nobel_prize" class="mw-redirect" title="Nobel prize">Nobel prize</A> laureates affiliated with the medical faculty, and fifteen in total with the University of Vienna. These include <A href="/wiki/Robert_B%C3%A1r%C3%A1ny" class="mw-redirect" title="Robert Bárány">Robert Bárány</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Julius_Wagner-Jauregg" title="Julius Wagner-Jauregg">Julius Wagner-Jauregg</A><SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP> and <A href="/wiki/Karl_Landsteiner" title="Karl Landsteiner">Karl Landsteiner</A>, the discoverer of the ABO <A href="/wiki/Blood_type" title="Blood type">blood type</A> system and the <A href="/wiki/Rhesus_factor" class="mw-redirect" title="Rhesus factor">Rhesus factor</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Sigmund_Freud" title="Sigmund Freud">Sigmund Freud</A> qualified as a doctor at the medical faculty and worked as a doctor and lecturer at the General Hospital,<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> carrying out research into cerebral palsy, aphasia and microscopic neuroanatomy.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP>
</P><P>In the 2014–15 Times Higher Education Rankings, the Medical University of Vienna is listed among the top 15 medical schools in <A href="/wiki/Europe" title="Europe">Europe</A> and  49th in the world. (Clinical, Pre-Clinical and Health).<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP>
</P><P>In 2016, there were 6,093 applicants for 660 places in medicine proper and 80 in dentistry, which corresponds to an admission rate of about 12.14%.<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP> Admission is based upon ranking in an admission test called "MedAT", which is carried out every summer in conjunction with the three other public medical schools of Austria: the <A href="/wiki/Medical_University_of_Graz" title="Medical University of Graz">Medical University of Graz</A>, the <A href="/wiki/Medical_University_of_Innsbruck" title="Medical University of Innsbruck">Medical University of Innsbruck</A> and the Medical Faculty at the <A href="/wiki/Johannes_Kepler_University_Linz" title="Johannes Kepler University Linz">Johannes Kepler University Linz</A>.
</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="History">History</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Medical_University_of_Vienna&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: History">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Founding">Founding</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Medical_University_of_Vienna&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Founding">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Muw_herbst.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Muw_herbst.jpg/220px-Muw_herbst.jpg" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Muw_herbst.jpg/330px-Muw_herbst.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Muw_herbst.jpg/440px-Muw_herbst.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1024" data-file-height="682" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Muw_herbst.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>Department of studies, Medical University of Vienna.</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:AKH_Wien_MedUniWien.JPG" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/AKH_Wien_MedUniWien.JPG/220px-AKH_Wien_MedUniWien.JPG" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/AKH_Wien_MedUniWien.JPG/330px-AKH_Wien_MedUniWien.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/AKH_Wien_MedUniWien.JPG/440px-AKH_Wien_MedUniWien.JPG 2x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1200" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:AKH_Wien_MedUniWien.JPG" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>View of Vienna, Austria at dusk from the roof of the Vienna General Hospital (AKH Wien).</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="From_the_middle_ages_to_the_Age_of_Enlightenment">From the middle ages to the <A href="/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment" title="Age of Enlightenment">Age of Enlightenment</A></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Medical_University_of_Vienna&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: From the middle ages to the Age of Enlightenment">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>As the founding member of the <I>Alma mater Rudolfina</I> (<A href="/wiki/University_of_Vienna" title="University of Vienna">University of Vienna</A>) founded in 1365, the medical faculty was already widely renowned in <A href="/wiki/Medieval" class="mw-redirect" title="Medieval">medieval</A> times as an authority in medicine. Faculty records from as far back as 1399 document its mediation in disputes between barber surgeons, midwives, and local landowners. During the reign of <A href="/wiki/Maria_Theresia" class="mw-redirect" title="Maria Theresia">Maria Theresia</A>, Viennese medicine first attained international significance. The Habsburg Monarch summoned the Dutch physician, <A href="/wiki/Gerard_van_Swieten" title="Gerard van Swieten">Gerard van Swieten</A>, to Vienna. He in turn laid the foundation for the Vienna Medical School and paved the way for other leading figures. <A href="/wiki/Anton_de_Haen" title="Anton de Haen">Anton de Haen</A>, <A href="/wiki/Maximilian_Stoll" title="Maximilian Stoll">Maximilian Stoll</A>, <A href="/w/index.php?title=Lorenz_Gasser&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Lorenz Gasser (page does not exist)">Lorenz Gasser</A>, <A href="/wiki/Anton_von_St%C3%B6rck" title="Anton von Störck">Anton von Störck</A>, and the discoverer of the <A href="/wiki/Percussion" class="mw-redirect" title="Percussion">percussion</A> technique, <A href="/wiki/Leopold_Auenbrugger" title="Leopold Auenbrugger">Leopold Auenbrugger</A>, all taught and conducted research in the imperial city. Based on longstanding traditions, what now is referred to as "bedside teaching" also became the paradigmatic educational method during this period.
</P><P>When the Vienna General Hospital opened in 1784, physicians acquired a new facility that gradually developed into the most important research center. During the 19th century, the "Second Viennese Medical School" emerged with the contributions of physicians such as <A href="/wiki/Karl_Rokitansky" class="mw-redirect" title="Karl Rokitansky">Karl Rokitansky</A>, <A href="/wiki/Josef_Skoda" class="mw-redirect" title="Josef Skoda">Josef Skoda</A>, <A href="/wiki/Ferdinand_von_Hebra" class="mw-redirect" title="Ferdinand von Hebra">Ferdinand von Hebra</A> and <A href="/wiki/Ignaz_Philipp_Semmelweis" class="mw-redirect" title="Ignaz Philipp Semmelweis">Ignaz Philipp Semmelweis</A>. Basic medical science expanded and specialization advanced. Furthermore, the first <A href="/wiki/Dermatology" title="Dermatology">dermatology</A>, <A href="/wiki/Eye" title="Eye">eye</A>, as well as <A href="/wiki/Otolaryngology" class="mw-redirect" title="Otolaryngology">otolaryngology</A> clinics in the world were founded in Vienna.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP>
</P>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Wien-Alsergrund,-Spitalgasse-4,-Pathologisch-Anatomisches-Institut-(1898).jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Wien-Alsergrund%2C-Spitalgasse-4%2C-Pathologisch-Anatomisches-Institut-%281898%29.jpg/220px-Wien-Alsergrund%2C-Spitalgasse-4%2C-Pathologisch-Anatomisches-Institut-%281898%29.jpg" width="220" height="113" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Wien-Alsergrund%2C-Spitalgasse-4%2C-Pathologisch-Anatomisches-Institut-%281898%29.jpg/330px-Wien-Alsergrund%2C-Spitalgasse-4%2C-Pathologisch-Anatomisches-Institut-%281898%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Wien-Alsergrund%2C-Spitalgasse-4%2C-Pathologisch-Anatomisches-Institut-%281898%29.jpg/440px-Wien-Alsergrund%2C-Spitalgasse-4%2C-Pathologisch-Anatomisches-Institut-%281898%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2362" data-file-height="1211" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Wien-Alsergrund,-Spitalgasse-4,-Pathologisch-Anatomisches-Institut-(1898).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>The Pathological–Anatomical Institute in 1898.</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<H4><SPAN id="At_the_height_of_the_Austro.E2.80.93Hungarian_Empire"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="At_the_height_of_the_Austro–Hungarian_Empire">At the height of the <A href="/wiki/Austro%E2%80%93Hungarian_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Austro–Hungarian Empire">Austro–Hungarian Empire</A></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Medical_University_of_Vienna&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: At the height of the Austro–Hungarian Empire">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>At the beginning of the 20th century, Viennese Medicine belonged to the first class internationally. <A href="/wiki/Clemens_von_Pirquet" title="Clemens von Pirquet">Clemens von Pirquet</A> defined the concepts of "allergy" and "serum sickness," <A href="/w/index.php?title=Ernst_Peter_Pick&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Ernst Peter Pick (page does not exist)">Ernst Peter Pick</A> conducted significant experiments on the chemical specificity of immunological reactions, and the Vienna School of Dentistry (founded by <A href="/w/index.php?title=Bernhard_Gotlieb&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Bernhard Gotlieb (page does not exist)">Bernhard Gotlieb</A>) reached its zenith in the 1920s. All four Nobel Prizes, which were granted to (former) Viennese physicians during the next decades <A href="/wiki/Robert_B%C3%A1r%C3%A1ny" class="mw-redirect" title="Robert Bárány">Robert Bárány</A> (1914), <A href="/wiki/Julius_Wagner-Jauregg" title="Julius Wagner-Jauregg">Julius Wagner-Jauregg</A> (1927), <A href="/wiki/Karl_Landsteiner" title="Karl Landsteiner">Karl Landsteiner</A> (1930), and <A href="/wiki/Otto_Loewi" title="Otto Loewi">Otto Loewi</A> (1936)], were the result of work undertaken at this time. The excellent tradition and research extended well into the <A href="/wiki/First_Austrian_Republic" title="First Austrian Republic">First Austrian Republic</A>. Under the auspices of the Medical Association of Vienna, which was founded in Vienna, well-received postgraduate courses for doctors worldwide were organized into the 1930s.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="During_the_Second_World_War">During the Second World War</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Medical_University_of_Vienna&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: During the Second World War">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>With the annexation of Austria by <A href="/wiki/National_Socialist_Germany" class="mw-redirect" title="National Socialist Germany">National Socialist Germany</A> on 13 March 1938 the darkest phase in Viennese medicine began. More than half of the University medical instructors, mostly those of <A href="/wiki/Jewish" class="mw-redirect" title="Jewish">Jewish</A> descent, and 65% of Viennese physicians were dismissed. Many renowned researchers, physicians, and students were forced to <A href="/wiki/Emigrate" class="mw-redirect" title="Emigrate">emigrate</A> or died in <A href="/wiki/Concentration_camps" class="mw-redirect" title="Concentration camps">concentration camps</A> and under other tragic circumstances.
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="After_the_Second_World_War">After the Second World War</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Medical_University_of_Vienna&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: After the Second World War">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>In the aftermath of <A href="/wiki/World_War_II" title="World War II">World War II</A> difficult years lay ahead of the University. The past glory had faded considerably. Moreover, 75% of all university medical instructors had to be dismissed because of their moderate to heavy involvement with the National Socialist regime. They were gradually replaced by a newly trained generation of educators. This double rupture in Viennese Medicine, which occurred in just a few years, caused repercussions that lasted for long after the war.<SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="From_the_Faculty_of_Medicine_of_the_University_of_Vienna_to_the_Medical_University_of_Vienna">From the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Vienna to the Medical University of Vienna</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Medical_University_of_Vienna&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: From the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Vienna to the Medical University of Vienna">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:University_Vienna_Oct._2006_002.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/University_Vienna_Oct._2006_002.jpg/220px-University_Vienna_Oct._2006_002.jpg" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/University_Vienna_Oct._2006_002.jpg/330px-University_Vienna_Oct._2006_002.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/University_Vienna_Oct._2006_002.jpg/440px-University_Vienna_Oct._2006_002.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1536" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:University_Vienna_Oct._2006_002.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>The Medical University of Vienna was the University of Vienna's faculty of medicine during 639 years before becoming a wholly independent university.</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>After the independence of the medical faculty as an independent institution the newly founded pure medical university could reposition itself in international research and regain international recognition.<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP> For example, in the fields of <A href="/w/index.php?title=Bionic_reconstruction&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Bionic reconstruction (page does not exist)">bionic reconstruction</A>, some notable results could be achieved. A <A href="/wiki/United_Kingdom" title="United Kingdom">British</A> soldier who lost his arm during the <A href="/wiki/War_in_Afghanistan_(2001%E2%80%93present)" title="War in Afghanistan (2001–present)">Afghanistan war</A> received a bionic reconstruction at the department of surgery of the <A href="/wiki/Vienna_General_Hospital" title="Vienna General Hospital">Vienna General Hospital</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14">[14]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP>
Furthermore, the Vienna General Hospital and Medical University of Vienna are the largest centre for lung transplantation in Europe and the second-largest lung transplantation centre worldwide after the <A href="/wiki/University_of_Pittsburgh" title="University of Pittsburgh">University of Pittsburgh</A>. Up until 2009, over 1,000 lung transplants had been performed and currently about 100 transplantations are carried out per year.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP>
</P><P>The Medical University of Vienna is the reference center of <A href="/wiki/Siemens" title="Siemens">Siemens</A> for the seven <A href="/wiki/Tesla_(unit)" title="Tesla (unit)">Tesla</A> <A href="/wiki/Magnetic_resonance_imaging" title="Magnetic resonance imaging">magnetic resonance imaging</A> scanner "MAGNETOM 7T". Founded in 2003, the High Field MR Centre (HFMR) acts today as a core research facility for the Medical University of Vienna. It combines basic research and development of methods with a strong focus on applications in neuroscience, musculoskeletal research, oncology and metabolism. The declared goal is to validate the potential of ultra-high field (UHF) MRI in clinical applications.<SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP>
</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Studies">Studies</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Medical_University_of_Vienna&action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section: Studies">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Currently, there are five eligible programmes:
</P>
<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Medicine" title="Medicine">Medicine</A></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Dentistry" title="Dentistry">Dentistry</A></LI></UL>
<P>Medicine and dentistry both are of a duration of six years and require higher education entrance qualification. In <A href="/wiki/Austria" title="Austria">Austria</A> and <A href="/wiki/Switzerland" title="Switzerland">Switzerland</A> this would correspond to a <A href="/wiki/Matura" title="Matura">Matura</A>, in <A href="/wiki/Germany" title="Germany">Germany</A> the <A href="/wiki/Abitur" title="Abitur">Abitur</A> or similar qualifications from other <A href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">EU</A> countries.
Language of instruction is <A href="/wiki/German_language" title="German language">German</A>, but usually students are expected to be able to be fluent in <A href="/wiki/English_language" title="English language">English</A>. A diploma thesis is required to graduate and can be written in German or English.
</P><P>The courses of study lead to the degree of "Dr. med. univ." for medical doctors and "Dr. med. dent." for dentists, which correspond to <A href="/wiki/Doctor_of_Medicine" title="Doctor of Medicine">MD</A> in the <A href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</A> or MBBS or MBChB in the <A href="/wiki/United_Kingdom" title="United Kingdom">United Kingdom</A>.
Graduates have the right to move freely within the <A href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</A> and to start a specialty training.
</P>
<UL><LI>Medical informatics</LI></UL>
<P>Medical informatics is a master's degree and requires a bachelor's degree (<A href="/wiki/Bologna_Process" title="Bologna Process">Bologna Process</A>) for application.
</P>
<UL><LI>Programme of Applied medical science</LI>
<LI>PhD</LI></UL>
<P>Applied medical science and PhD both are postdoc programmes i.e. require a medical degree or similar.
For students of the university, possibility is given to start the PhD-programme during the medical programme.
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Museum">Museum</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Medical_University_of_Vienna&action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section: Museum">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Josephinum_P2.JPG" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Josephinum_P2.JPG/220px-Josephinum_P2.JPG" width="220" height="91" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Josephinum_P2.JPG/330px-Josephinum_P2.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Josephinum_P2.JPG/440px-Josephinum_P2.JPG 2x" data-file-width="7660" data-file-height="3168" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Josephinum_P2.JPG" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>The early-classicistic Josephinum was built in 1785 under <A href="/wiki/Joseph_II_of_Austria" class="mw-redirect" title="Joseph II of Austria">Joseph II of Austria</A>. It now houses the museum for anatomical wax models and, along with the Florentine Library, is among the largest in Europe.<SUP id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-19">[19]</A></SUP></DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>The Museum of the Medical University is mainly housed in the "Josephinum", designed and built in 1783-1785 to house the medical-surgical academy.
The building includes a six-room collection of 1,192 wax anatomical and obstrectical models made in Florence by <A href="/wiki/Clemente_Susini" title="Clemente Susini">Clemente Susini</A> under the supervision of <A href="/wiki/Paolo_Mascagni" title="Paolo Mascagni">Paolo Mascagni</A> between 1784 and 1788.<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP>
</P>

<P><I><B>Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves</B></I> is a 1991 American <A href="/wiki/Romance_film" title="Romance film">romantic</A> <A href="/wiki/Action_film#Subgenres" title="Action film">action adventure film</A>, based on the English folk tale of <A href="/wiki/Robin_Hood" title="Robin Hood">Robin Hood</A> which originated in the 15th century. The film was directed by <A href="/wiki/Kevin_Reynolds_(director)" title="Kevin Reynolds (director)">Kevin Reynolds</A>. The film's principal cast includes <A href="/wiki/Kevin_Costner" title="Kevin Costner">Kevin Costner</A> as <A href="/wiki/Robin_Hood" title="Robin Hood">Robin Hood</A>, <A href="/wiki/Morgan_Freeman" title="Morgan Freeman">Morgan Freeman</A> as Azeem, <A href="/wiki/Christian_Slater" title="Christian Slater">Christian Slater</A> as <A href="/wiki/Will_Scarlet" title="Will Scarlet">Will Scarlet</A>, <A href="/wiki/Mary_Elizabeth_Mastrantonio" title="Mary Elizabeth Mastrantonio">Mary Elizabeth Mastrantonio</A> as <A href="/wiki/Maid_Marian" title="Maid Marian">Maid Marian</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Alan_Rickman" title="Alan Rickman">Alan Rickman</A> as the <A href="/wiki/Sheriff_of_Nottingham" title="Sheriff of Nottingham">Sheriff of Nottingham</A>.</P>
<P>The film grossed over $390 million worldwide, ranking as the <A href="/wiki/1991_in_film#Highest-grossing_films_(international)" title="1991 in film">second-highest-grossing film</A> of 1991. For his role as George, Sheriff of Nottingham, Rickman received the <A href="/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role" title="BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role">BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role</A>. The film's theme song, "<A href="/wiki/(Everything_I_Do)_I_Do_It_for_You" title="(Everything I Do) I Do It for You">(Everything I Do) I Do It for You</A>", by <A href="/wiki/Bryan_Adams" title="Bryan Adams">Bryan Adams</A>, was nominated for the <A href="/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Song" class="mw-redirect" title="Academy Award for Best Song">Academy Award for Best Song</A> and won the <A href="/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Song_Written_for_Visual_Media" title="Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media">Grammy Award for Best Song Written Specifically for a Motion Picture or Television</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Plot">Plot</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Robin_Hood:_Prince_of_Thieves&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Plot">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P><A href="/wiki/Robin_Hood" title="Robin Hood">Robin</A> of <A href="/wiki/Loxley,_South_Yorkshire" title="Loxley, South Yorkshire">Locksley</A> — an English nobleman who joined <A href="/wiki/Richard_I_of_England" title="Richard I of England">Richard the Lionheart, King of England</A> in the <A href="/wiki/Third_Crusade" title="Third Crusade">Third Crusade</A> — is imprisoned in <A href="/wiki/Jerusalem" title="Jerusalem">Jerusalem</A> along with his comrade, Peter Dubois. Facing the amputation of Peter's hand by the <A href="/wiki/Ayyubid_dynasty" title="Ayyubid dynasty">Ayyubid</A> prison guards, Robin escapes with Peter, saving the life of a <A href="/wiki/Moors" title="Moors">Moor</A> named Azeem in the process. Robin, Peter, and Azeem escape through a sewer and into an alley, but Peter is shot and mortally wounded by an archer. Before making his last stand against the approaching guards, Peter has Robin swear to protect his sister, Marian. Robin returns to <A href="/wiki/England" title="England">England</A> with Azeem, who has vowed to accompany him until Azeem's <A href="/wiki/Life-debt" class="mw-redirect" title="Life-debt">life-debt</A> to Robin is repaid.</P>
<P>In England, with King Richard away in France, the cruel <A href="/wiki/Sheriff_of_Nottingham" title="Sheriff of Nottingham">Sheriff of Nottingham</A> rules over the land, aided by his cousin <A href="/wiki/Guy_of_Gisbourne" title="Guy of Gisbourne">Guy of Gisbourne</A>, the <A href="/wiki/Witchcraft" title="Witchcraft">witch</A> Mortianna, and the corrupt <A href="/wiki/Bishop_of_Hereford_(Robin_Hood)" title="Bishop of Hereford (Robin Hood)">Bishop of Hereford</A>. At Locksley Castle, Robin's father, who is loyal to <A href="/wiki/Richard_I_of_England" title="Richard I of England">King Richard</A>, is killed by the Sheriff's men after refusing to join them.</P>
<P>Robin returns to England to find his father dead, his home in ruins, and the Sheriff and his men oppressing the people. After telling Marian of Peter's demise, and while fleeing the Sheriff's forces afterwards, Robin and Azeem encounter a band of outlaws hiding in <A href="/wiki/Sherwood_Forest" title="Sherwood Forest">Sherwood Forest</A>, led by <A href="/wiki/Little_John" title="Little John">Little John</A>. Among the band is <A href="/wiki/Will_Scarlet" title="Will Scarlet">Will Scarlet</A>, who holds a belligerent grudge against Robin. Robin assumes command of the group, training them to defend themselves and fight against Nottingham. They rob soldiers and convoys that pass through the forest, then distribute the stolen wealth among the poor. One of their early targets is <A href="/wiki/Friar_Tuck" title="Friar Tuck">Friar Tuck</A>, who subsequently joins these <A href="/wiki/Merry_Men" title="Merry Men">Merry Men</A>. Marian begins to sympathize with the band and renders Robin any aid she can muster. Robin's successes infuriate the Sheriff, who increases the mistreatment of the people, resulting in greater local support for Robin Hood.</P>
<P>The Sheriff kills Gisbourne for his failure to prevent the looting of several convoys, and hires <A href="/wiki/Celts" title="Celts">Celtic warriors</A> from <A href="/wiki/Scotland" title="Scotland">Scotland</A> to assist his forces in assaulting the hideout. The Sheriff manages to locate the outlaws' hideout and launches an attack, destroying the refuge and capturing most of the outlaws. With the Bishop's help, the Sherrif has Marian confined when she tries to summon help from France. To consolidate his claim to the throne, the Sheriff proposes to Marian (who is Richard's cousin), claiming that if she accepts, he will spare the lives of the captured outlaws. Nevertheless, several of the rebels are due to be executed by hanging as part of the wedding celebration. Among the captured is Will Scarlet, who makes a deal with the Sheriff to find and kill Robin in exchange for his freedom.</P>
<P>Will meets up with Robin and a handful of his aides who survived the Celt's assault. Will informs Robin of the Sheriff's plans to marry Marian and execute Robin's men. Will continues to display anger against Robin, which motivates Robin to question why Will hates him so much. Will then reveals himself to be Robin's younger <A href="/wiki/Legitimacy_(family_law)" title="Legitimacy (family law)">illegitimate</A> <A href="/wiki/Half-brother" class="mw-redirect" title="Half-brother">half-brother</A>; Will's mother was a peasant woman with whom Robin's father took comfort after Robin's mother died. Robin's anger toward his father caused him to separate from her and leave Will fatherless. Despite his anger, Robin is overjoyed to learn that he has a brother, and reconciles with Will.</P>
<P>On the day of the wedding and hangings, Robin and his men infiltrate Nottingham Castle, freeing the prisoners. Although Robin's band originally planned to free their friends and retreat, Azeem reveals himself and his willingness to fight the Sheriff, inciting the peasants to revolt. After a fierce fight, Robin kills the Sheriff, but is attacked by Mortianna with a spear. Azeem slays Mortianna, fulfilling his life-debt to Robin. Tuck kills the Bishop by burdening him with treasure and <A href="/wiki/Defenestration" title="Defenestration">throwing him out a window</A>.</P>
<P>Robin and Marian profess their love for each other and are married in the forest. Their wedding is briefly interrupted by King Richard, who blesses the marriage and thanks Robin for his deeds.</P>
