<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Characteristics">Characteristics</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Characteristics">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Concept_and_creation">Concept and creation</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Concept and creation">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>After getting frustrated with a drawing of production designer Gavin Bocquet, <A href="/wiki/Iain_McCaig" title="Iain McCaig">Iain McCaig</A> started covering it in tape. Both he and Lucas liked the result, described as "a kind of <A href="/wiki/Rorschach_inkblot_test" class="mw-redirect" title="Rorschach inkblot test">Rorschach pattern</A>". The final drawing had McCaig's own face, with the skin removed, and some Rorschach experimentation (dropping ink onto paper, folding it in half then opening).<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Darth Maul's head originally had feathers, based on prayer <A href="/wiki/Totem" title="Totem">totems</A>, but the Creature Effects crew led by Nick Dudman interpreted those feathers as horns, modifying his features into those common in popular depictions of the <A href="/wiki/Devil" title="Devil">devil</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-myth_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-myth-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>
<P>His clothing was also modified, from a tight body suit with a muscle pattern to the Sith robe based on <A href="/wiki/Samurai" title="Samurai">samurai</A> pleats, because the lightsaber battles involved much jumping, spinning, running, and rolling.<SUP id="cite_ref-databank_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-databank-4">[4]</A></SUP> Another concept had Maul a masked figure, something that could rival <A href="/wiki/Darth_Vader" title="Darth Vader">Darth Vader</A>, while the senatorial characters would sport painted and tattooed faces. It was later decided to apply the painted and tattooed faces to Maul rather than the senator.<SUP id="cite_ref-databank_4-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-databank-4">[4]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Portrayal">Portrayal</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Portrayal">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Darth Maul was physically portrayed by actor and <A href="/wiki/Martial_artist" class="mw-redirect" title="Martial artist">martial artist</A> <A href="/wiki/Ray_Park" title="Ray Park">Ray Park</A> in <I>The Phantom Menace</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP> The character was voiced by comedian/voice actor/director <A href="/wiki/Peter_Serafinowicz" title="Peter Serafinowicz">Peter Serafinowicz</A> in <I>The Phantom Menace</I> and <A href="/wiki/Lego_Star_Wars:_The_Video_Game" title="Lego Star Wars: The Video Game">Lego videogame adaptation of the prequel trilogy</A>; while <A href="/wiki/Samuel_Witwer" class="mw-redirect" title="Samuel Witwer">Samuel Witwer</A> performed the character's voice in the animated series <I>The Clone Wars</I>, <I>Rebels</I>, and in the live action movie <I><A href="/wiki/Solo:_A_Star_Wars_Story" title="Solo: A Star Wars Story">Solo: A Star Wars Story</A></I>. Actors <A href="/wiki/Gregg_Berger" title="Gregg Berger">Gregg Berger</A>, <A href="/wiki/Jess_Harnell" title="Jess Harnell">Jess Harnell</A>, <A href="/wiki/Stephen_Stanton" title="Stephen Stanton">Stephen Stanton</A>, <A href="/wiki/Clint_Bajakian" title="Clint Bajakian">Clint Bajakian</A>, and David W. Collins have all voiced him in <I>Legends</I> adaptations and minor appearances.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Appearances">Appearances</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Appearances">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Star_Wars_canon" class="mw-redirect" title="Star Wars canon">Star Wars canon</A></DIV>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Films">Films</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Films">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="The_Phantom_Menace"><I>The Phantom Menace</I></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: The Phantom Menace">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_Episode_I_-_The_Phantom_Menace" class="mw-redirect" title="Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace">Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace</A></DIV>
<P>Introduced in <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_Episode_I_%E2%80%93_The_Phantom_Menace" title="Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace">Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace</A></I>, Darth Maul is ordered by Darth Sidious to capture Queen <A href="/wiki/Padm%C3%A9_Amidala" title="Padmé Amidala">Padmé Amidala</A>. On <A href="/wiki/Tatooine" title="Tatooine">Tatooine</A>, Maul fights <A href="/wiki/Qui-Gon_Jinn" title="Qui-Gon Jinn">Qui-Gon Jinn</A> while approaching the Queen's starship. While <A href="/wiki/Darth_Vader" title="Darth Vader">Anakin Skywalker (the future Darth Vader)</A> gets on board, Qui-Gon engages Maul in a lightsaber duel, but the <A href="/wiki/Jedi" title="Jedi">Jedi Master</A> escapes. Eventually, Maul fights Qui-Gon and <A href="/wiki/Obi-Wan_Kenobi" title="Obi-Wan Kenobi">Obi-Wan Kenobi</A> simultaneously. Maul duels Qui-Gon and eventually kills him. Although Obi-Wan is almost knocked down into a shaft, he uses the <A href="/wiki/Force_(Star_Wars)" class="mw-redirect" title="Force (Star Wars)">Force</A> to propel himself out of the pit, and equips himself with Qui-Gon's lightsaber to bisect Maul, seemingly killing him, after which the two separated pieces of Maul's body fall into the shaft.<SUP id="cite_ref-tpm_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-tpm-6">[6]</A></SUP></P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Solo:_A_Star_Wars_Story"><I>Solo: A Star Wars Story</I></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Solo: A Star Wars Story">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Solo:_A_Star_Wars_Story" title="Solo: A Star Wars Story">Solo: A Star Wars Story</A></DIV>
<P><A href="/wiki/Ray_Park" title="Ray Park">Ray Park</A> reprises his role from <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_Episode_I_%E2%80%93_The_Phantom_Menace" title="Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace">The Phantom Menace</A></I> as Darth Maul, with <A href="/wiki/Sam_Witwer" title="Sam Witwer">Sam Witwer</A> providing the voice,<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> reprising his role from the animated series, <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_The_Clone_Wars_(2008_TV_series)" title="Star Wars: The Clone Wars (2008 TV series)">The Clone Wars</A></I> and <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars_Rebels" title="Star Wars Rebels">Star Wars Rebels</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> Maul is revealed to be the master of the crime syndicate Crimson Dawn that crime lord Dryden Vos answers to. Qi'ra tells Maul that Vos and his men were killed by Tobias Beckett and his accomplices, but neglects to name <A href="/wiki/Han_Solo" title="Han Solo">Han Solo</A> and <A href="/wiki/Chewbacca" title="Chewbacca">Chewbacca</A>. Maul commands her to meet with him on Dathomir and warns her that they will work more closely from now on, igniting his lightsaber.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Animated_series">Animated series</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Animated series">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="The_Clone_Wars"><I>The Clone Wars</I></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section: The Clone Wars">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_The_Clone_Wars_(2008_TV_series)" title="Star Wars: The Clone Wars (2008 TV series)">Star Wars: The Clone Wars (2008 TV series)</A></DIV>
<P>Darth Maul appears in the fourth and fifth seasons of the animated series <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_The_Clone_Wars_(2008_TV_series)" title="Star Wars: The Clone Wars (2008 TV series)">Star Wars: The Clone Wars</A></I>.</P>
<P>In the third season, Darth Maul’s origins are elaborated upon: he is portrayed as a warrior of the Nightbrother clan on the planet <A href="/wiki/Dathomir" class="mw-redirect" title="Dathomir">Dathomir</A> inhabited by the dominant Nightsister <A href="/wiki/Witchcraft" title="Witchcraft">witchcraft</A> society led by <A href="/wiki/Mother_Talzin" class="mw-redirect" title="Mother Talzin">Mother Talzin</A>. Maul’s tattoos are described as the markings of a warrior (in contrast to earlier sources which identify his body art as Sith markings). Talzin has <A href="/wiki/Savage_Opress" class="mw-redirect" title="Savage Opress">Savage Opress</A> find his long-lost brother.</P>
<P>In the fourth season, Darth Maul is revealed to be alive, having survived his presumed death at Obi-Wan Kenobi’s hands. Having ended up on the junkyard planet Lotho Minor via a dumpster craft, Maul has suffered from amnesia since Obi-Wan defeated him. Opress finds Maul and brings him to the devastated Dathomir, where Talzin restores Maul’s mind and gives him robotic legs. Maul and Opress set about a plan to exact revenge on Obi-Wan.<SUP id="cite_ref-tcw_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-tcw-9">[9]</A></SUP> Maul proceeds to attack a village on planet Raydonia as his first attempt on Obi-Wan's life, only to be thwarted due to <A href="/wiki/Asajj_Ventress" title="Asajj Ventress">Asajj Ventress</A>’s unexpected appearance to collect a bounty on Opress. Maul and Opress overpower Obi-Wan and Ventress, but Maul lets them go upon realizing that the Jedi know of his existence, deciding to await another opportunity.<SUP id="cite_ref-ew_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ew-10">[10]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In the fifth season, Maul takes Opress as his apprentice, and begins building a criminal empire. Needing followers, they travel to Florrum and manage to convince Weequay pirate Jiro and his crew to join them and betray their leader Hondo Ohnaka. Maul’s pirates attack Hondo’s loyal forces, and Maul once again duels Obi-Wan while Opress fights and kills Jedi Master <A href="/wiki/Adi_Gallia" class="mw-redirect" title="Adi Gallia">Adi Gallia</A>. Obi-Wan and Hondo forces retreat and regroup inside Hondo’s compound. Maul's forces eventually break in and Obi-Wan draws the two brothers away from the pirates, engaging them in a two-on-one duel while the pirate factions fight elsewhere in the compound. Obi-Wan, though outnumbered, cuts off Opress’s arm and forces the Sith Lords to retreat. Meanwhile, Honda wins back his crew by “persuading” them under threat of heavy artillery. Obi-Wan blows off one of Maul’s robotic legs and badly damages Maul’s ship. Maul and Opress manage to escape, but get stuck in dead space due to the damage to their ship. After several days, they are found close to death by the Death Watch Mandalorian warriors, led by Pre Vizsla, who gives Maul a new set of legs and Opress a new mechanical arm. Maul offers Vizsla the chance to reclaim Mandalore by recruiting the Black Sun and Pyke crime families and <A href="/wiki/Jabba_the_Hutt" title="Jabba the Hutt">Jabba the Hutt</A>’s minions to create the criminal syndicate named The Shadow Collective.</P>
<P>From there, Maul engineers Vizsla’s rise to power: he orders his henchmen to attack Mandalore so the Death Watch can arrest them and appear as heroes to the denizens who have long lived under Duchess Satine Kryze’s <A href="/wiki/Pacifist" class="mw-redirect" title="Pacifist">pacifist</A> rule. Vizsla betrays Maul, imprisoning both Savage and him. Easily breaking free, Maul challenges Vizsla to a duel to take over the Death Watch and Mandalore; he succeeds in killing Vizsla and then claims his former co-conspirator’s darksaber.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template" style="margin-left:0.1em; white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify" title="Wikipedia:Please clarify"><SPAN title="The text near this tag may need clarification or removal of jargon. (June 2018)">clarification needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> He wins the loyalty of most Death Watch members, but Bo Katan retreats along with those loyal to their previous leader. Maul then puts the disgraced former prime minister Almec, whom Satine had imprisoned for corruption, in power as a puppet leader, solidifying his control over Mandalore. Maul then anticipates Satine being broken out of prison and her attempt to contact the Jedi Council as part of his plan to get Obi-Wan to Mandalore. Once Obi-Wan arrives and attempts to rescue Satine, Maul captures him and exacts revenge on the Jedi by murdering Satine right in front of him, hoping to make the Jedi suffer as much as he once did. Obi-Wan is later freed by the Night Owl rebels (Bo Katan’s Death Watch faction) who request Republic aid.</P>
<P>Maul senses Darth Sidious arriving on Mandalore. Although impressed with his former apprentice’s survival, Sidious declares Maul a rival and uses the Force to push and choke him and Opress. He then engages them both in lightsaber combat, fatally injuring Opress. After Opress dies from his wounds, Sidious reminds Maul of the <A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_Darth_Bane:_Rule_of_Two" title="Star Wars: Darth Bane: Rule of Two">Rule of Two</A>, and tells him that he has been replaced. Enraged, Maul pulls out both his lightsaber and darksaber <SUP class="noprint Inline-Template" style="margin-left:0.1em; white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify" title="Wikipedia:Please clarify"><SPAN title="The text near this tag may need clarification or removal of jargon. (June 2018)">clarification needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP> and proceeds to fight Sidious on equal ground, but Sidious ultimately defeats him. Maul pleads for mercy, but Sidious ignores him and tortures him with blasts of <A href="/wiki/Force_lightning" class="mw-redirect" title="Force lightning">Force lightning</A>. Sidious reveals that he has no intention of killing Maul, remarking that he has other uses for his former apprentice.</P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Rebels"><I>Rebels</I></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section: Rebels">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Star_Wars_Rebels" title="Star Wars Rebels">Star Wars Rebels</A></DIV>
<P>An older Maul appears in the season 2 finale of <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars_Rebels" title="Star Wars Rebels">Star Wars Rebels</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rebels_11-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rebels-11">[11]</A></SUP> Tracked by an Inquisitor named the Eighth Brother, Maul is stranded on the ancient Sith world of Malachor, where he is discovered by series protagonist <A href="/wiki/Ezra_Bridger" class="mw-redirect" title="Ezra Bridger">Ezra Bridger</A> among the ruins. Introducing himself as "Old Master" and seeking revenge against Sidious, Maul leads Ezra into an ancient Sith temple, where they discover a holocron that Maul claims can give them the knowledge needed to defeat the Sith. After recovering it, the two find Ezra's master Kanan Jarrus and former Jedi <A href="/wiki/Ahsoka_Tano" title="Ahsoka Tano">Ahsoka Tano</A> locked in battle with the Eighth Brother. They also find the Fifth Brother and the Seventh Sister, who have been pursuing the Rebels for some time. Maul – having cast aside the title of Darth – then reveals a new lightsaber disguised as a walking stick and joins the Jedi in battling their enemies.</P>
<P>After the Inquisitors retreat, Maul wins the Jedi's trust by denouncing the Sith, and tells them that he cannot defeat <A href="/wiki/Darth_Vader" title="Darth Vader">Darth Vader</A> on his own. Working together, he and the Jedi ascend towards the top of the Sith temple and successfully defeat the three Inquisitors. It is then that Maul reveals his intention to take Ezra as his apprentice, having already tricked him into activating the temple. After blinding Kanan, Maul briefly duels Ahsoka before facing Kanan again, only to be knocked off the temple's edge. However, he survives the fall and escapes Malachor in the Eighth Brother's <A href="/wiki/TIE_Fighter" class="mw-redirect" title="TIE Fighter">TIE Fighter</A>.</P>
<P>Months after the events on Malachor, Maul once again reveals himself to the Jedi as he takes the <I>Ghost</I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</SPAN>s crew hostage. He threatens to kill them unless Kanan and Ezra bring both the Sith and Jedi holocrons to him. Despite an attempt by the Rebels to escape, Maul successfully recaptures them and takes them to a remote base in the Outer Rim where he awaits the arrival of the Jedi. After they arrive, the holocrons are hazardously united allowing Ezra and Maul to see visions of their desires: Ezra sees images of a way to destroy the Sith, images including "twin suns", while Maul sees a vision of his own. Kanan begs Ezra to look away before he sees something he doesn't want to while Maul tells him to ignore Kanan and keep looking. Ezra heeds his master's words and breaks off the connection, which causes a great explosion. Maul escapes in the confusion, uttering, "He lives."</P>
<P>Maul reappears after finding the Rebellion's secret base. He tells Ezra that because the connection was severed, they got bits and pieces of each other's visions. With the holocrons destroyed from the events of their previous meeting, Maul discovered another way to get the information he needed. With Ezra he travels to <A href="/wiki/Dathomir" class="mw-redirect" title="Dathomir">Dathomir</A>, former home of the Night Sisters, and recreates one of their spells to temporarily meld his and Ezra's minds. After the spell is completed Ezra, who was still looking for a way to destroy the Sith, and Maul realize they are both looking for <A href="/wiki/Obi-Wan_Kenobi" title="Obi-Wan Kenobi">Obi-Wan Kenobi</A>.</P>
<P>In the episode "Twin Suns", Maul is shown lost on <A href="/wiki/Tatooine" title="Tatooine">Tatooine</A>. He decides to use Ezra to lure Obi-Wan out of hiding. During their confrontation, Maul deduces that Obi-Wan is not only hiding, but is protecting <A href="/wiki/Luke_Skywalker" title="Luke Skywalker">someone</A>. In a swift duel, Obi-Wan fatally wounds Maul. As he lies dying in Obi-Wan's arms, Maul asks if the person he is protecting is the Chosen One, and Obi-Wan replies "he is". Maul declares that this "Chosen One" will avenge them, and dies.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Comics">Comics</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section: Comics">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Darth_Maul"><I>Darth Maul</I></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section: Darth Maul">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<P>In 2017, <A href="/wiki/Marvel_Comics" title="Marvel Comics">Marvel</A> released <I>Star Wars: Darth Maul</I> a 5-issue prequel series centered on Darth Maul before the events of <I>The Phantom Menace</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP></P>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Darth_Maul:_Son_of_Dathomir"><I>Darth Maul: Son of Dathomir</I></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section: Darth Maul: Son of Dathomir">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Darth_Maul:_Son_of_Dathomir" title="Darth Maul: Son of Dathomir">Darth Maul: Son of Dathomir</A></DIV>
<P><A href="/wiki/Dark_Horse_Comics" title="Dark Horse Comics">Dark Horse Comics</A> produced <I><A href="/wiki/Darth_Maul:_Son_of_Dathomir" title="Darth Maul: Son of Dathomir">Darth Maul: Son of Dathomir</A></I> based on the scripts and storyboards of an unproduced 4-episode story arc intended for <I>The Clone Wars</I> Season 6. After killing Savage Opress, Darth Sidious takes Maul to a Separatist prison, where <A href="/wiki/Count_Dooku" title="Count Dooku">Count Dooku</A> tortures him for information about the Shadow Collective. Prime Minister Almec arranges Maul's escape and the latter then heads back to Zanbar to command the Death Watch army. However, he is followed there by <A href="/wiki/General_Grievous" title="General Grievous">General Grievous</A> and his droids, who then battle with Maul and the Mandalorians. While they put up a fierce fight, Maul and his minions are ultimately overwhelmed by the droids. During the battle, Maul tears through the droid ranks and attacks Grievous, but is overpowered and forced to retreat. Afterwards, Maul confers with Mother Talzin (revealed to be his biological mother) and plots to draw out Sidious by capturing Dooku and General Grievous. The scheme works, and Talzin is able to restore herself to her physical form, but she sacrifices herself to save Maul. Although Maul escapes with a company of loyal Mandalorians, the Shadow Collective has fallen apart due to the conflict with Sidious, as the Hutts, Pykes, and Black Sun have all abandoned Maul.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Novels">Novels</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=14" title="Edit section: Novels">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<H4><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Ahsoka"><I>Ahsoka</I></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=15" title="Edit section: Ahsoka">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H4>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_Ahsoka" title="Star Wars: Ahsoka">Star Wars: Ahsoka</A></DIV>
<P>In flashbacks during the novel <I>Star Wars: Ahsoka</I>, it is revealed that during the final days of the Clone Wars, Maul and his forces were besieged on Mandalore by an army of clone troopers led by Ahsoka Tano and <A href="/wiki/Captain_Rex" title="Captain Rex">Captain Rex</A>. During the siege, Maul confronts and duels Ahsoka, and though he proves to be the stronger fighter, the former Jedi outwits him and traps him in a ray shield. However, before Maul can be taken into official custody, Order 66 is enacted and the clone troopers following Ahsoka turn on her, with the exception of Rex. With Rex's life in peril, Ahsoka abandons the chance of killing Maul, allowing the former Sith to escape once again. This battle was originally intended to be depicted in the series finale of <I>The Clone Wars</I> had the series not been prematurely cancelled – Anakin and Obi-Wan were dispatched to Mandalore with Ahsoka, but were immediately called back to Coruscant to rescue Chancellor Palpatine, thus leading into the opening sequence of <I>Revenge of the Sith</I>.</P>
<H3><SPAN id="Legends.2FNon-canonical"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Legends/Non-canonical"><I>Legends</I>/Non-canonical</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=16" title="Edit section: Legends/Non-canonical">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>With the 2012 acquisition of <A href="/wiki/Lucasfilm" title="Lucasfilm">Lucasfilm</A> by <A href="/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company" title="The Walt Disney Company">The Walt Disney Company</A>, most of the licensed <I>Star Wars</I> novels and comics produced since the originating 1977 film <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars_(film)" title="Star Wars (film)">Star Wars</A></I> were rebranded as <I>Star Wars Legends</I> and declared non-canon to the franchise in April 2014.<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-SW_Legends_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-SW_Legends-14">[14]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-SW_Adult_15-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-SW_Adult-15">[15]</A></SUP></P>
<P>As portrayed in the novel <I><A href="/wiki/Darth_Plagueis" class="mw-redirect" title="Darth Plagueis">Darth Plagueis</A></I>, the titular Sith Lord sends his apprentice, Darth Sidious, to the Force-rich world of Dathomir. A Dathomiri witch, or Night-sister, senses Sidious' power in the Force and approaches him. She assumes he is a Jedi and begs him to take her <A href="/wiki/Zabrak_(Star_Wars)" class="mw-redirect" title="Zabrak (Star Wars)">Zabrak</A> infant son. She realizes Sidious is not a Jedi, and explains how she is trying to save her son from a Nightsister named Talzin, who killed Maul's father. It is implied that Maul has a twin brother and that Talzin is only aware of one child. Sidious realizes the infant is strong in the Force, and would become a threat if found by the Jedi. Concealing the existence of his own master, Sidious raises Maul to believe that he is a Sith apprentice, but he actually intends him to be an expendable—albeit useful—minion rather than an heir. Maul himself acknowledges his shortcomings, such as his limited understanding of politics, even as he tries to become a true Sith.</P>
<P>As portrayed in the novel <I><A href="/wiki/Darth_Maul:_Shadow_Hunter" title="Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter">Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter</A></I>, Maul was raised by Sidious for as long as he can remember. He then trains Maul as a Sith, marking his body with Sith tattoos. Maul initially goes on several missions of <A href="/wiki/Terrorism" title="Terrorism">terror</A> for his master, killing politicians, crime bosses, merchants and warlords.</P>
<P>Several sources depict Maul returning from the dead in several different forms. The story "Resurrection" from <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars_Tales_9" class="mw-redirect" title="Star Wars Tales 9">Star Wars Tales 9</A></I> depicts a cult creating a duplicate of Maul as a replacement for <A href="/wiki/Darth_Vader" title="Darth Vader">Darth Vader</A>, only for Vader to kill him. The story "Phantom Menaces" in <I>Star Wars Tales</I> #17 (set after <I><A href="/wiki/Return_of_the_Jedi" title="Return of the Jedi">Return of the Jedi</A></I>) depicts <A href="/wiki/Luke_Skywalker" title="Luke Skywalker">Luke Skywalker</A> visiting Maul's home planet of <A href="/wiki/Iridonia" class="mw-redirect" title="Iridonia">Iridonia</A> in an ambassadorial capacity, where he faces a "solid state hologram" of Maul projected from Maul's salvaged brain as part of a scientist's attempt to recreate Maul as Iridonia's "champion". Luke recognizes the disruption that Maul's existence is causing in the Force, and shuts down the life-support systems keeping the brain alive.</P>
<P>In 2005, <A href="/wiki/Dark_Horse_Comics" title="Dark Horse Comics">Dark Horse Comics</A> published <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_Visionaries" title="Star Wars: Visionaries">Star Wars: Visionaries</A></I>, a compilation of comic art short stories. One story "Old Wounds", considered to be non-canonical to <I>Star Wars</I> lore, depicts Maul, now with longer horns on his head, surviving his bisection at Obi-Wan's hands, replacing his missing bottom half with <A href="/wiki/Cybernetic" class="mw-redirect" title="Cybernetic">cybernetic</A> legs, similar to those of <A href="/wiki/General_Grievous" title="General Grievous">General Grievous</A>. He then follows Obi-Wan throughout the <A href="/wiki/Star_Wars_galaxy" class="mw-redirect" title="Star Wars galaxy">galaxy</A>, finally tracking him down on <A href="/wiki/Tatooine" title="Tatooine">Tatooine</A> a few years after the events of <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_Episode_III_%E2%80%93_Revenge_of_the_Sith" title="Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith">Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith</A></I>. Maul taunts Obi-Wan, saying that after he kills him, he will take a toddler-aged Luke Skywalker to his master, Emperor Palpatine. Maul plans to kill Darth Vader, and resume his rightful place at Palpatine's side as his apprentice. He ignites his new double-bladed lightsaber, and engages Obi-Wan in a lightsaber duel, but Obi-Wan again bests him in combat, cutting off his opponent's horns. The Sith Lord is killed, unexpectedly, by a blaster bolt to the head from <A href="/wiki/Owen_Lars" class="mw-redirect" title="Owen Lars">Owen Lars</A>. Obi-Wan thanks Owen, and says he will take Maul's body into the desert and burn it so he can never come back.</P>
<P>In early 2012, a <A href="/wiki/Young_adult_fiction" title="Young adult fiction">young adult</A> novel entitled <I><A href="/w/index.php?title=Star_Wars:_The_Wrath_of_Darth_Maul&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Star Wars: The Wrath of Darth Maul (page does not exist)">Star Wars: The Wrath of Darth Maul</A></I> was released by <A href="/wiki/Scholastic_Corporation" title="Scholastic Corporation">Scholastic</A>. In the 2014 novel, <I><A href="/wiki/Star_Wars:_Maul:_Lockdown" title="Star Wars: Maul: Lockdown">Star Wars: Maul: Lockdown</A></I>, set before <I>The Phantom Menace</I>, Darth Maul is sent into an infamous galactic prison. Maul is also featured prominently in comic series starting in this period, <I>Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Sith Hunters</I> & <I>Darth Maul: Death Sentence</I>. Set in the period of the Clone Wars around the various episodes that featured Maul, <I>Sith Hunters</I> and <I>Death Sentence</I> detail his and Savage Opress' journey across the galaxy as they seek vengeance on the Jedi.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="In_popular_culture">In popular culture</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Darth_Maul&action=edit&section=17" title="Edit section: In popular culture">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Since the release of <I>The Phantom Menace</I>, Darth Maul has proven to be a popular character. <A href="/wiki/IGN" title="IGN">IGN</A> named Darth Maul the 16th greatest <I>Star Wars</I> character, noting, "Of the countless characters to walk in and out of the <I>Star Wars</I> saga, none looks or acts more badass than Darth Maul."<SUP id="cite_ref-ign_16-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ign-16">[16]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Darth Maul-related merchandise was popular among <A href="/wiki/Hasbro" title="Hasbro">Hasbro</A> <I>Star Wars</I> toy lines, with plastic recreations of his double bladed lightsaber and various action figures in his likeness developed. Darth Maul has been the focal point of the toy marketing campaign surrounding the <A href="/wiki/2012_in_film" title="2012 in film">2012</A> re-release of <I>The Phantom Menace</I>, being featured on the packaging for the toy line.<SUP id="cite_ref-merch_17-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-merch-17">[17]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In December 2017, an 8-year-old <A href="/wiki/Ontario" title="Ontario">Ontario</A> boy went <A href="/wiki/Viral_video" title="Viral video">viral</A> on the Internet with a video of him pretending to be Darth Maul and displaying his martial arts skills.<SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP></P>

<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:John_D._Rockefeller.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/John_D._Rockefeller.jpg/220px-John_D._Rockefeller.jpg" width="220" height="333" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/74/John_D._Rockefeller.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="244" data-file-height="369" /></A>

<A href="/wiki/John_D._Rockefeller" title="John D. Rockefeller">John D. Rockefeller</A> is often considered the wealthiest person in modern history.<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP></DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>The <B>list of the wealthiest historical figures</B> gathers published estimates as to the (<A href="/wiki/Real_versus_nominal_value_(economics)" title="Real versus nominal value (economics)">inflation-adjusted</A>) net-worth and fortunes of the wealthiest <A href="/wiki/Historical_figure" title="Historical figure">historical figures</A> in comparison. Due to problems arising from different definitions of wealth, ways of measuring it, various economic models throughout history, as well as multiple other reasons—this article discusses the wealthiest people in the following separate historical periods: <A href="/wiki/Classical_Antiquity" class="mw-redirect" title="Classical Antiquity">Antiquity</A>, <A href="/wiki/Middle_Ages" title="Middle Ages">Middle Ages</A> and <A href="/wiki/Modern_period" class="mw-redirect" title="Modern period">modern period</A>. Accordingly—because of the previously mentioned difficulties—it is not possible to determine the single richest person in all of history.</P>
<P>For the <A href="/wiki/Modern_period" class="mw-redirect" title="Modern period">modern period</A>, wealth can be measured more or less objectively via <A href="/wiki/Inflation_adjustment" class="mw-redirect" title="Inflation adjustment">inflation adjustment</A>, e.g. comparing the <A href="/wiki/Economy_of_the_United_States" title="Economy of the United States">nominal GDP of the United States</A> of the respective periods, and then converting it into contemporary United States dollars. For the medieval and ancient history, comparison of wealth becomes more problematic, on one hand due to the inaccuracy or unreliability of records, on the other due to the difficulty of comparing a pre-industrial economy to a modern one, and especially in the presence of <A href="/wiki/Absolute_monarchy" title="Absolute monarchy">absolute monarchy</A>, where an entire kingdom or empire is considered the ruler's personal property (this is also an issue in early modern to modern period, e.g. Davidson (2015) lists <A href="/wiki/Joseph_Stalin" title="Joseph Stalin">Joseph Stalin</A> among <I>The 10 Richest People of All Time</I> for his "complete control of a nation with 9.6% of global GDP").<SUP id="cite_ref-time.com_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-time.com-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Excluding <A href="/wiki/Monarch" title="Monarch">monarchs</A> and <A href="/wiki/Autocracy" title="Autocracy">autocrats</A>, the wealthiest private individual in the history of <A href="/wiki/Capitalism" title="Capitalism">capitalism</A> is variously identified as <A href="/wiki/Jakob_Fugger" title="Jakob Fugger">Jakob Fugger</A> (died 1525), of the early modern <A href="/wiki/Fugger" title="Fugger">Fugger</A> family of merchants and bankers,<SUP id="cite_ref-Fugger_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Fugger-4">[4]</A></SUP> and early 20th-century American entrepreneurs <A href="/wiki/Andrew_Carnegie" title="Andrew Carnegie">Andrew Carnegie</A> (died 1919)<SUP id="cite_ref-Carnegie_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Carnegie-5">[5]</A></SUP> and <A href="/wiki/John_D._Rockefeller" title="John D. Rockefeller">John D. Rockefeller</A> (died 1937). Frequently, one of these few people is considered to be the richest person of all time, depending on source.</P>
<P>While the <A href="/wiki/Rothschild_family" title="Rothschild family">Rothschild family</A> rose to the status of the <A href="/wiki/List_of_wealthiest_families" title="List of wealthiest families">wealthiest family</A> of bankers in the 19th century, their wealth was distributed among a number of family members, preventing them from appearing among the wealthiest individuals. The richest among the Rothschilds was the head of its English branch—<A href="/wiki/Nathan_Mayer_Rothschild" title="Nathan Mayer Rothschild">Nathan Mayer Rothschild</A>—the richest person of his time.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> Bernstein and Swan in <I>All the Money in the World</I> (2008) mention the top three <A href="/wiki/List_of_richest_Americans_in_history" title="List of richest Americans in history">richest Americans ever</A>—all <A href="/wiki/Tycoons" class="mw-redirect" title="Tycoons">tycoons</A> of the <A href="/wiki/Gilded_Age" title="Gilded Age">Gilded Age</A>—respectively: John D. Rockefeller, Andrew Carnegie and <A href="/wiki/Cornelius_Vanderbilt" title="Cornelius Vanderbilt">Cornelius Vanderbilt</A>; <A href="/wiki/Henry_Ford" title="Henry Ford">Henry Ford</A> was ranked only 12th.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP></P>
<P>According to Close (2016), the <A href="/wiki/List_of_female_billionaires" title="List of female billionaires">wealthiest woman</A> in the history of capitalism, excluding monarchs, is <I>L'Oréal</I> heiress <A href="/wiki/Liliane_Bettencourt" title="Liliane Bettencourt">Liliane Bettencourt</A>, whose net worth was at $40.7 billion in 2015.<SUP id="cite_ref-Close_8-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Close-8">[8]</A></SUP> Including monarchs, he mentions <A href="/wiki/Empress_Wu" class="mw-redirect" title="Empress Wu">Empress Wu</A> for Antiquity, <A href="/wiki/Isabella_of_Castile" class="mw-redirect" title="Isabella of Castile">Isabella of Castile</A> for Middle Ages, and <A href="/wiki/Catherine_the_Great" title="Catherine the Great">Catherine the Great</A> for modern history.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP></P>
<P></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Antiquity">Antiquity</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_wealthiest_historical_figures&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Antiquity">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Marcus_Licinius_Crassus_Louvre.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Marcus_Licinius_Crassus_Louvre.jpg/170px-Marcus_Licinius_Crassus_Louvre.jpg" width="170" height="236" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Marcus_Licinius_Crassus_Louvre.jpg/255px-Marcus_Licinius_Crassus_Louvre.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Marcus_Licinius_Crassus_Louvre.jpg/340px-Marcus_Licinius_Crassus_Louvre.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1892" data-file-height="2632" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Marcus_Licinius_Crassus_Louvre.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
<A href="/wiki/Marcus_Licinius_Crassus" title="Marcus Licinius Crassus">Marcus Licinius Crassus</A> is held to be the wealthiest person in Roman history, as he had a personal net worth equal to the treasury of Rome.<SUP id="cite_ref-TrivLibCrassus_39-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TrivLibCrassus-39">[39]</A></SUP></DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>For <A href="/wiki/Classical_Antiquity" class="mw-redirect" title="Classical Antiquity">Classical Antiquity</A>, even more than for the <A href="/wiki/High_Middle_Ages" title="High Middle Ages">High Middle Ages</A>, the definition of personal wealth becomes difficult to compare with the modern period; especially in the case of <A href="/wiki/Imperial_cult" title="Imperial cult">divine kings</A>, where an entire empire might be considered the personal property of a deified emperor.</P>
<TABLE class="wikitable">
<TBODY><TR>
<TH>Name</TH>
<TH>Lifetime</TH>
<TH>Description</TH>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Marcus_Licinius_Crassus" title="Marcus Licinius Crassus">Marcus Licinius Crassus</A></TD>
<TD>c. 115 BC – 53 BC</TD>
<TD>Crassus inherited a fortune of 7 million <A href="/wiki/Sesterces" class="mw-redirect" title="Sesterces">sesterces</A> after the death of his father in 87 BC. After several years of exile, Crassus was able to rebuild his family fortune by seizing the property of executed convicts for himself.<SUP id="cite_ref-TrivLibCrassus_39-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-TrivLibCrassus-39">[39]</A></SUP> Crassus also expanded his wealth by trading in slaves and by purchasing whole neighborhoods of Rome as they burned, for drastically less than market value. Crassus was known in Rome as <I>Dives</I>, meaning "The Rich". It is believed that Crassus expanded his personal fortune to 170 million sesterces, while <A href="/wiki/Pliny_the_Elder" title="Pliny the Elder">Pliny the Elder</A> surmised his fortune to be valued even higher, at 200 million sesterces. This would place Crassus's net worth equal to the total annual budget of the Roman treasury.
<P>Crassus has often been listed among the "wealthiest individuals in history", although depending on the estimate of the "adjusted value" of a Roman <A href="/wiki/Sesterce" class="mw-redirect" title="Sesterce">sesterce</A>, his net worth may also be placed in the range of US$200 million to US$20 billion.<SUP id="cite_ref-Bernstein_40-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Bernstein-40">[40]</A></SUP></P>
</TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Augustus_Caesar" class="mw-redirect" title="Augustus Caesar">Augustus Caesar</A></TD>
<TD>63 BC – 19 August 14 AD</TD>
<TD>Listed by <I>Time Magazine</I> with "$4.6 trillion" because he "personally owned all of Egypt".<SUP id="cite_ref-time.com_3-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-time.com-3">[3]</A></SUP></TD>
</TR>
<TR>
<TD><A href="/wiki/Croesus" title="Croesus">Croesus</A></TD>
<TD>died c. 546 BC</TD>
<TD>The name of Croesus, a historical king of <A href="/wiki/Lydia" title="Lydia">Lydia</A>, was proverbial for wealth already in antiquity; this is probably due to his being the first ruler to issue true <A href="/wiki/Gold_coins" class="mw-redirect" title="Gold coins">gold coins</A> with a standardised purity for general circulation and not necessarily for his personal wealth.</TD>
</TR>
</TBODY></TABLE>

<P><A href="/wiki/Liverpool_F.C." title="Liverpool F.C.">Liverpool Football Club</A>, an English professional <A href="/wiki/Association_football" title="Association football">association football</A> club, is Britain's most successful team in <A href="/wiki/UEFA" title="UEFA">Union of European Football Associations</A> (UEFA) competitions. Since 1964, they have won eleven European trophies: the <A href="/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League" title="UEFA Champions League">UEFA Champions League</A> (formerly known as the European Cup) five times, the <A href="/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League" title="UEFA Europa League">UEFA Europa League</A> (formerly known as the UEFA Cup) three times, and the <A href="/wiki/UEFA_Super_Cup" title="UEFA Super Cup">UEFA Super Cup</A> three times.
</P><P>Qualification for European competitions is determined by a team's success in its domestic league and cup competitions from the previous season. Liverpool competed in European competitions for 21 consecutive seasons until the <A href="/wiki/1985_European_Cup_Final" title="1985 European Cup Final">1985 European Cup Final</A>, the occasion of the <A href="/wiki/Heysel_Stadium_disaster" title="Heysel Stadium disaster">Heysel Stadium disaster</A>, following which the club was banned from European competitions for six seasons. Since being readmitted in 1991, they have qualified for the Champions League (the successor to the European Cup) nine times and the Europa League (the successor to the Uefa Cup) nine times.
</P><P>As a result of their victory in the <A href="/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_Final" title="2005 UEFA Champions League Final">2005 UEFA Champions League Final</A>, Liverpool won the <A href="/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs%27_Cup" title="European Champion Clubs' Cup">European Champion Clubs' Cup</A> trophy outright, and were awarded a <A href="/wiki/UEFA_badge_of_honour" class="mw-redirect" title="UEFA badge of honour">multiple winner badge</A>. Liverpool's total of three UEFA Cup wins has been bettered only by <A href="/wiki/Sevilla_FC" title="Sevilla FC">Sevilla</A>, who have won the competition five times. They have also won the UEFA Super Cup on three occasions, a total only Milan and <A href="/wiki/FC_Barcelona" title="FC Barcelona">Barcelona</A> (five titles each)  have bettered.
</P><P><A href="/wiki/Bob_Paisley" title="Bob Paisley">Bob Paisley</A> is the club's most successful manager in Europe, with five trophies. Liverpool's biggest-margin win in Europe is an 11–0 victory over <A href="/wiki/Str%C3%B8msgodset_IF" title="Strømsgodset IF">Strømsgodset</A> in the <A href="/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_European_Cup_Winners%27_Cup" title="1974–75 European Cup Winners' Cup">1974–75 European Cup Winners' Cup</A>. In European competitions, <A href="/wiki/Jamie_Carragher" title="Jamie Carragher">Jamie Carragher</A> holds the club record for the most appearances, with 150, and <A href="/wiki/Steven_Gerrard" title="Steven Gerrard">Steven Gerrard</A> is the club's record goalscorer, with 41 goals.
</P>
