<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Background">Background</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Liverpool_F.C._in_European_football&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Background">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information on the origins of European football: <A href="/wiki/European_Cup_and_UEFA_Champions_League_history" title="European Cup and UEFA Champions League history">European Cup and UEFA Champions League history</A></DIV>
<P>Club competitions between teams from different European countries can trace their origins as far back as 1897, when the Challenge Cup was created for clubs in the <A href="/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Austro-Hungarian Empire">Austro-Hungarian Empire</A>, who did not meet under normal circumstances. The <A href="/wiki/Sir_Thomas_Lipton_Trophy" title="Sir Thomas Lipton Trophy">Sir Thomas Lipton Trophy</A>, named after entrepreneur and sportsman <A href="/wiki/Thomas_Lipton" title="Thomas Lipton">Thomas Lipton</A>, was established in 1909 and was contested between clubs from Italy, Great Britain, Germany and Switzerland; the competition lasted for two years.<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP> The earliest attempt to create a cup for national champion clubs of Europe was made by Swiss club <A href="/wiki/FC_Servette" class="mw-redirect" title="FC Servette">FC Servette</A>. Founded in 1930, the <A href="/wiki/Coupe_des_Nations" title="Coupe des Nations">Coupe des Nations</A> featured clubs of ten major European football leagues and was deemed a success. Due to financial reasons, the competition was abandoned.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP>
</P><P>The first continental competition organised by <A href="/wiki/UEFA" title="UEFA">UEFA</A> was the <A href="/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League" title="UEFA Champions League">European Cup</A> in 1955. Conceived by <A href="/wiki/Gabriel_Hanot" title="Gabriel Hanot">Gabriel Hanot</A>, the editor of <I><A href="/wiki/L%27%C3%89quipe" title="L'Équipe">L'Équipe</A></I>, as a competition for winners of the European national football leagues, it is considered the most prestigious European football competition.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMoore2000217_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMoore2000217-3">[3]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP> When the European Cup was first played, Liverpool were in the <A href="/wiki/Football_League_Second_Division" title="Football League Second Division">Second Division</A>, following relegation from the <A href="/wiki/Football_League_First_Division" title="Football League First Division">First Division</A> after the 1953–54 season, and thus were ineligible for the competition.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKelly198850–51_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKelly198850–51-5">[5]</A></SUP> During their time in the Second Division, two further competitions were created: the <A href="/wiki/Inter-Cities_Fairs_Cup" title="Inter-Cities Fairs Cup">Inter-Cities Fairs Cup</A> and <A href="/wiki/UEFA_Cup_Winners%27_Cup" title="UEFA Cup Winners' Cup">UEFA Cup Winners' Cup</A>. Established in 1955, the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup was later re-branded as the <A href="/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League" title="UEFA Europa League">UEFA Cup</A> when it came under the auspices of UEFA in 1971.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMoore2000220_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMoore2000220-6">[6]</A></SUP> Since the 2009–10 season, the competition has been known as the UEFA Europa League.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> The UEFA Cup Winners' Cup was inaugurated in 1960 for the winners of domestic cup competitions.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMoore2000220_6-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMoore2000220-6">[6]</A></SUP>
</P><P>In 1962 Liverpool were promoted to the First Division. Two years later, they won the Football League championship, thus making their European debut in the <A href="/wiki/1964%E2%80%9365_European_Cup" title="1964–65 European Cup">1964–65 European Cup</A>. In the following years, further European competitions were inaugurated. The first, the <A href="/wiki/UEFA_Super_Cup" title="UEFA Super Cup">UEFA Super Cup</A>, was originally a match played between the winners of the European Cup and the Cup Winners' Cup. First established in 1973, it changed formats in 2000; since then, it has been contested between the winners of the Champions League (formerly the European Cup) and the Europa League (formerly the UEFA Cup), following the Cup Winners' Cup amalgamation into the latter.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> The <A href="/wiki/Intercontinental_Cup_(football)" title="Intercontinental Cup (football)">Intercontinental Cup</A> was a competition for the winners of the European Cup (later, the UEFA Champions League) and the South American equivalent, the <A href="/wiki/Copa_Libertadores" title="Copa Libertadores">Copa Libertadores</A>. Established in 1960, the Intercontinental Cup was jointly organised by UEFA and the <A href="/wiki/CONMEBOL" title="CONMEBOL">Confederación Sudamericana de Fútbol</A> (CONMEBOL). It ran until 2004, when the <A href="/wiki/FIFA_Club_World_Cup" title="FIFA Club World Cup">FIFA Club World Cup</A>, which includes the winners of all <A href="/wiki/FIFA#Structure" title="FIFA">six confederations</A>' regional championships replaced it.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="History">History</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Liverpool_F.C._in_European_football&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: History">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN id="First_steps_in_Europe_.E2.80.93_the_Shankly_years_.281965.E2.80.9374.29"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="First_steps_in_Europe_–_the_Shankly_years_(1965–74)">First steps in Europe – the Shankly years (1965–74)</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Liverpool_F.C._in_European_football&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: First steps in Europe – the Shankly years (1965–74)">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Bill_Shankly_statue,_Anfield_2018.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="Statue of a man with his arms held aloft" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Bill_Shankly_statue%2C_Anfield_2018.jpg/170px-Bill_Shankly_statue%2C_Anfield_2018.jpg" width="170" height="253" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Bill_Shankly_statue%2C_Anfield_2018.jpg/255px-Bill_Shankly_statue%2C_Anfield_2018.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Bill_Shankly_statue%2C_Anfield_2018.jpg/340px-Bill_Shankly_statue%2C_Anfield_2018.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3340" data-file-height="4980" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Bill_Shankly_statue,_Anfield_2018.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>Statue of <A href="/wiki/Bill_Shankly" title="Bill Shankly">Bill Shankly</A> outside <A href="/wiki/Anfield" title="Anfield">Anfield</A>. Shankly was the first Liverpool manager to win a European trophy.</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P><A href="/wiki/Bill_Shankly" title="Bill Shankly">Bill Shankly</A> began managing Liverpool in 1959, and it was under him that the team first competed in European competition in <A href="/wiki/1964%E2%80%9365_European_Cup" title="1964–65 European Cup">1964–65</A>, qualifying for the European Cup by winning the First Division championship the <A href="/wiki/1963%E2%80%9364_in_English_football" title="1963–64 in English football">previous season</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKelly198867_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKelly198867-10">[10]</A></SUP> The club's first opponents were <A href="/wiki/Knattspyrnuf%C3%A9lag_Reykjav%C3%ADkur" title="Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur">Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur</A> of Iceland, who they played in the preliminary round. Liverpool won 11–1 on <A href="/wiki/Aggregate_score" class="mw-redirect" title="Aggregate score">aggregate</A>. The next round, against Belgian club <A href="/wiki/RSC_Anderlecht" class="mw-redirect" title="RSC Anderlecht">Anderlecht</A>, was the first time in Liverpool's history that they wore their now common all-red strip. The decision was made to change from red shirts, white shorts and socks by Shankly, who wanted his players to make more of a psychological impact on opponents.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP> They beat Anderlecht and progressed to the semi-finals, where they met Italian team <A href="/wiki/F.C._Internazionale_Milano" class="mw-redirect" title="F.C. Internazionale Milano">Internazionale</A>. Before the first <A href="/wiki/Two-legged_tie" title="Two-legged tie">leg</A> at <A href="/wiki/Anfield" title="Anfield">Anfield</A>, Shankly asked two injured players to parade the <A href="/wiki/FA_Cup" title="FA Cup">FA Cup</A>, which Liverpool had won the previous week, to intimidate the Italians.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting199218_12-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting199218-12">[12]</A></SUP> The team won the match 3–1,<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP> but Inter won the second leg 3–0, securing a 4–3 aggregate victory. The second leg was controversial; Shankly described it as "a war".<SUP id="cite_ref-Hodgson_Independent_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Hodgson_Independent-14">[14]</A></SUP> He felt that the referee, Jose Maria Ortiz de Mendibel, had shown bias towards Internazionale,<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting199220_15-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting199220-15">[15]</A></SUP> and the Liverpool players felt cheated by his decisions.<SUP id="cite_ref-Hodgson_Independent_14-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Hodgson_Independent-14">[14]</A></SUP> The club's <A href="/wiki/1964%E2%80%9365_FA_Cup" title="1964–65 FA Cup">1964–65 FA Cup</A> victory ensured qualification for the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup the following season, and in that competition, they reached their <A href="/wiki/1966_UEFA_Cup_Winners%27_Cup_Final" class="mw-redirect" title="1966 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup Final">first European final</A>. <A href="/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund" title="Borussia Dortmund">Borussia Dortmund</A>, Liverpool's opponents, employed counter-attacking tactics that had paid dividends in previous rounds and did so again, with the West Germans beating Liverpool 2–1 after <A href="/wiki/Extra_time" class="mw-redirect" title="Extra time">extra time</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELiversedge199167_16-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELiversedge199167-16">[16]</A></SUP>
</P>
<DIV class="thumb tleft"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Elftal_van_Liverpool,_Bestanddeelnr_919-7002.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Elftal_van_Liverpool%2C_Bestanddeelnr_919-7002.jpg/220px-Elftal_van_Liverpool%2C_Bestanddeelnr_919-7002.jpg" width="220" height="145" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Elftal_van_Liverpool%2C_Bestanddeelnr_919-7002.jpg/330px-Elftal_van_Liverpool%2C_Bestanddeelnr_919-7002.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Elftal_van_Liverpool%2C_Bestanddeelnr_919-7002.jpg/440px-Elftal_van_Liverpool%2C_Bestanddeelnr_919-7002.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3648" data-file-height="2406" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Elftal_van_Liverpool,_Bestanddeelnr_919-7002.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>Liverpool face <A href="/wiki/FC_Petrolul_Ploie%C8%99ti" title="FC Petrolul Ploiești">Petrolul</A> in the first round of the <A href="/wiki/1966%E2%80%9367_European_Cup" title="1966–67 European Cup">1966–67 European Cup</A>.</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>In the next four seasons, they competed in the European Cup and Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, but failed to progress past the third round in either competition.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting199252–57_17-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting199252–57-17">[17]</A></SUP> A tie against Dutch team <A href="/wiki/AFC_Ajax" title="AFC Ajax">Ajax</A> during the <A href="/wiki/1966%E2%80%9367_European_Cup" title="1966–67 European Cup">1966–67 European Cup</A> was to prove pivotal in the history of Liverpool in European competition.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKelly198878_18-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKelly198878-18">[18]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Ajax_5%E2%80%931_Liverpool_(1966)" title="Ajax 5–1 Liverpool (1966)">Ajax beat Liverpool 7–3 on aggregate</A>. However, the style of football that Ajax played – a patient passing game, inspired by <A href="/wiki/Johann_Cruyff" class="mw-redirect" title="Johann Cruyff">Johann Cruyff</A> – convinced Shankly that Liverpool had to replicate this style to be successful in Europe.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting199248_19-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting199248-19">[19]</A></SUP> Liverpool reached the semi-finals of the <A href="/wiki/1970%E2%80%9371_Inter-Cities_Fairs_Cup" title="1970–71 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup">1970–71 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup</A>, losing 1–0 on aggregate to <A href="/wiki/Leeds_United_A.F.C." class="mw-redirect" title="Leeds United A.F.C.">Leeds United</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKelly198895_20-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKelly198895-20">[20]</A></SUP> They competed in the <A href="/wiki/1971%E2%80%9372_European_Cup_Winners%27_Cup" title="1971–72 European Cup Winners' Cup">1971–72 European Cup Winners' Cup</A>, despite losing the <A href="/wiki/1971_FA_Cup_Final" title="1971 FA Cup Final">1971 FA Cup Final</A>, as the FA Cup winners, <A href="/wiki/Arsenal_FC" class="mw-redirect" title="Arsenal FC">Arsenal</A>, had also qualified for the European Cup by winning the league championship. Liverpool were eliminated in the second round by <A href="/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich" title="FC Bayern Munich">Bayern Munich</A> of Germany, losing 3–1 on aggregate.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting199262–63_21-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting199262–63-21">[21]</A></SUP>
</P><P>The changes made to Liverpool's tactics came to fruition during the <A href="/wiki/1972%E2%80%9373_UEFA_Cup" title="1972–73 UEFA Cup">1972–73 UEFA Cup</A>. The club reached their <A href="/wiki/1973_UEFA_Cup_Final" title="1973 UEFA Cup Final">second European final</A>, where they faced <A href="/wiki/Borussia_M%C3%B6nchengladbach" title="Borussia Mönchengladbach">Borussia Mönchengladbach</A> of Germany. Liverpool won the first leg 3–0 as a result of two goals from <A href="/wiki/Kevin_Keegan" title="Kevin Keegan">Kevin Keegan</A> and one from <A href="/wiki/Larry_Lloyd" title="Larry Lloyd">Larry Lloyd</A>. Victory in this first leg meant Liverpool only needed to avoid losing by three or more goals in order to win the final. This influenced their tactics – <I><A href="/wiki/The_Times" title="The Times">The Times</A></I> reported that Liverpool employed a "holding action" against the "attacking Germans".<SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP> The tactics worked, allowing Mönchengladbach only two goals, granting Liverpool a 3–2 aggregate victory.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKelly1988105_23-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKelly1988105-23">[23]</A></SUP> Liverpool also won the First Division championship that season, and as a result qualified for the <A href="/wiki/1973%E2%80%9374_European_Cup" title="1973–74 European Cup">1973–74 European Cup</A>, where they were eliminated in the second round by <A href="/wiki/Red_Star_Belgrade" title="Red Star Belgrade">Red Star Belgrade</A> of Yugoslavia. At the end of that season, Shankly retired.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELiversedge199139_24-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELiversedge199139-24">[24]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H3><SPAN id="European_domination_.E2.80.93_the_Paisley_years_.281974.E2.80.9383.29"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="European_domination_–_the_Paisley_years_(1974–83)">European domination – the Paisley years (1974–83)</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Liverpool_F.C._in_European_football&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: European domination – the Paisley years (1974–83)">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Shankly was succeeded by his assistant, <A href="/wiki/Bob_Paisley" title="Bob Paisley">Bob Paisley</A>, in 1974.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGraham198544_25-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGraham198544-25">[25]</A></SUP> Liverpool competed in the Cup Winners' Cup during Paisley's first season and defeated <A href="/wiki/Str%C3%B8msgodset_IF" title="Strømsgodset IF">Strømsgodset</A> of Norway 11–0 at Anfield. This remains the club's largest margin of victory in all matches.<SUP id="cite_ref-Matches_26-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Matches-26">[26]</A></SUP> They lost in the next round to Hungarian side <A href="/wiki/Ferencv%C3%A1rosi_TC" title="Ferencvárosi TC">Ferencváros</A> on the <A href="/wiki/Away_goals_rule" title="Away goals rule">away goals rule</A>. In 1975–76 the club entered the UEFA Cup after a second-place finish in the First Division. Victories over <A href="/wiki/Hibernian_F.C." title="Hibernian F.C.">Hibernian</A> (Scotland), <A href="/wiki/Real_Sociedad" title="Real Sociedad">Real Sociedad</A> (Spain), <A href="/wiki/%C5%9Al%C4%85sk_Wroc%C5%82aw" title="Śląsk Wrocław">Śląsk Wrocław</A> (Poland), <A href="/wiki/Dynamo_Dresden" title="Dynamo Dresden">Dynamo Dresden</A> (East Germany) and <A href="/wiki/FC_Barcelona" title="FC Barcelona">Barcelona</A> (Spain) took Liverpool to their third European final. Crucial to their progress was goalkeeper <A href="/wiki/Ray_Clemence" title="Ray Clemence">Ray Clemence</A>, who made two important <A href="/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football)" title="Penalty kick (association football)">penalty</A> saves against Hibernian and Dresden, saving Liverpool from elimination on the away goals rule on both occasions.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELiversedge1991180_27-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELiversedge1991180-27">[27]</A></SUP> Their opponents in the final were <A href="/wiki/Club_Brugge_KV" title="Club Brugge KV">Club Brugge</A> of Belgium. Liverpool recovered from a two-goal deficit to win the first leg at Anfield 3–2, with <A href="/wiki/Ray_Kennedy" title="Ray Kennedy">Ray Kennedy</A>, <A href="/wiki/Jimmy_Case" title="Jimmy Case">Jimmy Case</A>, and Keegan scoring a goal each in a span of six minutes. A 1–1 draw at the <A href="/wiki/Jan_Breydel_Stadion" class="mw-redirect" title="Jan Breydel Stadion">Jan Breydel Stadion</A> in <A href="/wiki/Bruges" title="Bruges">Bruges</A> meant Liverpool won 4–3 on aggregate, earning their second UEFA Cup.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKelly1988118_28-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKelly1988118-28">[28]</A></SUP>
</P>
<DIV class="thumb tleft"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Anfield_Stadium_-_IMG_2164.JPG" class="image"><IMG alt="A set of gates with the inscription "Paisley Gateway" at the top. In the middle of the sets of gates are two emblems" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Anfield_Stadium_-_IMG_2164.JPG/220px-Anfield_Stadium_-_IMG_2164.JPG" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Anfield_Stadium_-_IMG_2164.JPG/330px-Anfield_Stadium_-_IMG_2164.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Anfield_Stadium_-_IMG_2164.JPG/440px-Anfield_Stadium_-_IMG_2164.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4320" data-file-height="3240" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Anfield_Stadium_-_IMG_2164.JPG" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>The Paisley Gateway is a tribute to former manager <A href="/wiki/Bob_Paisley" title="Bob Paisley">Bob Paisley</A>, who won a record three European Cups—and three European trophies in successive seasons—as Liverpool manager.</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>As the <A href="/wiki/1975%E2%80%9376_in_English_football" title="1975–76 in English football">1975–76 league champions</A>, the club entered the <A href="/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_European_Cup" title="1976–77 European Cup">1976–77 European Cup</A>. They defeated <A href="/wiki/Crusaders_FC" class="mw-redirect" title="Crusaders FC">Crusaders</A> of Northern Ireland and <A href="/wiki/Trabzonspor" title="Trabzonspor">Trabzonspor</A> of Turkey to reach the quarter-finals, where they faced the runners-up from the previous season, <A href="/wiki/AS_Saint-%C3%89tienne" title="AS Saint-Étienne">Saint-Étienne</A>. The French team won the first leg 1–0. The second leg at Anfield began well for Liverpool when Keegan scored in the first two minutes. Saint-Étienne equalised to make the score 2–1 on aggregate in their favour. Kennedy scored for Liverpool, but the away goals rule meant they still needed another goal to win the tie. With six minutes remaining, <A href="/wiki/David_Fairclough" title="David Fairclough">David Fairclough</A> was brought on to replace <A href="/wiki/John_Toshack" title="John Toshack">John Toshack</A>; he immediately scored in front of the <A href="/wiki/Spion_Kop_(stadiums)" title="Spion Kop (stadiums)">Kop</A>, ensuring a 3–2 aggregate victory for Liverpool.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992103_29-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992103-29">[29]</A></SUP> In the semi-finals, they defeated <A href="/wiki/FC_Z%C3%BCrich" title="FC Zürich">FC Zürich</A> of Switzerland 6–1 on aggregate to reach the final, where they met their opponents from the 1973 UEFA Cup Final, Borussia Mönchengladbach. The <A href="/wiki/1977_European_Cup_Final" title="1977 European Cup Final">final</A> was held in Rome, four days after the club had lost the <A href="/wiki/1977_FA_Cup_Final" title="1977 FA Cup Final">1977 FA Cup Final</A> to <A href="/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C." title="Manchester United F.C.">Manchester United</A>. Before the match, Paisley announced that striker Toshack would be fit to start. However, he was not named in the matchday squad. This change upset the Germans' game plan and allowed Keegan to torment his marker, <A href="/wiki/Berti_Vogts" title="Berti Vogts">Berti Vogts</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-30">[30]</A></SUP> Liverpool won 3–1 to become European champions for the first time.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELiversedge1991186_31-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELiversedge1991186-31">[31]</A></SUP>
</P><P>By winning the European Cup, they qualified for the European Super Cup and played the winners of the Cup Winners' Cup, German team <A href="/wiki/Hamburger_SV" title="Hamburger SV">Hamburg</A>, who had just signed Keegan.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992130_32-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992130-32">[32]</A></SUP> Liverpool won <A href="/wiki/1977_European_Super_Cup" title="1977 European Super Cup">the tie</A> 7–1 on aggregate.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992131_33-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992131-33">[33]</A></SUP> Liverpool entered the <A href="/wiki/1977%E2%80%9378_European_Cup" title="1977–78 European Cup">1977–78 European Cup</A> as champions and received a <A href="/wiki/Bye_(sports)" title="Bye (sports)">bye</A> in the first round. They defeated Dynamo Dresden and Portuguese team <A href="/wiki/S.L._Benfica" title="S.L. Benfica">Benfica</A> in the second round and quarter-finals, respectively. In the semi-final, the club again met Borussia Mönchengladbach, who won the first leg 2–1. Liverpool won the second leg 3–0, progressing to a second successive <A href="/wiki/1978_European_Cup_Final" title="1978 European Cup Final">European Cup final</A>, this time against Club Brugge at <A href="/wiki/Wembley_Stadium_(1923)" title="Wembley Stadium (1923)">Wembley Stadium</A> in London. In the final <A href="/wiki/Kenny_Dalglish" title="Kenny Dalglish">Kenny Dalglish</A>, who had been signed to replace Keegan, scored the winning goal after receiving the ball from a <A href="/wiki/Graeme_Souness" title="Graeme Souness">Graeme Souness</A> pass. The 1–0 victory meant Liverpool became the first British team to retain the European Cup.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELiversedge1991188_34-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELiversedge1991188-34">[34]</A></SUP> They faced Anderlecht in the <A href="/wiki/1978_European_Super_Cup" title="1978 European Super Cup">1978 European Super Cup</A>, but failed to retain the trophy, losing 4–3 on aggregate against the Belgian side.<SUP id="cite_ref-35" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-35">[35]</A></SUP> Liverpool were eliminated in the first round of the <A href="/wiki/1978%E2%80%9379_European_Cup" title="1978–79 European Cup">1978–79 European Cup</A> by English champions <A href="/wiki/Nottingham_Forest_F.C." title="Nottingham Forest F.C.">Nottingham Forest</A>. Nottingham Forest won the tie 2–0 on aggregate, and went on to win the competition.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKelly1988133_36-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKelly1988133-36">[36]</A></SUP> Liverpool entered the <A href="/wiki/1979%E2%80%9380_European_Cup" title="1979–80 European Cup">1979–80 European Cup</A> as English champions but were again eliminated in the first round, this time beaten 4–2 on aggregate by <A href="/wiki/FC_Dinamo_Tbilisi" title="FC Dinamo Tbilisi">Dinamo Tbilisi</A> of the Soviet Union.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELiversedge1991189_37-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELiversedge1991189-37">[37]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Liverpool participated in the <A href="/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_European_Cup" title="1980–81 European Cup">1980–81 European Cup</A> as English league champions, defeating Finnish champions <A href="/wiki/Oulun_Palloseura" title="Oulun Palloseura">Oulun Palloseura</A>, Scottish club <A href="/wiki/Aberdeen_F.C." title="Aberdeen F.C.">Aberdeen</A> and <A href="/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Sofia" title="PFC CSKA Sofia">CSKA Sofia</A> of Bulgaria to qualify for the semi-finals, where they faced three-time champions Bayern Munich. The first leg at Anfield finished goalless. In the second leg at the <A href="/wiki/Olympic_Stadium_(Munich)" class="mw-redirect" title="Olympic Stadium (Munich)">Olympiastadion</A> in Munich, Ray Kennedy scored in the 83rd minute and, although the German side equalised, Liverpool went through to the final on the away goals rule.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992154_38-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992154-38">[38]</A></SUP> They faced Spanish side <A href="/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F." title="Real Madrid C.F.">Real Madrid</A> in the <A href="/wiki/1981_European_Cup_Final" title="1981 European Cup Final">final</A>, held at the <A href="/wiki/Parc_des_Princes" title="Parc des Princes">Parc des Princes</A> in Paris. <A href="/wiki/Alan_Kennedy" title="Alan Kennedy">Alan Kennedy</A> scored the only goal to give Liverpool a 1–0 victory, which secured the club's—and Paisley's—third European Cup. As champions of Europe, Liverpool competed in the Intercontinental Cup against South American champions <A href="/wiki/Clube_de_Regatas_do_Flamengo" title="Clube de Regatas do Flamengo">Flamengo</A> of Brazil. Liverpool lost <A href="/wiki/1981_Intercontinental_Cup" title="1981 Intercontinental Cup">the match</A> 3–0.<SUP id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-39">[39]</A></SUP> The club's defence of the European Cup in <A href="/wiki/1981%E2%80%9382_European_Cup" title="1981–82 European Cup">1981–82</A> was ended by CSKA Sofia in the quarter-finals.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKelly1988154_40-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKelly1988154-40">[40]</A></SUP> Another quarter-final exit occurred in the <A href="/wiki/1982%E2%80%9383_European_Cup" title="1982–83 European Cup">1982–83 European Cup</A> when Polish club <A href="/wiki/Widzew_%C5%81%C3%B3d%C5%BA" title="Widzew Łódź">Widzew Łódź</A> eliminated Liverpool 4–3 on aggregate.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992163–164_41-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992163–164-41">[41]</A></SUP> Paisley retired as manager at the end of the season and was succeeded by his assistant, <A href="/wiki/Joe_Fagan" title="Joe Fagan">Joe Fagan</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGraham198553_42-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGraham198553-42">[42]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H3><SPAN id="Triumph_and_tragedy_.E2.80.93_the_Fagan_years_.281983.E2.80.9385.29"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Triumph_and_tragedy_–_the_Fagan_years_(1983–85)">Triumph and tragedy – the Fagan years (1983–85)</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Liverpool_F.C._in_European_football&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Triumph and tragedy – the Fagan years (1983–85)">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Liverpool_4_European_Cups.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="Four trophies inside a glass cabinet. The trophies have ribbons on them and there is memorabilia next to them" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Liverpool_4_European_Cups.jpg/220px-Liverpool_4_European_Cups.jpg" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Liverpool_4_European_Cups.jpg/330px-Liverpool_4_European_Cups.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Liverpool_4_European_Cups.jpg/440px-Liverpool_4_European_Cups.jpg 2x" data-file-width="640" data-file-height="480" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Liverpool_4_European_Cups.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>Replicas of the four European Cups Liverpool won from 1977 to 1984 on display in the club's museum</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>Liverpool entered the <A href="/wiki/1983%E2%80%9384_European_Cup" title="1983–84 European Cup">1983–84 European Cup</A> as league champions for the fourth time in five seasons. Victories over <A href="/wiki/Odense_Boldklub" title="Odense Boldklub">Odense</A> of Denmark and Spanish champions <A href="/wiki/Athletic_Bilbao" title="Athletic Bilbao">Athletic Bilbao</A> brought Liverpool to face Portuguese champions Benfica in the quarter-finals.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992164_43-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992164-43">[43]</A></SUP> Liverpool won the first leg at Anfield 1–0. In the second leg, their tactic of withdrawing Dalglish into midfield put Benfica's game plan into disarray,<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992166_44-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992166-44">[44]</A></SUP> leading to a 4–1 match victory and a 5–1 aggregate victory. Their opponents in the semi-finals were <A href="/wiki/FC_Dinamo_Bucure%C8%99ti" title="FC Dinamo București">Dinamo București</A> of Romania. The tie proved a <A href="/wiki/Liverpool_vs._Dinamo_Bucharest,_1984_European_Cup_Semi-Final" class="mw-redirect" title="Liverpool vs. Dinamo Bucharest, 1984 European Cup Semi-Final">brutal encounter</A>, characterised by Souness breaking the jaw of the Bucharest <A href="/wiki/Captain_(association_football)" title="Captain (association football)">captain</A> <A href="/wiki/Lic%C4%83_Movil%C4%83" title="Lică Movilă">Lică Movilă</A>, and was won 3–1 on aggregate by Liverpool.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992166_44-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992166-44">[44]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Fagan's first season in charge of Liverpool had been a successful one. When they reached their fourth European Cup final, they had already won the <A href="/wiki/Football_League_Cup" class="mw-redirect" title="Football League Cup">Football League Cup</A> and the league championship;<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGraham198554_45-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGraham198554-45">[45]</A></SUP> victory in the European final against Italian side <A href="/wiki/A.S._Roma" title="A.S. Roma">Roma</A> would complete an unprecedented <A href="/wiki/Treble_(association_football)" title="Treble (association football)">treble</A>. The final was played at Rome's <A href="/wiki/Stadio_Olimpico" title="Stadio Olimpico">Stadio Olimpico</A>, and Liverpool went ahead in the 13th minute when <A href="/wiki/Phil_Neal" title="Phil Neal">Phil Neal</A> scored, though Roma equalised towards the end of the first half. The score remained the same throughout full and extra time; Liverpool won the subsequent <A href="/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football)" title="Penalty shoot-out (association football)">penalty shoot-out</A>, with Alan Kennedy scoring the winning penalty after goalkeeper <A href="/wiki/Bruce_Grobbelaar" title="Bruce Grobbelaar">Bruce Grobbelaar</A> had put off <A href="/wiki/Francesco_Graziani" title="Francesco Graziani">Francesco Graziani</A>, causing him to place his penalty over the crossbar.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992169_46-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992169-46">[46]</A></SUP> After the game, gangs of Roma fans assaulted Liverpool supporters travelling back to their hotels.<SUP id="cite_ref-47" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-47">[47]</A></SUP> Success in the European Cup entitled Liverpool to compete in the <A href="/wiki/1984_Intercontinental_Cup" title="1984 Intercontinental Cup">1984 Intercontinental Cup</A>. However, they were unable to beat the winners of the Copa Libertadores, <A href="/wiki/Club_Atl%C3%A9tico_Independiente" title="Club Atlético Independiente">Independiente</A> of Argentina, who claimed a 1–0 victory.<SUP id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-48">[48]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Liverpool entered the <A href="/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_European_Cup" title="1984–85 European Cup">1984–85 European Cup</A> as champions, and once again progressed to the final, where their opponents were <A href="/wiki/Juventus_F.C." title="Juventus F.C.">Juventus</A> of Italy. They aimed to win their fifth European Cup and keep the trophy. The <A href="/wiki/1985_European_Cup_Final" title="1985 European Cup Final">1985 European Cup Final</A> was held at the <A href="/wiki/Heysel_Stadium" class="mw-redirect" title="Heysel Stadium">Heysel Stadium</A> in Brussels. The choice of venue had been criticised due to the dilapidated state of the stadium, and the club tried to persuade UEFA to change the venue.<SUP id="cite_ref-49" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-49">[49]</A></SUP> Before the kick-off, Liverpool fans breached a fence separating the two groups of supporters and charged the Juventus fans. The resulting weight of people <A href="/wiki/Heysel_Stadium_disaster" title="Heysel Stadium disaster">caused a retaining wall to collapse</A>, killing 39 people and injuring hundreds more.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGraham198555_50-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGraham198555-50">[50]</A></SUP> Despite calls for an abandonment, the match was played, as it was felt that further trouble would be caused otherwise.<SUP id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-51">[51]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Juventus won the match 1–0; <A href="/wiki/Michel_Platini" title="Michel Platini">Michel Platini</A> scored from the <A href="/wiki/Penalty_spot" class="mw-redirect" title="Penalty spot">penalty spot</A> to give Juventus their first European Cup.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992189_52-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992189-52">[52]</A></SUP> UEFA laid the blame for the incident solely on the Liverpool fans: the official UEFA observer stated, "Only the English fans were responsible. Of that there is no doubt".<SUP id="cite_ref-53" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-53">[53]</A></SUP> Three days after the final, UEFA banned all English clubs from European competition for an indefinite period. Liverpool were initially given an additional three-year ban.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992189_52-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992189-52">[52]</A></SUP> Fagan retired after the 1984–85 season and was succeeded by Dalglish, who took over as <A href="/wiki/Player-coach" title="Player-coach">player-manager</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-54" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-54">[54]</A></SUP>
</P><P>The ban on English clubs in European competitions ultimately lasted for five years, and even when the ban was lifted in 1990, Liverpool were not re-admitted; they had to serve an extra year. The ban prevented them qualifying for the European Cup in 1986 (as league champions and FA Cup winners), the UEFA Cup in 1987 (as league runners-up), the European Cup in 1988 (as league champions), the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1989 (as FA Cup winners) and the European Cup in 1990 (as league champions).<SUP id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-55">[55]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H3><SPAN id="Return_to_Europe_.281991.E2.80.932004.29"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Return_to_Europe_(1991–2004)">Return to Europe (1991–2004)</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Liverpool_F.C._in_European_football&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Return to Europe (1991–2004)">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P>Liverpool were allowed to return to European competition in the 1991–92 season, a year later than other English clubs. They qualified for the UEFA Cup as runners-up in the English league. Their manager by this stage was <A href="/wiki/Graeme_Souness" title="Graeme Souness">Graeme Souness</A>, who had taken over towards the end of the previous season following Dalglish's resignation.<SUP id="cite_ref-56" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-56">[56]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Their first match, in the <A href="/wiki/1991%E2%80%9392_UEFA_Cup" title="1991–92 UEFA Cup">UEFA Cup</A>, was against Finnish side <A href="/wiki/FC_Lahti" title="FC Lahti">Kuusyi Lahti</A>, which they won 6–1.<SUP id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-57">[57]</A></SUP> A 6–2 aggregate victory set up a tie against <A href="/wiki/AJ_Auxerre" title="AJ Auxerre">Auxerre</A> of France in the second round who they beat 3–2 on aggregate.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992204_58-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992204-58">[58]</A></SUP> The club defeated <A href="/wiki/FC_Swarovski_Tirol" title="FC Swarovski Tirol">Swarovski Tirol</A> of Austria in the third round 6–0 on aggregate before losing to <A href="/wiki/Genoa_C.F.C." title="Genoa C.F.C.">Genoa</A> (Italy) 4–1 over two legs in the quarter finals.<SUP id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992206_59-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHalePonting1992206-59">[59]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Liverpool's victory over <A href="/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C." title="Sunderland A.F.C.">Sunderland</A> in the <A href="/wiki/1992_FA_Cup_Final" title="1992 FA Cup Final">1992 FA Cup Final</A> qualified them for the <A href="/wiki/1992%E2%80%9393_European_Cup_Winners%27_Cup" title="1992–93 European Cup Winners' Cup">1992–93 European Cup Winners' Cup</A>, but this campaign was short-lived, as they were eliminated in the second round by Russian side <A href="/wiki/FC_Spartak_Moscow" title="FC Spartak Moscow">Spartak Moscow</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-60" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-60">[60]</A></SUP> Liverpool finished no higher than sixth in the <A href="/wiki/Premier_League" title="Premier League">Premier League</A> during the next two seasons, thus failing to qualify for European competition. In the <A href="/wiki/Liverpool_F.C._season_1995%E2%80%9396" class="mw-redirect" title="Liverpool F.C. season 1995–96">1995–96 season</A>, they entered the UEFA Cup, but again progressed no further than the second round, this time losing to <A href="/wiki/Br%C3%B8ndby_IF" title="Brøndby IF">Brøndby</A> of Denmark.<SUP id="cite_ref-61" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-61">[61]</A></SUP>
</P>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:202px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Liverpool-PSG_1997.png" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Liverpool-PSG_1997.png/200px-Liverpool-PSG_1997.png" width="200" height="148" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Liverpool-PSG_1997.png/300px-Liverpool-PSG_1997.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b7/Liverpool-PSG_1997.png 2x" data-file-width="391" data-file-height="289" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Liverpool-PSG_1997.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV><A href="/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C." title="Paris Saint-Germain F.C.">Paris SG</A> halted Liverpool's progress at the semi-final stage of the <A href="/wiki/1996%E2%80%9397_UEFA_Cup_Winners%27_Cup" title="1996–97 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup">1996–97 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup</A>.</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>As runners-up to League champions Manchester United in the <A href="/wiki/1996_FA_Cup_Final" title="1996 FA Cup Final">1996 FA Cup Final</A>, Liverpool were able to compete in the <A href="/wiki/1996%E2%80%9397_UEFA_Cup_Winners%27_Cup" title="1996–97 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup">1996–97 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup</A>. This proved the club's most successful campaign since their return to European competition, as they reached the semi-finals, where they were eliminated 3–2 on aggregate by <A href="/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C." title="Paris Saint-Germain F.C.">Paris Saint–Germain</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-62">[62]</A></SUP> In the next two seasons, Liverpool played in the UEFA Cup but were eliminated at an early stage of the competition, by <A href="/wiki/RC_Strasbourg_Alsace" class="mw-redirect" title="RC Strasbourg Alsace">Strasbourg</A> and <A href="/wiki/Celta_de_Vigo" class="mw-redirect" title="Celta de Vigo">Celta de Vigo</A>, respectively.<SUP id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-63">[63]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-64" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-64">[64]</A></SUP> A seventh-place finish in the <A href="/wiki/1998%E2%80%9399_FA_Premier_League" title="1998–99 FA Premier League">1998–99 FA Premier League</A> meant the club did not qualify for Europe in <A href="/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Liverpool_F.C._season" title="1999–2000 Liverpool F.C. season">1999–2000</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-65">[65]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Having finished fourth in the <A href="/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_FA_Premier_League" title="1999–2000 FA Premier League">1999–2000 FA Premier League</A>, Liverpool qualified for the <A href="/wiki/2000%E2%80%9301_UEFA_Cup" title="2000–01 UEFA Cup">2000–01 UEFA Cup</A>. Their victory in this competition marked a third win for a club. The entire season was the club's most successful since the <A href="/wiki/1983%E2%80%9384_Liverpool_F.C._season" title="1983–84 Liverpool F.C. season">1983–84 season</A>, as they won a cup treble consisting of the UEFA Cup, the FA Cup and the League Cup. Their opponents in the <A href="/wiki/2001_UEFA_Cup_Final" title="2001 UEFA Cup Final">final</A> in <A href="/wiki/Dortmund" title="Dortmund">Dortmund</A> were <A href="/wiki/Deportivo_Alav%C3%A9s" title="Deportivo Alavés">Alavés</A> of Spain. The match was tied at 4–4 in extra time when Alavés defender <A href="/wiki/Delf%C3%AD_Geli" title="Delfí Geli">Delfí Geli</A> scored an own goal to give Liverpool victory on the <A href="/wiki/Golden_goal" title="Golden goal">golden goal</A> rule.<SUP id="cite_ref-66" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-66">[66]</A></SUP>	
The performance of <A href="/wiki/Gary_McAllister" title="Gary McAllister">Gary McAllister</A>, whose free-kick resulted in the winning goal, was praised as "outstanding" by <A href="/wiki/Trevor_Brooking" title="Trevor Brooking">Trevor Brooking</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-67" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-67">[67]</A></SUP> This was the club's first European trophy since their European Cup victory in 1984.<SUP id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-68">[68]</A></SUP> As UEFA Cup winners, Liverpool played in the <A href="/wiki/2001_UEFA_Super_Cup" title="2001 UEFA Super Cup">2001 UEFA Super Cup</A> against Champions League winners Bayern Munich and won 3–2.<SUP id="cite_ref-69" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-69">[69]</A></SUP>
</P><P>In the <A href="/wiki/2001%E2%80%9302_Liverpool_F.C._season" title="2001–02 Liverpool F.C. season">2001–02 season</A>, Liverpool returned to the European Cup, now called the UEFA Champions League, for the first time since the Heysel disaster. A 2–0 victory over Roma in the second group stage meant they progressed to the quarter-finals.<SUP id="cite_ref-70" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-70">[70]</A></SUP> They faced German club <A href="/wiki/Bayer_Leverkusen" class="mw-redirect" title="Bayer Leverkusen">Bayer Leverkusen</A> and won the first leg 1–0. The outlook for the second leg appeared to be to Liverpool's advantage, as their counter-attacking style of play had served them well during away matches throughout the season;<SUP id="cite_ref-71" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-71">[71]</A></SUP> however, they lost the second leg 4–2 and were eliminated 4–3 on aggregate.<SUP id="cite_ref-72" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-72">[72]</A></SUP>
</P><P>A second-place finish in the <A href="/wiki/2001%E2%80%9302_FA_Premier_League" title="2001–02 FA Premier League">2001–02 FA Premier League</A> entitled Liverpool to participate in the Champions League for a second successive season, but they only finished third in their group and were eliminated from the competition.<SUP id="cite_ref-73" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-73">[73]</A></SUP> The third-place finish meant they entered the <A href="/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_UEFA_Cup" title="2002–03 UEFA Cup">2002–03 UEFA Cup</A>. Liverpool beat Dutch team <A href="/wiki/Vitesse_Arnhem" class="mw-redirect" title="Vitesse Arnhem">Vitesse Arnhem</A> and Auxerre to set up an all-British tie with Scottish team <A href="/wiki/Celtic_F.C." title="Celtic F.C.">Celtic</A>. A 1–1 draw in the first leg meant Liverpool would progress to the semi-finals if they did not concede a goal in the second leg at Anfield. However, Celtic scored before half-time and again in the second half to win 3–1 on aggregate.<SUP id="cite_ref-74" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-74">[74]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Liverpool entered the UEFA Cup for the <A href="/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_Liverpool_F.C._season" title="2003–04 Liverpool F.C. season">2003–04 season</A>, after <A href="/wiki/Chelsea_F.C." title="Chelsea F.C.">Chelsea</A> beat them on the final day of the <A href="/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_FA_Premier_League" title="2002–03 FA Premier League">previous league season</A> to claim the fourth place needed to qualify for the Champions League.<SUP id="cite_ref-75" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-75">[75]</A></SUP> Liverpool were eliminated in the fourth round by eventual runners-up <A href="/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille" title="Olympique de Marseille">Marseille</A> of France. At the end of the season, manager <A href="/wiki/G%C3%A9rard_Houllier" title="Gérard Houllier">Gérard Houllier</A> was replaced by <A href="/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez" title="Rafael Benítez">Rafael Benítez</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-76" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-76">[76]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H3><SPAN id="Renewed_European_success_.E2.80.93_the_Ben.C3.ADtez_years_.282004.E2.80.9310.29"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Renewed_European_success_–_the_Benítez_years_(2004–10)">Renewed European success – the Benítez years (2004–10)</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Liverpool_F.C._in_European_football&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Renewed European success – the Benítez years (2004–10)">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tleft"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Amicizia.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="A stand of people standing up holding a mosiac which spells out Amicizia" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Amicizia.jpg/220px-Amicizia.jpg" width="220" height="69" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Amicizia.jpg/330px-Amicizia.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Amicizia.jpg/440px-Amicizia.jpg 2x" data-file-width="949" data-file-height="299" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Amicizia.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>Fans in the <A href="/wiki/Spion_Kop_(stadia)" class="mw-redirect" title="Spion Kop (stadia)">Kop</A> hold a <A href="/wiki/Card_stunt" title="Card stunt">mosaic</A> during the match with Juventus, 6 April 2005. <I>Amicizia</I> means "friendship" in Italian.</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>Liverpool had finished fourth in the <A href="/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_FA_Premier_League" title="2003–04 FA Premier League">2003–04 season</A>, which qualified them to compete in the Champions League in the <A href="/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Liverpool_F.C._season" title="2004–05 Liverpool F.C. season">2004–05 season</A>. A poor start in the group stages, with two losses in their first five games, had the club facing elimination. A 3–1 victory over Greek side <A href="/wiki/Olympiacos_F.C." title="Olympiacos F.C.">Olympiacos</A>, however, eventually ensured their passage to the knock-out rounds. Liverpool beat Bayer Leverkusen and Juventus to reach the semi-finals, and progressed to the final after they beat Chelsea 1–0 on aggregate; the goal scored by <A href="/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_(footballer,_born_1978)" title="Luis García (footballer, born 1978)">Luis García</A> was referred to as a "<A href="/wiki/Ghost_goal" title="Ghost goal">ghost goal</A>" by Chelsea manager <A href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho" title="José Mourinho">José Mourinho</A>, as it was unclear whether the ball crossed the goal line.<SUP id="cite_ref-77" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-77">[77]</A></SUP> Liverpool's performances in Europe contrasted strongly with their league form, where they struggled to finish in the top-four and thus ensure qualification for the next Champions League season.<SUP id="cite_ref-78" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-78">[78]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Liverpool faced six-time European champions Milan in the <A href="/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_Final" title="2005 UEFA Champions League Final">final</A> at the <A href="/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium" title="Atatürk Olympic Stadium">Atatürk Stadium</A> in <A href="/wiki/Istanbul" title="Istanbul">Istanbul</A> on 25 May 2005. Trailing 3–0 at half-time, they scored three goals in a six-minute spell in the second half to level the score at 3–3. There were no goals during extra time, so the match was decided by a penalty shoot-out. With the shoot-out score at 3–2, Liverpool goalkeeper <A href="/wiki/Jerzy_Dudek" title="Jerzy Dudek">Jerzy Dudek</A> saved <A href="/wiki/Andriy_Shevchenko" title="Andriy Shevchenko">Andriy Shevchenko</A>'s penalty to give Liverpool victory.<SUP id="cite_ref-79" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-79">[79]</A></SUP> The nature of Liverpool's comeback victory has led to the match being referred to as the "miracle of Istanbul."<SUP id="cite_ref-80" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-80">[80]</A></SUP> As this was the club's fifth European Cup victory, Liverpool were allowed to keep the <A href="/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs%27_Cup" title="European Champion Clubs' Cup">European Champion Clubs' Cup</A> permanently, and a new trophy was commissioned for the following year's competition.<SUP id="cite_ref-81" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-81">[81]</A></SUP> The victory also entitled Liverpool to compete in the <A href="/wiki/2005_UEFA_Super_Cup" title="2005 UEFA Super Cup">2005 UEFA Super Cup</A> at <A href="/wiki/Stade_Louis_II" title="Stade Louis II">Stade Louis II</A>, Monaco in August. They defeated UEFA Cup winners <A href="/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Moscow" title="PFC CSKA Moscow">CSKA Moscow</A> of Russia 3–1(aet.) to win their third Super Cup.<SUP id="cite_ref-82" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-82">[82]</A></SUP> Their success in the Champions League meant Liverpool also qualified for the <A href="/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship" title="2005 FIFA Club World Championship">2005 FIFA Club World Championship</A>, where they lost 1–0 in the <A href="/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_Final" title="2005 FIFA Club World Championship Final">final</A> to Brazilian team <A href="/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC" title="São Paulo FC">São Paulo</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-83" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-83">[83]</A></SUP>
</P><P>A fifth-place finish in the Premier League in 2004–05 meant Liverpool were not guaranteed entry into the Champions League, and faced the prospect of not being able to defend their European title. UEFA eventually ruled that they would be allowed to do so, but would be <A href="/wiki/Liverpool_F.C._2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Champions_League_qualification" title="Liverpool F.C. 2005–06 UEFA Champions League qualification">required to start</A> in the first qualifying round, with no country protection, meaning they could face a team from England in the group stages.<SUP id="cite_ref-84" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-84">[84]</A></SUP> This turned out to be the case—Liverpool advanced through three qualifying rounds and were drawn with Chelsea in the group stages. They progressed from their group as winners but were beaten by Benfica in the first knock-out round.<SUP id="cite_ref-85" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-85">[85]</A></SUP>
</P><P>In the <A href="/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_UEFA_Champions_League" title="2006–07 UEFA Champions League">2006–07 Champions League</A>, Liverpool progressed from the group stages and beat holders Barcelona, <A href="/wiki/PSV_Eindhoven" title="PSV Eindhoven">PSV</A> and Chelsea to face Milan in a rematch of the 2005 final.<SUP id="cite_ref-86" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-86">[86]</A></SUP> The Liverpool team, which contained only five players from the 2005 final, enjoyed more possession than in 2005,<SUP id="cite_ref-87" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-87">[87]</A></SUP> but two goals from <A href="/wiki/Filippo_Inzaghi" title="Filippo Inzaghi">Filippo Inzaghi</A> gave Milan their seventh European Cup in <A href="/wiki/2007_UEFA_Champions_League_Final" title="2007 UEFA Champions League Final">a 2–1 win</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-88" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-88">[88]</A></SUP>
</P>
<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Arsenal_Liverpool_CL0708.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="A line of people on a field, behind them are three red banners.UEFA Champions League quarter-final" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Arsenal_Liverpool_CL0708.jpg/220px-Arsenal_Liverpool_CL0708.jpg" width="220" height="124" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Arsenal_Liverpool_CL0708.jpg/330px-Arsenal_Liverpool_CL0708.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Arsenal_Liverpool_CL0708.jpg/440px-Arsenal_Liverpool_CL0708.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2816" data-file-height="1584" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Arsenal_Liverpool_CL0708.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>Liverpool lining up at Arsenal in the quarter-finals of the <A href="/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Champions_League" title="2007–08 UEFA Champions League">2007–08 UEFA Champions League</A></DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>Liverpool were eliminated from the <A href="/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Champions_League" title="2007–08 UEFA Champions League">2007–08 Champions League</A> in the semi-finals by Chelsea, who they had beaten in the semi-finals in 2005 and 2007. A fourth-place finish in the <A href="/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Premier_League" title="2007–08 Premier League">2007–08 Premier League</A> secured their entry into the <A href="/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_UEFA_Champions_League" title="2008–09 UEFA Champions League">2008–09 Champions League</A>. Liverpool reached the quarter-finals and again faced Chelsea, but lost 7–5 on aggregate.<SUP id="cite_ref-89" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-89">[89]</A></SUP>
</P><P>A second-place finish in the <A href="/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Premier_League" title="2008–09 Premier League">2008–09 Premier League</A> entitled Liverpool to compete in the <A href="/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UEFA_Champions_League" title="2009–10 UEFA Champions League">2009–10 UEFA Champions League</A>, but their campaign was short-lived; they finished third in their group, and were eliminated from the competition. They entered the <A href="/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UEFA_Europa_League" title="2009–10 UEFA Europa League">2009–10 UEFA Europa League</A>, progressing to the semi-finals, where they were eliminated by eventual winners <A href="/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid" title="Atlético Madrid">Atlético Madrid</A> of Spain on the away goals rule after the tie finished 2–2 on aggregate.<SUP id="cite_ref-90" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-90">[90]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H3><SPAN id="Decline_and_Resurgence_.282010.E2.80.93present.29"></SPAN><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Decline_and_Resurgence_(2010–present)">Decline and Resurgence (2010–present)</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Liverpool_F.C._in_European_football&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Decline and Resurgence (2010–present)">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tleft"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:152px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Klopp_(24669321424).jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Klopp_%2824669321424%29.jpg/150px-Klopp_%2824669321424%29.jpg" width="150" height="248" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Klopp_%2824669321424%29.jpg/225px-Klopp_%2824669321424%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Klopp_%2824669321424%29.jpg/300px-Klopp_%2824669321424%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2347" data-file-height="3878" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Klopp_(24669321424).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV><A href="/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Klopp" title="Jürgen Klopp">Jürgen Klopp</A> managing Liverpool in a <A href="/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Europa_League" title="2015–16 UEFA Europa League">2015–16 UEFA Europa League</A> match against <A href="/wiki/FC_Augsburg" title="FC Augsburg">FC Augsburg</A>.</DIV></DIV></DIV>
<P>Rafael Benítez left the club at the end of the 2009–10 season and was replaced by <A href="/wiki/Roy_Hodgson" title="Roy Hodgson">Roy Hodgson</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-91" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-91">[91]</A></SUP> A seventh-place finish in the <A href="/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Premier_League" title="2009–10 Premier League">2009–10 Premier League</A> meant Liverpool would be competing in the <A href="/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_UEFA_Europa_League" title="2010–11 UEFA Europa League">2010–11 Europa League</A>. They beat <A href="/wiki/FK_Rabotni%C4%8Dki" title="FK Rabotnički">Rabotnički</A> of Macedonia and <A href="/wiki/Trabzonspor" title="Trabzonspor">Trabzonspor</A> of Turkey to progress to the <A href="/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_UEFA_Europa_League_group_stage" title="2010–11 UEFA Europa League group stage">group stage</A>, where Liverpool were drawn alongside <A href="/wiki/S.S.C._Napoli" title="S.S.C. Napoli">Napoli</A>, <A href="/wiki/FC_Utrecht" title="FC Utrecht">FC Utrecht</A> and <A href="/wiki/FC_Steaua_Bucure%C8%99ti" title="FC Steaua București">Steaua București</A>. They won two games and drew four to finish top of their group with ten points and progress to the round of 32.<SUP id="cite_ref-92" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-92">[92]</A></SUP> They were drawn against <A href="/wiki/AC_Sparta_Prague" title="AC Sparta Prague">Sparta Prague</A> in the next round. Before the tie was played, however, Hodgson was replaced by former manager Kenny Dalglish, who initially served as a <A href="/wiki/Caretaker_manager" title="Caretaker manager">caretaker manager</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-93" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-93">[93]</A></SUP> A 1–0 aggregate victory ensured progression to the round of 16, in which Liverpool lost 1–0 on aggregate to eventual runners-up <A href="/wiki/S.C._Braga" title="S.C. Braga">Braga</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-94" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-94">[94]</A></SUP> A sixth-place finish in the <A href="/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Premier_League" title="2010–11 Premier League">2010–11 Premier League</A> meant the club failed to qualify for European competition for the first time since 1999.<SUP id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-95">[95]</A></SUP> On the following season, victory in the <A href="/wiki/2012_Football_League_Cup_Final" title="2012 Football League Cup Final">League Cup final</A> ensured Liverpool a place in the <A href="/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_UEFA_Europa_League" title="2012–13 UEFA Europa League">2012–13 Europa League</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-96" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-96">[96]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Liverpool qualified for the <A href="/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase" title="2012–13 UEFA Europa League knockout phase">knockout phase</A> of the 2012–13 Europa League after winning their group at the <A href="/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_UEFA_Europa_League_group_stage" title="2012–13 UEFA Europa League group stage">group stage</A>, but were eliminated from the competition at the round of 32 by <A href="/wiki/FC_Zenit_Saint_Petersburg" title="FC Zenit Saint Petersburg">Zenit Saint Petersburg</A> on the away goals rule after a 0–2 loss away and a 3–1 win at home.<SUP id="cite_ref-97" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-97">[97]</A></SUP> A seventh-place finish in the <A href="/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Premier_League" title="2012–13 Premier League">2012–13 Premier League</A> and a failure to secure qualification via domestic cups meant Liverpool failed to qualify for any European competition in the 2013–14 season. A second-placed finish in the <A href="/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Premier_League" title="2013–14 Premier League">2013–14 Premier League</A>, ensured Liverpool qualified for the group stage of the <A href="/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Champions_League" title="2014–15 UEFA Champions League">2014–15 Champions League</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-98" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-98">[98]</A></SUP> One win out of six in the group stage meant they were eliminated and entered into the <A href="/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase" title="2014–15 UEFA Europa League knockout phase">knockout phase</A> of the <A href="/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Europa_League" title="2014–15 UEFA Europa League">2014–15 Europa League</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-99" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-99">[99]</A></SUP> The campaign was short-lived, as Liverpool eliminated by <A href="/wiki/Be%C5%9Fikta%C5%9F_J.K." class="mw-redirect" title="Beşiktaş J.K.">Beşiktaş</A> in the <A href="/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase#Round_of_32" title="2014–15 UEFA Europa League knockout phase">round of 32</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-100">[100]</A></SUP>
</P><P>Finishing sixth in the <A href="/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League" title="2014–15 Premier League">2014–15 Premier League</A> qualified Liverpool directly to the <A href="/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Europa_League_group_stage" title="2015–16 UEFA Europa League group stage">group stage</A> of the <A href="/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Europa_League" title="2015–16 UEFA Europa League">2015–16 Europa League</A>, where they faced <A href="/wiki/FC_Sion" title="FC Sion">Sion</A>, <A href="/wiki/FC_Girondins_de_Bordeaux" title="FC Girondins de Bordeaux">Bordeaux</A> and for the first time, Russian side <A href="/wiki/FC_Rubin_Kazan" title="FC Rubin Kazan">Rubin Kazan</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-101">[101]</A></SUP> During the group stage, manager <A href="/wiki/Brendan_Rodgers" title="Brendan Rodgers">Brendan Rodgers</A> was replaced by <A href="/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Klopp" title="Jürgen Klopp">Jürgen Klopp</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-102">[102]</A></SUP>  After winning the group, Liverpool qualified for the knockout phase, beating <A href="/wiki/FC_Augsburg" title="FC Augsburg">FC Augsburg</A> in the round of 32 before facing <A href="/wiki/Liverpool_F.C.%E2%80%93Manchester_United_F.C._rivalry" title="Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry">bitter rivals</A> Manchester United in the round of 16, the two clubs' first meeting in Europe.<SUP id="cite_ref-103" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-103">[103]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-104" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-104">[104]</A></SUP> Liverpool defeated them 3–1 on aggregate and victory led to a quarter-final tie with Klopp's former team <A href="/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund" title="Borussia Dortmund">Borussia Dortmund</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-105" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-105">[105]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-106" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-106">[106]</A></SUP> After a 1–1 draw in the first leg at <A href="/wiki/Westfalenstadion" title="Westfalenstadion">Signal Iduna Park</A>, Dortmund went 3–1 up in the return leg at Anfield with 33 minutes remaining, requiring Liverpool to score three goals due to the <A href="/wiki/Away_goals_rule" title="Away goals rule">Away goals rule</A>. Goals from <A href="/wiki/Philippe_Coutinho" title="Philippe Coutinho">Philippe Coutinho</A>, <A href="/wiki/Mamadou_Sakho" title="Mamadou Sakho">Mamadou Sakho</A> and a last minute winner from <A href="/wiki/Dejan_Lovren" title="Dejan Lovren">Dejan Lovren</A>, however, saw Liverpool complete the comeback and qualify for their first European semi-final since 2010.<SUP id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-107">[107]</A></SUP> There they faced <A href="/wiki/Villarreal_CF" title="Villarreal CF">Villarreal</A>, completing a second comeback after overturning a 1–0 defeat in the first leg at <A href="/wiki/Estadio_El_Madrigal" class="mw-redirect" title="Estadio El Madrigal">El Madrigal</A> to qualify for the final with a 3–1 aggregate win.<SUP id="cite_ref-108" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-108">[108]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-109" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-109">[109]</A></SUP> Liverpool played <A href="/wiki/Sevilla_FC" title="Sevilla FC">Sevilla</A> in the <A href="/wiki/2016_UEFA_Europa_League_Final" title="2016 UEFA Europa League Final">final</A> at <A href="/wiki/St._Jakob-Park" title="St. Jakob-Park">St. Jakob-Park</A>, <A href="/wiki/Basel" title="Basel">Basel</A>, on 18 May, losing 3–1. A 4th-place finish in the <A href="/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Premier_League" title="2016–17 Premier League">2016–17 Premier League</A> qualified Liverpool for the <A href="/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League" title="2017–18 UEFA Champions League">2017–18 UEFA Champions League</A> and a return to Europe's premier club tournament for only the second time in 8 years during the 2010s.
On 17 October 2017, Liverpool won 7-0 away to <A href="/wiki/NK_Maribor" title="NK Maribor">Maribor</A> in the third round of matches of the <A href="/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage" title="2017–18 UEFA Champions League group stage">group stage</A> of the 2017–18 UEFA Champions League. The win was a record away win for Liverpool in European competitions and also the biggest away win by an English team in the history of the European Cup.<SUP id="cite_ref-110" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-110">[110]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-111" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-111">[111]</A></SUP> After qualifying top of their group, they proceeded to defeat Porto 5-0 at the Estadio de Dragao, before holding them to a 0-0 draw on the return leg, then defeated domestic rivals Manchester City 3-0 and 2-1, and in the semi-finals, defeated Roma 5-2 at Anfield, before a 4-2 loss led to a 7-6 aggregate win, taking them to the <A href="/wiki/2018_UEFA_Champions_League_Final" title="2018 UEFA Champions League Final">final</A>, against holders Real Madrid. Liverpool lost the final by 3-1 but finished 4th in the <A href="/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Premier_League" title="2017–18 Premier League">2017–18 Premier League</A> to qualify for the <A href="/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League" title="2018–19 UEFA Champions League">2018–19 UEFA Champions League</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-112" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-112">[112]</A></SUP>
</P>

<H1 id="firstHeading" class="firstHeading" lang="en"><I>You'll Never Make Love in This Town Again</I></H1>			<DIV id="bodyContent" class="mw-body-content">
				<DIV id="siteSub" class="noprint">From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia</DIV>				<DIV id="contentSub"></DIV>

				<DIV id="mw-content-text" lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr"><DIV class="mw-parser-output"><P><I><B>You'll Never Make Love In This Town Again</B></I> is a book published in January 1996 which describes the stories of three prostitutes and one actress about their sexual encounters with various Hollywood celebrities. The sisters <A href="/wiki/Robin_Greer" title="Robin Greer">Robin Greer</A> and <A href="/wiki/Liza_Greer" class="mw-redirect" title="Liza Greer">Liza Greer</A> are contributors along with Linda Hammond and Alexandra D. Datig, identified in the book as "Tiffany". The book generated extensive notoriety and sales, and was also the subject of a low-budget documentary.<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP></P>
<P>The book was the subject of several reported lawsuits. On 1 March 1996 the woman referred to as "Tiffany" sued the publisher Dove Books, and its executive, <A href="/wiki/Michael_Viner" title="Michael Viner">Michael Viner</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> The action was dismissed by the Superior Court on October 23, 1996, but on July 15, 1999, it was reinstated and remanded for further proceedings by the <A href="/wiki/California_Court_of_Appeal" class="mw-redirect" title="California Court of Appeal">California Court of Appeal</A> (Second District). In its published opinion, the court noted that "it appears that defense counsel violated several state wide rules of court and local rules, and that these violations resulted in unnecessary litigation and cost to plaintiff and her attorney in time and money," and instructed the Superior Court to consider sanctions against defendants and their attorneys.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP> Linda Hammond sued Viner for sexual harassment. The suit was dropped.</P>
<P>In another case, Viner sued Hollywood <A href="/wiki/Madam" title="Madam">madam</A> <A href="/wiki/Heidi_Fleiss" title="Heidi Fleiss">Heidi Fleiss</A> for <A href="/wiki/Slander" class="mw-redirect" title="Slander">slander</A>, based on statements Fleiss made on a radio talk show about Viner and authors of the book. In 2000 a jury ruled in Fleiss's favor.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP> In another case, one of the authors claimed that she had been forced unfairly to agree to reduced royalties under her contract with the publisher, and she won a jury verdict in her favor.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>
<P>There were two sequels <I>Once More With Feeling: You'll Never Make Love in This Town Again Again</I> was published in 1996. It told the stories of prostitute Michelle (who appears on the cover), prostitute Lisa, and graphic artist Sophie, among others.</P>
<P><I>Hooking Up: You'll Never Make Love in This Town Again Again</I>, appeared in 2006. It told the tales of prostitute Olivia, porn publicist <A href="/wiki/Carly_Milne" title="Carly Milne">Carly Milne</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> and prostitute Amanda.</P>

<H1 id="firstHeading" class="firstHeading" lang="en">Urban heat island</H1>			<DIV id="bodyContent" class="mw-body-content">
				<DIV id="siteSub" class="noprint">From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia</DIV>				<DIV id="contentSub"></DIV>
				<DIV id="jump-to-nav"></DIV>				<A class="mw-jump-link" href="#mw-head">Jump to navigation</A>
				<A class="mw-jump-link" href="#p-search">Jump to search</A>
				<DIV id="mw-content-text" lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr"><DIV class="mw-parser-output"><DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:302px;"><A href="/wiki/File:HeatIsland_Kanto_en.png" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/HeatIsland_Kanto_en.png/300px-HeatIsland_Kanto_en.png" width="300" height="225" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/HeatIsland_Kanto_en.png/450px-HeatIsland_Kanto_en.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/HeatIsland_Kanto_en.png/600px-HeatIsland_Kanto_en.png 2x" data-file-width="2000" data-file-height="1500" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:HeatIsland_Kanto_en.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
<A href="/wiki/Tokyo" title="Tokyo">Tokyo</A>, an example of an urban heat island. Normal temperatures of Tokyo go up more than those of the surrounding area.</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>An <B>urban heat island</B> (<B>UHI</B>) is an <A href="/wiki/Urban_area" title="Urban area">urban area</A> or <A href="/wiki/Metropolitan_area" title="Metropolitan area">metropolitan area</A> that is significantly warmer than its surrounding <A href="/wiki/Rural_area" title="Rural area">rural areas</A> due to human activities. The <A href="/wiki/Temperature" title="Temperature">temperature</A> difference usually is larger at night than during the day, and is most apparent when <A href="/wiki/Wind" title="Wind">winds</A> are weak. UHI is most noticeable during the <A href="/wiki/Summer" title="Summer">summer</A> and <A href="/wiki/Winter" title="Winter">winter</A>. The main cause of the urban heat island effect is from the modification of land surfaces.<SUP id="cite_ref-dx.doi.org_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-dx.doi.org-1">[1]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Waste_heat" title="Waste heat">Waste heat</A> generated by energy usage is a secondary contributor.<SUP id="cite_ref-liyan2012_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-liyan2012-3">[3]</A></SUP> As a population center grows, it tends to expand its area and increase its average temperature. The less-used term <B>heat island</B> refers to any area, populated or not, which is consistently hotter than the surrounding area.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Monthly <A href="/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Precipitation (meteorology)">rainfall</A> is greater downwind of cities, partially due to the UHI. Increases in heat within urban centers increases the length of <A href="/wiki/Growing_season" title="Growing season">growing seasons</A>, and decreases the occurrence of weak <A href="/wiki/Tornado" title="Tornado">tornadoes</A>. The UHI decreases <A href="/wiki/Air_quality" class="mw-redirect" title="Air quality">air quality</A> by increasing the production of pollutants such as <A href="/wiki/Ozone" title="Ozone">ozone</A>, and decreases water quality as warmer waters flow into area streams and put stress on their <A href="/wiki/Ecosystem" title="Ecosystem">ecosystems</A>.</P>
<P>Not all cities have a distinct urban heat island. Mitigation of the urban heat island effect can be accomplished through the use of <A href="/wiki/Green_roof" title="Green roof">green roofs</A> and the <A href="/wiki/Reflective_surfaces_(climate_engineering)" title="Reflective surfaces (climate engineering)">use of lighter-colored surfaces</A> in urban areas, which reflect more sunlight and absorb less heat.</P>
<P>There are concerns raised about possible contribution from urban heat islands to global warming. Research on China<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP> indicates that urban heat island effect contributes to climate warming by about 30%.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> On the other hand, one 1999 comparison between urban and rural areas proposed that the urban heat island effects have little influence on global mean temperature trends.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> Many studies reveal increases in the severity of the effect with the progress of climate change.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP></P>
<P></P>
