<P><B>Ethan and Grayson Dolan</B><SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP> (born December 16, 1999<SUP id="cite_ref-cleveland_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-cleveland-2">[2]</A></SUP>), collectively known as <B>The Dolan Twins</B>,  are an <A href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">American</A> comedy duo who rose to prominence in May 2013<SUP id="cite_ref-heavy_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-heavy-3">[3]</A></SUP> on the video sharing application <A href="/wiki/Vine_(service)" title="Vine (service)">Vine</A>. They are currently signed to <A href="/wiki/AwesomenessTV" title="AwesomenessTV">AwesomenessTV</A>, and have been since 2015.<SUP id="cite_ref-tubefilter_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-tubefilter-4">[4]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-hollywoodlife_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-hollywoodlife-5">[5]</A></SUP>
</P><P>The twins are from the <A href="/wiki/Long_Valley,_New_Jersey" title="Long Valley, New Jersey">Long Valley</A> section of <A href="/wiki/Washington_Township,_Morris_County,_New_Jersey" title="Washington Township, Morris County, New Jersey">Washington Township, Morris County, New Jersey</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> On December 19, 2017 they published a video, highlighting what type of twins they are.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> In the video Ethan Dolan expressed doubt that they were identical twins, in truth they are.
</P><P>Since their beginnings, the duo has accumulated over 6.4 million followers on Vine and 4.4 million subscribers on YouTube, and embarked on a world tour titled the "4OU" Tour in 2016.<SUP id="cite_ref-tubefilter1_8-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-tubefilter1-8">[8]</A></SUP> The duo was also involved in a <A href="/wiki/Twitter" title="Twitter">Twitter</A> ad campaign for the social network's new stickers feature.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> At the <A href="/wiki/2016_Teen_Choice_Awards" title="2016 Teen Choice Awards">2016 Teen Choice Awards</A>, the duo won the awards for Choice Web Star: Male<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP> and Choice YouTuber.
</P><P>On March 27, 2018 it was reported that the two would be taking a step back from YouTube, through a video on their channel entitled <I>Bye For Now.</I><SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP> In the video they state that this is to re-evaluate themselves creatively and focus on their lives outside of YouTube.<SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP>
</P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Work_Outside_of_YouTube">Work Outside of YouTube</SPAN></H2>
<P><A href="/wiki/MTV" title="MTV">MTV'</A>s <I>Total Request Live</I> reboot added the Dolan twins to the shows lineup as correspondents, and provide on-air hosting duties across platforms.<SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP> It was announced in August 2018 that the twins had directed a music video for the Australian <A href="/wiki/Alternative_rock" title="Alternative rock">alt-pop</A> group <A href="/wiki/Cub_Sport" title="Cub Sport">Cub Sport</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14">[14]</A></SUP>
</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Controversy">Controversy</SPAN></H2>
<P>In September 2017, they claimed that the <A href="/wiki/Jake_Paul" title="Jake Paul">Jake Paul</A>'s version of their origins, seen in his memoir <I>You Gotta Want It</I> was not exactly the truth. In his book, Jake Paul claimed that the twins were only popular now because he featured them on his channel. They disputed this statement during an interview with fellow vlogger <A href="/wiki/Caspar_Lee" title="Caspar Lee">Caspar Lee</A>, instead stating that Jake and <A href="/wiki/Logan_Paul" title="Logan Paul">Logan Paul</A> "showed them the ropes".<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP>
</P><P>During a London Fan-Meet-Up in November 2017, miscommunication, large crowds, and delays caused the <A href="/wiki/Hyde_Park,_London" title="Hyde Park, London">Hyde Park</A> meetup to be a disaster. One mother claimed thousands of young fans had already arrived before the event was to start, causing chaos when the event was canceled 15 minutes before it was to start.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP> Afterwards the twins used Twitter to express their sorrow that the event was cancelled and asked for fans to be respectful and safe.
</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Fans">Fans</SPAN></H3>
<P>In October 2017, a fan called to attention through Twitter concerns about hateful and at times racist language from some fans that were being aimed at others. In some occasions it seemed to appear that entire accounts on Twitter and other social media sites, were created to harass people of color in the fan base.<SUP id="cite_ref-:0_17-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-:0-17">[17]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP> In response to reported actions of other fans, the original user who brought forward the concerns; @blck_goddess, revived the hashtag #dolanpoc to "highlight the POC in the dolan fandom..."<SUP id="cite_ref-:0_17-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-:0-17">[17]</A></SUP>
</P>
